## Securities Module Overview


This document provides comprehensive documentation for the **Securities** module of Temenos Transact. It covers **9 sub-modules** with a total of **197 feature areas**.

The Securities module consists of 9 interconnected sub-modules. Securities Core (SC) serves as the central hub, connecting trade execution to portfolio management, corporate actions, custody, and regulatory reporting.


### Sub-Module Summary


| # | Sub-Module | Code | Features | Description |
|---|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| 1 | **EU Financial Transaction Tax** | `EF` | 3 | EU Financial Transaction Tax module of Temenos Transact |
| 2 | **European Savings Directive** | `ET` | 4 | European Savings Directive module of Temenos Transact |
| 3 | **Global Custody** | `GC` | 5 | Global Custody module of Temenos Transact |
| 4 | **MiFID II Compliance** | `MIFID2` | 7 | MiFID II Compliance module of Temenos Transact |
| 5 | **Securities Core** | `SC` | 86 | Securities Core module of Temenos Transact |
| 6 | **Corporate Actions** | `SC_CA` | 46 | Corporate Actions module of Temenos Transact |
| 7 | **Central Securities Depositories Regulation** | `SCCSDR` | 5 | Central Securities Depositories Regulation module of Temenos Transact |
| 8 | **Securities Portfolio** | `SP` | 28 | Securities Portfolio module of Temenos Transact |
| 9 | **Tax Lots** | `TL` | 13 | Tax Lots module of Temenos Transact |


### How to Use This Guide


Each feature in this document is organized into the following sections:

- 📖 **Introduction** — Overview and purpose of the feature
- ⚙️ **Configuration** — How to set up and configure the feature
- 🔧 **Working With** — Operational usage and field descriptions
- 📋 **Tasks** — Step-by-step procedures
- 📊 **Outputs** — Reports, enquiries, and generated outputs

Each feature includes a **Quick Reference Card** at the top with application names, key fields, prerequisites, and a summary. Appendices provide a full glossary, consolidated field tables, and end-to-end use-case scenarios.

### 1.1  Derivatives


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The EUFTT functionality has the ability:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Agreement Date*, *Buy or Sell*, *Call or Put*, *Contract*, *Customer No.1*, *Effective Date*, *Ftt Countries*, *Ftt Tax Type* ... +9 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The EUFTT functionality has the ability:

- To identify the tax base to be considered on which the FTT is calculated.
- To have a link to specify the tax code or tax type condition at the contract or deal level.
- To understand the logic of residency and issuance principles.
- To identify the contract groups on which FTT needs to be applied.
- To get linked to the core tax framework and calculate the FTT amount.
- To store the FTT amounts along with the local equivalents.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configuration of EUFTT.PARAMETER application in Temenos Transact .


##### EUFTT.PARAMETER

This application is used to record the details of the institution’s agreement with the Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT), the effective date of the Financial Institution (FI), status (opt-in or opt-out) and certain default conditions.

While configuring the application, it is mandatory to,

- State the countries opted for EU FTT regulation.
- Update the Effective Date field with a value, since when the FIs started complying to the provisions of EU FTT regulation
- Provide the Agreement Date , when the respective countries agree to follow the EU FTT regulation. The value in the Agreement Date field must be greater than the value in the Effective Date field.

> **⚠️ Note:** Currently, there are 11 countries in favour of getting the EU FTT into effect. The user can add more countries by multi-valuing the Ftt Countries field.


#### 🔧 Working With

The applicability of EU FTT for derivatives transactions is explained in the below flow chart.

There are two key principles that govern the applicability of EU FTT residence and issuance principles. Both the principles apply for bonds, securities and equities. Only the residence principle is applicable for OTC derivatives and they are exempted from the issuance principle.

From the above statement, it is clear that a Temenos Transact bank or FI that engages itself in DX transactions are subject to FTT payment under the following circumstances.


##### Temenos TransactBank or FI is a Resident of Member State of EU FTT Zone

If Temenos Transact bank or FI is a resident of member state of EU FTT zone,

- It is liable for FTT on OTC deals.
- The respective counterparty is either a financial or non-financial entity.
- The respective counterparty is either a resident or non-resident of EU FTT zone.


##### Temenos TransactBank or FI is Not a Resident of Member State of EU FTT Zone

If Temenos Transact bank or FI is not a resident of member state of EU FTT zone,

- The respective counterparty (financial or non-financial) is a resident of the FTT zone.
- It is not liable for EU FTT. This is applicable for OTC derivatives. In case of exchange traded derivatives, further check is applicable for the issuance principle.


##### Issuance Principle is Not-Applicable

OTC derivatives do not come under the purview of issuance principle and hence not applicable.


##### FTT on Options and Futures

The FTT is calculated as part of the transaction. The details of notional amount, tax amount in base currency, local currency or EUR along with the details of tax type are stored in the contract.

When the contract is between the Temenos Transact bank and a non-financial institution, there is a single instance of tax to the account of Temenos Transact bank. When the contract is between the Temenos Transact bank and another bank or FI (either resident or non-resident of EU FTT) the instance of tax is double.

Temenos Transact bank is responsible for its own payment, if the respective counterparty is responsible for its tax liability. Also, the counterparty can calculate FTT, based on settings in the DX.CUSTOMER and DX.TRADE applications.

The Ftt Tax Type is specified in the DX.PARAMETER application. This provides the link to the tax framework. The FTT calculation details are stored in the transaction ( DX.TRADE ). In case of exchange traded derivatives, the FTT applicability is determined based on a transaction involving a FI, residence principle and issuance principle. There is a provision to exclude certain contracts (control at DX.CONTRACT.MASTER and DX.TRADE level) from the purview of FTT. The exemption field from the DX.CONTRACT.MASTER application is shown in the below screenshot.

The FTT in derivatives trade is on both the primary and the secondary side. However, it is possible to exclude the secondary side (that is, broker side) from the purview of FTT, if the broker is acting in a capacity that is considered as an exempt. The exclusion is based on the settings in the DX.CUSTOMER application where the customer roles are defined.


##### Chargeable Event Occurrence

The chargeable event for the FTT occurs when the financial transaction takes place. The FTT is also applicable on exercise.


##### Tax Base Amount Calculation

The base for tax calculation is the notional amount of the derivative contract. The notional amount is calculated as follows:

For futures, the notional amount is based on the forward price.


##### Chargeable Tax

As explained above, all derivative contracts attract a levy of 0.01% tax and accordingly these contracts are charged at 0.01% on the tax base amount.


##### TAX Base Currency, Tax Currency and Conversion rate used

Tax is always payable in EUR irrespective of the tax base currency or the country in which the tax is collected. In case of transactions involving EUR, the same is considered for tax base amount and 0.01% tax is applied to derive the tax amount. In other cases, the calculated tax amount is in different currency, which need to be converted to EUR.

Transactions with the European Central Bank and National Central Banks are exempted from the scope of the FTT. National banks of other EU members who are not party to EU FTT are also exempted.

Tax levied on the DX contracts must be accounted in the system. The three values to be stored at the contract level are:

- Tax currency and amount in FCY (that is, CHF).
- Tax currency and amount in EUR (converted into EUR).
- Tax currency in local equivalent in LCY (that is, USD).

> **⚠️ Note:** Where the tax calculated is in EUR and LCY is EUR, the same appears in all the three fields.

| S.No | Temenos Transact bank’s LCY | Tax arrived in | Tax payable in | Notional conversion | Debit PL | Credit suspense | Actual Conversion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | EUR | EUR | EUR | NA | EUR | EUR | NA |
| 2 | EUR | USD | EUR | USD-EUR | EUR | EUR | NA |
| 3 | EUR | GBP | EUR | GBP-EUR | EUR | EUR | NA |
| 4 | USD | EUR | EUR | NA | USD | EUR | EUR to USD |
| 5 | USD | USD | EUR | NA | USD | EUR | USD to EUR |
| 6 | USD | CHF | EUR | CHF-EUR | USD | EUR | EUR to USD |
| 7 | GBP | EUR | EUR | NA | GBP | EUR | EUR to GBP |
| 8 | GBP | GBP | EUR | NA | GBP | EUR | GBP to EUR |
| 9 | GBP | CHF | EUR | CHF-EUR | GBP | EUR | EUR-GBP |


##### When Tax calculated is in EUR which is not LCY

- Debit - PL category in local CCY (equivalent of EUR) ( as defined in DX.Parameter - this can also be an internal account).
- Credit - Suspense a/c (as defined in tax record) in EUR.


##### When Tax calculated is in USD which is also LCY

- Debit - PL category in local CCY (USD). This can also be an internal account.
- Credit - Suspense a/c in EUR.


##### When Tax calculated is in CHF which is neither LCY nor EUR

- Debit - PL category in LCY (equivalent of EUR). This can also be an internal account.
- Credit - Suspense a/c in EUR.


##### When Tax calculated in EUR and Local Ccy is also EUR

- Debit - PL category in EUR (this can also be an internal account).
- Credit - Suspense a/c in EUR.


##### Exchange Traded derivatives

In case of exchange traded derivatives, one leg of the FTT is posted to the customer or counterparty account and the other to the tax suspense account (defined in tax record).


##### DX.PARAMETER

In order to apply FTT on derivatives, the DX.PARAMETER application must be setup.


##### DX.TRADE

Using the DX.TARDE application, the calculated FTT is stored in the respective transactions after applying the customer type and domicile checks.

The European Union Financial Transaction Tax (EU FTT) is a proposal made by the European Commission to introduce a Financial Transaction Tax (FTT) within the member states of the European Union. The tax impacts financial transactions between financial institutions and would result in charging 0.10% against the exchange of Shares and Bonds, and 0.01% across Derivative contracts, if just one of the financial institutions resides in a Member State (MS) of the EU FTT. The following modules in Wealth supports FTT in Temenos Transact :

- Securities (SC)
- Derivatives (DX)

Besides the above, FTT is also supported in SWAP, FOREX and FRA contracts. These modules generate the financial transactions, which falls under the preview of the FTT regulation.


##### Product Configuration

The EUFTT.PARAMETER is used to record the details of the institution’s agreement with the EFT, the effective date of the FI, status (opt-in or opt-out) and certain default conditions. It is necessary to state the countries opted for EU FTT regulation.

It is mandatory to update the Effective Date field, since when the FIs start complying to the provisions of EU FTT regulation and the Agreement Date field is updated when the respective countries agree to follow the EU FTT regulation. The value in the Agreement Date field must not be lesser than the value in the Effective Date field.

> **⚠️ Note:** There are 11 countries in favour of getting the EU FTT into effect. By multi-valuing the Ftt Countries field, more countries can be added by the user.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

EUFTT.PARAMETER is a company-level parameter containing information about the institutions agreed for FTT with associated countries. This parameter holds the following details:

- Agreement and effective dates from when the respective financial institution agrees to follow the EUFTT regulations.
- Current status of the financial institution with respect to EUFTT compliance.
- List of countries that have adopted this regulation.


##### Illustrating Model Products

Model products are not applicable for this module.

#### 📖 Introduction

The EUFTT functionality has the ability:

- To identify the tax base to be considered on which the FTT is calculated.
- To have a link to specify the tax code or tax type condition at the contract or deal level.
- To understand the logic of residency and issuance principles.
- To identify the contract groups on which FTT needs to be applied.
- To get linked to the core tax framework and calculate the FTT amount.
- To store the FTT amounts along with the local equivalents.
- To define the FTT rates specific to a particular security and use the same to calculate the FTT amount.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configuration of EUFTT.PARAMETER application in Temenos Transact .


##### EUFTT.PARAMETER

This application is used to record the details of the institution’s agreement with the Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT), the effective date of the Financial Institution (FI), status (opt-in or opt-out) and certain default conditions.

While configuring this application it is mandatory to,

- State the countries opted for EU FTT regulation.
- Update the Effective Date field with a value, since when the FIs started complying to the provisions of EU FTT regulation.
- Provide the Agreement Date , that is, when the respective countries agree to follow the EU FTT regulation. The value in the Agreement Date field must be greater than the value in the Effective Date field.

> **⚠️ Note:** Currently, there are 11 countries in favour of getting the EU FTT into effect. The user can add more countries by multi-valuing the Ftt Countries field.


##### Configuring FTT Rates for a Specific Instrument

To configure FTT rates for a specific instrument,

1. Set the Ftt By Sm field in EUFTT.PARAMETER to Yes to allow FTT Tax to be defined at the SECURITY.MASTER level.
2. Once this is setup, set the tax type in the FTT Type field in SECURITY.MASTER . The system then calculates the FTT for a transaction based on the tax type defined in SECURITY.MASTER . It does not calculate any FTT for transactions in securities where the Ftt Type (tax type) is not defined in SECURITY.MASTER .

> **⚠️ Note:** If the Ftt By Sm field is set to Yes in EUFTT.PARAMETER , the FTT calculation is based only on the FTT tax type defined in SECURITY.MASTER . No other checks are performed to determine if FTT is applicable.

Different FTT rate for securities instruments can be configured in two ways:

- Directly update the FTT Type in the SECURITY.MASTER record of the respective instrument.
- In many cases the same FTT tax type is applicable for multiple instruments, example all German domiciled Instruments follow the same FTT tax type. In this case, the SC.SM.TAX.CONFIG table can be used to define the FTT Type for all instruments with the same attribute. For example, instruments with the SM Attribute as SECURITY.DOMICILE and Attribute Value as DE, the FTT Type field is defined as *FTTDE. Once this record is authorised, the FTT Type field is automatically updated in all SECURITY.MASTER records that satisfy the given criteria.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user can manually amend the FTT Type at the instrument level.


#### 🔧 Working With

The applicability of EU FTT for Securities transactions is explained in the below flowchart.

The FTT is applicable only on transactions involving FIs. The FIs are identified based on the customer attribute (for example, sector). The SC transactions involving individuals and certain specified FIs are exempted from the provisions of FTT.

Once it is established that the customer is a FI, the domicile check is performed. The list of EU FTT countries is maintained in the EUFTT.PARAMETER application. The system validates whether the customer is domiciled in one of the countries in the list. If the customer is domiciled in one of these countries, the transaction is subject to tax. If the customer is not domiciled in one of the FTT countries, the next validation is the product domicile check.

This validation is only for SC income. If the product is not domiciled in one of the FTT countries, the transaction is exempted from FTT. The security domicile is defined in the SECURITY.MASTER application. However, it is possible to exempt certain securities (for example, government bonds issued to manage public debt) from FTT.

The Security Domicile field is used to identify the product domicile and the FTT Exempt field is used to exempt certain securities from the preview of FTT. The FTT is applicable on the following SC transactions:

- Securities trade
- Securities transfer
- Specific Corporate Actions (CA)

The transactions that subject to FTT, tax type of FTT and other parameters (include accrued interest for bonds) are specified in the SC.PARAMETER application. Certain transactions like primary market new issue and bond issue are exempted from FTT. FTT has different definitions of the taxable amounts based on the nature of the transactions being:

Financial transactions other than derivatives:

- Consideration paid or owed for the transfer.
- Market price (= at arm’s length price) if: Consideration is lower than market price or Transfer of financial instruments happen between entities of a group, when they do not constitute a purchase or a sale.

For SEC.TRADE , the base amount is the gross consideration (for bonds, it is gross consideration including the accrued interest). For transfers, the base amount is in the market price for free of payment transfers that do not constitute a purchase or sale. For transfers with payments, the base amount is either the consideration or the market price (whichever is higher).

The FTT calculated can be directly paid by the bank to the authorities or it can be remitted through the broker. A field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application controls this activity.

The FTT is also applicable on own book transactions, if the FI is domiciled in a FTT country. In such a scenario, the PL account is debited for the FTT. The FTT calculated is stored in the respective transactions (trade, transfer, events) as shown in the below screenshot.

When the tax is remitted in EUR, there is a field to specify the exchange rate for conversion to EUR, as a part of the transaction.


##### SC.PARAMETER

The transactions subject to FTT and other parameters are setup in the SC.PARAMETER application. The Tax Type field is setup as per the standard Temenos Transact tax framework.


##### SEC.TRADE

The FTT calculated is stored in the respective transactions after applying the customer type, customer domicile, product domicile and transaction type checks.


##### SECURITY.TRANSFER


##### Calculating FTT inSEC.TRADEusing COB Rate

In cross currency trades, if the customer account currency is different from the security currency, then FTT is calculated in account currency using the COB rate published by the central banks. The Ftt Cob Mkt field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Yes if the Cob Val Ccy Market field has a value in SC.PARAMETER . If Ftt Cob Mkt field is set to Yes, the system calculates the FTT in the customer’s account currency using below logic. The system removes the FTT value from Cu Net Am Trd field and converts the balance customer net amount using the market rate. The FTT amount is converted separately using the Cob Val Ccy Market field in SC.PARAMETER . Both values are added and updated in Cu Net Am Trd field, and processing is continued.

The security currency is in USD and customer account currency is in CHF. The FTT is calculated in EUR. The customer buys 100 shares at 1 USD. The net amount is account currency is calculated as shown below: (100*1*0.92) + (2*0.9) = 93.8 The accounting entry for the trade is generated as shown in the below screenshot.


##### Calculating FTT Based on Rate Defined at Instrument

When the Ftt By Sm field in EUFTT.PARAMETER is set to Yes, then FTT is calculated considering the FTT Type of the respective instrument in SECURITY.MASTER . FTT calculation is not applicable for those instruments where the FTT Type field is blank in SECURITY.MASTER . The parameter to identify the transactions subject to FTT and the parameter to include the accrued interest for bonds are still being referred from the SC.PARAMETER application.

#### 📖 Introduction

Introduction to Retail Sweeping ⓘ Content migrated: Old structure mapped (To be planned)

Related topic:

- Temenos Transact Services

The EU COUNCIL DIRECTIVE 2003/48/EC dated June 3, 2003 on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments (known as the European Union Savings Directive) came into force on July 1, 2005.

“The ultimate aim of the Directive is to enable savings income in the form of interest payments made in one Member State to beneficial owners who are individuals resident for tax purposes in another Member State to be made subject to effective taxation in accordance with the laws of the latter Member State.”

The European Union (EU) taxation on savings income is a system of tax retention initially of 15%, rising to 20% and then to 35% from 2011. The system of tax retention applies to all interest payments which a paying agent makes to an individual resident for tax purposes in an EU member state. It also allows the foreign bank customers to choose between a system of tax retention and a declaration to the tax authorities (voluntary declaration). The directive includes detailed descriptions regarding to whom this applies and where, as well as exceptions and special cases.


###### Directive Scope

All banks resident within the EU or in countries intending to comply with the directive (that is, Switzerland and other off-shore banking centers) is obliged to report the interest earned on all debt instruments. Certain specified funds fall within the scope of the directive or to calculate retention tax on such instruments held by EU citizens who are resident in another member state according to new rules as stated in the directive. In all cases, the new calculation rules is used to calculate the amount of taxable income which must be either reported to the customer's home country, or in the case of certain countries used to deduct retention tax. Where retention tax is deducted, the taxable income is split between the countries of residence of the bank and beneficial owner.

> **⚠️ Note:** These new rules apply only when the residency of the bank and the customer is different. All existing retention tax rules are same for dealing with residents of the same country, as the bank remain in force and are unaffected by this directive.


###### Affected Countries

The EU Savings Directive has an impact in the following countries:

- All member states of the EU (including new joiners)
- Austria, Belgium and Luxembourg are allowed to charge withholding tax, all other EU countries report the tax earnings
- Andorra
- Cayman Islands
- Caribbean Territories
- Gibraltar
- Guernsey
- Isle of Man
- Jersey
- Liechtenstein
- Monaco
- Netherlands Antilles
- Switzerland

Temenos Transact handles the withholding of tax to comply with the EU Savings Directive. This feature requires to install the European Tax (ET) module.


##### Product Configuration

This feature explains the necessary setup required in Temenos Transact for EU savings tax calculation.

Follow the below steps to do the initial installation:

1. Install the latest appropriate service pack and any subsequent patches.
2. Add the European Tax (ET) and Tax Engine (TX) products in the SPF application, along with the required license codes.
3. Add the ET and TX product codes to the required record in COMPANY .
4. Authorise the following released records in:

> **⚠️ Note:** The released records in TX.TXN.BASE.PARMS and TX.TXN.BASE.MAPPING are examples only. It must be authorised only after ensuring that the structure of the base is satisfactory.

The design workflow of EU Savings Directive i s explained in the below flowchart.

For transactions that are considered as ‘pending settlements’, the system updates the EU.TAX.LINK on the settlement date. For transactions in SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER and POSITION.TRANSFER with the transaction codes for pending settlement transactions, the system updates the EU.TAX.LINK from SC.SETTLEMENT . To enable the pending settlement transaction for SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER and POSITION.TRANSFER , the user should set the Sect Pend field as All in SC.PARAMETER . The transaction codes for such transactions are defined in the Sc Trans Name field in SC.PARAMETER .

The image below shows the design workflow of EU.TAX.LINK update for pending settlement transactions.

The details about the parameters are provided in the following sections.

Recording of the effective date for in-scope customers is mandatory. In-scope customers are further classified as those who are subject to retention tax and those who are only reporting (info customers). The classification of customers can be based on any of the existing core or local reference fields in CUSTOMER or a new local reference field is to be created for this purpose. It is recommended to create a Local reference field to hold the EU Status (used to record the customer’s status with regard to EU retention tax, for example, WHT applicable or EXEMPT).

The user must ensure the fields created for grouping customers for tax, are populated for existing customers before the initial base is built. This can be done either manually or through local routines. When new customers are created, ensure these details are populated for in-scope customers and the user can have version level checks for this.

The CONDITION.PRIORITY application details the conditions to be considered to create customer groups. This application needs to be amended for tax if the bank requires addition of new conditions on which the grouping of customers are based on. If the existing grouping conditions are sufficient, then amendments are not required. A combination of the Residence field and EU.STATUS local reference can be used to define the customer groups and route tax postings to separate accounts per EU member state. Therefore, these two fields must be added to the CONDITION.PRIORITY with the appropriate record in TAX as shown below.

The following fields in the TAX.TYPE application relates to the EU Savings Directive:

- Effective Date - Holds the effective date from which tax is applicable. An appropriate back-date may be setup for testing purpose.
- Local Tax Param - If EU tax is to be calculated, this field should be set to EU.TAX.PARAM . The name of this application cannot be changed and is hard-coded in the system. If any value other than EU.TAX.PARAM is set-up, EU tax is not calculated.
- Cust Chk Rtn - Contains the routine which checks whether the customer is liable for this tax or not. The SC.EU.SCOPE.CHECK routine is provided as part of the ET module. This routine needs to be specified in this field.

The TAX.TYPE record for the EU Savings Directive is set-up as follows:

The TAX.GEN.CONDITION application defines the customer groups for each type of tax. The groups are defined using the factors listed in CONDITION.PRIORITY record called TAX. The user must input a record for each customer group for EU retention tax. The record in CUSTOMER.CHARGE for each customer confirms the group applied for a specific customer.

> **⚠️ Note:** This application is updated as part of the COB, unless specifically adjusted for a particular customer.

The TAX application defines the specific characteristics of the tax itself, including the rate, category and transaction codes. For EU savings, the Base Amt Routine field is populated with the routine SC.EU.CALC.TAX.

The TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application establishes which record in the TAX application is to be used for the customer groups for this specific type of tax.

When there are joint holders in a portfolio, the EU tax is split between the holders in the ratio of their holdings. To achieve this, in the CUSTOMER.RELATIONSHIP application, the joint relationships are specified and the Relationship Type field is set to Tax.

Then, the CUSTOMER.RELATIONSHIP application is linked to portfolio using the Cus Relationship field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application. The CUSTOMER.RELATIONSHIP application has the effective date as part of the ID, so that the underlying application can process the tax by considering the latest record. It also ensures that the existing record is not changed even if there are any amendments in the customer.relationship application. The amendments are done through a new record in CUSTOMER.RELATIONSHIP , so that the historical information are retained in the system.

The system splits the EU taxes in the ratio of holdings specified in the CUSTOMER.RELATIONSHIP application. An example screenshot of Customer Relationship Id linked to the SEC.ACC.MASTER application is illustrated below. This determines the joint holders of a portfolio and the percentage of holding.

#### 📖 Introduction

Eureopean Union (EU) savings tax is calculated on the distribution received from mutual funds. The dividend is declared for a certain period. However, the customer may not have held the units for the full period. The customer may have acquired the units over different period of time. The customer should only be taxed on the income amount pertaining to the period that the customer has held the units, that is based on the holding period. The holding period is from the value date of the transaction (purchase) to the ex-date of the corporate event. This feature explains how the system calculates EU savings tax based on the holding period.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details the tax setup to be applied based on the holding period.


##### TXN.TAX.CODE

The Share Amount Base field in TXN.TAX.CODE accepts a value of holding period interest (HPI). This can be set for trade, transfer and also distribution type CA events like coupon, cash dividend and so on. The Txn Applic field holds the record in DIARY.TYPE pertaining to the distribution type event.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section details the tax calculation on distribution of mutual funds.


##### Determining Holding Period Interest

If holding period interest (HPI) is specified for a distribution event, then the holding period of each individual transaction that builds the qualifying holding for the event is considered and the base amount for tax is computed considering this holding period.

Example:

- Purchase Date July 1, 2005
- Distribution Date July 31, 2005
- Holding Period 30 days
- Nominal 5,000
- Distribution Rate 0.50
- Published % relating to interest 100 % (as this event is interest distribution)
- Gross Distribution 2,500
- Taxable Amount 2500*30/365 = 205.48
- Withholding Tax 30.82 (@15%)

The holding period is from the value date of the transaction (purchase) to the ex-date of the corporate event. If there is an interim distribution, the holding periods for subsequent distributions is from the ex-date of the earlier distribution.

The generic formula is:

If the last distribution date is not known, the entire distribution is taxed. The logic of computing holding period is based on the existing holding period options. (buy date or status date or EU date).

The Share Amount Base field still accepts a value of ID for distribution. If ID is specified, the tax calculation for the above example is as per the below table.

- Gross distribution 2,500
- Taxable amount 2,500 (no adjustment for holding period)
- Withholding tax 375

However, ID and HPI cannot be specified together.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Share Amount Base allows a value of ID only for distribution ( DIARY.TYPE ) and not for SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER .


##### Calculating Tax

For distributions, the interest distribution factor must be furnished in DIARY ( Int Dist Factor ), if only a portion of the distribution pertains to interest. If this is not input, the entire distribution is considered as interest distribution and is subjected to tax accordingly. The tax calculated is reflected in ENTITLEMENT . The Man Tax Acy field enables to apply manual tax to an ENTITLEMENT . When a manual tax is input, accounting entries are raised based upon this value and not on the system-calculated tax. The total in the Net Amount field on the transaction has only the manual tax amount deducted.

Both the system-calculated tax and manual tax are recorded on the transaction EU.ALLOCATION.DETS and EU.TXN.BASE. Whenever a back-dated corporate action event is input (even if the sale has already occurred), the system calculates the European savings tax. For cash events, the allocation is performed along with the rework process at the initial stage to enable the tax calculation.


##### Resetting of Interest Counter after Distribution

The interest distribution by funds is subject to tax. The interest counter in all underlying transactions covered by the distribution is reset to zero, so that when a subsequent sale is made, the base amount is depended upon the interest counter prevailing at the time of sale.

> **⚠️ Note:** For corporate actions, the interest counter is reset when a fund setup for interest counter tax calculation distributes its earnings.

- Setup TXN.TAX.CODE as distribution and HPI for calculating tax.
- Also, setup TXN.TAX.CODE as distribution and ID.

Input a DIARY for a full distribution event with the Rate Type set to Gross.

- After authorising the ENTITLEMENT , check the EU.TAX.LINK and EU.ALLOCATION.DETS applications to calculate tax for HPI.

For a mutual fund, setup some positions for info customers and customers who are in scope with the value date same as the trade date.

- Setup TXN.TAX.CODE as distribution and HPI for calculating tax.

- Also, set up TXN.TAX.CODE as distribution and ID.

Input a DIARY for an interim distribution event with the Rate Type set to Gross.

After authorising the ENTITLEMENT , check the EU.TAX.LINK and EU.ALLOCATION.DETS applications to calculate tax for HPI.

### 2.3  Tax on Redemption of Debt Instruments


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *European Union (EU) savings tax is deducted on income on debt instruments. When the instrument is redeemed below or above par, the difference over the initial subscription cost is treated as income and taxed. This feature explains how such income is calculated and taxed in Temenos Transact .*
> 
> **Prerequisites:** `DIARY`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.POSITION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Avg Disc*, *Avg Hpi*, *Bd Amt Base*, *Issue Price*, *Period Disc Prem*, *Redem Price*, *Sc Tax Code*, *Sc Tax Type* ... +4 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

European Union (EU) savings tax is deducted on income on debt instruments. When the instrument is redeemed below or above par, the difference over the initial subscription cost is treated as income and taxed. This feature explains how such income is calculated and taxed in Temenos Transact .


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following set up must done in Temenos Transact , to handle the tax deducted on income on debt instruments.


##### EU.TAX.PARAM

The Total Disc Prem field holds premium/discount rate upto which Total discount or premium is exempted from tax. If the premium/discount rate is higher than this amount, then the interest is taxable.. The Period Disc Prem field holds the premium or discount for a period below which interest is not taxed. If the difference between the issue price and redem price of the bond is lesser than or equal to Total Disc Prem and the difference between the issue price and redeem price divided by the no of year is lesser than or equal to Period Disc Prem then interest is not taxable.

> **⚠️ Note:** If different countries have different exemption percentages, the record in EU.TAX.PARAM must be set company wise with the respective values.


##### TXN.TAX.CODE

The Bd Amt Base field is set to AP (adjustment of premium). This works similar to holding period interest (HPI), it also computes the discount amount and deducts the discount amount from the HPI. The deduction of the discount is to the extent of the HPI.

> **⚠️ Note:** The discount computation and deduction is done at the time of sale of the security, that is, for all sell transactions. However, in case of a coupon payment through ENTITLEMENT , deduction is done only on the last interest payment. For all other coupons, the standard HPI calculation without any deductions are applicable.


##### TAX.TYPE

The record in this application is given as per the regular setup.


##### TAX.TYPE.CONDITON

The record in this application as per the regular setup.


##### TXN.TAX.CODE

Tax details for redemption are set in this application.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section details the tax on redemption of debt instruments.


##### Taxation of Premium and Discount

When a bond issued is redeemed below par, the difference between the redemption price and the initial subscription price constitutes taxable interest in the hands of the receiver. When a bond issued is redeemed above par, the excess paid at the time of subscription over the redemption price constitutes negative interest and it must be deducted from any taxable interest. The taxable interest remaining after this deduction is then subject to European Savings Directive (EUSD) taxation.

The banks consider the premium or discount at the point when the individual investor sells the security or when the security is redeemed. In some countries, the taxable interest is exempted from tax, if certain conditions are met.

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Total Hpi | Holds the average total interest of the outstanding nominal |
| Avg Hpi | Holds the average interest of the position |
| Total Discount | Holds the average total discount of the outstanding nominal |
| Avg Disc | Holds the average discount of the position |

#### 📖 Introduction

Where funds or debt instruments are sold or transferred, income needs to be computed for the purpose of European Union (EU) savings tax.

This feature document briefs on how the taxes are applied on bonds or other interest bearing component while performing a trade, security transfer, position transfer or in the event of a Corporate Action (CA).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Read the EU Savings Directive - Configuration document for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following sections details how the tax is calculated for various transaction.

The tax calculation in SEC.TRADE is triggered, when Cust Price field is input in a security trade (sale trade) involving customers and securities in scope of the directive. The tax is calculated and the details regarding tax code, tax amount in trade currency and tax amount in local currency are updated in the Cu Tax Code , Cu Tax Tcy and Cu Tax Lcy fields in SEC.TRADE respectively, tax is recorded in SEC.TRADE as shown in the below screenshot.

If the user inputs a transaction and if there are any changes to the transaction details like Customer , Security, Trade Date , Value Date or Nominal , the tax calculation has to be triggered again by re-entering the value in Cust Price field.

If the user inputs a trade involving funds (where the Base Amount Option is set to IC), the Interest Counter must be input prior to the entry of Cust Price . This is because when the option is set to IC, the base amount is lesser than the capital or interest counter gain. As a result, the interest counter needs to be input prior to input of Cust Price, so that the system can calculate the correct tax.

The Cu Mantaxtcy field applies a manual tax to a SEC.TRADE transaction. When a manual tax is input, accounting entries are raised based on this value and not on the system calculated tax. The value in the Net Amount field on the transaction has the manual tax amount only deducted. Both the system calculated tax and manual tax are recorded on the transactions in EU.ALLOCATION.DETS and EU.TXN.BASE. The manual tax recorded in the SEC.TRADE application is shown in the below screenshot.

While using the SECURITY.TRANSFER application, if TXN.TAX.CODE is set to compute tax on specific transfers, the tax is computed as shown in below screenshot.

The above TXN.TAX.CODE is set to compute the security transfers involving the transaction code TRO. When a transfer with this transaction code is input, the tax calculation is triggered by entring either PRICE or COST. A tax recorded on SECURITY.TRANSFER is shown in the below screenshot.

If the acquisition date of the security is not the same as the transfer date, the acquisition date must be input in Trfr Eff Date . Then, the holding period is computed from the Trfr Eff Date as this is considered as the purchase date. For inward transfers, if the Trfr Eff Date is not available, the acquisition date is considered to be the latest of EU tax, customer or security effective dates. For transfers out, if the Trfr Eff Date is not available, the trade date is considered the acquisition date.

The Cu Tax Tcy field applies a manual tax to a SECURITY.TRANSFER transaction. When a manual tax is input, accounting entries are raised based upon this value and not the system calculated tax. The total in the Net Amount field on the transaction has only the manual tax amount deducted. Both the system calculated tax and manual tax are recorded on the transaction, EU.ALLOCATION.DETS and EU.TXN.BASE . Manual tax recorded on SECURITY.TRANSER is shown in the below screenshot.

While processing the records in SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER , it is possible to record the NAV as either NET or GROSS of transaction costs. This is controlled in the Cu Nav Type field.

If NET is selected,

,

.

If GROSS is selected, the charges or commissions are ignored.

The difference between the cost of the acquisition and the sale consideration are considered as the capital gain and are subject to tax accordingly. Sample records for TXN.TAX.CODE and a SEC.TRADE are shown in the below screenshot.

An Interest Counter (IC) record in TXN.TAX.CODE is shown in the below screenshot.

A Capital Gains (CG) record in TXN.TAX.CODE is shown in the below screenshot.

The SEC.TRADE application is shown in the below screenshot.

Where agreements are allowed, it is possible to deduct charges for funds owned by customers who fall within the scope of the European Savings Directive before applying the European savings tax.

When a customer is selling funds that fall within the European Savings Directive, it is possible to deduct commissions or charges in processing the SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER . Such deductions are applied only to the interest counter element of the calculation and not to the capital gains calculation. If this deduction results in a negative value, the interest counter is considered zero and tax is not applied.

The system still considers the lower value of either Capital Gain or Interest Counter for calculation. To initiate the process of taxing funds that fall within the scope of the European Savings Directive net of charges, EU.FEES.DEDUCTION must be setup. The SEC.TRADE record in EU.FEES.DEDUCTION application is setup as shown in the below screenshot.

The POSITION.TRANSFER application does not involve any tax calculation. ### 3.1  Creation of Trades and Transfers


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This feature explains the creation of trades and transfers from incoming SWIFT (MT540-543) instructions for eligible institutional customers of banks (custody only).*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allowed Sec Type*, *Auto Cust Sett*, *Broker*, *Broker Nominal*, *Client No*, *Custody Eligible*, *Delivery Instr*, *Depot Advice Reqd* ... +24 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This feature explains the creation of trades and transfers from incoming SWIFT (MT540-543) instructions for eligible institutional customers of banks (custody only).

The feature also explains the transmission of settlement status message through SWIFT (MT548) to the institutional customers or External Asset Managers (EAM) to convey the settlement status of the instruction provided through MT540-543.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

For custody only business, the bank acts as a custodian for the Institutional Customers. The banks receive delivery or receipt instructions (MT540-543) from Institutional Customers or External Asset Managers (EAM). Based on the message received, the bank should register and settle the trade.


##### Trade Creation from Incoming SWIFT

The Temenos Transact system creates a trade from the incoming SWIFT message in the following ways:

- If Temenos Transact receives delivery or receipt instructions (MT541 or MT543) from Institutional Customers or EAM based on the message received, the system registers the trade with appropriate transaction codes.
- Simultaneously, the system also updates a log table SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG with the SEC.TRADE ID and relevant information.

- If the instruction is received from the EAM or Institutional Customers with Tag 23G=NEWM, then a record in SEC.TRADE is created for the ordering customer’s portfolio available in Tag 97A:// SAFE. The SECURITY.MASTER is identified using Tag 35B://ISIN. The Broker field in SEC.TRADE is an internal broker, which is defaulted from the SC.CUSTODY.PARAM application.

- After recording all the required fields in SEC.TRADE , the status in SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG application is marked as INPUT.

- The system creates the trade in IHLD status due to the following reasons: The ISIN and currency combination in the incoming message does not correspond to any of the record in SECURITY.MASTER . Customer security account in the incoming message does not correspond to any of the portfolio records in the system.

> **⚠️ Note:** For the cases mentioned above, if the system is not able to create the trade then the Status field in the log table is marked as HLD.

- Once the record is created in the SEC.TRADE application, the system checks for the below rules before authorising the trade: The security product for which the SEC.TRADE is created should fall in one of the sub-asset types defined in the Allowed Sec Type field in SC.CUSTODY.PARAM application. The customer in the trade should be eligible for custody only business. The Custody Eligible field in SEC.ACC.MASTER application is set to YES for the portfolio. The trade is not authorised when the appropriate cash account is missing in the incoming message (97A CASH) and if appropriate cash account is not defined in SEC.ACC.MASTER application. The EAM, who sends the incoming SWIFT has an appropriate mandate from the customer ( Eam Id field in SEC.ACC.MASTER application must record the EAM for the portfolio). The sub-asset type of the SECURITY.MASTER for which the SEC.TRADE is created is recorded in the Mandate Recd field in SEC.ACC.MASTER application.

If any of the above rules are not satisfied, then the system leaves the trade in unauthorised status and updates the Stp Fail Reason field with the appropriate reasons in SEC.TRADE and SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG . After the trade is authorised (automatically or manually), the status in SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG is updated as authorised.

Creating a sell trade from incoming MT543

The system receives a MT543 (NEWM) from the EAM and a SEC.TRADE is created for the ordering customer. The trade is authorised and the Status field in SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG is updated as Authorised.

Creating a buy trade in INAU due to authorisation failure

If the trade is created in INAU, then the system updates the failure reason in both SEC.TRADE and SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG . At this stage, the Status field is flagged as Input. Then the user manually authorises the trade. After authorising the trade, an MT541 is generated and sent to the depository.

The SEC.TRADE is created from incoming SWIFT instruction as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system additionally supports the creation of trade from an incoming MX sese.023. When an incoming sese.023 message is received with payment tag as AMPT (Against Payment Settlement), the system registers the trade with appropriate transaction codes. Simultaneously, the system also updates a log table SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG with the SEC.TRADE ID and relevant information. When a security transaction cancellation request (sese.020) is received and if the corresponding SEC.TRADE is authorised, the system updates the log and generates an outward sese.020 to the EAM or the customer. If the corresponding SEC.TRADE is unauthorised, the SEC.TRADE is deleted after the sese.020 message is received.


##### Transfer Creation from Incoming SWIFT Messages

The transfer is created from the incoming SWIFT messages by the following methods.

When the system receives an MT540/542, with one customer security account in Tag 97A::SAFE//, a security transfer is created and the status in SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG is updated as INPUT.

The created transfer is not authorised if the EAM does not appropriate mandate from the ordering customer (the Eam Id field in SEC.ACC.MASTER the EAM for the portfolio). The user manually authorises the transfer record. After authorising, the SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG is updated as Authorised and an MT540 or MT542 is sent out to the depository.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system additionally supports external transfers based on the details from an incoming MX sese.023. When an incoming sese.023 message is received with payment tag as FREE (meaning separate settlement), the system creates a record in SECURITY.TRANSFER .

When the system receives a MT542 with two customer security account in Tag 97A::SAFE//, the two records in Security.Transfer are created by the system. The SECURITY.TRANSFER transaction for transferring the position out is created for the delivering customer present in (MT542/FIAC Sequence/ Tag 97A/ (SAFE). The SECURITY.TRANSFER transaction for transferring the position in is created for the receiving customer present in (MT542/SETDET/SETPRTY/BUYR sequence/Tag97A/(SAFE//).

The SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG is created only for the SECURITY.TRANSFER (transfer out) transaction, with the status as INPUT. The ID of the SECURITY.TRANSFER (transfer in) record is updated in the Linked Txn field in the log table.

As mentioned in external transfer, the created transfer is not authorised if the EAM does not appropriate mandate from the ordering customer ( Eam Id in SEC.ACC.MASTER the EAM for the portfolio). The user manually authorises the transfer record. After authorising, the SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG is updated as Authorised. For all internal transfer transactions, the Auto Cust Sett field is defaulted to YES and the Depot Advice Reqd is defaulted to NO in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application. The ID of the SECURITY.TRANSFER application is updated in the Linked Txn field in the log table.

The Gen Eam Sett Del (in CUSTOMER.SECURITY ) in the Transfer In settlement is always NO for internal transfers.

Internal transfer created from MT542

The system updates the SC.CTDY.MSG.LOG for the transfer out transaction and the Linked Txn field is updated with the transfer in transaction reference.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system supports internal transfers based on the details from incoming MX sese.023. When an incoming sese.023 message is received with payment tag as FREE (meaning separate settlement), Securities Movement Type tag as DELI (Delivery) and has two safekeeping account, then the system creates two records in SECURITY.TRANSFER .


##### Trade Settlement and Settlement Confirmations

When the trade is authorised (manual or automatic), the system generates the settlement instructions to the depository (MT541 or MT543). The outgoing message has the broker and the settlement details as per the incoming SWIFT.

On the value date, the settlement is confirmed by the bank’s depository through MT545 or MT547 SWIFT messages. Based on the incoming SWIFT message, the system settles the trade in the SC.SETTLEMENT application.

After settlement, the system generates an appropriate settlement confirmation messages to both the instructing party and the ordering customer (if they are flagged to receive the messages).

The system receives a MT545 message from the depository and the SEC.TRADE is settled. An outward MT545 is sent out to the EAM and the ordering customer based on the setup in CUSTOMER.SECURITY application ( Gen Eam Sett Del and Gen Sett Del ). The delivery references are stored in the SC.SETTLEMENT application.

The generation of MT545 for the ordering customer is shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system also supports the generation of the MX Settlement Transaction Confirmation message (sese.025) and MX Securities Settlement Transaction Reversal Advice (sese.026) to the ordering customer based on the setup of the Gen Set Del field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application.


##### External Transfer Settlement and Settlement Confirmations

When the transfer is authorised (manual or automatic), the system generates the settlement instructions to the depository (MT540 or MT542). The outgoing message has the broker and settlement details as per the incoming SWIFT.

On the value date, the settlement is confirmed by the bank’s depository through MT544 or MT546 SWIFT messages. Based on the incoming SWIFT message, the system settles the trade in the SC.SETTLEMENT application. After settlement, the system generates the appropriate settlement confirmation messages to both the instructing party and the ordering customer.


##### Settlement Status Instruction through SWIFT MT548

When a trade or transfer is created in Temenos Transact from incoming instructions (MT540-543) or when a trade or transfer is created either through interface or directly, automatic or manual transmission of settlement status updates through MT548 is supported if the customer has subscribed to the same.

If Temenos Transact encounters any errors while creating the transactions (trade or transfers), the customer or EAM is notified through MT548 rejection advices. Temenos Transact also receives MT548 from the custodian in response to the MT54n messages sent to the custodian. The response from the custodian is also transmitted to the ordering customer or EAM.

The system builds a record in SC.CTDY.MT548.INSTRUCT for all the transactions (trade or transfer) created from incoming instructions as well as the transactions originating in Temenos Transact. The user can also use this application to manually enter the matching and settlement status of all the open transactions.

The Status field indicates the status of the settlement instruction during the life cycle of the transaction. The application also records high level statuses in the High Lvl Stat field:

- 548 Unmatched
- Failed Settlement
- New
- Ok
- Partially Settled
- Settled

The user can update the relevant information along with the status manually in SC.CTDY.MT548.INSTRUCT and trigger an outward message. The High Lvl Stat field indicates the stage or status of the transaction. It is updated automatically at various stages of the transaction. For example, as soon as the transaction is authorised, the status changes to New from Blank. This status is updated automatically at different stages and finally once the settlement is done, it changes to Settled.

If errors or overrides are not encountered while committing the transaction created from incoming MT540-543, the Latest Status field in SC.CTDY.MT548.INSTRUCT is updated as IPRC//PACK. The High Lvl Stat field is changed from blank to New. The status update notification through MT548 is generated for the ordering customer from the respective application ( SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER or POSITION.TRANSFER ).

When an incoming MT54n message from the customer has an error due to which Temenos Transact creates the security transaction on hold, an MT548 rejection advice is automatically triggered to the customer. The SC.SETT.REASON.CODES table contains the set of reason codes (SWIFT codes) that is updated in MT548 rejection advices. Temenos Transact checks the reason for failure and maps the reason code for the trades or transfers created from incoming MT540-543 messages.

If the customer has subscribed to MT548 status updates through SWIFT ( Gen Mt548 Instr field set to YES), the settlement status (received from the sub-custodian though MT548) is forwarded to the customer. In case, the status message is received from the sub-custodian through other channels, that is, Email or fax, then the customer can trigger an MT548 from SC.CTDY.MT548.INSTRUCT .

A record could be in the repair queue due to non-existent Temenos Transact reference or due to missing match code, or unmatched security ID, security movement type or quantity. In such cases, the user can manually reconcile the issues.

The MT548.REPAIR.RECONCILE lists all the items in the SC.MT548.REPAIR.QUEUE . Where the record is in the repair queue due to a non-existent Temenos Transact reference, the user can manually match the record with a Core Banking product transaction. If the user can identify the transaction then Temenos Transact reference can be updated in the Manual Recon Id field. Also, the particular transaction record can be updated with the relevant details in SC.MT548.MATCH.QUEUE .

If the record is in repair due to missing match code or unmatched security ID and if the user is able to reconcile the issue, then a proper narration can be updated in the Manual Recon Id field. All records in SC.MT548.REPAIR.QUEUE with Manual Recon Id field can be treated as reconciled.

If a message is in repair queue but subsequently a follow on message arrives where everything is matched, then Core Banking product automatically updates the Manual Recon Id field in SC.MT548.REPAIR.QUEUE and also the message details in SC.MT548.MATCH.QUEUE .

> **⚠️ Note:** When a trade or transfer is created in Temenos Transact from incoming instructions (MX sese.023) or when a trade or transfer is created either through interface or directly, then automatic or manual transmission of settlement status updates through sese.024 or sese.027 is supported if the customer has subscribed to the same by selecting the Gen Mt548 Instr field to Mx in CUSTOMER.SECURITY .

### 3.2  Custody Only Corporate Action


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This feature explains how Temenos Transact supports the custody only functionality for Corporate Actions (CA). Using Temenos Transact as custodian, the banks can:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Additional Narrative*, *Def Instr Apply*, *Depository*, *Entitlement Amt*, *Err Narrative*, *Gen MT567.1*, *Gen Mt564*, *Gen Mt564 Method* ... +16 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This feature explains how Temenos Transact supports the custody only functionality for Corporate Actions (CA). Using Temenos Transact as custodian, the banks can:

- Generate CA notification (MT564) to inform the institutional customers about the CA event.
- Generate additional narrative details (if any) related to the CA, through MT 568.
- Record the quantity of eligible holdings instructed by the customer for each option, after the customer elects the options through an MT565.
- Generate the processing status of the incoming MT565 to the institutional customers through an MT567.
- Handle the custodian confirmation for the CA instruction to the institutional customers through SWIFT MT566, to confirm the result of the CA (credit/debit of cash and/or stock).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the workflow of the custody only functionality for CA.


##### Transmitting MT564 to Institutional Customers

The SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION application is used to generate the CA related notifications MT564, 566, 567 and 568 for the institutional customers.

> **⚠️ Note:** The ID of this application is Corp Reference * Portfolio * Depository* Sub Account.

For each SWIFT message (MT564-MT568) generated by Temenos Transact, a set of fields relevant to that message type in this application are multi-valued. This application also stores the incoming MT565, recording the elections made by the institutional customers. The records in this application are created when there is an incoming MT564 or when the DIARY is created manually and the entitlements are created for the manual DIARY . The following options can be set in the Msg Function field in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION for MT564:

An MT564 message with the Msg Function set to NEWM is shown in the below screenshot.

A record in SC.PRE.DIARY is created, when an incoming MT564 is received (with Msg Function set to NEWM). The system determines the list of eligible customers and their qualifying holdings (based on ex-date or record date) and creates a record in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION similar to entitlement creation, provided the rules are set in SC.CTDY.CA.ADVICE .

If the user creates a record in DIARY manually in Temenos Transact, the system creates the records in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION along with the records in ENTITLEMENT .

If the rules are setup in SC.CTDY.CA.ADICE and if the Gen Mt564 Method field is set to STP, then MT564 is generated automatically and the delivery reference is stored in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION . In this case, the Sent By field is updated as STP, subject to rules (if any) defined in SC.CTDY.CA.ADVICE .

If the Gen Mt564 Method field is set to MANUAL, then MT564 is not be generated automatically for each of the institutional customers holding a position in the event security (as on record date or ex-date). The users need to manually trigger the bulk generation of MT564 from either SC.PRE.DIARY or DIARY application by setting the Gen Mt564 field to YES.

MT564 can also be generated for a particular portfolio. For this, the users need to multi-value the set of fields from Msg Type and update the Msg Function and Msg Status fields in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION . When the Send Msg field is set to YES, an outward MT564 is generated for that portfolio. In this case, the Sent By field is updated to MANUAL and check is not made against SC.CTDY.CA.ADVICE.

When an incoming MT564 with the Msg Function field as REPL is received and DIARY is not yet created or authorized, the changes due to REPL are updated in SC.PRE.DIARY and DIARY and no REPL is automatically sent to the institutional customers. When the DIARY is authorised, The status COMP is sent with the updated fields.If REPL is received after the DIARY is authorised, then Temenos Transact automatically sends out an MT564 REPL message.

When an incoming MT564 with the Msg Function field as REPE is received, the system updates the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG and MT564 is not sent automatically to the institutional customers. When the user re-runs the DIARY :

- The system sends an REPE to the institutional customers, where there is a change in eligible holdings.
- Only the institutional customers who have subscribed for receiving REPE in SC.CTDY.CA.ADVICE receives the notification automatically, whenever their position is changed.

If REPE is triggered manually from SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION for a specific customer, Temenos Transact generates the MT564 notification without checking the subscription status in SC.CTDY.CA.ADVICE .

When DIARY is re-run and the entitlement is dropped, Temenos Transact sends an MT564 with the status as REPE denoting the eligible holdings as 0 (in 93B://ELIG) to the institutional customers for whom an MT564 with NEWM was already sent.

| S.No | Cases | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | SC.PRE.DIARY is yet to be authorised | The Status field in SC.PRE.DIARY is set to CANC and SC.PRE.DIARY is authorised. However, DIARY is not created. When SC.PRE.DIARY is reversed manually, an MT564 CANC is sent out to those institutional customers who received the earlier notifications (MT564) from SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION. |
| 2 | SC.PRE.DIARY is authorised | An MT564 CANC is received, but DIARY is in INAU status. In this case, the system sets the Status field in SC.PRE.DIARY to CANC and deletes the record in INAU in DIARY . When the SC.PRE.DIARY is reversed, outward MT564 CANC is generated. |
| 3 | When DIARY is authorised | The system updates the Msg Status field in DIARY to CANC. The DIARY is not re-run due to this status update. When the DIARY is reversed, MT564 CANC is sent out to institutional customers from SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION . If the user needs a narration for cancellation, the DIARY has to be manually amended, authorised and then reversed. |


##### Transmitting MT568 to Institutional Customers

Temenos Transact supports outward MT568 messages to institutional customers. Generation of MT568 is always a manual process that is, it has to be triggered either from SC.PRE.DIARY or DIARY application. MT568 is not sent if the MT564 for the same PRE.DIARY or DIARY has not been sent.

The Gen Mt568 field in SC.PRE.DIARY and DIARY is used to trigger MT568 to the institutional customers. The user needs to manually set this field to YES to trigger the MT568. The last function and status is mapped to the MT568 along with the narration in the Additional Narrative fields. Once the record is committed MT568 is sent in bulk to the eligible institutional customers.


##### Receiving Elections Through MT565 from Institutional Customers

Temenos Transact supports the inward MT565 instruction from the institutional customers to convey the choice of elections in the event. For an optional event, Temenos Transact receives the MT565 per option. Each MT565 received, updates:

- The quantity of the eligible positions elected against each option in ENTITLEMENT , which is in INAU.
- Separate multi-values in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION application and the message reference is stored in the Inc Mt565 Ref field.

Any MT565 received after the cut-off date or after the ENTITLEMENT is authorised, does not update the ENTITLEMENT . Instead, it is recorded in the SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION application with Status as ERR and Narrative as Deadline Missed. An MT567 conveying this status can be triggered manually, if required. The cut-off date can be:

- Option Reply By Date if available for each option.
- Internal Reply By Date if available in DIARY.
- Def Instr Apply in DIARY.TYPE.
- Reply By Date in DIARY.

| Error Reason | Validation in Temenos Transact |
|---|---|
| Disagreement on quantity | The quantity elected for the option is not possible due to the difference in the trading quantity. A soft override is triggered. User can change this override to ERROR to ensure that entitlement is not authorised and instead Status is updated as ERR and sent to the customer |
| Lack of securities | The sum of elected quantity (for all the options) is more than the eligible quantity. A soft override is triggered. User can change this override to ERROR to ensure that entitlement is not authorised and instead Status is updated as ERR and sent to the customer |
| Market deadline missed | MT565 received after the internal cut-off date |
| Narrative | If ENTITLEMENT cannot be processed for any other reason apart from the above |


##### Transmitting MT567 to Institutional Customers

Temenos Transact supports outward MT567 message to acknowledge or reject each MT565 received from the institutional customers. The SEME REF of MT565 is updated in the LINK section of MT567.

If Proc Status field in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION is set to OK, then a MT567 with Msg Function (Tag 23G) set to INST and Msg Status (Tag 25D) set to IPRC or PACK is sent automatically. If Proc Status field in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION is set to ERR, then MT567 is not automatically sent. The reason for the error is defaulted in the Err Narrative field. In this case, the user needs to manually trigger the generation of MT567 individually by setting the Gen Mt567 field to YES.

The appropriate reason for error is mapped to Tag 70E in MT567. The message is sent with Msg Function set to INST and Msg Status (Tag 25D) set to IPRC or REJT. The reason code in Tag 24B is updated based on the below reasons:

| Tag 25D | Tag 24B | Tag 70E | Validation in Temenos Transact |
|---|---|---|---|
| IPRC or REJT | DQUA | Disagreement on quantity | The quantity elected for the option is not possible due to the difference in the trading quantity |
| LACK | Lack of Securities | The sum of elected quantity (for all the options) is more than the eligible quantity |  |
| LATE | Market Deadline missed | MT565 received after the Internal cut-off date |  |
| NARR | Narrative | If ENTITLEMENT cannot be processed for any other reason apart from the above |  |

> **⚠️ Note:** The user can also manually trigger the MT567 message from SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION upon configuring the editable fields manually.

The MT567 generated for the institutional customer is shown in the below screenshot.


##### Transmitting MT566 to Institutional Customers

Temenos Transact generates an MT566 to institutional customers confirming the events in which securities or cash movements occur. MT566 can be generated to convey entitlement authorisation (Tag 23G-NEWM) and entitlement reversal (Tag 23G-REVR).

- When Temenos Transact receives an MT566, (Tag 23G=NEWM), the system authorises the entitlements for all the portfolios, if the quantity or cash is reconciled (in case of omnibus accounts). In segregated accounts, an MT566 is received for separate portfolio. When reconciled, the entitlement is authorised.
- When the entitlements are authorised, a new multi-value is updated in the record in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION and an MT566 is generated for the institutional customers (if configured for receiving MT566 per option).
- For an event with options, if elections are made through MT565 per option, then MT566 is also sent per option.
- An MT566 is also generated for reversal of entitlement. For this, the user needs to manually reverse the record in ENTITLEMENT . When an entitlement is manually reversed, a multi-value is created in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION and an MT566 with Tag 23G-REVR is sent to the customer.

MT566 reversal is also generated when DIARY is reversed. When DIARY is reversed, the underlying entitlements are also reversed and results in an outward MT566 REVE.

- Manage Order Confirmation Cancellation - Custody

It covers settlement instructions, settlement confirmation, statement of holdings, corporate action notification, instruction management and confirmation handling. This module hand...*
>

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

The Institutional Custody (GC) module handles the account servicing functionality to the bank's institutional customer. It covers settlement instructions, settlement confirmation, statement of holdings, corporate action notification, instruction management and confirmation handling. This module handles incoming SWIFT messages from qualified institutional customers, and generates outgoing notifications and confirmations.

This module also supports the creation of order based on SWIFT (MX) messages. The entire chain of MX messages related to order creation and management are supported in Temenos Transact.


##### Product Configuration

The following configuration is set up to enable the system to automatically create the trades and transfers for the customers (through incoming SWIFT MT540-543).

This application is used to record the global parameter details for custody only business. The broker for custody only trades is an internal technical broker. The technical broker must be defined in this application using the Internal Broker field.

The Trd Cr Txn , Trd Dr Txn , Ext Trf Cr Txn, Ext Trf Dr Txn, Int TrfCr Txn and Int Trf Dr Txn fields are configured with the transaction codes which is to be used for the trades and transfers created from the incoming MT54n message. The sub-asset types allowed for custody business are updated in the Allowed Sec Type field.

This application stores the role of a customer. The sender of SWIFT instruction is generally the external asset manager (EAM) for the trades and transfers for institutional custody. In this application, the role of the EAM is flagged as shown below.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Custody Port No | Stores the alternate portfolio ID that is identified in the settlement instructions (MT 540-543). |
| Custody Eligible | Stores if the portfolio is authorised for custody business. |
| Eam Id | Stores the Eam Id, who has the mandate on behalf of this portfolio and sends the settlement instructions. |
| Mandate Recd | Stores the sub-asset type, for which the EAM has the mandate. |
| Hold Stmt Freq | Holds the time-frequency based on which the MT535 message is generated for this portfolio. Allowed frequencies are daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly. |
| Balance Type | Implies the type of balance to be sent in the MT535 message. Allowed values are : Traded, Contractual, and Settled. |

The system handles the below Corporate actions (CA) functionality for institutional custody, if the following parameters are configured.

- Transmission of CA notification to institutional customers (through SWIFT MT564)
- Transmission of CA narrative to institutional customers (through SWIFT MT568)
- Receive elections from institutional customers (through SWIFT MT565)
- Transmission of CA instruction status to institutional customers (through SWIFT MT567)
- Transmission of CA confirmation to institutional customers (through SWIFT MT566)

|  | Incoming MT564 | SC.CTDY.CA.ADVICE | Comment |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | Function | Status | Function | Status |  |
| Initial Message | NEWM | PREU | NEWM | - | MT564 should be generated |
| NEWM | PREU | NEWM | PREC | MT564 should not be generated |  |
| NEWM | COMP | NEWM | COMP | MT564 should be generated |  |
| Amendment Message | REPL | COMP | REPL | - | MT564 should be generated |
| REPL | COMP | REPL | COMP | MT564 should be generated |  |
| CANC | COMP | CANC |  | MT564 should be generated |  |

The CA notification (through MT564) is generated only for institutional customers, if the Gen Ca Advice field is set to 564.

The Gen Mt564 Method field in DIARY.TYPE allows the creation of MT564 message for that event type. This field accepts NO, STP and MANUAL values. The Mandatory Voluntary Flag field in DIARY.TYPE identifies the type of the event (MAND or VOLU or CHOS). If the DIARY.TYPE is for a mandatory event (MAND or CHOS), the Gen Mt564 Method field defaults to STP and if the DIARY.TYPE is a voluntary event (VOLU), the Gen Mt564 Method field defaults to MANUAL. The user can change the defaulted value, if required.

If the Gen Mt564 Method field is set to NO, then MT564 or MT568 is not generated for this event type.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The model parameters for GC module are explained below:

| Parameters | Description |
|---|---|
| Internal Broker | Indicates the internal broker used in creation of SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER while processing the incoming MT540-543 messages from institutional customers. |
| Trd Cr Txn | Defines the credit transaction of SEC.TRADE created out of incoming MT541 or MT543. |
| Trd Dr Txn | Defines the debit transaction of SEC.TRADE created out of incoming MT541 or MT543. |
| Ext Trf Cr Txn | Defines the credit transaction of SECURITY.TRANSFER created out of incoming MT540 or MT542. |
| Ext Trf Dr Txn | Defines the credit transaction of SECURITY.TRANSFER created out of incoming MT540 or MT542. |
| Int Trf Cr Txn | Defines the credit transaction code for internal security transfer created out of incoming MT542. |
| Ext Trf Dr Txn | Defines the debit transaction code for internal security transfer created out of incoming MT542. |
| Allowed Sec Type | Defines the allowed security types (asset type or sub-asset type) for custody or account service operations. Defining ALL in this field allows all product groups for this operation to create and authorise respective trades or transfers through incoming MT540-543 messages. |
| OFS Source | Indicates the OFS channel used for creation of trades or transfers. |
| OFS Version | Indicates the OFS version of trade or transfer that are used to create trade and transfers. |
| Mkt Fee Calc | Indicates whether the Market Fee for Security Trades has to be calculated based on Charge Calculation rules ( SCDX.CHARGE.PARAMETER ) or based on the value in the Incoming Swift. Default setup is to apply from Incoming 54n message. |

| Parameters | Description |
|---|---|
| Send MT564 Canc | Defines whether to generate MT564 when DIARY is reversed. |
| In MT564 Func | Holds the function of incoming MT564 for which outward MT564 needs to be sent. |
| In MT564 Status | Holds the status of incoming MT564 for which outward MT564 needs to be sent. |
