### 3.4  Order Management for Institutional Customers


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Institutional customers can send their order instructions through SETR.004 or SETR.010 for placing a redemption order or a subscription order respectively. The system performs line of instructions related to order flow, that is:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Action Notes*, *Action Status*, *Amend Expected*, *Amt*, *Broker*, *Broker / client*, *Broker Side Amount*, *Buy or Sell* ... +56 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Institutional customers can send their order instructions through SETR.004 or SETR.010 for placing a redemption order or a subscription order respectively. The system performs line of instructions related to order flow, that is:

- Receive order placement instruction from the institutional customer and create the order.
- Send order communication to the broker when the transaction is authorised.
- Receive order status change notifications from the broker.
- Send order status communication to the institutional customer.
- Receive order confirmation from the broker and execute the order.
- Send order confirmation to the institutional customer.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Customers who are eligible for SWIFT based order creation are identified by the Swift Order Instr field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY .

The sender of the SWIFT instructions can be an institutional customer itself or related bank on behalf of the institutional customer. The sender is configured in Swift Ord Sender field in SEC.ACC.MASTER of the institutional customer.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details about the creation and management of order based on the MX messages.


##### Creating Orders based on Incoming MX Messages

Institutional customers can send their order instructions through SETR.004 or SETR.010 for placing a redemption or subscription order respectively. Customers who are eligible to send SWIFT for order creation are identified by the Swift Ord Instr field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY .

On receiving MX order instruction messages SETR.004 (redemption order) or SETR.010 (subscription order), the system:

- Creates an order in SEC.OPEN.ORDER for the ordering customer if the customer eligibility criteria is met. The customer eligibility criteria is provided below. The tag from the incoming SWIFT (SETR.004 or SETR.010) must have the SEC.ACC.MASTER ID or Custody Port No of the customer for whom the order needs to be created. The Swift Ord Instr field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY should be set to Yes. The BIC of the SWIFT order sender needs to be defined in the Swift Ord Sender field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER .

- Updates the SC.ORD.INSTR.LOG simultaneously to capture the line of instructions from the order creation stage for each customer. The ID of the log is the SEC.OPEN.ORDER reference.

- Groups the created order and transmits at the cut-off time, if grouping conditions are met.

If Temenos Transact is not able to commit the SEC.OPEN.ORDER due to customer ineligibility, the SEC.OPEN.ORDER is not created. Instead, a record is created in SC.ORD.INSTR.LOG (ID as sender’s message reference, (that is, Msg ID of SETR.004 or SETR.010)) with all the details for the user to take corrective actions. The system simultaneously sends out MX rejection message (SETR.016) to indicate that the order is rejected.

If Temenos Transact is not able to commit the SEC.OPEN.ORDER due to missing details in the instruction, the SEC.OPEN.ORDER is created and kept in IHLD for the trading room user to investigate. If the trading room user completes the order, SETR.016 is sent to the customer with Order Instruction Status as RECE from the SEC.OPEN.ORDER .

If the order is incorrectly transmitted to the wrong broker, then the Deal Status and Order Status fields are set to Rejected. The system allows the user to amend the broker details, so that a new SETR.004 or SETR.010 can be transmitted to the correct broker.

> **⚠️ Note:** When the record in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is committed, a SETR.004 or SETR.010 is sent to the respective broker for transmitting the order.


##### Generating Order Status MX messages

When Temenos Transact receives a status change advice (Accepted, Rejected, Cancelled, Transmitted and Expired) from the broker (through MX message SETR.016), the system updates the Order Status field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS with the appropriate status. The SEC.OPEN.ORDER is also updated with the status change in Order Status field. The SC.ORD.INSTR.LOG is also updated with the status in the Order Status field and holds the incoming MX message references (that stores the reference of the incoming message).

If the Swift Ord Instr field is set in CUSTOMER.SECURITY to receive the respective status change advice, then whenever there is a change in the Order Status , the status change is communicated (manually) to the ordering customer through SETR.016. The Send Ord Status Adv field is used to trigger the SETR.016 to the institutional customer.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the Order Status is Accepted, the status is automatically conveyed to the institutional customer through SETR.016.


##### Confirming Order through Outward SWIFT MX Message

When Temenos Transact receives MX order confirmation messages from the broker or when the order is filled manually, the record in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDER is executed partially or fully. After the order is executed, the record in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDER is moved to the history file and the trade is created in IHLD. If the customer is SWIFT equipped (that is, Swift Ord Instr field is set in CUSTOMER.SECURITY ), then SETR.006 (redemption order confirmation) or SETR.012 (subscription order confirmation) is generated to the sender of the order instruction from SEC.TRADE .


##### Cancelling Orders based on Incoming MX Messages

Institutional customers can send cancellation requests for the previously sent redemption (SETR.004) or subscription order (SETR.010) by sending SETR.005 (redemption order cancellation request) or SETR.011 (subscription order cancellation request) respectively. On receiving MX order instruction messages, that is, SETR.005 (redemption order cancellation request) or SETR.011 (subscription order cancellation request), the system:

- Finds the previously created order using the order reference in the incoming message (stored in Cust Out Reference field of SC.ORD.INSTR.LOG )
- Checks whether the order is a single or group order which is based on the value in the Group Order field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER . If the Deal Status is blank for a single order, the system updates the Order Status field as Int Cancellation Accepted. If Deal Status is selected as Transmitted, the system updates the Order Status field as Cancellation requested and sends the cancellation request to the broker through SETR.005 or SETR.011. If the Deal Status is updated as Grouped for a group order, the system updates the Order Status field as Int Cancellation Accepted. If Deal Status is selected as Transmitted, the system updates the Order Status field as Int Cancellation Rejected.

Brokers confirms the status of cancellation request through SETR.017 message. The SETR.017 can be received with the below statuses:

- Cancel Request Received (RECE)
- Cancel Request Accepted (CAND)
- Cancel Request Rejected (RJCTD)

Once the cancellation status is received from the broker, system updates the Order Status field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER with the respective status (Cancellation Received, Cancellation Accepted, and Cancellation Rejected).

| Order Status | Deal Status | SETR.017 Status to Institutional Customers |
|---|---|---|
| Int Cancel Accepted | Cancelled | CAND |
| Int Cancel Rejected | Transmitted | RJCTD |
| Cancellation Requested | Transmitted | RECE |


##### Updating Incoming Order Confirmation Cancellation Instruction

A broker confirms the execution of an order through an incoming message. However, there are situations where the execution is cancelled post the order confirmation. This may be due to wrong quoting of price or nominal or in certain cases the broker might have triggered the message incorrectly.

The Subscription or Redemption Order Confirmation Cancellation Instruction (SETR.047 or SETR.051) is sent to cancel one or more previously sent subscription or redemption order confirmation message (SETR.012 or SETR.006) respectively. When the system receives a Subscription or Redemption Order Confirmation Cancellation Instruction (SETR.047 or SETR.051), the system directly updates the SC.ORD.INSTR.LOG with the details of the message under the multi-value fields Conf Canc Recd . The Conf Canc Status field is set to New when the message is received. Then, further action is not taken by the system.

The Order Stage field indicates the status of the order in the system when the message is received. The following are the possible status updated by the system:

| Record Status | When Day Trade functionality is set | When Day Trade functionality is not set |
|---|---|---|
| When SEC.TRADE for the order is not created | Partially executed | Execution pending |
| In case when SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is still in IHLD and also a SEC.TRADE for the order is created (partial execution) | Partially executed | Trade pending, if SEC.TRADE is in INAU Trade authorised, if SEC.TRADE in LIVE |
| When SEC.TRADE for the order is created (execution fully completed) | Trade pending, if SEC.TRADE is in INAU Trade authorised, if SEC.TRADE in LIVE | Trade pending, if SEC.TRADE is in INAU Trade authorised, if SEC.TRADE in LIVE |

The Amend Expected field indicates whether a SETR.012 or SETR.006 is sent following the cancellation. A Manage Confirmation Cancellation Message (SC.CTDY.CONF.CANC.MSG) enquiry allows the user to view the status and take appropriate action. If the execution is pending, the execution details can be manually removed or modified when the confirmation is cancelled. Similarly, if trade is in INAU, the back office user can choose to wait for the amendment of the confirmation and make the changes. If the cancellation is final and amendment is not expected, then the back office user can delete the trade.

When trade is already authorised and then if the broker cancels the confirmation, the back office user must reverse the trade and rebook when the amendment is received.


##### Generating Outgoing Order Confirmation Cancellation Instruction

For a customer, if the

- Swift Ord Instr field is enabled in CUSTOMER.SECURITY and
- DE.PRODUCT is configured,

then SETR.047 or SETR.051 can be sent to the customer only if the Send Conf Canc Msg is set to Yes in SC.ORD.INSTR.LOG . The details of the SETR.047 and SETR.051 messages are updated in the log. When the back office user tries to resend the SETR.047 or SETR.051 message to the customer, then the system displays the 'SETR 047 Outward message already sent' or 'SETR 051 Outward message already sent' warning message.


##### Confirming Securities Trade

The incoming SETR027 message carries the securities trade confirmation. Similar to the SETR004 and SETR010 messages that deliver trade details, SETR027 message is used to reconcile the trade details.

> **⚠️ Note:** SETR027 is similar to the MT515 message.

| SETR027 Tag | SEC.TRADE Field |
|---|---|
| SettlementDate | Value Date |
| DealPrice | Price |
| Side | Buy or Sell (from Broker side) |
| Depository | Depository |
| SettlementAmount Amount | Broker Side Amount |
| ConfirmationQuantity | Nominal |
| FinancialInstrumentIdentification ISIN | Security No |
| TradeDate | Trade Date |
| TransactionIdentification | Order ID |


##### Cancelling Securities Trade Confirmation

The SETR029 message is sent by an executing party to an instructing party directly or through Central Matching Utility (CMU) to cancel the referenced Securities trade confirmation message that was previously sent. This cancellation is recorded in the SC.TRADE.MSG.DETS application so that the user can manually act on it.

When SETR029 is received, based on the order ID in the message, the record in the SC.TRADE.MSG.DETS application is identified. Already, a record is available for the transaction on receipt of SETR027. Thereby, on receiving SETR029, an additional multi-value set record the cancellation details received as part of it.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Msg Type | Holds the type of message received - SETR029 in this case |
| DealPrice | Holds the deal price |
| Sender ID | Indicates the Transact Customer ID of the sender or the BIC code, if the sender ID cannot be identified |
| Trade ID | Holds the @ID of the corresponding record in SEC.TRADE , based on the order ID above. If there are multiple trades available for the order, then this field appears blank. |
| Msg Process Status | If the Msg Type field is SETR029, this field is blank |
| Link Msg Ref | Displays the SETR027 message, for which the cancellation is received. The inward reference of SETR027 is identified and populated in this field. |
| Action Status | By default, this field remains blank and it is a free format field, where the user can enter any value to indicate that an action is taken |
| Action Notes | Allows users to enter any note regarding the action |

When an SETR029 is received, which is the cancellation message for the previously received SETR027, the system updates the trade details as a record in the SC.TRADE.MSG.DETS application. The ID of the record is the same as the one in SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE .

> **⚠️ Note:** If the system is unable to identify the record in SEC.OPEN.ORDER or SEC.TRADE , the system takes the inward message sender's reference as the ID.

When an SETR029 is raised for a record that already exists in SEC.TRADE , the system raises an override saying, "Confirmation Cancellation msg received."


##### Confirming Response in Securities Trade

This section deals with the setup to automatically and manually generate the SETR030 MX trade confirmation response message.

The MX Instruction field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY triggers the SETR030 message. Upon receiving an SETR027 message, based on the BIC address, the customer record of the sender is identified. If the corresponding record in CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the sender is defined with SETR030 in the MX Instruction field, then SETR030 is automatically triggered on the receipt of SETR027.

SETR030 is sent by an instructing party to the counterparty, which has sent SETR027 previously, to confirm the trade details. If all the details provided by SETR027 match with the trade details already recorded in the system, then the system responds with an affirmed status as part of SETR030, indicating that the trade details are accepted.

In case of any mismatch in the details, the system triggers an SETR030 with an unaffirmed status carrying a rejection note.

An SETR030 with affirmed status is sent, only if all the trade details of SETR027 that is previously received match with the details saved in the system.

On receipt of SETR027, the system validates the match between the trade details in the message and the system. Once the match is confirmed, the trade is authorised and an SETR030 is generated with affirmed status to be sent to the sender of the previously received SETR027.

> **⚠️ Note:** The tag is updated with the order ID, for which the SETR027 message is received.

If any of the trade details in the received SETR027 does not match with the one in the system, the trade is not authorised. Instead, a record is updated in SP.STATUS with the mismatch reason.

On updating the record in SP.STATUS , the system automatically generates an SETR030 to the sender of the previously received SETR027. The SETR030 message carries the status as unaffirmed and the reason for rejecting the SETR027 message, received previously.

The tag in SETR030 is updated with the reason for the unaffirmed status code and the value for this tag is populated from the Reason Code field in SP.STATUS . The reason narrative from the Narrative field in SP.STATUS is mapped to the tag in SETR030 message.

> **⚠️ Note:** The tag is updated with the order ID populated from the Ord Exe Ref field in SP.STATUS .

If the MX Instruction field is not set as SETR030 in CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the sender of SETR027, then SETR030 is not generated automatically by the system. However, the user can still generate an SETR030 manually from SP.STATUS .

> **⚠️ Note:** The tag is updated with the order ID populated from the Ord Exe Ref field in SP.STATUS .

To send an SETR030 manually, the user must set the following fields in SP.STATUS :

- Set the Send Msg field as SETR030.
- Update the Ord Exe Ref field with the order reference, received as part of SETR027.
- Update the Receiver field with the Customer ID of the receiver, to whom the SETR030 is be sent.
- Update the Status Code field with either of the following, as applicable: AFFI – If the previously received SETR027 is affirmed NAFI – If the previously received ETR027 is unaffirmed
- Update the Reason Code field with the reason code for the unaffirmed status. This field gets enabled, only if the Status Code field is set as NAFI.
- Update the Narrative field with the reason, if required.

The Msg No field in SP.STATUS is used to record the message number and update it in the SETR030 message.

Certain institutional clients use SETR.010 and SETR.004 SWIFT messages to instruct the Purchase or Sale of securities respectively. On receiving the instruction, if the client is eligible for order creation through SWIFT, then the securities order is created in the system for the customer and also transmitted to the market. The institutional customer, who has instructed the purchase or sale, needs to be informed of change in order status. The change in order status is informed to the client through SETR.016 message. Once the order is executed, the client is notified through order confirmation messages SETR.006 and SETR.012 for purchase and sale of securities respectively. This includes informing the client when an order is partially or fully executed in the market.

### 3.5  Statement of Holdings for Institutional Clients


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *MT535 is a statement of holdings message sent by an account servicer (account servicing institution) to an account owner or their designated agent. Temenos Transact allows the generation of MT535 for institutional client portfolios at a defined frequency in SC.HOLDINGS.INSTRUCT or on an ad-hoc basis...*
> 
> **Applications:** `DE.PRODUCT`, `SC.HOLDINGS.INSTRUCT`, `SEC.ACC.MASTER`, `SECURITY.POSITION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Balance Type*, *Closing Bal No Nom*, *Custody Eligible*, *Generated By*, *Hold Stmt Freq*, *Portfolio ID*, *Unsett Nom Cr*, *Value Dated Posn*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

MT535 is a statement of holdings message sent by an account servicer (account servicing institution) to an account owner or their designated agent. Temenos Transact allows the generation of MT535 for institutional client portfolios at a defined frequency in SC.HOLDINGS.INSTRUCT or on an ad-hoc basis. The balance reported can be traded, settled, or value-dated.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To configure the statement of holdings for institutional clients, the DE.PRODUCT and the SEC.ACC.MASTER applications must be set as described below.


##### DE.PRODUCT

The DE.PRODUCT application is set up to send the statement messages through SWIFT.


##### SEC.ACC.MASTER

The system generates an MT535 during COB, which is the start of the day for the institutional clients, based on the frequency setup in SEC.ACC.MASTER .

The screenshot below shows that the Hold Stmt Freq field holds the time frequency based on which the message is generated. The various frequencies allowed are daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly.

The Balance Type field implies the type of balance to be sent in the message. The balance types available for selection are:

- Traded balance - holds Closing Bal No Nom of SECURITY.POSITION .
- Contractual balance - holds Value Dated Posn of SECURITY.POSITION .
- Settled balance - holds the value derived based on ' Closing Bal No Nom - Unsett Nom Cr ' of SECURITY.POSITION .

The Hold Stmt Freq and Balance Type fields can be input for a given portfolio only if the client is an Institutional Client ( Custody Eligible set to YES).

> **⚠️ Note:** This report cannot be sent for portfolios with multiple CUSTODY.PORT.NOs. Only one reporting frequency and balance can be set for a particular portfolio.


#### 🔧 Working With

For institutional clients, the system automatically generates an MT535 message at the portfolio level on the given frequency date with the defined Balance Type , such as traded, contractual, or settled.


##### Recording MT535 Delivery References usingSC.HOLDINGS.INSTRUCT

The system creates an MT535 message during COB of the defined frequency date and generates multiple MT535 messages for a single portfolio with numerous holdings.

The SC.HOLDINGS.INSTRUCT application holds the details of the messages generated. The system creates a new record when a message is generated for each portfolio. It holds the:

- Portfolio ID for which the message is generated
- Date and time when the message was generated
- Delivery references of the messages generated.

The system marks the Generated By field as ‘System’, as shown in the screenshot below.


##### Generating Ad-hoc MT535 for Portfolio

It is also possible to generate the MT535 messages ad-hoc through the SC.HOLDINGS.INSTRUCT application for institutional portfolios.

To generate ad-hoc MT535, a new record must be created in the SC.HOLDINGS.INSTRUCT application. The portfolio for which the message is required and Balance Type should be entered. On authorising the record, the system generates the MT535 messages for the given portfolio with the delivery references.

When the report is generated manually, the Generated By field holds the value ‘Manual’ to denote it was an ad-hoc message generation, as shown in the screenshot below.

Sample MT535 generated for an institutional client is shown in the screenshot below.


#### 📋 Tasks

MT535 is a statement of holding message sent by an account servicer (account servicing institution) to an account owner or its designated agent. Temenos Transact allows generation of MT535 for institutional client portfolios at a defined frequency or on an ad-hoc basis. The balance reported can be Traded or settled or Value dated. This feature helps to list the messages generated for institutional clients.

#### 📖 Introduction

MiFID II is a legislative framework instituted by the European Union (EU) to regulate financial markets in the European bloc and improve protections for investors. The aim of MiFID II is to standardize practices across the EU and restore confidence in the industry, especially after the 2008 financial crisis. A revised version of the original MiFID rolled out on January 3, 2018, after six years.

> **⚠️ Note:** MiFID II applies to the legislative framework, and the rules it outlines are actually the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation (MiFIR), but in general, the term MiFID is used to mean both.

There are several key regulatory requirements in MiFID II. Temenos Transact supports the following:

- Refund of Inducements

- Instrument and Other Indicators Required for MiFID II

- MiFID Pre-trade Check support for Ex Ante fees and Target Market Data

- Support for UCITS and PRIIPs Instruments that are subject to Undertakings for the Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) and Packaged Retail and Insurance-based Investment Products (PRIIPs) regulations need to be identified. Specific pre-trade checks may be required for UCITS portfolios. Temenos Transact captures instrument details but does not handle the pre- trade checks. The PTCC checks are handled in the front end system.

> **⚠️ Note:** MiFID Costs and Charges disclosure works with SC license


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Read Configuring Trailer Fees for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details the MiFID costs and charge disclosures.


###### MiFID Pre-trade Check Supports Ex Ante Fees and Target Market Data

Based on the target market data, pre-trade check needs to be performed before a customer places an order. Also the Ex-ante fees need to be reported to customer in good-time. Hence it is necessary to capture the target market data and Ex-ante fees.

As per MiFID II regulation, the cost and charges data provided by the issuer (both ex ante and ex-post) must be stored in the system at instrument master level. These fields are mapped from an external system (bank’s own internal master tool called SMF (Securities Master File) daily through automatic and online process. Within Temenos Transact, these fields are for information purpose only and hence triggers or calculation is not expected based on these fields. The SC.MIFID.PDT.FEE.TYPE application stores the category and description of various product fees used for MiFID reporting. The ID of this application is the product fee code.

The SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS application holds the MiFID fee details of an instrument. For Securities instruments, the ID of the application is SECURITY.MASTER ID (For example, 100046-000) and for ETD derivatives instruments, the ID of the application is DX*DX.CONTRACT.MASTER.ID (For example, DX*110000).

MiFID II regulations require the financial institutions to report all the cost and charges related to the product and transaction level costs to customers in detailed components. The ex ante cost are the detailed estimation of costs and charges that are likely to be incurred on placing an order. The customers need know all the all the ex ante cost and charges before placing the order that is, in good-time.

The ex ante estimations of transaction cost are integrated already as a service at order entry level. However the periodic fees estimations is included in order through an additional enquiry Periodic fee estimate (SC.API.PERIODIC.FEE.EST.1.0.0). Once the order is placed in the front end system, it triggers this enquiry with the order details. The enquiry returns the estimate of periodic fees to be incurred by the customer for this transaction. The estimates are reported to the customer in the front end system. The periodic fees include:

- Management or Advisory fees
- Safekeeping fee
- Inducement fee or Trailer fee

The basic set up for the fee mentioned above are available in the system. Refer the related fees setup documents for more information.

The Priip Kiid Link and Ucits Kiid Link fields in SECURITY.MASTER and DX.CONTRACT.MASTER are used to capture URL that provides the link to the Key Investor Information Document (KIID) stored in the document repository of the bank.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Instrument Type field in SECURITY.MASTER and DX.CONTRACT.MASTER is used to identify whether the instrument belongs to PRIIPS or UCITS directive.

The bank depositary services among other services to some of its customers, which can be Undertakings for the Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) or Alternative Investment Fund (AIF). UCITS and AIFs are specific types of funds. Under the depositary services provided the bank needs to monitor the specific measures of these customer’s portfolios on a daily basis as per the UCITS investments guidelines law. As per UCITS law paragraph: 48.2.a. A UCITS may not acquire more than 10 % of the non-voting shares of a single issuing body. It is required to identify the non-voting shares. The Non Voting Shr field in SECURITY.MASTER is used to identify the non-voting shares.

The UCITS and AIF have various regulatory guidelines under which the portfolio needs to be monitored. In order to cover the various UCITS or AIFs investment guidelines, the group issuer has to be captured at the security level, other than the direct issuer of the security. Hence, the group issuer of the security needs to be captured at the instrument master level. The Issuer Group field in SECURITY.MASTER captures the group issuer.

UCITS and AIF portfolios must be clearly identified among all portfolios in the system as those portfolios has to be handled specifically starting from the static data, front office controls and booking. The Fund Port Type field in SEC.ACC.MASTER is used to identify the UCITS or AIF portfolios.

In order to oblige to the regulatory requirements, an UCITS fund may not acquire more than 10% of the debt securities of a single issuing body. So, the loans in circulation must be captured and kept in history. The Loans In Cir field in CUSTOMER is used to capture the loans in circulation for the issuer and the Loans In Circcy field captures the currency in which the loan amount is denoted.

### 4.2  MiFID Questionnaire


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *MiFID II is an extension of the existing Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID) I, the directive goal is to raise the bar in the European Union (EU) financial markets in the following areas:*
> 
> **Applications:** `SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO`, `SC.MIFID.INV.PGM.PARAM`, `SC.MIFID.PARAM`, `SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS`, `SEC.ACC.MASTER`, `SEC.OPEN.ORDER`, `SEC.TRADE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Age*, *Allowed Investor*, *Answer*, *App Field*, *Asset Class*, *Asset Class 1*, *Asset Type*, *Assets Held * Value Assets* ... +59 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

MiFID II is an extension of the existing Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID) I, the directive goal is to raise the bar in the European Union (EU) financial markets in the following areas:

- Transparency
- Microstructural issues
- Data publication and access
- Requirements applying to trading venues
- Commodity derivatives
- Market data reporting
- Post trade issues and
- Investor protection

MiFID questionnaire is used by the banks to understand the customer’s personal details, knowledge in various financial products and risk appetite. Based on the customer’s response in MiFID questionnaire, banks can assign an investment program to the customer.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details the setup required for dynamic additions of questions in MiFID questionnaire and assigning the investment program, based on customer response.


##### Enabling Dynamic Addition of Questions

The SC.MIFID.PARAMETER application is used to include additional questions in MiFID questionnaire ( SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO ). The ID of a record in SC.MIFID.PARAMETER is the same as the company ID. The below fields are available in SC.MIFID.PARAMETER .

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Suitability Chk | If this field is set to Yes, the following fields get enabled: Asset Type Sub Asset Type |
| Asset Type | Holds the valid asset type from the ASSET.TYPE application |
| Sub Asset Type | Holds the valid sub asset type from the SUB.ASSET.TYPE application The Sub Asset Type field is a subset of the Asset Type field. Thereby, assigning a value to the Sub Asset Type field is not allowed when the Asset Type field is empty. |
| Question ID | Holds the question ID. This is a free text field, where the input must be without space, for example, QUESTION.1 or QUESTION.TAX. |
| Question | Holds the question. For example, What's your marital status? |
| Mandatory | Indicates whether the question is mandatory or not. The values in this field are Yes or No and the default value is No. |


##### Setup to Determine Investment Program

The SC.MIFID.INV.PGM.PARAM application is used to assign points to the customers and determine the most suitable investment program for them. The Company ID forms the ID of this application. The following fields are available in SC.MIFID.INV.PGM.PARAM .

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Score Id | Displays alphanumeric values to select from These values are created in EB.LOOKUP . |
| Max Score Points | Holds the maximum points for the score ID |
| Min Score Points | Holds the minimum points for the score ID |
| App Field | Assigns the points for determining the most suitable investment program. This field accepts any Question ID and the following field names from the SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO application: Age Education Level Profession Income Source * Income Assets Held * Value Assets Fin Commit * Val Fin Commit Invest Amount Invest Period Investment Objective Risk Appetite Expect Return Asset Class Sub Asset Class |
| Operand | Can be EQ (equal to) or RG (range) |
| Value | Holds the expected value in the App Field |
| Points | Holds numeric points |
| Point Operand | Holds the operand associated with Points Scored field to identify the suitable investment program for the customer. The allowed values are EQ, GT, LT, RG. |
| Points Scored | Holds the total points scored |
| Eligible Invest Program | Holds the eligible investment program, based on the points scored by the customer |
| Default Invest Program | This is a mandatory field. If an eligible investment program cannot be determined using the points logic explained above, then value in this field is applied for the customer, by default. |


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with updating questions in the SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO application and assigning an investment program to the customer.


##### Updating Questions in MiFID Questionnaire

Once, the SC.MIFID.PARAMETER application is authorised, the additional questions are displayed in the SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO application. If the Suitability Chk field in SC.MIFID.PARAMETER is set to Yes, the below fields in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO are disabled.

- Bonds
- Money Market Instruments
- Fixed Deposits
- Shares
- Mutual Funds
- Hedge Funds
- Pvt Equity
- Structured Prds
- Warrants
- Derivatives
- Metals Commo

If the Suitability Chk field in SC.MIFID.PARAMETER is Yes, then the Asset Class , Know Asset Class , Sub Asset Class and Know Sub Asset Class fields are enabled.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Asset Class 1 | Defaults values from the At Desc field from SC.MIFID.PARAMETER |
| Know Asset Class 1 | Determines the customer knowledge in the asset class |
| Sub Asset Class 1 | Defaults the value from the Sat Desc field from SC.MIFID.PARAMETER |
| Know Sub Asset Class 1 | Determines the knowledge in the Sub Asset Class field |
| Question Id | Holds the value defaulted from the Question Id field from SC.MIFID.PARAMETER |
| Question | Holds the value defaulted from the Question field from SC.MIFID.PARAMETER |
| Answer | Holds the response from the customer |


##### Assigning an Investment Program

For MiFID eligible customers, when the record in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO is authorised, the system calculates the total points scored by the customer, based on the response received.

The system updates the following fields in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO table, once the total points is calculated and an investment program in assigned.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Score Id | The Score Id is defaulted from SC.MIFID.INV.PGM.PARAM as multi-values. |
| Sys Points | Holds the system populated points determined for this customer for the Score ID |
| Points | Holds the value from SYS.POINTS , by default that can be changed by the user |
| Total Points | Holds the system populated total value of all the multi-value Points fields |
| Sys Investment Pgm | Holds the system populated investment program as determined by the system |
| Chosen Investment Pgm | Holds the value from SYS.INVESTMENT.PGM , by default that can be changed by the user |


##### MiFID PTCC Checks

This section explains about the instances, at which the system displays overrides.


##### Selecting Investment Program inSEC.ACC.MASTER

In case of MiFID eligible customers, while selecting the investment program in SEC.ACC.MASTER , the system checks if the selected program is the same as the Chosen Investment Pgm field in SC.MIFID.CUST.INV.PGM .

If the selected program in SEC.ACC.MASTER is different from the one in the Chosen Investment Pgm field, the system displays an override saying, 'Investment Program different from the Chosen Investment Program'.


##### Mismatch in Investment Program Risk Level and Instrument Risk Level

The Ranking field in INVESTMENT.PROGRAM is used to hold the maximum allowed risk level for the investment program. When a value is entered in SEC.OPEN.ORDER or SEC.TRADE , the system checks the Risk Level field in SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS record with the Ranking field in the investment program attached to the customer portfolio.

If the value in the Ranking field in the investment program is different from the value in Risk Level field, the system raises an override saying, 'Risk Level Mismatch'.


##### Adhering to MiFID Regulation

The below MiFID II related Pre-Trade Compliance Checks (PTCC) are only performed, if the Suitability Chk field in SC.MIFID.PARAM is set to Yes and if the SEC.ACC.MASTER involved in the transaction is set for MiFID.

In case of MiFID eligible customers, the system matches the Investment Objective field in SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS with the Investment Objective field in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO while processing the records in SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE applications. The system displays an override as 'Investment Objective Mismatch' when there is a mismatch in the values in these two fields.

While processing the SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE applications, the system matches the Allowed Investor field in SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS with the Classification field in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO . The system raises an override as 'Allowed Investor Mismatch' when there is a mismatch in the values in these two fields.

While processing the SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE applications, the system matches the Invest Tenor field in SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS with the Invest Period field in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO . The system displays an override as 'Investment Period Mismatch' when there is a mismatch in the values in these two fields.

In case of MiFID eligible customers, while selecting the managed account in SEC.ACC.MASTER of the customer, the system checks whether the selected account type is same as Distribution Strategy in the SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS table.

If the selected managed account in SEC.ACC.MASTER is different from SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS , then the system raises an override as 'Managed Account Mismatch'.

The Liquidity field in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO stores whether the investor needs to hold the investment till maturity or the investor can have the option to exit before maturity.

While processing the SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE , system matches the value in the Liquidity field in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO with the value in the Liquidity field in SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS . If there is a mismatch in the value in these two fields, then the system raises an override as 'Liquidity Mismatch'.

The Loss Tolerance field in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO stores the customer tolerance towards loss. The system raises an override as 'Loss Tolerance Mismatch', when there is difference in the value in the Loss Tolerance field in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO and SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS .

When the Suitability Chk field is set to Yes in SC.MIFID.PARAM , perform the below checks:

- When SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE are inputs, the system checks the asset and sub-asset type of the traded instrument with the customer response in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO for same asset and sub-asset type.
- If the customer response in SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO for the traded asset and sub-asset type is set to knowledge or experience, then the order is excepted without any overrides.

If the customer does not have any experience in the traded instrument, then the system displays an override as 'Customer does not have knowledge in traded asset and sub-asset type'.

Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID) Questionnaire is used by the banks to understand the customer’s personal details, knowledge in various financial products and the risk appetite. Scoring is defined for responses given by the customer. Based on the total points, suitable investment program is assigned to the customer.


##### Workflow

In MiFID Questionnaire, the user can perform the following tasks:

This screen enables the user to configure the MiFID parameter, where bank can include any number of additional questions that can be used further to obtain customer’s responses.

2. In the MIFID Parameter screen, enter values in the following fields: Suitability Check Asset Type Sub Asset Type Question Id Question Mandatory
3. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides, if any.
4. Click the Commit icon.

This screen enables the user to configure the MiFID investment program parameter. Each response is assigned with a score. Based on the total score, suitable investment program is suggested to the customer.

1. MIFID Investment Program Param .
2. In the MIFID Investment Program Param screen, enter values in the following fields: Score Id Min Score Points Max Score Points App Field Operand Value Points Points Operand Eligible Points Eligible Invest Program Default Invest Program
3. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides, if any.
4. Click the Commit icon.

This screen enables the user to capture the MIFID related information from the customer. It consists of a set of questionnaire, which should be responded by customers to obtain their knowledge in various investment products and risk appetite. Based on the responses to the questionnaire, suitable investment program is suggested to the customer.

1. Customer MiFID Details .
2. In the Questionnaire screen, enter customer response for each question.
3. Click the Validate icon to update the calculated investment program by the system in the Sys Investment Pgm field.
4. In the Investment Program Calculation screen, enter values in following fields to modify the investment program manually. Points Manually Chosen Investment Pgm
5. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides, if any.
6. Click the Commit icon.

### 4.3  MiFID Regulation Valuation Drop Notification


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *As per MIFID II regulation, banks should record the instances whenever the portfolio valuation drops by 10% or more with respect to the portfolio market value, on any particular trading day from the start date of the valuation period. Any subsequent falls in multiples of 10% also have to be recorded...*
> 
> **Applications:** `SC.MIFID.PARAM`, `SC.PF.DROP.INSTANCES`, `SEC.ACC.MASTER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Currency*, *Drop Date -  xx*, *Drop Pct Recorded -  xx*, *Drop Percent Val*, *Mifid Val Drop Chk*, *Pf Value -  xx*, *Portfolio No*, *Reject > xx Sec Acc Master* ... +4 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

As per MIFID II regulation, banks should record the instances whenever the portfolio valuation drops by 10% or more with respect to the portfolio market value, on any particular trading day from the start date of the valuation period. Any subsequent falls in multiples of 10% also have to be recorded. The bank should inform customers about the valuation drop on the same business day.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes the fields in SC.MIFID.PARAM .


##### ConfiguringSC.MIFID.PARAM

To record the instances of portfolio valuation drop, the following fields in the SC.MIFID.PARAM application should be setup:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Drop Percent Val | Stores the percentage drop in the portfolio value (and multiples) that should be recorded for MiFID II purpose. As per current MiFID II guidelines, this should be configured as 10. |
| Reporting Freq | Stores the reporting frequency. The allowed values are: Daily - The system checks the percentage drop set in the Drop Percent Val field with the closing balance of the previous day. Monthly - The system checks the percentage drop set in the Drop Percent Val field with the opening value on the first day of the month. Quarterly - The system checks the percentage drop set in the Drop Percent Val field with the opening value on first day of the quarter. Semi-annually Annually |
| Reporting Freq St Date | Stores the start date of the reporting frequency. If reporting frequency is set to Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-annually, Annually, the user should define the start date in this field. If the user sets the frequency to Quarterly, the user can define the quarter month. If the start date is set to Jan 1, the first quarter is set from January to March and the other quarters are set subsequently. If set to Feb 1, the first quarter is set from February to April and the other quarters are set subsequently. |

A record set up in

is shown below.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section describes how to record instances of drops in the portfolio value.


##### Recording Instances of Portfolio Value Drop

The SC.PF.DROP.INSTANCES application is used to record instances whenever the portfolio value drops by the percentage setup in SC.MIFID.PARAM . This application is updated during COB, based on the portfolio performance as on the date defined in Reporting Freq field in SC.MIFID.PARAM .

The following fields in SC.PF.DROP.INSTANCES are updated during COB for the portfolio experiencing the drop. The record ID of the table is Portfolio ID* Reporting Freq St Date field value.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Portfolio No | Holds the portfolio ID for which the record is created |
| Currency | Holds the reference currency of the portfolio |
| xx | Holds the start date of the reporting period. This is updated based on the setup in SC.MIFID.PARAM |
| Reporting Prd End Date - xx | Holds the end date of the reporting period. This is updated based on the setup in SC.MIFID.PARAM |
| Drop Date - xx | Date on which x% drop occurred for the first time in the MiFID reporting period |
| Drop Pct Recorded - xx | Stores the actual drop (multiples of drops like 10%, 20% etc., as parameterised) in portfolio valuation that was recorded |
| Pf Value - xx | Stores the portfolio valuation on the drop day in the reference currency of the portfolio. |
| xx Sec Acc Master | The system defaults this configurable field to N. If set to Y, it indicates that this drop is recorded due to some internal system error and a letter need not be sent to the client to inform the drop. |

This table should be updated during COB.

> **⚠️ Note:** The portfolio value drop check is only performed for those portfolios, where the Mifid Val Drop Chk field in SEC.ACC.MASTER is set to Yes.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for MiFID Regulation for Valuation Drop Notification feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for MiFID Regulation for Valuation Drop Notification feature.


> **Related Applications:** `SC.MIFID.PARAM`, `SC.PF.DROP.INSTANCES`, `SEC.ACC.MASTER`

### 4.4  MiFID Transaction Reporting And MiFID PTCC Checks


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *As part of the MiFID II regulation, the investment firms are obliged to report all the transactions which they execute for their customers not later than the end of the next working day that is, T+1 day to the competent authorities.*
> 
> **Applications:** `ASSET.TYPE`, `COMPANY`, `CUSTOMER`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `DX.TRADE`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `SC.PARAMETER`, `SCDX.ARM.MIFID.DATA` ... +6 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Ben Owner Change*, *MiFID Report Status*, *Mifid Report Status*, *Option*, *Post Update Rtn*, *Reportable Indicator*, *Tap Report Stat*, *Tap Report Status* ... +1 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

As part of the MiFID II regulation, the investment firms are obliged to report all the transactions which they execute for their customers not later than the end of the next working day that is, T+1 day to the competent authorities.

All transaction details which has to be reported must be captured at the trade level. Once the transaction is authorised, the details pertaining to Approved Reporting Mechanism (ARM) is populated in the live database. Once the database is populated, the files can be extracted in any defined format using the Data Formatting Engine (DFE).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The configuration for transaction reporting involves the parameter and database setup as explained below.


##### Setting up the Parameter

The Transaction Reporting field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Yes, so that the transaction base is built and the details to be reported are stored.


##### Holding Reportable Details in Database

The SCDX.ARM.MIFID.DATA record (transaction base) in the TX.TXN.BASE.PARMS application with all the reportable details of a transaction is shown below. If more fields must be reported, then additional fields can be added to this transaction base by amending the SCDX.ARM.MIFID.DATA record in TX.TXN.BASE.PARMS .

For each field added in the SCDX.ARM.MIFID.DATA record (transaction base) in the TX.TXN.BASE.PARMS application, the mapping must be provided to fetch the value related to the transaction. Mapping the fields in the transaction base from SEC.TRADE record is shown below.


##### Data Formatting Engine

The Data Formatting Engine (DFE) must exist to generate the file from the database. Using DFE, the data can be extracted in any file formats such as csv, text file and so on. The records in DFE.PARAMETER and DFE.MAPPING must exist in order to extract the data from the database. The mapping and the field position in the report must be configured in DFE.MAPPING table.

The SCDX.ARM.UPD.DATE.TIME routine is available in core. The routine is attached in the Post Update Rtn field in DFE.MAPPING to ensure that the files are created only in the database after the last extraction is selected and extracted.

Similar mapping of fields to the database from SECURITY.TRANSFER (SECURITY.TRANSFER* SCDX.ARM.MIFID.DATA ) and ENTITLEMENT (ENTITLEMENT*SCDX.ARM.MIFID.DATA ) is available in TX.TXN.BASE.MAPPING .


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with the workflow of MiFID transaction reporting in SC module.


##### Transaction Reporting

The trades entered in the system are reported, if the configurations are already set.

The Tap Report Stat field is defaulted as Newt whenever a new transaction is input in the system. The Newt status shows that the transaction is a new transaction in the MiFID transaction report.

Using the MIFID II - Reporting Transactions (SCDX.ARM.MIFID.DATA) enquiry, the database updated with the transaction details can be viewed.

Click Fields and Descriptions for more information about the fields available in SEC.TRADE

In case of options and swaptions, the buyer shall be the counterparty that holds the right to exercise the option and the seller shall be the counterparty that sells the option and receives a premium. In case of futures and forwards other than futures and forwards relating to currencies, the buyer shall be the counterparty buying the instrument and the seller the counterparty selling the instrument. In case of forward rate agreements, the buyer shall be the counterparty paying the fixed rate and the seller the counterparty receiving the fixed rate. For an increase in notional, the buyer shall be the same as the acquirer of the financial instrument in the original transaction and the seller shall be the same as the disposer of the financial instrument in the original transaction. Monetary value covered by a single swap contract where the quantity field indicates the number of swap contracts in the transaction. For a future or option on an index, the amount per index point. For spreadbets the movement in the price of the underlying instrument on which the spreadbet is based. The information reported in this field shall be consistent with the values provided in fields 30 and 33. |  |
| UnderlyingInstrumentCode | ISIN code of the underlying instrument. For ADRs, GDRs and similar instruments, the ISIN code of the financial instrument on which those instruments are based. For derivatives or other instruments which have an underlying, the underlying instrument ISIN code, when the underlying is admitted to trading, or traded on a trading venue. Where the underlying is a stock dividend, then ISIN code of the related share entitling the underlying dividend. For Credit Default Swaps, the ISIN of the reference obligation shall be provided. In case the underlying is an Index and has an ISIN, the ISIN code for that index. Where the underlying is a basket, include the ISIN of each constituent of the basket that is admitted to trading or is traded on a trading venue. ##### Generating the File Extract

Whenever the file (extracted excel sheet) needs to be generated, the bank user must trigger the BNK/OC.ONLINE.REPORTS service (or similar service). Once the service is triggered, the file extract is generated. Read SCDX.ARM.REPORT for more information on the data extracted from the SCDX.ARM.MIFID.DATA database into the csv sheet.


##### Modifying Reportable Transaction

When a MiFID II reportable transaction is modified, a report with Tap Report Stat set to Canc is submitted. Then, a new record with modified data is submitted as a new report. When the bank user wants to make any modifications, the user needs to change the Tap Report Stat field to Canc and submit the trade ( SEC.TRADE ).

The live database is updated with new record without any change in values except for the Tap Report Stat field changed to Canc and a change in time stamp. This cancels the first report submitted with the same transaction reference.

> **⚠️ Note:** This section provides the instructions to modify the required details, if a bank user wants to change any values. This is an optional step.

Then, the bank user needs to open the trade again and do the required modifications and must change the status in the Tap Report Stat field to Newt and submit again.

A new record is populated again in the live database with the modified data and Tap Report Status set to Newt for the same transaction reference.

> **⚠️ Note:** For cancellations and deletions or reversals of transactions, the same procedure is followed and a cancellation report with Tap Report Stat set to Canc is submitted.

Transaction Reporting for Corporate Action Events

Elective corporate action events where the user has the option to decide, whether to follow any of the suggested options are reportable. Corporate action events resulting from a default option are reportable, as the user or investor is deemed to have taken an investment decision. The Reportable Indicator field in DIARY.TYPE is set to Yes for corporate action events that must be reported for transaction reporting.

If the Option and Reportable Indicator fields in DIARY.TYPE are set to Yes, then the system checks the conditions defined in TX.CONDITION for each new transaction. If the deal is reportable, then the system authorises ENTITLEMENT and updates the database. In such case, the system defaults the Mifid Report Status field to Newt.

> **⚠️ Note:** All entitlements are updated in the reporting database when the Reportable Indicator field is set to YES in DIARY.TYPE . The record in TX.CONDITION for entitlement can be set to include only certain entitlements

When the authorised record in ENTITLEMENT is reversed, the MiFID Report Status field is set to Canc and the database is updated . The MiFID II - Reporting Transactions (SCDX.ARM.MIFID.DATA ) enquiry lists the updated transaction details.

Transaction Reporting for Transfers

The Ben Owner Change field in SECURITY.TRANSFER is set to Yes to indicate the transfer in or transfer out transactions are reported in MiFID II regulation. The system checks the conditions defined in TX.CONDITION for every new transaction. If the deal is reportable, then the system updates the database. The MiFID II - Reporting Transactions (SCDX.ARM.MIFID.DATA) enquiry lists the updated transaction details.

> **⚠️ Note:** If certain transfers are not reported, then the record in TX.CONDITION for SECURITY.TRANSFER must be modified to define the reported transfers.

Click Fields and Descriptions for more information about the fields available in SECURITY.TRANSFER .

| BuyerId | Code used to identify the acquirer of the financial instrument. Where the acquirer is a legal entity, the LEI code of the acquirer shall be used. Where the acquirer is a non-legal entity, the identifier specified in Article 6 shall be used. Where the transaction was executed on a trading venue or on an organised trading platform outside of the Union that utilises a central counterparty (CCP) and where the identity of the acquirer is not disclosed, the LEI code of the CCP shall be used. Where the transaction was executed on a trading venue or on an organised trading platform outside of the Union that does not utilise a CCP and where the identity of the acquirer is not disclosed, the MIC code of the trading venue or of the organised trading platform outside of the Union shall be used. Where the acquirer is an investment firm acting as a systematic internaliser (SI), the LEI code of the SI shall be used. ‘INTC’ shall be used to designate an aggregate client account within the investment firm in order to report a transfer into or out of that account with an associated allocation to the individual client(s) out of or into that account respectively. In case of options and swaptions, the buyer shall be the counterparty that holds the right to exercise the option and the seller shall be the counterparty that sells the option and receives a premium. In case of futures and forwards other than futures and forwards relating to currencies, the buyer shall be the counterparty buying the instrument and the seller the counterparty selling the instrument. In the case of swaps relating to securities, the buyer shall be the counterparty that gets the risk of price movement of the underlying security and receives the security amount. The seller shall be the counterparty paying the security amount. In the case of swaps related to interest rates or inflation indices, the buyer shall be the counterparty paying the fixed rate. The seller shall be the counterparty receiving the fixed rate. In case of basis swaps (float-to-float interest rate swaps), the buyer shall be the counterparty that pays the spread and the seller the counterparty that receives the spread. In the case of swaps and forwards related to currencies and of cross currency swaps, the buyer shall be the counterparty receiving the currency which is first when sorted alphabetically by ISO 4217 standard and the seller shall be the counterparty delivering this currency. In the case of swap related to dividends, the buyer shall be the counterparty receiving the equivalent actual dividend payments. The seller is the counterparty paying the dividend and receiving the fixed rate. In the case of derivative instruments for the transfer of credit risk except options and swaptions, the buyer shall be the counterparty buying the protection. The seller is the counterparty selling the protection. In case of derivative contract related to commodities, the buyer shall be the counterparty that receives the commodity specified in the report and the seller the counterparty delivering this commodity. In case of forward rate agreements, the buyer shall be the counterparty paying the fixed rate and the seller the counterparty receiving the fixed rate. For an increase in notional, the buyer shall be the same as the acquirer of the financial instrument in the original transaction and the seller shall be the same as the disposer of the financial instrument in the original transaction. For a decrease in notional the buyer shall be the same as the disposer of the financial instrument in the original transaction and the seller shall be the same as the acquirer of the financial instrument in the original transaction. | CUSTOMER | Legal ID will be mapped from the customer record mentioned in the field CUSTOMER.NO. This field will be populated only when customer is transferring in the positions i.e. TRANSACTION.TYPE inSECURITY.TRANSFER indicates a credit of securities. |

For transactions executed on a trading venue, the level of granularity shall be in accordance with the requirements set out in Article of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/574(2). For transactions not executed on a trading venue, the date and time shall be when the parties agree the content of the following fields: quantity, price, currencies in fields 31, 34 and 44, instrument identification code, instrument classification and underlying instrument code, where applicable. For transactions not executed on a trading venue the time reported shall be at least to the nearest second. Where the transaction results from an order transmitted by the executing firm on behalf of a client to a third party where the conditions for transmission set out in Article 4 were not satisfied, this shall be the date and time of the transaction rather than the time of the order transmission. |  |  |

| Quantity | The number of units of the financial instrument, or the number of derivative contracts in the transaction. The nominal or monetary value of the financial instrument. For spread bets, the quantity shall be the monetary value wagered per point movement in the underlying financial instrument. For credit default swaps, the quantity shall be the notional amount for which the protection is acquired or disposed of. For increase or decrease in notional amount derivative contracts, the number shall reflect the absolute value of the change and shall be expressed as a positive number. The information reported in this field shall be consistent with the values provided in fields 33 and 46. | SECURITY.TRANSFER |  |
| QuantityCurrency | Currency in which the quantity is expressed. Only applicable if quantity is expressed as nominal or monetary value. | SECURITY.TRANSFER |  |

| PriceNotation |  |  |  |
| Price | Traded price of the transaction excluding, where applicable, commission and accrued interest. In the case of option contracts, it shall be the premium of the derivative contract per underlying or index point. In the case of spread bets it shall be the reference price of the underlying instrument. For credit default swaps (CDS) it shall be the coupon in basis points. Where price is reported in monetary terms, it shall be provided in the major currency unit. Where price is currently not available but pending, the value shall be ‘PNDG’ Where price is not applicable the value shall be ‘NOAP’ The information reported in this field shall be consistent with the values provided in fields 30 and 46. | SECURITY.TRANSFER |  |
| PriceCurrency | Currency in which the price is expressed (applicable if the price is expressed as monetary value). | SECURITY.TRANSFER |  |
| NetAmount | The net amount of the transaction means the cash amount which is paid by the buyer of the debt instrument upon the settlement of the transaction. This cash amount equals to: (clean price * nominal value)+any accrued coupons. As a result, the net amount of the transaction excludes any commission or other fees charged to the buyer of the debt instrument. Field only applies when the financial instrument is debt. | SECURITY.TRANSFER |  |
| Venue | Identification of the venue where the transaction was executed. Use the ISO 10383 segment MIC for transactions executed on a trading venue, Systematic Internaliser (SI) or organised trading platform outside of the Union. Where the segment MIC does not exist, use the operating MIC. Use MIC code ‘XOFF’ for financial instruments admitted to trading, or traded on a trading venue or for which a request for admission was made, where the transaction on that financial instrument is not executed on a trading venue, SI or organised trading platform outside of the Union, or where an investment firm does not know it is trading with another investment firm acting as an SI. Use MIC code ‘XXXX’ for financial instruments that are not admitted to trading or traded on a trading venue or for which no request for admission has been made and that are not traded on an organised trading platform outside of the Union but where the underlying is admitted to trading or traded on a trading venue. |  |  |

For derivatives or other instruments which have an underlying, the underlying instrument ISIN code, when the underlying is admitted to trading, or traded on a trading venue. Where the underlying is a stock dividend, then ISIN code of the related share entitling the underlying dividend. For Credit Default Swaps, the ISIN of the reference obligation shall be provided. In case the underlying is an Index and has an ISIN, the ISIN code for that index. Where the underlying is a basket, include the ISIN of each constituent of the basket that is admitted to trading or is traded on a trading venue. Field 47 shall be reported as many times as necessary to list all reportable instruments in the basket. | SECURITY.MASTER | ISIN of the security specified in the field UNDERLYING |

### 4.5  Misc

The aim of MiFID II is to standardise practices across the EU and restore confidence in the industry, especially after the 2008 fina...*

> 
> **Key Fields:** *Field Value*

#### 📖 Introduction

The MiFID II is a legislative framework instituted by the European Union (EU) to regulate financial markets in the European bloc and improve protections for investors. The aim of MiFID II is to standardise practices across the EU and restore confidence in the industry, especially after the 2008 financial crisis.

The directive goal is to raise the bar in the European Union (EU) financial markets in the following areas:

- Transparency
- Microstructural issues
- Data publication and access
- Requirements applying to trading venues
- Commodity derivatives
- Market data reporting
- Post trade issues and
- Investor protection

The MiFID II module allows the banks to:

- Setup a MiFID questionnaire and assign a suitable investment program to the customers based on the response in the MiFID questionnaire
- Send alerts to the customers whenever the customer portfolio values drop more than 10 percentage during the reporting period
- Create a setup to determine the client NCI (National Client identifier)


##### Product Configuration

Some of the key parameter records that are set in the MiFID II module before the transactions are processed are described below. This feature provides a high-level overview about the product.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The main parameters present in the MiFID II module are listed below:

| Parameter File | Transaction ID | Description |
|---|---|---|
| SC.NCI.PARAMETER | System | Holds the logic to build the concat code. The concat code is formed by concatenating the nationality, date of birth, first name and the surname. The Field Value field holds the field name in the CUSTOMER application from which the value is derived. |
| SC.NCI.PRIOROTY | Country Code | Holds the priority order in which the identifications are considered as NCI for a person who belongs to this nationality. The priority is the order in which the identifier is updated in this application. Configures at the country level to hold the identifications that are considered as NCI by the respective country. |
| SC.MIFID.PARAMETER | Company Code | Helps in including additional questions in the MiFID questionnaire ( SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO ). The ID of a record in SC.MIFID.PARAMETER and the Company ID are the same. |
| SC.MIFID.INV.PGM.PARAM | Company Code | Assigns points to the customers and determines the most suitable investment program for them. The Company ID is the ID of this application. |


##### Illustrating Model Products

Model products are not applicable for this module.

> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

MiFID II is a legislative framework instituted by the European Union (EU) to regulate financial markets in the European bloc and improve protections for investors. The aim of MiFID II is to standardize practices across the EU and restore confidence in the industry, especially after the 2008 financial crisis. A revised version of the original MiFID rolled out on January 3, 2018, after six years.

> **⚠️ Note:** MiFID II applies to the legislative framework, and the rules it outlines are actually the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation (MiFIR), but in general, the term MiFID is used to mean both.

There are several key regulatory requirements in MiFID II. Temenos Transact supports the following:

- National Client Identifier (NCI) / Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) Determination

- Refund of Inducements

- Instrument and Other Indicators Required for MiFID II

- MiFID Pre-trade Check support for Ex Ante fees and Target Market Data

- Support for UCITS and PRIIPs Instruments that are subject to Undertakings for the Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) and Packaged Retail and Insurance-based Investment Products (PRIIPs) regulations need to be identified. Specific pre-trade checks may be required for UCITS portfolios. Temenos Transact captures instrument details but does not handle the pre- trade checks. The PTCC checks are handled in the front end system.

> **⚠️ Note:** NCI Determination for MiFID works with SC license


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the setup to be done in the applications for NCI determination.


##### Determining NCI

Based on the priority applicable for the country, bank needs to determine the appropriate NCI for the customer,

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| National Idntr Type | Helps to store the possible national identifiers. The values accepted in this field are: Passport Number NCI Concat Customer Identification Number National Identity number Social Security Number Tax Identification Number No Reference. |
| Identifier Code | Holds the identifier codes for the identifier set in the National Idntr Type field. This field has the following values as the identifier codes. CCPT – Passport Number CUST - Customer Identification Number NIDN - National Identity number SOSE - Social Security Number TXID - Tax Identification Number |

This SC.NCI.PRIORITY application is configured at country level to hold the identifications that are considered as NCI by that country. This application holds the priority order in which the identifications must be considered as NCI for a person belonging to this nationality. The priority is the order in which the identifier is updated in this application.

In the below case, three identifications are defined as the NCIs for Czech Republic nationality. The system considers the value in the Priority Identifier field based on the multi-value. For example, the system considers the National Id as NCI, if the person holds a valid Id, or looks for the Passport. If Priority Identifier2 is invalid or not available, then the system determines the concat code for the person and reports it.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Lei Nci Chk Req | Accept values as blank, Yes or NCI. If this field is set to Yes, Transact performs the Legal Entity Identifier or National Client Identifier check. If this field is set to NCI, only NCI is checked for fields that have the customer ID in them. This can be set to Yes only if Legal Entity module is licensed. Defaults to the Transaction field and can be overridden at transaction level. |
| Nci Override Err | Accepts the values as Override or Error. If this field is set to Error, Transact displays an error when system is not able to find a valid NCI. Can be set if Lei Nci Chk Req is set to Yes or NCI. |


#### 🔧 Working With

The nationality of the customer is used to determine the NCI applicable for the country. The bank needs to determine the appropriate NCI for the customer, based on the priority applicable for the country.

This section details the NCI Determination for MiFID II and the costs and charges disclosure of MiFID.


##### Determining NCI

This section details the steps in determining the NCI applicable.

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Customer Lei Nci | Holds Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) or NCI of the CUSTOMER of the transaction |
| Decision Maker Id | Holds LEI or NCI of the Decision Maker |
| Tap Instr Mkr | Holds LEI or NCI of the Instruction Maker (input allowed only where Enterprise Wealth (EW) is licensed) |
| Tap Trader | Holds LEI or NCI of the Trader (input allowed only where EW is licensed) |
| Tap Manager | Holds the LEI or NCI of the Manager (input allowed only where EW is licensed) |

In some countries instead of a document such as a passport or national ID, a concatenated value that helps to identify the individual is used as NCI. The concat code is a concatenation of Nationality (ISO country code) + Date of Birth (YYYYMMDD) + First Name + Surname. The values required for the concatenation and the concatenation logic are determined in the SC.NCI.PARAMETER application. The concatenation is formed based on the below steps:

1. The values for country code or nationality, date of birth, first name and surname are derived from respective fields in the CUSTOMER application.
2. The list of prefixes defined in the Prefix field in SC.NCI.PARAMETER is removed from these values.
3. Transliteration characters are replaced based on the values defined in the Input and Output fields in SC.NCI.PARAMETER .
4. The number of characters to be used from each value is obtained. And if the number of characters available in that value is lesser than the number of characters defined, then # is padded for the remaining unavailable characters.
5. The obtained values must be concatenated into a single value.

The values for nationality, date of birth, first name and surname are obtained from the Nationality , Date Of Birth , Given Names and Family Name fields in CUSTOMER application respectively. The number of characters from each value to be considered is defined in the No Of Char field. As per the definition, the following character count must be considered:

- two characters from nationality
- eight characters from date of birth
- five characters from first name
- five characters from surname

Prefix such as Mr and Mrs needs to be removed from the values. The transliteration character ä has to be replaced with A. The values defined in the SC.NCI.PARAMETER are shown in the below screenshot.

For a customer with following values, the concat value is formed as shown in the below screenshot.

Nationality of the customer is IN in the IF.EVENTS.INTERFACE.TABLE application as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** When five characters are to be reported but field value is shorter than five, # is used as padding.

For the customer’s nationality, the NCIs of the customer and concat of the customer along with other details are sent to the front office system with the priority in which it needs to be considered as NCI for the on boarding customers.

All the IDs and concat are sent along with priority, issue date, expiry date and NCI code.

The Legal Ent Type field in CUSTOMER application records the customer type where EW module is installed. This field allows the following values:

- Customer
- Economic group
- Household
- Organization
- Person
- None

This field flows to TAP as part of the customer IF flow. TAP uses this value to determine if LEI needs to be checked or NCI. Hence, it has to be mandatorily filled for LEI or NCI checks to happen in front office TAP. If this field is blank, checking is not done.

The NCI priority for each country is defined in the SC.NCI.PRIORITY application. Using the NCI Priority (SC.NCI.PRIORITY.LIST) enquiry, the customer can view the list of NCI priority records defined for each country.

There may be a rare occurrence where the NCI priority of a country might change. The SC.NCI.PRIORITY application needs to be edited with the new priority order and the priority order must be updated as per the new order. The new priority takes effect immediately once the table has been amended and committed.

However, where EW module is installed or where NCIs along with priority needs to be updated in the front end system, this does not automatically happen. It is required to identify all the customers with nationality as the country whose priority has changed. Then each record in CUSTOMER needs to be recommitted with a minor change, to ensure that the system generates an exit point with the NCIs and the new priority. The NCI Priority (SC.NCI.PRIORITY.MODIFIED) enquiry lists the country records where the NCI priority has changed along with the date on which it was modified.

The drill down available for each record can be accessed to list the existing customer records belonging to that nationality. The user has to manually modify and recommit all the customer records to ensure that NCI and priority are recalculated and sent to the front office system.

Following are the applications that uses the Lei NCI Chk Req field to determine if LEI or NCI check is required for the transaction:

- SEC.OPEN.ORDER
- SEC.TRADE
- ENTITLEMENT
- DX.TRADE
- DX.ORDER
- SC.BULK.TRANSFER
- SECURITY.TRANSFER
- POSITION.TRANSFER

When the user inputs a transaction in Transact, the system checks the Lei NCI Chk Req field in the transaction. This field can be left blank or set as Yes or NCI. The field can be set to Yes only if Legal Entity (LE) module is licenced.

When the user inputs the securities transaction, the system updates the NCI with the ID N-customerid-ncivalue-ncitype. The Identifier Code field in SC.NCI.PARAMETER fetches the value for NCI type.

For customer 100292, if the system fetches the NCI value as passport number, then the NCI type is updated as CCPT. Hence, NCI is updated in this field as N-100292-ABC123-CCPT

System updates the LEI or NCI of the decision maker and order Initiator . The user inputs the decision maker ID in the Decision Mkr ID or Tap Order INIT field in the SEC.TRADE application that fetches the LEI or NCI of the decision maker or order initiator and updates them . If LEI or NCI is not identified for the decision maker or order initiator, the system displays an error as Valid NCI not found.

| Nationality (country code) | Other Nationality (country code) | Country code considered for NCI | Condition applied |
|---|---|---|---|
| IN | SP | SP | SP is an EU country code |
| US | SP and FR | FR | FR is alphabetically first within EU countries |

| Applications | Fields | Values |
|---|---|---|
| SEC.OPEN.ORDER SEC.TRADE ENTITLEMENT DX.TRADE DX.ORDER SC.BULK.TRANSFER SECURITY.TRANSFER POSITION.TRANSFER | Decision Maker ID Order Initiator Trader Manager Instruction MKR | Valid T24 Customer ID. LEI*xxxx L-CustomerID-xxxx N-CustomerID-xxxx-xxxx |
