Various validations are performed to ensure the correctness of the information entered. If the position exists, there is sufficient security available to meet the lending request. The below example shows the result if the securities are not located in the specified depository.

There following are the two problems reported:

- No position is present.
- The amount of security being lent is omitted.

These need to be corrected to proceed with the transaction.

In this instance, the nominal amount of security is greater than the nominal amount in the depository.

The other details (like dates and so on) are also validated. After the transaction is successfully entered and authorised, the SECURITY.POSITION record is updated to confirm the lending operation. Since the original transaction is at the portfolio level, the position for the customer is updated as shown in the below screenshot.

The position remains the same except for an update to the No Nom Bond Lent field as recorded in the BLM transaction (in this case 1,000 shares).

The SC.DEPOT.POSITION records the following in the customer position.

If the BLM request is at depot level, only the SC.DEPOT.POSITION record is updated and all customer positions remain unchanged.

Since the user has a position of 1,500 shares of which 1,000 are lent out, 500 shares are left. The system displays override on any attempt made to sell or transfer-out an amount of security in excess from the available 500 shares, which must be accepted or declined.The above screenshot displays a transfer-out of 1,500 shares in a position from which 1,000 shares are of a lending arrangement.

The system indicates that a number of securities were lent over and above the normal overrides, on committing the transaction, as shown in the below screenshot).

There are two overrides in the above screenshot. The first indicates that 1,000 is lent at the portfolio level. The second indicates that 1,000 are lent from 4447 at the depot level.

Accepting overrides indicate that the securities are lent out and physical settlement does not happen unless the depository automatically returns the lent securities when it identifies the delivery requests. In case, if the lending is returned but not recorded in the system, the user may continue or set the transaction to IHLD (hold) status and close BLM, and then return to SECURITY.TRANSFER to effect the input.

The above example results in a SECURITY.POSITION similar to the below screenshot. The Closing Bal No Nom field has the value zero, indicating that the customer have no security and the No Nom Bond Lent field indicates one or more outstanding lending transactions.

Similar overrides occur for SEC.TRADE, SEC.OPEN.ORDER, SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS and ENTITLEMENT transactions within Temenos Transact . The security lending set-up, and how the committed transactions affect the position in the security for any outstanding lending situations are explained below. The below section explains how to effect full or partial closure of a lending operation.

> **⚠️ Note:** The process of partial returns is available only for depot level lending.

The user must setup a depot level BLM transaction in a position.

The setting-up of a lending transaction at depot level does not require the specification of the portfolio of the security. Therefore, the Security Account field is left blank or cleared on an attempt to identify a portfolio. The Expiry Date field is left blank as the new lending is made open-ended and has no expiry date. As the above transaction is at depot level, only the depot SECURITY.POSITION is updated to indicate the security lent, as shown in the below screenshot.


##### Returning Process of the Bond Lent

To return all or part of a lending, the original transaction is opened and required changes are entered. The additional fields, which are unavailable for input during the setting-up process, now become available for input. Some are multi-value fields to support multiple partial returns by the depository. The first example is of an assumption that all original lent amount is returned.

The main fields are:

- Adj Date - Indicates the date the lending is returned
- Adj Nominal - Indicates the amount of the lending returned

The return of a lending must be preceded with a '-' (negative) sign. If not, the system assumes the lending is to be increased.

Although the BLM allows the user to increase the lending nominal without any problem, it is recommended that each instance of lending be supported by its own BLM record for easier reconciliation of the eventual commission receipt from the depository. If the depository commissions are unchecked, the existing lending can be increased as required. After all the security is returned, any lending in the security requires a new BLM raised.

On committing the record, the Nominal field is recalculated to indicate that there is no outstanding lending amount, as shown in the below screenshot.

When the above transaction is authorised, the transaction updates the underlying SC.DEPOT.POSITION . In case of portfolio lending, the portfolio SECURITY.POSITION is also updated.

The below two screenshots illustrate the SC.DEPOT.POSITION depot, before and after the authorisation of the above BLM in which a full return of the lending is made.

Before BLM is authorised, the No Nom Bond Lent field continues to report the amount of the security lent.

On authorisation of the BLM, the No Nom Bond Lent field is updated as zero to indicate there is no outstanding lending. After a BLM is completed, the full original lent amount is returned in a single tranche or by partial receipts and the transaction is considered to be closed. In this case, further input is not allowed although the transaction may be examined or enquired in the normal way.

The user can attempt to record the partial return of the security lent. The depot position underlying this scenario is shown in the below screenshot, which indicates that 2,000 shares are lent.

Similar to the full return of a lending, the BLM is updated each time a tranche of security is returned. This process continues until all the security is returned and the operation is complete.

The above screenshot illustrates how a BLM may appear following the input of a partial return of 750 shares. In this case, the Nominal field is reduced from the original amount of the lending by the amount of the shares returned.

The Adj Date and Adj Nominal multi-value fields can be updated as shown in the above screenshot and the record can be committed. The user can also add any free-format narrative.

The Adj Narrative field indicates each movement, be it a returned or increased security. The Notes field records the ad hoc notes concerning the lending operation as a whole. The Adj Narrative and Notes fields are not mandatory and can be left blank, if required.

The Nominal field value is updated again to reflect the second return of shares. The original lending of 2,000 is reduced by 1,700 and it now displays 300 remaining shares to be returned.

After the BLM R recording of the returned nominal is duly authorised, the SC.DEPOT.POSITION is updated to display the new outstanding lending amount, which is 300 in this example.

This process continues until the Nominal field value in each BLM becomes zero, after which the transaction is considered closed and further input is not allowed.

For a portfolio level lending operation, the set-up of the initial BLM is almost similar to that of a depository level setup except that the identification of the source portfolio must be specified for the portfolio level.

For a portfolio level lending, the Lending Type field is set to Portfolio and the portfolio sourcing the securities are added to the Securities Account field., Temenos Transact expects a tentative date, on which the securities are returned which is indicated in the Expiry Date field, for portfolio level lending.

This applies for returns and/or increases as well similar to the depository level lending except that the lending cannot be partially returned for portfolio level. The user can enter the fees received from the depository and reduce this amount by the bank’s share of this commission while entering a return of security. This process is illustrated in the following screenshot.

In the above example, the commission paid by the depository amounts to USD 23.75 less the bank’s share of the charges USD 6.95. The net amount of USD defined in the Account Number field must be credited to the customer’s account. On committing and authorising the above record, the Temenos Transact accounting process happens and may be enquired upon, if required.

The BLM authorised completely is shown in the below screenshot. The below screenshot displays a completely closed and authorised BLM record in which all the standard information are stored including the details in the Statement Nos and Delivery Key fields.

The below screenshot displays the closure of a lending where the source is a dealer book (bank owned portfolio). The closure operation is almost identical to that for a customer portfolio except for the charges. In case of dealer books, the user must enter the same amount in the Charges field, since all the commission are credited to the bank’s P/L account.

### 5.33  Brokerage Only Transactions


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
>

Once the transaction (purchase or sale) is executed by the bank with a broker on behalf of the customer, bank delivers or receives th...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Broker / client*, *Broker Only*, *Broker Only Cat*, *Broker Only Cty*, *Broker Only Port*, *Broker.1*, *Cash to Settle.1*, *Client* ... +22 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In some cases, bank acts only as the intermediate broker for some customers. Bank places the order on behalf of the customer, whose custody and cash is held external. Once the transaction (purchase or sale) is executed by the bank with a broker on behalf of the customer, bank delivers or receives the securities versus payment to the customer’s account at its custodian according to the customer’s standard settlement instruction. As these transactions are done only for the interim brokerage, they are known as brokerage only transactions.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic details the configuration for brokerage only transactions in Securities (SC) module.


##### Setting up Broker Only Portfolio

The Broker Only field in SEC.ACC.MASTER is set to Yes to denote that the custody of the customer is external and the transactions performed for this portfolio are brokerage only transactions.

The Ext Bic field defines the Bank Identification Code (BIC) of the customer’s custodian or the external party to whom the MT541 or MT543 needs to be sent. The Ext Cust Acc field defines the customer’s security account in the external custodian. This account is mapped to the Tag 97A::SAFE// sent to the customer’s custodian for brokerage only transactions.


##### Recording Synthetic Portfolio and Counterparty

The Broker Only Cty field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE defines the synthetic counterparty (intermediate broker) to be updated in broker of the first trade (Trade 1). The synthetic counterparty is the bank which acts as an intermediate broker. The Broker Only Port field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE defines the synthetic portfolio (intermediate customer portfolio) to be updated in customer portfolio of the underlying trade (Trade 2). The synthetic portfolio is the bank’s portfolio, where bank is acting as an intermediate customer. The Broker Only Cat field defines the suspense account used for accounting entry processing for brokerage only transactions. This is an internal account and the suspense account for all the brokerage only transactions.


##### Configuring SSIs for Customers

The standard settlement instructions (SSIs) for the customer needs to be sent as part of the MT541 or MT543 sent to bank’s custodian (Trade 1) as the custody of the customer is held external. Set the SSIs for the customers in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT with ID as Customer ID.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic details how brokerage transactions are handled in Securities (SC) module.


##### Handling Brokerage Only Transactions

The brokerage only portfolios hold both position and cash externally. The customer instructs an order either by call or email or any other communication, to the trading room and an order is placed on behalf of the customer. On confirmation of the execution from the external broker, the system creates two trades. The first trade (Trade 1) is between the customer and bank, where the bank acts as an intermediate broker (synthetic counterparty) and the second trade (Trade 2) is between the bank’s synthetic portfolio (intermediate customer portfolio) and the external broker, where the bank acts as a synthetic customer (synthetic portfolio).

MT541 or MT543 is sent to the bank’s custodian in the first trade to settle the transaction with the customer’s custodian. MT541 or MT543 is sent to the customer’s custodian in the first trade (if configured for the customer). MT541 or MT543 is sent to bank’s custodian in the second trade to settle the transaction with the broker’s custodian.

On customer’s instruction, an order is placed for the brokerage only Portfolio 123123-1. The order details are:

- Portfolio – 729397-1
- Transaction – Buy
- Security – 625136-001
- Nominal – 1000

The order is executed by the broker 625136 in the market.

On confirmation of execution from the external broker, the trades are created on two sides on hold. The first trade (Trade 1) is between the customer and bank, where the bank acts as an intermediate broker and the second trade (Trade 2) is between bank and the external broker, where the bank acts an intermediate customer.

In the below screenshot, the trade (Trade 1) is between the customer and bank, where the bank acts as an intermediate broker (synthetic broker).

In the below screenshot, the trade (Trade 2) is between bank and the external broker, where the bank acts an intermediate customer (synthetic customer).

Both trades are linked by populating a common reference for both the trades in the Link Reference field.


##### Instruction for Depository Messages

The Depo Advice Reqd? field in SEC.TRADE is used for triggering the depository messages from the trade. If this field is set to No, then SWIFT messages are not sent to depository for this transaction. If the field is set to Yes, then SWIFT messages are sent to bank custodian only. In case of brokerage only transaction, the bank’s user can decide whether the SWIFT messages need to be sent to bank custodian or customer’s custodian or both using Depo Advice Reqd? field.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Client and Both values are applicable for the brokerage only transaction (Trade 1) between the customer and bank, where bank acts as an intermediate broker (synthetic broker). The screenshot below shows the field set as Both.

On authorising Trade 1, MT543 (as it is a buy trade) is sent to customer’s custodian.

The SSI set for the bank in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT is defaulted to the trade. The SSI can be amended at the trade level.

The standard instruction of the bank defaulted in trade is sent as part of the MT541 message that is sent to the customer’s custodian.

MT543 is sent to bank’s custodian to settle the transaction with the customer’s custodian. The SSIs of the customer are sent as part of this message.

The SSI set for the customer in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT is defaulted to the trade (only for brokerage only transactions). The SSI can be amended at the trade level.

The standard instruction of the customer defaulted in trade is sent as part of the MT543 message that is sent to the bank’s custodian.

MT541 is sent to bank’s custodian in the second trade to settle the transaction with the broker’s custodian.


##### Settlement Records

On authorising the trades, separate settlement records are created for both trades. The first settlement record is for the bank to settle with the customer and the second settlement record is for the bank to settle with the external broker. The below screenshots illustrate the settlement record for Trade 1 and Trade 2.


##### Accounting Entries

On settlement, the below shown accounting entries are raised for Trade 1 and Trade 2 in the system for the transaction.

In the first trade, USD 10800 is receivable from the customer through the custodian, which includes USD 800 brokerage charged by the bank to the customer. In the second trade, USD 10400 is payable to the external broker through the custodian, which includes USD 400 brokerage to be paid to the broker. The difference in commission receivable and commission payable of USD 400 is the bank’s intermediate commission, which is booked to the bank’s P&L account.

Temenos Transact supports different tax lot methods. The tax lot method to be used is definable at individual portfolio level or portfolio group and overall at the comp...*
>

> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account Nos*, *Accrued Int*, *Broker Comms*, *Calc Tax*, *Cg Base Update*, *Cg Incl Accr Int*, *Cg Incl Expense*, *Cg Manual Input* ... +81 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Capital Gains Tax (CGT) is chargeable on capital gains generated by disposal of Securities that have been acquired at a fixed cost. Temenos Transact supports different tax lot methods. The tax lot method to be used is definable at individual portfolio level or portfolio group and overall at the company level, per asset class. This feature document briefs on the standard methods applicable for capital gain calculation and also the basic parameter setup necessary for calculating the CGT.

This document details the capital gains calculation in securities processing, based on the standard methods that allow adjustment of an acquired security cost with the inflation index applicable at the time of its disposal.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This CGT transaction base builds up initially from the raw Security transactions or from the records in SECURITY.TRANS and updates it into the system over the period of time. Security transactions generated only by SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER or DIARY through its child ENTITLEMENT transaction updates the transactions base. The methods used in building the base must be specified in the CG.PARAMETER application. The parameters allow for flexibility in defining time frames and processing sort orders in the trading periods. This is explained in the below table.

| Time Period | Method Used |
|---|---|
| Prior to April 6, 1965 | Last in First Out (LIFO) |
| April 7, 1965 to Apr 6, 1982 | 1982 pool (trades are amalgamated into one with the amount decided with respect to the price of the security as on 6th April 1965) |
| April 7, 1982 to Apr 6, 1985 | 1985 pool (trades are amalgamated into one with the amount decided with respect to the price of the security as on 6th April 1982) |
| After April 7, 1985 | First In First Out (FIFO) |

The CGT position base is maintained in a trade date and time order. The transaction date and time, costs, expenses and accrued interest are taken directly from the records in SECURITY.TRANS that lead to the update. Exceptions to this rule are only applicable, when rules processing is used. Read CG.TXN.RULES for definitions of this functionality. The following fields in SECURITY.TRANS application are used to define CGT data:

- Cost is extracted from Gross Amt Sec Curr
- Accrued interest from Interest Amt
- Expenses from the sum of Commission , Broker Comms , Stock Exchange Fees , Other Foreign Fees , Stamp Tax , Ebv Fees and Fees Misc.

The above details leads to the addition of a transaction to the CG.TXN.BASE . The cost of GBP 236.40 and expenses of GBP 15.00 does not necessarily rises to any taxation liability. The trade date (September 11, 2002) and time (10:53) are used to place the transaction in the correct position within the base. The CG.TXN.BASE application is shown in the below screenshot .

Several actions must be taken to properly utilise the CGT processing. This is illustrated in the following sections.


##### SEC.ACC.MASTER

It should be noted that while performing transactions for a particular customer, the system allows to use account numbers which are not linked to the Account Nos field of the corresponding customer portfolio in SEC.ACC.MASTER . However the capture of STMT.ENTRY IDs in CG.TXN.BASE relies on the present link. This link is essential so that an account number can be linked to a portfolio and hence the CG.TXN.BASE . The account numbers belong to SEC.ACC.MASTER records in the same PORTFOLIO.GROUPING causes the same problem in the CG.TXN.BASE .

If this happens the tax entries are posted, neither adding the tax STMT.ENTRY IDs to the CG.TXN.BASE nor changing the Tax Status field status to POSTED. Further, reversing these underlying transactions that generated the tax entries does not reverse the tax entries at all, as the Tax Status field leading the system to understand that tax entries does not exist and displays TO_BE_CALC. Therefore, manual adjustment by DATA.CAPTURE is required to rectify the situation.


##### SC.PARAMETER

Allows the system to maintain the data for calculating capital gains in CG.TXN.BASE , set the Cg Base Update field to YES or RULES. A SC.PARAMETER record with the above settings is shown in the below screenshot.


##### CG.PARAM.CONDITION

This application allows to group customers based on certain conditions and also allow to apply different tax rules to these groups using the CG.PARAMETER application. The grouping can be done based on certain selection criteria using the fields available in the application CUSTOMER , SECURITY.MASTER or SUB.ASSET.TYPE .

The process of checking how the CG.PARAM.CONDITION applies to a transaction involves validating the records in alphabetical order, whether the condition applied from the first set of parameters match. Therefore, Temenos Transact user must ensure that the conditions are setup correctly, to match data with the most specific conditions first and more general conditions at the end.

> **⚠️ Note:** Temenos Transact selects the first match and does not find the best match.

For instance if two CG.PARAM.CONDITION records exist where one has the customer and residence values set to GB and the other has the customer and residence region values set to LONDON. Then, the more accurate match for a customer with a residence region equal to LONDON is the second record. However, the first record is also true, so a selection is made of the record which is discovered first in the list.

CGT is chargeable on capital gains generated by disposal of securities that are acquired at a fixed cost. Either the financial institution ( Temenos Transact user) acting on behalf of the customer who has the tax liability or with the depository that sets the disposal transaction holds the responsibility of withholding CGT (collecting and paying to the relevant tax authority).

If the Temenos Transact user is responsible for withholding the tax, it is termed as LOCAL and if the depository withholds the tax, it is termed as SOURCE. It is possible to define whether CG tax must be LOCAL or SOURCE in each record in CG.PARAM.CONDITION . Tax laws change different groups of customers or securities come in or drop out of the source net. Therefore, it must be possible to allow a change from SOURCE to LOCAL or vice versa from a specified future start date. This is achieved by inputting the LOCAL or SOURCE value to the Src Lcl Tax field. The associated Tax Start Date field is left blank for the earliest LOCAL or SOURCE setting. The input of a future date into the Tax Start Date field and the SOURCE or LOCAL value into the Src Lcl Tax field may effect a change. If LOCAL is selected, the resultant records in STMT.ENTRY debit the customer and credit the tax category account. If SOURCE is selected, the customer is debited and the depository nostro account is credited, as the depository usually deducts the source tax from the disposal proceeds. A record in CG.PARAM.CONDITION is shown in the below screenshot.

The condition shown in the above screenshot is applied to all customers who have a value GB in the Residence field in the CUSTOMER application. Groups may be defined using the CUSTOMER (as above), SEC.ACC.MASTER , SECURITY.MASTER or SUB.ASSET.TYPE applications and any of the fields in these applications. Any number of conditions may be applied. If the transaction is before Apr 5, 2003, the Temenos Transact system withholds the tax, otherwise the depository withholds the tax.


##### CG.PARAMETER

Once the user sets the above group, the CG.PARAMETER application is used to set the tax, capital gain method and the related parameters.

The above settings indicates the capital gains method to be used while calculating a gain that is FIFO . Any purchases made within 14 days ( Reacq Prd ) of a sale is dropped from any associated losses on these sales. The setting for Reacq Prd and Reacq Drop Loss can also be specified at SECURITY.MASTER level. The settings in SECURITY.MASTER takes precedence over those in CG.PARAMETER level.

The tax charged on any gain is defined using the CGT record in TAX.TYPE.CONDITION . Read the System Tables section in User Guide for more information on how to setup taxes and use the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application.

When the capital gain is calculated, the inclusion or exclusion of accrued interest and expenses in the costs is determined by setting the Cg Incl Accr Int , Cg Incl Expense , Wcg Incl Accr Int and Wgc Incl Expense fields. The setting of the parameters for inclusion or exclusion of accrued interest and expenses can be specified additionally at ASSET.TYPE or SECURITY.MASTER level. The same fields exist in these applications and the system uses the settings from SECURITY.MASTER in preference to those in ASSET.TYPE . In turn, this is used in preference to those in CG.PARAMETER , thereby offering greater flexibility depending upon specific security issues, security types or generally through the parameter file.

Before any tax is calculated on a gain, the inflation index is applied (if Use Infl Indx field is set to YES) and taper relief is applied (if Cg Taper Relief field is set to 2) using the record defined in Cg Taper Relief field. If Use Infl Indx is not YES, indexation is not applied and if the Cg Taper Relief field is blank, taper relief is not applied. Taper relief may not be applied, if any of the Cg Method multi-values are AVERAGE.

Where a disposal of securities acts against multiple acquisitions, the disposal proceeds are applied proportionately against each acquired nominal to calculate the gain or loss, if any. These gains and losses are netted and tax are applied only if the net effect is an overall gain.

Using the FIFO method purchases of:

1,000 for USD 10,000.00

1,000 for USD 20,000.00

1,000 for USD 40,000.00

And a sale of:

3,000 for USD 180,000.00

Gives separate CG amounts of:

USD 50,000.00 gain

USD 40,000.00 gain

USD 20,000.00 gain

Therefore, tax is charged on the net gain of USD 110,000.00. However, a sale of 3,000 at USD 90,000.00 gives separate CG amounts of:

USD 20,000.00 gain

USD 10,000.00 gain

USD 10,000.00 loss

Therefore, tax is chargeable on the net gain of USD 20,000.00.

Therefore, those instances that result in a loss do not attract tax although all underlying transactions that continue to feature in the CG.TXN.BASE . Therefore by default, it affects the taxable situation of any subsequent transaction (although this is subject to any restrictions that may exist to cover re-acquisitions of the same stock. Read the Working with Capital Gains for more information).


#### 🔧 Working With

The tax lots methods are:

FIFO

First In, First Out (FIFO) is an asset-management and valuation method in which the assets produced or acquired first are sold, used or disposed of first. FIFO may be used by an individual or a corporation.

LIFO

Last In, First Out (LIFO) is an asset-management and valuation method that assumes that assets produced or acquired last are the ones that are used, sold or disposed of first.

AVERAGE

A system of calculating the cost basis on mutual fund positions held in a taxable account to determine the profit or loss on them. The average cost basis method adds up the cost basis for the entire position in a specific mutual fund and divides it by the total number of fund shares owned to arrive at an average cost per share.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is also possible to apply taper relief percentages to a gain, prior calculating any tax due.

Inflation indexation can be applied to the costs of the original acquisition. To enable this, the Use Infl Indx field in CG.PARAMETER is set to Yes. The inflation index to be used is defined in the Residence and Residence Region fields in the CUSTOMER application. The Residence Region takes priority over the Residence field. If Residence Region is set, the inflation index figures are retrieved from the REGION application, otherwise they are retrieved from the COUNTRY application.

The types of inflation index values supported by Temenos Transact are: Standard (STD) - Where the months or years progress, the index for the current month increases and is usually expressed as a number in relation to a base figure of 100. Spanish (ES) - Where the current month is expressed as 1 and preceding months as a multiplication factor. The type of index to be used is specified in SC.PARAMETER in the Infl Indx Meth field. A record in SC.PARAMETER application with the above setup is shown in the below screenshot.

The following transactions are made:

A purchase of 12,000 shares is made at a cost of 15000 USD on 1st May 1999, a second purchase is made of 10,000 shares at a cost of 16,000 USD on 1st January 2000. A sale for 17,000 shares is then made and the proceeds of which are 25,000 USD on the current business day.

When retrieving the inflation indexes from the COUNTRY or REGION application using the ES method, the system appends the transaction year to the key before reading the data. For example, a disposal transaction in 1999 for a customer with a Residence Region of ES01 attempts to read the record keyed by ES01.1999 from the REGION application. If that fails, the key ES01 is used.

If the STD method is used, the transaction years are not used to suffix the key and only the field from the record in COUNTRY is used. A standard record in COUNTRY application which utilises a STD method is shown in the below screenshot.

The inflation indexes entered using the STD method is seen in the above screenshot.

Using the above screenshot, the cost of the shares purchased on May 01, 1999 is calculated as:

(1 + (123.6 – 121.8) / 121.8) * 15,000 = 15,221.70

The cost of the shares purchases on 1st January 2000 are calculated as:

(1 + (123.6 – 123.1) / 123.1) * 16,000 * 5,000/10,000 = 8,032.48

This gives a total cost of 23,254.18 USD and a gain of 1,745.82 USD. The inflation indexes entered using the ES method is displayed in the below screenshot.

Using the above screenshot the cost of the shares purchased on 1st May 1999 are calculated as:

1.23 * 15,000 = 18,450.00

The cost of the shares purchases on 1st January 2000 are adjusted as:

1.04 * 16,000 * 5,000/10,000 = 8,320.00

This gives a total cost of 26,770 USD and a loss of 1,770.00 USD.

> **⚠️ Note:** The above applications are for guidance only and do not resemble the actual inflation index amounts in any way.

This application allows the Temenos Transact users to specify reduction percentages to be applied and gain after any indexation is applied. A CG.TAPER.RELIEF record is shown in the below screenshot.

The above record only applies to sale transactions made on or after 1st January 1999. The use of the date in the ID allows for changes in the taper relief percentages over time. Only the first part of the ID is specified in the record in CG.PARAMETER , then the system automatically determines which record to use. The fields set in this record applies a reduction of 10%, to the holdings held for at least five years but less than 10 years. A reduction of 15% is applied to holdings held for at least 10 years but less than 20 years, holdings held for at least 20 years but less that 30 years receives a 25% reduction. Holdings held for less than five years receives no reduction. Holdings held for at least 30 years receives a reduction percentage of 30%.

However, it is possible to determine the rate to be used by inputting, instead a user defining a local subroutine. A user defined local subroutine can be used to calculate the reduction percentage and the subroutine name must be entered in the Reduct Pct field prefixed by the @ symbol.

The subroutine must have five subroutine arguments. The first three are passed by the calling routine, which are the transaction base record. The rest are multi-value position of the sale in the base record and the multi-value position of the purchase in the base record. The remaining two arguments are reduction percentage, which must be returned by the local subroutine and an error message variable, which is reserved for future use.

If there are any doubts about this particular facility and how to setup, contact the Temenos Transact support team.

Holding periods can be specified as either months or years in Held Period Type field. If the holding are held for part of a period, the fractional element can either be rounded up to one or down to 0, as specified in Held Period Round field.

The Pur Qual Date and Sale Qual Date fields are used to capture whether a holding qualifies for taper relief. If the Pur Qual Date field is populated, the purchase is on or before the date specified and if the Sale Qual Date field is populated, the sale is on or after the date specified. If both fields are populated, then both the sale and purchase satisfies the conditions for the taper relief to be applied.

If the Held Period Cutoff field is used, the maximum holding period is limited by this date. If the sale date is greater than the date in this field, the date in this field is used for calculating the holding period. Taper relief is not applied, if a loss is made on a transaction.

This application allows the Temenos Transact user to group the portfolios of a customer, for CGT purposes. A PORTFOLIO.GROUPING record is shown in the below screenshot.

The above record maintains a separate transaction base records for each portfolio belonging to the customer 888. However, it is possible to setup the system to group all the customer portfolios for CGT purposes as shown below.

The above record groups all transactions from portfolios 897-1 and 897-2 for CGT purposes.

If the Group Name is set to ALL, only one group may be used and any new portfolio for the customer must be added to the same group. However, it automatically adds a new portfolio to the ALL group, when the first transaction is made. If the ALL group is not used, the system automatically adds a new group for each new portfolio with its own group code to the record in PORTFOLIO.GROUPING , when the first transaction is made. The group code is set as the portfolio code.

If the Temenos Transact user does not want the system to automatically allocate portfolios to groups and set group names, they must setup or amend the record in PORTFOLIO.GROUPING whenever a new record is added to SEC.ACC.MASTER and before any transactions, SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER are made in that portfolio. A portfolio cannot be moved between groups or deleted from groups, if there are any security positions for the concerned portfolio.

When the application is setup for the first time the system creates the records in PORTFOLIO.GROUPING for each portfolio referenced in the CG.TXN.BASE . This setup is done as part of the conversion routine. The records are setup using the CUSTOMER ID and each portfolio is added with a Group Name , that is the same as the SEC.ACC.MASTER ID.

The user can allow the system to setup these records. As each new SEC.ACC.MASTER executes a transaction for the first time, the setup is identical, a new Group Name is added to the record in PORTFOLIO.GROUPING and it is same as the SEC.ACC.MASTER ID. An override message is displayed at transaction level.

If the Temenos Transact user wishes to change this default action, before each record in SEC.ACC.MASTER executes a transaction the record in PORTFOLIO.GROUPING must be updated with the Temenos Transact user’s preferred settings.

This application is used only when the settings for Cg Base Update field in SC.PARAMETER record is set to RULES. If Cg Base Update is set to YES, the CG.TXN.RULES application is ignored altogether and the setting up of new records is not allowed.

The CG.TXN.RULES enables the user to specify an event to be performed when a transaction updates the CGT transaction base. This also enables the Temenos Transact user to specify which particular transaction type updates the transaction base. A CG.TXN.RULES record is shown in the below screenshot.

The application allows to setup records using the transaction name as in the:

- Sc Trans Name field
- SUB.ASSET.TYPE ID or
- SECURITY.MASTER ID

The record containing a SECURITY.MASTER ID is used in preference to one with a SUB.ASSET.TYPE ID, which in turn is used in preference to one containing just the transaction name.

Each record can specify a particular capital event using the Event Type field. The Event Type field has the drop-down list with the following values:

- ACTION.WARRANT
- BONUS.SHARE
- BUY
- CAPINCR.RIGHTS
- CAPITAL.REDUCTION
- CONVERSION
- MERGER
- REDEMPTION
- REDENOMINATION
- RIGHTS
- SEL
- SPINOFF
- SPLIT
- STOCK.DIVIDEND
- TAKE.OVER

> **⚠️ Note:** Validations are not made between the origin of the transaction and the Event Type , therefore it is possible to link a security purchase to a Corporate Action (CA) type event such as a SPINOFF, but in such cases the results are unpredictable.The Event Type used in CG.TXN.RULES must not be confused with the Event Type field as defined in DIARY , which refers to a valid record in the DIARY.TYPE application.

For an ENTITLEMENT to be used to update the CG.TXN.BASE , the CG.TXN.RULES selected is obtained from the ENTITLEMENT belonging to a parent DIARY to the underlying DIARY.TYPE , SC.TRANS.TYPE , SC.TRANS.NAME and CG.TXN.RULES . A DIARY with any Event Type ( DIARY.TYPE ) may be linked to any of the valid Event Type values in CG.TXN.RULES, as listed above.

While using a DIARY.TYPE that does not create any cash posting naturally, (that is, only securities are produced as in SPINOFF), the Update Nostro field must be set to NO in order for tax postings to be created for the capital gains.

The following are the various event types listed in the Event Type field present in the CG.TXN.RULES application.

The warrant is disposed of and the new shares are added to the transaction base at the cost of exercising the warrant and at the cost (if any) of the warrants themselves. The warrants are disposed at cost yielding zero capital gain. If the warrant is lapsed, new shares are not created.

If the Upd Orig Nom field is set to Y and:

- If the bonus shares are the same as the original security, the new shares are spread over to all open transactions in proportion to the number of shares in the active Cg Nominal that is already on the base.
- If the bonus shares are in a new security or securities, the new shares are added to a new transaction base record and the cost is apportioned between the transaction base records in proportion to the number of shares. If the Orig Acq Dt field is Y, the new shares are added to the new base using the dates of the original acquisitions, otherwise the new shares are added using the Pay Date from the DIARY application.

If the Upd Orig Nom field is not set to Y, any new shares are added as a single transaction using the Pay Date in the DIARY application.

A transaction is added to the base using the Trade Date field, if transaction originates from either SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER or DIARY or Pay Date field. If the transaction originates from SEC.TRADE and the Cust No Nom field which contains more than one sub-value, then one transaction is added for each of these sub-values.

If the transaction originates from a DIARY, the CG.TXN.BASE for the rights security is updated with the appropriate number of rights for zero cost with an acquisition date equal to the ex-date of the DIARY .

The costs of the purchase or sale is added to or subtracted from the transaction base of the security that created the rights entitlement:

- If the transaction originates from SEC.TRADE and
- If the transaction is a purchase or sale for rounding (achieving the correct number rights to enable take up of a whole number of new securities) indicated by Odd Rts Cgt field (set to Y) in the SEC.TRADE and Rstl Updt Orig (set to Y)

. At the same point, the Odd Rts Sam and Odd Rts Bam in ENTITLEMENT is adjusted by the nominal amount purchased or sold. Then the transaction is added to the rights security transaction base with the cost adjusted by the amount distributed to the original security transaction base.

If the Odd Rts Cgt is not set to Y, the transaction is added to the base as either a BUY or SEL in the Event Type field.

If the rights are exercised, so that the transaction originates from DIARY , the rights securities position becomes zero and the new security or securities position is created. If the new security is same as the security that facilitates corporate action, the new shares are either distributed over the existing transactions ( Upd Orig Nom field as Y) or added as a single new transaction with an acquisition date equal to the payment date in DIARY .

If the new security is different from the security that facilitated corporate action, a new transaction base is created with the cost apportioned between the transactions bases. The new base uses the dates from the original acquisitions, where an amount remains unsold.

This event takes the cash repaid to the customer and reduces the costs of the transactions in the base by an amount proportional to the Cg Nominal field.

This event removes the holdings from the original security and creates new base records for each of the securities resulting from the conversion.

The cost or proceeds of the movement out of the original security is the market value of the new security, based on the New Market Price field in DIARY . The conversion premium and accrued interest can be included in this disposal cost or the acquisition cost using the Conv Incl Accr and Conv Incl Prem flags. Therefore, there is a capital gain or loss calculated that may be material, if different from the original cost. The user can suppress the tax posting by setting the Calc Tax field to NO on the CG.TXN.RULES application.

The cost of the new securities are calculated using the new market price, in the New Market Price field in DIARY . Depending on the settings of Conv Incl Accr and Conv Incl Prem fields the original accrued interest and conversion premium can be added to this cost.

This event closes down the transaction base for the original security and creates new base records for the new security or securities.

There are two types of MERGER processing which is determined by the Fiscal Eff flag:

- With or
- Without fiscal effect

If Fiscal Eff is not Y the old security is removed at the original acquisition cost and the new security or securities are added with the original acquisition cost allocated proportionally.

If Fiscal Eff is Y, the Mkt Val Old , Mkt Val New , Mkt Val High or Mkt Val Low flags determines the costs to be used. Only one of these flags can be specified. For example, if Mkt Val High is set, the old security is removed and the cost is the highest of the old security or the new security or securities. The new securities are added using the same cost and spread proportionally, if required. While calculating the costs, the Old Market Price and New Market Price fields from the DIARY application are used.

A disposal transaction is added to the base using the Trade Date field, if transaction originates from either SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER or Pay Date or from DIARY . If the transaction originates from SEC.TRADE and the Cust No Nom field contains more than one sub-value, one transaction is added for each of these sub-values. The disposal proceeds are the redemption proceeds from the record in SECURITY.TRANS which is derived from the ENTITLEMENT application.

A transaction is added to the base using the Trade Date field, if transaction originates from either SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER or Pay Date or from DIARY . If the transaction originates from SEC.TRADE and the Cust No Nom field contains more than one sub-value, one transaction is added for each of these sub-values. The rights security is disposed and the new security or securities are added to the transactions base. This functionality is suppressed by the CAPINCR.RIGHTS event type, which is more comprehensive.

A transaction is added to the base using the Trade Date field, if the transaction originates from either SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER or Pay Date or from DIARY . If the transaction originates from SEC.TRADE and the Cust No Nom field contains more than one sub-value, one transaction is added for each of these sub-values.

There are two types of SPINOFF, as defined in the Fiscal Effect field in CG.TXN.RULES application.

- With or
- Without fiscal effect

When the flag is set to Y, the original securities are removed from its corresponding record in CG.TXN.BASE at the sum of the market valuations of the original and new securities. The original securities are re-acquired at their own market valuation and the new securities are acquired at their own valuation.

When the flag is set to N, the original securities are disposed from its CG.TXN.BASE at its original cost. The re-acquisition cost and acquisition costs of the original and new securities are the original cost split in proportion to the market valuation of the original and new securities inferred by the Old Market Price and New Market Price fields in the DIARY application.

This event updates the active Cg Nominal fields on the CG.TXN.BASE application. It spreads the new split position across all the active Cg Nominal amounts in the proportion of the previous Cg Nominal value divided by the total of the previous active Cg Nominals.

This event updates the original Cg Nominal fields in the transaction base, if Upd Orig Nom is Y or a new transaction is added to the base. The cost of the new securities are determined by setting the Mkt Val New field. If the Upd Orig Nom field is set to Y, the cost of the new securities are distributed over the active Cg Nominal positions. When the security derived from the stock dividend is different from the original security, a new transaction base record is created.

A transaction is added to the base using the Trade Date field, if the transaction originates from either SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER or Pay Date or from DIARY . If the transaction originates from SEC.TRADE and the Cust No Nom field contains more than one sub-value, one transaction is added for each of these sub-values. The original security is disposed and the new security or securities are added to the transaction’s base. The costs used are those on each of the records in SECURITY.TRANS from the Gross Amt Sec Curr field. This is the original functionality, which preceded CG.TXN.RULES and it is recommended that MERGER must be used for CAs that require more flexible TAKE.OVER type functionality.

The Calc Tax field is used to trigger the calculation of capital gains tax. Tax is calculated if this field is set to Y, otherwise the transaction does not generate any tax accounting entries. The Manual Allowed field is used to limit whether the transaction type can be used in Cg Manual Input or not. It may only be set to Y, if the Event Type is either BUY or SELL.

The Update Method field can be set either to ONLINE or BATCH. When set to BATCH all updates to the transaction base, CG.TXN.BASE and tax calculations takes place during COB batch process and is only performed for authorised transactions. If set to ONLINE, the transaction base is updated when the transaction is validated, that is, at unauthorised status and the tax is calculated at the same time. The tax postings at this stage is NAU or forward value dated entries and they are fully posted when the underlying records are authorised, if the system date is equal to or greater than the value date of the transaction.

In case of forward value dated entries, they are posted and the CG.TXN.BASE is updated in the start of day processing in the COB routine. For instance, a transaction value dated 20th updates the base in the COB routine for 19th, which processes the start of day routines for 20th. The STMT.ENTRY IDs are recorded in the Stmt Nos in CG.TXN.BASE and in the authorised underlying record. At the same time, the Tax Status field in the CG.TXN.BASE is changed to POSTED.

> **⚠️ Note:** The only record in ENTITLEMENT that updates the transaction base at unauthorised stage are rights type CAs, where the new rights securities are added to the base with an acquisition date equal to the ex-date of the DIARY .

Specifically for those records in DIARY.TYPE with the Rights field set to Y, the setting method to ONLINE may cause a high number of history records to be stored, as each change to an underlying transaction in the base and its subsequent authorisation updates the Curr No of the record.

This application is used only when Cg Base Update field in SC.PARAMETER is set to RULES. While using this application the amendments to the transaction base generates no accounting entries. It allows the Temenos Transact user to either enter a capital gains transaction base for a customer, or correct positions within the base. The CG.MANUAL.INPUT does not create records in SECURITY.TRANS or updates the records in SECURITY.POSITION .

Therefore, to create a transaction history for a position for a newly acquired customer, a SECURITY.TRANSFER in which the Transaction Type field value indicates a receipt must be used with a Sc Trans Name field value not specified in the CG.TXN.RULES application, which does not updates the CG.TXN.BASE .

When using CG.MANUAL.INPUT to create the history, the user has to input the transaction ID of the record in SECURITY.TRANS including the suffix (that is, SCTRSC0005300001.1) into the Transaction Id field. If the ID does not already exist in the CG.TXN.BASE , the following fields are populated automatically by the system:

- Portfolio No
- Group Name
- Security No
- Security Ccy
- Master Trd Nominal

The following multi-valued fields are populated to reflect the trade history comprising the nominal amount displayed in Master Trd Nominal field:

- Trade Date Time
- Txn Type
- Trd Nominal
- Trd Value
- Accrued Int
- Expenses

If the user tries to commit the record, when the sum of the Trd Nominal fields is not equal to the Master Trd Nominal an error message is displayed. Each multi-valued set is added to the record in CG.TXN.BASE , when the record in CG.MANUAL.INPUT is authorised. The CG.TXN.BASE position nominal is now in line with the SECURITY.POSITION . The user can also create a CG trade history record by adding a record in CG.MANUAL.INPUT, which is not connected to an underlying transaction, but this is likely to put the SECURITY.POSITION and CG.TXN.BASE position out of synchronisation and makes it difficult to reconcile and control. | 3 | 4,875 | 9 |

All expenses from SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER are included in expense calculation ( Expense in CG.TXN.BASE ). If the bank wants to exclude a certain fee from expense calculation and the respective fee is set through multiple charge framework ( SCDX.CHARGE.PARAMETER ), the respective fee is set in Excl Expense . The excluded fee is considered in the expense calculation ( Expense in CG.TXN.BASE ).

> **⚠️ Note:** As the excluded fee or charge is not part of the Expense , the fee is not included in cost and proceeds calculation.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Capital Gains feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Capital Gains feature.

### 5.35  Central Hub Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Banks can manage their securities and derivatives orders through a central hub. All the securities and derivatives orders that are Non-OTC (Over The Counter) are placed in the central hub company.*
> 
> **Applications:** `COMPANY`, `CUSTOMER`, `CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `DX.CONTRACT.MASTER`, `DX.ORDER`, `DX.PARAMETER`, `DX.TRADE`, `OFS.SOURCE` ... +11 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *@ID*, *Additional Info*, *App Field*, *App Field 1*, *App Field 2*, *App Field 3*, *App Field 4*, *App Field 5* ... +43 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Banks can manage their securities and derivatives orders through a central hub. All the securities and derivatives orders that are Non-OTC (Over The Counter) are placed in the central hub company.

The following are performed in the hub company:

- Manage trade and settlement
- Maintain positions

The hub will be a COMPANY , and each portfolio’s own company is considered as its own COMPANY . The customers ( CUSTOMER ) and the portfolio's ( SEC.ACC.MASTER ) should be shared across the companies.

While portfolios are created in the respective portfolio’s own company, the securities and derivatives orders are placed directly in the hub company, and all further Hub processing are handled at the hub. The valuation is done at each portfolio’s own company.

Local customisation of enquiries can be performed to allow the users of the portfolio’s own company to view the transactions of their customers in the hub.

In the case of specific funds like Canadian funds, trades can be booked in the portfolio’s own company instead of the hub company. The trades are controlled by the SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM table, which defines the conditions based on the fields from the CUSTOMER , SECURITY.MASTER and DX.CONTRACT.MASTER applications. If the conditions are satisfied, the order is routed to the portfolio’s own company, else order is routed to the hub company. The valuation is done in the portfolio’s own company. The trades created in the portfolio’s own company will also be included in the valuation.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section defines the configuration required for the Hub processing.

The tables below need to be configured appropriately to enable the Hub processing.

The file classification of SEC.ACC.MASTER is 'Cus' type, and Customer Company should be shared between the hub company and the portfolio's own company. In the COMPANY record of each company, the Hub Company field is populated with the ID of the hub where the central processing takes place.

When creating portfolios in the respective portfolio’s own company in SEC.ACC.MASTER , the Port Comp ID field should hold the ID of the hub company where securities and derivatives orders need to be placed.

With this setup in place, the system allows securities and derivatives orders and trades to be placed only in the hub company of the portfolio and not in the portfolio’s own company.

If there are exceptions where orders need to be placed in the portfolio’s own company, the SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM table should be configured. Any transaction that satisfies the rules in SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM are allowed in the portfolio’s own company and not in the hub company.

> **⚠️ Note:** The key requirement in the Hub processing is SECURITY.POSITION with the same key that is not being duplicated in the hub and portfolio’s own company.

The SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM table defines the conditions for securities transactions to be booked in the portfolio’s own company instead of the hub company. The exception rules are defined in SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM based on the fields in SECURITY.MASTER , DX.CONTRACT.MASTER and CUSTOMER . If the conditions defined in SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM match with the corresponding values in SEC.OPEN.ORDER , SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER , DX.ORDER , and DX.TRADE , then the transactions are booked in the portfolio’s own company, else it is booked in the hub company.

The central hub processing rules for the securities and derivatives transactions are given below:

- Customer Company should be shared between Port Comp ID and Own Comp ID in the respective COMPANY .
- @ID of SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM is *SC or *DX.

The table below defines the fields used in SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM .

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Company | System-defaulted value based on @ID |
| Application | System-defaulted value based on @ID . The following are the possible values: SC DX |
| App File | Specifies the applications for defining the conditions based on which order or trade will be created in portfolio’s own company. It is the start of the multi-value field. It is a multi-value field with the following values: SECURITY.MASTER DX.CONTRACT.MASTER CUSTOMER If ID is *SC, SECURITY.MASTER and CUSTOMER are allowed. If ID is *DX, DX.CONTRACT.MASTER and CUSTOMER are allowed. |
| App Field | Specifies any field from the application defined in the App File field |
| App Operand | Specifies the value of the operand. The following are the possible values: EQ NE |
| App Value | Specifies the field value defined in App Field |
| Joints | Specifies the conditions that can be defined using the combination of fields from SECURITY.MASTER and CUSTOMER or DX.CONTRACT.MASTER and CUSTOMER . The following are the possible values: And Blank denotes OR |

The SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM table can be configured based on any fields from the following combinations:

- SECURITY.MASTER or DX.CONTRACT.MASTER
- CUSTOMER and SECURITY.MASTER
- CUSTOMER and DX.CONTRACT.MASTER

If any of the conditions are met, then the transaction will be allowed in the portfolio’s own company and not in the hub company.

| Field | Value |

| App File 1 | SECURITY.MASTER |
| App Field 1 | SECURITY.DOMICILE |
| App Operand 1 | EQ |
| App Value 1 | CA |
| Joints 1 |  |
| App File 2 | SECURITY.MASTER |
| App Field 2 | SUB.ASSET.TYPE |

| App Operand 3 | EQ |

| Joints 3 |  |

| Joints 5 |  |

It should be noted that SECURITY.POSITION key should be unique across the companies for the same portfolio-instrument combination. The same position key cannot exist in two companies. When the same portfolio can hold positions in the hub company and the portfolio’s company for the same instrument, the depository ID or sub-account ID should be different in the respective trades in both companies.

For example, the hub company uses Clearstream as depository for the instrument 100041-000, and the portfolio's own company also uses Clearstream as depository for the instrument 100041-000. Then, either separate customer records for Clearstream need to be opened and use one for the hub company and the other for the portfolio’s own company or set up different sub-accounts and routing conditions in both cases.


##### Setting up to Route Orders from WealthSuite FO (TAP)

When the securities and derivatives orders are placed in the portfolio’s own company in WealthSuite FO (TAP), it is routed to the correct company automatically in Temenos Transact based on the rules defined in SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM . This is performed by an OFS intercept.

In the PGM.FILE of Temenos Transact applications, SEC.OPEN.ORDER and DX.ORDER , the Additional Info field should contain ‘.STHCOMP’ as highlighted in the below screenshot.

The OFS.SOURCE record used by WealthSuiteFO (TTI) should include Attribute set as COMPANY.SWITCH.


#### 🔧 Working With

The securities and derivatives transactions are created and executed in the hub company. As a result of this, the securities and derivatives position, settlement, and corporate actions are created in the hub company. The valuation can run only from the portfolio’s own company.


##### Routing Orders Automatically to Correct Company

The securities or derivatives orders from WealthSuite FO (TAP) are routed to the correct company in Temenos Transact automatically based on rules defined in SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM . This is perfomed through OFS intercept. Read OFS intercept for more information.

In the case of manual input in Temenos Transact, the system checks SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM and an error is raised if the transaction should not take place in that company.

For example, the system raises an error when a transaction is manually input in portfolio’s own company for a security which can only be transacted at the hub company.


##### Portfolio Valuation Inclusion of Positions Created in Portfolio’s Own Company

When SC.VAL.COST enquiry is run for a portfolio in the portfolio's own company, the valuation includes all the securities and derivatives positions of the portfolio, which are created in the portfolio's own company in addition to the positions created in the hub company.

For example, trades placed in the hub company – DXTRA093572FVWM, DXTRA0935795GPD and trades placed in the portfolio’s own company – DXTRA093575KQS1. The screenshot below shows the valuation of all three trades.


##### Processing of OTC Securities and Derivatives Trades

The processing happens as explained in the section below for OTC securities and derivatives trades.

| Scenario | PORT.COMP.ID (Hub) | OWN.COMP.ID (portfolio's own company) |
|---|---|---|
| Customer buy VS Dealer book sell | Trade 1 - Customer buy VS Internal broker sell | Trade 2 - Dealer book sell VS Internal broker buy |
| Customer sell VS Dealer book buy | Trade 1 - Customer sell VS Internal broker buy | Trade 2 - Dealer book buy VS Internal broker sell |

In the case of derivatives, it is possible to ensure that all OTC trades are always booked in the portfolio’s own company. The following are the possible values set for Otc Own Comp ID in DX.PARAMETER :

- Y - Any OTC trade involving an OTC instrument, which is identified through Exchange Type as OTC in DX.CONTRACT.MASTER is always allowed only in the customer portfolio’s own company. The system does not check for SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM rules in this case.
- Null - The system checks for the rules defined in SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM . If the conditions match, the trade is created in the customer portfolio’s own company, else it is created in the hub company.

When an FX Option is exercised, the underlying FOREX trade is created in the company where the trade is created. When an equity option is exercised or assigned, the underlying SEC.TRADE can be created either in the hub company or the portfolio’s own company based on the conditions in SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM .


###### Underlying Created in Hub

If the underlying Security Master (SM) does not match any rules in SC.HUB.PROCESS.PARAM , then the SEC.TRADE for the customer leg needs to be created in the hub company, whereas the SEC.TRADE for the own book leg will be created in the portfolio's own company. The system therefore creates two SEC.TRADE , one in the hub company between customer portfolio and internal broker and the other in dealer books own company between dealer book and internal broker.

The custodian or depository of each company needs to be informed through the settlement messages from respective companies to move positions amongst them. The settlement messages (MT54n) should have the Standard Settlement Instructions (SSI) of the other company, that is, the settlement message from the own company should have the SSI details of the hub and the message from the hub should have the SSI details of the portfolio's own company. To handle this, separate internal brokers are created for each company in the hub and an internal broker representing the hub has to be created in the individual entity companies. The internal broker details are parameterised company-wise in SC.PARAMETER .

In SC.PARAMETER record corresponding to the hub company, the internal broker details corresponding to other companies are defined. Similarly in SC.PARAMETER record corresponding to portfolio's own company, the internal broker details corresponding to the hub company are defined.

For example, in SC.PARAMETER ID, 'CH0010001' (hub), the Entity , Entity Broker , and Entity Int Categ fields for each entity are configured.

Similarly in SC.PARAMETER record ID 'DB0010001', the Entity , Entity Broker , and Entity Int Categ fields of the hub are configured.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Entity | Defines Company ID corresponding to other leg of the trade. It is the start of the multi-value set |
| Entity Broker | Stores the internal broker ID corresponding to Entity . It should be a valid CUSTOMER.SECURITY with customer type as Broker |
| Entity Int Categ | Stores the category of internal account corresponding to Entity Broker . It is the end of the multi-value set |

Consider the below set up in SC.PARAMETER .

|  | CH0010001 (Hub) | GB0010001 | DB0010001 | SG0010001 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Entity 1 | DB0010001 | CH0010001 | CH0010001 | CH0010001 |
| Entity Broker 1 | 2050 | 1041 | 1041 | 1041 |
| Entity Int Categ 1 |  |  |  |  |
| Entity 1 | SG0010001 |  |  |  |
| Entity Broker 1 | 2051 |  |  |  |
| Entity Int Categ 1 |  |  |  |  |
| Entity 1 | GB0010001 |  |  |  |
| Entity Broker 1 | 2052 |  |  |  |
| Entity Int Categ 1 |  |  |  |  |

The following field values are set based on the above table:

- Port Comp ID of the customer portfolio is CH0010001
- Own Comp ID is DB0010001
- Dealer book Own Comp ID is DB0010001

When SEC.TRADE is created in CH0010001 for the customer portfolio in the hub company, the system reads Own Comp ID of the customer portfolio, which is DB0010001, default Entity Broker (2050), and Entity Int Categ corresponding to DB0010001 Entity defined in SC.PARAMETER record 'CH0010001'.

On the opposite leg for the 'Dealer book VS Internal broker' in the Dubai entity, Entity (CH0010001) is read in SC.PARAMETER record 'DB0010001' and corresponding Entity Broker (1041) and Entity Int Categ are defaulted.

The buyer account or seller account is read from Sub Acc Ext Id of the sub account, defaulted in the opposite leg of the trade, and is updated in Buyr Seller Ac in the respective trade. DX.TRADE reference is stored in the respective SEC.TRADE . In DX.TRADE , the respective SEC.TRADE IDs are stored with the company mnemonic.

Buyr Seller Ac is mapped from Sub Acc Ext ID defined in SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT of dealer book in DB0010001 (portfolio's own company).

Buyr Seller Ac is mapped from Sub Acc Ext ID defined in SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT of customer portfolio in CH0010001 (hub company).

There are no Tasks available for the Central Hub Processing feature.
