### 5.36  Coupon Calculation for Bonds


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A coupon is the annual interest rate paid on the bond generally expressed as a percentage of face value and paid until maturity. These coupons can be fixed for the entire bond period or may vary at specific intervals depending upon the underlying bond or instrument issued.*
> 
> **Applications:** `PERIODIC.INTEREST`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.TRANSFER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Abs Index Issue*, *Application Inflation Index*, *Bond or Share*, *Buid Coupon Date*, *Build Coupon Date*, *Business Centres*, *Cap Rate*, *Coupon Fix Date* ... +41 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A coupon is the annual interest rate paid on the bond generally expressed as a percentage of face value and paid until maturity. These coupons can be fixed for the entire bond period or may vary at specific intervals depending upon the underlying bond or instrument issued.

There are different kinds of bonds available in the market. They are primarily distinguished based on the kind of coupon offered as follows:

- Zero coupon bonds do not pay any interest to the investor
- Fixed rate bonds continue to pay the same rate of interest until maturity
- Floating rate bonds have variable interest rates that reset periodically

This document explains how Temenos Transact achieves the different coupon setups required for interest calculation of bonds.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Bonds are opened as instruments in the SECURITY.MASTER application. The SECURITY.MASTER setup is one time and does not require user intervention mostly. For example, fixed rate bonds require less maintenance once a new record is authorised. In case of the fixed rate bonds, the system automatically updates the last and next coupon dates using the frequency indicator to build the new coupon period details. The setup for coupons works only if the Bond or Share field is set to B (Bond).

Read the Instrument Master for more information about setting up a record in SECURITY.MASTER .


#### 🔧 Working With

Temenos Transact uses a very high-level indicator to differentiate bond and share paper types within the SECURITY.MASTER application. The amount and type of information required to build a complete record in SECURITY.MASTER depends on the indicator selected.


##### Fixed Rate Bonds

A fixed rate bond is a bond that pays the same rate of interest over its entire term. The below screen shot shows a record in SECURITY.MASTER with respect to fixed rate bond having equal coupons every year. These bonds have the same rate of interest until maturity.

Read the Interest Basis section in the System Tables Configuration Guide for more information on the Interest days basis supported including the Brazilian Market method.


##### Floating Rate Bonds

Unlike traditional bonds that pay a fixed rate of interest, floating rate bonds have a variable rate that resets periodically.

Temenos Transact can process floating rate bonds, where the coupon rate is typically linked to a benchmark rate such as the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR). The rate of interest in such bonds is reset at specified intervals to change with the movements in the benchmark rate. The setting up of a security for a floating rate bond is different from that of a standard bond.

The following screenshot of a record in SECURITY.MASTER illustrates the fields for setting up the floating rate bonds.

By multi-valuing the Interest Rate and Rate Changed Date fields in the SECURITY.MASTER application, the user can capture applicable rates and future dated rate changes until the maturity of the bond.

The applicable rate of interest from 03 February 2020 is 4.13%, which is applicable till 02 March 2020. The new rate from 03 March 2020 will be 3% as defined in the above screenshot.

In this method, users can capture the new rate change dates and new rates as and when a COB report notifies them. Manual input of dates and rate of interest is a tedious task. It is possible to build the rate change cycle information automatically to avoid manual input of dates and rates. To achieve this, the following fields must be set up in SECURITY.MASTER .

If the Coupon Method field is set to Standard, the system automatically builds the rate change cycle. If this field is set to Null, the rate change cycle needs to be entered manually. The value in the Build Coupon Date field is the starting point for the rate change date. This field indicates whether to populate adjusted date or non-adjusted date in the Rate Changed Date field depending upon the business day. The first two characters in the Build Coupon Date field should be equal to the first two characters in the Interest Payment Date . Depending on the value in the No of Payments field, the system calculates the next Rate Changed Date value.

While calculating the next Rate Changed Date , the system also checks if it is a favorable business day only if the Build Coupon Date field has the value 01ADJ.

If the

field is set to 01ADJ, then the system checks if it is a favorable business day by checking the record in the

application corresponding to the country specified in the

field. Further, the system considers the value specified in the

field to arrive at the best estimate of the next

value. This derived value is automatically populated in the

(multi-valued) and

fields.

After specifying the dates, the user must specify the interest rates for the reset by choosing the appropriate record key in in the Interest Key field in the PERIODIC.INTEREST application. The Rate Selection field allows the user to choose either the Bid or Offer rate from the record in PERIODIC.INTEREST . The user can further specify a spread (if required) in the Coupon Rate Spread field that increases or decreases the all-in-rate for the bond. Then, the appropriate rate of interest applicable to the bond is updated from the record in PERIODIC.INTEREST .

In the SECURITY.MASTER application, the interest payments are 12, that is, monthly, and the user has specified the BID rate to be chosen with a positive spread of 22.5 basis points. Therefore, the system picks up the bid rate corresponding to the Rest Period of 01M, which is 0.69175% and then adds the spread of 22.5 basis points that computes to an all-in-rate of 0.91675%. The same value is displayed in the third multi-value Interest Rate field.

> **⚠️ Note:** As the PERIODIC.INTEREST table is effective from April 1 2020, the first two interest rates shown in the below screenshot are obtained from an earlier record in PERIODIC.INTEREST .

This rate is populated in the Interest Rate field by the COB job that checks the Coupon Fix Date field to determine the lead-time required for the new rate reset. The value of 33 in the Coupon Fix Date field notifies the system to check for a new reset rate 33 days before the Rate Changed Date value. If the Coupon Method field is set as SIMPLE or COMPOUND, the system allows coupon changes within the interest period. As per the normal functionality, if the rate changes within the coupon period, the revised rate is applied for the entire interest period.

If the interest period is from 1 January to 31 March and the interest changes on 1 March, then the revised rate is applied for the interest period from 1 January. However, if the Coupon Method field is set to either SIMPLE or COMPOUND, the rate applicable for the period from 1 January to 28 February is the old rate and the new rate is applied from 1 March.

There is a facility to compound the interest calculations wherein the interest is applied (considering the above example) from 1 March. It is computed using the new rate on the principal and interest accrued from 1 January to 28 February. When the Coupon Method field is set to either SIMPLE or COMPOUND, the Rate Change Elapse field becomes mandatory. This field defines the frequency in which rate change from periodic interest needs to be automatically updated.

Though the interest is paid semiannually, the Interest Rate is changed based on the Rate Change Elapse field. As the Elapse Days field is set as one day, the rate change happens on everyday COB.


##### RFR Coupon Rate Calculation

The coupon rates for securities such as floating rate bonds are calculated using benchmark rates such as LIBOR.

The interest spread depends on the risk and other factors but kept fixed throughout the life of the bond. At the end of each period, that is, on the payment date, the coupon rate for the next period is calculated based on the existing benchmark rate at that time.

As a replacement of LIBOR, banks are moving towards the alternative Risk-Free Rates (RFR) or near risk-free overnight rates which are fundamentally different from the Interbank Offered Rates (IBORs). If the coupon rate is to be derived based on the RFR, then the Coupon Method field in SECURITY.MASTER should be set to RFR.

RFRs are backward looking rates without any forward term or tenor or credit risk associated with time embedded. RFRs are compounded daily until a final rate is fixed at the end of the contract as opposed to LIBOR that are currently available at the beginning of each interest period.

The RFRs are computed based on the characteristic defined for the instrument. Hence, the RFR-related characteristics are captured at the security level in SECURITY.MASTER . The Rfr Convention , Rfr Lag Days , Rfr Lookback Lag Days , Rfr Calc Method , Rfr Adj Spread and Rfr Rounding fields in SECURITY.MASTER capture the RFR characteristics of the instrument.

The Rfr Convention field holds the market convention for processing the risk-free rates. The values allowed are:

| Field Values | Description |
|---|---|
| Lock Out | Indicates the daily compound averaging of RFRs with last N days set as lockout days. If contract matures on 30th of a particular month, with lockout period of 5 days, the system takes the rate available on 25th and use it for each subsequent day until maturity. Assume if the rate on 25th is 0.85%, then on 26th, 27th, 28th, 29th and 30th the rate is 0.85% (assuming no holidays in between). |
| Look Back | Indicates the daily averaging of historical RFRs with a lag of N days set as lookback days to arrive at the average rate applicable for a given interest period, that is, for every day in the current interest period, the RFR rate from k days earlier is used. |
| Lookback With Lockout | This is a combination of lock out and look back. |
| Plain Arrears | Indicates the daily averaging of RFRs, that is, system takes the rate available as on date of the interest period. |
| Reset Cut Off | Indicates the daily simple averaging of RFRs with last N days set as cut-off days. This uses the last RFR available in the averaging. |

The Rfr Lag Days and Rfr Lookback Lag Days fields hold the number of lockout and look back days respectively. Lookback market convention can be of two types. The Rfr Look Back Type field indicates the type of lookback method applied for rate compounding or averaging. It has the following types for rate calculations:

- Narrow Definition – Uses the original interest period day count with lookback rate.

If Wednesday rate is used for Friday, apply the Friday’s weight (three days) to the Wednesday’s rate.

- Observation Shift – Uses the original day count of the lookback rate.

If Wednesday rate is used for Friday, apply the Wednesday’s weight (one day) to the Wednesday’s rate.

The Rfr Calc Method field denotes the calculation methods for RFR averaging. The values allowed are Simple and Compound. The Rfr Spread Ind field indicates the spread treatment methods during the RFR averaging. The values allowed are:

- Spread Inclusive - Uses the spread within the averaging calculation along with daily rates.
- Spread Exclusive - Adds the spread separately after RFR averaging is done.

The spread rate to be applied on the benchmark rate in order to arrive at the final coupon rate is given in the Rfr Adj Spread field. The Rfr Rounding field provides the rounding level of the calculated risk-free rate. The Rfr Negative Rate field indicates whether the flooring is applicable. The possible values are:

- YES - Negative rates are allowed and no flooring is applied.
- NO – a zero floor is applied on the overall Interest rate if the overall rate is below zero. For RFR deals, this is a total rate floor applied on the average risk-free rate plus spread.
- DAILY – If the risk-free rate published each business day is below zero, a zero floor is applied and taken for rate averaging.
- AVERAGE - a zero floor applied on the average Risk-Free Rate; for Spread-Exclusive margin treatment, whenever the average Risk-Free Rate is below zero, the rate calculation routine applies a floor on it and returns only the spread.

Based on the characteristics set in SECURITY.MASTER , the securities module passes the following details to the Term rate calculating routine which returns the RFR rate. The values passed from Securities are:

- RFR convention (Plain Arrears, Look Back, Lock Out, Reset Cut Off, Lookback With Lockout)
- Interest key
- RFR Lag Days
- RFR Look Back Type (Narrow or Observation Shift)
- RFR Calculation Method (Compound or Simple)
- RFR Adjustment Spread
- RFR Rounding

The RFR is calculated based on the ID of PERIODIC.INTEREST table mentioned in the Interest Key field (in SECURITY.MASTER ) and the RFR characteristics defined for the instrument. Based on the RFR and the spread, the coupon rate for the instrument is deduced. The coupon payment for the next payment date is based on the new coupon rate calculated and the face value of the bond.


##### Bond with Factors

Temenos Transact can process certain securities with additional pricing factors. These bonds include mortgage-backed securities (MBS) and Brady bonds, which includes Brazilian C bonds and others. MBS includes issues such as Government National Mortgage Association (GNMA), also known as GINNIE Mae. To allow the processing requirements of the Ginnie Mae securities, the following processes take place in:

- capability of partial redemption
- capability of being able to factor-down the consideration calculated
- capability of being able to factor-down the interest calculated
- capability of being able to factor-down the valuation amount

In the SECURITY.MASTER application, the Factor field enables the specification of historical and current factors. In addition to the specification of the factor, Brady bonds such as Brazilian C securities require a capitalisation rate. To allow the processing requirements of Brazilian C bond, the following processes take place in:

- ability to calculate the capitalised interest and coupon interest accrued upon specification of a capitalisation rate for bonds
- ability to factor-up the consideration calculated
- ability to factor-up the interest calculated
- ability to factor-up the valuation amount

The setting up of a security for bonds with factors is different from that of a standard bond for which a factor is a part of the pricing process. When the Cpn Rate field is given, the Interest Rate field becomes a no input field. Any value provided in the Interest Rate field is overwritten using the value in the Cpn Rate field.

The above screenshot helps the user to set up a Ginnie Mae or most other mortgage-backed paper for which a factor and a current interest rate are required. The Cpn Date field stores the application from date. The user must enter the data in such a way that the latest details are always displayed first (that is, in descending date order).

In case of Brady type securities, the capitalisation rate must be provided for the current period. The user must also record the historical rates, which may be required to enter any back-value trades. The following screenshot displays a typical Brazilian C bond with user-specified coupon date, coupon, capitalisation and factor rate values.

This particular security type should include the Cap Rate value, which distinguishes factor bonds from ordinary bonds, if the Factor field is set. The value in the Cap Rate field advises whether the security is a Brady bond type or not. If this field is blank, the security is assumed to be a mortgage-backed security.


##### Inflation-Indexed Bonds

There are two types of inflation-linked bonds with inflation factors:

- Bonds with inflation index applied to the coupon rate or interest Bonds with an inflation index applied to the coupon rate are effectively inflation-linked products that offer a premium rate to issued coupon rate. This premium that is added to the issued coupon rate is based on an inflation index. For example, a bond issued with a coupon rate of 1% with a current inflation index of 3%. The coupon rate applied to the nominal amount is 4% (original coupon rate + inflation index).
- Bonds with inflation index applied to the nominal amount If an annual coupon of a nominal bond was 5% and the underlying principal of this bond was USD100, the annual coupon payment is USD5. In the case of an inflation-linked bond, if the inflation index increases by 75% over the life of the bond, the principal of the bond increases to USD100 x 175% = USD175.

> **⚠️ Note:** The inflation index period should be same as bond coupon periods and should be updated manually. Inflation index is not allowed for bonds with a factor set (mortgage-backed securities).

The below screenshot shows a record in SECURITY.MASTER for an inflation-indexed bond. The Inflation Index is linked to the bond coupon period specified in the Cpn Date field. The Application Inflation Index field helps to determine whether the inflation index has to be applied on principal only (final maturity amount), interest (accrued interest or coupon payments) or both. If this field is set blank, then it is assumed that the inflation index is to be used for both principal and interest.


##### Recording the Index for a Linked Bond

The inflation index for each period needs to be entered as a factor of base index in SC.INDEX.LINK application and not in SECURITY.MASTER .

An inflation bond is issued on December 31, 2018 and the inflation (Consumer Price Index (CPI)) at the time of issue of the bond is 110. This is considered as the base index. In the

application, the base inflation index (on the issue date) is always 1. If the inflation index is received as 125 after one month, that is, on January 31, 2018, the inflation index is entered as a factor of the base index. In

, the index on January 31, 2019 is entered as 1.13636 (125/110).

The application is at the SECURITY.MASTER level. Whenever the index changes, a new record is created in this table which is associated with an effective date. The fields are displayed as below:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Id | Indicates the ID is SECURITY.MASTER ID * Index Eff Date |
| Index Eff Date | Specifies the effective date given in the ID is defaulted in this field |
| Index Factor | Specifies the index factor which is used for all the transactions that occur on or after the effective date is given here |
| Abs Index Issue | Holds the absolute inflation value at the time of issue of the instrument This is a display only field. |

Consider three records in the application as below:

- 100046-000*20181231
- 100046-000*20190131
- 100046-000*20190228

If a transaction happens on January 14, 2019 for the instrument 100046-000, the system takes the index defined in the 100046-000*20181231 record.

The Application Inflation Index field in SECURITY.MASTER must be set to Both for applying the inflation index to both principal and accrued interest. In the following scenarios, it is possible to protect the linked bond with floor index and cap index.

- If the current inflation index ( Index Factor ) goes above the cap index, the cap index is used for generating the inflation linkage entries for both principal and accrued interest.
- If the current inflation index ( Index Factor ) goes below the floor index, the floor index is used for generating the inflation linkage entries for both principal and accrued interest.

The Link Floor Index and Link Cap Index fields in SECURITY.MASTER are used to protect the linked bond with floor index and cap index.

> **⚠️ Note:** The index available in SC.INDEX.LINK takes precedence over the index available in SECURITY.MASTER .


###### Separating Linkage Entries for Inflation Linked Bonds for Own Book Portfolios

For linked securities (Inflation index bonds) held in own book portfolios, the linkage accounting entries (due to changes in the inflation index) can be separately posted to different categories for the principal amount and interest or coupon amount. In order to separate the linkage entries in an inflation lined bond:

- The Multi Linkage field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Yes.
- The Split Link Entry field is set to Yes in SEC.ACC.MASTER for the own book portfolio.
- The below fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER are used to setup the categories to post the inflation linkage entries for principal and interest: Infl Intr Dr Cat Infl Intr Cr Cat Infl Prin Dr Cat Infl Prin Cr Cat

| Entries | Amount | Debit/ Credit |
|---|---|---|
| Principal | USD 109,523.81 | Debit Customer |
| Inflation linkage on Principal | USD 5,476.19 | Debit Customer |
| Accrued Interest | USD 205.48 | Debit Customer |
| Inflation linkage on Accrued Interest | USD 10.27 | Debit Customer |
| Broker side entry | USD 115,215.75 | Credit Broker |

Whenever daily accrued interest entries are generated (during COB):

- The accrued interest is split for the accrued interest portion (calculated from the accrual start date till current day) and the inflation portion and posted as two separate entries.
- The credit entry split for accrued interest is posted to the category in the Int Recd Cat field. The credit entry for the inflation component of accrued interest is posted to Infl Intr Cr Cat .
- The inflation linkage is applied on the accrued interest calculated based on the latest available inflation index.

The entry for accrued interest calculated during COB is posted as the difference between accrued interest from accrual start date to current day and accrued interest posted before current day’s COB.

The entry for inflation on accrued interest calculated during COB is posted as the difference between inflation linkages on the calculated accrued interest from accrual start date to current and inflation posted before today COB.

Where the Split Link Entry in SEC.ACC.MASTER is set to Yes, an additional principal linkage entry is raised during COB.

Where, price denotes the clean price of the bond. It is stored in the Cur Cost Position field in SC.TRADING.POSITION . The Net Cost Position field in SC.TRADING.POSITION stores the net cost of the position (less accrued interest) unadjusted for inflation. This is calculated as:

During COB, the principal linkage difference entry is calculated based on the difference between the value in the Net Cost Position field adjusted based on latest inflation index and the value in the Cur Cost Position field is posted as principal linkage difference to the respective Profit & Loss (P/L) category for principal ( Infl Prin Cr Cat ).

where, the value in the Inflation Index field is the latest value available inflation index in SC.INDEX.LINK .

> **⚠️ Note:** The debit entry of principal linkage difference is posted to the LIVEDB category and the credit is posted to Infl Prin Cr Cat . If the inflation index does not change, the same discount amount is posted every day. If the inflation index changes, the discount posted is different for each day. The daily discount debit is posted to the P/L category defined in Discount Category field in SEC.ACC.MASTER of the existing own book portfolio. The above discount processing is done only for straight line method of discount processing.

During coupon event, the coupon amount receivable is adjusted based on the latest available inflation index. In the below screenshot the various entries (accrued interest, inflation on accrued interest, discount entries and principal entries) are posted as separate entries to specific categories.

where, the inflation index is the index on the coupon date.

The accounting entry is posted as a single entry, that is, split is not done for inflation and actual coupon separately. On the coupon payment date from ENTITLEMENT application, the category defined for coupon receivable ( Cpn Receivable Cat in SEC.ACC.MASTER ) is credited with the coupon amount including the inflation and the broker nostro is debited for the same. The debit entries posted during COB for the accrued interest and inflation are reversed. During maturity or redemption (or during sale of the bond), the holdings in the bond reduces partially or fully. The net cost (accrued interest sold for the quantity redeemed or sold) is calculated posted at the time of sale. In case of redemption or maturity events, the redemption amount is calculated as follows:

where, the inflation index is the inflation index at the time of redeeming the bond.

### 5.37  Crypto Assets


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Crypto assets are a digital representation of value that can be transferred, stored, or traded electronically. This includes cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, NFTs and so on.*
> 
> **Applications:** `ASSET.TYPE`, `CURRENCY`, `CUSTOMER`, `CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `EB.OBJECT`, `SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT`, `SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS`, `SC.SETTLEMENT` ... +8 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Block Chain*, *Blocking Date*, *Blocking Narr*, *Crypto Asset*, *Cust No Nom*, *Customer Type*, *Default Depo*, *Default Depository* ... +8 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Crypto assets are a digital representation of value that can be transferred, stored, or traded electronically. This includes cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, NFTs and so on.

Crypto assets use:

- Cryptography to protect digital data
- Distributed ledger technology to record transactions

Crypto assets may run on their own blockchain or use an existing platform such as Ethereum. A blockchain is a form of secure digital ledger used to store a record of crypto transactions.

Though blockchains are termed as currencies, crypto coins or tokens, they are generally treated as assets and not monies by most regulators. In Temenos Transact, cryptocurrencies are modelled as security instruments associated with their blockchain that is defined as a Depository.

Temenos Transact allows the following:

- Capturing cryptocurrency orders
- Executions
- Trades

- Temenos Transact does not handle any validation or life cycle processing.
- The terms crypto assets and cryptocurrencies are used interchangeably in this user guide.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section defines the required configuration to process cryptocurrencies in Temenos Transact.


##### Handling Crypto Precision

The cryptocurrencies are traded with high precision to a maximum of 18 decimal places. In Temenos Transact, the precision is handled for all nominal values, since cryptocurrencies are modelled as security instruments.

Temenos Transact supports this high precision with a configuration in EB.OBJECT . A record with ID as NOMINAL.FIELD is created in the EB.OBJECT application. When this configuration is available, the system supports extended decimal places (up to 18) in any nominal fields of securities transactions. The value in Max Length will be the total number of digits that will be supported by the NOMINAL.FIELD, including 18 digits of decimal.

The Max Length field defined in the NOMINAL.FIELD record overrides the one defined in STANDARD.SELECTION of the respective application.

The extended precision will be applied to Trading Units in SECURITY.MASTER , No Nominal in SEC.OPEN.ORDER , Cust No Nom in SEC.TRADE and all the fields that are defined as nominal in STANDARD.SELECTION .

> **⚠️ Note:** The default precision in the TAFJ properties file is updated to 18 to support the high precision of crypto trading. temn.tafj.runtime.default.precision=18


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the processing of crypto transactions in Temenos Transact.


##### Creating Blockchain

Cypto assets are closely linked to a blockchain. Each blockchain is created as a depository.

To create blockchain as depository in Temenos Transact,

1. Create a record in CUSTOMER .
2. Go to CUSTOMER.SECURITY . Set Customer Type as Depository. Set Block Chain as Yes.


##### Whitelisting or Creating New Cryptocurrency

The whitelist is a term used to introduce a new crypto asset for trading in the blockchain and cryptocurrency space. Temenos Transact defines the crypto assets for the customers to hold positions in them. In Temenos Transact, whitelisting a new crypto asset refers to creating the crypto asset as a new security instrument in SECURITY.MASTER . To create a crypto asset,

1. Go to SECURITY.MASTER .
2. Set Security Currency and Price Currency (conventional currency) as USD.
3. Enter the Default Depository as a blockchain depository to link the crypto instrument with the blockchain where it is traded.
4. Select a value in Crypto Asset . The following are the possible values: Native – The crypto asset is a blockchain’s own coin. In other terms, the crypto asset being traded is a blockchain itself. For example, Ether (ETH) on Ethereum. Non.Native - The crypto asset is any other coin or token listed under the blockchain. For example, LINK on Ethereum.


##### Blacklisting Crypto Asset

Blacklisting a crypto asset means disabling the asset from trading. This is achieved by updating the respective crypto asset's Blocking Date and Blocking Narr in SECURITY.MASTER .


##### Creating Wallets

A wallet address is created when the assets are held for trading in crypto assets. The wallets are classified in to:

- Omnibus - The omnibus wallet is defined as a sub-account under the respective blockchain depository in CUSTOMER.SECURITY . The Sub Acc Ext Id field holds the wallet address.
- Segregated – The segregated wallet is created as a separate portfolio in SEC.ACC.MASTER or multiple crypto wallets are linked to the same portfolio.

The wallets are modelled as sub-accounts in Temenos Transact and set accordingly. Read Depository-Omnibus and Segregated accounts for more information.

A wallet is created as a sub-account under the blockchain depository. A separate wallet address can be created for native and non-native assets of a blockchain. Temenos Transact supports the following scenarios:

- A separate portfolio per blockchain can be maintained
- All assets can be maintained in a single portfolio

To create a customer wallet in Temenos Transact,

1. Go to SEC.ACC.MASTER .
2. Enter the values in the following fields. Blockchain ID in Default Depo Internal sub-account in Sub Account (accept up to 35 characters) Wallet ID in Sub Acc Ext Id (accept upto 110 characters)

The screenshot below shows two separate wallet address updated for Native and Non-native assets of a blockchain depository ETHEREUM.

Bank creates their own wallet to hold their assets like customer wallet. This is used to pay the network fees by creating a dummy customer record (say 999999) for the bank and updating the wallet address in the own book portfolio.


##### Processing Crypto Assets Transaction

This section defines the transactions that are performed using crypto assets.

> **⚠️ Note:** Crypto precision should be set as explained in the configuration section before processing the crypto transactions in the system.

The buy or sell orders are created using the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application in Temenos Transact. The trade currency is a regulated currency such as USD, EUR and so on. The fill or execution is updated in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS and the trades are completed in SEC.TRADE . Temenos Transact allows capturing cryptocurrency orders, executions, and trades. Temenos Transact supports the settlement process post trade creation for the buy or sell of crypto. The securities leg settlement is expected to be actual for crypto processing which creates a record in SC.SETTLEMENT . However, there is no validation and contractual settlement is also possible.

In SEC.TRADE of Crypto Asset, the depository needs to be a blockchain depository. The SEC.TRADE is set as Free of Payment (FOP) trade, since cash settlement is expected to happen separately. The transaction’s wallet address is populated in the Sub Acc Ext Id field of SEC.TRADE . The wallet address should be defined in SEC.ACC.MASTER or SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT or in CUSTOMER.SECURITY (Omnibus) for it to be defaulted in the transaction.

The trade details are exposed to the external system (for interfacing) through an Integration Framework (IF) event setup for the SEC.TRADE with the required field mapping. When this setup is available, the system creates an IF event as and when the trade is committed for a crypto asset.

The settlement confirmation of trades can be shared from the external system (through IRIS API or direct interface mapping). This includes quantity, date, time, transaction reference (trade reference), wallet address, order reference, and so on. Provided all details are available, the SC.SETTLEMENT can be completed automatically.

Crypto transactions have inherent network fees that must be paid in the native asset. This fee varies for each transaction as it is dependent on the network traffic during the time of the transaction.

The fees are charged in the trade currency in Temenos Transact. The crypto assets are not supported as currencies in Temenos Transact but as instruments. The trade currency is a standard currency set in the CURRENCY table for crypto orders and transactions. The fees are calculated and debited from the customer in this currency. However, the network fees are paid in the native currency of the blockchain. Bank collects fees from the customer in trade currency and parks it in an internal account to handle it. Bank uses the funds to acquire native crypto assets in its own book and the crypto asset to pay the fees.

The purchasing of native crypto using fees collected has to be handled manually. Similarly, payment of fees to the Network, in native crypto has to be handled manually through a security transfer.

Bank charges standard fees in trade currency to the customer for any transaction. The fees can be set up to debit customer accounts and credit any internal account through a multiple-charge setup ( SCDX.CHARGE.PARAMETER ). It is possible to set that the crypto fee (for example, CRYPTO.FEE) can be charged from the customer, only when the instrument traded is a crypto asset. It is done by specifying the ASSET.TYPE or SUB.ASSET.TYPE of crypto asset as a priority while defining charges.

Bank maintains a wallet with every blockchain to pay the network fees in the native asset. When the network fees are calculated either per transaction or periodically, the payment of fees from the bank’s wallet is done outside Temenos Transact and the details of the fees debited are intimated to Temenos Transact along with the bank’s wallet address from which the fee was debited. The user can create a SECURITY.TRANSFER out from the bank’s own book along with the fee reference to ensure that the bank’s position in the crypto asset is maintained appropriately.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Crypto Assets feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Crypto Assets feature.

### 5.38  Customer FX Margin

Market exchange ...*
> 
> **Applications:** `CURRENCY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `FX.COMM.GROUP`, `FX.GEN.CONDITION`, `FX.GROUP.CONDITION`, `SC.PARAMETER`, `SC.STD.POS.TRANSF` ... +5 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Apply Cus Fxmargin*, *Consol Rate*, *Consolidate FX*, *Cu Ex Rate Acc*, *Cu Exch Profit*, *Cu Margin Perc*, *Cu Margin Pips*, *Cu Sys Ex Rate Acc* ... +19 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

When a securities transaction involving FX conversion (trade currency being different from customer’s account currency) is booked, the system applies an FX margin on the treasury rate for the currency conversion and generates market exchange profit and loss (PL) entries accordingly. Market exchange profit is the profit the bank makes in this implicit FX conversion and is the difference between the bank-level treasury rate and customer rate (inclusive of the FX margin) applied on the transaction amount. The system calculates this profit entry and posts it in the local currency.

Banks can offer a different FX margin for different groups of customers, so the margin must be configured based on customer groups. Customer group or customer FX margins for securities transactions are configured in the system using the FX.GROUP.CONDITION application. The SC.PARAMETER application is used to configure the transaction codes for which the customer margin is applied. With these configurations in place, the system calculates the market exchange profit of the transaction based on the FX margin group, the customer belongs to.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configuration required when applying customer margin and calculating market exchange profit.


##### Configuring Customer Margins for Customer Groups in Securities

Customers are grouped using the FX.GEN.CONDITION application. The FX margin percentage for a group of customers is defined using the FX.GROUP.CONDITION application. To define a specific margin for securities transactions, the margin or FX.COMM.GROUP must be configured for the Securities (SC) deal type.

Read Configuring Automatic Defaulting of FX Margin for more information on the configuration of customer or customer group-based margin for SC.


##### Configuring Transaction Codes

Following is the configuration of the transaction codes that require the application of FX spread based on customer groups.

To define the transactions where the customer group-based FX margin is applicable, the bank can parameterize the list of transactions in the Cus Fxmargin Trans Type field in SC.PARAMETER .

This field can be defined in 2 ways:

- Specific transaction codes from SC.TRANS.NAME can be defined as multi-value to apply a customer-specific margin for those specific securities transactions from trade or transfer.
- By setting the Cus Fxmargin Trans Type field to ALL, the system applies customer or customer group-based margins for all securities transactions booked through the SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER applications.

To apply the customer group-based FX margin for corporate action event processing, the Apply Cus Fxmargin field in the DIARY.TYPE application must be set to YES for the respective corporate action event.


##### Configuring PL Category to Post Market Exchange Profit

The below configuration is a pre-requisite to define the PL category and to post the market exchange profit out of the securities transaction.

| Securities Transaction | Parameter Application | Field |
|---|---|---|
| Security Trade | SC.STD.SEC.TRADE | Exchange Pl Cat |
| Security Transfer | SC.STD.POS.TRANSF | Exchange Pl Cat |
| Corporate Action | DIARY.TYPE | Exchange Pl Cat |

The screenshots below show the Exchange Pl Cat field configured in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE , SC.STD.POS.TRANSF and DIARY.TYPE applications.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the application of customer group-based FX margin for securities transactions like Security Trade, Security Transfer, and Corporate Action event processing. The setup for applying customer FX margin must be available as explained in the configuration section.


##### Processing FX Margin for Security Trade, Security Transfer and Corporate Action Events

The system performs the following steps to calculate the FX margin based on customer group, for the transactions involving foreign exchange conversion, that is, when the trade currency is different from the customer account currency.

1. Validates if the configuration to apply customer group-based FX margin exists and this is done using the Cus Fxmargin Trans Type field in SC.PARAMETER for trades and transfers, or the Apply Cus Fxmargin field in DIARY.TYPE for corporate action processing.
2. Derives the customer-level FX rate based on the customer FX spread defined for the customer FX group (customer FX group is updated in the Fx Group Cond Id field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application), treasury rate, and transaction amount, if the securities transactions are eligible for applying customer group-based margin and if the configuration for the SC deal type of FX.GROUP.CONDITION exists. The system derives the value for the following attributes: Margin Percentage (FX spread defined for the group or customer) Margin Pips (Margin Pips = Treasury Rate * Margin Percentage) Customer FX Rate (Customer FX rate = Treasury Rate +/- Margin Pips)
3. Calculates the exchange profit based on this FX conversion and stores it in the Exch Profit field of the security transaction along with Margin Percentage , Margin Pips and Customer FX Rate , using the derived value of these fields.
4. Calculates the exchange profit based on the customer spread (if any) defined in the CURRENCY application, if the configuration of FX margin is missing for the SC deal type in the respective group condition record in the FX.GROUP.CONDITION application.
5. Recalculates the customer FX rate when the Margin Percentage or Treasury Rate at the transaction level is manually modified by the user.
6. For corporate action event processing, the system updates the derived values of the Margin Percentage , Margin Pips and Customer FX Rate fields when the entitlements move to the unauthorised stage (INAU). When the Diary is re-run, the system recalculates the customer FX rate based on the latest available exchange rate.

The table below lists the fields in the SEC.TRADE application used to calculate the FX margin for the transaction.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Cu Treasury Rate | Indicates the bank-level treasury rate between the trade currency and customer account currency. The user can modify this field and the system recalculates the customer FX rate based on the revised value of this field. |
| Cu Margin Perc | Indicates the margin percentage to be applied on the treasury rate to derive the customer FX spread, which is defaulted from FX.GROUP.CONDITION of the respective customer group. The user can modify this field when the customer transaction is eligible to apply customer FX margin based on the Cus Fxmargin Trans Type field in SC.PARAMETER . |
| Cu Sys Margin Perc | Indicates the system-defaulted margin percentage defaulted from FX.GROUP.CONDITION based on the customer group. |
| Cu Margin Pips | Indicates the margin spread which is derived by applying Margin Percentage or Treasury rate . This field derives the customer FX rate between the trade and customer account currency. |
| Cu Ex Rate Acc | Indicates the customer FX rate between the trade currency and the customer account currency. It is recalculated whenever the user modifies the Cu Treasury Rate or Cu Margin Perc fields, provided the customer rate is not manually modified. |
| Cu Sys Ex Rate Acc | Indicates the system-defaulted FX rate between trade currency and customer account currency. |
| Cu Exch Profit | Indicates the market exchange profit derived from FX conversion of the trade currency and customer account currency and is posted in the local currency of the system. |
| Trea Fx Rate | Indicates the bank-level treasury rate between the trade currency and customer account currency field which is stored for parent and child trades. This is allowed for input only in parent trade and not for child trades. The system uses the modified value for the subsequent child trades in the given currency pair. |

The table below lists the fields in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application used to calculate the FX margin for the transaction.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Cu Treasury Rate | Indicates the bank-level treasury rate between the security currency and customer account currency. The system recalculates the customer FX rate based on the revised value in this field whenever the user modifies this field. |
| Cu Margin Perc | Indicates the margin percentage to be applied on the treasury rate to derive the customer FX spread. This is defaulted from FX.GROUP.CONDITION of the respective customer group. The user can modify this field when the customer transaction is eligible to apply customer FX margin based on the Cus Fxmargin Trans Type field in SC.PARAMETER . |
| Cu Sys Margin Perc | Indicates the system-defaulted margin percentage defaulted from FX.GROUP.CONDITION based on the customer group. |
| Cu Margin Pips | Indicates the margin spread derived by applying margin percentage on treasury rate. This field derives the customer FX rate between the security currency and the customer account currency. |
| Cu Ex Rate Acc | Indicates the customer FX rate between the security currency and customer account currency. The system recalculates the FX rate whenever the user modifies the Cu Treasury Rate or Cu Margin Perc provided the customer rate is not manually modified. |
| Cu Sys Ex Rate Acc | Indicates the system-defaulted FX rate between the security currency and customer account currency. |
| Cu Exch Profit | Indicates the market exchange profit derived from FX conversion of the security currency and customer account currency and is posted in the local currency of the system. |

The table below lists the fields in the ENTITLEMENT application used to calculate the FX margin for the transaction.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Treasury Rate | Indicates the bank-level treasury rate between the event currency and customer account currency. The system recalculates the customer FX rate based on the revised value of Treasury Rate whenever the user modifies this field. |
| Margin Perc | Indicates the margin percentage to be applied on treasury rate to derive customer FX spread. This is defaulted from FX.GROUP.CONDITION of the respective customer group. The user can modify this field when the customer FX margin applies to the corporate action event, that is, when the Apply Cus Fxmargin field is set to YES in DIARY.TYPE . |
| Sys Margin Perc | Indicates the system-defaulted margin percentage defaulted from FX.GROUP.CONDITION based on the customer group. |
| Margin Pips | Indicates the margin spread which is derived by applying Margin Percentage on Treasury Rate. This derives the customer FX rate between event currency and customer account currency. |
| Ex Rate Acc | Indicates the customer FX rate between event currency and the customer account currency.The system recalculates the customer FX rate whenever the user modifies the Treasury Rate or Margin Perc , provided the customer rate is not manually modified. |
| Sys Ex Rate Acc | Indicates the system-defaulted FX rate between event currency and customer account currency. |
| Exch Profit | Indicates the market exchange profit derived from FX conversion of the event currency and customer account currency and is posted in the local currency of the system. |

The following workflow describes the application of customer or customer-group-based FX margin for securities transactions.

The following are examples for calculating FX margin:

| Description | Value |

##### Updating Customer Rate when Creating Security Order

Whenever the securities order involving FX conversion (trade currency is different from the customer account currency) is created, the system populates the indicative customer rate in Cu Ex Rate Acc based on the applicability of customer FX margin.


##### Executing Security Orders and Recalculating Customer Exchange Rate in Trade

Whenever a trade is created through order execution, the system defaults the value of the Cu Ex Rate Acc field from the execution to trade. The system then uses this rate to determine the transaction amount in the customer’s account currency. The Recalc Cust Rate field in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE parameter application enables the customer FX rate ( Cu Ex Rate Acc ) to be recalculated in the trade; thus the latest prevailing exchange rate is used to determine the transaction amount in customer’s account currency.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Recalc Cust Rate in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is set to YES | The system clears the value of the Cu Ex Rate Acc field in SEC.TRADE when the creation of SEC.TRADE through order execution. This enables the Cu Ex Rate Acc field to be recalculated based on the latest available exchange rate in the SEC.TRADE application. |
| Recalc Cust Rate in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is set to NULL | The system defaults the value of the Cu Ex Rate Acc field in SEC.TRADE with the one available in the order execution. |


##### Processing Parent-Child Trades

Creating a trade and applying a customer-based FX margin for bulk orders (Parent-child) is the same as single order processing. When bank-level executions trigger the generation of child trades in the scope of group orders, the system applies the same bank-level Treasury Rate for all the child trades involving the same currency pair.

However, the FX margin is calculated based on the customer FX rate for each child trade separately.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is not mandatory to enter the Consol Rate field in SEC.TRADE if Consolidate FX is set to YES in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE , when the transaction is eligible to apply customer-based margin (Transaction Code configured in Cus Fxmargin Trans Type in SC.PARAMETER ) and the margin configuration exists for the respective customer group in FX.GROUP.CONDITION .

| Customer | Trade Ccy | Account Ccy | Treasury Rate | Customer Margin | Customer FX Rate |

### 5.39  Delivery


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Sections:** 🔧 Working With


#### 🔧 Working With

The Delivery module in Temenos Transact facilitates delivering and receiving messages as and when the transactions are input, authorised, amended or deleted based on the set up in the respective applications. The Securities (SC) module supports both inward and outward SWIFT Messages. Both ISO15002 and ISO20022 messages are supported.

The full set of supported messages and stages when they are produced are detailed in the below features.

- Securities STP - Straight Through Processing
- Corporate Actions – Delivery
- Settlement Delivery
- Institutional Custody


##### Supporting Fund Order Messages Through Delivery Core Framework

MX ISO 20022 fund messages generated from Securities (SC) complies with the Delivery Framework. The SC module supports XMLISO using Camel for MX ISO20022 fund messages, which support Distinguished Name (DN).

The Distinguished Name (DN) is an information that is part of the financial messaging header. It allows to identify an entity that can be detailed in a hierarchical directory structure by department, geographical location, application or individual. A DN must be read from right to left. The first part of the DN specifies the channel (SWIFT) and the second part is set with the Business Identifier Code (BIC) of the broker.

Fund message can be sent directly to the transfer agent or through a fund routing platform. These transfer agents are set as Counterparties in the SC module. For each counterparty, the bank needs to setup DE.DISTINGUISH.NAME.RULES . Read Configuring MX Messages through SWIFT Interact Services to know more about configuring DE.DISTINGUISH.NAME.RULES .

Additionally, DE.CARRIER must be defined with the Format Module as XMLISO. On doing so, the Delivery module performs the following functions:

1. Verifies the DE.CARRIER configuration with record ID as FUNDS.
2. Determines the details expected in the technical header, including the DNs of the Requestor and Responder.
3. Sends the final message to the SWIFT Alliance Temenos connector.

When the same carrier is enabled for the receiver of the message, the delivery framework handles the transformation in the delivery transformation layer.

Once DE.DISTINGUISH.NAME.RULES is configured, the delivery framework has the capability of identifying the DN and updating the DE.O.HEADER application with the relevant responder and requestor.

> 
> **Applications:** `CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `FT.COMMISSION.TYPE`, `SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT`, `SEC.ACC.MASTER`, `SEC.ACC.MASTER, CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.POSITION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *App Value*, *Application Field*, *Application Operand*, *Application Value*, *Authorised Broker*, *Br Direct Chgs*, *Br Set Acc*, *Br Sett Internal* ... +22 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Counterparty is the opposite player with whom a customer transaction takes place. It could be a broker, a transfer agent or, in some instances, the bank’s own book. The Depository or Custodian is the place where the securities are held. A securities transaction has to be intimated to the correct depository such that movement of securities can take place smoothly.

This feature explains the setup required to create the counterparties in Temenos Transact and the related tables.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The first step to create a Counterparty or Depository in Temenos Transact is to create a CUSTOMER record. Once a CUSTOMER record is setup in Temenos Transact , a record in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application is created for the customer. The Customer Type field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY determines the role that the counterparty plays.


##### Configuring Broker or Counterparty

A BROKER record in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application is shown in the following screenshot:

The following applications validate the broker status when the user performs any transactions:

- SEC.TRADE
- SECURITY.TRANSFER
- SEC.OPEN.ORDER
- SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS


##### Configuring Depository and Broker

- The depository is a crucial player in the securities market. All security holdings are maintained with a depository, who handles the transfer of securities between parties and facilitates the smooth transfer of funds between them. Banks offering private banking services usually hold an omnibus account with a depository. All their client holdings are aggregated and held together in a single omnibus account with the depository. The advantage of this model is that it is cost effective where the clearing member pays lesser fees, which results in lesser fees for the individual customers. Corporate actions are received at the omnibus level allowing the clearing member the right to allocate the proceeds. This model is not very beneficial to the individual customers as they rely on the clearing member
- Even in an omnibus model, the bank may maintain multiple omnibus accounts with the depository. This is mainly due to regulatory requirements.
- Most countries expect the bank to separate its own holdings from that of its customers. Hence, own holdings are held in as separate omnibus account. This is also known as omnibus segregated account model. A bank can have multiple omnibus accounts with the same depository. These are referred to as omnibus sub-accounts.
- The other model is where each individual customer holdings are held separately with the depository. Thus, the accounts are individually segregated and this model is known as individual segregated account model. It is possible to have a combination of the omnibus segregated account model and individual segregated account model. In Singapore, it is segregated accounts for Singapore nationals and permanent residents (PRs), whereas it is omnibus for others.

For the counterparties to use internal or cash account, the Br Sett Internal field must be set to Yes to indicate that the broker does not support a nostro or vostro relationship. Hence, the settlement account must either be internal or a cash account in Temenos Transact .

> **⚠️ Note:** The Br Sett Internal field can be set as Yes for any type of counterparty.

When this field is set to Yes, the Br Set Acc field can accept either a cash account or an internal account category. Internal category must be entered with prefix ‘I –‘. The cash account can be directly entered in this field without any prefix.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Br Set Acc field is mandatory, if the Br Sett Internal field is set to Yes. An override is generated, if the Br Sett Internal field is set to Yes and a nostro account is entered in Br Set Acc field.

To create a depository in Temenos Transact , the user has to create a CUSTOMER record. Once the customer is created using the same ID, a record needs to be opened in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application with the Customer Type field set as Depository.

The user can specify the commission types, which the bank is charged by the depository (if the user is aware of the rate), for each Corporate Action types. These charge types must exist in the FT.COMMISSION.TYPE application and on the corporate actions DIARY.TYPE application. The settlement tolerance amount per currency can be set in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application. When funds are received at the omnibus level from the depository for a corporate action (for example, cash dividend), the system authorises the entitlements if the amount received is within the specified tolerance amount. Some of the field validation is returned by the system based on the values populated in the Customer Type field.

The user can enter values in the Depository Account , Sub Account and Sett Tol Ccy fields only for a record that is defined as Depository in the Customer Type field.

Certain field validations are returned by the system based on the values populated in the Customer Type field.


#### 🔧 Working With

Brokers and depositories are stakeholders of every transaction other than the customer. Apart from creating the broker and depository, certain parameter level setup needs to be done to define their transaction level processing. All the setups and the processing are described in the below headings.


##### Unapproved Brokers

Brokers and counterparties are classified as authorised or unauthorised. To specify as unauthorised, the Authorised Broker field needs to be set to No. A value of Yes or NULL (default value) means that the broker or counterparty is authorised. This classification can be changed as required. If the broker or counterparty is unauthorised, an override message is generated when committing the record. If the override is accepted, the message is written to the EXCEPTION.LOG table with an error code of 455.

At the end of the day, a report is produced to display all transactions that were undertaken with an unauthorised broker. The Unauthorised Broker Transaction Rpt (UNAUTH.BROKER.RPT) enquiry can be run as a standalone enquiry for intraday. It is also added to the BNK/SC.BATCH.REP record in the BATCH application in the Job Name and Data fields. These fields are updated during the COB. It uses the ENQUIRY.REPORT and REPORT.CONTROL records of the same name.


##### Broker Fees

When defining a broker, the user can enter the commission rates (if the user knows the details) that the broker charges the organisation for the transactions in shares and bonds. These rates must exist as valid records in the FT.COMMISSION.TYPE application. If more complex rules are required to determine broker fees, they can be set up in the SC.BROK.STK.EXCH.FEES application. Read the Detailed Broker Commission Fees section for more information.

In some markets, the fees and brokerage due to the broker are directly paid to the broker at the time of trade, instead of paying through a custodian. The Br Direct Chgs field must be set to YES, if the brokerage needs to be paid directly. The details of the fees to be paid directly are defined in the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT application, and it is calculated and credited directly to the broker’s fees account in the SEC.TRADE application. It is also possible that for some brokers, it may be required to check the fees and modify for every execution. In such cases, where there is a straight through processing (STP) setup, it is possible to set that the STP be halted at either execution stage or trade stage and also allow manual correction. Then, the Exe Hlt and Trade Hlt fields must be set for halting the STP.


##### Standard Settlement Instructions (SSI)

Standard settlement instructions for a broker can be set up using the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT application. Read SSI Parameter section in Settlement feature for more information.


##### Depository – Omnibus and Segregated Accounts

Accounts with the depository or custodian can be held omnibus or at a segregated level. There could also be multiple omnibus sub-accounts as well. Omnibus sub-accounts can be held for any purpose such as residence, taxes and type of account (for example, in Spain, there is separate omnibus account for residents and non-residents). In some countries, omnibus accounts can co-exist with the segregated accounts (for example, in Singapore, they use segregated accounts for Singapore nationals and PRs, whereas they use omnibus accounts for others).

Where there is a single omnibus account per depository, the depository ID by itself identifies the omnibus account. The Dep Account Extension ID field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY should be updated with the external ID of the omnibus account and is used in messages sent to the depository. Where there are multiple omnibus sub-accounts with the same depository, then there are two possible ways to set this up:

- Separate CUSTOMER and CUSTOMER.SECURITY records are created per omnibus sub-account. All of them represent the same depository and hence have the same Bank Identification Code (BIC). One of them is the main record and the others are the omnibus sub-accounts. In this case, the Parent Depository field should be updated so that the system can identify that the record is only a sub-account. The Parent Depository field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY should be updated with the customer ID of the parent depository record or it can be updated with some unique ID. If a unique ID is populated, the same ID should be populated for all omnibus sub-account records.

- Rules to default the correct ID can be set (Read Setting Rules to Default Depository section for more information) and positions are held separately based on separate depository ID. Each depository record has its own Dep Account Extension ID updated which is the external ID of each omnibus account.

A single depository record is created, and within CUSTOMER.SECURITY of this depository, the different omnibus sub-accounts can be defined using the Sub Account and Sub Acct Ext ID fields.

The Sub Account field is populated with a unique random ID. This is treated as the internal ID of the omnibus sub-account and appended to the SECURITY.POSITION record. The Sub Acc Ext Id field holds the actual ID of the sub-account with the depository. This is the value that is mapped to all SWIFT messages sent to the depository.

In some markets (for example, Malaysia), different cash accounts (nostro) can be linked to the sub-accounts and the Cash Account field is used for this purpose. Rules to default the correct depository and sub-account can be set (Read the Setting Rules to Default Depository section for more information) and positions are held per sub-account. The record in SECURITY.POSITION in these cases has the depository and the sub-account as part of the ID.

| Portfolio Number | Depository | Sub-Account |
|---|---|---|
| 190153-1 | 100472 | 111111 |
| 100287-1 | 100472 | 555555 |
| 100286-1 | 100472 | 888888 |


##### Setting Rules to Default Depository and Sub-account in Transactions

When there are multiple depositories and sub-accounts within depositories, it is important to set rules to default the correct depository and sub-account while creating transactions. This enables positions to be maintained correctly and avoids errors due to manual selection. The defaulting rules can be set as below:

In the record in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application, the user can define the fields to default a specific depository in the SEC.TRADE or SEC.OPEN.ORDER application.

They are part of a multi-value group and within this multi-value group, the Application Field , Application Operand and Application Value fields can be expanded as a multi sub-value set. The input to the Default Depository field is restricted for records that are defined as Depository in the Customer Type field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application. The input to the Application Field field is restricted to fields defined in the SECURITY.MASTER standard selection application. Therefore, input can only be a field in the SECURITY.MASTER application. The input to the Application Operand must be an operand. A drop-down list displays the operands that can be used, which are as follows:

- EQ – Equal to
- GE – Greater than or equal to
- GT – Greater than
- LE – Less than or equal to
- LT – Less than NE – Not equal to

The input to Application Value can be anything. After the user enters appropriate values in SEC.OPEN.ORDER or SEC.TRADE , the system validates to check whether there are any values in these decision fields. After a valid check is returned, then the depository defined in the Default Depository field is defaulted on the contract.

Whenever an order ( SEC.OPEN.ORDER) or trade ( SEC.TRADE ) is input in the system, the system looks for depository default setup in the SEC.ACC.MASTER record of the portfolio for which the transaction input. If the transaction is input for the portfolio shown in above screenshot and If the Last Price field in SECURITY.MASTER ( security for which the transaction is input) is less than or equal to 10 and the Price Currency is equal to GBP, then the depository defaulted in the contract is CUSTOMER ID 100472. Otherwise, the user moves onto the next multi-value set of fields. If the Industry Code field in SECURITY.MASTER is greater than 10, then the depository record 100492 is defaulted. If none of the above matches, then the system checks SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT. If the validation fails, the system checks the default depository in SECURITY.MASTER .

The SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT application is used to set default depository based on several conditions. If rules are not defined in SEC.ACC.MASTER or default is not found in SEC.ACC.MASTER , then the system checks SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT to work out the default depository and/or sub-account. The ID of the table can be any of the following:

- Company
- Company*Security
- Company*Security*Stock Exchange
- Company*Portfolio
- Company*Portfolio*Stock Exchange

This makes it possible to set different default logics based on security, stock exchange portfolio and combinations. Further more, granular default conditions can be set within the SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT .

The File field is used to define the application based on which the condition is defined. The Application Field , Operand and Application Value fields are used to define the conditions based on which the depository needs to be defaulted. In the above example, the depository 100492 with sub-account 123123 defaulted in order or trade, when portfolio 100273-1 trades on NYSE stock exchange and the sub-asset type is 301, that is, Equities. The depository is defaulted to 100492, but the sub-account is defaulted to 321321 for the same portfolio trading on NYSE for a bond (sub-asset type = 101).

- SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT rules can be setup for the segregated accounts as well as omnibus accounts. If SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT is used for defaulting the omnibus sub-account, the omnibus sub-account should have been defined in CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the depository. For setting default for customer segregated account, the account need not be defined at the portfolio level. The segregated account can be directly updated in SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT .
- Both sub-account internal ID as well as external ID (they can be same) need to be defined in SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT . The external ID is the reference mapped to all the SWIFT messages (account details).

> **⚠️ Note:** The external ID field is mapped to the SWIFT messages.

If no condition is satisfied or no conditions exist in SEC.ACC.MASTER and SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT , then the system defaults the Default Depository from the respective record in SECURITY.MASTER . The default depository for the security is defined in the Default Depository field in SECURITY.MASTER.


##### Defaulting Depository and Sub-Account in Transactions

When a transaction is input, the defaulting of DEPOSITORY and CU.DEPOSITORY uses the following sequence:

| Application | Description |
|---|---|
| SEC.ACC.MASTER | Defaults the depository based on the selection criteria defined from the Default Depo to App Value fields |
| CUSTOMER.SECURITY | Defaults the value in the Default Depository field in the customer’s record in CUSTOMER.SECURITY |
| SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT | Enables the default depository at the customer, portfolio or stock exchange level. The various options available in the sequence are: COMPANY*PORTFOLIO*STOCK EXCHANGE COMPANY*CUSTOMER*STOCK EXCHANGE COMPANY*PORTFOLIO COMPANY*CUSTOMER COMPANY**STOCK.EXCHANGE COMPANY |
| SECURITY.POSITION | Defaults the default depository from the existing SECURITY.POSITION (if it exists) if default is not obtained from the applications ( SEC.ACC.MASTER, CUSTOMER.SECURITY and SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT . |
| SECURITY.MASTER | Defaults the value in the Default Depository field |

The depository and the sub-account are defaulted in the transaction and can be changed. The SECURITY.POSITION application is built with the depository as part of the key. If an omnibus sub-account or a segregated account is set, then the same is also part of the key. This ensures that positions are held separately. Position can be moved from one depository to another or from one segregated account to another using the POSITION.TRANSFER application. The omnibus account or segregated account external ID is mapped in all SWIFT messages to the depository. When the position is moved between two segregated accounts or from an omnibus account to a segregated account with the same depository, the system can automatically generate MT540 or MT542 movement messages. If this functionality is required, the Child Depo Advice field should be set to Move.


##### Standard Settlement Instructions (SSI) for Depository

Standard settlement Instructions set up for a depository can be set using the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT application. Read the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT for Depository section in Settlement feature for more information. The instructions are applied when there is a transfer from one depository to another through POSITION.TRANSFER .


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Depository and Broker feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Depository and Broker feature.


> **Related Applications:** `CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `FT.COMMISSION.TYPE`, `SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT`, `SEC.ACC.MASTER`, `SEC.ACC.MASTER, CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.POSITION`

### 5.41  IFRS Impairment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**

The revaluation gain or loss, with respect to securities held as available for sale (AFS) portfolios, is posted to equity (internal accounts) rather than Profit and L...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accrue*, *Amt*, *Cancel*, *Cancel Date*, *Cat*, *Categ*, *Cur*, *Curr* ... +35 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Under IFRS regulations, the accounting of any asset (such as a bond or a loan), which goes into a default situation, may be modified. The revaluation gain or loss, with respect to securities held as available for sale (AFS) portfolios, is posted to equity (internal accounts) rather than Profit and Loss (PL) accounts.

However, for an impaired security, any current loss booked to equity must be reversed and booked to PL accounts. As part of impairment processing, it is possible to:

- Identify a security as impaired and record the reason
- Move the loss from an internal account to PL account for an impaired security
- Cancel impairments


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Impairment and Impairment Categ fields in both the SC.PARAMETER and SEC.ACC.MASTER applications enable the impairment processing for AFS own book portfolios.


##### SC.PARAMETER

The Impairment field can be set to YES or Null, to enable impairment at the portfolio level.


##### SEC.ACC.MASTER

The Impairment Categ field only accepts a valid P&L category from the CATEGORY application.

> **⚠️ Note:** The impairment processing is possible only when there is a valid category record.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with the working mechanism of the impairment processing in Temenos Transact .


##### SEC.ACC.MASTER

The Impairment field can only be set to YES for an own book portfolio, if the Portfolio Type field is set to AVAIL.SALE. The Impairment Categ field must be a valid CATEGORY record.

When a security is impaired, the revaluation P&L booked to an internal category is moved to the specified P&L category. The SC.IMPAIRMENT application is used for the impairment processing of a security with a valid SECURITY.MASTER record ID. For an impaired own book AFS portfolio, the Portfolio field is mandatory. The Impairment Reason field records the reason for the impairment. The Impairment Date field marks the date from when the security is impaired. The Cancel field is used to cancel the Impairment and the Cancel Date field marks the date from which the impairment cancellation is effective.

The SC Impairment Details (SC.IMPAIRMENT.DETAILS) enquiry displays the trade details and impairment amounts booked.

Other enquiries, such as Contracts with Impairment Evidence (CONTRACT.IMPAIR.EVIDENCE), Impaired Contracts (CONTRACT.IMPAIRED) and Unimpaired Contracts (CONTRACT.UNIMPAIRED) are based on the EB.CASHFLOW application.


##### SC.TRADING.POSITION

The SC.TRADING.POSITION application contains any the Orig Impair Amt field and any current amount recorded in the Curr Impair Amt and Cur Impair Amt Lcy fields as shown in the below screenshot.

The impairment processing for AFS portfolios are follows. The headings below are explained for all the following cases:

- Date - Date of transaction input
- ID - Transaction ID
- T.DATE - Trade date
- V.DATE - Value date
- PORTFOLIO - SEC.ACC.MASTER ID
- SECURITY - SECURITY.MASTER ID
- NOM - Number of nominal (bought or sold)
- PRICE -Trade price
- M.PRICE - Market/closing price
- Impaired - Whether security is impaired or not
