##### Reclassification

The financial assets IAS 39 prescribes four major categories of classifications based on the nature and characteristics of the asset:

- Held for Trading (HFT)
- Available for Sale (AFS)
- Held till Maturity (HTM)
- Loans and Receivables (LAR)

Based on the classification, the assets are measured at either amortised cost or fair value.

IAS 39 prescribes the rules for the reclassification of financial assets from one category to the other provided the nature and characteristics of that asset has undergone a change.

It must be possible to:

- Reclassify the assets from one category to the other based on the prescribed rules as per IAS 39.
- Change the accounting method prospectively based on the revised classification.

IAS 39 requires a non-derivative financial asset to be classified into one of the following categories, at inception:

- Fair value through profit and loss
- Loans and receivables
- Held-to-maturity or
- AFS

An internal portfolio can be a trading, investment or AFS portfolio. IAS 39 allows reclassification of these portfolios after the initial recognition.

The following table illustrate the reclassifications that is possible for debt securities and equities, respectively.

The Reclassification field in SEC.ACC.MASTER is set to YES, to enable the reclassification of portfolios. The reclassification is applicable only for internal (own book) portfolios.

The categories need to be specified for own portfolios, to which the various accounting entries of securities are posted. For example, revaluation profit and loss and discount accruals. Based on the portfolio type, category codes are specified in SEC.ACC.MASTER for the system to raise the necessary accounting entries. For example, the Revaluation field is set to Y for HFT (trading) portfolios and unrealised P&L are posted to the category codes specified in Unreal Pl Cat Prt and Unreal Pl Cat Loss fields, respectively. For HTM (investment) portfolios, the assets are measured at amortised cost.

After a portfolio is reclassified, the details of discount processing and unrealised processing must be amended manually. The category codes are entered in line with the revised classification of the portfolio. The accounting entries raised in old categories are reversed and raised to new categories (if any).

If an AFS portfolio is reclassified as a HTM portfolio, the revaluation category codes are deleted, revaluation processing is turned ‘off and discount processing ( Accrue Discount and Discount Cat ) is turned ‘on. In this case, the system reverses the old entries, updates (pertaining to revaluation) and carries out the subsequent processing (discount accrual) in line with the revised classification.

The Post Disc Upfont field specifies whether the discount is posted upfront and amortised daily or if upfront policy is not required with discounts and premiums to be accrued, for the portfolio. Initially, if this field is set to NO, (grossing up of underlying assets is not required), it cannot be changed to YES at the time of reclassifying the portfolios. Read the IFRS section of User Guides for more information regarding the impairment and re-classification processing in general and detailed accounting entries.


##### Trade Date Posting Realised and Unrealised Profits

In a trade dated system, the unrealised and realised P&L are recognised immediately and posted to profit/loss or suspense, as specified in the SC.PARAMETER .

If the value date position is ZERO, the purchase of stock traded on the current bank date for a forward value date resides in the system under the specified value date. However, when the COB valuation is run, revaluation profits (if any) are posted that day for the value of the same day. Also, for a forward purchase and forward sale, the realised profit (if any) is also taken on the day the sale was entered in the system. There are many permutations such as short positions being reduced or closed out entirely. In all cases, P&L is recognised immediately.

The system date is set to 10th November, so the Trade Date accounting for both accounts and securities as displayed as shown in the below screenshot.

After running the COB STMT.ENTRY , the forward value date of the nostro entry is confirmed as shown in the below screenshot.

The below screenshot displays the forward Value Date of the RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY (LIVE debit asset purchase).

After checking the revaluation entry for the above position, the user must verify the Value Date of the current bank date.

The contra entry of the revaluation suspense (as shown above) indicates the spot entry posted to P&L as shown in the below screenshot.

The user now simulates a sale of 50% of the position. Though both the purchase and sale have a forward value, any resultant realised and revaluation P&L are considered immediately.

After the COB, the previous day’s revaluation entry is reversed as the test account is set to perform the I/O method of revaluations (like, revalue one day, reverse the previous day, revalue afresh, and so on) rather than ADJ (like, revalue one day, update the next by an adjustment up or down as required).

The reversing entry takes the value of next working day (in this case, 13th November). This is replaced with the next day’s revaluation P&L.

Since a part of the forward position is sold, the realised profit is also booked for the current bank date ( as shown in the below screenshot).

The realised P&L also updates SECURITY.POSITION and a RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY is built to update the LIVE debit balance of the holding in the security as shown in the below screenshot.

The following is the calculation of revaluation:

SYSTEM DATE = 10th November VAL.DTE

Purchase 10,000 at 13.5 15/11 135,000

EOD/COB

Revaluation at 15.0 on 10/11 = 15,000 (10,000 * (13.5 – 15.0))

NEXT DAY = 13th November

Sale 5,000 at 14.25 on 16/11 for 71,250

Realised P/L on 10/11 is 3,750

Position is 5,000 and 67,500

Thus, revaluation at 15.1875 on 13/11 is 8,437.50 (5,000 * (13.5 – 15.1875)


###### Discount Realisation on Discounted Securities

For own book sale of discounted bonds, Temenos Transact posts the:

- Realised PL entries on the trade date
- Discount realisation entry on the value date

The Disc Real Pl field in SC.PARAMETER must be set to YES to post the realised PL entries on the value date for sale of securities where discount has been accrued. Both the realised PL and discount realisation entries are posted on the same date (value date).


##### Posting of Unrealised Profit and Loss

The revaluation of securities based on the exchange rate movements, that is the posting of revaluation gains and losses are posted to the equity (internal accounts). The revaluation of currency profits and losses of the positions in foreign currency securities of an AFS portfolio can be posted to internal suspense account categories. If the Fx Reval field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application is set to Y, the revaluation of currency profits and losses are posted during the SC.REVAL.PROCESSING at the COB. This field is applicable only for AFS portfolios. The revaluation entries are posted to the categories, as specified in the Unreal Fx Prt and Unreal Fx Loss fields of the SEC.ACC.MASTER application, depending on whether there is a gain or loss. The actual posting method is based on the value entered in the Reval Post Method field of the SEC.ACC.MASTER . The values of this field are I/O or ADJ.

The below screenshot displays the fields of a typical own portfolio in which various rules are defined such as whether to post unrealised (revaluation) profits and losses (or both) into the accounts together with the frequency at which the revaluation is to be performed. The following are the options in the Post Unreal Pl field:

- NONE - Indicates that no unrealised profits or losses are posted.
- LOSS - Indicates that only unrealised losses are posted to P&amp;L.
- BOTH - Indicates that unrealised profits and losses are posted to P&amp;L.
- LOWER.COST - Indicates that the cost price or market price (whichever is the lowest) is used.
- RVAL - Indicates that the positions for this portfolio are re-valued against the Revaluation Price field in the SC.TRADING.POSITION and unrealised losses are posted. The Revaluation Price field is the lowest recorded market price, since the position was opened.

This revaluation method is not appropriate for short positions. The unrealised P&L is posted to the categories defined in the Unreal Pl Cat Prt and Unreal Pl Cat Loss fields.

If revaluation is set for a dealer book portfolio, the system raises one of the following set of entries:

- Categ entry and spec entry with asset type as LIVE
- Categ entry and statement entry
- Statement entry and spec entry with asset type as LIVE
- Statement entry and statement entry

These entries are raised based on the setup in the SEC.ACC.MASTER record of the dealer book portfolio. One leg of the entry is based on the setup in the Unreal Pl Cat Prt and/or Unreal Pl Cat Loss fields. If this field is set to a PL category, a CATEG.ENTRY is raised and if an internal account category is provided (available only when the Portfilo Type field is set as AVAIL.SALE) a STMT.ENTRY is raised. The second leg of the entry is based on the Unreal Loss Prov and/or Unreal Profit Susp fields.

The Unreal Loss Prov and/or Unreal Profit Susp fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER also accept an internal account category, PL category or Null. If these fields are set as Null, a CRF entry with asset type as LIVE is raised. If this field is set as an internal account category, a STMT.ENTRY for this category is raised.

However, if the PL category is provided, the system raises one of the following entries:

- Categ entry and CRF entry with asset type as PL category defined in these fields.
- Statement entry and CRF entry with asset type as PL category defined in these fields.

The unrealised P&L is posted to the categories defined in the Unreal Pl Cat Prt and Unreal Pl Cat Loss fields.

### 5.42  Initial Public Offer


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Initial public offering (IPO) or stock market launch is a type of public offering in which the shares of a company are sold to the public. A private company turns into a public company through this process. The companies, which expand the capital to monetise the investments of early private investor...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account*, *Alloted*, *Allotment Price*, *Allotment Qty*, *Amount*, *Bid*, *Bid Price*, *Block* ... +24 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Initial public offering (IPO) or stock market launch is a type of public offering in which the shares of a company are sold to the public. A private company turns into a public company through this process. The companies, which expand the capital to monetise the investments of early private investors to become publicly traded companies use IPO. After the IPO, when shares trade freely in the open market, money passes among the public investors.

The capital raised through IPO is an important factor for the business growth and expansion as it enables more stock options, equity awards and benefit the initial investors with liquidity.


##### Processing Initial Public Offer

The issuer wanting an IPO does the following:

- Nominates a lead merchant banker as the book runner
- Specifies the number of securities to be issued
- Specifies the price band for the orders
- Appoints syndicate members for bidding process.

Investors place their order with a syndicate member who inputs the orders into the electronic book. This process is similar to open auctions. A book typically remains open for five days. The bids cannot be lesser than the floor price. The bidder can revise bids before the issue closes.

After the book-building period, the book runner evaluates the bids based on the evaluation, which may include the following:

- Price aggression
- Investors’ quality
- Earliness of bids and so on.

The book runner company concludes the final price for the stock and allocation of securities. The number of shares are fixed and the issue size is frozen based on the price per share found through the book building process. The allocation of securities is done to the successful bidders and refund is processed for unsuccessful bids.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Temenos Transact IPO functionality relates to the role of the syndicate member and not the merchant banker or book runner.


##### Understanding the types of Initial Public Offer

The two types of IPO are as follows:

The issuing company (on agreements with its appointed investment banker) offers IPOs to the investors at a pre-determined fixed price. In this process, the investors know the allocation price in advance.

The IPO issuing company specifies the price range along with the maximum number of securities that are issued. The investors can bid for the securities at different prices. The same investors can also place multiple bids at different prices.

These orders are recorded in an electronic book and the bidding continues for a specified period. The bid prices lesser than the floor price of the price band are not accepted. The issuing price of the IPO is found only after the book building closes. The issuing company determines the final price with its investment banker (book-runner). The price evaluation process includes depends on the following factors:

- Earliness of the bid
- Quality standard of the applicant investors
- Aggression of price

After considering these factors, IPO allocation is done based on the final price.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The configuration of IPO includes the setup of SC.PARAMETER and SC.ORDER.TYPE applications.


##### SC.PARAMETER

The internal account category is defined in the Ipo Susp Account field in SC.PARAMETER for posting the IPO category.

The subscription amount debited from the customer is maintained in this suspense account.

> **⚠️ Note:** The payment to the book runner or broker is a manual process. The single funds transfer debits the suspense account and credits the nostro account of the book runner or broker.


##### ORDER.TYPE

The Ipo Fpo field is set to YES which indicates the order type as an IPO order.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details Temenos Transact IPO processing with examples.


##### Deal Processing

- The Ipo Fpo field is set to YES in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application to capture the IPO subscriptions.
- At the time of subscription, investors must have sufficient funds in their accounts. There are two ways to ensure the investor’s commitment to the allotted shares. BLOCK: A lien is placed on the customer’s account for the subscription amount. This is posted as an F entry to ensure the customer does not withdraw the funds from his account. DEBIT: The subscription amount is debited from the customer’s account. For non-allotment or partial allotment, the investor receives a refund. If the Debit Time field in the SECURITY.MASTER is set to IMMEDIATELY, the system debits the subscription amount for the customer. The position for the paid-up value is created with zero nominal. Modifications to the order results in reverse and rebook of the debit entry and adjustment of the paid-up position. The cancellation of the order results in the reversal of the entry and paid-up position. If the Debit Time field in the SECURITY.MASTER is set to BOOKCLOSURE, a lien is posted on the customer’s cash account, using an F entry for the subscription amount. Subsequently a COB job, on the date specified in the Ipo End Date field debits the customer’s cash account and creates the paid-up position. The funds debited from the customer is maintained in a suspense account ( Ipo Susp Account field setup in SC.PARAMETER ). The mechanism changes for each IPO and needs to be specified in the SECURITY.MASTER application.

Allotment and refund details are captured in the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS application. The number of shares allotted can be updated in the Nominal Recd field and the issue price can be updated in the Price field.

The Cu Refund Amount field accepts input or defaults the value as Cu Subscription Amount minus (allotted shares * issue price), if left blank. After the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS application is committed and authorised, background actions work depending on the value in the Block Type field in SECURITY.MASTER .

In case a customer is not allotted with any shares, the entire subscription amount is refunded.

| Customer | Bid Price | Bid Quantity |
|---|---|---|
| Customer 1 | 50 | 100 |
| Customer 2 | 60 | 200 |
| Customer 3 | 60 | 200 |
| Customer 4 | 55 | 100 |
| Customer 5 | 55 | 100 |

Related topics:

An initial public offering (IPO) refers to the process of offering shares of a private corporation to the public in a new stock issuance. Public share issuance allows a company to raise capital from public investors.

The transition from a private to a public company can be an important time for private investors to fully realise gains from their investment as it typically includes share premiums for current private investors. Meanwhile, it also allows public investors to participate in the offering.

### 5.43  InstrumentMaster


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The instrument master or securities master is a record of all the instruments that are available for trading in the system. Securities can be broadly categorised into equities and debts. However, the system can support different types of securities including equities, fixed income, debt, funds, note...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *12M NAV High*, *12M NAV Low*, *Accum Income*, *Adj Margin Rate*, *Admin Fee Cap*, *Admin Fee Categ Avg*, *Admin Fees*, *Agency Id* ... +188 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The instrument master or securities master is a record of all the instruments that are available for trading in the system. Securities can be broadly categorised into equities and debts. However, the system can support different types of securities including equities, fixed income, debt, funds, notes and so on. Each type of instrument has unique attributes.

In Temenos Transact , all attributes of different instruments are captured in the SECURITY.MASTER application. This feature describes the creation of the securities master and the underlying tables required to support the creation.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the basic configuration to be set before instruments are created in the SECURITY.MASTER application.


##### SM.PARAMETER

The SM.PARAMETER application stores the details of SECURITY.MASTER related parameters that are shared across companies. It allows only one record with the ID as SYSTEM.

The Price Qual Format field indicates if cum and ex markers are to be in SWIFT format or not. The concatenation of cum and ex markers is handled using the Cum Indicate and Ex Indicate fields. However, input to these fields are allowed only if the value in the Price Qual Format field is set to SWIFT. Input to these fields are validated against the record in DE.TRANSLATION in order to ensure SWIFT compatibility.

The Alt Index Dup field controls the level of duplication allowed in the Isin Number , Euroclear Number , Cedel Number , Sedol Number , Swiss Number and Cusip No fields that are defined as alternate indexes in SECURITY.MASTER . The Alt Index Dup field can be setup with any of the following values.

| Values | Description |
|---|---|
| 001 or BLANK | Indicates duplication of the index keys are allowed. Only one security with a suffix of '-000' is allowed per index key. For example, 100027-000 and 100027-001 can share the same ISIN code, but 100027-000 and 100028-000 cannot share the same ISIN code. |
| No | Indicates that a one to one relationship must exist between the security master key and alternate index key. Duplication is not allowed in any of the fields |
| Yes | Indicates that validation is not performed on the index keys and they can be used any number of times on any number of records in SECURITY.MASTER . |
| Override | Generates an override message. If the key is already used, then acceptance of the override allows duplication. |

The Isin Validation field determines whether the ISIN code entered through the SECURITY.MASTER application is validated. If this field is set to Yes, the check digit must be as calculated by the system. The Alpha Key field enables the input of alphanumeric characters in the security master ID. If this is set to Yes, the system does not perform the formatting of SECURITY.MASTER reference based on the format specified in the Security Format field of SC.PARAMETER .

The Alt Index Check field defaults the SECURITY.MASTER ID when the user enters an alternate identifier such as ISIN in Sec.Open.Order , Sec.Trade or Order.By.Cust application. The Sec Domicile SSI field is used to determine whether security domicile must be considered for SSI search when Place of Settlement field is not defined in SECURITY.MASTER . Read Defaulting Settlement Instructions section for more information on SSI setup.


##### ConfiguringSM.PARAMETERfor Setting Company-specific Instrument Attributes

In a multi-entity setup, the attributes related to SECURITY.MASTER are shared across the companies of a given group. Even though most of the instrument level attributes are same across the companies, a few of them can vary per entity.

In order to enable the configuration of instrument level attributes that can vary per entity, the Nonshared SM field in SM.PARAMETER is set to Yes. This allows the users to create a record in the SC.SM.MC.DEFINITION table.

SC.SM.MC.DEFINITION is a Fin level table that can be created in each company with the same record ID as in SECURITY.MASTER and the values specific to the company can be updated in this table.


#### 🔧 Working With

The SECURITY.MASTER application contains most of the information relative to each security on the system. The various security transactions obtain the latest information relating to the instrument that is featuring in the transaction. Thus, each record must be possibly up-to-date. Temenos Transact uses a high-level indicator to differentiate bond and share paper types within the SECURITY.MASTER application. The amount and type of information required to build a complete record in SECURITY.MASTER highly depends on the indicator selected.

Most master records can safely be ignored once set up. For example, ordinary shares requires less maintenance once a new record is authorised.


##### Recording Basic Details of the Security

The Bond or Share field indicates whether the record is created for a share or bond. The below record is an example for equity share. The first set of fields allows the user to record the particulars of the issuing or the parent company. The Mnemonic field specifies a unique short code provided for each security for easy identification.

The Company Domicile field refers to the country of the parent company issuing the security. The Security Domicile specifies the country where the security is issued. The Security Ccy indicates the place where the security is issued and the Price Currency field indicates the currency in which the security is traded. This field accepts a valid record from the CURRENCY application. The below screenshot is an example of a record in SECURITY.MASTER .

The Par Value field holds the face value of the stock. The smallest nominal amount that can be traded is provided in the Trading Units field.

If the Trading Units field value is 100, the system throws an error when an investor tries to place an order for 50 units. The Default Depository field specifies the depository where this particular stock is kept. The International Security Identification Number (ISIN) specifies the code as a code that uniquely identifies a specific securities issue.


##### Recording Price Details and Price Change for Securities

The current price of a security can either be updated manually or automatically (through Bloomberg, Reuters, Telerate feeds and so on). This can be specified in Price update Code field of the SECURITY.MASTER application. This field gives the list of the possible options. If the user selects the manual input, the user can change the price in Last Price field, therefore the system date automatically defaulted into the Date Last Price field. The Price Type field defines the calculation method that is used when calculating the price of a trade.

In addition, to update the prices, it may be a requirement with some forms of securities such as unit trusts and funds to record income and accumulated income. This can also be recorded manually or automatically in the Income , Accum Income and Income Date fields.

This application indicates the system how a price type calculation is to be performed within any given transaction in the Securities module. The Multiply Factor field indicates the weighting attached to the price quoted on a security. For example, if each unit of the nominal amount represents an option on 1000 shares, then the value in this field will be 1000. In order to accrue or amortise the discount amount when a security is traded, the Disc Instrument field must be set to Y. This process is carried out only for the bank’s own portfolios.

The input of historic prices and income in SECURITY.MASTER can be controlled using the PRICE.UPDATE application. The Past Update Price and Past Update Income fields allow the user to input Yes, No and Override. Based on this setup when a historic price, income or accumulated income is input using the SECURITY.MASTER application, the input is either, disallowed, allowed or allowed upon the acceptance of a warning message.

The SECURITY.MASTER application need not be launched every time when the user updates price or income. The SC.PRICE.CHANGE application allows the user to make any changes as required and stores the historic price or income data, whenever there is a change in the Last Price , Date Last Price and Price Qual Mark fields in SECURITY.MASTER .

Price can also be updated automatically via TDS (Temenos Data Source). The below image demonstrates how price is updated in SECURITY.MASTER application and how historical prices are stored in SC.PRICE.CHANGE application through the TDS interface.


##### Defining Cum And Ex Markers

The price of a security is affected by cum and ex periods and the Price Qual Mark field reflects these markers in the SECURITY.MASTER application.

Input in this field is validated against SM.PARAMETER . The input allowed is NULL or a valid SWIFT. If the field is set to Swift, multi-value input is allowed and the values can be any of the value defined in the Cum Indicate and Ex Indicate fields in SM.PARAMETER if they are not conversing within the same multi-value set. That is, a price cannot be both cum and ex dividend (CDIV and XDIV) at the same time.

The historic details of the price conditions for a date are stored in the SC.PRICE.CHANGE application. This application is automatically updated with the values in the Price Qual Mark fields in the SECURITY.MASTER application, whenever there is a change in the field.


##### Recording the Industry and Stock Exchange Details

The Industry Code field defines the industry to which the instrument belongs too. This critical information is required for several regulatory reports, such as, for defining portfolio strategies and for rebalancing portfolios. This field links to the SC.INDUSTRY application. The stock exchange at which the security is normally traded is provided in the Stock Exchange field. This field accepts a valid record in STOCK.EXCHANGE .

The industry codes defined in this application are assigned to each record in SECURITY.MASTER to identify the industry to which the security belongs too. The Industry Code and Sc Ind Internal fields in the SECURITY.MASTER application are used to capture the industry code from the SC.INDUSTRY application. The below screenshot is the record in SC.INDUSTRY for the above SECURITY.MASTER.

The ID of this application can accept a maximum of eight characters. This application also supports GICS codes. If the Gics Code field in SC.INDUSTRY is set to Yes, the system updates the Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS) hierarchy fields automatically. The GICS hierarchy is as follows:

- The first two digits of the ID in the Sector field
- The first four digits of the ID in the Industry Group field
- The first six digits of the ID in the Industry field
- The complete ID in the Sub Industry field

This application records the details of the stock exchange in which the security trades. The cut-off time for the stock exchange in the Cut off time field for the stock exchange.

In global practice, many stock exchanges operate on different trading platforms. Therefore, each stock exchange is subject to have a primary trading venue and one or more secondary trading venues which are generally identified based on the Market Identification code (MIC). Each secondary trading venue is stored as a separate record in the STOCK.EXCHANGE application with respective MIC as their ID. All the secondary trading venue are linked to their primary stock exchange through the Primary Exchg field.

If the Primary Exchg field is blank, then trading venue is considered as the primary trading venue and the respective stock exchange as the primary stock exchange. If the Primary Exchg field has a valid ID, then the trading venue is considered as a secondary trading venue and the respective stock exchange is obtained from the Primary Exchg field.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Mkt Idn Code | Sets the market identification code (MIC) as in STOCK.EXCHANGE |
| Isin Exception | Indicates the ISIN code of the security for which cross settlement cannot be performed |


##### Recording Alternate Security Index

In Temenos Transact , securities are captured in the SECURITY.MASTER application with unique ID. However, the market securities are identified by their common identifiers such as ISIN and CUSIP ID. Therefore, it is important to record these alternate IDs and also provide a mechanism by which the system can identify the SECURITY.MASTER ID when the user enters a valid alternate ID while trying to input the values in the order related fields (such as Sec.Open.Order , Sec.Trade or Order.By.Cust application). There are multiple ways to capture the alternate IDs as explained below:

Method 1

Using the Alternate Index field in SC.PARAMETER . Read SC.PARAMETER for more information. Two or more records in SECURITY.MASTER can have the same alternate ID if the Alt Index Dup field is set in SM.PARAMETER .

Method 2

A specific way to reference security identifications is to use the Alt User Index field in SC.PARAMETER application. This method of indexing the SECURITY.MASTER application is an alternative way for using the Alternate Index field (as detailed earlier in this user guide). The created records in ALT.SEC.PARAMETER must be added to the SC.PARAMETER application.

The Alt User Index and Alternate Index fields are mutually exclusive to one another. If the Alt User Index field is input, the Alternate Index field is disabled and vice-versa. Input to this multi-value field must be a valid key in the ALT.SEC.PARAMETER application.

Once a record in ALT.SEC.PARAMETER is created, the system automatically updates all the records in SECURITY.MASTER and adds this value to the Alt Security Id multi-value field. A sample record of SECURITY.MASTER with the unique identifier added is shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Alt Security No field can be used to add a unique identifier for each security.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Max Length | Determines the maximum length of the particular alternative ID. The value in the Max Length field is automatically adjusted when the alternative ID exceeds the length specified in the Max Length field in the EB.OBJECT . |
| Min Length | Determines the minimum length of the alternative ID. This field cannot be more than the number specified in the Max Length field. |
| Id Format | Sets the format of the alternative ID For example, 2N3A3X would be two numeric followed by three alpha characters followed by three alpha numeric. The total number of characters entered here are validated against the value in the Max Length and Min Length fields. A link to a subroutine could also be input for validating the ID. This is achieved by prefixing the subroutine name with @. |
| Display Mask | Allows the user to setup a mask for the identifier. For example, if ### - ## - # is selected, the 123456 value that is entered is displayed as 123-45-6. |
| Used In Sm | This system maintained field is set to YES when any record in the SECURITY.MASTER application has a value corresponding to this alternate index. |

When the Alt User Index field is used and a user enters a valid alternate ID in the Security Number field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER , SEC.TRADE or ORDER.BY.CUST , the system automatically defaults the correct security master ID.

When a user enters the alternate ID in the Security Number field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER , SEC.TRADE or ORDER.BY.CUST , the system automatically defaults the correct SECURITY.MASTER ID. If there are two records in SECURITY.MASTER with same alternate ID, the system defaults the first record in SECURITY.MASTER . The user has to check and change, if required.

> **⚠️ Note:** Two or more records in SECURITY.MASTER can have the same alternate ID, if the Alt Index Dup field is set in SM.PARAMETER application.

The defaulting logic applies when the value in the Alternate Index field is used and the Alt Index Check field is set in the SM.PARAMETER application. There are multiple exchanges offering dual currency trading. Dual currency securities are fully fungible in the primary and secondary (dual) currency exchanges. An investor may hold long position in one currency and sell position in alternate currency. One way to handle securities that are traded in different currencies is to open separate records in SECURITY.MASTER for the same security with different trade currencies, and duplicate the alternate ID in them.

In this case, when a user enters the alternate ID in the Security Number field in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER , SEC.TRADE or ORDER.BY.CUST application, the system automatically defaults the first record in SECURITY.MASTER (immaterial of the trade currency) and the user has to manually check and input the correct security master IDs in other records. To enable a better defaulting logic, the following feature is enabled:

- In SECURITY.MASTER , the user can set various currencies and/or exchanges in which the security can be traded.
- In SEC.OPEN.ORDER or SEC.TRADE , if the currency and exchange are entered followed by the ISIN, the system defaults the SECURITY.MASTER after checking through these fields.

The Trade Currency , Trade Exch , Alt Sec Id and Alt Sec No fields are part of an associate multi-value set and can be used to define the various currencies and exchanges in which the security is allowed to be traded and also the relevant alternate index that is applicable. These fields can be set only if the Alt Index Check field is set to YES in the SM.PARAMETER .

If the user inputs a trade currency that is not defined in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER , ORDER.BY.CUST or SEC.TRADE application, an override is raised to indicate that the trade is not an approved trade currency. If a valid trade currency is input, then the system automatically defaults the stock exchange if it is set in these applications. The Primary Market field identifies the duplicate alternate index setup, and the SECURITY.MASTER with this field set-up is returned in order and trade screens when ISIN is inputted.

This live table is built when the above shown details are entered in the SECURITY.MASTER application and the record is authorised.

It is possible that a single ISIN could correspond to multiple records in SECURITY.MASTER in Temenos Transact . In such a scenario, the matching logic for determining the corresponding SECURITY.MASTER is based on the verification involving combination of:

- Case 1: Alternate identifier (other than ISIN) + cases, where only ISIN is provided without the MIC and trade currency.
- Case 2: ISIN + currency (trade) + exchange (MIC), when match is not found based on the above criteria. This is the next criteria to determine the match.
- Case 3: ISIN + currency (trade).

ISIN is checked based on the value in the ISIN Number field in SECURITY.MASTER . The matching logic selects only the securities that are not suspended, de-listed (security status and status date), blocked (blocking date), expired (expired) or matured (maturity date). The matching logic for determining the corresponding is explained below based on chronological order.

If an alternate identifier (other than ISIN) or ISIN alone is provided (without the Market Identifier Code (MIC) and trade currency) as part of the search criteria, the record in SECURITY.MASTER is identified based on the following steps:

1. If the alternate identifier (for example, Reuters Instrument Code (RIC)) matches a record in SECURITY.MASTER , select the record in SECURITY.MASTER . If there is no match, SECURITY.MASTER is returned and the order is not booked.

1. If trade exchange details are available (stock exchange in the transaction), check whether the cross-settlement is allowed with the stock exchange of the SM (provided the trade exchange is not the same as exchange in SM). This includes the ISIN exception check.

1. Check if the customer holds the position in any of the security. If yes, select the SM. If there is a match with multiple SMs, proceed to step 4.
2. If trade currency is available (in the transaction), check whether the trade currency is the same as the security currency of the SM. If there is a match with multiple SMs, proceed to step 5.
3. Select the SM with the Primary Market field set to Y. If there is a match with multiple SMs, proceed to step 6.
4. Prioritise the SM selection in the ascending order.

This case is invoked if the search input criteria includes the ISIN , Trade Currency and MIC fields.

1. If the ISIN corresponds to only one SM and the trade currency or security currency of the SM matches with the trade currency of the transaction, the transaction is booked using that SM. If the order or trade exchange (in the transaction) is not defined as one of the stock exchange for the SM, and there is no existing cross-settle record, security is not returned and the order is not booked. If there is a cross-settle record and the trade exchange (from transaction) does not match the stock exchange defined for the SM, and is not a part of the same cross-settle group in STK.EXC.CROSS.SETTLE , security is not returned and the order is not booked. ISIN exception check is also carried out as part of this evaluation.

1. If there are multiple records in SECURITY.MASTER with the same ISIN, check if the trade exchange (from transaction) is fungible with the stock exchange in SM based on the record in STK.EXC.CROSS.SETTLE . If the trade exchange is not the same as the stock exchange of the SM, check whether the record in STK.EXC.CROSS.SETTLE exists for the group. If Yes is selected, the check for the Isin Exception field must be done as defined in the previous section. If not, the exchanges are not considered fungible and security is not returned.

1. If there are multiple records in SECURITY.MASTER returned based on step 2, check whether the trade currency in the transaction matches with the currencies in SECURITY.MASTER (check the trade currency if it exists, otherwise check the security currency).

1. Check if the customer holds position in any of the security. If there is a match with one instrument, select the SM, else select the security where the security currency in SM is equal to the trade currency (from the transaction). If there is a match with multiple SMs, proceed to step 5.
2. Check if the stock exchange in SM is the same as the exchange in the transaction. If Yes, select the SM. If there is a match with multiple SMs, proceed to step 6.
3. Select the SM with the Primary Market field in SM set to Y. If there is a match with multiple SMs, proceed to step 7.
4. Prioritise the SM selection in the ascending order.

If match is not found at the end of the process, security is not returned.

This is invoked if the search input criteria includes the ISIN Number and Trade Currency fields.

1. If the ISIN corresponds to only one record in SECURITY.MASTER and the trade currency or security currency of the SECURITY.MASTER matches with the trade currency of the transaction, the transaction is booked using that SECURITY.MASTER . If the order or trade exchange (in the transaction) is not defined as one of the stock exchange for the SECURITY.MASTER , and existing cross-settle record does not exists, security is not returned and the order is not booked. If there is a cross-settle record and the trade exchange (from transaction) does not match the stock exchange defined for the SECURITY.MASTER and are not part of the same cross-settle group in the STK.EXC.CROSS.SETTLE , security is not returned and the order is not booked. ISIN exception validations are also carried out as part of this evaluation.

1. Check the trade currency in the transaction with the currencies in the record in SECURITY.MASTER (check trade currency if it exists, otherwise check security currency).

1. If there are multiple records in SECURITY.MASTER with the same ISIN, check if the trade exchange (from the transaction) allows cross-settling with the stock exchange in SM based on the record in STK.EXC.CROSS.SETTLE (including ISIN exception check). If the trade exchange (from transaction) is not the same as the stock exchange of the SM and if a record in STK.EXC.CROSS.SETTLE does not exist for the group, the exchanges are not considered fungible and security is not returned. If there is a match with only one SM based on the above criteria, select the SM. If there are multiple matches, proceed to step 4. If match is found, the order is not booked. The verification of cross-settle record involves checking whether the MIC of the stock exchange (in transaction) is present in any cross settle record and the ISIN not being in the ISIN exception list. If Yes, then the system checks the cross-settle record and processes as above. If not, proceed to step 4. If the stock exchange is not available in the transaction, this step is skipped and the system proceeds to step 4.
2. Check if the customer holds position in any of the security. If Yes, select the SM. If there is a match with more than one SM, proceed to step 5.
3. Select the SM with the security currency in SM equal to the trade currency (from transaction). If there is a match with multiple SMs, proceed to step 6.
4. Select the SM with the Primary Market field in SM set to Y. If there is a match with multiple SMs, proceed to step 7.
5. Prioritise the SM selection in the ascending order.

If match is not found at the end of the process, security is not returned.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the Trade Currency , Trade Exch , Alt Sec Id and Alt Sec No fields are not set for a security master, the defaulting logic works as per earlier methods (as discussed above).


##### Recording the Details of Minimum Holding

The SECURITY.MASTER application allows the specification of a minimum nominal that a portfolio must have in the respective stock it trades. The below screenshot shows a sample of the record in SECURITY.MASTER with the Minimum Holding field set to 200,000.

The multi-value field Min Hold Check in SC.PARAMETER contains the transaction codes against which the minimum holding validation is processed. The below screenshot shows a sample of a record in SC.PARAMETER with a value set in the Min Hold Check field.

The Min Hold Check field contains securities purchase (BUY) and securities sale (SEL). A SEC.TRADE utilising BUY for the purchase or SEL for a sale of a security validates against the minimum holding for the particular security and gives a suitable override message, if the total holding of the portfolio is less than the minimum holding. If the Min Hold Check field is left blank, minimum holding validation does not take place in the system.

The SECURITY.MASTER is shown above with the Minimum Holding field set to 200,000. Assume that the user wants to buy 100,000 of the stock through SEC.TRADE using BUY, the application checks whether the total holding for the security in the portfolio meets or exceeds the minimum holding requirement. In the above case, if the user already has 100,000 or more stocks, the total position for the security in the portfolio meets the minimum requirements. If it is not meet, the system generates an override message.

Similarly, when the user tries to sell the stock and if the total position for the stock in the portfolio falls below the minimum holding requirement, an override message is displayed. The only exception is that if the user tries to sell off all stocks in the portfolio, that is, if the position for the stock in the portfolio after the sale is zero, then override is not generated.


##### Blockage of All Activity in One Security

If the user enters a date in the Blocking Date field, the security is prohibited for any type of transaction from that date. The Narrative field can be populated with a free format text. As per the screenshot shown below the security is not available to trade from April 11, 2020.


##### Security Status

The status of the security is mentioned in the Sec Status field. The possible values are

- Def - Denotes that this security has defaulted coupon payments but the trading can continue.
- Del - Denotes that the security is de-listed from the exchange, or expired and trading cannot be performed on this security.
- Sus - Denotes that the security is suspended with an effective date and trading is not allowed.
- Non-Tradable - Denotes that the security is non-tradable with an effective date.

The date from which the Sec Status field is effective is defined in the Status Date field. The Sec Expired field denotes that it is an expired security, if marked as Y. The Scrip field denotes that this is a scrip, if it marked Y. Scrips denote a certificate that can be exchanged for a fractional share of stock. The security status fields are used to default the correct security master ID when an alternate index is used.


##### Ratings

In the SECURITY.MASTER application, the Rating field is used to describe the rating of a bond. Any input to this field must be defined on the EB.RATING application. The Rating Update field is used to identify the source of the bond rating recorded and is restricted to the following two options:

- Manual
- Automatic

The manual option indicates that the rating must be manually input by the user and the automatic option indicates that the rating is received through an external source as shown in the below screenshot.

The EB.RATING application is used to identify the rating of a bond or a particular record in SECURITY.MASTER application. The ID of this record is limited to five characters only.

The SI Hvcre Rating field can accept any of the following values:

- Default
- Good
- Satisfactory
- Strong
- Weak

The Agency Id field of EB.RATING can be linked to an EB.RATING.AGENCY application as shown in the below screenshot, if required.


##### Restricting Dealers Trading In a Security

The Grp Dept Code field in SECURITY.MASTER application captures the information regarding the dealers who can trade in that particular security. In most cases, these securities are not sourced from data providers, the usage of such securities are restricted. These securities can only be traded using SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER with external custody code defined in SC.PARAMETER or through SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TXN . Normal trades or transfers are not allowed for the securities with Grp Dept Code field being set. This field indicates that only the dealers or users under this department code can trade in the corresponding SECURITY.MASTER .


##### Attributes Relating To Funds

Funds are collective investments, which pools in the investor’s money. A fund manager uses that money to buy and sell a wide range of investments on behalf of the investor, in order to achieve a fund’s objective. The following fields allow the users to capture the fund attributes in the SECURITY.MASTER application.

| Field | Descriptions |
|---|---|
| Fund Inception | Holds the date of fund inception |
| Fund Issuer | Denotes the name of the fund issuer |
| Fund Advisor | Records advisors of the fund |
| Fund Sub-advisor | Records sub-advisors of the fund |
| Fund Manager | Records name of the fund managers |
| Registration Status | Indicates the countries where fund is registered |
| Trustee Name | Denotes the name of the trustee |
| Fund Classification | Defines any market categorisation or classification for the fund (based on investment objective, risk profile and so on) |
| Sub-Classification | Defines any sub-category or classification for the fund |
| Open or close ended | Denotes whether fund is open-ended or close-ended. The allowed values are OPEN and CLOSE. Open-ended funds allow the investor to invest anytime during the life of the fund, whereas the close ended funds allows the investor to invest only at the initial fund offer and does not allow the investor to redeem the fund until maturity. |
| Direct or Fund of Fund | Denotes whether it is a direct fund or a fund of fund. The allowed values are DIRECT and Fund of Funds (FOF). |
| Hedge Indicator | Denotes whether the fund is the hedge or not |
| Exchange Traded Fund | Denotes whether it is an exchange trade. The allowed values are YES and blank, where a blank field denotes non Exchange Traded Funds (ETF). |
| Derivatives Indicator | Indicates whether the fund uses derivatives as part of its investment or not. The allowed values are YES and NO. |
| Applicable Currencies | Defines the applicable currencies linked to the fund |
| Issue Size | Denotes the initial size in security currency |
| NFO Close Date | Denotes the initial fund offer closure date |
| Restriction | Allows the users to mention restrictions, if any |
| Closed To all | Denotes whether trading is not allowed. Allowed values are YES or NO |
| Closed To new | Denotes whether the fund is closed for new investors. Allowed values are YES or NO |
| Management Fee cap | Denotes the maximum stated management fee in percentage |
| Admin Fee Cap | Denotes the maximum stated admin fee in percentage |
| Currency related to minimum amount | Denotes the currency related to investment or redemption check file of CURRENCY |
| Amount of initial investment | Denotes the amount of initial investment |
| Amount of subsequent investment | Denotes the amount of subsequent investment |
| Minimum SIP amount | Denotes the minimum Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) amount |
| Minimum Redemption amount | Denotes the minimum redemption amount. This is an associated multi-value set from the Min Invt Ccy to Min Redem Amt fields. |
| 12M NAV High | Denotes the highest Net Asset Value (NAV) in last 12 months |
| 12M NAV Low | Denotes the lowest NAV in last 12 months |
| Subscription Start Date | Records the start date of subscription period. The hedge funds accept subscriptions on monthly basis, whereas, the others do on quarterly basis |
| Subscription End Date | Records the end date of the subscription period, which has to be filled along with the Subscription Start Date field |
| Redemption Start Date | Records the start date of the redemption period, whereas, some hedge funds allow redemption only during a certain period |
| Redemption End Date | Records the end date of the redemption period, which has to be filled along with the Redemption Start Date field |
| Minimum Holding Period | Denotes the allowed number of days the fund should be held before redemption or the number of notice days required for hedge funds |
| Minimum Holding Override | Indicates whether the minimum holding period can be overridden by paying a fee |
| Cool Cancel Period | Indicates the cooling or cancellation period, by when an investor can opt out of the contract |
| Switch Allowed | Indicates whether the switch is allowed for the fund and what type of switch is allowed. It is a multi-value field that accepts the values UNIT, AMOUNT, PERCENTAGE and ALL. |
| Unapproved | Denotes whether the fund is approved or not. If set to Yes, the fund is considered unapproved. If the field is blank, the fund is considered approved. Orders placed for unapproved funds are not allowed for grouping. |
| Wrap Eligible | Denotes whether fund is eligible for a wrap or not |
| Cut off time | Denotes the fund house cut-off time |
| Cut Off Time Zone | Denotes the time zone for the associated cut off time |
| Default Upfront | Triggers the defaulting upfront security. If set to YES, the upfront security from SC.PARAMETER is defaulted based on security currency and sub-asset type. |
| Entry Load | Indicates the entry load in terms of percentage |
| Exit Load | Indicates the exit load in terms of percentage |
| Switch Comm | Indicates the switching commission in terms of percentage. The switching commission is applicable on intra-fund switches and denotes the commission applicable while transferring from this fund. |
| Cool Cancel Period | Denotes the cooling period duration for the fund For example, if the cooling period is four days from the date of purchase of the fund, then the Cool Cancel Period field is populated with 4D. If an order is placed with the fund mentioned above and executed, the respective record in SEC.TRADE is created. Read SEC.TRADE section in trade creation for more information. |
| Entry Load Method | Identifies how the entry load is calculated and handled. There are different options as shown below: Bid Offer Bankpl The default method (if the field is blank) is BANKPL. This field is also available in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE application for company level setting. The field at SECURITY.MASTER level overrides the company level setting. |
| Exit Load Method | Identifies how the exit load is calculated and handled. There are different options as shown below: Netamt Bid Offer The default method is Bid Offer. This field is also available in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE for a company level setting. The field at SECURITY.MASTER level overrides the company level setting. |
| Entry Rebate | Indicates the rebate (if any) on entry load in terms of percentage. The rebate is applicable only when the Entry Load Method is Bankpl. |
| Till Date | Indicates the date until when the rebate on entry load is applicable |
| Sub Amt Adj | Determines whether the customer’s investment (subscription amount) needs to be retained or reduced based on the rebate or discount offered, if rebate or discount is offered on the entry load. If this field is set to No or left blank, the original subscription amount is retained (by grossing up the investment amount) and the customer is debited for the same after applying the rebate (and channel discount) on entry load. If this field is set to Yes, the subscription amount is reduced in line with the rebate or channel discount. The field at SECURITY.MASTER level overrides the company level setting. |


##### Determining SSI using Isin and Issuer Group

SSI can be set up for a group of ISINs or for all instruments issued by the same issuer. Where several ISINs or issuers need to be grouped together to set up a single SSI, then all the respective records in SECURITY.MASTER must have the same value updated in the Ssi Isin Group and Ssi Issuer Group fields.

If the values are not entered in the Ssi Isin Group field, then the SECURITY.MASTER ID is automatically defaulted in the Ssi Isin Group field and can be amended by the user. If value is not entered in Ssi Issuer Group field, the value in Issuer field is automatically defaulted in Ssi Issuer Group field and can be amended by the user.

##### Non-Stop Security Master Update

Instruments like equities and funds are traded in exchanges spread across the globe. New instruments are introduced on a regular basis and existing product attributes undergo changes constantly. All these can be updated in the system on a real time basis to enable investors to trade seamlessly and allow quick feedback and actions. To enable non-stop updates to the SECURITY.MASTER application, the Non-Stop (NS) module needs to be licensed. When the NS module is installed, the new records in SECURITY.MASTER can be created 24x7 and existing records in SECURITY.MASTER can be amended 24X7.

The following settings need to be noted:

- The Last Price and Sub Asset Type fields in the SECURITY.MASTER are required for calculations in terms of various COB processes. When these changes happen during a COB, it could lead to inconsistent calculations.

- Updates can continue to happen 24x7 to the Last Price field. In a multi-entity single instance installation, COB is initiated at different times during the day as the companies could be in different time zones. However, for any particular instance (company) where COB has started, the price in the Last Price field of the instrument at the beginning of the COB valuation batch, is used for all valuation and COB calculations until the COB is complete.

- Similarly, system uses the Sub Asset Type field at the beginning of the COB process for all COB related calculations. If the sub-asset type must be changed, it must be updated in the New Sub Asset Type field. Once the COB is completed, the value in the New Sub Asset Type field is updated as the Sub Asset Type field thus allowing the positions to be rebuilt.


##### Multi-companySECURITY.MASTERSetup

The SC.SM.MC.DEFINITION table allows users to set company-specific fields related to the SECURITY.MASTER application. The records in SC.SM.MC.DEFINITION should be manually created to capture the instrument level attributes specific to the company. The table contains only the SECURITY.MASTER fields that may vary by entity. Customer-related fields, such as Default Depository can be set in SC.SM.MC.DEFINITION , only when the respective customer records are not to be shared across the companies. The ID of a given record in the SC.SM.MC.DEFINITION table is the same as that in the SECURITY.MASTER application.

To create a record in the SC.SM.MC.DEFINITION table, the Nonshared SM field must be set to Yes for the respective record in SECURITY.MASTER . This can be set only when the Nonshared SM field in SM.PARAMETER is set to Yes.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Nonshared SM field should be set to Yes in both SECURITY.MASTER and SM.PARAMETER to enable creation of a record in the SC.SM.MC.DEFINITION table.

Applications and routines that call the SECURITY.MASTER application first checks the SC.SM.MC.DEFINITION table for the required details of the given company, provided the Nonshared SM field is set to Yes in the respective SECURITY.MASTER record. For those required details that are not available in the SC.SM.MC.DEFINITION table, the system refers to the details provided in SECURITY.MASTER for the corresponding record.

> **⚠️ Note:** The SC.SM.MC.DEFINITION application is not meant for margin-related fields. To set up different margin rates per company, the SC.MARGIN.RATES application should be used.

### 5.44  Limit


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Limits can be set at different levels in Temenos Core Banking. Customer level limits ensure that customers trade within the exposure allowed to them. Customer level limits are explained in a separate feature called online valuation.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Auto*, *Auto Settle Limit*, *Be*, *Bond*, *Book*, *Br Gross Am Trd*, *Br Net Am Trd*, *Check* ... +14 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Limits can be set at different levels in Temenos Core Banking. Customer level limits ensure that customers trade within the exposure allowed to them. Customer level limits are explained in a separate feature called online valuation.

Limits can also be set to restrict own book exposure to particular Issuers and/or counterparties. This feature explains Issuer and Counterparty limits.

- Issuer Limits - Limits can be set-up for issuers of securities, designated as bonds, which are traded for the bank's own portfolios.
- Counterparty Limits - The SEC.TRADE application also allows counterparty limits, that is, broker limits to be monitored for the delivery of the cash value for the security traded.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The configuration is made using the LIMIT.PARAMETER application.


##### Limit Parameter - Counterparty Limit

For counterparty limits, the link between the SEC.TRADE and the Limit products is defined in the LIMIT.PARAMETER application.


##### Limit Parameter - Issuer Limit

For issuer limits to set-up a limit reference for bonds, the conditions for the limit references applicable to SECURITY . MASTER are defined in the LIMIT.PARAMETER application.


##### Configuring Counterparty Limit inSC.STD.SEC.TRADE

In most cases, the broker’s side is not contractually settled. Hence, it is necessary to define the counterparty risk for the broker’s side and assign a limit for the risk the bank is willing to take against the broker. For trades with brokers, banks have the option to adjust the exposure value of the trade against this limit, either only for the own book trades or only for their customer trades or both, based on the setting in the Cpty Limit Chk field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE .

If the Cpty Limit Chk field is set to

- All – The system adjusts the counterparty limit for all trades, irrespective of the trade being customer or own book trade.
- Cust – The system adjusts the limit only for customer trades.
- Null – The system adjusts the limit only for bank’s own book trades.

Banks can also decide on whether to adjust the limit for the gross amount of the trade or the net amount to the counterparty, that is, to include or exclude the broker’s commission. The decision is based on the value in Exc Comm Cpty Limit field. If set to Yes, then the counterparty limit is adjusted with the gross amount to the broker (excluding commission) and if set to Null, the net amount, which is inclusive of the commissions is applied


#### 🔧 Working With

This section helps the user to understand the issuer and counterparty limits used in Temenos Transact .


##### Issuer Limits

The bonds are defined as securities with the Bond Or Share field set to B in SECURITY.MASTER application. The bank's own portfolios that are identified by the Dealer Book field set in SEC.ACC.MASTER record and are subject to issuer limit if the Check Limit field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER record is set to Y.

The limit amounts must be setup for each issuer before a limit reference is assigned to a security. The limit reference conditions for SECURITY . MASTER are defined using LIMIT PARAMETER . For example, the bonds can be set at a different limit reference to certificates of deposit. Whenever a trade takes place for a relevant security and portfolio, limit validation takes place and generates an override if the limit is exceeded.

The actual limit update relates to the Current Position amount on the relevant SC.TRADING.POSITION record. When the record is updated, the old limit is backed out and the new limit is used to update the limits, if the limit is greater than zero.

If the available limit is 10 million, current position is five million and new position is seven million (indicating a purchase of two million), the available limit is calculated as follows:

10m + 5m - 7m = 8 million


##### Steps to Setup Issuer Limit

1. Setup a limit reference for bonds as a child limit for the parent placements.
2. Define the conditions for the limit references applicable to SECURITY . MASTER .
3. A placement (parent) limit is setup for the customer 100307 (the issuer).
4. Setup a limit reference for the issuer in the SECURITY.MASTER record. The limit reference is not accepted if an issuer and active limit with a limit amount are not defined.
5. Activate the bank’s own book for limit validation. The Dealer Book is defined and Check Limit is set to Y.

Any transaction involving the bond for the book shown in the above screenshot is subjected to limit validation and updation.

This is viewed in the placements line of the Limit Summary/Customer Liability enquiry, which launches the relevant SC.TRADING.POSITION record.

The limit override is generated for the trade, if applicable.

The updated SC.TRADING.POSITION record is shown in the below screenshot.


##### Counterparty Limits

The Delivery Control ( SEC.DEL.CONTROL ) module monitors the delivery or receipt of Securities and interacts with the Limits system.

When a security trade takes place for a trading book involving a broker or counterpart, the participant’s (broker or counterpart) available limit is reduced by the net value of the trade. When settlement occurs, the broker’s available limit is increased by the value of the settlement. The type of limit set using the SC.DEL.INSTR application is used to define delivery instructions.

The Counterparty Limit field indicates whether counterpart limits are applied for the particular delivery instruction setup. If this field is set to YES, the Auto Settle Limit field indicates whether the limit is automatically settled on the value date of the trade. If Auto Settle Limit is Yes, the settlement of the limit takes place during the Temenos Transact end-of-day batch with full settlement and authorisation of the relevant SEC.DEL.CONTROL record.

Though a delivery is settled automatically, it can also be recorded manually if required. For manual settlement, the delivery amounts are manually updated in the SEC.DEL.CONTROL record. The limit remains until the recording of the complete delivery. Partial deliveries happen for the limits reduced by manual settlements (cash received or paid amount) recorded in the SEC.DEL.CONTROL record.

The input is allowed only for the Counterparty Limit and Auto Settle Limit fields if delivery is due ( To Be Recd Or Del is set to Y).

There are two types of broker delivery to cater for:

- Delivery against payment (DAP), where payment is made at delivery.
- Free of payment (FOP), where delivery or receipt happens without payment.

The risk of default for DAP deliveries is lesser than FOP deliveries. Therefore, each type allocates a different Limit product with the limit percentages allocated accordingly. For example, the DAP product is set as 10% of the value of the trade, and the FOP product is probably set at 100%.

For DAP settlements, the risk depends on the changes in the market price of the underlying security. Hence, the fraction of the transaction cash value is used. However, for a FOP settlement the risk must amount to 100% of the transaction, since the securities or cash movements are independent.

The Limit products are setup through the LIMIT.REFERENCE application.

In the above example, for DAP trades 15% of the actual cash value of the transaction and it is used to update the limit. In this instance, 100% of the cash value of the transaction is used to update the limits.

The link between the SEC.TRADE and the Limit products is defined in the LIMIT.PARAMETER application.

The DAP deliveries are assigned a separate limit, than for FOP trades.

It is also possible to set up different Limit products dependent on the type of security involved in the trade. The set-up is based on any field in SEC.TRADE application. If different counterparty Limit product is needed for say Bonds, a field to indicate if the security is a Bond needs to be included in the STANDARD.SELECTION of the SEC.TRADE application.

When a record in SEC.TRADE is input for a bank’s own book or customer portfolio, the system attempts to default a limit reference for the corresponding broker in the Cpty Limit Ref field, based on the value in Cpty Limit Chk in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE . When the Exc Comm Cpty Limit field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is set to Yes, the counterparty limit is adjusted with the gross amount in the Br Gross Am Trd field. Else, it is adjusted based on the value defined in the Br Net Am Trd field. Multiple brokers or counterparts are not allowed, if limit validation is required. The counterparty limit is reinstated when the trade is settled. If the trade is partially settled, the counterparty limit is reinstated to the extent of the value settled.

There must be a single or multiple customers for a bank’s own book, if the limit validation is required. In such instances, the overall broker amount is used to perform the limit validation.

The corresponding SEC.DEL.CONTROL application records the delivery information and settles the limit when delivery occurs. The Limit Summary/Customer Liability enquiry examines the current counterpart limits and enables the user to access the relevant component SEC.TRADE records.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Issuer and Counterparty Limits feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Issuer and Counterparty Limits feature.

### 5.45  LTV Determination based on Rating


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Loan-to-value (LTV) ratio is a financial term used by banks and other lenders to express the ratio of a loan to the market value of an asset. LTV of a bank is based on its credit policy and it changes from bank to bank. According to the credit policy, the LTV for an instrument will be derived based ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Agency Priority*, *Ltv Agency*, *Ltv Ranking*, *Ranking*, *Rating*, *Rating Agency*, *Rating Update*, *Rating Value*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Loan-to-value (LTV) ratio is a financial term used by banks and other lenders to express the ratio of a loan to the market value of an asset. LTV of a bank is based on its credit policy and it changes from bank to bank. According to the credit policy, the LTV for an instrument will be derived based on the attributes of the instrument, such as market, index, asset class, sub asset class, sector, and so on.

The rating of the instrument is also considered as an instrument attribute based on the LTV derived. Fixed income instruments such as bonds may have multiple sources of credit ratings from credit rating agencies, such as Moody’s, Fitch, Bloomberg, and so on. In such cases, banks define priorities based on which the bond rating from a credit rating agency is selected and LTV is derived based on that. When ratings are available from multiple sources, banks define rules such as ranking of the ratings and priority of the rating agency based on which the rating is determined.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The section details explains about the configuration required in SC.PARAMETER , EB.RATING.AGENCY and EB.RATING so that the functionality works successfully.


##### Setting Ranking inSC.PARAMETER

The Ltv Ranking field in SC.PARAMETER determines if the system has to consider ranking of the ratings when multiple ratings are available from multiple sources. This field can be marked as:

- Highest - The rating provided in the Rating field in the EB.RATING application with highest ranking is considered as the credit rating for determining LTV.
- Lowest - The rating with lowest ranking is considered as the credit rating for determining LTV.


##### Setting Priority inEB.RATING.AGENCY

When there are multiple sources of rating, the rating based on which LTV is determined is selected based on the priority of the rating agency. The priority of each rating agency is recorded in the Agency Priority field in EB.RATING.AGENCY .


##### EB.RATING

When there are multiple sources of rating for an instrument and if all the ratings are different, then the user has to derive at the credit ranking based on the internal ranking defined for each rating provided by each agency.

| Rank | Moody’s | S&P | Fitch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Long-term | Long-term | Long-term |  |
| 22 | Aaa | AAA | AAA |
| 21 | Aa1 | AA+ | AA+ |
| 20 | Aa2 | AA | AA |
| 19 | Aa3 | AA- | AA- |
| 18 | A1 | A+ | A+ |
| 17 | A2 | A | A |

The Ranking field in EB.RATING holds the ranking of each rating provided by the rating agencies.


#### 🔧 Working With

The system determines the appropriate rating to be used for LTV calculations and populates the Ltv Agency field with the rating agency whose rating has to be considered for determining the LTV.


##### Case 1: Only One Rating

If only one rating is available for the instrument, then that rating agency (rating available by default) is populated in the Ltv Agency field in SECURITY.MASTER . The Rating field refers to the EB.RATING record.


##### Case 2: Multiple Ratings with Different Rankings

The system checks the Ltv Ranking field in SC.PARAMETER . If the Ltv Ranking field in SC.PARAMETER is set as Highest, then rating with highest ranking and rating agency is considered for determining LTV. The Ltv Agency field is populated with the rating agency whose rating has the highest ranking.

If the Ltv Ranking field in SC.PARAMETER is set as Lowest, then rating with lowest ranking and rating agency is considered for determining LTV. The Ltv Agency field is populated with the rating agency whose rating has the lowest ranking. The Ltv Ranking field in SC.PARAMETER is set as Lowest, hence the rating with Ranking 1 is considered for determining LTV.


##### Case 3: Multiple Ratings with Same Rankings

After finding the ranking of each rating, if the rankings are same, then the system considers the rating provided by the rating agency with highest priority as the credit rating.

Both ratings have same rankings.

The system looks for the rating agency with highest priority.

As FITCH has the highest priority, system considers the rating provided by FITCH for determining LTV.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the Ltv Ranking field in SC.PARAMETER is not set, then the rating provided by the rating agency with highest priority is considered for determining LTV (as illustrated in case 3). The Ltv Agency field is populated with the rating agency which has the highest priority. If Ltv Ranking field in SC.PARAMETER is not set and the Agency Priority is not available for the rating agencies, then system populates the Ltv Agency field with the rating agency available in the multi-value set (such as Rating , Rating Agency , Rating Value and Rating Update in SECURITY.MASTER .

Based on the rating determined, the actual LTV is calculated by the Banking Framework module.
