> 
> **Key Fields:** *>Min Max Ccy*, *Acc Calc*, *Account No*, *Account Officer*, *Accrual Categ*, *Add on Fee Type*, *Adjust Fees*, *Adjust Value Date* ... +69 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Management or advisory fees are the fees charged by the bank for managing a customer’s portfolio. It is usually a percentage of the assets under management (AUM). This fee is for the advisory services offered and for effectively managing the customer’s portfolio. Temenos Transact has an extensive functionality to setup and charge Management Fees. The fees can be charged to the customer portfolios in a pre-defined frequency automatically.

> **⚠️ Note:** The management fees and advisory fees mean the same and are used interchangeably in this document.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The configuration of management fees or advisory fees in Temenos Transact is detailed in this section.


##### CONDITION.PRIORITY

This is the main parameter to be set for grouping customers and for charging fees. A record with ID as SC.MANAGEMENT must be setup. This application allows the user to set the various fields from CUSTOMER and/or SEC.ACC.MASTER applications that can be used to group customers for charging the respective fees.


##### SAFECUSTODY.VALUES

This application is used to setup both management and safe custody fees. It specifies the top-level information including the category, which posts the fees and transaction codes to be used. The management fees run frequency is controlled by the Charge Frequency field associated with the Charge Type field set to Ic (Investment Advisory charge). The different date ranges are specified in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES for prompt calculation of fees for the opening and closing accounts. The four ranges specified in the Calc Type field are:

| Options | Description |
|---|---|
| PERIODIC.OPEN | Used for an automatic charging run controlled by the frequency in the Charge Frequency field and the portfolio is open since the last automatic run |
| PERIOD.NORMAL | Used for an automatic charging run controlled by the frequency in the Charge Frequency field and the portfolio was open at the time of the last fee run |
| CLOSURE.NORMAL | Used for the fee calculation because a portfolio is closed which was open at the time of the last fee run |
| CLOSURE.OPEN | Used for the fee calculation because a portfolio is closed which is kept open since the last fee run |

The associated fields are Period Start , Period End, No Of Months , Deliv Start and Deliv End for which the input is alphanumeric. The symbols used and their representation are detailed in the below table.

| Symbols | Representation |
|---|---|
| - | Indicates days before current date |
| + | Indicates days after opening date |
| L | Indicates date of the last fees run |
| C | Indicates current system date |
| O | Indicates date of the portfolio opening |

The symbols are entered together with numeric input to build a date. For example:

- C-1 is the calendar date before the current date of the portfolio.
- O+1 is the calendar date after the opening date.

The management fees functionality works on a monthly basis. If the user wants the management fees calculated from the last run date up and the current date, the input for the Period Start field is L+1.

If the current working date is March 31 1999 and the last run was on December 311998, the values of the variables are L as 199812 and C as 199903. The system considers the last run date to be the first of the month, this translates a

of L and a

of C, as the period from December 1, 1998 to March 311999, which is four months. Whereas, the

of L+1 and a

of C gives a period from January 01 1999 to March 31 1999, which is three months.

Min Max Ccy , Min Amount , Max Amount and Def Min Max Ccy fields. The Country Check field includes the security domicile, security country domicile or stock exchange domicile based on which the system calculates the base amount for management fees. The Management Fee s can be calculated at the company level or per portfolio. This is based on the Company Calculation field. The calculation frequency set in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is displayed in the Management Fees calculation fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER irrespective of whether th e Management F ees are calculated company-wide or portfolio basis.

The management fees are calculated in the frequency setup at the company level, if the Company Calculation field is set to Y. The frequency cannot be amended in SEC.ACC.MASTER with this setup. The management fees are calculated for all portfolios simultaneously, that is, a company-wide management fees is run as the associated Company Calculation field is set to Y. The SC.SAFE.ADV.CHG job runs during the COB, checks the system date against this date, and if the date is less than the next working day, the system automatically calculates the management fees for all the customer portfolios in the system. If the Company Calculation field in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is set to No, the management fees is calculated in the frequency setup at the portfolio level. The frequency fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER can be amended. If not, the value in this field is display-only. The date of the last run and the ID of the SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION to which this portfolio is linked are also display-only information.

In addition to the periodic management fees calculation, the management fees are also calculated for a portfolio. Whenever a portfolio is closed (date defined in the Closure Date field in SEC.ACC.MASTER for the portfolio) the portfolio is charged for any pending fees. The safekeeping and management fee runs are calculated independently.

The posting of management fees is controlled from the SAFECUSTODY.VALUES by the Company Post field. If this field is set to Y, the posting of management fees for all portfolios in the company are posted together. If set to No, the SC.ADV.FEES.POST application is used to post the management fees for particular portfolios or all the portfolios of a particular account officer simultaneously.


##### Grouping Customers and Configuring Charges for each Group

The user must first group the customers and then setup a charging structure for each group to calculate the management fees for a portfolio.

Customers are grouped using the SCPM.GEN.CONDITION application. The record ID is any numeric value. The record opens with the fields defined in SC.MANAGEMENT record in CONDITION.PRIORITY . Values are assigned to the fields of SEC.ACC.MASTER to define the group. For example, Group 003 would be all portfolios with managed account as 5 and investment program as 1 whose customer sector is 1001 and customer’s nationality is US.

This makes any CUSTOMER (setup with the above defined criteria) to have the 003 record in SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION as default for calculating the management fees for its portfolios. A blank SCPM.GEN.CONDITION must exist in the system by default, that is, a record with no selection criteria in any of the fields except GB Description, that is Description field. The ID of this record must be 999.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Sc Application | Is followed by three associated fields allowing the user to link a portfolio to a particular record in SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION |
| Portfolio | Defines the portfolio or has the value ALL |
| Sc Def Group | Populated automatically by the system based on the SCPM.GEN.CONDITION to which the portfolio belongs |
| Sc Act Group | An user input field that can be used to set the actual group to be used for charges, a different group other than the group specified in Sc Def Group should be used |

This application defines the rule which is used to calculate the base amount used for calculating the management fee for that security type. The ID of this application can be a security number or an asset type or a sub-asset-type or all.

The fee can be calculated at a nominal or value level and the user may consider the highest or lowest calculated figure. The user can decide whether to request the calculation using the Average, Closing, Monthly Average, Close Period or Prev Month Close option for daily accrual exclusively.

| Calc Method | Description |
|---|---|
| Total | Total base amount for the portfolio's holdings is used to calculate the fees |
| Detail | For each Security Type, individual fees is calculated for each portfolio based on the base amount for each security and then accumulated to determine the total charge |


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details how the management fees are accrued, calculated and posted in Temenos Transact .


##### Calculating Management Fees

The management fees are calculated during the COB as part of the SC.SAFE.ADV.CHG batch job. The frequency of calculation is defined at a company or portfolio level with the SAFECUSTODY.VALUES application. The frequency of calculation is displayed in the management fees calculation fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER irrespective of whether the management fees is calculated company-wide or portfolio basis, as shown in the below screenshot.

The Advisory Frequency field defines the date of the next management fees run along with the frequency. If the Company Calculation field in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is set to No, the frequency is amended. If not, the value in this field is read-only. The date of the last run and the ID of SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION to which this portfolio is linked are also read-only information. The Portfolio Fees field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application is set to Automatic for the fees to be calculated automatically by the system. If it is set to Manual or None, then the system does not calculate any fees. This field defaults to Automatic for a customer portfolio.

During COB, the system validates the system date against the date in the Advisory Frequency field for any customer portfolio with the Portfolio Fees field set to Automatic. The management fees is automatically calculated if the date is before the next working day, and the value in the Managed Account field in SEC.ACC.MASTER relates to the values in the Acc Calc field in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES with the Charge Type as IC (Investment Advisory Change) in the SAFECUSTODY.VALUES application.


##### Posting of Management Fees

The management fees are posted in the following applications.

The details of the calculated management fees are entered in SC.ADVISORY.CHG . The account officer of a particular portfolio can review the calculated management fees and amend them, if necessary, before posting the management fees. Some of the fields that can be amended are Account No , Value Date and Local Fees Lcy fields.

The portfolios can be locked at this stage to block any new back-dated transaction affecting SC.ADVISORY.CHG . If the portfolio is locked in the calculated status and the locking date is equal to or greater than the advisory charge frequency date, back-date has no impact to SC.ADVISORY.CHG for a new back-dated transaction entered, if any. If the portfolio is unlocked and a new back-dated transaction is input, the transaction is processed.

Once all the records in SC.ADVISORY.CHG are reviewed, the management fees are posted, which depends on the SAFECUSTODY.VALUES application that is setup for the respective company. If the Company Post field is set to Y, the posting is made by setting the Post Charges field and setting the Charge Type field to Y in SAFECUSTODY.FEES application. The charges are posted automatically during the next COB.

The fees are posted online by running the SC.ADV.FEES.POST application. The Post Charges field must be set to No to enable this option. The SC.ADV.FEES.POST application is used to input and authorise the un-posted records in SC.ADVISORY.CHG for the company. The record ID of SC.ADV.FEES.POST (as shown in the above screenshot) is the value of the Account Officer field in SEC.ACC.MASTER . When the un-posted records are entered, system posts the fees for all portfolios whose SEC.ACC.MASTER has the value in the Account Officer field same as the ID of SC.ADV.FEES.POST . It is also possible to enter only certain portfolio(s) belonging to that officer, using the multi-value field Portfolio No and in this case, the fees for only these portfolios are posted.

It is also possible to post fees for all un-posted records in SC.ADVISORY.CHG by setting the ID of SC.ADV.FEES.POST as ALL. In this case, the Portfolio No field is a no input field.

If the Post Online field is set to No, the posting takes place in the Start of Day (SOD) by SC.SAFE.CHGS.ACC job. If Post Online field is set as yes, then as soon as SC.ADV.FEES.POST is authorised, the entries are posted. After authorising the record in SC.ADV.FEES.POST , the system automatically sets the Service Control field in TSA.SERVICE to START. This service processes all the records in SC.ADVISORY.CHG with Process Stage as calculated and posts the management fees.

Management fees are not recalculated, if a back-dated transaction is input. Recalculation of management fees in this case is possible if Asset Management module is installed.The portfolios can be locked once the fees are reconciled. This blocks any new back-dated transaction affecting the record in SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED . If the portfolio is locked in the posted status and the locking date is equal to or greater than the advisory charge frequency date, there is no impact to the record in SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED for a new back-dated transaction entered, if any. If the portfolio is unlocked and a new back-dated transaction is input, the repost or adjust entry is posted based on the setup at the portfolio level.

The Fee Adjustment Type field in AM.PARAMETER holds the options Repost and Adjust. The options cannot be modified and the default value is set to Adjust, which indicates the posting of differential fees between the already posted and newly computed fees. The Repost option indicates that the new fees are to be posted as a new entry and the old entries are to be reversed.

The Fee Adjustment Type field is also available in SEC.ACC.MASTER , which defaults the value from the AM.PARAMETER and it can be amended anytime at the portfolio level.

If a back-dated transaction is input with the portfolio in unlocked status, the system reposts or adjusts as per the setup in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application. The posting can be adjusted at the SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED level by setting the Adjust Fees field to Yes and by entering a valid value date in the Adjust Value Date field, which overwrites the setup at the portfolio level.

The values of the Adjust Fees field are Yes or Null. If this field is set to Yes, the Adjust Value Date field must be updated. The value date of posting the adjustment entries is entered in the Adjust Value Date field.

If the Adjust Fees field in SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED is set to Yes, the fees posted as part of SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED is adjusted in STMT.ENTRY as shown in the below screenshot.

If Adjust Fees in CATEG.ENTRY is set to Yes, the SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED is adjusted in CATEG.ENTRY as shown in the below screenshot.

If Adjust Fees in SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED is set to Null, the SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED is reposted in STMT.ENTRY as shown in the below screenshot.

If Adjust Fees in CATEG.ENTRY is set to Null, the SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED is reposted in CATEG.ENTRY as shown in the below screenshot.

Read the Close of Business User Guide for more information on the operation of TSA.SERVICE and its agents.


##### Accrual of Management Fees

The user can choose whether to request the calculation of management fees using the Average Closing Balance, Monthly Average or Prev Month Average option for daily accrual.

The daily accrual of fees can also be setup for safekeeping and management fees. Set the Perform Accrual in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES to Daily to enable the daily accrual option.

The accruals are always calculated for the exact number of days in the period. For example, if the charge period is from January 1 to March 31, the accrual is calculated for 41 days on February 10. On March 31, the accrual is calculated for 90 days. The EB.ACCRUAL application stores the accrual details. On fee realisation, the statement entries are raised for debiting the customer's account. The contra for the same is RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY for fee capitalisation. The anticipated charge for the period is reflected in a 'F' entry prior to realisation of the fee, which is viewed in the STMT.ENTRY application. After posting the fees, the Posting Stage field in the SAFEKEEP.HOLDING application is changed to Posted.

The STMT.ENTRY and RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY for the posting is shown in the below screenshots, respectively.

The accruals are calculated daily for the next calculation period including the fees pending, until the fee is posted. After the posting is done, the accruals are only for the current period fees. If the calculated fee is amended prior to posting, the accrual booked is adjusted to match the same. If the detail method is defined in SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION or SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION , the supporting details of the fee calculation can be viewed in the SC.DAILY.ACCRUAL.DETAIL application.

The category to which the user can post the monthly accruals must be defined by specifying an appropriate category code in the range of 11000 to 19999 in the Accrual Categ field, as shown in the below screenshot, where category 13333 is opened for this purpose.

The Perform Accrual field is set to Monthly to make the accruals as per the user's requirement.

The setup displayed in the above screenshot instructs the system to perform accruals at each month end. These accruals are based on the average daily balance for every month during the charge cycle, which in turn can be monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or annually as required. The accruals are performed every month end and posted to the account that is opened using value setup in Accrual Categ field. This is displayed in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES (as shown in the above screenshot) and the corresponding STMT.ENTRY is shown in the below screenshot.

The user can view the accrual posted to the suspense account USD-12011-00010001. The accruals are always made in local currency for which the currency is USD (US Dollars). The contra entry to the above accrual to suspense account is made to the Profit & Loss (P/L) account as shown in the below screenshot.

After posting the fees, the Process Stage field is displayed as Posted. The STMT.ENTRY also displays the respective entries as posted to the customer’s account.

This method is based on the average daily balance for each month du ring the charge cycle. This process enables the fees to be accrued monthly to Profit & Loss (P/L), while the contra entry is posted to an internal pre-defined suspense account. All calculations are performed in the local currency of the system. This method requires some additional setup and caters only if the charge frequency is global (that is, the same for all customers). It is not designed to run parallel with the management fee- calculation for monthly accrual (Read Calculating Management Fees for Monthly Accruals for more information).

If the bank is already using monthly accruals calculation, the user must first ensure that the current charge cycle for all customers are completed. The user must ensure that the Company Calculation field in the SAFECUSTODY.VALUES application is set to Y, so that all the customers are charged simultaneously for the frequency defined in the Charge Freq field of the same record.

The advisory fee accrual entries are raised in the month-end as follows:

- DR - Advisory fee accrual account ( Advisory Accr Acct in SEC.ACC.MASTER )
- CR - P&L ( Cr Categ Code in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES for Charge Type is IC)

If the user adjusts the calculated charges in the SC.ADVISORY.CHG , the system passes the adjustment entries to adjust the accruals. If the charge is increased, then:

- DR - Advisory fee accrual /account with the increase
- CR - P&L with the increase

If the charge is decreased, then:

- CR - Advisory fee accrual account with the decrease
- DR - P&L with the decrease

On the final posting of charges, the accounting that follows is:

- CR - Advisory fee accrual A/C
- DR - Customer’s charge account

The accruals of advisory charges are posted in unique accrual Profit and Loss (P&L) category codes. The Advisory Accr Pl and Advisory Accr Acct fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER application posts the accruals of advisory. The Advisory Accr Pl field defines the accrual PL category for advisory.

The Advisory Accr Acct field allows internal accounts of different category, which are not specified in the Accrual Categ field in the SAFECUSTODY.VALUES application.

The discount on advisory fees are posted to a different P&L category code in the SAFECUSTODY.VALUES application. The Discount Pl field in SC.ADVISORY.CHG is used to post the discount on advisory. This multi-value field indicates the P&L category for discount posting. During accruals, the Accrual Categ in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES takes precedence over the one in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES . During discount postings, the discount PL category specified in the charge records takes precedence over the value in Discount Pl in the SAFECUSTODY.VALUES application.

The discount on advisory fees that is posted is tagged to a different P&L category code in the SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED application. The Discount Pl field in SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED is used to post the P&L category for discount posting. This field is defaulted from SAFECUSTODY.VALUES but it can be overridden.

If the transaction fee is amended post review, the Charges Lcy field is adjusted automatically. The total fee in the Charges Lcy field can also be amended before posting. The total fee is posted to the account in the Account No field (one entry is posted to the account for the consolidated fee and the other entry to the P&L account).

##### Posting Periodical Fee by Cumulating Monthly Charges

This section explains the monthly fee accrual calculation and posting the accrued fee on the cut-off date without recalculation.

| Application Name | Fields | Values |
|---|---|---|
| SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION | Calc Method | Total/ Total.addon |
| SAFECUSTODY.VALUES | Perform Accrual | Monthly |
| SCPM.CHARGE.PARAMETER | Average Closing | Month.Average |

The process above continues across all months until it reaches the posting date. The system adds the fee charged for each month and builds the SC.ADVISORY.CHG record when the posting date is reached. The recalculation of fees is not performed.

Read Storing Monthly Fee Details in Safe Custody Fees for more information.


##### Locking Portfolio Value After Calculating Fee

When the Lock Aum field in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is set for IC, then any backdated transaction or market price change for previous month or period does not rebuild SC.ASSET.BAL or SC.ADV.FEES.ACTIVITY or SC.ASSET.BAL.POSTED . The system rebuilds SC.ASSET.BAL or SC.ADV.FEES.ACTIVITY only for the current month. Thus, there are no changes in fees accrued or posted due to backdated transaction or market price change since the total average asset balance on which the fees are charged remains frozen.


##### Add-on Fees for Advisory Charges

Add-on fees for advisory charge is charged in addition to the standard administration or management fees collected by the bank. Add-on fees are configured for specific asset type or sub-asset type or instrument and can have a specific minimum and/or maximum amount or neither for each fee type.

When Cumulate Post field is set to Yes for the Charge Type Ic in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES , and the Calc Method field in SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION is set to Tot.addon, then during every month end:

- The system estimates the total fees for the portfolio based on the total average asset balance. The total average asset balance is based on the rules for deriving the base amount. The fee details given in the Tot Comm Code and Tot Percent fields in SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION are used to calculate the total standard administration fees.
- In addition to the total fees, the add-on fee is calculated for each position based on the asset type or sub-asset type or security number. The system takes the value of each position, determines the rate, and calculates the fee for each position. When the add-on is set at: Asset type or Sub-asset type - The fee is calculated separately for each position within that asset type or sub-asset type. If for a portfolio six securities fall within the same sub-asset type, the system calculates the add-on fee separately for each of the six security master positions and checks minimum and maximum for each position. Security and for a sub-asset type and the security falls within that sub-asset type – The system calculates the add-on fees for the security and again for that sub-asset type. Thus, the same position can have two add-on fees.
- Different FT.COMMISSION.TYPE records can be configured for various add-on fees. These details are to be set up in SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION with Security Type prefixed with AD to indicate it’s an add-on fee charge, the respective commission type mentioned in Det Comm Code and the percentage to be applied in Det Percentage .

> **⚠️ Note:** Add-on fee is calculated for an asset or sub-asset type pertaining to a security. That is, add-on fees are not applicable to other asset types such as fiduciary, cash account and so on. When an add-on fee is set for a security master record and the rules for those are not defined in SCPM.CHARGE.PARAMETER , the system checks the definition of sub-asset type or asset type or ALL definition to determine the asset balance. Add-on fees cannot be configured when Security Type = ALL.

The monthly calculation considers the following:

- Total Fee Cumulative of minimum and maximum up to the current month and then determine the monthly fee. If the sum of fees for previous months and the current month is less than the cumulative minimum, the cumulative minimum is considered. If the sum of fees for previous months and the current month is more than the cumulative maximum, the cumulative maximum is considered. Else, the cumulative system-calculated fee is considered.
- Add on Fee For each position where add-on fee is applicable, Cumulative of minimum and maximum up to the current month and then determines the monthly fee. If the fee for previous months plus the current month is less than the cumulative minimum, the cumulative minimum is considered. If the fee for previous months plus the current month is more than the cumulative maximum, the cumulative maximum is considered. Else, the cumulative system-calculated fee is considered. A single accrual entry is posted by cumulating the total fee and add-on fees up to the current month – cumulative fees accrued till previous month.

The above process continues across all months till the posting date is reached. When the posting date is reached, the system adds the fee accrued for each month (total fee plus add-on fee) and builds the SC.ADVIOSRY.CHG record. No recalculation of fees is done.

The attached excel shows the calculation logic on how the system cumulates and posts the fees for total and add-on

Read Calculation logic on how the system cumulates and posts the total and add-on fees .

When Cumulate Post in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is Yes for Charge Type Ic, every month when the accrual is calculated, the system stores the average asset balance on which the fees are charged, the minimum amount (based on the Overall Min Amt field in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ), the maximum amount (based on the Overall Max Amt field in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ) and the system-calculated amount (based on the Calc Type field in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ) for each position where the add-on fee is applicable in SC.PORT.PERIODIC.FEE .

A record is created for each position when the add-on fee is applicable. The ID of the table is appended with IC to indicate that the charges pertain to the advisory charges.

The Add on Fee Type field shows the asset type or sub-asset type or security master ID based on which the add-on fee is charged for the positions. The below screenshot shows that the add - fee is calculated for security 100100-000 based on the sub-asset type definition.


##### Backdated Rate Change

When the Bv Rate Change field is set to Ic in SC.PARAMETER , then the system recalculates the fees based on the rate changes with backdated effective date. When a backdated rate change is input in SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION , as a part of the end-of-day process (COB) Temenos Transact automatically detects that a backdated modification has taken place and recalculates the fee accrued.

Backdated rate change is triggered either

- Due to an amendment to an existing SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION record such as Rate change – by attaching a new FT.COMMISSION.TYPE in Det Comm Code or Tot Comm Code Percentage on the charge calculated – by amending either the Det Percentage or Tot Percent Change in the calculation of basis amount – by amending Security Type Including new add-on fees to the existing group condition.
- Or by creating a new SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION with a backdated ID.

If new addon fees are added, then the system calculates the add on fees for the securities and updates the new fees to be debited from the customer.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system does not recalculate fees if any other attributes in SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION is changed.

If the tariff change is within the current fee period, the system reworks the accruals for the current fee period. If the tariff changes back dates to the previous period, then the system reworks on the previous period charge and updates in SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED .


##### Backdated group change

This application is built when the Enable Sc Customer Charge field in CONDITION.PRIORITY SYSTEM record is set to Sc.management. This application supports dated records in the ID format, as * * .

Refer to the Calculation of Safe Custody Fees section for more information about the recalculation of fees due to backdated rate change.

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The Securities (SC) module allows trading in equities, bonds, mortgage backed securities and funds. The product supports trading, position keeping, valuation and maintaining the tax lots. Both, exchange traded and over the counter orders are supported. The Securities product may be used by banks trading on their own behalf, trading on behalf of their customers or offering their customers brokerage services.


##### Product Configuration

The parameters are one of the most important applications in Temenos Transact which define how the product functions for a particular module. Parameter records contain critical settings and default values that the system uses for various functionalities. Many of the settings cannot be changed once the system is live. Hence, the parameters must be set correctly before creating transactions.

This document describes some of the key parameter records that need to be set in the Securities (SC) module before transactions can be processed. While individual feature documents highlight the parameter settings for that particular feature, this document provides a high-level overview. The main parameter applications present in the SC module are listed in the following table:

| Parameter File | Transaction ID | Description |
|---|---|---|
| SC.PARAMETER | Not Applicable | Main parameter setup for the SC module to function properly |
| SC.STD.SEC.TRADE | SEC.TRADE | Execution of securities |
| SC.STD.POS.TRANSF | SECURITY.TRANSFER POSITION.TRANSFER | Transfer of Securities Transfer Portfolio Contents |
| SC.STD.CLEARING | SC.CLEARING.SYSTEM | Clearing Systems |
| SC.STD.BOND.LEND | BOND.LENT.MASTER | Bond Lending |
| SC.TAX.PARAMETER | TAX | Coupon and Dividend Tax |
| VAULT.PARAMETER | VAULT.EXPECT | Safe Custody Control |

Apart from the major SC parameters, there are other parameters that are specific to certain functionalities and these are detailed in the relevant feature document. In a multi-company environment, it is mandatory for the user to set up the parameter files for all companies.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Valuation Subr | Controls the default valuation routine required to produce valuation reports |
| Local Stock Exch | Holds the ID of the stock exchange where the company usually trades. The ID of the local stock exchange is already defined in the STOCK.EXCHANGE application. |
| Bulk Limit | Allows the user to specify the number of transactions required before running a background bulk processing. For example, this field in SC.PARAMETER enables the user to enter hundreds of individual customer purchases or sales of securities and release the session while the transaction runs in the background. |
| Security Format | Enables the user to define the main ID for the record in the SECURITY.MASTER application, which holds the list of the various securities in which the organisation trades. The default format is (######-###). Example: The default format enables the user to define a security ID as 000001-000. This format supports the Telekurs security identification numbers. If Telekurs format is not required, the user can define any format using up to 12 characters. The user can use only the # and - characters in both the Telekurs and user-defined format where # indicates a numeric equivalent and – separates the suffix part of the ID. This field cannot be modified once the record in SC.PARAMETER is authorised. |
| Alternate Index | Enables the user to specify an alternative means of accessing individual security records for examination or entry into the transactions and enquiries. This field also enables the user to use other system IDs, such as the EUROCLEAR Clearance ID (if any), as well as the main ID. Usage of this field is no longer recommended. Instead, use the ALT.SEC.PARAMETER application. |

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Synthetic Port | Indicates the synthetic portfolio used for parent child processing. This portfolio is updated in the customer side of parent transaction. |
| Synthetic Cpty | Indicates the synthetic counterparty used for parent child processing. The counterparty specified here is updated into broker side of child portfolio. |
| Synthetic Susp Cat | Used for parent child processing. The internal account category specified in this field is used for entry processing in parent and child trades. For parent and child trade, customer and broker side account is the internal account formed using this category. |
| Trade Creation | This field is set to Parent Child for creating parent child trades on execution |
| Authorise Child | If set to Yes, the child trades are authorised on authorisation of the parent. Child trades are also automatically authorised, if the Authorise Trade field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS of the parent is set to Yes. |
| Upd Child Link | Determines whether the child link records such as SC.CHILD.ORDER.LINK and SC.CHILD.TRADE.LINK are to be updated. These backend files hold a link between the parent and child orders and trade. This is useful for reports and enquiries. |
| Parent Child Depo | Specifies whether parent trades are to be created based on each depository. The value is defaulted to the similar field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS . |
| Bulklog Purge Days | Indicates the number of days to hold the purging of SC.BULK.EXCEPTION.LOG. The records with value date prior to the date calculated from the current date are purged. |
| Order Alloc Subr | Accepts an API that is used for the allocation of the executed nominal among different customers in the case of bulk orders. The arguments to an API are SEC.OPEN.ORDER record and SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record in dimensioned format. If the API is defined in the Order Alloc Subr field, the prorating process calls the local API to allocate the nominal for customers based on the API logic. |

The SC.STD.POS.TRANSF application contains the company-level default values, which are used to process the POSITION.TRANSFER , SECURITY.TRANSFER and SC.BULK.TRANSFER transactions. It allows the user to specify the default charge category for the bulk charges and specify the status for the record in SECURITY.TRANSFER generated from the bulk transfer. The initial fields contain many CATEGORY and TRANSACTION codes relating to debit and credit transaction entries posted during the transfer out and in as shown in the screenshot below:

For a POSITION.TRANSFER transaction, the system defaults to a delivery instruction type as mentioned in the Del Instrn field.

If the Short Transfer field is set to Yes, the system allows transfer of short position.The Ofs Source and Default Version fields are used to create and authorise the applications used in the SC.BULK.TRANSFER application. The Stamp Tax Categ field is used for defaulting category for stamp tax posting from security transfer, where the Stamp Tax Dr Tr field defines the debit transaction code for the stamp tax posted and the Stamp Tax Cr Tr defines the credit transaction code for the stamp tax posted.

The value in the Default Counterparty field should be a valid record in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application with any one of the following customer types such as BROKER, COUNTERPARY or CLIENT. This is the default counterparty at the company level for transfers.

The SC.TAX.PARAMETER application is used to define stamp tax. Different tax rates can be applied based on the application, security, stock exchange, sub-asset type and so on.

The Tax Code field defines the tax code used to calculate the tax amount. This field accepts the tax code defined in either the TAX application or the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application. The ID of the record in TAX.TYPE.CONDITON should be prefixed with *. If this field has a defined TAX.TYPE.CONDITION value, the system calculates the tax based on the tax codes defined for the respective customer group defined in the record in TAX.TYPE.CONDITION . If this field has a defined tax code, the system performs tax calculation based on the tax code record defined in the TAX application.

Rules of the clearing systems are set in this application. The Sec Depo Ac field must be a valid record in CUSTOMER.SECURITY .

This table contains company-level default values, which are used when processing bond lending transactions.

Before Temenos Transact begins to control the contents of the vault, it is mandatory to complete the configuration of the VAULT.PARAMETER application, which enables the system to identity the vault(s), depositories or areas within the vault. The VAULT.PARAMETER application is required for each company to use the vault application facilities provided by Temenos Transact . The vaults must also be set up on the records in CUSTOMER and CUSTOMER.SECURITY before they are defined in the VAULT.PARAMETER application. This application controls whether vault (safecustody functionality in Temenos Transact ) is turned on or off, and which depositories are turned on or off. If the vault is active, then records in the VAULT.EXPECT application can be produced from the VAULT.CONTROL application.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The model parameters for the Securities (SC) module are explained below:

The SC.PARAMETER application is the main parameter record for the SC application that defines the company level default values which must be setup for the SC module to run correctly. These default values apply irrespective of the application, transaction type or user. Each record is created against each company running the SC module. The following are the key features of this application:

- Each attribute of this parameter are specific to the company.
- Local stock exchange and default stock exchange can be setup at company level.
- The Alternative Index field enables the user to specify an alternative means of accessing individual security records for examination or entry into any of the various transactions and enquiries.
- Some fields require the specification of a category or a record from another application.
- If the user wishes to perform price integrity validation on certain asset types, then the Price Asset field is specified with the valid ASSET.TYPE record. If the user wants to use the Corporate Actions (CA) system to process their bond redemptions, this field contains the DIARY.TYPE ID that is used to process the redemptions.
- The Cg Base Update field in the SC.PARAMETER application allows the user to control the update of the capital gains transaction base. If this field is set to Yes, the system maintains a transaction base that can be used to display the capital gains positions on portfolio trading in a security.
- The Source Tax Split and Local Tax Split fields can be used in conjunction when processing the CA events. If these fields are set to Yes, separate source or local tax accounting entries are posted. The customer is posted with the gross amount for the cash entitlement and a separate source or local tax amount.
- The Hub Company field specifies the centralised HUB, where all SC and DX trades take place. This is particularly relevant in the customer setup, where trades are always done in a central location.
- The Actual Settlement field defines whether the trades or corporate is settled manually or automatically (contractual settlement).
- The Default Ccy Market field defines the currency market used for all FX Intraday transactions and valuations.
- The COB Ccy Market field defines the currency market used for all portfolio or position valuations done during COB.
- If the user wishes to perform manual grouping of orders, then the Group Order field should be specified as ‘Manual’.
- When the CA Separate Orders field is set to Yes, the system creates a separate order for each entitlement for events such as, Reinvest, Rights and Oddlot.
- When the No Def Opt Inst field is set to Yes then the system does not send MT565 for the quantity selected in the default option.

The SC.STD.SEC.TRADE application advises the system on how to process a SEC.TRADE transaction. This includes the buy or sell and other trade related transactions, and mainly the processing rules. The following are the key features of this application:

- The initial core fields contains the CATEGORY and TRANSACTION codes which relate to debit and credit transaction entries that are posted during trade capture.
- The Synthetic Port field is used for parent child processing. This portfolio updated in the customer side of parent transaction and the Synthetic Cpty field is used for parent child processing. The counterparty specified here is updated into broker side of child portfolio.
- The Authorise Child field accepts a value Yes, to denote that child trades are to be authorised on authorisation of parent. Child trades are also automatically authorised, if the Authorise Trade field in the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS application of parent is set to Yes.
- The Consolidate Fx field indicates whether the user wants the system to total the currency requirements of each customer into a single amount for which a consolidated rate can be obtained from the Forex dealers and entered into the Consol Rate field of the SEC.TRADE transaction.
- The Currency Calendar field is defined so that the system calculates the settlement date (value date) for security transactions based on both the holiday tables of the currency’s country and the stock exchange country.
- The Transmit Order field is set as ‘Yes’ to transmit the grouped orders.
- The Broker Only Cty field holds the synthetic counterparty for Broker only transaction. This is used for the Broker Only Trade (Customer Vs Intermediate Broker).
- The Broker Only Port field holds the Bank’s synthetic portfolio for Broker only transaction. This is updated in the Customer portfolio for the underlying trade (Intermediate Customer Vs External Broker) in Broker only processing.
- The Broker Only Cat field holds the suspense category, which is used for Broker only processing.

The SC.STD.POS.TRANSF application contains the company level default values which are used to process the POSITION.TRANSFER and SECURITY.TRANSFER transactions. It allows the user to specify the default charge category for the bulk charges and specify the status for SECURITY.TRANSFER or FUNDS.TRANSFER record generated from the bulk transfer. The following are the key features of this application:

- For a POSITION.TRANSFER transaction, the system defaults to a delivery instruction type as contained within the SC.DEL.INSTR application. If delivery instructions are not contained within the POSITION.TRANSFER application, the Delivery Instr field must contain the exact user requirement.
- The Ofs Source and Ofs Version fields are used to create and authorise the applications used in SC.BULK.TRANSFER .
- Each business transaction within Temenos Transact is allocated a category code which enables the construction of reports that give an accurate view of the bank's operations.
- The Stamp Tax Categ field is used for defaulting category for stamp tax posting from security transfer, where the Stamp Tax Dr Tr field defines the debit transaction code for the stamp tax posted and the Stamp Tax Cr Tr defines the credit transaction code for the stamp tax posted.
- The value in the Default Counterparty field should be a valid CUSTOMER.SECURITY record with any one of the following customer types BROKER, COUNTERPARY or CLIENT. This is default counterparty at the company level for transfers.

The SM.PARAMETER application is used to store the SECURITY.MASTER related parameters that are shared across companies. Only one record is allowed with the ID as SYSTEM. The following are the key features of this application:

- The Price Qual Format field indicates if the cum and ex markers are to be in SWIFT format or not.
- The Isin Validation field determines whether the ISIN code entered through the SECURITY.MASTER application is validated. If this field is set to Yes, the check digit must be as calculated by system.
- The Alpha Key field enables the input of alphanumeric characters in the SECURITY.MASTER ID. If this is set to Yes, the system does not perform the formatting of SECURITY.MASTER reference, based on the format specified in the Security Format field in the SC.PARAMETER application.
- The Alt Index Check field is used to default the SECURITY.MASTER ID, when the user enters an alternate identifier like ISIN in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER or SEC.TRADE records. Read the Alternate Security Index section in Instrument Master feature under Securities User Guide for more information.
- The Sec Domicile Ssi field determines whether the security domicile must be considered for SSI search, when the Pl Sett field is not given in the SECURITY.MASTER record. Read the Settlement feature under Securities user guide for more information.
- The non-shared SM allows the user to create a record in SC.SM.MC.DEFINITON to define company specific security attributes.

The SC.LOCAL.TAX.PARAM application is the main parameter application which holds the local tax that is applicable for SC. This can be defined for specific TXN.TAX.CODE and COMPANY or SYSTEM. The following are the key features of this application:

- This application defines the tax basis for calculating the withholding tax.
- The Tax Basis field indicates the type of transaction basis for the allocation and unallocation of nominal (for example, FIFO, LIFO and so on).

The SC.ORDER.ROUTING application is the main parameter to define the routing of orders at company level. The routing conditions can be set-up based on any field in SECURITY.MASTER or SEC.ACC.MASTER applications. Record ID of this application can be SYSTEM or a Company ID.

The following are the key features of this application:

- The Default Company and Default Portfolio fields are set as the default routing conditions if all other conditions fail to match.
- If the Exe Orig Comp field is set to Yes, then the routed order is executed in the originating (Bank) company and the execution is mirrored in the route-to (Broker-dealer) company.

The SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.PARAM application is the main parameter application that holds the details applicable for personal assets set up in the core banking system.

The user can define the following list of fields based on the company and are required to create the personal assets:

- Transaction Codes (Buy, Sell, Write-In, Write-out, Maturity, Liability In, and Liability Out)
- Suspense Category
- Price Source
- Industry type
- Wash Depository
- Coupon Tax Code
- Stock Exchange

The SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TYPE application enables the user to record the attributes relevant to each Personal Asset Type. The ID of this application is a SUB.ASSET.TYPE record.

Application allows the user to enter if SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.PARAM record exists for the company.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| SECURITY.MASTER | A valid SECURITY.MASTER can be defined as the ID (100040-000) |
| SUB.ASSET.TYPE | A valid SUB.ASSET.TYPE can be defined as ID (S-102) |
| ASSET.TYPE | A valid ASSET.TYPE can be defined as ID (A-10) |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| DEFAULT.PRODUCT | Allows the bank to report Profit and Loss earned as trailer fees. |
| ACCRUAL.METHOD | Accrual method can be set to, DAILY - If the field is set to DAILY, then daily accrual of trailer fees occurs. NULL - If the field is set to NULL, then accruals happens on the respective calculation dates. |
| TR.FEE.SUSP.CAT | Allows to set suspense category account which is treated as a wash account for posting capitalisation entry and apportioning of difference amount. |
| REIMBURSE.ALLOWED | This field must be set to ‘Yes’, if the bank decides to reimburse the trailer fees to their customers. |

The SC.SM.TAX.CONFIG application provides the flexibility to define common tax set-up for securities based on its attributes. The user can define the TAX for group of securities based on Sub Asset Type or Asset Type. The record ID for Sub Asset Type begins with S- and for Asset Type A- .

Using the below set of fields, the tax set-up for a group of securities can be defined based on a condition or set of conditions.

- The SM Attributes field holds the field names from SECURITY.MASTER
- The Attribute Operand field holds the list of available operands
- The Attribute Value field holds the values against the field specified in SM Attributes
- The Sc Tax Code field holds the security tax code
- The Coupon Tax Code field holds the tax code to calculate tax on dividends and coupons
- The Txn Tax Code field holds transaction tax code for the security

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Field Name.1 | Indicates the field name from which the value needs to be retrieved. The allowed values are Nationality, Date of Birth, First Name and Surname. |
| Field Value.1 | Indicates any valid field from CUSTOMER application, which holds the value specified in FIELD.NAME . |
| No of Char.1 | Holds the number characters that needs to be extracted for framing the CONCAT. |

The SC.CSDR.PARAMETER application is a company level parameter to define the tolerance amount, which is to be linked with the settlement amount, depository wise.

Based on the settlement amount, the system applies tolerance check and process the settlement if the difference between the settlement amount in the confirmation and the intended settlement is within the tolerance range.

The difference is posted to P&L or internal suspense account defined in SC.PARAMETER .

- Depository – The ID of the depository for which the tolerance check is required.
- Transaction Amount – The actual transaction amount of the trade.
- Tolerance Amount – The tolerance range to apply the tolerance check.
- Bilateral Cancellation – To denote whether bilateral cancellation is applicable for this depository.

### 5.48  Mortgage Backed Securities


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A mortgage-backed security (MBS) is a type of asset-backed security, which is secured by a mortgage or collection of mortgages. Such security provide periodic payments, which is similar to coupon payments. Also, the mortgage must have originated from a regulated and authorised Financial Institution ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accrual Start Date*, *Amt*, *Cap Rate*, *Consid+Int*, *Consideration*, *Cpn Date*, *Cpn Rate*, *Factor* ... +4 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A mortgage-backed security (MBS) is a type of asset-backed security, which is secured by a mortgage or collection of mortgages. Such security provide periodic payments, which is similar to coupon payments. Also, the mortgage must have originated from a regulated and authorised Financial Institution (FI).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

MBS consists of one basic product (a mortgage pass-through Security (SC)) and two Derivative (DX) products (collateralised mortgage obligations and stripped mortgage backed securities).

Each loan is for USD 100,000 and total loans are USD 1 million.

There are 10 mortgage loans and cash flow from these loans as shown in the below screenshot. For clarity, it is assumed that the amount in each loan is USD 100,000. Hence, the aggregate value of the 10 loans is USD 1 million. The cash flows are monthly and consist of:

- Interest
- Scheduled principal repayment and
- Prepayments

The risk element in the above cash flow corresponds to the pre-payments. The more the number of loans owned by the investor, the better the chances of predicting the pre-payment risk.

If an entity purchases all the 10 loans and pools them, those loans can be used as collateral for the issuance of a security. This includes the cash flow from the security reflecting the cash flow from the 10 loans. If 40 units of this security are issued, each unit is initially worth USD 25,000 (USD 1 million divided by 40). Each unit is entitled to 2.5% (1/40) of the cash flow. This security created is called a mortgage pass-through security.

Although the total amount of pre-payment risk is not changed, an investor with an amount less than USD 1 million can be exposed to the total pre-payment risk of all 10 loans, instead of encountering the risk of an individual mortgage loan. Moreover, by selling a pass-through, the investor can dispose all the 10 loans than disposing each loan one by one. The pass-through is a more efficient transactional vehicle for investing in mortgages, than purchasing individual mortgages.


##### Collateralised Mortgage Obligation (CMO)

The investor is exposed to total pre-payment risk. The distribution of the principal (both scheduled and pre-payments) is done on some prioritised basis instead of distributing the monthly cash flow on a pro-rate, as in the case of the pass-through type.

| Class | Par Value (USD) | Units | Each Unit’s Entitlement (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 400,000 | 50 | 2 |
| B | 350,000 | 100 | 1 |
| C | 250,000 | 200 | 5 |


##### Mortgage Backed Securities - Security Transactions

The SEC.TRADE application does the necessary processing in case the underlying security is identified as an MBS type, such as a Ginnie Mae (GNMA) issue. The reference to the SECURITY.MASTER record for the security is populated in the Factor field but the Cap Rate field is left blank.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Factor | 0.14975 |
| Last Price | 105.1875 |
| Interest Rate | 8.5 % |
| Accrual Start Date | 30-JUN-99 |


##### Mortgage Backed Securities - Revaluations

This section explains how the revaluation routines use the same concept to ascertain the current value of a holding.

The SC.VAL.MARKET revaluation enquiry uses the latest market price as recorded in the Last Price field in the SECURITY.MASTER . During the run request is raised for an online valuation.

In the previous section, it was explained how SEC.TRADE proceeds are derived. Using the same security and the date changed to 3-OCT-95, the user can now view the results of running an online revaluation.

The current position in the example security is given in the fourth line item of the above screenshot (security number 005509-000). The current market price is changed to 104.1875 and the system date is changed to 3-OCT-95.

The original SECURITY.MASTER record is as follows.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Matures | 30-JUN-05 |
| Last Coupon Date | 30-JUN-95 |
| Next Coupon Date | 30-DEC-95 |
| Interest Rate | 8.5 % |
| Factor | 0.1575 |

The consideration is calculated as follows:

$500,000 x 104.1875 / 100 = $520,937.50 (as standard bonds)

Then,

$520,937.50 x 0.1575 (the factor) = $82,047.65

The interest is calculated as follows:

$500,000 x 0.1575 = $78,750.00

$78,750 x 93 (days) x 8.5\% / 360 = $1,729.22

93 days difference between the last coupon date 30-JUN-95 and 3-OCT-95 (assuming the number of days as 30 for each month)

### 5.49  MutualFunds

Mutual funds pool money from the investing public and use that money to buy other securities, usually sto...*
> 
> **Applications:** `EB.LOOKUP`, `SC.CHARGE.TAX.CALC`, `SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS`, `SC.ORDER.TYPE`, `SC.STD.SEC.TRADE`, `SCDX.CHARGE.PARAMETER`, `SEC.OPEN.ORDER`, `SEC.TRADE` ... +1 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Asset/ Sub Asset Type.1*, *Ben Account*, *Ben Account.1.1*, *Ben Bank*, *Ben Bank.1.1*, *Broker.1*, *Buyer Account.1*, *Buyer.1* ... +66 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A mutual fund is a type of financial instrument made up of a pool of money collected from many investors to invest in securities such as stocks, bonds, money market instruments and other assets. Mutual funds pool money from the investing public and use that money to buy other securities, usually stocks and bonds. The value of the mutual fund institution depends on the performance of the securities it holds.

Mutual funds are operated by professional money managers, who allocate the fund's assets and try to maximise returns. They are considered less risky than equities. Mutual funds are traded in the markets just as equities these days. However, there are some unique features to funds such as Switches and Right to cancel that are handled differently from equities.

Mutual fund transactions can be handled through the Securities (SC) module. Each fund is a separate security with its own identifier and a separate security master record is created. The price of the fund security is the net asset value (NAV) declared by the fund house. This feature explains how mutual funds can be handled through the SC module.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains about the basic configuration to be set up for handling mutual funds in the SC module.


##### Creating Fund Security

Mutual funds are opened as records in the SECURITY.MASTER application in the Securities (SC) module. The SECURITY.MASTER application holds the various details of the fund and the Mutual Fund field needs to be flagged to ensure that the security is treated as a fund. This application also has the fields to update the minimum subscription amount, minimum holding period, fees that are charged by the fund and so on. Some additional fund attributes are also updated in the SECURITY.SUPP application.


##### Transfer Agency Account and Settlement Details

In the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT application, the default beneficiary and beneficiary account details ( Ben Bank and Ben Account ) are specified. These fields in the SEC.TRADE application are used as payment instructions for making payment to the fund house or transfer agency.

The details can be specified for:

- Group of funds (prefixed with ‘S-‘ for sub-asset type and ‘A-‘ for asset type)
- A specific fund ( SECURITY.MASTER ID)
- All funds

The defaults can be specified by the currency in which the fund is denominated.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic explains how mutual funds are handled in the Securities module.


##### Subscription and Redemption Orders

A mutual fund order is placed in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application like any other equity order. A subscription order is usually a cash order, while a redemption order is for a nominal. Read the Order Processing feature for more information.

Fund orders are generally grouped and sent to the fund house at the cut-off time. When the NAV is declared, the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS application is updated with the NAV and execution nominal, and finally, a record in SEC.TRADE is created to complete the process.


##### Dividend Pay-out vs Dividend Reinvestment Orders

Mutual funds can be Growth funds where dividends are not paid out. Instead, the profits are re-invested directly by the fund house, thus increasing the NAV of the fund. However, mutual funds that are Dividend funds offer two choices to unit holders. In the Cash payout option, cash is paid out to the investors, as and when dividends are declared. Under the Dividend re-investment option, a dividend is declared and the same is re-invested into further units of the fund. The choice of opting for cash pay-out or re-investment of dividends should be made by the unit holder at the time of investing in the fund.

The SECURITY.MASTER application has fields to define if the re-investment option is allowed. Further, it is necessary to specify a separate depository for each dividend option such that positions are held separately and when dividend is declared, only those positions which were acquired as dividend pay-out are selected for the dividend event.

The fields defined are:

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Reinvest Allowed | Accepts the input as Yes or No |
| Invest Option Type | Beginning of the multi-value set. This field accepts the values based on the EB.LOOKUP application with ID starting with SC.INV.OPT.TYPE. The field contains the cash and re-invest options. |
| Option Depository | End of the multi-value set. This field accepts the valid depository ID. Based on the option selected in the Invest Option Type field, the depository is defaulted in SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE . |

> **⚠️ Note:** The Invest Option Type and Option Depository fields are used to hold positions in different accounts at the depository based on the dividend method opted by the investor.

The Invest Option Type field is set up in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE applications. This field accepts Cash or Reinvest value based on the investor’s choice of the dividend method. Depending on the option selected by the investor in the Invest Option Type field, the corresponding option depository is populated.

If the customer selects the cash option in the

field, the depository in the

field in

corresponding to the cash option is defaulted. This ensures that the

is held separately for fund holdings with dividend payout option and fund holdings with re-invest option. If the customer does not select an option in the

field for an order for a dividend fund, the default option is Cash.


##### Subscription Order with Upfront Payment

Some funds require the subscription amount to be paid upfront when the order is placed. The NAV is however declared later, sometimes several days later and the units are credited once the NAV is known. Read the Preserving Portfolio Value on Upfront Payment feature for more information.


##### Switch Orders

An order which is exclusive to mutual funds is the switch order. The SC module supports fund switch orders for both intra-fund (within the same fund house) and inter-fund switches. Normally, the switch orders are sell-driven. The investor specifies the redemption (sell) details and the net redemption proceeds are used to subscribe to the new funds. The units of the fund subscribed depend on the redemption amount. However, the switch can also be buy-driven in goal-driven investing. The investor or his asset manager indicates the funds he wishes to subscribe and based on the subscription amount required, one or more existing fund holdings are sold.

The Switch Order field in the SC.ORDER.TYPE application indicates if the order is a switch order. A SEC.OPEN.ORDER with the SWITCH order type is a switch order and it allows either the Nominal , Cu Cash Amount or Percentage field to be specified. The Switch Suspense Category field in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE application holds a valid internal account category. All accounting entries for the order amount in intra-fund switch orders are posted to this suspense account.

> **⚠️ Note:** All switch orders are not to be grouped with other orders.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Order Type | This field must be set to SWITCH to allow specifying the Switch quantity as unit, amount or percentage |
| Switch Order/ Switch Method | This field must be set to INTRAFUND in all the orders |
| Com Order Master/ Master Order of Switch | The value Yes in this field indicates that this is the master order in this switch and to be transmitted for the single SWIFT to be sent. This determines if the SWIFT is buy-driven or sell-driven. If a redemption (switch out) order is the master, it is sell-driven and if a subscription (switch in) order is the master, it is buy-driven switch. This field can be set for only one order in the switch combination. This is checked at the time of transmitting the order. This field is mandatory for intra-fund orders |
| Com Order Ref/ Switch Reference | The value in this field indicates the common reference of all the orders forming the switch. Based on this field, Temenos Transact treats these as a combined intra-fund switch order |
| Com Order Count/ No of Orders in Switch | The value in this field indicates the total number of orders that forms this switch request. This field is mandatory in the master order |

Inter-fund switching refers to switching between funds of different fund houses. This switch involves the following functionalities.

The inter-fund switches are received as separate redemption and subscription orders. The Order Type field must be set to SWITCH and the Switch Method field must be set to Interfund. This allows to specify either the No Nominal, Cu Cash Amount or Percentage field. All orders in a switch combination can be identified by the Com Order Ref field. The following screenshot shows a sell-driven redemption inter-fund switch order.

If the Com Order Master field is not set, the orders in the switch combination are treated as separate orders for all purposes for inter-fund switch orders. They are grouped with other individual orders and transmitted accordingly.

If the Com Order Master field is set in a subscription (switch in) order, it is a buy-driven switch request. The redemption (switch out) order is processed only after the subscription (switch in) order is confirmed and total subscription (switch in) amount is known. Temenos Transact allows the redemption (switch out) orders to be transmitted only if all the subscription (switch in) orders are executed. If the Com Order Master field is set in a redemption (switch out) order, it is a sell-driven switch request. For a sell-driven inter-fund switch order, the system checks for a value in the Transmit Date field. This field is set in inter-fund switch orders with a redemption order as the master order.

After all the redemption orders in the switch transaction are executed, the system tries to transmit the subscription orders. During transmit, the system

- Checks if the Transmit Date field is updated. If it is updated and the date is less than or equal to the current day, the subscription order is transmitted automatically. If the Transmit Date field is not updated, the system checks all the redemption orders in the switch transaction and calculates the last settlement date amongst all the redemption orders.
- Calculates the transmit date for the subscription orders in the switch transaction by working out the settlement days (T+2 or T+3) of the subscription legs.
- Transmits the subscription order if the transmit date calculated is less than or equal to the current bank day.
- Updates the calculated transmit date in the Transmit Date field if the transmit date is greater than the current bank day. It changes the Value Date of the order as well but the orders are not transmitted. The order is transmitted only on the Transmit Date .

The execution of inter-fund switch orders (subscription [switch in] and redemption [switch out]) is handled as per the standard redemption and subscription functionality. The incoming MX confirmation message completes the execution and trade. If the original order is for an amount, Temenos Transact does not calculate the nominal while creating records in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS on HOLD status. The actual units received can be updated in the Nominal Recd field in the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS application.

If the original order is for specific units, Temenos Transact treats the execution as full (irrespective of whether units received are greater than or less than the units specified in the order) on update of the nominal in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS , completes the execution and creates the record in SEC.TRADE . Separate cash movements are shown in the customer’s account.

If cancellation of an inter-fund switch combination is required, each order is manually cancelled. Temenos Transact only raises an override to indicate that the order is part of a switch and is being cancelled.

The MX messages for redemption and subscription are applicable.

The inter-fund switches are separate redemption and subscription orders. All the fees (fund house fees or bank fees) are handled accordingly.


##### Cooling Period and Right to Cancel

In certain markets, the investors have the rights to cancel their subscription to a fund within a certain number of days from the date of purchase of units (the cancellation or cooling period). The amount to be refunded to the investor (cancellation proceeds) pursuant to a cancellation request is calculated based on the current NAV for the trading funds and initial offer price for the new funds.

The cancellation proceeds payable is without any deduction of any front-end fees; however, banks can levy administrative charge for processing the cancellation request. If the cancellation proceeds exceeds the original subscription amount invested, then such excess amount is retained in the fund.

The Cool Cancel Period field in SECURITY.MASTER should be set to indicate that cooling period is available for the fund. An SC.ORDER.TYPE called CANC is also available to handle cancellation orders for such funds.

When a record in SEC.TRADE is created for a fund which has a cool cancel period, then based on the value in the Cool Cancel Period field in SECURITY.MASTER , the system calculates the right to cancel the date and it is stored in the Cancel By Date field in SEC.TRADE . An investor can cancel the subscription to a fund before this date.

If the date of purchase (Trade Date) is December 17, the Cancel By Date is December 21 (when the

field is set to 4 days in

). If December 21 is a holiday, then the

is the next working day (based on Security Domicile).

The subscription for a fund can be cancelled by the investor before the cool off date. The subscriber can apply for cancellation and it needs to be approved. (This process is outside of Temenos Transact ). Once the cancellation is approved, a record in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is created with the Order Type as CANC. In the Cancel Trade Ref field, the ID of the SEC.TRADE record created for the original buy that needs to be cancelled or revoked must be updated..

The entry load, rebate charge and rebate tax are refunded to the investor, whereas, the cancellation charges are deducted from the refund. The system automatically updates a value in the Order Type field with the designated order type, once a value is input in the Cancel Trade Ref field as shown in the following screenshot.

As soon as the above SEC.OPEN.ORDER is executed, a sell SEC.TRADE is created to revoke the original subscription. Upon executing the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application, a record in SEC.TRADE is created with the Transaction Type field set as SEL as shown in the following screenshot.

The charges (entry load, rebate charge and rebate tax) are refunded to the investor’s account upon cancelling the subscription as shown in the following screenshot.

##### Funds – Entry or Exit Loads and Other Charges

Entry load (also known as sales charge or front-end load) is applicable on fund subscriptions and can be defined in the SECURITY.MASTER application. If the same entry load is applicable for a class of funds (for example, 2.25% entry load on all equity funds in a given market) instead of defining at individual fund level, the entry load can be specified in the SC.CHARGE.TAX.CALC application.

The entry load is determined by the fund house and normally disclosed in the prospectus or the offering document of each fund. It is a charge by the fund house and forms the revenue of the fund house. However, the fund houses may also choose to waive (partially or wholly) the sales charge depending on some criteria, such as investment amount, promotion and so on. The fund house may also share it with their distributors who provide additional channels for selling the funds. There are two methods of charging the front-end load as explained below.

Bid and offer price – While subscribing, the entry load is added to the NAV to derive what is known as the offer price. In case of redemption, the fund house deducts the exit load from the NAV to derive the bid price.

- Order amount (A) : 10,000
- Entry load : 5%
- Entry load (B) : 500
- NAV (including entry load) : 10.52631579
- Net amount : 10,000
- Units (net amount/ adjusted NAV) : 950
- Amount debited from customer : 10,000
- Amount remitted to fund house : 10,000

The difference between the bid and offer price is the fund house’s spread.

The units are allotted based on NAV (not offer price) and the entry load or sales charge is shared wholly or partially with the bank (distributor for the fund). This method has two options for sharing the entry load:

1. The units are allotted based on NAV (not offer price). The fund house allocates the units for the net amount (subscription amount - entry load). The entry load or sales charge is shared wholly or partially with the bank (distributor for the fund) separately. Order amount (A) : 10,000 Entry load : 5% Entry load (B) : 500 NAV (including entry load) : 10 Net amount : 9,500 Units (net amount/ adjusted NAV) : 950 Amount debited from customer : 10,000 Amount remitted to fund house : 10,000
2. The units are allotted based on NAV (not offer price). The entry load is calculated and the net amount alone (subscription amount - entry load) is passed on to the fund house. The entry load or the sales charge is booked to the bank’s profit and loss (P&L). The system identifies the applicable method based on the value in the Entry Load Method field in SECURITY.MASTER or SC.STD.SEC.TRADE application and processes the entry load accordingly.

The same framework ( SCDX.CHARGE.PARAMETER or SC.CHARGE.TAX.CALC ) is used to define the applicable entry or exit loads and other attributes related to these fees.

On the entry load, the bank can provide:

- Rebate – if any rebate on the loads given by bank to the customer (in terms of percentage).
- Channel-based discount – on entry load based on channel (for example, orders through online platform).

On entry load, rebate is captured in terms of percentage. If the rebate is 100%, it denotes that the entire load should be waived. It is possible to specify the end date for a rebate (for example, end of promotional period) and all the transactions beyond that date are subject to the standard entry load. The rebate can be at fund level ( SECURITY.MASTER ) or for all funds or a class of funds ( SC.CHARGE.TAX.CALC ).

- Order amount (A) : 10,000
- Entry load : 5%
- Rebate : 60%
- Entry load (B) : 500
- Rebate : 300
- NAV : 10
- Net amount : 9,500
- Units (net amount/ adjusted NAV) : 950
- Amount debited from customer : 9,700
- Amount remitted to fund house : 9,500

Similarly, when the customer is purchasing mutual funds through online mutual fund platform (through internet banking), a discount may be given to the customer. The Sec Type field in SC.CHARGE.TAX.CALC accepts the channel identifier (asset type or sub-asset type suffixed with a channel identifier separated by a dot). The valid channels are defined in EB.LOOKUP application with ID starting with SC.CHANNEL. If the channel specified here matches the value in the Txn Channel field in order or trade, the customer is eligible for a discount.

Rebate- and channel-based discount is applicable only on entry load. It is applicable only if the Entry Load Method field is set to BANKPL (where the sales charge is calculated by the bank and only net amount is passed onto the fund house, the sales charge is booked to bank’s P&L). When a rebate or discount is offered, the system grosses up the investment so that the customer subscription amount is retained (the customer is debited for the original subscription amount). There is also an option where rebate or discount reduces the customer’s original investment amount.

If a customer places a subscription order for USD 10,000 subject to entry load of 5% and rebate on entry load of 60%, the customer’s account is debited only for USD 9,700 (USD 10,000 - rebate of USD 300).

Exit load may be applicable for some fund redemptions. The fund house applies the exit load and the balance amount (redemption amount - exit load) is remitted by the fund house to the bank or customer account. The exit load has two options:

- The fund house deducts the exit load and the balance amount is remitted to the bank.
- Option 1 - Exit load adjusted from the redemption amount and balance received from fund Units to redeem : 950 Exit load : 1% NAV : 100 Redemption amount : 94,050 Exit load : 950 Net amount : 94,050 Amount received from fund house : 94,050 Amount credited to customer : 94,050

- The bid price is arrived by deducting the exit load from the NAV. The redemption is done at bid price. Units to redeem : 950 Exit load : 1% NAV : 99 Redemption amount : 94,050 Exit load : 0 Net amount : 94,050

Based on the Exit Load Method field setting, the applicable method is determined.

A switching commission is applicable while switching from one fund to another (intra-fund, that is, within the same fund house). The switching commission is the spread between the switch-out amount and the switch-in amount. The switch-out (equivalent to redemption) is at NAV. During switch in (equivalent to subscription), the switching commission (for example, 1%) is deducted from the amount before allocating the units. The switching commission is applicable only on intra-fund switches because inter-fund switches are considered equivalent to redemption and subscription.
