### 5.50  Non-Stop Functionality


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Non-Stop (NS) functionality enables the bank to continue its operations even when the Close Of Business (COB) activity is on.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Actual Settlement*, *Last Cob Txn*, *Last Cob Txns Date*, *Update Ns Log*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The Non-Stop (NS) functionality enables the bank to continue its operations even when the Close Of Business (COB) activity is on.

In case of a customer (excluding bank’s own portfolio), the following new transactions are performed:

- Creation of record in CUSTOMER.SECURITY and SEC.ACC.MASTER applications
- Input ad execution of an order and execution (both partial and full), till the completion of trade
- Input of a direct trade, with the value date greater than or equal to the bank date
- Input of SECURITY.TRANSFER record for a customer portfolio, with the value date greater than or equal to the bank date.
- Back-value transactions are not allowed.
- If the Actual Settlement field in SC.PARAMETER is set to YES, the trades updated till the creation of settlement records are completed. When the system reaches the ONLINE stage during COB activity, the actual settlement happens.
- When INAU is set, the user can amend the transactions input in COB. The amendment of authorised record (input before or during COB) is not allowed except for the SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS records.
- The SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS records that are created before or during the COB, can be reversed, cancelled or amended during the COB process.)
- All valuation enquiries can be processed during COB, with respect to the positions created before or during COB.

The log of the records input during COB is created using NS functionality in Securities, if the Update Ns Log field in SC.PARAMETER application is set to YES.

The SC.TXNS.WHILE.COB table displays the log details of the records input during COB.

The Last Cob Txns Date and Last Cob Txn fields in the SECURITY.POSITION record for the transaction input during COB are updated as shown in the below screenshot.


##### Valuations Run During COB

When valuation is processed before COB, the record is created in SC.POS.ASSET for the portfolio as shown in the below screenshot.

The details of the valuation processed during COB are available in SC.POS.ASSET.WHILE.COB record.

### 5.51  Order Execution


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *When the orders are placed, the order details are verified and transmitted to the broker for execution. These orders can either be grouped together and transmitted during cut-off time or transmitted as and when they are placed. After the order is executed, the broker informs the execution details of...*
> 
> **Applications:** `>SEC.OPEN.ORDER`, `SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS`, `SC.EXEC.SEC.ORDERS`, `SEC.OPEN.ORDER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amt To Broker*, *Authorise Trade*, *Br Broker Comm*, *Br Ebv Fees*, *Br Fees Misc*, *Br Foreign Fee*, *Br Stamp Tax*, *Broker* ... +44 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

When the orders are placed, the order details are verified and transmitted to the broker for execution. These orders can either be grouped together and transmitted during cut-off time or transmitted as and when they are placed. After the order is executed, the broker informs the execution details of the order. The broker can either

- Execute the order completely
- Execute the order partially
- Reject the order

This feature explains how Temenos Transact handles order execution.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The SC.STD.SEC.TRADE application contains company-level default values which will be used when processing buy and sell transactions. Read the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE section in Securities for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

The SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS application records the execution for each authorised record in SEC.OPEN.ORDER .


##### Creating records in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS

The record in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is created either when authorising the SEC.OPEN.ORDER or when the Deal Status field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is set to Transmitted. If the Transmit Order field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is set to No, then the record in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is created as soon as the record in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is authorised.

If the Transmit Order field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is set to Yes, then the system validates whether a record in the SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS application is available for this security. If the group is not set or not available, then

- Set the Confirmation field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER to Yes (to send message to counterparty).
- Set the Deal Status field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER to Transmitted.

The order is then automatically transmitted and the record in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is created on Hold. When straight through processing is required without manual intervention (for specific securities alone), the STP field in the SECURITY.MASTER application can be set to Yes. When an order is placed, the system:

- Defaults the broker from the Broker field in SECURITY.MASTER .
- Sets the Authorise Trade field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS to Yes.
- Sets the Amt To Broker field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS to Sum (sum of all the customer's amounts).


##### Execution Details

The data in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is populated from SEC.OPEN.ORDER . The SC.EXEC.SEC.ORDERS application records the execution details from multiple brokers simultaneously. The execution details can be updated automatically through an incoming SWIFT message from the broker or can be manually filled. Each execution update can create a separate trade, or a single trade can be created for all executions in a day.

It also handles the customer nominal pro-rating functionality for multiple broker executions. If the records in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS are authorised, the system creates a record in SEC.TRADE in IHLD status. The system can be set to create the trade directly in live (authorised) status. The OFS Source and Ofs Version fields must be defined in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE application. The system uses the OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE to create the trades.

If the Authorise Trade field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is set to Yes, then when the order is created or executed, the trade is created in LIVE status. During this process, a record in S C.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is also created. The system can be parameterised to create trade directly in live and authorised status. The OFS Source and Ofs Version fields must be defined in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE parameter record.

The details of execution are updated in SEC.OPEN.ORDER . The S C.EXE.SEC.ORDERS executes the trades between a customer and broker, counterparty, customer or bank portfolio. While authorising the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS , the forward accounting entries raised by SEC.OPEN.ORDER are deleted and new forward accounting entries are raised separately for the nominals executed and that are pending execution. The forward accounting entry raised for nominal executed and pending execution is raised with the SEC.TRADE reference and SEC.OPEN.ORDER reference, respectively. This process is repeated for each execution.

If the Prorata Nominal field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is set to Yes, the override message, ‘Do You Wish To Pro-rata The Nominal’ with Yes or No options is suppressed in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDER, and the nominal is prorated. If the Prorata Nomina l field is set to No, the override is raised and the Nominal Recd field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is entered. If an API is entered in the Order Alloc Subr field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE , the executed quantity is allocated among the customers based on this routine. Else, the nominals are prorated.

If the Cancel Remain Ord field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is set to Yes, the override message, ‘Want To Put the Order To History’ is displayed when the record in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is authorised. If Cancel Remain Ord field is set to No, the override is suppressed and the related record in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is moved to history. This record is held in the live table for further execution.

The Customer Depository field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is defaulted from the Customer Depository field in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER . If the Customer Depository field in the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS has the updated values, the record in SEC.TRADE creation is processed similar to how it is processed when Trade Creation is set to By Depo in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE . As Customer Depository field is a multi-value field, separate records in SEC.TRADE are created for different depositories.

The Trade Time field records the time of the trade for each broker. If the Trade Time Flag field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is set to Yes, the Trade Time field defaults the current system time (HH.MM.SS format). If the user authorises the record in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS , each broker nominal executed is recorded in SEC.OPEN.ORDER with the relevant value in the Trade Time field. These values are also carried forward into a SEC.TRADE record, with the relevant trade times being defaulted into the Broker Trade Time field in this record.

The Cum Ex Ind field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER indicates the price conditions applicable to the transaction. This field can be updated only if the Price Qual Format field in the SM.PARAMETER application is set to Swift. The value in this field is validated against the Cum Indicate and Ex Indicate fields in SM.PARAMETERs . Any values entered in the Cum Ex Ind fields in SEC.OPEN.ORDER are carried forward. Amendments (if any) are allowed at this stage, and post-amendment, the values are carried forward when a record is created in SEC.TRADE . The Parent and Parent Reference fields in SEC.OPEN.ORDER are used for the parent child order functionality. Read the Parent Child Orders feature for more information.

A partial order is when only a part of the order quantity gets executed. Temenos Transact supports execution of partial orders. The following section explains how the system handles partial execution of orders.

When a single record in SEC.TRADE record is required for all the partial executions, the record in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is placed in IHLD status after each execution. Each execution updates the same record until the order is completely executed or the cut-off time is reached. The cut-off time is set as per broker and stock exchange in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY and STOCK.EXCHANGE applications, respectively. The Day Trade field in the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS must be set to Yes for the trade creation to happen at the end of day before COB after the specified cut-off time. When the cut-off time is reached, the system automatically picks the records in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDER s in IHLD status which have the values as Yes in the Day Trade field, thus automatically authorising them. The remaining nominals (if any) are cancelled. The system must be set up to enable automatic authorisation based on the cut-off time. The Cut Off Exec field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE defines whether the cut-off time for creating trades of partially executed orders is based on the CUSTOMER.SECURITY or STOCK.EXCHANGE application. In this scenario, the cut-off time is based on the record in STOCK.EXCHANGE .

The Cut off time field must be set in the STOCK.EXCHANGE application.

The orders are created and authorised with 1,000 nominal and Deal Status as Transmitted.

If the Stp Order field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is set to Yes, the trade for partial orders is created automatically using MT513 message.

The orders are partially executed for 700 nominal and the record is kept in IHLD status.

To cancel the remaining orders, the Cancel Remain Ord field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is set to Yes. After the cut-off time, the system authorises the record in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS and SP.CONSOLIDATION.SERVICE and OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE services run in auto mode to create the corresponding record in SEC.TRADE . The trade record is created for the partial orders in IHLD status.

When STP is enabled to prevent each MT513 message creating separate trades for the same order, the Consolidate Exec field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY must be set to Yes. In this case, a single record in SEC.TRADE is created after the order is fully executed.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| By Cust | Creates a separate SEC.TRADE for each customer |
| By Portfolio | Creates a separate SEC.TRADE for each portfolio |
| By Broker | Creates a separate SEC.TRADE for each broker |
| By Depo | Creates a separate SEC.TRADE for depository |
| By Default | Creates a SEC.TRADE (if multiple depositories exist, SEC.TRADE is created using the By Depo option) |
| Parent Child | Creates a SEC.TRADE for parent child orders |

| Broker Charges | Customer Charges |
|---|---|
| Br Broker Comm | Cu Brkr Comm |
| Br Foreign Fee | Cu Foreign Fee |
| Cl Commission | Cu Commission |
| Br Stamp Tax | Cu Stamp Tax |
| Br Ebv Fees | Cu Ebv Fees |
| Br Fees Misc | Cu Fees Misc |

### 5.52  Order Grouping


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Orders for the same instrument and with similar attributes (such as Security No , Order Type , Transaction Code , and so on) can be grouped and sent as a single order. Grouping is done for fund orders where the fund houses have a cut-off time and all orders received by the fund house (up to the cut-...*
> 
> **Applications:** `SC.GROUP.PARAM`, `SC.GRP.ORD.SERVICE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account Manager*, *Act Cut Off Date*, *Amt To Broker*, *Auto Group Id*, *Broker*, *Broker.1*, *Cash Chk Routine*, *Chk Domicile Region* ... +53 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Orders for the same instrument and with similar attributes (such as Security No , Order Type , Transaction Code , and so on) can be grouped and sent as a single order. Grouping is done for fund orders where the fund houses have a cut-off time and all orders received by the fund house (up to the cut-off time) are executed at the same Net Asset Value (NAV).

Grouping of orders saves on costs, and also provides benefit for larger deals. Temenos Transact supports both manual grouping of orders and automatic grouping, and transmission.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following configuration is set up to enable order grouping functionality.


##### SC.PARAMETER

The Group Order field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Manual.


##### OFS.SOURCE

Set up a record in OFS.SOURCE as shown in the below screenshot and update it in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE application.


##### SC.STD.SEC.TRADE

The Transmit Order field is set to Yes in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE application. The OFS.SOURCE and OFS.VERSION applications are linked.


##### SC.GROUP.PARAM

This application has a set of mandatory system fields for grouping, which is displayed in the below screenshot. A record with ID as Company ID must be available so that the orders can be grouped.

User cannot enter values in the Sys Fields fields. When the orders are grouped, these fields in SEC.OPEN.ORDER are validated for a similar value. The additional parameters are allowed to be set up by the user in the User Fields multi-value fields. The following are the options in User Fields:

- Account Manager
- Cust Number
- Cust Acc No
- Cu Ex Rate Acc
- Liquidation Period
- Order Date
- Portfolio Type
- Premium Price
- Stock Exchange
- Investment Program
- Cu Depository

If any of the above fields are set-up in the User Fields , the values in these fields are also checked from the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application. If Portfolio Type is selected in the User Fields field, the system groups the records based on the Grp Port Desc field in MANAGED.ACCOUNT .

The MANAGED.ACCOUNT application is linked to a record in SEC.ACC.MASTER . To group the orders where the Portfolio Type is selected as a parameter for grouping, the orders are grouped based on the values defined in the Grp Port Desc field in the MANAGED.ACCOUNT application. If the value in the Grp Port Desc field is defined as ABC in a record in MANAGED.ACCOUNT and XYZ in another record in MANAGED.ACCOUNT and attached to a different SEC.ACC.MASTER application, the orders with such portfolios are not grouped together.

If Investment Program is selected in the User Fields field, the grouping is based on the value of the Investment Program field in the respective record in SEC.ACC.MASTER . A valid routine can be attached locally in the Group Routine field. This facilitates adding parameters for grouping locally.


##### SECURITY.MASTER

The following fields in SECURITY.MASTER application are provided by the fund house and are available in the instrument feeds. These fields help the user to create grouping records for each fund.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Domicile Region | Accepts a valid region record |
| Fund Subs Freq | Denotes the subscription frequency of the fund |
| Subs Day Offset | Indicates the number of days offset for funds subscription. Accepts both positive and negative values. Input is allowed only when Fund Subs Freq is set to Weekly or Defined. |
| Fund Redm Freq | Indicates the redemption frequency of a fund |
| Redm Day Offset | Indicates the number of days offset for funds redemption. Accepts both positive and negative values. Input is allowed only when Fund Redm Freq is set to Weekly or Defined. |

> **⚠️ Note:** The fields in SECURITY.MASTER are information only fields and can be referred for creating grouping records (that is, for every fund, a record can be created in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS for grouping the orders). Temenos Transact does not automatically create groups based on these fields and validation is not done against these fields.


#### 🔧 Working With

Temenos Transact supports both manual and auto grouping of orders.

The two levels of grouping can be achieved by setting the Group Order field in SC.PARAMETER as Automatic, Manual or Both. If the Group Order field is set to Both, manual and automatic grouping are enabled at the same time. The only distinction is that all records in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS application are considered for automatic grouping. If automatic grouping of records are set up in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS , the automatic grouping is performed and the other orders (for funds where the record in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS is not available) are to be grouped manually.


##### Manual Grouping of Orders

This section details with the manual grouping of orders that involves the setup of the following record.


###### SC.GROUP.PARAM

A record with company ID should be available by default. Apart from the default record, the user can set up grouping parameters for a particular security or sub asset type and so on. The record ID of SC.GROUP.PARAM can be set as follows:

| Application | Setup |
|---|---|
| SECURITY.MASTER | A valid SECURITY.MASTER ID can be defined as ID (100040-000) |
| SUB.ASSET.TYPE | A valid SUB.ASSET.TYPE can be defined as ID (S-102) |
| ASSET.TYPE | A valid ASSET.TYPE can be defined as ID (A-10) |
| SYSTEM | A generic parameter record used when specific parameter is not defined |

Whenever orders are grouped, a parameter record in SC.GROUP.PARAM with record id as SECURITY.MASTER , SUB.ASSET.TYPE , ASSET.TYPE and SYSTEM is checked. The same sequence is followed if a record with SECURITY.MASTER is found in the first instance and the grouping is based on this parameter record. If match is not found, the company level record is used as the parameter for grouping.

In many countries, individual states have different local holidays. Only certain holidays are common across the country. The cut-off date for grouping of orders is based on a working day in the state, where the operations of the fund are conducted. The Chk Domicile Region field in SC.GROUP.PARAM is set to Yes to define the cut-off date for grouping of orders. When this field is set to Yes, the system checks for the working day in the regional calendar based on Domicile Region field in SECURITY.MASTER and also checks if the same day is a working day in the country calendar.

If it is not a holiday in both the records in HOLIDAY (country and regional calendar), the next cut-off date is processed as it exists. If a holiday is found in either of the records in HOLIDAY (that is, records in HOLIDAY with ID related to the Local Country and Local Region specified in COMPANY or Domicile Region in the SECURITY.MASTER ), the system checks the value in Day Convention field in SECURITY.MASTER and processes the next cut-off date as a working day in both calendars. If the value is specified in the Subs Days Offset field in SECURITY.MASTER , the Day Convention field is not checked. Instead, Temenos Transact checks if the resultant day is a working day in domicile calendar and then in the local calendar (after applying the value in Days Offset field).

> **⚠️ Note:** The value in Domicile Region field is not mandatory. If it is not set, the system checks only the holiday of the local region that is set in COMPANY .

Multiple records in SEC.OPEN.ORDER can be grouped using the SC.GROUP.ORDERS application. The user creates a record in SC.GROUP.ORDERS and adds the record IDs of SEC.OPEN.ORDER to be grouped.

When SC.GROUP.ORDERS is input, a validation is made using the SC.GROUP.PARAM application. The grouping is allowed based on the parameters defined in the SC.GROUP.PARAM application. If the orders have different values in the fields defined as a parameter in the SC.GROUP.PARAM application, applicable error messages are displayed and grouping is not allowed. If all the parameter fields have the same data, the individual orders are allowed for grouping. This function of bulking the records in SEC.OPEN.ORDER helps in placing a single order to the broker for similar transactions. When the user wants to transmit the grouped orders, the user should authorise the record in SC.GROUP.ORDER with Transmit field set to YES.

On authorisation of SC.GROUP.ORDER , an Open Financial Services (OFS) job is initiated to authorise the grouped record in SEC.OPEN.ORDER . To enable authorisation of grouped records in SEC.OPEN.ORDER , a version of the SEC.OPEN.ORDER and OFS.SOURCE must be input and the same is updated in the Ofs Version and Ofs Source fields in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE application. When a record in SC.GROUP.ORDERS is in INAU status, the original SEC.OPEN.ORDER is updated with the Deal Status field set to Grouped.

The forward accounting entry (if any) is reversed for the original orders and a new order generates a fresh forward entry. The security positions for open orders are deleted for the old orders and recreated for the grouped order.


##### Automatic Grouping of Orders

This section details the automatic grouping of orders that involves the setup of the following record.

The record in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS is used for automatic grouping of orders. The ID of a SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS can be set as follows:

- Security No S - followed by a valid SUB.ASSET.TYPE A - followed by a valid ASSET.TYPE
- All
- Security No*Transaction code

When the system groups the orders, the record ID with Security No*Transaction code takes the highest priority and record ID with ALL takes the least priority. The orders for unapproved funds cannot be grouped if the Unapproved field in SECURITY.MASTER is set to Yes.

The Cut Off Date and Cut Off Time must be set in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS , if the grouped orders have to be consolidated and transmitted. A cut-off frequency is also set in the Cut Off Freq field.

- The Cut Off Time can be set directly in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS .
- The Cut Off Time and the Cut Off Time Zone of the fund house is available in the SECURITY.MASTER application.

If the cut off time is set in SECURITY.MASTER , the

- Time is expressed in co-ordinated universal time (UTC) with a special UTC designator Z.
- Time is expressed in the local time with a time zone offset in hours and minutes. A time zone offset of ‘+hh:mm’ indicates that the date or time uses a local time zone, where 'hh' is hours and 'mm' is minutes ahead of UTC. A time zone offset of ‘-hh:mm’ indicates that the date or time uses a local time zone, where 'hh' is hours and 'mm' is minutes behind UTC.

Time is expressed as 1994-11-05T13:15:30Z indicates that the time is measured in UTC.

Time and date are expressed as 1994-11-05T08:15:30-05:00, where the date or time corresponds to November 5, 1994, 8:15:30 am, US Eastern standard time (-05.00 is the offset).

However, the time set in SECURITY.MASTER is not automatically updated in the record in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS of that security. The cut-off date and time are entered manually and the bank user must ensure that the cut-off time entered is aligned with the cut-off time specified for the fund in SECURITY.MASTER .

The bank user can configure an extended cut-off time after the grouping cut-off time. If the Extd Cut Off Time field in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS is set, the orders received between the Cut Off Time ;and Extd Cut Off Time ;are transmitted instantly without the grouping queue. Any order received after the Extended Cut Off Time is grouped and transmitted during the next cut-off cycle.

If the user enters the Cut Off Date as 18 APR 2017, Cut Off Time as 16:00, Cut Off Freq as DAILY and Extended Cut Off Time as 17:00, then the transition window is for an hour and any order received during this window are transmitted individually on 18 APR 2017 without getting grouped. An order received after 17:00 are grouped and transmitted in the next grouping cycle on 19 APR 2017.

- The Cut Off Frequency field allows the cut-off frequency to be set. The next cut-off date is calculated by the system based on this frequency. This field supports several defined frequencies such as - last day of the month, every Thursday of the week and so on.
- When the Cut Off Date for grouping of fund orders is a bank holiday in the country where the transactions are executed, the automatic grouping of orders can be set to consider the previous or next business day as per the Day Convention field in the record in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS . The Prev Cut Off Date and Act Cut Off Date fields store the previous cut-off date and captures the actual cut-off date after the calculation of new cut-off date. Both the cut-off dates change after each grouping is done, that is, after running the SC.GRP.ORD.SERVICE .

While determining the cut-off date, if the Chk Domicile Region field is set to Yes in SC.GROUP.PARAM , the system additionally checks the records in HOLIDAY for the ID as the region ID is specified in Domicile Region field in the SECURITY.MASTER . Only if it is not a holiday in both the records in HOLIDAY (country and regional calendar), the next cut-off date is processed as it is. If a holiday is found in either of the records in HOLIDAY , the system checks the day convention and processes the next cut-off date as a working day in both calendars.

If there is any value specified in the Days Offset field, day convention is not checked initially. The system first calculates the date based on the Cut Off Frequency set, and then adds or subtracts the value specified in Days Offset to arrive at the final value in the Cut Off Date field. The day convention is applied only if the resultant day is a holiday after applying the value in the Days Offset field.

Resetting Cut-Off Date

The cut-off date is recycled only when cut-off time is reached. If it is required to recycle the date immediately after the group order is manually transmitted, then the Reset Cut Off Date field in SC.GROUP.PARAM should be set to 'Yes'. Recycling happens only if the order is manually transmitted on the cut-off date but before cut-off time. If the order is manually transmitted on a date before cut-off date, then the recycling is restricted.

Cut Off Date – 15 APR 2021

Cut Off Time – 15:00

Cut Off Freq – WEEKLY

As on 15 APR 2021 13:41 hours, several orders have been grouped and are waiting for transmission.

If the user manually transmits the order at 13:45 hours, then the system recycles the cut-off date to 22 APR 2021 based on the cut-off frequency even though the cut-off time, 15:00 hours is not reached.

In above example, if the group order was transmitted manually on 14 APR 2021, then the cut-off date is not recycled and remains as 15 APR 2021, 15:00 hours.


##### Cancelling Grouped Order before Transmission

If an automatically grouped order needs to be cancelled before the cut-off date and time, the value in the Order No field in SC.GROUP.ORDERS is deleted. On deleting it, the system:

- changes the status in the Deal Status ;field in the original SEC.OPEN.ORDER from Grouped to Null.
- deletes the order number from the Order No field in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS .
- deletes the data from the respective Group Order field if the record in SC.GROUP.ORDERS is deleted.
- makes the original SEC.OPEN.ORDER available for modifications and re-grouping on authorisation.

Whenever a grouped order is purged or moved to history file, the system excludes such orders from grouping in SC.GROUP.ORDERS .


##### Processing Grouped Orders

The SC.GRP.ORD.SERVICE groups the orders and keeps running. If auto grouping is enabled and the user opts for it, it denotes that the bank has opted for total automation (all the orders are submitted for grouping). During authorisation of a SEC.OPEN.ORDER , if any of the records in SECURITY.MASTER are setup in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS and if the records in SECURITY.MASTER matches with the authorising records in SEC.OPEN.ORDER , the system makes an entry in the Order No field in the SC.GROUP.ORDERS and SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS applications.

When an order is authorised, the order number is recorded in the Order No field in the SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS and SC.GROUP.ORDERS applications. The SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDER ID is recorded in the Auto Group Id field in SC.GROUP.ORDERS application. Again, the SC.GROUP.ORDERS ID is recorded in the Group Order No field in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS .

When the cut-off date and cut-off time is reached, an OFS job authorises the records in SC.GROUP.ORDERS based on the list in the Group Order No field in the record in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS . On authorisation of the records in SC.GROUP.ORDERS , the following actions are invoked:

- In SC.GROUP.ORDERS , the original individual SEC.OPEN.ORDER ID is submitted to OFS.IN-DIRECTORY with the reversal function to move the record to history without execution. This process also creates a grouped SEC.OPEN.ORDER , which collates all individual orders into a single order. The grouped SEC.OPEN.ORDER ID is submitted to OFS.IN-DIRECTORY with the authorisation function. This action sets the grouped SEC.OPEN.ORDER in the authorised status with the value in Deal Status as Transmitted.
- The entries in the Group Order No field and the Order No field in the SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS records are cleared. The Cut Off Date is recycled if the Cut Off Freq is set to daily or weekly or monthly. The grouped records in SEC.OPEN.ORDERS are created based on the method outlined in the manual grouping process.

If the Stp field in SECURITY.MASTER is set to Yes, the grouped SEC.OPEN.ORDER that is created is automatically transmitted. The broker is defaulted from the Broker field in SECURITY.MASTER and the Amt To Broker is defaulted as the sum of all the customers' nominal or amount. The Deal Status field is set to transmitted and the order is transmitted automatically.

The fund orders can be grouped and sent to the fund processing platform or counterparty intra-day (prior to fund house cut-off time) for various reasons.

If the orders are transmitted prior to 2 PM, the investor is allotted with units at the NAV of the previous day. For orders post 2 PM, the units are allotted with the NAV of that day. The users can manually trigger the grouping or transmitting prior to fund house cut-off time. All the orders placed by that time are grouped and transmitted.


##### Ungrouping Orders which Fail to Meet Cash Requirement

There are funds whose cut-off frequency could be weekly or even monthly. Subscription orders placed during the whole week or month are transmitted only at the cut-off date that is, several days later. If the cash accounts are held outside Temenos Transact , then it is difficult to ensure that funds are not withdrawn within that time.

In this case, bank may want to run a cash availability check before the grouped order is transmitted. If this is required, the bank has to locally create a cash check routine. This routine should be attached to the Cash Chk Routine field in SC.GROUP.PARAM . During the cut-off time, the system calls the routine in Cash Chk Routine field in SC.GROUP.PARAM (if it exists). The cash check routine is called only for groups where the transaction type is buy or subscription. The orders which fail to meet the cash requirement are removed from the group. The Deal Status of the removed records in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is marked as UNGROUPED. The balance orders in SC.GROUP.ORDERS are consolidated and the wholesale order is transmitted.

During the cut-off time, the orders with Deal Status set to UNGROUPED are removed from the group. The ungrouped orders are placed in the next grouping queue.


#### 📋 Tasks

Grouping of Orders can be done both manually and automatically, when set of orders have some common parameter values defined in SC.GROUP.PARAM application.

- In automatic grouping, a record is created for a security in SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS application with cut-off date, cut-off expiry date and cut-off frequency. The orders created within this specified time and date is grouped, if it meets the condition provided in SC.GROUP.PARAM application.
- In Manual grouping, we can group the orders by providing the order numbers in SC.GROUP.ORDERS application.

#### 📖 Introduction

In Temenos Transact , the order life cycle begins with the order capture and goes through various stages such as order placement, order execution and trade creation. There are various delivery messages (SWIFT) associated with each stage in the order life cycle. The system is configured to send and receive messages throughout the order life cycle.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configuration of the following tables.


##### SC.PARAMETER

The SC.PARAMETER record is setup for various attributes with which the order should be created and processed in Temenos Transact .

The Opn Ord Fwd Acct should be set to Y, if the forward accounting is raised when an order (that is, unexecuted orders) is input. If the forward accounting is already set in SC module, action is not required but it is recommended to set this field.


##### SC.STD.SEC.TRADE

This application has several fields controlling the various features of the order flow in SC module. Read Working with Order Processing for more information on the setup required for various processing.


##### SC.ORDER.TYPE

This application must be configured for different types of orders.

The Limit Price field in SC.ORDER.TYPE indicates that it is a limit order. If this field is set to Yes, the order is a price order and the Limit Price field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER becomes mandatory. If the Limit Price Check field is set to Yes and the execution price is greater than or less than the price specified in the order (buy or sell), an override is raised when the order is executed.

If the Limit Price Val field in SC.ORDER.TYPE is set to Yes for a limit order type, the approximate settlement amount in the Val in Sett Ccy field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is calculated based on the value in the Limit Price field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER . If the Limit Price Val field is not set, the approximate settlement amount in the Val in Sett Ccy field is calculated based on the value in the Market Price field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER . The Market Price defaults to the last price in SECURITY.MASTER but user can also enter values in the order.

The Cash Order field indicates whether the order is a cash order or not. Only the Cu Cash Amount field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER can be updated and not the nominal for cash orders. If the Full Trade field is set to Yes and an order is placed for the order type (that is, if the order is partially executed), then an override is raised.

The Stop Order field indicates whether the order type is a stop loss order. Stop loss order is an order to buy or sell a stock once the price of the stock reaches a specified price, known as the stop price. If this field is set to Yes for an order type and the corresponding order type (that is, a SC.ORDER.TYPE having the Stop Order field set to Yes) is used in SEC.OPEN.ORDER , then the Curr Price field holds the stop price.

> **⚠️ Note:** If both the Limit Price and Stop Order fields are set to Yes for an order type and if the corresponding order type is used in SEC.OPEN.ORDER for a buy transaction and if the value in the Limit Price field is less than the value in the Curr Price field, then the system displays the 'Limit price lower than stop price' override message. If it is a sell transaction and the value in the Limit Price is greater than the value in the Curr Price , then the system displays the 'Limit price greater than stop price' override message.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with the working mechanism of order processing in Temenos Transact . It covers the following topics:

- Order Initiation of standard orders and cash orders
- Capturing orders for done deals
- Order Expiry
- Order Cancellation


##### Initiating Orders

The orders are captured in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application as shown in the screenshot below. The SEC.OPEN.ORDER allows multiple customers and brokers. The Depository field must be updated to record the open order position in the Net Open Order Pos field in SECURITY.POSITION record.

Each customer can be associated to a different depository using the Cu Depository field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER .

- If the Cu Depository field is updated, the record in SECURITY.POSITION is updated with the depository defined in this field and not the value in the Depository field. If the Cu Depository field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER has a value, the value in the Sub Account field and the defaulting of values in the Sub Account field relates to the depository defined in the Cu Depository field.
- If the Cu Depository field is left blank, the Depository field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is used for the creating positions. If the Def Cust Depo field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Yes, the Cu Depository field is defaulted from the Depository field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER . The value in this field is defaulted to Cu Depository field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDER .

The Cu Depository field enables bulk order placement to a broker. If the records in SEC.OPEN.ORDER with multiple depositories (that is, customers with multiple depositories) is executed, multiple records in SEC.TRADE are created. The SEC.TRADE application handles the settlement (stock settlement to a particular depository) instruction to the broker.

The Deal Status field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is critical and controls the workflow.

- If the Deal Status field is blank, the order can be grouped.
- If the Deal Status field is Transmitted, the order is assumed to be transmitted to the market. The Temenos Transact t creates a record in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS to handle executions.

If the Trade Time Flag field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is set to Yes, the Order Time field defaults the current system time (in HH.MM.SS format). If this record is generated by an ORDER.BY.CUST record, the Order Time field in ORDER.BY.CUST defaults into the Order Time field in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER record. This value is carried forward to the Order Time field in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER record.

The Cum Ex Ind field indicates the price conditions applicable to the transaction. This field is updated only if the Price Qual Format field in the SM.PARAMETER record is set to Swift. This input is validated against the Cum Indicate and Ex Indicate fields in the SM.PARAMETER record. Any input made to this field is carried forward to the corresponding SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record.

The Parent and Parent Reference fields in SEC.OPEN.ORDER define if an order is a parent child order. Read Parent Child Orders for more information. The Parent field determines if the record is a parent leg (broker side) or not. The Parent Reference field holds a common reference, which links the parent and child transactions.

If the Deal Status field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is set to Traded, the execution is skipped and a SEC.TRADE is directly created in IHLD status after authorising the SEC.OPEN.ORDER record.

The system can be set to create the trade directly in LIVE (authorised) status. The Ofs Source and Ofs Version fields must be defined in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE record. The system uses the OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE, to create the trades and hence this service must be running. If the Authorise Trade field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is set to Yes when the order is created, the trade thus created and authorised is in LIVE status. During this process, SC.EXE.SEC.ORDER is not created and delivery messages are not generated. The forward accounting entries raised by SEC.OPEN.ORDER contains the SEC.TRADE reference.

For previously traded orders, the details such as broker, price, settlement account and so on can be updated in SEC.OPEN.ORDER . The Broker field is entered with the respective broker number. The Amt To Broker and Br Price sub-valued fields are used to record multiple executions for the same broker but with different prices. The customer charges and commissions defined in SEC.OPEN.ORDER are defaulted while creating a record in SEC.TRADE . When the next COB is run, the value in Record Status field is updated as MAT and the record in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is moved to history after authorisation.


##### Order Expiry

Orders placed in Temenos Transact stays in the system until the expiry date of the order. The Limit Exp Date field holds the expiry date. During the COB of the expiry date, the order is purged by the system. The Limit Exp Date is populated based on the value in the Limit Type field, which is GTD (Good Till date) by default. The Limit Exp Date is defaulted to the system date.

For Good this month (GTM) limit type, the

is calculated and defaulted to one month from the system date.

For Good-Til-Cancelled (GTC) limit type, the

field is blank. These orders cannot be purged or moved to History table. Such orders remain in the LIVE table until it is executed or cancelled.

However, the orders initiated from Wealth Front Office (TAP) are not purged automatically by the system, even when the system reaches the expiry date. Thus, orders with value in either Tap Ref Id or Tap Order Nature field is considered as TAP initiated orders. These orders are purged only when the Deal Status of the order is set to CANCELLED, CANCEL.CHILD or REJECTED.

If the Deal Status field in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER is set to GROUPED, then those orders does not consider the value Limit Exp Date field. These orders does not expire even if the date in Limit Exp Date field is reached.


##### Order Cancellation

Before an order is transmitted (that is, Deal Status in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is blank) the order can be cancelled by either reversing the record in SEC.OPEN.ORDER or by setting the Deal Status to CANCELLED.

If the order is transmitted and before execution, if the order has to be cancelled, the Order Status field is set as Cancellation Requested. The back-office users must contact the counterparty to accept the cancellation.

- Once the counterparty accepts the order cancellation request, the Order Status field must be changed to Cancellation Accepted. Deal Status is set to CANCELLED.
- If the counterparty rejects the cancellation request, the Order Status field must be changed to Cancellation Rejected. Deal Status remains TRANSMITTED.

In the case of parent child orders, the Deal Status is marked as CANCEL.CHILD. The Deal Status field determines if the order has to be moved to history and if forward accounting is to be dropped. The Order Status field provides information about the order status.


##### Order Type Cash

The following fields are involved in this transaction.

| Field | Functionality |
|---|---|
| Cu Cash Amount | Defaults from the corresponding field in the ORDER.BY.CUST transaction, if the transaction is derived from the ORDER.BY.CUST record (or) Represents the amount of cash the customer wants to commit in this transaction if this is a new transaction and the value in the Order Type field is Cash. After this field is updated with a cash amount, the system cross-validates this value with the Security Currency field in the SECURITY.MASTER record. The user can specify a different cash settlement currency in the Settlement Ccy field. The Cu Ex Rate Acc field can be modified to enter and exchange rate for the conversion. |
| Curr Price | Defaults from the corresponding Market Price or Market Price Cr fields in ORDER.BY.CUST depending on the transaction (buy or sell), if the transaction is derived from the ORDER.BY.CUST record (or) Defaults from the Last Price field in the SECURITY.MASTER record or entered manually if this is a new transaction. |
| Calc Chrgs | Carries forward the value or take it to the application, for the values Yes and No set in this field, respectively, if the transaction is derived from the ORDER.BY.CUST record (or) Indicates the user-defined value for system to calculate the charges and commissions if this is a new transaction and the value in the Order Type field is Cash. |
| Cash Chrgs | Defaults from the Cu Cash Amount field if the transaction is derived from the ORDER.BY.CUST record (or) Indicates the user-defined value for system to calculate the charges and commissions on net or gross basis, if this is a new transaction and the value in the Order Type field is Cash. The values are Net: The cash amount populated in Cu Cash Amount field includes all charges and commissions. The system makes necessary adjustments and calculates the nominal for purchase, based on the Curr Price field including the charges and commissions. The relevant charges and commission related fields are updated later. Gross: The system calculates the nominal from the Curr Price, adds the charges and commission and updates the relevant fields. |
| Split Chrgs | Defaults from the corresponding Split Chrgs field in the ORDER.BY.CUST transaction and the value in the Order Type field is updated as Switch. |
| Cash Rounding | Indicates the action for the cash amount when the Cash Chrgs field is set to Net. The values are: Exact: The system calculates the nominal balance to the nearest from the cash amount specified including the charges and commissions and any under or over adjustments are taken from the Cu Commission field amount to give an exact match to the cash amount initially specified. Under or Over: The system calculates the nearest trading unit under the cash amount for a purchase to the nearest trading unit over the cash amount for a sale. |
| Adjust Commission | Indicates if the system automatically adjusts the commission. The values are Yes and No. |
| Amt To Broker | Indicates the amount of an order placed with the broker defined in the Broker field and including the cash amount in the Cu Cash Amount field. |
| Br Cash Amount | Indicates the cash amount for the broker defined in the Broker field. This field is optional and relate the multi-value set of fields from Broker through Confirmation. This field is used in the same context as the Amt To Broker field. |
| Cancel Trade Ref | Indicates the trade reference to be cancelled. If a value is set in this field, the system automatically updates the Order Type field in SC.ORDER.TYPE with the order type designated for cancelled orders. |


##### Execute Open Orders

The SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS application records the execution for each authorised SEC.OPEN.ORDER record. Authorising a SEC.OPEN.ORDER record creates a SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record. The Transmit Order field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is used for automatic creation of the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record. If this field is set to No, a SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record is created automatically at the time of authorising a SEC.OPEN.ORDER record. If this field is set to Yes, the Deal Status field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER must be set to Transmitted to create a SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record.

The Stp field in SECURITY.MASTER is set to Yes and a default broker is set in the Broker field for the automatic creation of the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record, as soon as the SEC.OPEN.ORDER is authorised for specific securities alone.

When an order is placed for this security, the system:

- Defaults the broker from the Broker field in the SECURITY.MASTER application
- Sets the Authorise Trade field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is set to Yes
- Sets the Amt To Broker field as Sum (sum of all the customer's amounts)

The system validates this order, if a SC.AUTO.GROUP.ORDERS record is available. If the group is not set or not available, the system:

- Sets the Confirmation field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER to Yes and
- Sets the Deal Status in SEC.OPEN.ORDER to Transmitted

Then, the order is transmitted automatically.

The SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS data is populated from SEC.OPEN.ORDER and records the execution details from multiple brokers simultaneously. It also handles the customer nominal pro-rating functionality for multiple broker executions. If the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS records are authorised, it create a SEC.TRADE record in IHLD status.

The system can be set to create the trade directly in LIVE (authorised) status. The Ofs Source and Ofs Version fields must be defined in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE record. The system uses the OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE to create the trades.

If the Authorise Trade field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is set to Yes, when the order is created or executed, the trade is created and authorised in LIVE status. During this process an SC.EXE.SEC.ORDER record is also created. The system can be parameterized to create Trade directly in 'Live' that is; in authorised status. The Ofs Source and Ofs Version fields must be defined in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE parameter record. The system uses the OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE to create the trades and hence this service must be running.

The Authorise Trade field is used in Securities Buy Order ( SEC.OPEN.ORDER ) and Order execution ( SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS ) records. If this field is set to Yes when the order or execution was created, the trade created out of order is created and authorised in LIVE status.

The details of execution are updated in SEC.OPEN.ORDER for information. The SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS executes the trades between a customer and broker, counterparty, customer or bank-portfolio. While authorising the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS, the forward accounting entries raised by SEC.OPEN.ORDER are deleted and new forward accounting entries are raised separately for the nominals executed and pending execution. The forward accounting entry raised for nominal executed and pending execution is raised with the SEC.TRADE and SEC.OPEN.ORDER reference, respectively. This process is repeated for each execution.

If the Prorata Nom field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is set to Yes, the override 'Do You Wish To Pro-rata The Nominal' with Yes or No options is suppressed in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDER, and the nominal is prorated. If this field is set to No, the override is raised and Nominal Recd field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is entered. If an API is entered in the Order Alloc Subr field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE , the executed quantity is allocated among the customers based on this routine. Else, the nominals are prorated.

If the Cancel Remain Ord field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE is set to Yes, the override 'Want To Put the Order To History' is displayed when the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record is authorised. If Cancel Remain Ord is set to No, the override is suppressed and the related SEC.OPEN.ORDER is moved to history, this record is held in the LIVE table for further execution.

The Cu Depository field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is defaulted from the Cu Depository field in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER record. If Cu Depository field in the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS has the updated values, the SEC.TRADE creation is processed similar to how it is processed when Trade Creation is set to BY DEPO in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE . As Cu Depository is a multi-value field, separate SEC.TRADE records are created for different depositories.

The SC.EXE.SEC.ORDER s are authorised for each partial execution and each execution creates a separate SEC.TRADE record. When a SEC.TRADE record is required for all the partial executions, the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record are placed in IHLD status after each execution. Each execution updates the same record until the order is completely executed or the cut-off time is reached. The cut-off time is set per broker and stock exchange in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY and STOCK.EXCHANGE application, respectively. The Day Trade field in the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS must be set to Yes for the trade creation to happen at the end of day before COB after the specified cut-off time. When the cut-off time is reached, the system automatically picks the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS records in HOLD status and has the updates the values as Yes in the Day Trade field, thus automatically authorszing them. The remaining nominal (if any) are cancelled. The system must be set up to enable automatic authorisation based on the cut-off time. The Cut Off Exec field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE defines whether the cut-off time for creating trades of partially executed orders is based on the CUSTOMER.SECURITY or STOCK.EXCHANGE application. In this scenario the cut-off time is based on the STOCK.EXCHANGE record.

The Cut Off Time field must be set in the STOCK.EXCHANGE application.

The orders are created and authorised with 1000 nominal and Deal Status as Transmitted.

If the Stp Order field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is set to Yes, the trade for partial orders are created automatically using MT513 message.

The orders are partially executed for 700 nominal and the record is kept in IHLD status.

To cancel the remaining orders, the Cancel Remain Ord field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is set to Yes. After the cut-off time, the system authorises the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record and SP.CONSOLIDATION.SERVICE and OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE services must run in auto mode to create the corresponding SEC.TRADE record. The trade record is created for the partial orders in IHLD status.

When STP is enabled to prevent each MT513 creating separate trades for the same order, the Consolidate Exe field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record must be set to Yes. In this case, a single SEC.TRADE is created after the order is fully executed.

For cash order transactions the customer(s) nominal can be re-calculated at this stage, if required. All transaction values for example, values in the Customer No , Cust Nominal , Cust Price , Cu Cash Amount fields all calculated. The vales in commission and charges are defaulted from the associated transaction and the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application.

The trigger for re-calculating the new nominal is when the broker details and a value in the Price field is entered. This Broker Price entered is automatically defaulted to each customer's multi-value set of Cust Price fields.

> **⚠️ Note:** The only exception to this flow is when there are multiple brokers in the transaction. In this instance, the customer nominal and price must be entered manually to reflect the broker values.

| Application | Functionality |
|---|---|
| Application | Functionality |
| SEC.ACC.MASTER | Defaults values based on the selection criteria defined the fields from Default Depo to App Value fields |
| CUSTOMER.SECURITY | Defaults the value in the Default Depository field |
| SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT | Defaults values at customer or portfolio or stock exchange level. The various options available in sequence are: COMPANY*PORTFOLIO*STOCK EXCHANGE COMPANY*CUSTOMER*STOCK EXCHANGE COMPANY*PORTFOLIO COMPANY*CUSTOMER COMPANY**STOCK.EXCHANGE COMPANY |
| SECURITY.POSITION | Defaults the values from this record , if available. If default value is not obtained from the above applications |
| SECURITY.MASTER | Defaults the value in the Default Depository field |

##### Order Routing

The securities orders originate from a modelling session or customer request to buy or sell securities from the portfolio. After the order details are verified, the order can be transmitted to the broker for execution.

If the Deal Status field in is set to Transmitted, the system creates a SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record with the same reference as the order ID. The execution details received from the broker are recorded in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS . The execution can either be for the full order nominal or part of the order and can be with a single or multiple brokers.

The trade is created automatically by the system on authorisation of the execution record. The back office can validate the details of the trade including the nominal, execution price, charges or commissions and proceed with the settlement.

The order can be a multi-customer order for purchase or sale of the same security. In such case, the system allows the creation of a single or multiple trade(s) for the order. This is controlled by the Trade Creation field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS and allows all types of trade creation, like:

- Trade by cust
- Trade by depo
- Trade by broker or
- Trade by portfolio

Also, the system allows the grouping of individual orders before transmitting them to the broker for execution. The orders can be routed to an execution hub or internal broker or dealer. In this case, the orders originating from a location (company or book in case of a multi-book environment) is routed to an execution hub (another company or book) based on the pre-defined conditions. Then, the execution hub handles the street-side executions and pass back the order or execution status to the originating location. The routing is controlled based on SC.ORDER.ROUTING wherein, the routing conditions can be setup based on any field in SECURITY.MASTER and SEC.ACC.MASTER applications.

The order routing record can be created at both system level and company level. The order of priority is:

1. Company level
2. System level

In this case, all the orders pertaining to securities being traded in the London Stock Exchange (LSE) are set to be routed to the GB.EXEC.HUB company. Any order meeting the above condition, from any company (other than GB.EXEC.HUB) or book are routed to GB.EXEC.HUB.

In SC.ORDER.ROUTING , multiple routing conditions are set and the routing company is defaulted based on the best fit.

In this case, all LSE equity orders are routed to GB.EXEC.HUB. However, if the order pertains to bonds, it is routed to GB.BOND.DESK. The Rout Sec Acc in SC.ORDER.ROUTING reflects the valid cross-trading portfolio or the wash portfolio used in the executing company for placing an order with the executing broker. The cross-trading portfolio must be valid portfolio in the executing company. An order with routing conditions set are explained below in detail.

1. Since this is a LSE equity trade, this must be routed to GB.EXEC.HUB. The executing company receives the order and execute the same through the executing broker. After execution, the executing company requests for settlement at its account with the depository. Based on the routing instructions set, the routing details are defaulted in the order.
2. Based on the routing instructions, an order is created in the executing (or routed) company.
3. The customer is the cross-trading portfolio from the Rout Sec Acc field of the original order. The broker and depository details are updated from the parent order.
4. After the order is executed in the hub, the execution is mirrored in the originating company. The routed order cannot be executed manually in the originating company.

If the order flows from TAP to Temenos Transact , the Tap Order Ref captured in the originating company flows to the routed order in the execution company as well. This is a common reference for the order throughout Wealth Suite. If the incoming MT515 message could not identify the order based on the SEC.OPEN.ORDER reference, the SEC.TRADE is identified based on this common order reference.


##### Flow for Execution

The flow of execution can be setup in the SC.ORDER.ROUTING application. The Exe Orig Comp field decides where the order is executed. If the Exe Orig Comp field is set to Yes, the execution takes place in the originating company and the execution is mirrored in the execution hub. Whereas, if the Exe Orig Comp field is set to No, execution takes place in the execution hub and execution is mirrored to the originating company.

The SEC.ACC.MASTER can be shared across companies. When FILE.CONTROL for SEC.ACC.MASTER is CUS, the order routing is not valid. Instead, it is possible to specify the hub company in the Port Comp Id field in SEC.ACC.MASTER . All trades and transactions for the portfolio can take place directly in the hub company without any routing. The accounting entries on the customer side can be posted automatically in the portolio's own company, identified by the Own Company field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application. Similarly, the broker charges, commissions and taxes can be re-invoiced to the portfolio's own company.

After the execution is complete, the trades are created both in the executing company and the originating company. In the execution company, there are two trades:

- The street-side trade routed through the cross trading or wash portfolio ( Rout Sec Acc field defined in the order). The depository is from the original order and indicates the location of the positions. The broker is the executing broker from the original order. The portfolio is the value in the Rout Sec Acc from the original order and denotes the cross-trading portfolio used for the street-side trade of the routed order. The broker is the executing broker from the original order.
- The second trade is to deliver the stock to the beneficiary. For the execution hub, the beneficiary is the originating company from where the order was routed. The originating company is identified through a portfolio defined for it in the executing (routing) company.


##### Fund Orders

The SC module supports different type of funds offered by the fund houses like growth and dividend.

In this option, the fund house does not pay out dividends. The profits are re-invested directly by the fund house, thus increasing the NAV of the fund.

In this option, two choices are available to the investors. In the Cash payout option, cash is paid out to the investors, as and when dividends are declared. Under the dividend re-investment option, a divided is declared and the same is re-invested into further units of the fund. The choice of opting for cash pay-out or re-investment of dividends is made at the time of investing in the fund.

This feature helps in setting up the dividend options at instrument master for the various fund types and provides the dividend pay-out or dividend re-investment option at the order level to the customers.

The fields highlighted in the below screenshot are setup in SECURITY.MASTER to capture the attributes of the fund.

The fund orders are processed in Temenos Transact :

- The Fund Type field is setup in SECURITY.MASTER to identify the type of fund. The field accepts either growth or dividend as values.

The following fields are setup in SECURITY.MASTER , to handle the different dividend options:

- The Reinvest Allowed field accepts the input as Yes or No.
- The Invest Option Type field is the beginning of the multi-value set and the field accepts the values based on the EB.LOOKUP application with ID starting with INVEST.TYPE. The table contains the options cash and re-invest.
- The Option Depository field is the end of the multi-value set. This field accepts the valid depository ID. Based on the option selected in Invest option Type field, the depository is defaulted in SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE .
- The Invest Option Type and Option Depository fields are used to hold positions in different accounts at the depository based on the dividend method opted by the investor.

The Invest Option Type field is setup in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE applications. This field accepts values Cash or Re-invest, based on the investor’s choice of the dividend method. Depending on the option selected by the investor in the Invest option Type field, the corresponding option depository is populated. For example, if the customer selects the cash as option, the depository in the Option Depository field in SECURITY.MASTER , corresponding to cash option is defaulted. This ensures that the SECURITY.POSITION is held separately for fund holdings with dividend payout option and fund holdings with re-invest option.

If the customer does not select an option in the Invest Option Type field for an order for a dividend fund, the default option is Cash.

The following types of SWIFT messages are supported in Temenos Transact for fund orders.

The MX message ‘setr.010.001.04’ has the value in the Invest Option Type field mapped to the tag income preference . If the value in the Invest Option Type field is Cash, the tag income preference is mapped as Cash. If the value in the Invest Option Type field is Reinvest, the tag income preference is mapped as Drip.

The MT502 message has the value in the Invest Option Type field mapped to tag 22H with qualifier as BUSE (buy sell indicator) and code as SUBS (subscription) or REDM (redemption). The field 22F with qualifier as CAOP has the code as Cash or DRIP (reinvest).

If an investor switches from dividend payout to dividend re-investment option, a position transfer is created to move from one depository (account) to the other.

The MT564 is received with DVCA code for the holdings with dividend payout option and an MT564 with SWIFT CAEV as DRIP is received for holdings with dividend re-investment option. Temenos Transact handles the diary accordingly.


##### Parent Child Orders

The bulk orders with multiple customers can be categorised into customer and market side, so that any amendment or cancellation of one side does not impact the other.

The security orders can be created as parent child orders in which the parent order holds the broker (market) side and the child orders holds each customer’s side. The parent-child orders are linked by a common reference and their separation continues into execution and trade creation. The separation of an order into broker side and customer sides can also be done at the time of execution. In this case, the system creates separate trades, a parent trade for the broker side and child trades for each of the customer’s side.

This functionality allows the users to amend or cancel one or more customer legs of an order or trade, without impacting the market side and vice-versa. To enable the parent child bulk orders are, the following parameters must be set-up. The users must create a synthetic counterparty and synthetic portfolio in the system and attach these to the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE record.

The following fields in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE must be set for this functionality to work.

- Synthetic Port - Indicates the synthetic portfolio used for parent child processing. The value specified here is updated in the customer side of the parent transaction.
- Synthetic Cpty - Indicates the synthetic counterparty used for parent child processing. The value specified here is updated in the broker side of the child transaction.
- Synthetic Susp Cat - Indicates the synthetic suspense category used for parent child processing .The internal account category specified here is used for entry processing in parent and child trades. For parent trade, the customer side account is the internal account formed using this category. For child trade, the broker side account is the internal account formed using this category.
- Trade Creation - Accepts the PARENT.CHILD value for creating parent child trades on execution. If this default setup is unavailable, this requirement can be specified at the execution stage in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS .
- Authorise Child - Indicates that the Child Trades are to be authorised on authorisation of Parent, if this field is set to Yes.
- Parent Child Depo - Indicates the creation of a separate parent trade for each depository if different depositories are involved.

This parameter informs the system about the fields to be the same in the parent and child transactions. If there is any discrepancy in these fields between the parent and child, the system updates an exception log file. The child transaction can be authorised only if the exceptions are resolved. By default, the system validates if the nominal and accrued interest matches between the parent and child transaction.

The Field Name multi-value fields refer to the fields in SEC.TRADE record. The Ord Field Name multi-value fields refer to the fields in SEC.OPEN.ORDER record. The Order Excep Check field determines if exception validations must happen for SEC.OPEN.ORDER s. If this is not set, then exception validation happens only for SEC.TRADE records.

The user can create a parent order with the synthetic portfolio on the customer side and the actual broker on the street-side. The Parent field must be set to Yes, to denote the parent order. The Parent Reference field must be updated with a unique reference, which links the parent and child orders.

The user can create any number of child orders. The customer is the actual customer and the broker is the synthetic counterparty. The Parent field is not set and the Parent Reference field must contain the same reference as given in the parent order.

The Parent Child Orders (SC.ORDER.PARENT.REF) enquiry is used to validate if the parent child orders are balanced and to amend or create new orders.

Only the parent order (broker side) is executed manually by setting the Order Status field to TRANSMITTED. The SC.PARENT.EXECUTION service in the background automatically executes the child orders and creates the respective SEC.TRADE records in IHLD status. Then a trade is created for the child orders.

The SEC.OPEN.ORDERS with multiple customers, can be split into parent child orders at the time of execution. The Trade Creation field defaults from the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE record and must be set to PARENT.CHILD

Then, on authorising the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record, the system splits and creates the following:

- Parent trade with the synthetic portfolio on customer’s side and the actual broker and
- As many child trades as required with the actual customers on the customer side and the synthetic counterparty on the broker side.

The trades are created in IHLD status and the SC.PARENT.TRADE.AUTHORISE service authorises all trades.

> **⚠️ Note:** The parent child trades can be aggregated as well. They can be aggregated for sending settlement messages and also for nostro aggregation.

The parent child orders configured for SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is shown in the below screenshot.

If the Parent Child Depo field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE record is set to Yes, the number of parent trade generated is based on the number of depositories involved. If there are multiple depositories, the Parent Child Depo and Parent Reference fields create the trades by portfolio and group the trades of different depositories into a parent trade for each depository.

The Parent Child Depo field is also available in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record and it defaults the value from SC.STD.SEC.TRADE record. However, it can be manually amended if the Trade Creation field contains the PARENT.CHILD value (that is, trade creation must be parent child, whereas order is single with multiple portfolios) or Parent Reference field has a value (that is, order is parent child).

If there is any difference between the nominals or accrued interest set in the parent transaction and the total nominals or accrued interest of all the child transactions; the system creates a record in this table. If there is any discrepancy in the fields specified in SC.BULK.TRANS.MATCHING record, this log is updated.

The user can verify the details and correct the exception. The child transactions can be authorised, only if there are no exceptions, else, the system displays an error message.

If the Authorise Child field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER or SEC.TRADE record is set, then a SC.CHILD.TRADE.AUTH service authorises all the child trades. The SC.BULK.CHILD.AUTHORISE application authorises the parent child transactions in bulk. A parent order or trade ID is updated and after the user authorises this record, the system triggers the SC.PARENT.TRADE.AUTHORISE (bulk authorisation) service and authorises all the child orders or trades.

If the Delete Child field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER or SEC.TRADE record is set to Yes in the parent and the record is left in INAU status, the SC.PARENT.CHILD.ORDER.REV or SC.PARENT.CHILD.TRADE.REV service deletes all the child transactions.

The SC.BULK.REPLACE application is used to replace or recapture an entire set of parent or child trades after authorisation. The parent trade ID is entered and when the record is authorised, the system triggers a SC.PARENT.CHILD.PROCESSING service. This service deletes all the existing parent and child trades and creates them afresh which are left IHLD status.

The SC.BULK.UPDATE.PARAMETER application is used to update the parent values into all child transactions. The ID is either of SEC.OPEN.ORDER and/or SEC.TRADE records. The list of fields to be updated into child transactions on changing the parent must be specified in this application. Either this can be the core or local reference fields (prefixed by L-).

After a parent transactions is amended and if a bulk update is to be performed, the Bulk Update field in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE must be set to Yes. The parent transaction is left in INAU status. The SC.PARENT.CHILD.PROCESSING service performs a bulk update into child transactions and either authorises both the parent and child transactions or leaves them in INAU status based on the Authorise Child field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE records.

The Rounding Factor field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER or SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record holds the values only in multiples of trading units. The execution of the order follows this order lot instead of the trading units.

Message MT502 is sent by an instructing party (client) to an executing party (broker) to instruct the executing party to buy or sell a given quantity of specified financial instrument.

This message is used to instruct the executing party to buy or sell a given quantity of a specified financial instrument.

MT502 replacement message is generated on modifying an existing order.
