### 5.54  Payment Order Generation for MT202 or MT103


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER applications have an in-built capability to handle payments made directly to the counterparty, in case of free of payment (FOP) contracts. This is generally done through book transfers or externally through correspondent banks, by generating SWIFT payments and adv...*
> 
> **Applications:** `>PAYMENT.ORDER`, `CUSTOMER`, `CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `PAYMENT.ORDER`, `PAYMENT.ORDER.PRODUCT`, `PWM.PO.PARAMETER`, `SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT`, `SC.SSI.PARAM` ... +2 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *@ID*, *Acct Trans Po*, *Acct With Bank Bic*, *Acct With Bank Customer*, *Acct With Bank Swift Addr*, *Bank to Bank Info*, *Beneficiary Account*, *Beneficiary Account No* ... +57 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER applications have an in-built capability to handle payments made directly to the counterparty, in case of free of payment (FOP) contracts. This is generally done through book transfers or externally through correspondent banks, by generating SWIFT payments and advices. The counterparty with whom the banks enter into a contract can be classified into two categories. One of the counterparties has an account relationship with Temenos Transact bank and the other does not.

- If an account relationship exists, then the settlement of cash generally takes place through those accounts.
- If an account relationship does not exist, then the settlement of cash takes place through a Nostro account with corresponding payment messages being generated.

If the settlement takes place through a Nostro account, the SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER applications can automatically determine the Nostro and generate a swift payment message (MT202 or MT103). Integrating SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER applications with the PAYMENT.ORDER application aims at centralising the external payment processing.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To enable the processing of external payments for FOP SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER contracts through the PAYMENT.ORDER application, a record needs to be created in PWM.PO.PARAMETER application.


##### PWM.PO.PARAMETER

The bank needs to setup this parameter file for the generation of a payment order. The ID of the application is the Company ID. The Po Product field holds a valid record in PAYMENT.ORDER.PRODUCT that is supported or used by the Securities (SC) module. Once set, this field becomes a no-input field. Banks can additionally configure the applications where a payment order is to be generated. The Po Application field is a multi-value set which holds the list of applications that has the capability of generating a payment order message. The banks can configure the suspense category, the payment category, payment method and so on for each application or create a single multi-value set with the Po Application field set to ALL.

The Po Susp Categ field holds a valid category account and acts as a wash account. For applications mentioned in Po Application , the system debits the customer’s account and credits the category account. The Nostro is not credited from the calling applications in SC module. Temenos Payments in turn debits the suspense account and credits the corresponding counterparty account (Nostro).

> **⚠️ Note:** If there are no records in the PWM.PO.PARAMETER application, then the system does not generate payment orders and continues with the old mechanism of handling settlements within the underlying application. The bank can also stop the payment order generation by setting the Acct Trans Po field to No without reversing the PWM.PO.PARAMETER .


##### Cash SSI Details

A counterparty can maintain an account with the issuing bank or some other bank. When an account is maintained with the bank, the system can directly make the payments. When the counterparty does not have an account with the bank, the system generates an external payment. However, for the external payment (SWIFT) the funds might need to move between different banks before they reach the recipient. The SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT application holds the account details of the counterparty and the intermediary bank details, if any. Read the SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT for Broker for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

When the banks opt for the settlement of payments through the PAYMENT.ORDER application, the system performs the following:

1. Generates a record in PAYMENT.ORDER application by passing the necessary details.
2. Suppresses the old mechanism of generation of payment messages by the underlying application


##### Payment Order Generation fromSEC.TRADE

When the Po Application field in PWM.PO.PARAMETER has value as either SEC.TRADE or ALL, all payments made directly to the counterparty from SEC.TRADE application is made through payment order if:

- Payment Reqd is set to Yes
- Delivery Instr is set to Free of Payment
- Counterparty’s account (Br Acc No) is not a Temenos Transact cash account or an internal category account other than the Po Susp Categ account or broker’s own Nostro account.
- The trade takes place in a credit or subscription scenario (that is, broker sells the securities)

> **⚠️ Note:** Payment order is not raised for a debit or redemption scenario.

The counterparty’s settlement account Br Acc No in SEC.TRADE is defaulted as per the priority given below. If Temenos Payments is not licensed, then:

- When Br Sett Instruct in the SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT application is set for the broker, then the same account defaults to the Br Acc No field (counterparty account field) in the SEC.TRADE application.
- When the counterparty’s settlement account is defined in Br Set Acc field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY , the system defaults the same account to the Br Acc No field (counterparty account field) in the SEC.TRADE application.
- When the broker has an account with the bank (broker’s own account), the same account is defaulted to the Br Acc No (counterparty account) field in the SEC.TRADE application.
- When a nostro account is defined, then the system defaults the same account to the Br Acc No (counterparty account) field in the SEC.TRADE application.
- When none of the above is applicable, the system throws an error. The customer gives a broker account manually.

If Temenos Payments is licensed, then:

- When Br Sett Instruct in the SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT application is set for the broker, then the same defaults to the Br Acc No (counterparty account field) in the SEC.TRADE application.
- When the counterparty’s settlement account is defined in Br Set Acc field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY , the system defaults the same account to the Br Acc No (counterparty account field) in the SEC.TRADE application.
- When the broker has an account with the bank (broker’s own account) the system defaults the same account to the Br Acc No (counterparty account field) in the SEC.TRADE application.

- When none of the above is applicable, then the system defaults the internal account based on the Po Susp Categ (formed with Br Account Ccy ) defined in the PWM.PO.PARAMETER .

> **⚠️ Note:** The system raises a payment order message only when the Br Acc No field is either a Nostro account not belonging to the broker himself or an internal suspense account formed using the Po Susp Categ fields defined in PWM.PO.PARAMETER .

The user configures the depository settlement account in CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the depository for Deliver Against Payment (DAP) trades.

Temenos Payments determines the receiver of the message. |

When the record in SEC.TRADE is placed for a subscription order with

- Payment Reqd field set to Yes and
- Broker Deliver Instruction field set to FOP trades,

the system then checks for the correct SSI in SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT based on the Broker No field provided the Cash Ssi Process field is set to Yes in SC.SSI.PARAM . If a valid SSI is found, then the system fetches and defaults all the beneficiary bank and intermediary bank details. Read the Defaulting Cash SSI Instructions in SEC.TRADE Transaction – Broker for more information. When the record in SEC.TRADE is authorised, the system maps the fields from SEC.TRADE to PAYMENT.ORDER . The payment messages from SEC.TRADE application are suppressed. The PAYMENT.ORDER ID generated is stored in the Po Br Reference field in the SEC.TRADE application.

Example

Consider a customer places a buy order. The broker’s delivery instruction is free of payment.

The payment order is created for the required amount with appropriate settlement instructions.

Once the payments system processes the payment, the system generates an appropriate SWIFT payment message.

When the SEC.TRADE is authorised, the system raises an accounting entry by debiting the customer account and crediting the Po Susp Categ account defined in PWM.PO.PARAMETER .

Temenos Payments debits the Po Susp Categ account and credits the counterparty’s Nostro account if the counterparty’s account is passed on from SEC.TRADE . Temenos Payments also determine the counterparty’s account if it is not passed from SEC.TRADE and then credits the Nostro account and debits the Po Susp Categ account.

> **⚠️ Note:** Use the payment system ID to view the accounting entries generated by PAYMENT.ORDER application.

When the contract is reversed in the SEC.TRADE application, there are two possible scenarios:

- Payment order is not generated and the system reverses the contract.
- Payment order is generated and the system raises an override: ’Payment Order has been generated’. If the override is accepted, the system reverses the SEC.TRADE transaction and changes are not made to the payment order. The user can handle the cancellation or reversal of the payment order manually.


##### Payment Order Generation fromSECURITY.TRANSFER

When Po Application in PWM.PO.PARAMETER has value set as either SECURITY.TRANSFER or ALL, all payments made to the counterparty from SECURITY.TRANSFER application is made through a payment order, if:

- Payment Reqd is set to Yes
- Delivery Instr is set to Payment Only
- Counterparty’s account (Broker Acc No) is not a Temenos Transact account or an internal category account other than the internal account formed with Po Susp Categ account or broker’s own Nostro account.

The transfer takes place for a credit scenario (transfer in).

> **⚠️ Note:** Payment order is not raised for a debit scenario (transfer out).

The counterparty’s settlement account (Broker Acc No) in SECURITY.TRANSFER is defaulted as per the priority given below.

If Temenos Payments is not licensed, then:

- When Br Sett Instruct in the SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT application is set for the broker, then the system defaults the same account to the Broker Acc No (counterparty account) field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application.
- When the counterparty has a Vostro account, then the system defaults the same account to the Broker Acc No (counterparty account) field in SECURITY.TRANSFER application.
- When the counterparty has an account with the bank (broker’s own account), the system defaults the same account to the Broker Acc No (counterparty account) field in the SEC.TRADE application.
- When the counterparty’s settlement account is defined using the Br Set Acc field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY , the system defaults the same account to Broker Acc No (counterparty account) field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application.
- When a Nostro account is defined, then the system defaults the same to the Broker Acc No (counterparty account) field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application.
- If none of the above is applicable, the system throws an error. The customer gives a broker or counterparty account manually.

If Temenos Payments is licensed, then:

- The system checks for the counterparty’s account in the SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT application or checks if the counterparty has a Vostro account or an account with the bank (broker’s own account) or checks CUSTOMER.SECURITY .
- If none of the above is applicable, then the system defaults the internal account based on the Po Susp Categ field defined in PWM.PO.PARAMETER .

> **⚠️ Note:** The system raises a payment order message only when the Broker Acc No is one of the following: A Nostro account not belonging to the broker himself An internal suspense account formed using the Po Susp Categ defined in PWM.PO.PARAMETER .

### 5.55  Personal Assets


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *External or other assets are assets that are held outside the bank’s books that the adviser/customer may include in their portfolio valuation or for capital gain calculation.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Acquisition Date*, *Adj Nom*, *Adj Reduce Cost*, *Adj Trd Cost*, *Amend Txn Id*, *Apply to all*, *Asset Desc*, *Asset Description* ... +58 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

External or other assets are assets that are held outside the bank’s books that the adviser/customer may include in their portfolio valuation or for capital gain calculation.

External assets can be any of the following:

- Externally held shares, funds, bonds and so on - They share the same security master ID as on-platform positions. The security and price are fed in from a data source and are common to both on-platform and external positions. These are also referred as shared assets.
- Personal Assets - They are unique to an individual portfolio. The asset is administered and priced at account level. Advisers look after personal assets of their own customers. Property, car, art collections, racehorse, insurance bonds, cash account in external bank and so on are non-shared assets.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following set up is required to record the personal assets in a portfolio.


##### SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.PARAM

This application holds the classification and attributes required for personal assets. Personal assets are created directly and these attributes are not sourced from any data provider, such as TDS or Bloomberg. Thus, the price source in most cases is set to manual for each personal asset. All the transaction codes to be defaulted while performing buy, sell, write-in and write-out are specified in this application. The wash depository specified here, acts as a dummy depository to record all personal asset positions.


##### ASSET.TYPE

For each asset allocation category, a separate record in ASSET.TYPE is created in Temenos Transact . A record named 63 in ASSET.TYPE is allocated to the property category. It is also acceptable to create a single asset type for all personal assets.


##### SUB.ASSET.TYPE

For each type of personal asset, a record in SUB.ASSET.TYPE needs to be created. This record must be linked to the correct asset allocation category. To ensure that this record falls under a personal asset category, the Personal Asset field must be flagged to Yes.

The record named 658 in

is allocated to Residential Investment Property falling under 63 record in

.


##### SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TYPE

This application enables the user to record the attributes relevant to each personal asset type. The ID of the record must be a valid record in SUB.ASSET.TYPE that is marked as personal asset.

In some cases the same personal asset can fall under two or more asset allocations. In such scenarios, a separate record in SUB.ASSET.TYPE must be created for each of them.

If a personal asset called Residential Investment Property has the asset allocation type set to Property or International Share, two separate records in SUB.ASSET.TYPE must be created(for Property and International Share) and two records in SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TYPE are also created.

The Disposal Tax Treatment set in this application is used to calculate the capital gains tax and is defaulted in the transaction record of the personal asset type. The Liability field is set to Yes for the asset types that needs to be treated as liability. Capital gains are not handled for liabilities.

If the Multiple Lots field is set to Yes, the system allows multiple purchase or sale for a particular personal asset. The Expense Tax Treatment and Income Tax Treatment fields are only for reporting purposes and are not mandatory. Sometimes, the CG are exempted on certain personal assets, if their acquisition cost is less than a certain amount. If Cg Exempt Value field is set and if the acquisition cost of the asset is less than or equal to this value, then the system calculates CG as zero on the disposal of such assets. The value defined in this field is always in the local currency.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Multiple Lots field cannot be set if the Cg Exempt Value field is defined.

All the personal asset types created are listed in the below screenshot. The user can edit or view the existing personal assets created. Also, new asset or sub asset type can be created using the below enquiry.


#### 🔧 Working With

All transactions pertaining to personal assets are recorded in SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TXN . The ID of the SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TXN is a free-format ID. The transactions created for personal assets are explained in below sections.


##### Initial Update

Initial update is the first transaction, which creates a unique Security Master for the portfolio for a particular personal asset. Position is not updated. For each personal asset in a portfolio, a unique Security Master is created.

Once the record is committed, the system creates a record in SECURITY.MASTER , whose ID is updated back into SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TXN .

The SECURITY.MASTER created for a portfolio’s personal asset has the Personal Asset field flagged. Direct SECTRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER are not allowed for such records in SECURITY.MASTER . These can only be traded through SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TXN .


##### Buy/Write-In of an Asset

This transaction is performed only if there is an initial update that has already created the record in SECURITY.MASTER . It records a position of a personal asset into the system. Necessary details such as Transaction Amt , Quantity and any other Txn Expenses are captured.

Once the record is committed the system creates a record in SECURITY.TRANSFER, whose ID is updated back into SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TXN . Generally, personal assets are brought into the books only for valuation and/or capital gain (CG) calculations. Hence, accounting entry is not expected.


##### Sale/Write-Out of an Asset

Partial sale of the personal asset is allowed if the Multiple Lots field is set in SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TYPE . However, when this field is not set, the entire asset is sold or transferred (write-out) that is, the system does not allow partial sale of personal assets.

Once the record is committed the system creates a SECURITY.TRANSFER out transaction, whose ID is updated back into SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TXN .

> **⚠️ Note:** If a value is specified in the Cg Exempt Value field in SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TYPE , the system checks the Cg Value Lcy field in SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TXN for that personal asset type. If the amount in the Cg Value Lcy field is less than or equal to the value specified in the Cg Exempt Value field, then the system calculates CG as zero. Else, the system calculates the CG based on the Disposal Tax Treatment set in SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TYPE .

The user can define the parcels that needs to be disposed-off when a sell or write-out transaction is entered. The Tax Lot Allocate field holds a valid tax lot ID pertaining to the position of the personal asset that needs to be disposed-off, and the Qty Allocated field holds the quantity that needs to be allocated for the specified tax lot ID.

When the user provides the tax lot ID to be allocated and quantity, the system maps these fields to the corresponding fields in the underlying record created in SECURITY.TRANSFER . The system uses the same details (values defined in Tax Lot Allocate and Qty Allocated fields) for allocation and calculation of capital gains (CG).


##### Modifying Buy or Sell Transactions Post Authorisation

If the user has entered the wrong price or quantity and wants to modify the existing buy or sell transaction, then the Transaction Type field is set to Amend Txn in SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TXN . If the Transaction Type field is set to Amend Txn, then the Amend Txn Id field becomes a mandatory input field that accepts a valid SECURITY.TRANSFER ID relevant to that transaction. When a valid SECURITY.TRANSFER ID is entered and when the record is validated, the system automatically updates the following fields from the relevant buy or sell transaction.

- Transaction Code (cannot be changed)
- Transaction Amount or Price
- Quantity
- Transaction Date
- Tax Effective Date

When the user changes the value and the record is authorised, the system reverses the previous record in SECURITY.TRANSFER and creates a new record in SECURITY.TRANSFER . The Reversal Ind field is updated as R in the multi-value pertaining to the reversed transaction.

> **⚠️ Note:** Initial update and maturity events cannot be amended.


##### Maturity

On maturity the entire asset is sold or transferred (write-out) that is, there is no partial maturity.


##### Update Price or Value

Personal assets are created directly and therefore the price is not sourced from any data provider, such as TDS or Bloomberg. This transaction allows the user to update the price as and when required.

The updated price is also reflected in SECURITY.MASTER .


##### Insurance Bond Contribution

Investors can make regular contributions on insurance bonds held. The Ins Bond Contribution option in Transaction Type field works similar to a Buy. However, the acquisition date of the tax lot created is the same as the first buy date. Hence, all contributions have the same acquisition date. Thus, it ensures that for CG purpose, the period of holding is based on the initial subscription to the insurance bond and does not change for each contribution. If the Reset Date field is provided, the acquisition date of all the tax lots are changed to the reset date. This may be required in some cases.

In Australia, if the contribution in any year exceeds 125% of the previous year’s contribution, the holding start date is reset to the year when the excess contribution was made. This date has to be manually input and there is no logic in the system to automatically update this.


##### Insurance Bond Withdrawal

Investors can withdraw either their entire contribution or a partial amount of the insurance bond. The Ins Bond Withdrawal option in Transaction Type field works exactly like a Sell. The main difference is in the calculation of the CG. Insurance bonds have the Disposal Tax Treatment field set to Special in SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TYPE .

For special disposal tax treatment of an insurance bond, the system considers the value in the Bond Bonus field to be the profit earned on withdrawal of the insurance bond.

For an insurance bond withdrawal, user have to enter the bonus earned on withdrawal. If Cg Calc Param field is set to AU in CG.PARAMETER , the system automatically calculates the bond factor. The bond factor is calculated by the system as below:

- If withdrawal date is after 10 years of acquisition, the bond factor defaults to 0 that is, there are no CG observed.

- If withdrawn between 9 to 10 years of acquisition, the bond factor defaults to 1/3 that is, 1/3 rd of bonus is CG

- If withdrawn between 8 to 9 years of acquisition, bond factor defaults to 2/3
- If withdrawn within 8 years of acquisition, bond factor defaults to 1, that is, the entire bonus is treated as a CG.


##### Personal Liability

External personal liabilities, such as loans or mortgage commitments can also be recorded in a portfolio for valuation. A SUB.ASSET.TYPE and SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TYPE should be created as in the case of personal asset. The SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TYPE application has a flag to indicate if this is a liability.

Transactions for personal liabilities can be recorded as in the case of personal assets through SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TXN . Capital gains are not calculated for personal liabilities.

When there is a buy/write-in of a liability, the system must create a position with a negative value. To achieve this, the SECURITY.TRANSFER created must be a Transfer-out.

This leads to a short position which is shown as negative in position and valuation.

When there is a write-out of liability, the negative position must be reduced or removed. Hence, the SECURITY.TRANSFER created by the system is a Transfer-in.

This removes or reduces the negative position from the portfolio, that is, it offsets the short position created during the write-in of a liability.


##### Capital Gains Calculation on Personal Assets

Temenos Transact supports CG calculation for personal assets. Every buy or write-in creates a unique tax parcel. On sell or write-out, CG is calculated based on the value in Disposal Tax Treatment field pertaining to the personal asset type as specified in SC.PERSONAL.ASSET.TYPE .

Various disposal tax treatment that can be set up in Temenos Transact are mentioned in the below table.

| Value in Disposal Tax Treatment field | Description |
|---|---|
| CG.EXEMPT | CG is not calculated. Lot is allocated to the disposal and closed. |
| REVENUE | CG is not updated. However, profit on disposal is shown as Income. |
| STANDARD.CG | CG are calculated as for any other asset. Indexation and discount factors are used, if applicable. If the portfolio is on MIN.GAIN method, the CG is calculated accordingly. Else, it is calculated on First In First Out (FIFO) basis. |
| SPECIAL | Currently, this special method only handles CG on insurance bonds as applicable in Australia. Australian tax law has a special treatment for insurance bonds. Insurance bonds are like managed funds combined with an insurance policy. The investors can make regular contributions. If held for minimum of 10 years, the bonus on withdrawals are tax free. If withdrawn between 9 to 10 years of holding, 2/3 rd of the bonus is exempted and rest is taxed. If withdrawn between 8 to 9 years, 1/3 rd of the gains are exempted from CG tax and if withdrawn within 8 years, the entire bonus is taxed. |

> **⚠️ Note:** No parcels are created for personal liabilities and no capital gain is calculated

When an externally held stapled security is brought into the books, tax parcels and capital gain calculation is handled only at the parent security level, that is, it works like regular equity security and not a staple. There is no break-up at child level and therefore child parcels are not maintained.


#### 📋 Tasks

- Manage Personal Asset

Personal Assets (Property, Car, Art collections, Racehorse, Insurance bonds, Cash account in External Bank and so on) are assets that are unique to an individual portfolio. Capturing of Non-shared Personal assets auto-creates a unique Security Master for each of the Personal Asset held by the Portfolio. For shared Personal assets, an External Asset Security Master needs to be created manually prior to capturing of Personal Asset details.

The Personal Assets (Shared and Non-Shared) that are held outside the Bank’s books. Based on advisors and client request, these assets can be included for Valuation or Capital Gain Calculations. No accounting entries are raised for any Personal Asset Transaction.

Transactions such as:

- Buy/ Write-In
- Sale/ Write-Out
- Update Price/Value
- Ins Bond Contribution
- Ins Bond Withdrawal
- Maturity

#### 📖 Introduction

A portfolio is a collection of stocks, bonds, funds, cash accounts or any other assets owned by an investor. By consolidating the holdings into a portfolio, it is possible to manage them easily. It also allows the advisors or portfolio managers to apply different investment strategies to different portfolios.s


#### ⚙️ Configuration

After a CUSTOMER record is set up in Temenos Transact , one or many portfolios can be defined for that particular customer. This is done in two stages:

1. A record in CUSTOMER.SECURITY is created for the customer.
2. A record in SEC.ACC.MASTER is set up for each portfolio linked to the CUSTOMER record.

> **⚠️ Note:** For a dealer book portfolio, a customer record in the CUSTOMER application and a corresponding record in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application must be set up.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic details the process of setting up a portfolio in Temenos Transact .


##### Creating CUSTOMER Record

A CUSTOMER record is mandatory before a portfolio is created. A separate cash account is required for each portfolio.


##### Linking Customer to Portfolio Management System throughCUSTOMER.SECURITY

After a CUSTOMER record is entered, Temenos Transact must be informed that this customer is linked to the portfolio management system. Thus, a record in CUSTOMER.SECURITY must be entered with basic setup as shown in the following screenshot.

The frequency and report-related fields are described in the portfolio valuation section.

> **⚠️ Note:** This CUSTOMER application is also used to define brokers, depositories and so on. Read the Securities User Guide for more information on the use of the CUSTOMER.SECURITY file and setting up of new records.

The users must be able to identify the customers with whom the various day-to-day security activities are performed, before using the Securities (SC) module. Thus, it is necessary to ensure that at least one standard CUSTOMER record exists in Temenos Transact for every securities customer.

If a CUSTOMER record exists, the user must advise the SC module with the capacity (or capacities) in which the customer is acting (that is, the role of the customer in the transaction whether he is a customer, broker, or counterpart and so on). The CUSTOMER.SECURITY application is set up for this purpose. This application defines the capacity in which the customer acts in relation to the organisation (as shown in the following screenshot).

Before the user commences the securities transactions with anyone, the user must ensure that (both) a CUSTOMER and CUSTOMER.SECURITY record exist. While the user is working in the SC module, Temenos Transact identifies if a particular customer is yet to have a CUSTOMER.SECURITY record setup. At the same time, validations are made to ensure that the role or roles that are defined in the Customer Type fields of the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record are compatible with the particular activity required. For example, the user cannot enter a customer into a broker-related field, if the record is set up to be only as a customer when the user is entering the security transactions.

A particular customer may require more than one role. For example, the user may effect the security transaction with another party who may occasionally act as a depository for some of the organisation’s securities. The following are the typical customer types in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record. The user can define any number of the following roles:

| Role | Description |
|---|---|
| Customer | Enables the user to open a portfolio account in which buy, sell, hold and maintain securities are possible on behalf of that particular customer. Read the SEC.ACC.MASTER section for more information. |
| Counterparty | Enables the user to enter non-broker trading entities into the broker-related fields of any security transactions. |
| Broker | Enables the user to enter customer IDs of the broker into the broker-related fields in security transactions. |
| Depository | Enables the user to enter or default the depository locations for delivery and receipt of securities within a trade. |
| Client | Indicates that the SEC.ACC.MASTER record is not required, but trading of securities is still allowed. Cash is sent or received through other means. |


##### Setting Up CustomerAccount

Before setting up a customer portfolio, the customer requires at least one customer account to be opened in Temenos Transact t and an unique account or accounts are required for each portfolio of the customer. A single portfolio can have any number of accounts linked to it. Customers have accounts in different currencies to aid their trading activities.

When a trade is created, the system defaults the account in the trade currency that is linked to the portfolio. If account is not found in the trade currency, the system defaults the first account updated in the portfolio record. It is possible to set up a series of defaults to advise the system in using the two accounts during transaction input. This may be achieved by utilizing the Ac Def Sys Code field together with the Ac Def Ccy and Ac Def Acct fields to obtain the precise account depending upon the level of detail defined in the Ac Def Sys Code field.

A default of SC is required to indicate that the default account is to be used by the SC module for the SEC.ACC.MASTER application. Thereafter, more elaborate defaults may be defined using the application ID (in this case, SC) by adding a separator (-) and then any valid record in SC.TRANS.TYPE . For example, receipts of dividends may be credited to one account, whereas receipts of interest may be credited to another. If these fields are not updated, then the system attempts to get an account from the Account Nos field in the transaction currency. If none of the account matched, then the first account mentioned is used.

An individual portfolio in Temenos Transact is defined in the SEC.ACC.MASTER record. The ID of this application is customer number and a suffix separated by a hyphen. A single customer can have more than one portfolio attached to it. This is done by defining extra SEC.ACC.MASTER records and using a different suffix to differentiate the different portfolios.

100291-1, 100291-2, 100291-3 and so on are all portfolios belonging to customer 100291. Portfolios up to 997 can be linked to a single customer as suffix, 999 is reserved for depositories and 777 is reserved for brokers.

> **⚠️ Note:** The following record is used to link the portfolio to an account officer (portfolio manager - 1) and INVESTMENT.PROGRAM ( Investment field) for portfolio modelling purposes. It is also used to set up the cash account defaulting structure for the portfolio.

The Port Comp Id field is used to hold the HUB Company. The HUB Company is where the portfolio is allowed to trade. This field is set and then it automatically defaults from the Hub Company field in the SC.PARAMETER application. This is particularly relevant in customer installations, where all trades and transactions take place in a centralised HUB for portfolios belonging to various companies. If central HUB concept is not required, then this field defaults to the company where the portfolio is created.

The Own Comp any Id field defaults to the company where the portfolio is created. If the portfolio needs to be shared across companies:

- For SC and DX transactions - Transaction can be entered only in the company specified in the Port Comp any Id field of SEC.ACC.MASTER . The valuation process considers the details only from the Port Comp any Id field.
- For other transactions - Transaction can be entered only for the company specified in the Own Comp any Id field of SEC.ACC.MASTER . The valuation process considers the details from the Own Comp any Id field.

The Iam Portfolio field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application identifies the portfolios that are managed by independent (third-party) asset managers. Fees (similar to management fees) can be calculated and posted for such portfolios. The independent asset manager (IAM) fees uses the management fee framework for calculating the fees. The IAM Fees ( SC.IAM.FEES.LIST) enquiry lists the portfolios with IAM fees.

The Reimburse Tr Fee field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER (portfolio) application indicates whether the trailer fees received must be reimbursed to the customer or not. If the user sets this field to Yes, then the entire trailer fee accrued is reimbursed to the customer. In the SEC.ACC.MASTER application, the set up is available to deliver the messages that are portfolio specific. Read the Delivery section for more information.

The Trading Right field in SEC.ACC.MASTER captures who among the related third party is entitled to initiate or place orders or act as a decision maker or both. This field accept customer IDs of the original party and the third parties defined in the CUSTOMER.RELATIONSHIP , who has trading rights on behalf of the portfolio.

A portfolio that is opened for usage for an organisation for its own securities is very different from one that is opened for a private customer. For private customer portfolios, the user must specify certain information such as each customer’s selected financial accounts that are to be used when purchasing and selling securities and for the distribution of dividends and other corporate activities.

An own portfolio requires the specification of categories to which the various accounting entries normally associated with securities activity needs to be posted. For example, trading and revaluation of P&L, interest income and expense. In addition, the user must also specify the information of whether the user wishes to post revaluation profits, losses or both rather than simply reporting them. The following screenshot illustrates how a typical SEC.ACC.MASTER might define the name for an own portfolio that may be required, if the organisation performs the securities activity for its own account.

> **⚠️ Note:** Refer to the Help text associated with each field for full details as to the various options that are available and might be applicable to the particular organisation. The user can only define an own account portfolio if the customer number is entered in the Dealer Book field on each SEC.ACC.MASTER record, which the user wants to open for the purpose. Therefore, a CUSTOMER record is mandatory for own book.

After the user has indicated that the record opened is an internal portfolio, most of the fields immediately following the Dealer Book field becomes mandatory. These require the details such as category codes, which post specific accounting entries and defines some processing rules. One such rule is to check whether to post unrealised (revaluation) profits and losses (or both) into the accounts together, with the frequency at which to perform the revaluation.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Joint Holder | Denotes the customer(s) who are either joint holders or are related in some way or have some role in the portfolio. It must be the ID of a valid record in CUSTOMER . It can also be the customer of the portfolio itself. |
| Relation Code | Indicates the relationship of the joint holder to the primary holder and must be an existing record in the RELATION application. |
| Joint Holder Role | Indicates the role of the customer with reference to the portfolio. The roles are defined in EB.ROLE . A few examples of the roles are Owner, Beneficiary, Key Contact, and Authorized Signatory. |
| Joint Notes | A free text field for the customer to enter their own details |


##### Updating Portfolio Positions

After the user defines a portfolio in Temenos Transact by entering a SEC.ACC.MASTER record, the portfolios can be updated with positions by various Temenos Transact applications. There are essentially three ways of updating positions into a portfolio in Temenos Transact :

- From an account linked to the portfolio.
- Through the SC module.
- Through the other Temenos Transact applications that are linked through the ASSET.TYPE application.

A customer portfolio can be linked to accounts in the system. However, as a customer may have several portfolios and any number of cash accounts, it is necessary to define which accounts belong to the portfolio when opening a SEC.ACC.MASTER application. This is done by using the appropriately named Account Nos , multi-value field into which all accounts that are to be linked to the portfolio must be entered.

When calculating the value of a portfolio, the balance of those accounts are included in the valuation. Temenos Transact takes the balance of the account from the Online Actual Bal field in the ACCOUNT record for that account. Temenos Transact prevents the user from closing an account linked to a portfolio. The account must be removed from the SEC.ACC.MASTER record before closing. As the Temenos Transact Portfolio Management System includes any future securities entries, any forward accounting entries generated by the SC module are added to (or subtracted from balance on the ACCOUNT record depending on the sign of the entry) the balance on the ACCOUNT record in order to find the account balance used by the Portfolio Management System.

The following screenshot displays how an account might appear in a SEC.ACC.MASTER application where it can be seen that account 89885 is designated as belonging to the underlying portfolio.

After the new portfolio is set up, it includes the ID of any accounts belonging to the customer that are deemed to be part of the portfolio components. The user can now view how this affects the portfolio value by providing the customer with some funds. The following screenshot shows that Temenos Transact has credited the account with USD 100,000. A portfolio valuation must be performed to view how this affects the portfolio value. This can be done online by simply running the enquiries.

The Portfolio Evaluation - Trade Dated (SC.VAL.MARKET) enquiry is run for the portfolio. The SEC.ACC.MASTER record valuation after cash inflow is shown in the following screenshot.

The SUB.ASSET.TYPE application is used to provide a break and total in the enquiry.

Any securities transaction must include the ID of one or more portfolios. Thus, any transaction input into the SC module updates a portfolio with the value of that transaction. The forward value security transactions are included in the portfolio valuation. As portfolios must have one or more accounts associated with them, this procedure is followed. For example, a delivery against payment purchase creates a security holding together with a reduction of the cash account from which the cost is met. The opposite applies if the portfolio are disposing of a security, in which case, the value of the security is added to the customer account.

In cases, where a security is received or delivered free, certainly if there are no cash movement except a processing charge of some form, then only the securities movement affects the portfolio.

Derivatives (DX) transactions and transactions in structured products follow the same principl e as updating positions from the SC module. The p ortfolio used in the contract is updated with the holdings in the instrument ( DX contract or structured product contract) , and any cash movement is automatically adjust ed in the cash account.

Other non-SC applications can update a portfolio if they are being linked to the SC module through the ASSET.TYPE application. The FUNDS.TRANSFER application records the receipt of funds into a notional portfolio. In all cases, the user has to make an input into the Portfolio No field in the transaction concerned to update the portfolio. If the Portfolio No field is not updated, then the system does not consider the transaction as it was linked to the portfolio.

A customer has invested some cash into a deposit account with the bank. In this case, the Temenos Transact Loans and Deposits (LD) application is used. The Portfolio Number field has the value as 1.

However, if the Portfolio N umber field is left blank in the transaction, then the contract is not included in the valuation of portfolio 100271-3.

> **⚠️ Note:** The exception to this is when the module concerned (in this case, LD) has been entered in the Default Suffix field for the SC.PARAMETER record entered in the ID of the company in which the portfolio is included. If it has an entry, then when the system calculates the valuation of the portfolio, it links any transaction for a portfolio customer (which has a blank portfolio field to the portfolio of that customer with the lowest suffix). That is, if a customer had two portfolios 888-1 and 888-2, then the transaction with a blank in the Portfolio No field is linked to portfolio 888-1. For this reason and to avoid erroneously allocating a transaction to an incorrect portfolio, it is recommended that this facility must be used only if all customer portfolios are set up with a -1 suffix.

Another valuation on the same portfolio is run so that the user can view the deposit. The customer’s current portfolio is reduced from USD 100,000 to USD 75,000 as USD 25,000 is taken on deposit by the bank.

The user can drill down and confirm by checking the current account movement.

Now, the user is able to confirm both the original and current balances in order to obtain the details of cash movements. In the portfolio, the cash USD 25,000 is invested in securities, and therefore, the portfolio value remains more or less constant. That is, the underlying securities are revalued.


##### Portfolio Modelling

Temenos Transact allows a simple modelling feature in the SC module as explained below. The SC module allows the user to define a portfolio investment model and link that model to a portfolio and then produces comparisons between the actual holdings of the portfolio against its model. It is produced as hardcopy reports and screen enquiries. If the model is defined at a security level, then the system can produce the suggested buy and sell orders to put the holdings as close as possible in line with the model.

A portfolio model is defined in Temenos Transact by inputting a record in POLICY.PARAMETER . A record in POLICY.PARAMETER is defined at SUB.ASSET.TYPE or ASSET.TYPE level and the type of model can be a security or country model. The total percentage of the model must be equal to 100. Elements within the model can consist of an ASSET.TYPE , which can further be broken down into individual securities.

In the example, the user is required to maintain the portfolio of at least 15% of its value in cash. However, it is required that the remaining funds in any portfolio running under this model must invest in the listed securities at varying percentages between 10 and 20%. An example of a security-level portfolio model defined at ASSET.TYPE level is shown in the following screenshot.

This facility allows the grouping of securities instruments by maturity band when defining investment portfolios. This generally applies to bonds and bond-like instruments as few other instruments have the maturity dates. Maturity bands are defined within a portfolio and may be in the form of days, weeks, months or years. Definition of the maturity bands involves entering from and to period, which indicates the period within which the maturity date of a security (in SECURITY.MASTER ) must fall in order to satisfy the portfolio criteria.

> **⚠️ Note:** The setting up of maturity bands within a portfolio for Asset or Sub Asset types must be done at the security level. Failure to do so or mixing Asset and Sub Asset types may produce unreliable results. After the portfolio model with maturity bands are created in POLICY.PARAMETER , it is advisable to re-run both the SC.PORT.COMPARE and SC.GROUP.COMPARE applications to ensure the validity of the models and results produced.

A portfolio is defined in Temenos Transact through the record in SEC.ACC.MASTER . In the SEC.ACC.MASTER record, there is a mandatory field Investment Program that enables a record in SEC.ACC.MASTER to be linked to an INVESTMENT.PROGRAM . The INVESTMENT.PROGRAM records are then linked to a POLICY.PARAMETER using the Policy Parameter field (as shown in the following screenshot).

Any portfolio ( SEC.ACC.MASTER ) record, in which the Investment Program field is set to 25, is linked to the FUND01 record in POLICY.PARAMETER . Therefore, these portfolios use this model when compared to actual holdings against the predefined investment model.


##### Order by Customer Purchase

To illustrate the process, the following screenshot is an imaginary ORDER.BY.CUST . For example, the portfolio manager 75 has access to 2,900 of security ID 100064-000, currently trading at USD 39.44 a share.

The user can simply add the portfolio manager's ID and the portfolio manager can enter the number of securities available. Temenos Transact checks whether those portfolios for which the manager is responsible has any available cash. This request is flagged in the version by entering YES in the Cash Avail Reqd field. Those having available cash is considered eligible to purchase an amount of stock. The actual amount of security allocated by the program depends upon the overall value of each eligible portfolio.

It is possible to validate the transaction that prompts Temenos Transact to work out the allocations of the security using the criteria set in the order. The transaction then remains on view.

> **⚠️ Note:** The validated process enables the user to have a preview of the results of the request as the transaction remains on view. On the other hand, if all the minimum required information are present, then the commit function immediately processes the transaction making it available for the next stage authori s ation process without allowing the users to view the suggested orders.

The following screenshot explains about the two multi-value fields. As there were five candidate portfolios eligible for a share of 2,900 available security offered, the following screenshot displays how the allocations are returned to the user for approval.

To calculate the allocations, Temenos Transact first works out the total value of the candidate portfolios and uses this total as a divisor as follows:

| Portfolio | Valuation | Calculation of Order Allocation | Allocation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100286-1 | 812,586.91 | 2,900 / 1,123,292.97 x 812,586.91 = 2,097 round up | 2,100 |
| 111653-3 | 258,244.96 | 2,900 / 1,123,292.97 x 258,244.96 = 666 round up | 700 |
| 111659-2 | 52,461.10 | 2,900 / 1,123,292.97 x 52,461.10 = 135 round down | 100 |
|  | 1,123,292.97 |  | 2,900 |

Usually, some rounding adjustments are made according to the overall value of the portfolio as shown in the table.

Dealer book portfolios and memo accounts are not selected as part of the initial generation, and it is not possible to add the details for a dealer book portfolio or a memo account.


##### Portfolio Constraint

This facility allows the control of exposure to a particular issuer within a customer’s portfolio and additionally permits the inclusion or exclusion of trades depending upon the criteria defined. For issuer limits, constraints may be defined at issuer level and to impose either a percentage limit (as a percentage of the portfolio value) or amount limit based on the level of trading. If either of these limits is set to zero, then trading is blocked.

When a trade is entered (through SEC.TRADE ), an override message is generated if the holding of a particular issuer exceeds either:

- The maximum percentage of the value of the portfolio.
- The maximum value permitted for the issuer within the portfolio.

This is determined by the constraint defined for the individual portfolio. Constraints may be setup at two levels in the PORTFOLIO.CONSTRAINT application, that is, at system level and at each individual portfolio level. The following screenshot displays how the basic SYSTEM default record must be set up. The setting up of this record ensures that any securities bought and not containing reference to an issuer is always be accepted for addition to the portfolio holdings.

If it is required that the securities issued by a particular issuer must not exceed either a percentage of the total value of a portfolio or a specific amount, it is necessary to define the required details using a reference to the portfolio for which the checking must take place. For percentage requests, the user can opt to prevent the inclusion of any securities belonging to a specific issuer (in this case, percentage to be set to zero ) or any percentage up to 100% as preferred by the user. This indicates that checking is not performed at all for that particular issuer.

For specific amount requests, the user is prompted to supply a currency code as well as the amount to which the user wishes to restrict a holding to in the portfolio. It is not necessary to have the same currency as the underlying security issue currency. The user can use any currency, and it is validated to ensure that any addition of security to a portfolio does not cause the total holding to exceed the equivalent specified in the constraint record.

Additionally, when trading in particular securities or types of financial instruments based on customer directives is required, constraints are defined by selecting any field in SECURITY.MASTER to include or exclude the particular security from this portfolio. For example, a customer may request the exclusion of any securities for which the issuer is involved in insurance. In this instance, the user can effect the restriction using the Industry Code field in the SECURITY.MASTER application.

The ability to either block the trade completely or issue a warning to inform the user, that this trade may not be desirable, is determined by defining the message type as either an ERROR or an OVERRIDE. When a trade is executed (through SEC.TRADE ), it is validated against the defined constraints for this portfolio and either an error message or override is generated accordingly.

> **⚠️ Note:** The constraints are triggered only when the issuer is defined in the associated SECURITY.MASTER record.

In the above instance, checking is done on all security purchases performed on behalf of portfolio 888-1:

- To ensure, that any securities issued by customer 100299 do not exceed 50% of the total portfolio value.
- For all other issuers, no restriction up to 100% of the portfolio value is permitted.

> **⚠️ Note:** Any trades for which the issuer is not defined on the underlying SECURITY.MASTER are unchecked by the application.

Temenos Transact may require to block trades in securities issued by an entity. This can be done either in the form of an error message or by override. The user can achieve this by setting up the required PORTFOLIO.CONSTRAINT record similar to the following extract.

From the above scenario we can infer that, when any transaction is done for the portfolio for a security for which the issuer is customer 3434, the system raises an OVERRIDE. The Override message displays the contents of the Narrative field. The user can select the situation to be covered by an ERROR or an OVERRIDE situation – specified within the Message Type field. If the override is requested, the following extract of the override portion of a SEC.TRADE illustrates how it is advised by Temenos Transact . In this instance, it is seen that the request to check with the account officer is displayed by the system. If the inputter of the transaction has the privilege to override, then input is given.

When the trade is accepted by the system, the override is stored in SEC.TRADE for future reference.

However, in cases where an error message is displayed (as in the following screenshot), input of the underlying SEC.TRADE does not occur.

If an override message is specified, inputs can only be effected subject to the user having satisfactory privilege.


##### Closing a Portfolio

A p ortfolio is considered closed when a Closure Date is set in SEC.ACC.MASTER and the date is reached. The system allow s the user to set a closure date even if there are pending positions, pending transactions and so on . T he user has to ensure that all accounts are delinked, all positions are transferred out and all corporate actions are completed before marking a p ortfolio for closure. The s ystem raise s suitable warnings regarding pending activities when the Closure Date is updated.

Temenos Transact continues to update the SC.VALUATION.EXTRACT application for a portfolio even after the portfolio is closed. Similarly, the performance-related fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER (fields relating to the contributions, withdrawals, invested capital and compare value) are updated every month end even after the portfolio is closed. If the information pertaining to closed portfolios is not going to be used, those updates that adversely affect the COB performance without any resultant benefits must be stopped.

If the Calc Closedport field in SC.PARAMETER is set to NO, then the system ignores the closed portfolios while updating the performance-related applications and fields.

- The updates to SC.VALUATION.EXTRACT are stopped from the day after the closure.
- The updates to performance fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER are stopped from the month after the closure (for example, if the portfolio is closed on 15 August, updates to these fields do not happen from September month end).
- The updates to SC.PORT.PERFORM application (as part of EOD PORT PERFORM process) are stopped from the quarter subsequent to the period in which the portfolio is closed.

Temenos Transact considers the portfolio to be closed only if the Closure Date field in SEC.ACC.MASTER is less than the system date and the fees (both safekeeping and advisory) are posted (that is, there are no dues in respect of these).

The Calc Closedport field in the SC.PARAMETER application is set to NO (for the above functionality to be triggered).


##### Portfolio Dormancy

A portfolio becomes dormant (inactive) when no customer-initiated activity has happened for the specific period configured in SC.DORMANCY.PARAM .

The user must configure below fields in the SC.DORMANCY.PARAM application for portfolio dormancy.

- The Port Dormant Period field holds a period within which if the customer has not initiated any activity in the portfolio, the system marks the portfolio as Dormant or Inactive.
- The Dormancy Chk Appl field defines the applications that is considered while determining whether a portfolio becomes dormant or not.
- The Dormancy Exempt Mgt Acct field defines the managed accounts for which a dormancy check is not required. The system exempts the portfolios that are defined under these managed accounts (managed by the bank) from the dormancy processing.

With the Dormancy check enabled for a portfolio, the system updates the Last Activity Date field in SEC.ACC.MASTER with the transaction date, whenever any transaction is authorised in an application defined in the Dormancy Chk Appl field of SC.DORMANCY.PARAM .

During COB processing, the system checks Last Activity Date of every portfolio with reference to Port Dormant Period configured in SC.DORMANCY.PARAM .

If the difference between today’s date and Last Activity Date is greater than Port Dormant Period , then the system updates Portfolio Status in SEC.ACC.MASTER as ‘Inactive’. The system watches the portfolio which is marked inactive closely when there is a customer-initiated activity in the portfolio to check the authenticity of the new transaction after it is marked inactive .

Consider the below scenario.

Port Dormant Period = 3 Months

Last Activity Date of Portfolio A = 10th April 2024

Today’s date = 16th August 2024

Portfolio A becomes inactive as the difference between today’s date and Last Activity Date is more than three months. If any transaction is processed for a portfolio, in any applications configured in Dormancy Chk Appl of SC.DORMANCY.PARAM , the system raises an override (warning) to state that the transaction is in an inactive portfolio. When the override is accepted and the transaction is authorized, the system updates Last Activity Date with the required details and resets Portfolio Status of SEC.ACC.MASTER to Blank.

A portfolio is a basket of assets that can include stocks, bonds, commodities, currencies, cash equivalents, as well as their fund counterparts. Non-publicly tradable securities like real estate, art, and private investments can also be included in a portfolio.

Asset allocation, risk tolerance, and the individual's time horizon are all critical factors when assembling and adjusting an investment portfolio.
