#### 📖 Introduction

Portfolios are valued mark to market on a daily basis. The valuation is updated in SEC.ACC.MASTER . There are also several reports and enquires to display valuation of a portfolio. If the necessary configurations are available, these reports and enquires can be generated ad-hoc or in a regular interval as per the configuration.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The batch job SC.VAL.EXTRACT must be run to use this functionality. This process can be run in a single or multi-company environment, if the same products are installed in all the companies that use the securities.

If the job is configured as shown in the below screenshot, the COB process generates a required flat table (that is, without multi-value fields). The records are very similar to the SC.POS.ASSET record generated by the standard valuations program.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with the working mechanism of this feature in Temenos Transact .


##### SC.VALUATION.EXTRACT

This table is used to export the portfolio valuation information in a flat table format (that is, without multi-values). This enables the compilation of various external reporting tools, such as crystal reports. This table is built from the information in the SC.POS.ASSET record and generates a record in SC.VALUATION.EXTRACT for each security holding, account or contract linked to a portfolio.


##### Portfolio Valuation Enquiries

The online valuations in the Securities (SC) module are run using the Portfolio Valuation - Cost (SC.VAL.COST) enquiry with the values of the Include Nau Txns field in SC.PARAMETER . The resultant output, which is sent to the SC.POS.ASSET record, is used by other enquiries such as Portfolio Valuation with P&L (SC.VAL.PL), Portfolio Valuation - Margin (SC.VAL.MARGIN) enquiry and so on.

The Include Nau Txns field indicates how the unauthorised transactions are dealt in the portfolio valuation. The values in this field are:

- Yes - Unauthorised transactions are included in the valuation
- No - Unauthorised transactions are not included in the valuation
- Auth - Authorised transactions are included in the valuation. The changes made after authorisation (if any) are excluded and the valuation displays the previously authorised values. This applies to unauthorised amendments and unauthorised reversals. This also affects any cost fields relevant to the valuation in progress. This value is applicable only to the SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER applications.

For example, if this field is set to No, a forward dated SEC.TRADE record is input and authorised followed by an online valuation. However, if the same trade is amended and left unauthorised, the trade is not taken into account in the subsequent valuation. The cash account remains unaffected.

If the value is set to No or Auth, the values of the unauthorised transaction are deleted from the valuation. If it is set to Auth, the previous live transaction is used to reconstruct the details required by the program and rebuilds the position prior to amendment. Further, these values are used to update the valuation.

> **⚠️ Note:** There might be a system performance issue when this setting is used, as the previously authorised transaction must be found and the details must be reconstructed from it.

Temenos Transact supports a number of standard portfolio valuation enquiry, out of which some are explained in the below table.

| Enquiry Name | Trade/Value Dated | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Portfolio Valuation - Cost (SC.VAL.COST) | Trade | Displays the position and its description, estimation, cost and market prices. |
| Portfolio Valuation - Margin (SC.VAL.MARGIN) | Trade | Trade Displays the position and its description and, estimation and margin value of the portfolio. |
| Portfolio Valuation with P&L (SC.VAL.PL) | Trade | Displays the position and its description, estimation and market price and the unrealized Profit and loss of each position |

The below screenshot displays the example of a portfolio valuation enquiry. The Portfolio Valuation - Cost (SC.VAL.COST) for the portfolio is 950-1, whose SEC.ACC.MASTER record is displayed in the below screenshot. The enquiry is broken down by SUB.ASSET.TYPE with the sub-totals for each.

As shown in the enquiry, any forex contract linked to a portfolio in Temenos Transact are split into two sides (buy and sell) and both are displayed separately. The portfolio value includes only the profit and loss due to differences in the exchange rate between the contract and current system exchange rates (or system forward rates, for a forward contract).

There is no value against the British Pound Sterling (GBP) side of the contract as the reference currency of the portfolio is GBP. There is always an exchange rate of one between the portfolio currency and contract currency. A loss is shown against the USD side of the contract, as the contract is to buy USD at a rate of 1.885, whereas the current forward rate for GBP-USD is 1.873. The exchange rate against the portfolio reference currency is used. The difference between the contracted and current forward rates provides the resultant valuation amount. The valuation enquiries also include the relevant information to a particular transaction and the amount of the accrued interest to date, as shown in the below screenshot.

The accrued interest is displayed against the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS transactions that are linked to the portfolio. This enquiry also includes the MM.MONEY.MARKET and other transactions against which the accruals are made. For interest bearing bond positions, the Temenos Transact enquiries list the interest amount due as of the enquired date but does not accrue customer interest.


##### Viewing Daily Interest Accrual on Cash Accounts After a backdated transaction

The SC.POS.ASSET application shows the accrued interest on cash accounts. When there is a backdated transaction affecting the cash account balance, the interest accrual is recalculated based on the day the backdated transaction was input. The SC.BACK.VAL.INT application displays the accruals for a backdated transaction for each day from back value date till current date.

When a backdated transaction is input, the system automatically updates the Module field as SC in the ACCT.BACK.VALUE table. As a part of COB, the SC.BACK.VAL.INT.ACCRUAL job fetches the details from ACCT.BACK.VALUE table and updates the SC.BACK.VAL.INT table for each day from back value date till date.

The SC.BACK.VAL.INT table holds the recalculated balance and accrued interest for each day when there is a back value transaction on an account. The ID of the table is a valid account number. The Co Code field denotes the company code to which the account belongs. The Date field holds the date on which the accrued interest is calculated.

If there are three back dated transactions on the same day, then the system calculates the accrued interest from the earliest back date. The system updates the accrual interest in the same record for all working dates from the earliest back date.

Assume that today is Feb 7, 2022. Consider the following scenario

- The capitalisation date was Jan 31, 2022.
- Assume that Feb 5, 2022 and Feb 6, 2022 were holidays.
- Three backdated transactions are input for Feb 4, 2022, Feb 2, 2022 and Feb 1, 2022 for portfolio 100291-1 with 123567 account number.

During COB, the system builds the SC.BACK.VAL.INT table. This table contains multi-value sets of accrued interest starting with Feb 1, 2022. So, this table consists the data for Feb 1, 2022 to Feb 4, 2022. The accrued interest for Feb 4 includes the interest of Feb 5 and Feb 6 which were holidays.

This accrued interest for each day from the back date of the transaction till the day of input is passed on to the Wealth Suite Front Office TAP, to ensure that the daily valuation and performance are calculated using the recalculated accrued interest.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system clears the existing records in the SC.BACK.VAL.INT table during each day COB cycle and updates the accounts which have a back dated transaction as on that date. When the backdated transaction falls on a holiday, then the system automatically sets the Holiday field as Yes.


##### Suppression of Unsettled Trades from Valuations (Additional Information)

Temenos Transact performs valuations and includes the receipts or withdrawals (if any) into a customer’s SECURITY.POSITION , irrespective of whether the underlying source transaction is settled or not.

The unsettled trades can be excluded from customer valuations and by default, the SECURITY.POSITION and the Closing Bal No Nom field is in the same record. The below section deals with the setup of this functionality.

The Sect Pend field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Yes, Post or All to exclude the unsettled trades from customer valuations. The following are the possible values in this field.

- Yes - The unsettled positions are excluded from customer valuations only for the SECURITY.TRANSFER transactions.
- Post - The unsettled positions is excluded from customer valuations for both SECURITY.TRANSFER and POSITION.TRANSFER transactions.
- All - The unsettled positions are excluded from customer valuations for SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER and POSITION.TRANSFER transactions.

The Sc Trans Name field in SECURITY.PARAMETER identifies the transaction types from the SC.TRANS.NAME record to be included or excluded from any valuations of the unsettled source transaction.

The SC.TRANS.NAME records are linked to SC.TRANS.TYPE records, which indicates whether a SC.TRANS.NAME is a receipt or a delivery of security. Multiple SC.TRANS.NAME records linking to one SC.TRANS.TYPE can be setup. This enables the differentiation by name for different purposes as in this case, whether or not to include in customer revaluations.

The below screenshot displays the SC.PARAMETER record for the Sect Pend and Sc Trans Name fields.

The Sc Trans Name is a multi-value field enabling the user to specify more than one value, if required. In the above example, SC.TRANS.NAME is allied to the SC.TRANS.TYPE - FNP as shown in the below screenshot.

The user has to input a SECURITY.TRANSFER using the Security Dr Code field as shown in the above screenshot and this is recorded in the SC.PARAMETER application.

The Transaction Type field indicates the SC.TRANS.NAME used to record the security receipt on behalf of the customer 950 for delivery into SEC.ACC.MASTER portfolio 950-1.

The SC.TRANS.NAME is defined in the Sect Pend and Sc Trans Name fields in SC.PARAMETER , which forces the usage of SC.SETTLEMENT . The user can input through a version, which sets the Sec Hold Settle field in SECURITY.TRANSFER to Yes.

In the above example, Temenos Transact displays an error. For the input to be effective, it is necessary to set the Sec Hold Settle field to Yes.

The Cu Nom Outstanding field confirms the customer transfer of 1,295 unsettled shares. The Trans Code field also confirms the SC.TRANS.NAME used (FNI in this case) in the source SECURITY.TRANSFER .

This process of inhibiting unsettled trades is used in several locations. For example, within SECURITY.POSITION for the security and customer.

The position above, for security 003621-000 in portfolio 930-1, displays zero in the Closing Bal No Nom field though the securities are added through an authorised SECURITY.TRANSFER . The position is updated in the Free Nom Pend field, as shown in the below screenshot.

The unsettled transactions are avoided from appearing in the customer valuations by running a valuation for the portfolio 930-1.

The above screenshot displays the customer portfolio contents. The data displayed in this view is connected to the current account with the SEC.ACC.MASTER portfolio displaying the current balance.

The below screenshot displays the valuations summary for the same portfolio.

There is no reference to the unsettled security transferred into the account. The security is included in the revaluation after settled. The user can settle the transfer to view the result. The relevant SC.SETTLEMENT record pertaining to the SECURITY.TRANSFER is located.

The above screenshot displays the first portion of the SC.SETTLEMENT . The customer settlement details are updated, as shown in the below screenshot.

The settlement amount and value date are updated, and the transaction is authorised after input. In this example, the system date is used for illustrative purposes. The valuation enquiry is run once again to check whether the security settled appears on the screen.

The effect of confirming the receipt of the unsettled security-003621-000 in the customer portfolio is shown in the above screenshot.

The valuation enquiries updates the SC.POS.ASSET record on settlement of the transactions matching the specified Sect Pend or Sc Trans Name field settings in the SC.PARAMETER record.

The unsettled transactions to be withheld from valuations based on the transaction type updated in SC.PARAMETER are collated and recorded in the Free Nom Pend field in the underlying SECURITY.POSITION .

> **⚠️ Note:** Valuations available in Temenos Transact system may refer to the on-line enquiries such as Portfolio Valuation with P&L (SC.VAL.PL) and the valuation reports (both on-line and the ones built during the COB). All valuations are applicable for unsettled transactions if the SC.TRANS.NAME is specified in the Sect Pend and/or Sc Trans Name fields in the SC.PARAMETER record.

If the securities are settled incorrectly, the relevant SC.SETTLEMENT record is updated to reverse the earlier settlement. The Temenos Transact system recognises this action and any further valuations again excludes the nominal or amount of the security.

The above scenario is illustrated in the below series of screenshots.

The SC.SETTLEMENT used in the above example is settled incorrectly.

- The reversal of the settlemepnt amount is initiated and the SC.SETTLEMENT is updated.
- The updated record is authorised and a further revaluation enquiry on the Customer Portfolio is carried out.
- The security details are omitted from the portfolio holdings. This happens irrespective of whether the underlying SC.SETTLEMENT is authorised or not. The unsettlement amount entered has an immediate impact on any subsequent valuation as the Free Nom Pend field in the SECURITY.POSITION is updated immediately and the change is made to the SC.SETTLEMENT record.
- As partial settlements are permitted within the SC.SETTLEMENT record, any amount settled is immediately eligible for reporting within a valuation. The same applies if a partial-unsettlement occurs.

In the above example, 1,295 stocks is settled, which is followed by an unsettlement of 740 stocks.

The Free Nom Pend field records the unsettled amount of stock.

The original settlement is 1,295 stocks out of which 740 stocks are unsettled resulting in 555 settled positions. The on-line valuation for the portfolio is run again as shown in the below screenshot.

This valuation includes only the amount of security actually settled as shown in the above screenshot.

When the Sect Pend field is set to Post, even POSITION.TRANSFER with transaction type defined in SC.TRANS.NAME undergoes the processing. When a POSITION.TRANSFER is placed, the Free Nom Pend field in SECURITY.POSITION is updated for both source and target portfolio. Both the source and target portfolio are updated with nominal in Closing Bal No Nom field in SECURITY.POSITION , only after the settlement of the POSITION. . The Sec Hold Settle field must be set to Yes, for the processing to be applicable.

When the Sect Pend field is set to All, and when a SEC.TRADE is input with a transaction code given in the Sc Trans Name field in SC.PARAMETER , then the respective trade behaves as a pending settlement transaction. When the record in SEC.TRADE is authorised, the system updates the Free Nom Pend field in SECURITY.POSITION with the unsettled nominal balance. The securities are not included in Portfolio Valuations and Corporate Actions as they are not available.

Forward entry amount is not included in the cash balance which is displayed in the Forward Acc Amt field in SC.POS.ASSET . Therefore, Portfolio Valuation is not be affected.

The system clears the Free Nom Pend field and updates the value in the Closing Bal No Nom field when the securities are delivered and settled using the SC.SETTLEMENT .


##### Portfolio Valuation Reports

In addition to the screen enquiries, a number of customised portfolio valuation reports are created to run within Temenos Transact . The portfolio valuation report(s) used by an individual system is specified in the Valuation Subr field in SC.PARAMETER . The JBC programs generates these reports and the required customisation can be created by their local Temenos Regional Development Department. The default report is SC.ASSET.VAL.REPS but the SC.ASSET.VAL.REPORTS.SIM or SC.ASSET.VAL.REPORTS.CAMBIO reports can also be used.

The below screenshot illustrates the request of a valuation report during the on-line phase. The request entered in the Account Officer field must be updated in the SEC.ACC.MASTER record for which the valuation is required.

The Online Val field must be set to Y to ensure that all the relevant records are up-to-date. The user must specify the current month numerically (for example, the value 11 in the above screenshot to indicate November). The user can also request historic valuation data (Read Historical Portfolio Valuation Reports for more information). This request is raised on behalf of the portfolio 888-1 and the valuation is for the current record. The record entered is validated to build the report.

The TSA.SERVICE initiates the online valuations using the OL.VAL.REPS application. This service starts and stops automatically if the TSM keeps running.

After the service agent is completed, the relevant SEC.ACC.MASTER reflects the current valuation.

The valuation reports are produced online by the OL.VAL.REPS application or automatically by the system during the COB stage in the frequency defined in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record for the customer of the concerned portfolio. These automatic reports are produced as part of the securities price feed, when they are produced after the frequency date (that is, with the previous day’s closing prices).

There are two frequencies in CUSTOMER.SECURITY (internal and external). This allows the bank to specify separate frequencies for a report for the account officer (internal) and customer (external). For example, the account officer may review the portfolio weekly while the customer wants it monthly.

The various types of reports and statements requested for the external and internal sources are indicated in the External Reps and Internal Reps multi-value fields in CUSTOMER.SECURITY , respectively. The valuation formats are available in the SC.REPORT.TYPE application and allows different versions of the same report to be specified. The OL.VAL.REPS requires a report type to be specified. The customised valuation reports produce specific layouts to suit different requirements. For example, the customer and the account officer wants to view different information in the report.

The valuation reports can be quite large, depending on the number of components a customer holds within his portfolio. The following examples display a small portion of a valuation report.

Displays the first page of the printable valuation report and displays only the customer’s cash account and outstanding forward forex transaction.

Displays the portfolio breakdown summary.


##### Historical Portfolio Valuation Reports

In addition to the portfolio valuation reports, Temenos Transact also retains information regarding the end of month position of all the customer portfolios for the last twelve months. These historical valuations are printed by OL.VAL.REPS or viewed through the screen enquiries such as SC.HIST.VAL.COST. The information behind these historical valuations is stored at the end of the month concerned and other than being updated with the end of month closing prices on the first security price update of the new month, left unchanged so that they are a true valuation as at the end of month.

The user can indicate the month of the report required in the Report Month field in OL.VAL.REPS record. For example, the current month is September and the user wants the report for April, the Report Month field is set to four. If the user enters, 10, then Temenos Transact assumes October of the previous year.


##### FIFO based Valuation and Average Price Calculation for Customer and Own Book Portfolio

The Val Method field in SC.PARAMETER determines the valuation and average price calculation method at a system level. This field accepts FIFO or null as values. If the Val Method field is set to FIFO, the system uses the FIFO valuation method for all the portfolios.

> **⚠️ Note:** After the field is selected as FIFO or null, then changes to this field cannot be done further.

The Val Method field in SEC.ACC.MASTER also determines the valuation and average price calculation method at a system level. This field accepts FIFO or null value and is defaulted from SC.PARAMETER when a portfolio is opened. The user can change the valuation method for specific portfolios or business models by updating the Val Method field before the first transaction is done for the portfolio. Before trading in own book or customer portfolio, this field needs to be setup as no further change is allowed once a trade is booked for the portfolio. If the valuation method is set to FIFO, the realised gains and average price are updated in the below tables based on the FIFO method:

- SECURITY.POSITION
- SC.TRADING.POSITION
- SC.TRADE.POS.HISTORY

> **⚠️ Note:** If the Val Method field is set to Null in SC.PARAMETER and FIFO in SEC.ACC.MASTER for a specific portfolio, then the system updates the cost of position on FIFO basis only for the FIFO portfolios while for other portfolios the existing weighted average method is used.

The SECURITY.POSITION.DETS table is created for all the portfolios where the Val Method field is set to FIFO. Every purchase transaction is recorded in this table as a security line or parcel. Any sell transaction is recorded below the allocated purchase transaction based on the FIFO method. The ID of this table is similar to SECURITY.POSITION . (PORTFOLIO.SM.DEPOSITORY.SUBACCOUNT)

Whenever the portfolio value drops by the % setup in the SC.MIFID.PARAM application, system automatically creates an entry in the SC.PF.DROP.INSTANCES to record such instances.

### 5.58  Position of Safekeeping


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Place of safekeeping is the place where the securities are held. When an instrument is traded in multiple markets, the custodian can use multiple settlement agents depending on the exchange. These agents, in turn can hold the positions at a different place of safekeeping. Thus, for the same security...*
> 
> **Applications:** `CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `DIARY`, `DX.CONTRACT.MASTER`, `DX.EXCHANGE.MASTER`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `POSITION.TRANSFER`, `SC.AGENT.PLACE`, `SC.BLOCK.SEC.POS` ... +13 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Build Sec Pos*, *Build Sec Pos field*, *Deli Pl Safekeep*, *Depository*, *Depository From*, *Depository To*, *Exchange*, *Exchange Type* ... +18 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Place of safekeeping is the place where the securities are held. When an instrument is traded in multiple markets, the custodian can use multiple settlement agents depending on the exchange. These agents, in turn can hold the positions at a different place of safekeeping. Thus, for the same security, the custodian can use a different place of safekeeping and place of settlement. Reconciliation of position is generally based on the place of safekeeping.

The Nokia shares traded on the Helsinki Exchange and settled in Finland are stored in a different place of safekeeping compared to the Nokia shares traded on the Euronext Paris stock exchange and settled in France.

Segregating positions by their place of safekeeping is important because it is more cost-effective to sell from the same place of safekeep where the positions are held.

Additionally, the custodian can send a separate MT564 corporate action notification message based on the place of safekeeping.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To distinguish the positions based on the place of safekeeping, the SECURITY.POSITION Id is enhanced to record the same. The sub-account part of the SECURITY.POSITION key includes ‘PSAF’ as suffix. This section explains the setup for segregating positions by Place of safekeeping.


##### Parametrisation

If the custodian maintains the position by place of safekeeping, then the Build Sec Pos field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY should be set as ‘By.Psaf’ for the respective depository. When this field is set,

- The positions are segregated by Place of safekeeping.
- For any corporate action notification received for the depository, based on the place of safekeeping tag, the system creates ENTITLEMENT records only for those positions with the respective place of safekeeping.

- If the Build Sec Pos field is set, the system appends the place of safekeeping to the sub account delimited with ‘*’, while building SECURITY.POSITION .
- When CUSTOMER.SECURITY is set to hold position By.Psaf, the system does not allow free format values directly for the Pl Safekeep field in SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER , POSITION.TRANSFER , and SC.SETT.INSTRUCT .


##### SC.AGENT.PLACE

PSAF can be a BIC code, a country code, or a free format value, which is known to the parties. When a free format value is used, it must be created in the SC.AGENT.PLACE table. The Psaf Narrative field in SC.AGENT.PLACE holds the free format narrative for the place of safekeeping.

Once the records are created as shown in the above screenshot, they can be used in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT (SSI recording table). The record can be mapped to the Pl Safekeep field prefixed with 'A-', for example, A-SHHE1. The system allows the user to attach only the SC.AGENT.PLACE records with the Psaf Narrative field defined.


##### SC.SSI.PARAM

The Primary stock exchange (place of listing) and the allowed Place of Safekeeping for a Place of settlement are configured in SC.SSI.PARAM . For each Place of Settlement (defined in the field Pset ), the user can define the allowed by multi-valuing the Pl Safekeep field with the respective Pl Cod . The primary stock exchange for the given Pset and Pl Safekeep combination is recorded in the Primary Plis field.

In the case of a sell order, the system selects a position that has enough quantity to sell. The PSAF of that position is updated in the place of safekeeping in the order. Then the system determines the stock exchange based on the value in the Primary Plis field for that Psaf, from the SC.SSI.PARAM .

> **⚠️ Note:** The Pl Safekeep field must be unique for each Pset.


#### 🔧 Working With

When an instrument is traded in multiple markets, the agent can hold the positions at different places of safekeeping. Thus, it is necessary to maintain positions based on the actual place of safekeeping. This section explains,

- Updating SECURITY.POSITION ID based on the place of safekeeping.
- Defaulting the place of safekeeping (PSAF) at transaction level.
- Handling Corporate Action events based on the place of safekeeping.
- Determining the exchange and place of safekeeping for trades created through Option Contracts.
- Blocking positions based on place of safekeeping.
- MT 535 Reconciliation by place of safekeeping.


##### UpdatingSECURITY.POSITIONID based on Place of Safekeeping.

If the Build Sec Pos field is set to ‘By.Psaf’, then on authorisation of trade or transfer (credit), the system builds the SECURITY.POSITION ID based on the combination of the Sub Account and Pl Safekeep fields. In Transact, the sub accounts can be configured in the following ways.

- When sub accounts are configured for each depository, the SECURITY.POSITION ID is built as 100291-1.100046-000.100492....2888991*F-BOFAUS33.
- When the depository itself is a sub account, the SECURITY.POSITION ID is built as 100291-1.100046-000.100492....*F-BOFAUS33.

The last part of the id (2888991*F-BOFAUS33) contains the sub account followed by Pl Safekeep prefixed with ‘F’, ‘C’, or ‘A’ denoting if it’s a BIC, country, or SC.AGENT.PLACE record respectively.


##### Defaulting Place of Safekeeping (PSAF) at Transaction Level

This section explains the defaulting of Place of safekeeping at transaction level during a credit transaction, debit transaction, a custodian-to-custodian transfer, sub account to sub account transfer, portfolio to portfolio transfer, and PSAF to PSAF transfer.

> **⚠️ Note:** Read Working with Standard Settlement Instructions section for more information on the rules to determine PSET.

When a buy order is input, the system determines the sub account and depository based on the existing process (either from SEC.ACC.MASTER , CUSTOMER.SECURITY , SC.CU.DEPO.DEFAULT or SC.SUB.ACC.ROUTING , and so on). When the order is authorised and if the value for the Pl Safekeep field is manually input by the user, the system creates or updates the SECURITY.POSITION ID based on the depository, sub account and PSAF combination, and updates the net open order position. If the Pl Safekeep field is left blank, then the system creates or updates the SECURITY.POSITION ID based on the depository and sub account combination.

For example, consider that the below order is placed in New York Stock exchange and the user manually enters the place of safekeeping as ‘A-SHHE1’. Based on the order details the system creates a SECURITY.POSITION record and updates the Net Open Ord Pos field as shown in the below screen shot.

When a buy order is executed at a different exchange, then based on where the order is executed, the system determines the place of settlement (PSET). Based on the PSET, the PSAF is determined at trade and based on the sub account and PSAF combination, the positions are created or updated.

For example, consider that the order is executed in NASDAQ exchange. Based on the transaction details the place of safekeeping is determined as ‘A-SHHE2’ at Trade. When trade is authorised, SECURITY.POSITION is updated as shown below. The net open orders in A-SHHE1 becomes 0.

- For transfers, the place of listing is the default stock exchange in SECURITY.MASTER record. For Buy order or Trades, the place of listing is the stock exchange in the Transaction.
- For Parent child trades, the Place of safekeeping defaulted at parent is cascaded to the child trades.

When a transfer out transaction is input, based on the quantity the system determines the position.

Following are the possible scenarios for a sale.

Scenario 1: When the market for order execution is given at the time of order input (Directed Sell)

When an order is received along with the stock exchange in Transact, the system treats it as a directed sell order, checks the quantity, picks the one that matches with the order quantity, and defaults the sub account.

If the order is executed at a different exchange, then based on where the order is executed, the system determines the place of settlement (PSET). Based on the PSET, the PSAF is determined again at trade. If the client has no position in that sub account +PSAF combination, an override is raised, for which the user must manually transfer the position to the respective sub account + PSAF combination to cover the short.

Scenario 2: When the market for order execution is not given at the time of order input

When an order is received in Transact without a stock exchange, then the system determines the exchange based on the PSAF derived from the SECURITY.POSITION Id. When the Build Sec Pos field is set for the depository, the system checks the quantity, picks the one that matches with the order quantity, and defaults the sub account and PSAF in SEC.OPEN.ORDER . Based on the PSAF found, the system identifies and defaults the stock exchange based on the Primary Plis field in SC.SSI.PARAM . If no Primary Plis are found for the given PSAF, the system defaults the stock exchange based on the Stock Exchange field in SECURITY.MASTER .

If the order is executed at a different exchange, then based on where the order is executed, the system determines the place of settlement (PSET). Based on the PSET, the PSAF is determined again at trade. If client has no position in that sub account +PSAF combination, an override is raised. The user then needs to manually transfer the position to the respective sub account + PSAF combination to cover the short.

> **⚠️ Note:** For parent child orders, If Trade Creation is by Parent.Child, then the Place of safekeeping of child is defaulted to the Parent. If PSAF is not specified in SC.GROUP.PARAM , PSAF of the Parent is defaulted from SC.SETT.INSTRUCT . If PSAF is specified in SC.GROUP.PARAM , PSAF of the Parent should be defaulted from Child.


##### Transfer of Positions

Securities can be transferred using the POSITION.TRANSFER or SC.BULK.TRANSFER application. If the POSITION.TRANSFER application is used directly and more than one SECURITY.POSITION record exists for the same combination, the system defaults all the positions. However, the SSI related fields are single fields, hence are not defaulted and the settlement message fails. When multiple positions need to be transferred, the user should always use the SC.BULK.TRANSFER application. Following are the scenarios for transfer of securities.

##### Handling Corporate Action events based on Place of safekeeping.

A single security can be stored in a different place of safekeeping based on the exchange it is traded in. The custodian can send a corporate action notification message based on place of safekeeping. Under such scenarios only the positions with the respective place of safekeeping are eligible for the event. The events can be created manually or through STP.

| 100404-1.100045-000.100492…6655555*A-SHHE1 | 4100 (Segregated account) |
| 100601-1.100045-000.100492… | 7000 |

When an MT 564 corporate action notification message is received, the system creates a separate SC.PRE.DIARY record for each message based on the place of safekeeping, provided that the Build Sec Pos field is set for the depository. If place of safekeeping ‘94a’ is received in an incoming MT 564, the system creates entitlements only for those customers having positions with respect to that place of safekeeping.

- If the Build Sec Pos field is set for the depository and if the MT 564 is received without any place of safekeeping, SC.PRE.DIARY is in IHLD with the warning ‘Missing place of safekeeping’.
- If the Build Sec Pos field is not set for the depository, the system creates entitlement records for all the portfolios belonging to that sub account or depository.
- If the first MT 564 is received without any place of safekeeping and a subsequent MT 564 with REPL is received with the place of safekeeping, a new SC.PRE.DIARY record is created. The entitlement records are created only for those records which have the respective PSAF.


##### Recording List of Exchanges

The Trade Exch field in SECURITY.MASTER can be used to record the list of available stock exchanges. When a SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SEC.TRADE is input, the system checks if the Stock Exchange field given is a valid exchange for the security by comparing the exchanges given in the Trad Exch or Stock Exchange field in the respective SECURITY.MASTER . If it is an invalid exchange the system raises a soft override ‘XXX is not a valid exchange in instrument’.


##### Determining the exchange for trades created through Option Contracts

When an option contract is exercised or assigned, the system maps the Stock Exchange field in SEC.TRADE based on the value given in the Stock Exchange field of the respective DX.EXCHANGE.MASTER . If the field is blank, the stock exchange is defaulted from the Stock Exchange field in SECURITY.MASTER . The respective trade is created in IHLD. Based on the defaulted stock exchange and other attributes the system determines the PSET and PSAF.

- Input to the Stock Exchange field is allowed only when the Exchange Type field is not OTC.
- The Stock Exchange field of the respective DX.EXCHANGE.MASTER should be one of the valid exchanges for the instrument given. The list of valid exchanges for the instrument is stored in the Trade Exch field in SECURITY.MASTER . The system raises an override in DX.CONTRACT.MASTER if the stock exchange in DX.EXCHANGE.MASTER it is not a valid exchange for the instrument.


##### Blocking Positions based on PSAF

The user can block and unblock positions using the SC.BLOCK.SEC.POS application. When the Build Sec Pos field is set for a particular depository, the user can block positions maintained in the specific place of safekeeping by mentioning in against the Pl Safekeep field.

The following screenshots show how SECURITY.POSITION is updated after blocking the position.

### 5.59  Preserving Portfolio Value(DirectMethod)


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *For some funds such as Hedge Funds, the Net Asset Value (NAV) is declared only at pre-defined frequencies, such as weekly or monthly. The payment for a subscription order is sent upfront to the fund house but the units and NAV are received later. While the cash is debited from the customer’s portfol...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Activity*, *Broker.1*, *Calculate Chrgs*, *Calculate Chrgs.1*, *Cash Amount*, *Cash Amount.1*, *Cash Chrgs*, *Chrgs Gross/Net* ... +25 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

For some funds such as Hedge Funds, the Net Asset Value (NAV) is declared only at pre-defined frequencies, such as weekly or monthly. The payment for a subscription order is sent upfront to the fund house but the units and NAV are received later. While the cash is debited from the customer’s portfolio and if the corresponding fund position is not available, it leads to a drop in the portfolio valuation and performance. To avoid this fall, it is necessary to include the amount paid upfront in the valuation until the units are known.

This feature explains how portfolio valuation is preserved when funds are paid upfront and units are awaited.

The following are the two ways to handle upfront payment

- Direct method
- Indirect method

> **⚠️ Note:** The recommended method is direct method.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Upfront Direct field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Yes, to enable the direct method of upfront payments. The transactions codes for upfront payment direct method are defined in the Upfront Txn Code field. This field can be set only if Upfront Direct field is set to Yes.


##### Configuring Upfront Payment through Internal Account

In some countries, for certain funds such as pension funds where payments are made upfront but units are allocated later, the banks are legally required to debit the customer’s account only when NAV and units are declared.

If the banks require the upfront payment to be made from an internal account and customer is to be debited only after NAV and nominal are known, the following set up is required.

The Upfront Int Acc field in SECURITY.MASTER is set to YES and the Upfront Int Categ field must be defined as an internal account category. Therefore, it is possible that different funds can have different internal account categories defined.


#### 🔧 Working With

If the Upfront Direct field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Yes, then the SEC.OPEN.ORDER placed with Order Type as CASH and the transactions codes defined in the Upfront Txn Code field in SC.PARAMETER are treated as upfront order.

After the order is placed, the system debits the customer’s account and credits the fund Nostro account as soon as the order is transmitted. The debit and credit entries are raised directly from SEC.OPEN.ORDER . In SEC.OPEN.ORDER , Cash Chrgs field can be set to Gross or Net and entries are raised suitably.

The amount paid upfront is updated in SECURITY.POSITION in the Upfront Amount field. The Closing Bal Nominal is not changed. If SECURITY.POSITION did not exist previously for this fund, the record in SECURITY.POSITION is created. The Closing Bal Nominal field is blank and Upfront Amount field is updated. The Upfront Amount in SECURITY.POSITION is updated with the value in the Cu Cash Amount field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER .

> **⚠️ Note:** The fees are not included in the Upfront Amount and the value in Cu Cash Amount is updated as provided.

The value in the Upfront Amount field is included in the valuation of the portfolio.

The record in SECURITY.POSITION is updated with the Cu Cash Amount value in the Upfront Amount field.

Once the units are allotted by the fund house, SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is updated for the order. After executing the record is authorised, the SEC.TRADE is created. Accounting entries are not raised from SEC.TRADE . On authorising the trade, the Closing Bal Nominal in SECURITY.POSITION is updated with the units received or calculated. The amount updated in the Upfront Amount field is blank. The units are now included in the valuation of the portfolio.


##### Example

This scenario explains the portfolio value at each stage.

Stage 1: Upfront order placed for fund FSF0003AU, but not yet transmitted.

|  | Units | Value in USD | Units | Value in USD | Units | Value in USD |

| Cash Hold (F entry) |  | (10,000) |  | (7,000) |  | (9,000) |
| Closing Cash Account balance |  | 20,000.00 |  | 25,000.00 |  | 15,000.00 |
| FSF0003AU |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Portfolio Value |  | 20,000.00 |  | 25,000.00 |  | 15,000.00 |

| Cash Hold (Order placed for FSF0003AU) |  |  |  |  |  |  |

The records in SECURITY.POSITION is notupdated, that is, neither the nominal nor the Upfront Amt fields is updated. P&L entry is not raised. Once the price is received and the units are allotted by the fund house, the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is updated for the order. Once the execution record is authorised, SEC.TRADE is created. On authorising the trade:

- The records in SECURITY.POSITION is updated with the nominal.
- Customer account is debited and the internal category account is credited.
- P&L entry is raised at this stage.

### 5.60  PriceTypes Yield Discount EIR


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This document explains the price types, processing of yield, discount, and effective interest rate (EIR).*
> 
> **Applications:** `CATEG.ENTRY`, `DIARY`, `DIV.COUP.CUS`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `PRICE.TYPE`, `RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY`, `SC.BOND.ROUNDING`, `SC.PARAMETER` ... +9 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accr*, *Accr, Post*, *Accrue Discount*, *Acr*, *Adj*, *Ai*, *Amort*, *Amount* ... +63 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This document explains the price types, processing of yield, discount, and effective interest rate (EIR).


##### Discount Processing

When a bond costs more than its redemption value, it must be purchased at a premium. Conversely, when a bond costs less than its maturity value, it is sold at a discount rate.

The former premium automatically reduces the effect of the future interest income, whereas the latter discount enhances the interest income. If the underlying security is of non-interest type, the discount is the income. The effect of holding the security until eventual maturity, when the holder can expect to receive the full redemption proceeds under normal circumstances, produces a final P/L amount equal to the original premium or discount amount, in addition to the final coupon. To eliminate the end maturity effect, which results in huge postings to P/L, the bank can elect to amortise the premium or discount over the remaining life of the security.


##### Effective Interest Rate

The effective interest rate (EIR) method calculates the amortised cost of a financial asset or a financial liability and allocating the interest income or interest expense over the relevant period. The EIR of a bond is described as the rate, at which the bond's future interest payments and its maturity value to the bond's current selling price are discounted that is, the current market price or present value. The EIR is a bond investor's yield-to maturity. EIR is different from the stated or contractual rate that appears on the face of the bond.


##### Bond Interest Rounding

The bond interest rounding method of calculation in Temenos Transact can be configured to meet polish requirements or any special market requirement, when the manipulation of specific components in the bond interest calculation needs to be applied.

Rounding methods such as, UP and DOWN, as well as the conventional rounding (round OFF) methods can be used. Conventional rounding OFF is defined as, rounding off the value with respect to the number next to the required decimal digit being greater, equal or less than five. If the decimal figure to the right of the required digit is five or more, rounding up to the next figure occurs. Whereas, rounding down occurs if the figure is less than five.

The methods of round UP and DOWN ignores all decimal digits succeeding the required number of decimal places. If UP is selected, the last digit rounds up by one figure and if DOWN is selected, the last figure remains the same.

Some bonds have an accrued interest amount calculated for a single bond unit before multiplying with the bond nominal amount, to obtain the full-accrued interest amount. In such cases, the bond rounding must be applied to the interest per unit before multiplying by the nominal factor.


##### Yield Processing

Bond yield is the return that an investor receives on a bond. The yield is a function of the bond's price and its coupon or interest payment. The yield is more accurate than the coupon yield, if the price of the bond is different from its face value.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configuration of price types, processing of yield, discount and EIR.


##### Effective Interest Rate

The Linear Comp Accr field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application has EIR as one of the options, that acts as a method to compute the daily amortisation cost of a bond. The LINEAR and COMPOUND are the other options available in this field.

When the Price Type field in the relevant SECURITY.MASTER record is set to DBOND:

- Coupon payments until maturity are determined based on the value dated positions, as of the current date.
- The previous day's NPV are calculated by adding the value date of the position, the coupon amount posted, and the discount posted until the previous day.
- EIR is calculated using the current cost of position and the future cash flows.
- The current day's NPV is calculated using the EIR, future coupon payments and the maturity value.
- Any coupon accrued for the day is added to the previous day's NPV.
- The difference between the current NPV and the previous day's NPV, including the coupon accrued for the day, becomes the discount accrual for the day.
- When a position is sold, the previous day's NPV is pro-rated based on the value dated position after the position is sold and is used for EIR and NPV calculations.
- Any sold discount is also calculated by pro-rating the discount amount accrued until the previous day, based on the value dated positions as on current date.


##### Discount Processing

Before Temenos Transact performs the discount processing on any instrument, the underlying PRICE.TYPE record that is recorded in the SECURITY.MASTER application for the security must be of a type, that enables this feature.

The PRICE.TYPE application advises Temenos Transact how to calculate the proceeds of a transaction or to revalue a position, given the price supplied on a trade or by the SECURITY.MASTER application. For example, Temenos Transact must know whether a price of 90 translates to GBP90 per unit, GBP0.90 per unit or 90% of a nominal amount. These rules and certain other rules are recorded this application.

Therefore, to enable Temenos Transact to perform discount processing, the Disc Instrument field in the PRICE.TYPE application must be set to Y. Otherwise, any securities held within a portfolio having been setup for this process is ignored. The following screenshot shows a PRICE.TYPE record setup for discount processing.

This illustrates how a bond type PRICE.TYPE record must be setup, so that Temenos Transact can perform discount processing in a compatible portfolio. The important fields in this application are the Calculation Method and Disc Instrument fields. In order to enable this process, the Disc Instrument field must be set to Y.

Now, it is necessary to ensure that a compatible value in the Calculation Method field is selected. Discount processing can only be performed when this field contains any of the following methods:

- DPRICE
- YIELD
- DISCOUNT

The DPRICE calculation method is similar to the standard PRICE method, which always enable the processing of bonds and similar instrument types. The exception in this instance is that, it advises Temenos Transact that discount processing is required, provided the underlying instrument is held within a compatible portfolio. Further validations ensures whether Temenos Transact automatically adds Y into the Disc Instrument field when the user flags Y in the Percentage field, as the DPRICE method is reserved for this purpose.

The DISCOUNT method is intended for usage in respect of non-interest bearing securities, which are traded at a discount and subsequently mature at their face value. Here, both the Percentage and Disc Instrument fields must be set to Y.

The YIELD method is also intended to be applied to certain interest and non-interest bearing securities. As before, both the Percentage and Disc Instrument fields must be set to Y. As this calculation method can be applied to both interest and non-interest bearing instruments, Temenos Transact must be advised for which interest bearing instrument, the user wants to apply the calculation. This is done in the Price Basis field where the user must enter either E or I. Where, E indicates that the underlying security is priced at a yield excluding interest and I indicates that the underlying security is priced at a yield including interest.

The following section illustrates some example of the PRICE.TYPE records being setup.

Security with a face (MATURITY) value of USD100,000 bought with 100 days remaining until maturity, which is dealt at a discount rate of 5% using a 365 day calculation basis.

Consideration = 100,000 * {1-[100*(5/100)/365]}

=100,000 * (1-0.01369863.013)

=100,000 * 0.98630136.987

=98,630.14

> **⚠️ Note:** The Calculation Method field is set to DISCOUNT representing the usage of the formula as shown in the above screenshot.


##### Yield Processing

Yield processing can be configured in the Price Basis field to EXC.ACCR or INC.ACCR.

The value in the Calculation Method field is set to YIELD and that the Price Basis is set to EXC.ACCR, as shown in the below screenshot. The maturity date used for yield calculations is either the maturity date or the average life maturity date.

The value in the Calculation Method field is set to YIELD and the Price Basis is set to INCL.ACCR, as shown in the below screenshot.

The value in the Calculation Method field is set to TYIELD , as shown in the below screenshot. This is a specific to Thai bonds.

The Yield Price Rounding field in PRICE.TYPE is used to define the rounding of the calculated price to “n” decimal places during yield to price conversion. It specifies the number of decimal places used to round the decimals while converting the yield to price.

> **⚠️ Note:** Input in Yield Price Rounding is allowed only when the Calculation Method field is set to Yield.


##### Bond Interest Rounding

To enable bond interest rounding, each SECURITY.MASTER record must have the Bond Rounding field set to YES, as shown in the below screenshot.

The Bond Round Table field is populated with the best applicable bond rounding method, while the record is entered or displayed. However, this does not indicate which method is used in the calculations. Each time a bond interest calculation is performed, the system validates to a certain the best available method while calculating.


#### 🔧 Working With

This sections explains the working of price types, processing of yield, discount and EIR.


##### Effective Interest Rate (EIR)

The portfolio is setup and trades are executed such that the interest accruals and discount accruals are posted among the CATEG.ENTRY and RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY tables. A sample scenario for the cash flow of bonds using EIR methodology is shown below.

##### Discount Processing

The following examples illustrate some simple scenarios involving a bond type security held in an own portfolio, requiring linear processing of discounts and premiums and is set to have the positions grossed up to par value. Assume that the example USD security matures in 10 days.

The Temenos Transact overnight processing accrues one day’s discount which in this case is USD1,000 / 10 days * 1 day, giving USD100 to be credited to the discount P/L account.

On the second day, a further purchase of the security has taken place. In this instance, the accrual comprises USD1,000 / 10 days * 1 day (for the original purchase) plus USD450 / 9 days * 1 day.

For the second purchase, the total accrual for the day is USD150. This daily process continues until final maturity, when the provision and the position at its cost removed (in conjunction with the required redemption or maturity entries). Temenos Transact process the sales of whole or part of a position, as shown in the below example.

For the sale transaction, the realised trading profit entry is passed based on the normal method of comparing the cost of the sale against the cost of the position price equivalent. In this case, the calculation is,

$60,000 * ((99.03333 - 99.25) / 100) giving $60,000 * .0021667 = $130

The next step is the removal of the provision, which was accumulating in respect of the respective portion of the position, which is sold. This is affected using simple pro-rating of the provision. In this case, the user has a provision brought forward of USD250 in respect of a holding of USD150,000. Therefore the over-provision is calculated as,

$250 / $150,000 * $60,000 = $100 and it is moved to the trading P&L account

The final step is to continue the discount accrual process with the current date calculation. This is done by taking the position at a cost of (USD90,000 * 99.03333) USD89,130 plus the provision accrued so far (the remaining amount) of USD150 to give USD89,280. Then this is subtracted from the maturity value of USD90,000, to give a potential income of USD720 over the eight days remaining until maturity(that is, USD720 / 8 = USD90 per day).

Assuming there were no further transactions for maturity, the situation on that day is illustrated in the below table.

The system is able to process premiums or discounts, including the positions comprising purchase and sale transactions containing both premiums and discounts.

> **⚠️ Note:** Apart from basic bond type securities, there are other security types which may be processed within a portfolio having been setup to perform accruals or amortisations of discounts or premiums. However, Temenos Transact carries out this function only when the Price Type field in the underlying SECURITY.MASTER record is set to enable this process.

Certain types of instruments such as asset backed securities, involve payment of some principal every month. In order to manage the pre-payment risk for such securities, an ALMD is calculated, which is the effective maturity date from which the actual maturity date may be different. The following fields in SECURITY.MASTER are used to capture such ALMD.

- Avg Life - This is field can be flagged either to Yes or No, which determines if this security has an average life.
- Avg Life Mat Date - This is a date field and is editable only if Avg Life field is set. The input date must be less than maturity date and greater than current date.
- Weighted Avg Life - This is a date field and the system automatically re-calculates the Avg Life Mat Date field value using the below formula. If a value is set for this field.

Weighted average life * 365 days + Current date.

If weighted average is 1.16 and the current date is 17th April 2014, the average life maturity date is computed as 14th Jun 2015.

(1.16 * 365) = 423.4

This is rounded to 423 and the average life maturity date is 423th day from 17th April 2014 which is 14th June 2015.

If ALMD is set, the yield and discount accrual are calculated considering the ALMD as the maturity date. The amortisation or accrual is changed accordingly, when there is a change to the ALMD. The discount accrual happens until this date and any transactions input after this date is not considered for discount accrual processing. This difference is raised as a realised PL entry during redemption or subsequent sale.

> **⚠️ Note:** The linear method of discount processing alone considers the ALMD.

This includes the ability to perform the discount accrual function using the compounding method, provided that the underlying instrument PRICE.TYPE has its Calculation Method field set to DPRICE. These are bond type securities, which are quoted, dealt and re-valued using a clean price.

Security transactions containing purchases and sales of securities is processed using these price types, must be located in a portfolio which is setup to utilise the linear method of amortisation. The user can alternatively locate these instruments into a non-amortisation portfolio. The compound method provides an alternative means of accruing or amortising discount or premium over the remaining life of an interest bearing bond-type security. Whereas, the utilisation of the linear method accrue or amortise on a straight-line basis, the compound method provides a lower daily accruals or amortisations during the earlier remaining life of the underlying security. These cash flows calculated by the compound method increases, as the security nearing its eventual maturity.

While the basis for calculating the daily accruals for the linear method is simple and straightforward, the basis for compound is more challenging, as it is based on the concept of average yield of the value-dated position. Whenever the position is changed, a new average yield is calculated and the outstanding discount or premium and the amortisation to the date figure is adjusted.

The rules to derive the average yield are as follows:

- If position changes from long to short or short to long, use the yield on the trade bringing over the switch.
- If position changes from buy on short or sell on long, use the current average yield on the position.
- Otherwise, work out the new average yield by using the true cost of position.

True cost of position = value-dated cost of position - discount provision

VD Pos - Value-dated position (the nominal as on value date)

VD Cost - Value-dated cost of position (the cost at average price on value date)

Disc Prov - Discount provision (the amount accrued/amortised so far)

It is in proportion of the value-dated discount or premium such that, the final amortisation amount is equal to the value-dated discount or premium calculated on the night before the maturity date. The amortised to date value is updated accordingly and the daily accrual is the difference between today’s value and yesterday’s value. The amortisation amount of the value-dated position is:

Another method of arriving at the amortized amount (when accrual has to be compounded) involves to determine the next day’s price based on the formula discussed earlier. The difference between the current value of the position and the new value (based on next day price) is then considered to be the accrual or amortization amount for the day.

To enable this functionality, the Amort Method field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application must be set to PRICE (it must be ensured that the compound method of discount accrual is set). It is appropriate to follow the above description of the SEC.ACC.MASTER application, to describe one of the main processing functions available in respect of Temenos Transact users own portfolios, separately . This function enables to accrue into P/L the difference between the cost of a security asset and the known future expected maturity or redemption value on a straight-line (linear) basis or compound basis (in certain cases).

A security bought for USD995,000 and having a face value of USD1,000,000 with 100 days to mature is accrue discount, on a linear basis at a rate of USD50 per day (USD1,000,000 - USD995,000 / 100 = USD50). The user can obtain more details of the linear and compound methods as follows.

Although this accrual or amortisation process is usually confined to non-interest bearing security types, Temenos Transact also process discounts or premiums arising on bonds, gilts and other similar interest bearing securities that are setup to include an acceptable value in the Price Type field. All security types requiring discount processing must also be traded over a portfolio, which are setup specifically to process discount or premiums (if required). However, a portfolio may contain both securities which are candidates for discount processing and some records may not apply for discount processing.

There are no restrictions for portfolio types, (for example, investment or trading) till all records are for own portfolios. Attempts are not made to introduce this processing into customer portfolio valuations. Using various parameters on the portfolio records, it is also possible to re-value discount securities. Special processing is included, so that Temenos Transact recognises whether the discount still exists to be amortised or has been accrued in respect of a specific SECURITY.POSITION with respect to the processing requirement (upfront or no upfront).

Before the bank can commence the processing of discounts and premiums on securities, it is necessary to ensure that the portfolio SEC.ACC.MASTER records designated for this operation are configured satisfactorily according to the particular local preference. Other records also require the setup of specific records, so that Temenos Transact is able to recognise candidate securities which are to undergo this special processing.

Before Temenos Transact can perform the discount process, it is necessary to configure the portfolios to enable this operation.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user cannot change existing portfolios to perform this operation, only new portfolios can be configured accordingly.

The following fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER are relevant to this feature:

- Linear Comp Accr - This field is used to specify whether linear or compound methods of discount accrual are required. Special processing is not performed, when this field is left blank or NONE is entered. There are some restrictions on the usage of the compound method.
- Post Disc Upfront - This field is used to specify if for the portfolio, the discount is to be posted upfront and subsequently amortised daily or a no upfront policy is required with discounts and premiums to be accrued. Upfront methodology requires the underlying assets to be grossed up to par or face value within the accounts, providing the discount or premium amount to be amortised through a contra entry. This process is performed automatically by Temenos Transact . The response must be Y, if the underlying assets to be grossed up and discount or premium is to be amortised until eventual maturity of each security asset. Input No, if the user prefers to have the underlying asset carried at its original cost and have the difference between that cost and the future maturity value accrued instead.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is possible to post discounts and premiums without daily accruals taking place. If accruals are required, then this must be specifically requested by setting the Accrue Discount field to Y.

- Accrue Discount - This field is used to specify whether the organisation requires the accrual or amortisation of discounts and/or premiums in respect of the own portfolio holdings of eligible security types. If this function is required, then the user is asked to update the Linear Comp Accr, Post Disc Upfront , Discount Cat and Discsold To Realpl fields.
- Discsold To Realpl - This field is normally set to NO. If it is set to Y, a sale transaction is entered and if any discount is accrued or amortised prior to the sale, and a proportion of the provision amount is calculated based on the quantity sold over the stock held. This proportional amount is then transferred from the discount P/L to the trading P/L under the entry type discount sold. Finally, the user has to specify the category, which is utilised to build the daily accruals and resultant accrual or amortisation entries in the organisation’s P/L accounts. This must be entered in the Discount Cat field and must fall within the range 50000 to 59999.

The below screenshot illustrates the typical portfolio setup to enable Temenos Transact to perform the accrual of discount and/or premium over the remaining life of a security.


##### Yield Processing

The following example uses a 365 days calculation, for security with a face (maturity) value of USD100,000 bought at a yield of 5%, that matures in 100 days.

= ( )

= 100,000/(1+0.01369860.13)

= 100,000/1.01369860.13

= 98648.65

| Year | Interest (USD) |
|---|---|
| 1 | 182,500.00 |
| 2 | 182,500.00 |
| 3 (leap year) | 183,000.00 |
| 4 | 182,500.00 |
| 5 | 182,500.00 |

The processing of Thai bonds priced based on a yield, require a specific PRICE.TYPE to enable Temenos Transact to select the correct calculation method required to derive the cash consideration.

For straight bond, price and settlement amount are calculated as follows.

Calculated gross price (price including accrued Interest) in term of percentage is compared with par value. Calculated accrued interest in term of percentage is calculated as:

AI - Accrued Interest (%)

- g x DCS/365 (in normal period)

- –g x DSC/365 (in case during XI period)

Accrued interest in term of percentage must be fixed, such that the decimal points do not exceeding six points (round-off) The sixth decimal point is rounded up, if the value of 7th decimal point is equal or greater than five and not rounded up if it is less than five.

Where,

- DSC - is number of day commencing from settlement date to next coupon payment date (day).
- DCS - is number of day commencing from last previous coupon payment date to settlement date (day).
- DCD - is number of day commencing from last coupon payment date to redemption date (day).
- y - is yield to maturity (% per annual)
- H - is number of coupon payment per year (time per year)
- G - is coupon rate on bond certificate (% per annual)

(In case of trading during XI period, calculation does not included first coupon period. g/H for the first period is 0)

- n - is remaining instalment of coupon payment (time)

Price including accrued interest (gross price or dirty price) and price not including accrued Interest (clean price) in term of percentage are to be fixed such that, the decimal points do not exceed six points (round-off). The sixth decimal point is rounded up, if the value of 7th decimal point is equal or greater than five and not rounded up (if it is less than five).

Calculated clean price (price not including accrued interest) in term of percentage is compared with par value.

Calculated settlement amount is rounded off to two decimal points. The second decimal point is rounded up, if the value of 3 rd decimal point is equal or greater than five and not rounded up, if it is less than five. All this is because of the usage of percentage of price and accrued interest with six decimal points (round up) for calculation.

- Gross value is Gross price/100 x Par x Number of unit
- Accrued interest is AI/100 x Par x Number of unit
- Clean value is Clean price/100 x Par x Number of unit

K - Unit price

P - Price in %

VK - Not-paid amount (same currency as the price or the security value)

VP - Unpaid amount expressed as a percentage of the nominal value

BS - Number of units in trust

BN - Nominal value at maturity

Percent is 100, if the Percentage field in the PRICE.TYPE record is Y and 1 if the Percentage field is NO. The Unpaid Amount field in the SECURITY.MASTER application stores the amount that is not included in a part paid security. In order to maintain Temenos Transact integrity for historic prices, changes are not made to this field, after the security is traded.

When further instalments are paid on a part paid security, a new SECURITY.MASTER must be input and the positions are moved on processing from DIARY and ENTITLEMENT .

When an Unpaid Amount value is entered in the SECURITY.MASTER , that has a PRICE.TYPE where the Percentage field is set to Y, the value entered cannot exceed 100.

These Telekurs prices types are used for calculating the value of securities traded in units, where the price is quoted per unit and the nominal is stated per security.

Where,

- K - Unit price
- BS - Number of units in trust
- N - Nominal value

- RN - calculation nominal

Currently, these price types can be setup within Temenos Transact . However this uses a separate PRICE.TYPE for each unit nominal, specifying the unit nominal as a fraction (that is, a unit nominal of 1000 is required to be specified as 0.001).

The following fields in the SECURITY.MASTER application can be used to overcome this complicated setup.

The Nominal Factor field has the same effect as the Multiply Factor field in the PRICE.TYPE application. If a value is entered in the Nominal Factor field, it overrides any value specified in the Multiply Factor field. This applies to all calculation method that currently use the Multiply Factor field in the PRICE.TYPE record. The Factor Type field can be set either to DIVIDE or MULTIPLY. This is used to decide if the value entered in the Nominal Factor field either divides or multiplies, when used in the price formula. Effectively the formulas remain the same and there is no change if MULTIPLY is selected. However, if DIVIDE is selected, the value in the Nominal Factor field (X) is used in the formula as 1/X.

In order to protect the integrity of Temenos Transact ’s historical price calculations, neither the Nominal Factor or Factor Type field can be changed after the security is trade. Any attempt to amend these fields after the security is traded, generates an error message.
