### 5.61  Private Equity


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The private equity firms, known as general partners (GPs), raise money from institutional investors and accredited investors. This money is deposited in a limited partnership managed by the GP and invested in unquoted companies, for either a minority or majority equity stake.*
> 
> **Applications:** `DIARY`, `EB.ACTIVITY`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `FT.COMMISSION.TYPE`, `Issuer Fee Desc`, `PE.CUSTOMER.TXN`, `PE.EVENT`, `PE.PARAMETER` ... +10 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Activity*, *Actual Pe Price*, *Base Amount*, *Base Amt*, *Br Broker Comm*, *Bulk Authorise*, *Capital Call Amount*, *Capital Call Amt* ... +65 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The private equity firms, known as general partners (GPs), raise money from institutional investors and accredited investors. This money is deposited in a limited partnership managed by the GP and invested in unquoted companies, for either a minority or majority equity stake.

The private equity funds have a fixed life span of 10 years. At maturity, the investor's capital and returns made (if any) are settled. This requires the investments to be sold, or to be in the form of quoted shares, before the end of the fund. The more the investors, the more the long-term gains.

In the private equity world, the money committed by limited partners to a private equity fund (committed capital), is not invested immediately. It is drawn down and invested over time as the investments are identified. The drawdowns or capital calls are issued to limited partners when the general partner has identified a new investment and a portion of the limited partner's committed capital is to be paid for that investment.

The major applications required for processing the PE in Temenos Transact and their descriptions are shown in the table below.

| Application | Description |
|---|---|
| PE.PARAMETER | Specifies the configuration table |
| PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS | Captures the life cycle events of the PE |
| PE.CUSTOMER.TXN | Holds the customer level transaction details |
| PE.POSITION | Holds the snapshot of various attributes such as commitment amounts, drawdown amount, capital called amount, units issued |
| PE.EVENT | Holds the event details |
| PE.TRANSACTION | Holds the details at transaction level |


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The PE.PARAMETER application stores the transaction codes used for the background security movement processing. Each event in the PE life cycle has an advice code, which is also stored in PE.PARAMETER as shown in the screenshots below.

The user must set the Cust Txn Auto Id field to Yes to create separate PE.CUSTOMER.TXN records for each PE event (capital call, equalization call, commitments, and so on).

Refer to Working with Private Equity section to know about the working of PE when the Cust Txn Auto Id field is not enabled.


##### Configuring Issuer Fees

The Issuer Fee Desc field in PE.PARAMETER holds various fees charged by fund managers, such as management fee, miscellaneous fee, and so on. The valid values of this field are:

- Net: Collects defined fees as a part of the commitment or capital called amount (the fees is part of the commitment amount).
- Gross: Collects defined fess in addition (over and above the committed amount) to the committed amount.

| Portfolio | Commitment (USD) | Capital Called (USD) | Management Fee (USD) | Invested Amt (USD) | Customer Amt Due (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100291-1 | 500,000 | 500,000 | 500 | 500,000 | 500,500 |
| 100292-1 | 800,000 | 800,000 | 800 | 800,000 | 800,800 |

The fees configured here is available in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS . The issuer fees charged for each customer is then passed on to the underlying trade if the Fee Chg Cumulative field is set as Yes. Else, the system does not pass the fee to the underlying trade and raise the accounting entries at PE.CUSTOMER.TXN . The screenshot below displays the Issuer fee setup in Transact.


##### Configuring Bank Fees

Banks can charge fees for providing the services besides the management fees charged by the fund manager. These fees are collected from the customers and paid to the bank. The user needs to pre-configure the fee definition in SCDX.CHARGE.PARAMETER with the PE.CUSTOMER.TXN*COMPANY record ID as shown in the screenshot below.

Once the fee definition is configured, the user must define the below in SC.CHARGE.TAX.CALC.CREATE .

- Select the Activity field as Pe.customer.txn
- Define the data elements that must be satisfied for the respective charge.
- Define Base Amount , that is to mention the charges that are to be applied on the capital called amount.
- Link the FT.COMMISSION.TYPE applicable for the charge in Chg Comm Code .

The below screenshots show SC.CHARGE.TAX.CALC and FT.COMMISSION.TYPE setup for bank charges. For transactions (capital call) in 991022-000 security, the system charges a 1 percent fee for all customers belonging to group 001 (as shown in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ). This fee is to be charged on the capital called amount and this is accounted during the capital call (as shown in SC.CHARGE.TAX.CALC ).

Refer SCDX.CHARGE.PARAMETER for more details on fee setup with the multiple charges fees.


#### 🔧 Working With

The private equity firms raise money from institutional investors and accredited investors. The money is pooled into a fund and the capital is invested in unquoted companies for potential growth of the capital for the investors.


##### Event Lifecycle

The below events occur in the lifecycle of a private equity fund.

- Fundraising period: The fund seeks commitment from various investors willing to invest in it. The fundraising can happen in multiple tranches where the PE funds can open up the fund for additional commitments.

- Investment Period: During the investment period, the following events take place.

- Harvest Period: During the harvest period, the following events take place.

- Maturity - When the private equity fund winds down, all holdings are liquidated, and the customer is credited with the maturity proceeds. Maturity is to be initiated for all investors in the PE Fund.

All the events are initiated by the fund except for the subscription, which is initiated by the customer.


##### Instrument Creation

In Temenos Transact, four records in SECURITY.MASTER represents each PE fund. Each record represents a particular component of a private equity fund.

| SECURITY.MASTER | Description |
|---|---|
| SM1 | Represents the initial commitment committed by a subscriber ( Last Price is 0) |
| SM2 | Represents the undrawn commitment (drawdown) of a subscriber ( Last Price is 0) |
| SM3 | Represents the capital contributed by the subscriber with pending unit allotment ( Last Price is 1) |
| SM4 | Represents the fund units issued by the PE fund. Last Price is the NAV as supplied by the PE fund. |

Once the user defines the security with Pe Type as initial commitment and defines the Common Ref in SM1, Temenos Transact creates SM2, SM3 and SM4 automatically by running XXX/OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE.

When the user authorises SM1, the service creates SM1, SM2, SM3, and SM4 with the Pe Type field as below:

- Drawdown
- Capital call
- Actual PE security

The system updates Common Ref in the other securities.

The screenshot below shows the Pe Type configuration of SM2, SM3, and SM4.


##### Applications for Processing PE Event

The below applications are required to process the PE events in Temenos Transact.

This is an event-level table to capture the lifecycle of the PE fund. The system automatically creates a record in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS for the first time during the SECURITY.MASTER creation and defaults the below fields:

- Issuer field based on the Issuer field in SECURITY.MASTER
- Commitment Type as Initial
- Commitment Status as Provisional

as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the user fails to give the Issuer details in SM1, then the system does not create a PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS automatically. The user must manually create a PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS for the respective SM.

This customer-level table captures the commitments and the subsequent lifecycle events for each customer. During the subscription period, the user inputs the initial and late commitment amount directly in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN to capture the customer commitment. During the investment period, the system processes the lifecycle events captured in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS for each customer and automatically creates a record in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN for eligible customers invested in that PE fund.

> **⚠️ Note:** A unique record is created per event for each customer.

The below screenshot demonstrates two unique records in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN for portfolio 100291-1 created during commitment and during a capital call. The user inputs the first record to capture the customer’s commitment and the system automatically creates a second record based on the capital call event input in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS .

On authorisation of PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS , the system automatically creates a record in PE.EVENT which holds the event details. The record ID serves as a link to identify the underlying records in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN created for each event. When the user wants to bulk authorise the underlying PE.CUSTOMER.TXN records created for the event, the Bulk Authorise field is set as Yes and the system authorises the underlying records in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN using the XXX/PE.UPDATE.CUSTOMER.TXN service .

The PE.POSITION table holds the snapshot of various attributes such as commitment amounts, drawdown amounts, capital called amounts, units issued, and so on. The system creates and updates a record automatically when the underlying PE.CUSTOMER.TXN is authorised for the respective event. The PE.POSITION holds both the current PE positions for each customer and the cumulative position at the issuer level.

The screenshots below show the PE.POSITION for portfolio 100285-1 and for the issuer 100472.

The PE.TRANSACTION holds the details at the transaction level. The system uses these details for various validations and processing.


##### PE Investment Processing

The following are the steps involved in processing the PE investments.

Once the funds are open for subscription, an investor starts subscribing to the fund. The user must create a PE.CUSTOMER.TXN record manually for inputting the commitment amount. The system records the commitment in the Commitment Amount field in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN . The user sets the Commitment Status field to PROVISIONAL and no further process is carried out. The status remains Provisional throughout the book-building period.

For example, in the below screenshot, the customer 100285 makes a commitment of 200,00 USD in Pe Fund 991022-000.

Once the fund issuer has achieved the target corpus, the commitment is formalized. When the closing date is reached and all legal formalities are completed, the Commitment Status field is set to Final in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS . The user can give the date on which the commitments are finalized in Commit Final Date . The system defaults the date to today’s date if this field is left blank.

Once the record is authorized, the system automatically updates Commitment Status as Final only for those customers whose Commitment Status is still in Provisional and updates Commit Final Date in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN through XXX/PE.UPDATE.CUSTOMER.TXN service as shown in the screenshot below.

- The user can make Commitment Status as Final and give Commit Final Date to individual PE.CUSTOMER.TXN manually when required.
- If the customer’s earlier commitments are finalized and if the customer wishes to increase the commitment, the system creates a new PE.CUSTOMER.TXN record for the additional amount provided the subscription is not finalized at PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS .

Once the Commitment Status field is set as Final, the system automatically updates the position (equivalent to the committed amount) by creating two SECURITY.TRANSFER IN records for the SM1 security (initial commitment) and SM2 security (undrawn commitment) through XXX/ OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE service. The system updates the No Nominal field with the commitment amount and uses the transaction code given in PE.PARAMETER .

The system updates the Value Date and Trade Date fields of the underlying SECURITY.TRANSFER as given below:

- When Commit Final Date is greater than today, Trade Date is mapped as Today and Value Date is the date given in Commit Final Date in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN .
- When Commit Final Date is less than or equal to today, the Value Date and Trade Date in the underlying SECURITY.TRANSFER is the date given in Commitment Status in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN .

The below screenshots show the two records in SECURITY.TRANSFER for SM1 and SM2 created automatically when the Commitment Status field is set to Final in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN . Since Commit Final Date is less than today, the Value Date and Trade Date fields are mapped to the date given in Commit Final Date .

The below screenshot shows therecords in SECURITY.POSITION for SM1 and SM2.

The PE.POSITION is updated as shown in the screenshot below.

The system generates the commitment advice based on the EB.ACTIVITY record attached in PE.PARAMETER . Additionally, the system restricts the user from editing the committed amount or new user to enter the committed amount once the commitments are finalized in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS . If a new customer is to be added to the wave due to an operational error, then the user needs to set Commitment Status as Provisional for the latest wave in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS and then create a PE.CUSTOMER.TXN record for the new investor.

In private equity investments, an investor is allowed to commit additional funds after the initial closing. The additional funds can come from a new investor, or an existing investor can increase their commitment in the subsequent tranche. This is known as late closing where there can be a new wave of commitments as a part of late closing.

When the PE fund is opened for an additional wave of investments, the user must manually enter the below fields in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS .

- Commitment Type as Late
- Commitment Ref - A unique reference for identifying additional waves of investment.
- Commitment Status as Provisional

The user needs to create the PE.CUSTOMER.TXN record manually for giving the commitment amount. The system automatically defaults the unique wave reference in the Commitment Ref field in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN to distinguish customers investing in the particular wave.

Once the Commitment Status field is set as Final, the system automatically updates the position (equivalent to the committed amount) by creating two SECURITY.TRANSFER IN records for the SM1 security (initial commitment) and for SM2 security (undrawn commitment) via XXX/ OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE service as explained in the Initial Commitment section.

> **⚠️ Note:** Until the initial Commitment Status is set to Final, the user cannot to create an additional wave of closing. When a subsequent wave is created, the previous wave cannot be modified.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Initial Commit Amt (USD) | 300000 | 500000 | 200000 | 100000 |  |
| Initial Commit Status | Cancelled | Final | Cancelled | Cancelled |  |
| Late Commit Ref | WAVE01 | WAVE02 | WAVE01 | WAVE02 | WAVE02 |

Once the customer finalizes the commitment, the PE fund issues capital calls when the fund issuer identifies investment opportunities. The user can capture the capital call event using PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS by giving the below details:

- Capital Call Type as Capital.Call
- Capital Call Ref
- Capital Call Date
- Payment Date
- Capital Call Percentage or Capital Call Amt
- Any issuer fees to be applied in Issuer Fee Desc multi-value set.

The fund manager can charge fees along with the capital call. Based on the setup in PE.PARAMETER , the system automatically populates the Issuer Fee Desc field. The user then inputs the overall fees charged by the fund manager for the capital call in Issuer Fee Amt in case of amount or in the Issuer Fee Perc field in case of percentage and also defines whether the percentage is applied to capital called amount or committed amount in the Base Amt field.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the defined issuer fee is not applicable for a specific fund, the respective multi-value set is left blank. If the user wants to override the default setup of Issuer Fee Type , the same can be done in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS .

After the authorisation of PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS , the values move below to the Save Cap Call set of fields in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS as shown in the below screenshot. Similarly, the fields related to issuer fees are moved below to the Save Issuer Fee set of fields as shown below. A Pe Event Id is generated to record the event details and serves as a link to the underlying PE.CUSTOMER.TXN record created as shown in the screenshots below.

When the user authorises PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS , the system automatically calculates the capital called amount for each customer based on the overall committed amount (Initial + Additional Commitment in case of late commitment) and updates the PE.CUSTOMER.TXN record for each customer through the XXX/PE.UPDATE.CUSTOMER.TXN service. Based on the configuration of the Bank Fees, the system also calculates and updates the fees charged by the bank in the Cu Charge Tax Amt field. This record is in INAU status.

When the capital called is by amount, the system prorates the amount based on the overall commitment. The prorated amount is rounded down as per the currency decimal. The system collects any difference due to rounding from the investor who has committed the highest amount. Also, the system prorates the fees charged by the issuer based on the overall commitment.

The screenshots below display the updated capital call for a customer.

Once the user authorises PE.CUSTOMER.TXN , the system automatically moves out the position equal to Event Amount from drawdown SECURITY.MASTER record (by creating a SECURITY.TRANSFER Out) and move in the position equal to Investment Amt to the capital call SECURITY.MASTER record (by creating a SEC.TRADE buy transaction). The underlying trade and transfer ID created is recorded in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN . The Value Date and Trade Date of the underlying SECURITY.TRANSFER / SEC.TRADE is updated as given below:

When Value Date (Payment date) in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN is

- Greater than today, then Trade Date is mapped as Today and Value Date is mapped as the date given in the field Value Date in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN .
- Less than or equal to today, then Value Date and Trade Date in the underlying SECURITY.TRANSFER is mapped as the date given in the Value Date field in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN .

The system updates No Nominal in SEC.TRADE with the value in Investment Amt . The bank’s fee charged is mapped to the respective Charge Tax Type field in SEC.TRADE . If the Fee Chg Cumulative field is set as Yes, the cumulative issuer fees charged are passed on to the Br Broker Comm and Cu Brkr Comm fields in SEC.TRADE .

The screenshots below show the underlying SEC.TRADE created for the capital call when the respective PE.CUSTOMER.TXN is authorized.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user can perform individual or bulk authorization of PE.CUSTOMER.TXN records using the Bulk Authorise field in PE.EVENT .

The PE funds can issue the units after receiving the actual NAV from the fund manager by updating the below fields in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS :

- Capital Call Ref
- Units Issued
- Units Issue Date
- Actual Pe Price

Once the user authorises the PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS , the system creates a PE.EVENT to record the event details and the values move below to the Save Cap Call set of fields in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS as shown in the screenshot below.

The system updates the PE.CUSTOMER.TXN record for each customer through the XXX/PE.UPDATE.CUSTOMER.TXN service.

The system creates a record in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN when the PE product events is authorised for that event as shown in the screenshots below.

The system automatically moves out the position equal to Event Amount from capital call SECURITY.MASTER record (by creating a SECURITY.MASTER Out) and moves in the position to the actual PE SECURITY.MASTER record (by creating a SECURITY.MASTER In). The SECURITY.POSITION of capital call SECURITY.MASTER record is 0.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Capital Call Ref can be multi-valued if the user wants to issue units for multiple capital calls with same price and date.

The screenshots below show the records in SECURITY.TRANSFER , when the position is moved out from the capital call record.

The screenshots below show the records in SECURITY.TRANSFER when the position is moved in.

The PE.POSITION is updated as shown below.

Late investors can enter a fund before or after capital calls. Since late investors can enter the fund post a capital call, they need to be called in to make the percentage of investment (capital called) the same for all investors. The late investors of the wave are to pay what the previous investors have paid in order to equalize the percentage of invested amount.

Equalization call is an event where late investors are called to equalize the previous investors. The equalization event is captured using PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS by entering the below details:

- Capital Call Type as Equalization
- Capital Call Ref
- Capital Call Date
- Payment Date
- Capital Call Percentage or Capital Call Amt
- Equalization Ref (must be a valid Commitment Ref , that is, the unique wave number)
- Any issuer fees to be charged.

The fund manager can charge a late closing interest (fees) along with other issuer fees. This fee is an overall fee applicable to all the concerned investors (late investors only) for investing in the fund after the initial closing. The late closing interest fee amount is determined by the fund manager.

Once the user authorises PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS , the system automatically calculates the equalization amount for each customer based on the late or additional committed amount linked to Equalization Ref and updates the PE.CUSTOMER.TXN record for each customer through the XXX/PE.UPDATE.CUSTOMER.TXN service. Based on the setup the system also calculates and updates the fees charged by the bank in the Cu Charge Tax Amt field. This record is in INAU status.

Once PE.CUSTOMER.TXN is authorized, the system automatically moves out the position equal to Event Amount from drawdown SECURITY.MASTER record (by creating a SECURITY.TRANSFER Out) and move in the position (equal to Investment Amt ) to the capital call SECURITY.MASTER record (by creating a SEC.TRADE buy transaction) as explained in the Capital Call section.

The system updates SECURITY.POSITION as shown in the screenshot below.

The issuer can charge fees without any accompanying capital call. The same is captured in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS by giving the below details:

- Issuer Fee Amt or Issuer Fee Perc
- Base Amt (in case of percentage)
- Issuer Fee Ref

On authorisation of PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS , the system creates a record in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN for each portfolio, debits the customer account and credits the issuer account when PE.CUSTOMER.TXN is authorised.

| Scenario | CALL01 | CALL02 | CALL03 | CALL04 | System Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before allocation of units | Units not allotted | Units not allotted | Units not allotted | Units not allotted | The return of capital can be to the extent of previous four capital called (capital called for CALL01 +CALL02 + CALL03 + CALL04) |
| After allocation of units | Units allotted | Units allotted | Units allotted | Units allotted | The return of capital is to the extent of previous capital called (CALL04). The system uses the NAV at which the units are allocated to determine the number of units to be redeemed. If the user wants to return an amount greater than the previous capital called, then the user first needs to do a return of capital to the extent of capital called (CALL04). Once the return is done, the user can do a return of capital to the extent of capital called amount (CALL03). |
| Mix – For few capital calls units are allocated and for few units are not allocated | Units allotted | Units allotted | Units not allotted | Units not allotted | The return of capital can be to the extent of previous two capital called (CALL03 + CALL04). If the user wants to return an amount greater than the previous two capital call, the user first needs to do a return of capital to the extent of previous two capital called (CALL03 + CALL04). Once the return is done, then the user can do a return of capital for capital called amount in CALL02. |

The user can distribute the funds through the DIARY and ENTITLEMENT applications. The DIARY event is on SM4 (Pe Type = Actual PE Security). The distribution can be either the combination or any of the below:

- Non-recallable capital distribution
- Recallable capital distribution
- Interest
- Dividends
- Capital gain

> **⚠️ Note:** If the distribution results in redemption of units, then the user needs to input a Redemption event type. If the distribution does not result in the redemption of units, the user needs to input either a Coupon or Dividend event type.

Recallable is an event where the capital which is distributed can be called back for investment in the PE fund. The recallable portion of the capital can be equal to or less than the capital returned. The recallable capital is captured using the below fields in PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS :

- Recallable Roc Amt
- Recallable Roc Date

On authorisation of PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS , the system automatically calculates the recallable capital amount for each customer based on the overall committed amount (Initial + Additional Commitment) and updates the Event Amount in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN record for each customer. The prorated amount is rounded down as per the currency decimal. The system allocates rounding differences to the investor who has committed the highest amount

Once PE.CUSTOMER.TXN is authorized, the system automatically creates a SECURITY.TRANSFER into the drawdown SECURITY.MASTER record (SM2).

> **⚠️ Note:** Once a recallable capital is initiated, new investors cannot invest in the PE fund through late closing.

If the PE fund wants to reduce the committed capital, the user needs to input the below fields.

- Commit Redn Perc
- Commit Redn Date

On authorization of PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS , the system automatically updates the PE.CUSTOMER.TXN for each customer using the XXX/PE.UPDATE.CUSTOMER.TXN service. When the user authorises PE.CUSTOMER.TXN , the system performs the following actions.

- Positions are moved out ( SECURITY.TRANSFER OUT) from the initial commitment SECURITY.MASTER record (SM1).
- Positions are moved out ( SECURITY.TRANSFER OUT) from the drawdown SECURITY.MASTER record (SM2).

When the private equity fund winds down, all holdings are liquidated, and the client is credited with the maturity proceeds, the system updates PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS with the below details as shown in the screenshot below.

- Maturity Price
- Maturity Date

On authorization of PE.PRODUCT.EVENTS , the system automatically updates the record in PE.CUSTOMER.TXN with Maturity Amount for each customer using the XXX/PE.UPDATE.CUSTOMER.TXN service. This record is updated in the unauthorised stage.

On authorization of PE.CUSTOMER.TXN , the system performs the following:

- Transfer out positions ( SECURITY.TRANSFER OUT) from the initial commitment SECURITY.MASTER record (SM1).
- If there are any positions available in the drawdown record, the system transfers out the positions ( SECURITY.TRANSFER OUT) from the drawdown SECURITY.MASTER record (SM2).
- If there are any positions available in the capital call record, the system the transfers out positions ( SECURITY.TRANSFER OUT) from the capital call SECURITY.MASTER record (SM3).
- If there are units allotted, then a sell transaction ( SEC.TRADE sell) from the actual PE SECURITY.MASTER record (SM4) is performed for the current holdings and the price is equal to the Maturity Price .

Thus, all four security positions become zero.


##### Valuation Report

Temenos Transact processes these events and reflects the customer’s valuation in the customer valuation report.

The details available in the customer valuation report are:

- Initial/Late capital commitment
- Drawdown – the portion of the initial commitment that is not drawn
- Capital Call – capital contributed pending unit allotment
- Actual PE security - NAV of the investment

|  | Quantity | Market Price | Valuation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Capital committed | 10,000,000 | 0 | 0 |
| Drawdown | 6,000,000 | 0 | 0 |
| Capital Call | 1,000,000 | 1 | 1,000,000 |
| Actual PE Security | 3,000,000 | 1.1 | 3,300,000 |

Refer to Working with Private Equity section to know about the working of PE when the Cust Txn Auto Id field is not enabled.

Private Equity firms, known in industry parlance as General Partners (GPs), typically raise money from institutional investors and accredited investors. This money is put into a fund structured as a limited partnership which is managed by the GP. The capital is used to invest in unquoted companies, either for a minority or majority equity stake. Private Equity funds typically have a fixed life span of 10 years and by the end of the 10 years they must return the investor’s original money with any additional returns made.

### 5.62  Recording ESG Attributes Scores


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) is part of a broader legislative package under the EU Commission’s Sustainable Finance Action Plan, with the target to improve transparency in the market for sustainable investment products. ESG implementation prevents greenwashing and increases the transpa...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Data Type*, *E S G Pillar*, *Indicator Category*, *Lookup Table*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) is part of a broader legislative package under the EU Commission’s Sustainable Finance Action Plan, with the target to improve transparency in the market for sustainable investment products. ESG implementation prevents greenwashing and increases the transparency around sustainability claims made by financial market participants.

The ESG criteria are used to screen investments based on corporate policies and to encourage companies to act responsibly. Temenos Transact records the ESG criteria and scores per instrument and/or per issuer, and passes those scores to Front Office systems. No further processing is done in Temenos Transact using the recorded values.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Temenos Transact records the ESG scores per indicator. The user can define the ESG indicators in the SC.ESG.INDICATOR table. It can be classified into high level and low level indicators.

- The high level indicators correspond to static fields in the SC.ESG.SCORES table in Transact. For example, overall rating, rating environment pillar score, controversy overall score and so on.
- The low level indicators are dynamic fields in the SC.ESG.SCORES table in Transact and correspond to multi-values. For example, rating, controversies, screening, Sustainable Development Goals (SDG), Classification, EU taxonomy and Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) adverse impact indicators needed by the bank.


##### Defining Indicator Structure

The SC.ESG.INDICATOR table records various ESG indicators, the indicator category, the pillar, the data type and the expected values for each of the indicators.

The table below lists the indicator categories and the user can specify it in the Indicator Category field.

| Indicator Category | Description |
|---|---|
| Rating/Score | It is a measure of a company's exposure to long-term environmental, social, and governance risks. |
| Controversies | It accounts for situations in which companies may act in conflict with established norms on responsible business conduct and through their adverse impacts may impede or obstruct the goals of the companies. ESG controversies allow institutional investors to analyse a company’s significant social, environmental, and governance impacts by identifying company involvement in major ESG controversies, adherence to international norms and principles, and assessing company performance with respect to these norms and principles. |
| Screening | The ESG screened indexes are designed for institutional investors and aim to exclude companies that: are associated with controversial, civilian, nuclear weapons and tobacco, derive revenues from thermal coal and oil sands extraction or are not in compliance with the United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) principles. |
| Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) | The United Nations adopted SDGs also known as the Global Goals, in 2015, as a universal call to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure that by 2030 all people enjoy peace and prosperity. Currently, there are 17 SDG goals. |
| Classification | The SFDR classification sets out mandatory ESG disclosure requirements for asset managers to comply with. The aim is to create more transparency in their investment strategies and prevent greenwashing. According to the SFDR’s classification system, a fund can be classified as an article 6, 8 or 9 fund depending on their characteristics and level of sustainability. Article 6 - Funds without a sustainability scope. Article 8 - Funds that promote environmental or social characteristics. Article 9 - Funds that have sustainable investment as their objective. |
| EU Taxonomy | The EU taxonomy for sustainable activities is a classification system established to clarify which investments are environmentally sustainable in the context of the European Green Deal. |
| SFDR Adverse Impact | Negative impact on sustainability factors that are resulted from the investment choices or advice performed by a legal entity. For example, the impact such as carbon footprint at the global level. |

The other fields available in the SC.ESG.INDICATOR table are,

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Type | Indicates the data type accepted for the corresponding indicator. |
| Lookup Table | Indicates the lookup ID if the Data Type corresponds to a lookup. |
| E S G Pillar | Indicates the pillar category such as environment, social or governance pillar to which the indicator belongs. |

This table can also record the static indicator definitions for information purpose. However, in case of static attributes, the system by default overrides the values specified by the user in the following fields.

- Indicator Category
- E S G Pillar
- Data Type
- Lookup Table


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Recording ESG Attributes and Scores feature.

There are no Outputs available for Recording ESG Attributes and Scores feature.

### 5.63  Safe Custody Fees


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Safe custody or safekeep fees are fees charged for handling custody of the customer’s holding on behalf of the customer. Temenos Transact has an extensive functionality to setup and charge safekeep fees. This fee can be charged to the customer portfolio in a pre-defined frequency automatically.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AM.PARAMETER`, `CG.SC.CUSTOMER.CHARGE`, `CONDITION.PRIORITY`, `CURRENCY`, `CUSTOMER`, `CUSTOMER.CHARGE`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `DX.CLOSEOUT` ... +31 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account*, *Account No*, *Account Nos*, *Accrual Categ*, *Adjust Fees*, *Adjust Value Date*, *Auto Trfr In*, *Average Closing* ... +112 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Safe custody or safekeep fees are fees charged for handling custody of the customer’s holding on behalf of the customer. Temenos Transact has an extensive functionality to setup and charge safekeep fees. This fee can be charged to the customer portfolio in a pre-defined frequency automatically.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details the configuration of safe custody fees in Temenos Transact .


##### CONDITION.PRIORITY

This is the main parameter to be set for grouping customers for charging fees. Create a record with ID as SC.SAFEKEEPING. The CONDITION.PRIORITY allows the bank user to set the various fields in CUSTOMER and/or SEC.ACC.MASTER applications that are used to group customers to charge the respective fees.


##### SAFECUSTODY.VALUES

This application is used to setup both management and safe custody fees. It specifies the top-level information including category, which posts the fees and transaction codes to be used. The management fees charging frequency is controlled by the Charge Frequency field associated with the Charge Type field set as Ic (Investment Advisory charge).

The Country Check field includes the security domicile, security country domicile, or stock exchange domicile based on which the system calculates the base amount for management fees.

The management fees is calculated in the frequency setup at the portfolio level, if the Company Calculation field is set to No. The safe custody fees are calculated for all portfolios simultaneously, that is, safe custody fees calculation for all the portfolios in the company is run as the associated Company Calculation field is set to Y. In addition to the periodic management fees calculation, the management fees are also calculated for a portfolio, whenever the portfolio is closed (that is, the date is defined in the Closure Date field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER for the portfolio). When the portfolio is closed, the portfolio is charged for any pending fees. The safekeeping and management fee runs are calculated independently.

The Company Post field in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES controls the posting of management fees. If this field is set to Y, the posting of management fees for all portfolios in the concerned company are posted together. If this field is set to No, the SC.ADV.FEES.POST application posts the management fees for particular portfolios or all the portfolios of a particular account officer simultaneously.


##### Grouping Customers and Configuring Charges for Each Group

The user must first group the customers and then set up a charging structure for each group to calculate the safe custody fees for a portfolio.

SECTOR indicates that all the records in CUSTOMER application with Sector field that equals 1001 is categorised under this group.

> **⚠️ Note:** If a record in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION is not available, then the system uses the default ID in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION . This ID is entered in the Depository Group field in CUSTOMER.CHARGE for the depository of the stock for which the safekeeping charges are defined.

When a record in CUSTOMER is authorised, the system automatically creates a record in CUSTOMER.CHARGE . When a record in CUSTOMER is created, a corresponding record in CUSTOMER.CHARGE is created automatically. When a record in CUSTOMER is created and authorised, a corresponding record in CUSTOMER.CHARGE is created automatically.If the Securities (SC) module is installed in the system, the SC Application field in CUSTOMER.CHARGE is set to SC SAFEKEEPING which defines a set of fields for the SC.SAFEKEEPING application as shown in the below screenshot.

The SC Application field is followed by three associated fields which allows the user to link a portfolio to a particular record in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION . In the above example, the portfolio 100285-1 is linked to 001 record in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION for the safe custody fees and all the other portfolios of customer 100285 are linked to 001 record in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION . The user can change this link, so that the portfolio 100285-1 is linked to the 005 record in future.

The SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION for any particular portfolio is linked to display the Safe Chg Scale field in the corresponding record in SEC.ACC.MASTER . Read the System Tables User Guide for more information on the creation of the record for CUSTOMER.CHARGE for a CUSTOMER .

| Matching Order | Classification | ID Format | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Security Number ’.’ Depository | nnnnnn-nnn ’.’ Depository | 123456-000.100001 |
| 2 | Security Number | nnnnnn-nnn | 123456-000 |
| 3 | SUB.ASSET.TYPE ‘.’ Depository | ‘S-’n to ‘S-’nnnn ‘.’ Depository | S-300.100001 |
| 4 | SUB.ASSET.TYPE | ‘S-’n to ‘S-’nnnn | S-300 |
| 5 | ASSET.TYPE ‘.’ Depository | ‘A-’n to ‘A-’nnn ‘.’ Depository | A-20.100001 |
| 6 | ASSET.TYPE | ‘A-’n to ‘A-’nnn | A-20 |
| 7 | Default ‘.’ Depository | ‘ALL’ ‘.’ Depository | ALL.100001 |
| 8 | Default | ‘ALL’ | ALL |


##### Creating Generic Groups inSCSK.GROUP.CONDITION

Banks can setup generic groups in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION application with record ID starting with G-XXXXXX. These generic groups can be set when the banks want to create groups that do not follow criteria from CUSTOMER or SEC.ACC.MASTER or FATCA.CUSTOMER.SUPPLEMENTARY.INFO applications. These generic groups can be created without any corresponding record in CONDITION.PRIORITY and SCSK.GEN.CONDITION .

The generic group ID needs to be manually linked to the Sc Act Group field under Sc Safekeeping record in the CUSTOMER.CHARGE application for the applicable customers.

Safekeep Fees Setup for DX Option Contracts

The Safekeep Fees Calc field in DX.PARAMETER is set to either Exchange Traded Derivatives (ETD), Over the counter (OTC) or both to calculate the safekeep fees for option contracts. When the Safekeep Fees Calc field in DX.PARAMETER is set to:

- ETD - The safekeep fees is calculated only for the exchange traded derivative option contracts.
- OTC - The safekeep fees is calculated only for the OTC option contracts.
- Both - The safekeep fees is calculated for both the ETD and OTC option contracts.
- Null - The safekeep fees is not calculated for DX option contracts.


##### Including Additional Assets into AUM to Calculate Fee

The user must set Common Othr Asset in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES to include additional assets (other than security position) while determining the portfolio’s AUM for the safe custody fee calculation. It is a multi-value field and lists all the additional products that can be included in the portfolio’s AUM calculation. The user can choose specific product types or ALL to include all additional product types. Based on the selected product, the system calculates the portfolio’s value on which the fee is calculated.

If Common Othr Asset is set (any value) in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES , the user,

- Cannot set Other Asset and Daily Fee Estimate .
- Must set Daily Extract as Yes, for Charge Type as Ic.
- Cannot set Safekeep Fees Calc in DX.PARAMETER , if Common Othr Asset contains the value DX or ALL.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with the working mechanism of safe custody fees in Temenos Transact .


##### Calculation of Safe Custody Fees

The safe custody fees are calculated during COB as part of the SC.SAFE.ADV.CHG batch job. The frequency of the calculation is defined at company or portfolio level in the SAFECUSTODY.VALUES application, which depends on the company ID.

The SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is used for both management and safe custody fees. It specifies the top level information concerning the category, to post the fees and use the transaction codes. The Charge Frequency field associated with the Charge Type field of the SC module controls the frequency of safe custody fees calculation.

The different date ranges are specified in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES to allow prompt calculation of fees for the opening and closing accounts. The four ranges specified in the Calc Type field are:

| Options | Description |
|---|---|
| PERIODIC.OPEN | Used for an automatic charging run controlled by the frequency in the Charge Frequency field and the portfolio is open since the last automatic run |
| PERIODIC.NORMAL | Used for an automatic charging run controlled by the frequency in the Charge Frequency field and the portfolio was open at the time of the last fee run |
| CLOSURE.NORMAL | Used for the fee calculation because a portfolio is closed which was open at the time of the last fees run |
| CLOSURE.OPEN | Used for the fee calculation because a portfolio is closed which is kept open since the last fee run |

The associated fields are Period Start , Period End , No Of Months , Deliv Start and Deliv End for which the input is alphanumeric. The symbols used are:

- -
- +
- L
- C
- O

where:

- O represents the date of the portfolio opening
- L represents the date of the last fees run
- C represents the current system date

These symbols are entered together with numeric input to build a date. Thus,

- C-1 is the calendar date before the current date
- O+1 is the calendar date after the opening date of the portfolio

The safe custody fees functionality works on a monthly basis. If the user wants the safe custody fees calculated from the last run date and the current date, the input for the Period Start field is L+1.

If the current working date is 31/03/99 and the last run was on 31/12/98, the values of the variables are L = 199812 and C = 199903. As the system considers the last run date to be the first of the month, this translates a

of L and a

of C as the period from 01/12/98 to 31/03/99, which is four months. The

of L+1 and a

of C gives a period from 01/01/99 to 31/03/99, which is three months.

A minimum and maximum value for the safe custody fees can be specified using the Min Max Ccy , Min Amount , Max Amount and Def Min Max Ccy fields in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION . The minimum and maximum values are calculated based on the safekeeping charge plus or minus the discount. Depository charges are not covered. The setup for safe custody fees is shown in the below screenshot.

The safe custody fees are calculated in the frequency setup at the company level as the Company Calculation field is set to Y. The value in the Safecustody Freq field in SEC.ACC.MASTER of the customer portfolios is the same as the Charge Frequency field in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES . The SC.SAFE.ADV.CHG job runs during the COB, checks the system date against this date, and if the date is less than the next working day, that the system automatically calculates the safe custody fees for all the customer portfolios on the system.

The calculation frequency is displayed in the safe custody fees calculation related fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER irrespective of whether the safe custody fees are calculated companywide or portfolio basis. The date of the next safe custody fees run for a portfolio and the frequency of calculation is indicated in the Safecustody Freq field. If the Company Calculation field in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is set to No, the frequency is amended. If not, the value in this field is display-only. The date of the last run and the ID of the SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION to which this portfolio is linked are also display-only information.

The Country Check field defines the security domicile, security country domicile or stock exchange domicile based on which the system calculates the base amount for safekeeping fees.

During COB, the system validates the system date against the date in the Safecustody Freq field for any customer portfolio with the Portfolio Fees field set to Automatic. If the date is before the next working day, then the system automatically calculates the safe custody fees for that portfolio.


##### Posting of Safe Custody Fees

The details of the calculated safe custody fees are entered in the SAFEKEEP.HOLDING application. The account officer of a particular portfolio can review the calculated safe custody fees and amend them before posting, if necessary.

Some of the fields that can be amended are Account No , Value Date , Foreign Charge Local Currency , Discounted Amount Lcy and Local Charge Lcy fields.

The portfolios can be locked at this stage to block any new back-dated transaction affecting SAFEKEEP.HOLDING . If the portfolio is locked in the calculated status and the locking date is equal to or greater than the advisory charge frequency date, then there is no impact to the records in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING for a new backdated transaction entered (if any). If the portfolio is unlocked and a new backdated transaction is input, then the transaction is processed for the calculation of safe custody fees for the period and added in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING , as per the existing functionality.

The portfolios can be locked at this stage to block any new back-dated transaction affecting the SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED .

| Application or Account Owner | Different Customer or Suspense Account | Different Portfolio of Same Customer |
|---|---|---|
| SAFEKEEP.HOLDING | Account not part of this portfolio owner | Account not part of this portfolio |
| SAFEKEEP.HOLDING.POSTED | Account not part of this portfolio owner | Account not part of this portfolio |
| SC.ADVISORY.CHG | Account not part of this portfolio owner | Account not part of this portfolio |
| SC.ADVISORY.CHG.POSTED | Account not part of this portfolio owner | Account not part of this portfolio |

As an alternative, the user can extend the average balance method, which is based on the average daily balance for each month during the charge cycle. This process enables the fees to be accrued monthly to Profit or Loss (P/L), while the contra entry is posted to an internal pre-defined suspense account. All calculations are performed in the local currency of the system. This method requires some additional setup and caters only if the charge frequency is global (that is, the same for all customers). It is not designed to run parallel to the earlier described process.

If the bank is already using this earlier described process, the user must first ensure that the current charge cycle for all customers are completed. The user must ensure that the Company Calculation field in the SAFECUSTODY.VALUES application is set to Y, so that all the customers are charged simultaneously in the frequency defined in the Charge Frequency field of the same application.

The Perform Accrual field is set to Monthly to make the accruals as per the bank user's requirement.

The setup in the above screenshot instructs the system to perform accruals at each month end. These accruals are based on the average daily balance for every month during the charge cycle, which in turn can be monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or annually as required. The accruals are performed every month end and posted to the account that is opened using value setup in the Accrual Categ field. After posting the fees, the Process Stage field is displayed as Posted. The STMT.ENTRY also displays the respective entries as posted to the customer’s account.

The accrual entries for safekeeping fees are raised at the month end as follows:

- DR - Safekeeping fee accrual account ( Safekeep Accrual Account in SEC.ACC.MASTER ).
- CR - P&L ( Cr Categ Code in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES for Charge Type set as Sc).

If the user makes any adjustments to the calculated charges in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING , the system passes the adjustment entries to adjust the accruals. If the charge is increased, then:

- DR - Safekeeping fee accrual account with the increase
- CR - P&L with the increase

If the charge is decreased, then:

- CR - Safekeeping fee accrual account with the decrease
- DR - P&L with the decrease

On final posting of charges, the accounting is shown below:

- CR - Safekeeping fee accrual account
- DR - Customer’s charge account

The system calculates the fee for the whole calculation period on any day of the last month in the charge cycle with the Prev Month Close option. While processing COB on the day before the date specified in Daily Post Date field in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES , the system calculates the charge for the whole period based on the parameters that are set and updates the charges in show-fee records like SAFEKEEP.HOLDING and SC.ADVISORY.CHG . This enables the account officer to review the calculated charges, make amendments and post them within the charge cycle.

If the

field is set to February 1, the fee records are created with the full period charges as part of COB on the last day of February. The account officer can review these records on March 1. The entire review and posting process can be completed within the charge cycle. If not, the fee records are available for review only on April 1, which is in the next charge period.

If the fees calculation is based on the previous month closing balances , then the safekeeping and management fees can be accrued daily. The Perform Accrual field is set to Daily in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES to enable the daily accrual option.

The different date ranges specified in the Calc Type field (such as PERIODIC.OPEN, PERIODIC.NORMAL and so on) have no stance in the daily accrual calculation. The accruals calculated daily are posted to the P&L categories defined for the safekeeping and management fees. Separate accrual entries are raised in case of different P&L categories defined for safekeeping charges, depository charges and management fees. The entries raised for accrual of safekeeping and depository charges of a portfolio on a particular day in the fee cycle is shown in the below screenshot.

The contra entry to the above is a record in RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY (due pending capitalisation) as shown in the below screenshot.

The system is configured to raise accrual entries every day by reversing the previous accruals booked. The categories for which the reversals and re-booking are required are configured using the ACCR.REV.PARAM application.

The I/O method of booking accruals is configured for the management fee, safekeeping fee and depository charge categories as shown in the above screenshot.

The accruals of earlier day including the current day accruals are reversed and re-booked. If the calculated fee is amended prior to posting, the accrual booked is also adjusted to match the same.

In general, the account balances are not considered for safekeeping fee calculations. The necessary configuration is done in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES in order to include the designated account balances for safekeeping fee calculation.

Based on this setup, all accounts with currency XAU are included for fee calculation.

If the safe keeping charges must be levied for the holdings of a metal trading of a portfolio with an account and metal account balance, this option can be considered.

The daily accrual of fees can also be setup for safekeeping and management fees. The Perform Accrual field is set to Daily in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES to enable the daily accrual. The accruals are always calculated for the exact number of days in the period. For example, if the charge period is from January 1 to March 31, the accrual is calculated for 41 days on Feb 10. On March 31, the accrual is calculated for 90 days. The EB.ACCRUAL application stores the accrual details. On fee realisation, the statement entries are raised for debiting the customer's account. The contra for the same is RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY for fee capitalisation. The anticipated charge for the period is reflected in 'F' entry prior to realisation of the fee, which is viewed in the STMT.ENTRY application.

After posting the fees, the Process Stage field in the SAFEKEEP.HOLDING application is updated as Posted.

The STMT.ENTRY and RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY for the posting are shown in the below screenshots.

The accruals calculated daily in the next calculation period includes the fees pending until posting the fee. After posting, the accruals are only for the current period fees. If the calculated fee is amended prior to posting, the accrual booked is adjusted to match the same. If the detail method is defined in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION , the supporting details of the fee calculation can be viewed in the SC.DAILY.ACCRUAL.DETAIL application.


##### Posting and Valuing Accruals of Safekeep

The accruals of safe keep charges are posted in unique accrual Profit and Loss (P&L) category codes. The Safekeep Accr Pl field in SEC.ACC.MASTER application is used to post the accruals of safe keep.

To exclude the safe keep charges from valuations, the link between Safekeep Chrg Acc and Account Nos fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER is broken. The override record is released with type as error, to raise an error or override on safe keep fees. The Safekeep Accr Acct field in SEC.ACC.MASTER allows the user to have an internal account of different category not specified in the Accrual Categ field in the SAFECUSTODY.VALUES application.

The discount on safe keep fees are posted to a different P&L category code in the SAFEKEEP.HOLDING application. The Discount Pl field in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING is used to post the discount on safe keep.

The discount on safe keep fees that is posted is tagged to a different P&L category code in the SAFEKEEP.HOLDING.POSTED application. The Discount Pl field in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING.POSTED is used to post the P&L category for discount posting. This field is defaulted from SAFECUSTODY.VALUES, but it can be overridden.


##### Split Posting of Customer’s Tax on Fees

On the Customer side, the system posts the accounting for tax on fees separately by enabling the Tax Split field as YES in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES . The system calculates the tax based on the Tax Code field in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE and posts the separate debit entries to the customer account, one for fees and other for Taxes. The system uses the transaction code from the TAX application for the tax entry.


##### Posting Periodical Fee by Cumulating Monthly Charges

This section explains the monthly fee accrual calculation and posting the accrued fee on the cut-off date without recalculation.

| Application Name | Fields | Values |
|---|---|---|
| SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION | Calc Method | Total/ Tot.addon |
| SAFECUSTODY.VALUES | Perform Accrual | Monthly |
| SCSF.CHARGE.PARAMETER | Average Closing | Month.Average |

The process above continues across all months until it reaches the posting date. The system adds the fee charged for each month and builds the SAFEKEEP.HOLDING record when the posting date is reached. The recalculation of fees is not performed.

When Cumulate Post is set to Yes in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES , then every month when accrual is calculated the following values are stored in SC.PORT.PERIODIC.FEE :

- Total average asset balance on which the fees are charged.
- Minimum amount (based on the Overall Min Amt field in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ).
- Maximum amount (based on the Overall Max Amt field in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ).
- System calculated amount (based on the Calc Type field in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ).

> **⚠️ Note:** The ID of SC.PORT.PERIODIC.FEE is appended with SC and IC to distinguish between the safe custody charges and advisory charges.


##### Locking Portfolio Value After Calculating Fee

When the Lock Aum field in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is set for SC, then any backdated transaction or market price change for the previous month or period does not rebuild SC.SAFEKEEP.ACTIVITY or SAFECUSTODY.EXTRACT or SAFECUSTODY.EXTRACT.POSTED . The system rebuilds SC.SAFEKEEP.ACTIVITY or SAFECUSTODY.EXTRACT only for the current month. Thus, there are no changes in fees accrued or posted due to backdated transactions or market price changes since the total average asset balance on which the fees are charged remains frozen.


##### Add-on Fees for Safecustody Charges

For specific assets, banks can charge an additional advisory or safe custody fee, over and above the standard fees for the portfolio. For example, non-recommended funds are charged an additional fee of .05 percentage.

Add-on fees can be configured for specific asset type or sub-asset type or instrument and can have a specific minimum and/or maximum amount or neither for each fee type. The add-on fees are calculated independently for each position and a minimum or maximum is applied for each position. If a position falls under multiple add-on fees, each add-on fee is calculated separately.

When the Cumulate Post field is set to Yes for Charge Type Sc in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES , and the Calc Method field in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION is set to Tot.addon, then during every month end,

- The system estimates the total fees for the portfolio based on the total average asset balance. The total average asset balance is based on the rules for deriving the base amount. The fee details given in the Tot Comm Code and Tot Percent fields in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION are applied to calculate the standard safe custody fees.
- In addition to the total fees, the add-on fee is calculated for each position based on the asset type or sub-asset type or security number. The system takes the value of each position, determines the rate, and calculates the fee for each position. Where the add-on is set at: Asset type or Sub-asset type - The fee is calculated separately for each position within that asset type or sub-asset type. For example, if for a portfolio, four securities fall within the same sub-asset type, the system calculates the add-on fee separately for each of the four security master positions and checks the minimum and maximum for each position. Security (for example, 100027-000) and for a sub-asset type (for example, S-302), and that security falls within that sub-asset type – The system calculates the add-on fees for the security and again for the that sub-asset type. Thus, the same position can have two add-on fees. That is, if 100027-000 falls under S-302, then add-on fee 1 based on the commission attached to 100027-000 is calculated and add on fee 2 based on the commission attached to S-302 is calculated.
- The user can configure different records in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE for various add-on fees. These details are to be set up in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION with Security Type prefixed with AD to indicate that it is an add-on fee charge, the respective commission type in Det Comm Code and the percentage to be applied in Det Percentage .

- When an add-on fee is set for a record in SECURITY.MASTER and the rules for it are not defined in SCSF.CHARGE.PARAMETER , then the system checks the definition of sub-asset type or asset type or ALL definition to determine the asset balance.
- Add-on fees cannot be defined when Security Type =ALL.

The monthly calculation considers the following:

- Total Fee Cumulative of minimum and maximum up to the current month and then determine the monthly fee. If the fee for previous months and the current month is less than the cumulative minimum, the cumulative minimum is considered. If the fee for previous months and the current month is more than the cumulative maximum, the cumulative maximum is considered. Else, the cumulated system-calculated fee is considered.
- Add-on Fee For each position where an add-on fee is applicable, Cumulative of minimum and maximum up to the current month and then determine the monthly fee. If the fee for previous months and the current month is less than the cumulative minimum, the cumulative minimum is considered. If the fee for previous months and the current month is more than the cumulative maximum, the cumulative maximum is considered. Else, the cumulated system-calculated fee is considered. A single accrual entry is posted by cumulating the total fee plus add on fees up to the current month – cumulative fees accrued till previous month.

The above process continues across all months till the posting date is reached. When the posting date is reached, the system adds the fee accrued for each month (total fee plus the add-on fee) and builds the records in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING . Recalculation of fees is not done.

Read Calculation logic for more information on how the system cumulates and posts the total and add-on fees.

When Cumulate Post in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is Yes, every month when the accrual is calculated, the system stores the average asset balance on which the fees are charged, the minimum amount (based on the Overall Min Amt field in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ), the maximum amount (based on the Overall Max Amt field in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ) and the system-calculated amount (based on the Calc Type field in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ) for each position where an add-on fee is applicable in SC.PORT.PERIODIC.FEE . A record is created for each position where the add-on fee is applicable. The ID of the table is appended with SC to indicate that the charges pertain to the safe custody charges.

The Add on Fee Type field shows the asset type or sub-asset type or security master ID based on which the add-on fee is charged for the positions. The below screenshot shows that the add-on fee is calculated for security 100100-000 based on the sub-asset type definition.


##### Backdated Rate Change

When the Bv Rate Change field is set to ‘Sc’ in SC.PARAMETER , the system recalculates the fees due to rate changes with backdated effective date. When a backdated rate change is input in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION , as a part of the end-of-day process (COB), Temenos Transact automatically detects the backdated modification and recalculates the fee accrued.

Backdated rate change is triggered either:

- Due to an amendment to an existing record in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION such as: Rate change – by attaching a new FT.COMMISSION.TYPE in Det Comm Code or Tot Comm Code Percentage on the charge calculated – by amending either the Det Percentage or Tot Percent Change in the calculation of basis amount – by amending the Security Type Inclusion of new add-on fees to the existing group condition.
- Or by creating a new SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION with a backdated ID.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system does not recalculate fees if any other attributes in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION is changed.

If the tariff change is within the current fee period, the system reworks on the accruals for the current fee period and post adjustment entries. If the tariff changes back date to the previous period, the system reworks on the previous period charge and updates the fees in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING.POSTED . The account officer of a particular portfolio can review the calculated safe custody fees and amend them before posting if necessary. The fees posted can be a reversal and rebook of the entire fees or adjustment of the fees based on the setup of the Fee Adjustment Type field in AM.PARAMETER or SEC.ACC.MASTER .

For example, consider the below records in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION with the fees calculated till April and the current date is 15 May, 2023.

- 001.20221201
- 001.20230217
- 001.20230320

The fees have been calculated till April with the current date 15 May, 2023.

|---|---|---|
| A new record 001.20230101 is created in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION | As the backdated record impacts the fees calculated for January month alone, the system recalculates the fee for January and updates the new fee to be debited from the client. | No change as the system uses the charges defined in 001.20230320 record for calculating the fees for the period. |
| A new record 001.20230201 is created in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION | No change as the system uses the charges defined in 001.20230217 record for calculating the fees for February. | No change as the system uses the charges defined in 001.20230320 record for calculating the fees for the period. |

Therefore, the system recalculates the fee for March and updates the new fee to be debited from the client. When Lock Aum in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is set, the system does not allow the amendment of Security Type field in existing SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION record. When a new record is created system defaults the previous dated SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION record definitions of Security Type into the new record.

- Backdated rate change can be set only when, The Daily Fee Estimate field in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is not set. The Average Closing field in SCSF.CHARGE.PARAMETER is set to Month.average.
- Backdated rate change can also be enabled when AM.PARAMETER is not configured.
- Backdated rate change is triggered only when Bv Rate Change is set as Sc in the company where the record is created or amended.
- When the user enables Bv Rate Change in SC.PARAMETER for Sc or Ic, the system does not allow the user to change Calc Method for groups before the date mentioned in Last Run Date . The user can change the Calc Method only in the current frequency, when a record is created in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION or SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION with date as LAST.RUN.DATE+1, provided it is the latest record for the group.
- If the user tries to reverse an existing group condition record, the system compares Calc Method of the respective record with the previous record. If Calc Method is same, the system allows the user to reverse the record, else it does not allow reversal.

##### Backdated Group Change

Temenos Transact allows the safekeep or advisory fee group to be changed with a back dated effect.

To allow such changes, the Enable Sc Customer Charge field in CONDITION.PRIORITY with ID as SYSTEM record should be set to Sc.safekeeping or Sc.advisory or both.

When this field is set, the system updates the periodic fee groups (Safekeep and Advisory fee groups) in a separate CG.SC.CUSTOMER.CHARGE application, instead of CUSTOMER.CHARGE . The ID of this application is * * .

Initially, the system creates a record in this application when a portfolio ( SEC.ACC.MASTER ) is newly opened. The is the current bank date when the record is being created. When there is any change in any field in SEC.ACC.MASTER or CUSTOMER that results in a group change, the system creates a new record in this table with the current date.

If a retrospective or back-dated group change is entered, a record is created with the retrospective date. It is also possible to manually create a record in this table.

> **⚠️ Note:** Once Enable Sc Customer Charge in CONDITION.PRIORITY is configured, it cannot be reverted to Null. Both Enable Sc Customer Charge in CONDITION.PRIORITY and the Bv Rate Change field in SC.PARAMETER should be set for the mandate change to work.

The system updates CG.SC.CUSTOMER.CHARGE during:

- Portfolio creation.
- Change in customer level attributes.
- Change in portfolio level attributes backdated to previous month, period, or current dated.

|---|---|---|

The below table denotes the system’s behaviour when the calc method changes due to backdated group change of a portfolio.

| Case | Cumulate Post = Yes | Cumulate Post = Null |
|---|---|---|
| Total to Tot.Addon | The system recalculates the fee for the entire period and updates SC.PORT.PERIODIC.FEE . | N.A. |
| Total to Detail / Tot.Addon to Detail | The system skips the recalculation of fees and retains the fees calculated for all the previous periods. For the current period, the system does not calculate fees as the method is Detail. | Based on the fee group, the system recalculates the fee for the entire period. This is done if the fees is already calculated or posted irrespective of whether the change in group is in the middle or beginning of the period. Tot.Addon to Detail is not applicable. |
| Detail to Total/ Detail to Tot.Addon | If the group change effective date is from the beginning of a period, the system recalculates the fee for the entire period. If the group change effective date is in the middle of a period, the system skips the recalculation for the respective period. For the subsequent periods, the system recalculate fees based on the calc method . | Based on the fee group, the system recalculates the fee for the entire period. This is done if the fees is already calculated or posted irrespective of whether the change in group is in the middle or beginning of the period. Detail to Tot.Addon is not applicable. |


##### Including Additional Assets into AUM to Calculate Fee

When Common Othr Asset contains a value, the system builds the SC.ADV.FEES.ACTIVITY record for all asset types irrespective of the values given in Man Acc Calc for Ic. The system refers to SCSF.CHARGE.PARAMETER to derive the base amount, based on which the fee is calculated. The system applies the fee percentage based on the setup defined in SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION for the portfolio. If Cumulate Post is set in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES for SC, the system calculates accruals for each month based on the average asset balance. Minimum amount on a period start to the current month basis is considered.

The system creates a record in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING for each portfolio to store the calculated safekeeping fee details once the cut-off is reached. Inc Othr Asset in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING records the list of additional assets that are included in the fee calculation for the respective period. Once the fees are posted, the system creates a record in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING.POSTED to record the details of the fee posted and also the additional asset type included for the period in Inc Other Asset.

When Cumulate Post is set to Yes, the user cannot add or remove additional assets once the fee accrual for the current period has begun. In SCSF.CHARGE.PARAMETER , the Depository ID should not be suffixed for non-SC assets. Depository ID appended to the asset or sub-asset type of other assets are not considered to determine the portfolio AUM.

When a backdated transaction, price change, group change, or rate change takes place, the system performs the following actions:

- If the change is in the beginning or middle of the current period, the system reworks on the current period accruals based on the current setup.
- If Common Othr Asset in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is set, the system includes all the defined asset types when recalculating the fee accrual for safekeeping fees.
- If the change is towards the end of the current period, the system does not make any change, as the fee has not been accrued for the respective month.
- If the change is in the previous period where the fees have already been posted, the system recalculates the fees for the given period by considering the additional asset types recorded in Inc Othr Asset in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING.POSTED .

For the current period, Common Othr Asset has the AD value and for the period of January to March, the user has defined additional assets AD and FD, which are recorded in Inc Othr Asset . The user has created a backdated transaction on 5th March. While recalculating the fees, the system determines the portfolio AUM by including the asset types AD and FD and then applies fee on the derived AUM.

| Asset Description | Sub Asset Type | SCSF.CHARGE.PARAMETER (Safekeeping) | SCPM.CHARGE.PARAMETER (Advisory) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fiduciary Deposits (FD) | S-200 | 100% | 100% |
| FX forwards | S-201 | 100% | 0% |
| Arrangement Deposits (AD) | S-100 | 100% | 100% |
| Security Positions | S-204 | 100% | 100% |

##### Safekeep Charges Calculation During Disposal of Securities

Banks deduct the cumulated safekeep fees at transaction level when there is a reduction or disposal of security positions by setting the Post Fees On Sale field to Sc. The fees charged at the transaction level is proportionate to the nominals disposed.

When the Post Fees On Sale field is set to Sc, then the system calculates the safekeep fees during the disposal of securities and shows it in the Safekeep Fee Lcy field in SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER and ENTITLEMENT . The Safekeep Acct No holds the customer account for debiting the safekeeping charges and the Safekeep Fee Acy holds the respective safekeep charged amount in account currency. The Safekeep Acct No is populated based on Safekeep Chrg Account in SEC.ACC.MASTER .

In case of corporate action events, the safekeep fees may not be required to be charged for all corporate action events where the position is reduced. Banks can decide if the safekeeping charges are to be deducted for a particular event type by setting the Safekeep Fees field in DIARY.TYPE to Yes. This field can be set only when Post Fee On Sale in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES is set to Sc and Retain Original in DIARY.TYPE to No.

When the SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER or ENTITLEMENT is authorised, separate entries are raised by debiting the account given in Safekeep Acct No and crediting the Profit and Loss or the accrual account appropriately.

> **⚠️ Note:** When accruals are performed monthly for a given period, then any fees charged at the transaction level for the period is credited to the accrual account until the accrual balance is satisfied. Once the accrual balance is satisfied, then the system automatically credits the remaining amount to the Profit and Loss. The accrual account is the Safekeep Accrual Account field in SEC.ACC.MASTER or an internal account formed using the Accrual Categ field account in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES .

When the transaction is authorised, the system stores the total fees charged in Fee Chrgd Amt Lcy in the SC.SAFEKEEP.ACTIVITY record. The Pl Recog Safe Lcy field in the SC.SAFEKEEP.ACTIVITY record stores the amount credited to the Profit and Loss directly when the transaction is authorised. During the close of business, system adds the Fees Chrgd Amt Lcy to the Tot Chrgd Amt Lcy . The Tot Chrgd Amt Lcy field holds the total fee amount that has been charged from the customer as on the previous day.

The enquiry transactions with SafeKeep Fees Posted (SC.SK.FEES.POSTED.ON.SALE ) displays the fee deducted and a drill down is provided to list the trades or transfers or entitlements where the fee has been deducted.

The following points are to be noted while charging safekeep fees at transaction level:

- The Post Fee on Sale field can be set to Sc only when Daily Estimate is set to Yes in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES .
- Banks can charge fees only when the calculation method is set to Month Average.
- The system ensures that the amount given in Safekeep Fee Lcy field is lesser than or equal to the cumulative of Tot Est Fee Lcy – cumulative of Tot Chrgd Amt Lcy - Fees Chrgd Amt Lcy for the given period. When the amount charged is greater, the system raises the following error “Safekeep charges are more than the total cumulated fee
- If fees calculated is more than the cumulative of Tot Est Fee Lcy – cumulative of Tot Chrgd Amt Lcy – Fees Chrgd Amt Lcy for the period, the system charges only to the extent of available balance.
- Short sale does not result in safekeep charges at the transaction level.
- It is not possible to calculate the safekeep charges on intraday positions . For example, if there is a buy and a sale on the same day, the buy nominal is not considered while calculating fees. Only previous day positions are considered while calculating the safekeep charges.
