When the SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER or ENTITLEMENT is reversed, then the system reverses the entries posted and subsequently reduce the respective amount from the Tot Chrgd Amt Lcy and Pl Recog Safe Lcy for the current period.

In case if the transaction is reversed on the same day, then the system reverses the entries posted and subsequently reduce the respective amount from the Fee Chrgd Amt Lcy and Pl Recog Safe Lcy for the current period.

In case if a backdated sale transaction occurs within the safekeep period, then the system calculates the safekeep fees as on the previous day, immaterial of the trade date of the transaction.

In case of backdated transaction for the previous period, the system does not calculate the safekeep fees at the transaction level.

The SC.BULK.TRANSFER application is used in case if the safekeep fees are to be charged while transferring out positions from one portfolio to another.

If the Auto Trfr In field is set to Yes, then the system automatically creates a transfer in the SECURITY.TRANSFER record for the portfolio mentioned in the Portfolio To field.

The transfer out and transfer in records are created only when the service XXX/SC.BULK.TRANSFER.SERVICE and XXX/OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE is triggered. The Security Acc field in SECURITY.TRANSFER in records holds the portfolio ID provided in the Portfolio To field.

When the Post Fee On Sale is set to Sc in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES , then the system populates the respective safekeep fees that is charged during the transfer out for each security in SECURITY.TRANSFER .

> **⚠️ Note:** Auto Trfr In can be set to Yes only when Post Fee On Sale is set to Sc and Transaction Type in SC.BULK.TRANSFER indicates a Transfer out.


##### Pricing of Fees at Portfolio level

If a new customer is introduced to the bank and portfolio with the required mandate is finalised and created, the applicable pricing conditions are negotiated with the customer and finalised.

The customers are grouped based on common conditions and fees or charges are priced differently for different groups. The group level pricing conditions can be set for periodic fees such as management fees, safe-custody fees and transaction fees. However, individual portfolios may have unique pricing conditions based on the portfolio's expected business potential and mandate.

Different customers with same portfolio mandate type can have different pricing conditions. The customers with different portfolio mandate type can have same pricing conditions on some fee types but does not follow logic of grouping. Therefore, it is possible to set fees pricing at a portfolio level. The charge groups defined in XX.GROUP.CONDITION can be created with ID in the ‘C-NNN’ format for customer specific charges or ‘P-NNN-N’ for portfolio specific charges. For safekeeping and management fees, the effective date also forms part of the ID in the form of ‘NNN.20150319’ or ‘C-NNN.20150319’ for customer specific charges or ‘P-NNN-N.20150319’ for portfolio specific charges.

In P-123456-1.20150319, the representation is as:

- P - Portfolio level
- 123456 – Customer number
- 1 - Portfolio Number ( SEC.ACC.MASTER suffix (SAM))
- 20150319 - Effective date

The portfolio level pricing set is updated in the Sc Act Group field in CUSTOMER.CHARGE as shown in the below screenshot.

The portfolio level pricing takes precedence over customer level pricing which in turn takes precedence over the group level pricing. If a portfolio level pricing record is reversed, the customer level pricing becomes default and takes precedence over the group level pricing.


##### Safekeeping Fees for Derivatives Option Contracts

Temenos Transact supports the computation and posting of safekeeping fees for option contracts. The system allows the configuration of safekeeping fees for Derivatives option contract based on the Asset Type or Sub Asset Type under SCSF.CHARGE.PARAMETER , SCSK.GEN.CONDITION and SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION application. If the option contract has a setup available for both the asset type and sub-asset type, then the system gives priority to the sub-asset type .

> **⚠️ Note:** Safekeep fees for a DX.CONTRACT.MASTER ID cannot be setup. The ID formats that has an associated depository appended to the key are not considered as the derivatives are not linked to the depository setup.

Read Calculation of Safe Custody Fees to know more about the safekeep fees setup.

The method of computation of safekeeping fees such as average, month average, closing and previous month close can be set for DX option contracts. During COB, if the Daily Extract field is set to Yes in SAFECUSTODY.VALUES , then the system populates the daily balances of the respective DX contract in SC.SAFEKEEP.ACTIVITY . The system uses the premium amount to calculate the asset balances. On the cut-off or calculation date, the system includes the DX fees along with SC fees and creates a single portfolio level fees in SAFEKEEP.HOLDING .

The Asset Management (AM) module must be installed and AM.PARAMETER must be set to recalculate the safekeep fees when there is a back-dated trade. In case of any back-dated transaction during the current or previous safekeeping period, the system rebuilds the record in SC.SAFEKEEP.ACTIVITY for every working day from the back-dated trade date till date. The system reposts or adjusts the fees as per the setup in SEC.ACC.MASTER , if the fees are already posted .

Read Posting of Safe Custody Fees more information on how to post safekeep fees.

The system reduces the customer’s position when the option contracts are assigned, exercised, expired or when a contra trade is performed. When the system or the customer exercises the options, it removes the DX position and credits the underlying security to the portfolio. The system removes the DX open positions when the options are expired.

When the bank sets the Post Fee On Sale field to Dx for the reduction of position, system deducts the cumulated safekeep fees at transaction level. The fees charged at the transaction level is proportionate to the disposed lots.

When the Post Fees On Sale field is set to DX, the system calculates the safekeep fees during the disposal of securities and displays it in the Safekeep Fee Lcy field in DX.CO.EXERCISE.MANUAL , DX.CO.EXERCISE.AUTO , DX.CO.EXPIRE.MANUAL , DX.CO.EXPIRE.AUTO , DX.CO.ASSIGN.MANUAL and DX.CO.ASSIGN.AUTO.

The system displays the calculated fees in DX.CLOSEOUT and raises the respective entries by debiting the account given in the Safekeep Acct No field and crediting the P&L or the accrual account appropriately upon authorising the record in DX.CLOSEOUT .

The Safekeep Fee Posted On Sale (DX.SK.FEES.POSTED.ON.SALE) enquiry list the fee deducted for the selected period and has a drill-down to list the closeout records where the fee has been deducted .

When contra trade is performed , the system shows the estimated safekeep fees that is charged through the Safekeep Fee Estimate On DX Orders (DX.SAFEKEEP.FEE.EST.ON.SALE) enquiry.

The system allows the user to calculate and post the safekeep fees for short positions.

Assume that a customer has sold 2000 lots of CALL Option with Maturity date as 20201001. The system builds the record in SC.SAFEKEEP.ACTIVITY as explained earlier (Read the Computation of Safekeep Fees Due to Short Sell, for more details).

Assume that the customer exercises 1000 lots on Day 24, the system populates the safekeep fees as follows.

Safekeep Fee = (0-0+15.577100000 -0)* 1000/2000 = 7.78855 USD

= 7.79 USD

(rounded off to the decimal place as per the record in CURRENCY ).

#### 📖 Introduction

Settlement refers to the process of transferring funds to the seller and securities to the buyer.

This process involves series of communication between different players and hence settlement date is later than the trade date. The settlement period i.e days between the trade date and date when settlement should take place, differs based on the exchange and type of security being traded. For example it is 3 days in the US market, referred to as T+3.

However, due to various reasons, the actual settlement of securities and funds can happen beyond the settlement date. Most banks have a policy to settle their customers on the settlement date, regardless of whether the settlement has actually occurred. The customer’s cash account is credited with funds on a sale and debited on a purchase on the due settlement date. This is also referred to as Contractual settlement.

In contrast, in Actual settlement, the banks settle customers only once the counterparty actually settles their leg.

This feature explains how the system should be configured to support Securities settlement and how the process works in Temenos Transact .

The Securities (SC) module supports both contractual and actual settlements. In a contractual settlement environment, the customer’s cash account is credited with funds on a sale and debited on a purchase on the due settlement date, regardless whether the settlement has actually occurred. In an actual settlement configuration, the accounting happens only when the settlement actually occurs.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The configuration of settlement in Temenos Transact involves the parameter and contract level setting as given below.


##### Parameter Setting

The Actual Settlement field in the SC.PARAMETER application is set to Yes, to enable the actual settlement. If this field is left blank or set to No, it is assumed that all transactions follow contractual settlement. It is recommended to set the Actual Settlement field to Yes so that both actual and contractual settlement can be handled, based on the settings in the individual transaction. In addition, the suspense account categories for posting customer, broker and fees and charges, need to be setup. The Settle Method field needs to be set to US.

> **⚠️ Note:** The processing details explained further in this section are based on the parameters set for actual settlement with the settlement method set to US.


##### Contract Level Setting

If the actual settlement is enabled, the actual or contractual settlement is controlled at the contract level, which is available in the following applications:

- SEC.TRADE
- SECURITY.TRANSFER
- POSITION.TRANSFER
- DIARY

The Sec Hold Settle and Cash Hold Settle , available in the SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER and DIARY applications or the Sec Hold Settle field in POSITION.TRANSFER application indicates if the settlement is contractual or actual, for each transaction. If the Sec Hold Settle field is set to Yes, the actual settlement is used for the security position updates of the transaction and if Cash Hold Settle field is set to Yes, the actual settlement is used for cash accounting.

In case of SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER , the contractual settlement can be enabled for only one leg (customer or broker leg), while the other leg is on actual settlement. The Cash Hold Settle and/or Sec Hold Settle, Auto Cust Sett (for contractual settlement of only customer leg) or Auto Brok Sett (for contractual settlement of Broker leg) fields are set to Yes.


#### 🔧 Working With

If the actual settlement is enabled in SC.PARAMETER the processing is as follows:

- In the individual transaction, if the Cash Hold Settle and Sec Hold Settle fields are set to No, the transaction works as a contractual settlement in the individual transaction.
- If the trade date is a value date, the customer’s cash account and broker’s account are debited or credited, respectively. The SECURITY.POSITION is updated immediately and unsettled position is not displayed.
- If the Cash Hold Settle and/or Sec Hold Settle fields are set to Yes in the original transaction, a SC.SETTLEMENT record is created in FHLD status. Most details of the original transaction are defaulted into the settlement record. The rest need to be entered at the time of settlement.
- In case of a SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER, only one settlement record is created per transaction. For POSITION.TRANSFER, DIARY or ENTITLEMENT more than one settlement record maybe created.
- Where there are multiple customer’s and/or broker’s in a SEC.TRADE , the Total Nominal for all the brokers and customers for every particular transaction are totalled and updated in SC.SETTLEMENT . The amount due to the broker is updated in the Broker Total Nominal field, and due to charges and commissions, this may be different from the amount due to/from the customer, which is updated in the Customer Total Nominal field.
- The Trade Currency field in SC.SETTLEMENT is defaulted from the underlying transaction. The Customer Nominee field is defaulted from the original transaction (if specified). The value in the Cust Trans Code field in SC.SETTLEMENT is the transaction code used by the customer in the original transaction.
- The Br Nom Del Ref, Br Amt Del Ref, and Cu Amt Del Ref fields in SC.SETTLEMENT are reserved for future use when delivery is automated.
- The Cu Xrate Acy field in SC.SETTLEMENT is the exchange rate between the account and trade currencies. This is defaulted from the original transaction and cannot be modified.


##### Settlement Process

The settlement process through incoming SWIFT messages are explained in this section.

The transactions are settled through incoming SWIFT messages, manually by users or using an interface.

The core-banking product processes the incoming settlement status messages. Both ISO15022 and ISO20022 status messages can be handled. Read Settlement Status Messages or MX Settlement Inward Messages for more information.

The SC.SETTLEMENT record can be updated directly by an incoming SWIFT message. Both ISO15022 and ISO20022 messages are supported. Read Settlement Confirmation Messages and MX Settlement Inward Messages for more information.

If the transaction is set for contractual settlement on customer leg and/or broker leg, the system COB processing jobs automatically updates the contractual leg as settled in the SC.SETTLEMENT record. This automatic update happens as a Start of Day (SOD) process on the value date (settlement date) or an End of Day (EOD) process. This is controlled by the Sod Acctg field in SC.PARAMETER, which can be overridden by setting the Eod Accounting field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY or STOCK.EXCHANGE as Yes.

For the trades with the customer leg settled contractually, the system should not automatically settle the trades during SOD, as emergency holiday could be declared just before the opening hours. To ensure that the trades are not automatically settled, the Eod Accounting and Suspend Settlement fields in STOCK.EXCHANGE and CUSTOMER.SECURITY applications must be set.

If a global custodian handles the clearing and settlement activities, the Eod Accounting and Suspend Settlement fields are set in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record of the custodian. In regions, where the stock exchange and clearing house are related, these fields are set in STOCK.EXCHANGE .

This field should be set for all those stock exchanges susceptible for emergency suspension of clearing and settlement activities. For example, Hong Kong stock exchange which is prone to typhoons. It can be set only for certain periods during the year, for example, during monsoon or typhoon seasons. Even if the system is set to settle at SOD automatically, this field indicates that the settlement is done only during EOD processing for the specific stock exchange or depository.

If this field is set at the time of trade input, the accounting entries are raised to a suspense account and they are not raised directly to the customer account on the trade date. When the settlement is processed, the entries are raised to debit or credit the customer’s account.

For SEC.TRADE records of the specific custodian or stock exchange, the SC.SETTLEMENT record has the Eod Accounting field as Yes.

If this field is not set to Yes at the time of trade, the accounting entries are raised to debit or credit the customer account at the time of trade with value date as settlement date. If the settlement day is a holiday, the blocking (if any) of these funds must be done manually.

This field is set to Yes when the settlement is suspended. After the emergency is cleared, this field must be set to No to indicate that the normal activities have resumed.

For all trades of the custodians or stock exchanges where the Eod Accounting field is set to Yes, the system creates SC.SETTLEMENT record with Eod Accounting field as Yes. All these SC.SETTLEMENT records are skipped during the SOD processing and included only during the EOD settlement.

Before settling the record, the EOD job checks if the Suspend Settlement field is Yes for any custodian or stock exchange. For such records, the system does not settle the trades and updates the Failed Sett Date field in the SC.SETTLEMENT record with dates of the skipped settlement. Thus, the skipped settlements are tracked and reported.

The trades are considered again during the next EOD processing and if the Suspend Settlement field is cleared by then, they are settled.

> **⚠️ Note:** Due to an emergency if a settlement holiday is declared, the Suspend Settlement field must remain Yes until COB is completed. It is set to No or Null only on the next working day.

The trades can be settled manually during the day using the SC.ONLINE.SETT.DATE.ACCTG service even if the Eod Accounting field is set to Yes. If this service is run, the system selects all the contractual SC.SETTLEMENT records due for settlement and settles them online. In addition, this service checks if the Suspend Settlement field is enabled for the custodian and stock exchange and settles only those contracts where settlement is not suspended.

The SC.SETTLEMENT record can be updated manually as well. A nominal settlement is entered in the Br Nom Recd Del field. The Total Nom Settled and Nominal To Settle fields are updated immediately with this settlement nominal by adding them to the existing value for broker and customer, respectively.

The user distributes the nominal settled by the broker among the customers in the Cu Nom Recd Del field. This updates the Nominal To Settle field by subtracting this nominal from the value in it. The total nominal distributed among the portfolios cannot exceed the total nominal settled by the broker that is, the sum of Cu Nom Recd Del must be equal to the sum of Br Nom Recd Del .

The nominal settled for each customer or broker cannot be greater than the nominal outstanding for that particular customer or broker, that is, the value in the Br Nom Recd Del field should be less than or equal to the value in the Br Nom Outstand field.

The total nominal settled by the broker has to be completely distributed among the customer portfolios, that is, the Nominal To Settle field must be equal to zero.

A similar process takes place for the amount settlements. When stock settlement takes place for a portfolio and if there is any cash to be settled, a corresponding amount is suggested for cash settlement depending upon the percentage of stock settled for that portfolio. This suggestion can be ignored, if required.


##### Reversal

The reverse function is not allowed in the SC.SETTLEMENT application as it is linked to the original transaction. However, the users can amend the previously authorised SC.SETTLEMENT record by using the reverse fields in the record.

A nominal settlement can be reversed using the Br Reverse Nom field. This updates the Total Nom Reversed and Nominal To Reverse fields. The nominal from the customer portfolios are reversed by using the Cu Reverse Nom field. For a broker, a nominal greater than the value in the Br Nom Settled field cannot be reversed. For a customer, a nominal greater than the value in the Cu Nom Settled field cannot be reversed. The sum of Cu Reverse Nom fields has to be equal to the sum of Br Reverse Nom fields. The cash settlements can also be reversed in the same way.

> **⚠️ Note:** The settlement and reversal cannot take place at the same time. A settlement record cannot be committed or authorised unless it has a settlement or reversal action.


##### SECURITY.POSITION

If the Sec Hold Settle field in the transaction is set to No, the SECURITY.POSITION is updated immediately on committing the record. The unsettled nominal is not displayed. If the Sec Hold Settle field in the original contract is set to Yes, the closing balance on the relevant SECURITY.POSITION is updated immediately when the contract is authorised.

However, the nominal involved in this transaction is also flagged as unsettled for that position by entering that nominal amount in the appropriate unsettled nominal fields, based on whether the nominal is credited or debited. The Unsettled Nom Cr and Unsettled Nom Dr fields are updated accordingly. The unsettled value in the broker side is also updated in the Unsett Nom Cr field (which is multi-valued per broker). This holds both the unsettled credit and debit values and is updated with positive or negative value depending on whether it is a credit or debit to the broker.

The total unsettled nominal of all brokers is updated in Unsettled Nom Cr and/or Unsettled Nom Dr fields.

The unsettled nominal appears on the valuation of the customer portfolio but is unavailable to sell or transfer out, until the override is accepted. When settlement takes place, the settled nominal amount is decreased or increased and the value in the unsettled nominal field is adjusted.

If the Sec Hold Settle field in the original contract is Yes, and the Auto Cust Sett or Auto Brok Sett field is set to Yes, the unsettled customer nominal or unsettled broker nominal is not shown, and that leg is treated as contractually settled.


##### SECURITY.TRANS

When the original transaction is authorised, the SECURITY.TRANS records are created for all the records updated by it. If the actual settlement is enabled for the transaction, the Unsettled Nominal field is updated by the nominal amount involved in the transaction. The settled nominal amount is reduced from the total unsettled nominal amount in the Unsettled Nominal field during settlement.


##### Accounting

If the Cash Hold Settle field is set to No, the customer’s cash account and broker’s account are debited or credited on the trade date (value date).

If the field Cash Hold Settle is Yes but Auto Cust Sett is set to Yes, the system debits the customer’s account on trade date (value date). The broker leg entry is posted to the suspense account defined in the Brok Act Susp Cat field. Similarly, if Auto Cust Sett is set to Yes, the broker account is debited or credited on the trade date (value date).

If the Cash Hold Settle field is set to Yes in the original transaction, and Auto Cust Sett and Auto Brok Sett fields are set to No, the accounting entries are raised to suspense accounts on committing the record. These accounts are defined in the Cust Act Susp Cat , Brok Act Susp Cat and Misc Act Susp Cat fields in SC.PARAMETER or in the individual transaction. When SC.SETTLEMENT is completed, the system debits or credits the customer and broker account and reverses the entries to the suspense account.

The accounts to which the accounting entries are raised on settlement, can be seen by launching the standard enquiries such as TXN.ENTRY or TXN.ENTRY.MB.


##### SEC.DEL.CONTROL

If the Sec Hold Settle field is not set to Yes in the original transaction, the SEC.DEL.CONTROL is updated as usual. If the actual settlement is requested for the stock in the original transaction, that is, Sec Hold Settle is set to Yes, SEC.DEL.CONTROL is not updated. The SC.SETTLEMENT application is used for the actual settlement.

The SEC.DEL.CONTROL record controls all security and related cash movements. Each SEC.DEL.CONTROL record contains multi-value fields to facilitate input for any partial delivery of security and payment of cash. The control is built to prevent the erroneous over-settlement of cash or security.

If there are no funds or securities outstanding in the SEC.DEL.CONTROL record, it is created in live record, if the Def Del Control field in the SC.PARAMETER record is set to Yes.


##### Separate Broker Fails for an Actual Settlement Trade

The separate broker fails for an actual settlement trade is discussed in this section.

The existing functionality posts the suspense entries resulting from actual settlement to the category specified in Broker Suspense Cat field in the SC.PARAMETER application.

The Brok Susp Dr and Brok Susp Cr fields in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application are used to post the broker suspense entries to specific brokers.

For an actual settlement trade, the broker mentioned for the specific broker field is checked before posting in the suspense field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY application.


##### Unsettled Enquires and Versions

The following are unsettled enquires and versions in this feature.

The unsettled trade details can be viewed using the following enquiries:

- SC.SETT.ENTRIES - Unauthorised accounting entries for the outstanding unsettled positions
- SC.UNSETTLED - Detailed enquiry for each unsettled transaction, which can be drilled down from SC.UNSETTLED.CUST
- SC.UNSETTLED.CUST - Unsettled transactions by customer
- SC.UNSETTLED.RPT - All unsettled transactions

- SC.SETTLEMENT, BROKER - Broker details only
- SC.SETTLEMENT, CUSTOMER - Customer details only
- SC.SETTLEMENT, FULL - For full settlement only

There are a number of version records included with the system (can be user-defined as well) to meet the organisation’s most frequently used transaction formats. The below screenshot displays the version of the SEC.TRADE transaction entered into the system.

.

Since this is a version, minimal information is necessary to effect input, the bulk of the input components are supplied by default. However, other information relating to the trade are also displayed.

The basic non-version SEC.TRADE transaction contains over 120 different fields. Therefore, versions are preferable over basic versions to avoid scrolling through multiple screens to locate the necessary fields.

The amount of data displayed in the screen depends on the particular version, which is already used to input or examine the transaction. The basic SEC.TRADE transaction screen must be used if the user is unsure of the contents of any other fields. The basic transaction always displays every field at the input stage.

Using SC.UNSETTLED.RPT, overnight settlement reports are created. These reports displays all unsettled transactions.

> **⚠️ Note:** Before reversing a transaction (for example, SEC.TRADE ) with related settlements, it is advisable to unsettle the settlements ( SC.SETTLEMENT ) first to avoid any issues.


##### Settlement Delivery

The SWIFT messages relating to securities settlement are detailed in the following sections. The core-banking product generates ISO messages required for security settlement. Both ISO15022 and ISO20022 settlement messages are supported. The preference for ISO20022 (MX) messages over the ISO 15022(MT) messages can be configured for each depository or counterparty using the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application.

The MX message series that the depository supports, needs to be given in the Mx Instruction field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY . This multi-value field allows multiple series of MX messages.

If this field is set, the messages relevant to this series are generated as MX messages instead of MT messages. If this field is not set for a particular series, then MT messages are generated.

For certain transactions, the core-banking product generates additional settlement instructions (MT54n messages) for transferring the positions from proprietary accounts to the customer accounts. Generally, these are the trades created following the exercise of principal over the counter (OTC) options for delivery of underlying securities. These transactions involve two legs:

- Customer leg (customer vs prop book)
- Street-side leg (prop book vs counterparty)

There could be a separate street leg for each customer leg or multiple customer leg transactions are hedged by a single street side transaction. The securities are delivered into the proprietary book account by the counterparty during settlement. On the customer leg, two additional instructions (MT541/543) are required to transfer the positions from the proprietary account and deliver into the customer’s account. The additional instruction generation are controlled by the Depo Advicd Reqd field in the SEC.TRADE application.

Similarly, in case of bulk trades where the system creates parent/child trades, additional instructions are generated to move the positions from the bulk omnibus account to the customer (child) account. The additional instruction generation is controlled by the Child Depo Advice field in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE application or in the individual CUSTOMER.SECURITY record for a depository. The value in CUSTOMER.SECURITY defaults from SC.STD.SEC.TRADE and can be changed at the individual CUSTOMER.SECURITY application level.

The Child Advice Wait field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application is set to indicate if the movement messages should await parent settlement. If this field is set, the system does the following for buy and sell trades.

- The system sends out the trade settlement message (MT541/MT543) immediately on authorising the trade.
- The movement messages (MT540/MT542) are sent automatically when the trade is fully settled.
- The value date for the movement messages are set to today, which is the date of settlement of the parent trade.

- The system sends out the movement message and parent settlement message immediately on authorising the trade.
- The movement from the customer account to the omnibus should be processed on the settlement date (immaterial of the settlement from the omnibus) for sell trades Therefore, the movement and actual settlement messages can be sent as soon as the trade is authorised.

The Core Banking product supports MT54x series of settlement messages.

The following settlement outward messages are generated from SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER and POSITION.TRANSFER applications.

The MT540 receive free message is generated, if the customer buys and broker sells the stock with the broker delivery instructions set to FREE ( SC.DEL.INSTR record with With Payment Flag set to No). The below screenshot displays the MT540 receive free message.

If SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER or POSITION.TRANSFER is reversed, the settlement cancellation instructions to depository are sent. As per ISO 15022 series, the MT540 receive free cancellation message is sent. The below screenshot displays the MT540 receive free cancellation instruction message.

The MT541 receive against payment message is generated, if the customer buys and broker sells the stock with the broker delivery instructions set to DAP ( SC.DEL.INSTR record with With Payment Flag set to Yes). The below screenshot displays the MT541 receive against payment message.

If SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER or POSITION.TRANSFER is reversed, the settlement cancellation instructions to depository are sent. As per ISO 15022, the series MT541 receive against payment cancellation message is sent. The below screenshot displays the MT541 receive against payment cancellation instruction message.

The MT542 deliver free message is generated, if the customer sells and broker buys stock with the broker delivery instructions set to FREE ( SC.DEL.INSTR record with With Payment Flag set to No). The below screenshot displays the MT542 deliver free message.

If SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER or POSITION.TRANSFER is reversed, the settlement cancellation instructions to depository are sent. As per ISO 15022 series, the MT542 deliver free cancellation message is sent. The below screenshot displays the MT540 deliver free cancellation instruction message.

An MT543 deliver against payment message is generated, if the customer sells and broker buys stock with the broker delivery instructions set to DAP ( SC.DEL.INSTR record with With Payment Flag set to Yes). The below screenshot displays the MT543 deliver against payment message.

If SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER or POSITION.TRANSFER is reversed, the settlement cancellation instructions to depository are sent. As per ISO 15022, the series MT543 deliver against payment cancellation message is sent. The below screenshot displays the MT543 deliver against payment cancellation instruction message.

The transaction settlement is either manually or by an incoming SWIFT message. The following messages are supported for processing an incoming settlement:

- MT544 - Receive free confirmation
- MT545 - Receive against payment confirmation
- MT546 - Deliver free confirmation
- MT547 - Deliver against payment confirmation

The system can also generate outward MT544—547 settlement messages. In this respect, the core-banking product covers the roles of both the account owner (processing of incoming settlement messages) and account servicer (generation of outbound settlement confirmation messages).

The outbound MT544–547 messages are generated on authorising the SC.SETTLEMENT records in respect of a SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER record. The Gen Sett Del field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY must be set to Y for the customer to receive these messages. These messages are not generated if this field is set otherwise. The Gen Sett Del field is also available in SC.SETTLEMENT . The value in this field is defaulted from CUSTOMER SECURITY , but this can be overridden.

The outbound messages with the new message function (NEWM) are generated if there is a customer side settlement of quantity or amount. The RVSL messages are generated when reversing already settled quantity or nominal for the customer from the SC.SETTLEMENT application and CANC messages are generated when the underlying trade is reversed.

If the trade or transfer is set for contractual settlement, the outbound messages (MT544–547) are not generated. If the customer side of the transaction is set for auto settlement ( Auto Cust Settle set to Yes), the outbound messages (MT544–547) is generated on authorisation of the transaction if the value date of the transaction is lesser than or equal to the current system date or is in future.

The settlement status and processing advice are detailed in this section.

The account servicer (account servicing institution) sends this message to an account owner or its designated agent. This message advises the status of a settlement instruction previously sent by the account owner if the function of the message is INST.

The message also reports future settlement or forward transactions, for example, free receipts for which no instruction is required and have become binding on the account owner. The underlying instruction must be either a deliver or receive and be either free or against payment. This message is also used to reply to a cancellation request previously sent by the account owner if the function of the message is CAST.

The inward MT548 messages for settlement are:

A new record is created in SC.MT548.MATCH.QUEUE application when a new SC.SETTLEMENT record is created, if the Process Mt548 In field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Y. The fields in this application are updated automatically by the system upon receipt of MT548 incoming messages. The SC.MT548.MATCH.QUEUE stores the latest received status and previous statuses are moved to history.

Though the use of one status sequence (and one reason sequence) covers a large majority of the status reporting needs, there are situations where the use of multiple status sequences is required. In some markets, both matching and settlement processes are run in parallel and therefore need to be reported at the same time. In a reduced settlement cycle environment, account servicers need to provide relevant information to their account owners.

The same applies for reason code. There are situations (though not a majority) where an instruction is rejected, unmatched or pending or failing for more than one reason. Again, a large majority of instruction status reporting implies the sending of one status, one reason, but institutions should be able to handle the sending or receiving of multiple reasons.

Different circumstances in which we can expect multiple status and reason:

- Receiving multiple status and processing advice (MT548) on the same day or on different days such as pre-settlement date, post-settlement date.
- Multiple status codes in the same instruction.

Multiple reason codes for the same status code are shown in the following screenshot.

The latest status is stored in the Sett Status field in SC.SETTLEMENT application, whereas the additional narrative is stored in the Addl Info field in the SC.SETTLEMENT application.

The SC.MT548.REPAIR.QUEUE is updated with the rejection reason on receipt of a MT548 message with an invalid reference and missing or invalid matching code.

The SC.MT548.MATCH.CODE application holds the various matching codes details processed against inbound SWIFT MT548. Based on the matching code, the SC.MT548.MATCH.QUEUE is updated. If the value in the Match Code is missing or incorrect, the SC.MT548.REPAIR.QUEUE is updated.

The SC.SETT.REASON.CODES application holds the list of reason codes present in the tag 24B// reason of the MT548 settlement status instruction. The additional reason codes can also be set in this application.

The incoming details of a MT548 SWIFT instruction received are mapped to SC.CTDY.MT548.INSTRUCT for the transactions from incoming instructions. These details are then mapped to the outgoing MT548. The user can manually update the relevant information and the status in SC.CTDY.MT548.INSTRUCT and trigger an outward message. The High Lvl Stat field indicates the stage or status of the transaction. It is updated automatically at various stages of the transaction. For example, after the transaction is authorised, the status changes from Blank to New. This status is updated automatically at different stages and finally it changes to Settled after the settlement.

The outward MT548 message is generated in response to the incoming MT54n message

If there are no errors or overrides, the Status field in SC.CTDY.MT548.INSTRUCT is set to IPRC or PACK. The High Lvl Stat field is changed from Blank to New. The status update notification through MT548 is generated for the ordering customer.

If a security transaction is created in Hold for an incoming MT54n message from the customer with error, a MT548 rejection advice is automatically triggered to the customer.

The SC.SETT.REASON.CODES table contains the set of reason codes (SWIFT codes) updated in MT548 rejection advices. Temenos Transact checks the reason for failure and map the reason code for the trades and transfers created from incoming MT540–543 messages. The below screenshot displays the outward MT548 in response to incoming MT548 message.

If the customer has subscribed to MT548 status updates through SWIFT (the Gen Mt548 Instr field is set to Yes), the settlement status received from the sub-custodian through MT548 is forwarded to the customer. If the status message is received from the sub-custodian through other communication channels, Temenos Transact forwards the message manually input.

A record could be in the repair queue due to various reasons like:

- Non-existent Temenos Transact reference
- Due to missing match code
- Unmatched security ID

Security movement type or quantity. In such cases, the user can manually try to reconcile the issues. An enquiry is available to list all the items in the SC.MT548.REPAIR.QUEUE. If the record is in the repair queue due to:

- Non-existent Temenos Transact reference - A core-banking product transaction is used for manual reconciliation of the issue. The identified transaction is updated in the Manual Recon Id field. Also, the particular transaction record can be updated with the relevant details in the SC.MT548.MATCH.QUEUE .
- Where the record is in repair due to the missing match code, unmatched security ID - and if user is able to reconcile the issue, then a proper narrative must be updated in the Manual Recon Id field for manual reconciliation of the issue.

All records in SC.MT548.REPAIR.QUEUE with a value in the Manual Recon Id field are treated as reconciled.

If a message is in repair queue but subsequently a follow on message arrives with everything matched, the core-banking product automatically updates the Manual Recon Id field in the SC.MT548.REPAIR.QUEUE and also updates the message details in SC.MT548.MATCH.QUEUE .

| MX Message | Description | Equivalent MT |
|---|---|---|
| sese.024.001.nn | Securities settlement transaction status advice Indicates the message sent in response to a securities settlement transaction instruction to give a status of the instruction. | 548 |
| sese.025.001.nn | Securities settlement transaction confirmation Indicates the message sent by the executing or servicing party in response to a securities settlement transaction instruction to confirm settlement. | 544 / 545 / 546 / 547 |
| sese.026.001.nn | Securities settlement transaction reversal advice Indicates the message sent to reverse a previously confirmed transaction. | 544 / 545 / 546 / 547 |
| sese.027.001.nn | Securities transaction cancellation request status advice Indicates the message sent to request cancellation of a previously sent transaction instruction. | 548 |
| sese.032.001.nn | Securities settlement transaction generation notification Indicates the notification that a securities movement is auto-generated without a matching trade or transfer (for example through a corporate action). | 548 |


##### Cross Currency Settlement – Broker Side

Temenos Transact enables a cross currency account in SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER , that is, an account different from the trade currency only for the customer side. Temenos Transact insists that the currency of the nostro account for the broker side to be the same as that of the trade currency. This functionality allows to input a broker account, different from the value in the Trade Ccy field. The profit or loss entries are not raised and the difference is adjusted with the second leg of the suspense account.

The Br Ex Rate Acc field in SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER indicates the broker nostro exchange rate for the trade. The exchange rate is defaulted for purchase or sale, but the rate can be manually changed.


##### Partial Settlement

Partial settlement is the settling of one unique instruction in multiple phases (for example, 5,000 on day 1, 10,000 on day 2,...) until the original settlement instruction is fully settled. For partial settlements, the account servicers keep the original instruction and confirm or report settlement on parts of the original quantity and amount. The account servicers provide partial settlement information in the confirmation using the existing functionalities.

The process is triggered for transactions that are lacking securities where the deliverer holds a portion of the instructed securities. The partial settlement process considers the minimum and multiple tradable amount. All settlement instructions that are being recycled at the time of the partial settlement run are eligible for partial settlement, if they have been configured. The system allows for opting out from partial settlement at the account level.

If an account owner wants to specify in its original instruction that partial settlement is not allowed, they must use the settlement condition indicator :22F::STCO//NPAR (no partial settlement allowed) component. Similarly, if an account owner wants to specify in its original instruction that partial settlement is allowed (for instance, to override a standing instruction not to allow partial settlement), the settlement condition indicator :22F::STCO//PART is used.

The rules for partial settlement for a depository and its subaccount are defined in the SC.PART.SETT.PARAM application.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Depository | Holds a valid depository |
| Sub Account | Holds the sub account in the depository defined in the Depository field. The Depository and Sub Account fields hold the combination for which partial settlement parameters are set in the fields below. |
| Allow Part Sett | Indicates whether partial settlement is allowed for this depository and sub account combination |
| Part Sett Qty | Holds the threshold parameter for quantity |
| Part Sett Amt | Holds the threshold parameters for amount |

If the Allow Part Sett field is set as No, then 22F::STCO/NPAR is sent as part of MT540-MT543 messages, indicating partial settlement is not allowed.

If the Allow Part Sett field is set as Yes, then the system checks the threshold parameters defined in the Part Sett Qty and Part Sett Amt fields.

- If the transaction quantity is less than the threshold defined in the associated Part Sett Qty field, then 22F::STCO/NPAR is sent as part of MT540-MT543; otherwise, 22F::STCO/PART is sent as part of MT540-MT543.
- If the transaction amount is less than the threshold defined in the associated Part Sett Amt field, then 22F::STCO/NPAR is sent as part of MT540-MT543; otherwise, 22F::STCO/PART is sent as part of MT540-MT543.

As discussed above, when transaction amount or quantity is more than the threshold, 22F::STCO/PART is sent as part of MT540-MT543, as shown below.


##### Split Settlement

Split settlement involves (for an instructing [splitting] party) requesting the replacement of an existing instruction by two or more instructions. CSD participants typically split their settlement (unilaterally or bilaterally) to, for example, enable the settlement of a customer instruction that is short.

- Bilateral splitting is when both parties to a trade must instruct and match for splitting, for example, Switzerland.
- Unilateral splitting is when only one party instructs the split, for example, UK.

For the split, the bank receives the reference to the original instruction that is cancelled and replaced by two or more instructions and the status that new instructions are created due to a split. When the split instructions settle, each confirmation is linked to the original instruction. The process of the split settlement is provided below.

- As a first step, cancellation of the original instruction is received. The MT548 can be identified from the 24B:CAND/CANZ tag. The original instruction reference is in 20C:RELA. On receipt, MT548.MATCH.QUEUE of the original instruction or transaction is updated.
- Then, the split instructions (MT548) are received. The 20C:RELA has the original instruction reference and so the MT548s update the same match queue.
- The Split Reference field in the SC.MT548.MATCH.QUEUE application holds the message reference of each split instruction. The Split Nominal and Split Amount fields hold the respective split nominal and amount.

The SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT table splits a delivery instruction into two or more instructions. SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT is the transaction ID, for which the settlement instructions need to be split.


###### Splitting Settlement Instructions

For a settlement split requirement, the user can create a new record in SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT . The transaction occurs on the generation of a settlement MT 54N message and for a pending settlement from the counterparty.

Specify split quantity in the Split Qty field. The system defaults the Split Amt based on the value of Split Qty . The system assigns a unique reference to each split quantity. Each split has a new value date when the split is settled.

The system triggers the settlement advice MT 54X when the Send Sett Adv field is set as yes. It then reverses the settlement MT 54N message from the original transaction by sending MT 54N CANC and generates MT 54N for the split quantities.

The original quantity in the SCTRSC20075R280Q trade is 1000, which triggers an incoming MT 541.

If the user prefer to split the 1000 units into two (500 and 500), then specify the split as 500 in the Split Qty field. The system triggers an MT 541 CANC for 1000 units and sends two new MT 541 for 500 each.

A split quantity can also be further split. In this case, system sends a cancellation for the earlier MT 54N split and regenerates two or more settlement messages.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user can reverse a record in SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT until an MT 54X triggers and by specifying NO in the Send Sett Adv field. Once a record creation is complete in SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT , the user cannot reverse the underlying record in SEC.TRADE and the system generates an override to prevent the trade reversal.

Upon the authorization of SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT record, the system creates a record in hold in SC.MT548.MATCH.QUEUE for each Split Ref , that is, for each settlement message sent across.

After receiving an incoming MT 548, match the reference that was sent in MT 54X from SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT and update the corresponding settlement record. On receiving an incoming MT 545 or MT 547 for each split quantity, if the related reference is not the exact transaction reference, then the system checks the SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT table. If the transaction is available in SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT , then update the corresponding settlement record based on the quantity confirmed in the message.

If the related reference is not available in SC.SETTLEMENT and SP.NET.SETTLEMENT , then the system updates SP.ERROR.LOG based on which manual actions initiated.


##### Trade Netting

Trade netting is a process of netting the buy and sell trades, and not settling those trades as individual transactions. This section describes the processing of trade netting, and re-netting and splitting of the netted transactions.

The SP.NET.SETTLEMENT table process the trade netting. The user should manually input the various transactions that require netting against each other. The system ensures that the trades entered for netting match the following criteria:

- Security No
- Broker No
- Depository
- Sub account
- Delivery Instruction (FREE, APMT, etc.)
- Trade Currency
- Stock Exchange

In SP.NET.SETTLEMENT , the multi-value field like New Txn Ref enables the user to input the transactions that are netting against each other.

The system triggers an incoming MT 54X cancellation from the individual trades and create a record in the SP.RECONCILIATION table for the residual quantity, after SP.NET.SETTLEMENT is authorised with the netted transactions that are provided with the criteria match.

The system triggers an MT 541 if the residual nominal ( Net Nominal ) results in a positive amount and updates the transaction code as BUYI in Net Trans Ind . It triggers an incoming MT 543 if the residual nominal ( Net Nominal ) results in a negative amount and updates the transaction code as SELL in Net Trans Ind .

After receiving MT 544-547 for the residual quantity confirmation and if the received quantity is full, the system settles all the individual transactions fully. If MT 544-547 received partially, then system pro-rates the settlement quantity in the broker leg for all the netted trades. The system settles the customer leg in full on the value date if Auto Cust Settle field is selected. The delivery reference of MT 544-547 is updated in SP.RECONCILIATION .

> **⚠️ Note:** After the record authorization, the system blocks the reversal of SP.NET.SETTLEMENT record. If the user reverse the underlying trades after the authorization of the netting record, it raises an override or error. If the user settle a netted transaction manually through SC.SETTLEMENT before the custodian confirms through MT 544 – 547, the system raises an override.

There are two sell trades of 1000 units each from the customer side, which are netting against a single buy trade of 1400 units from the customer side. Post netting, 800 units are nominal on the sell side which remains unsettled.

In the above case, there is a residual of 800 units after netting the buy and sell trades with value date. For the residual, the SP.RECONCILAITION table sends an MT 543 to the custodian. After receiving an MT 547 to confirm the 800 quantity, the system identifies the corresponding SP.RECONCILIATION ID and settle the underlying trades in SEC.TRADE that belong to the SP.NET.SETTLEMENT automatically.

User should open the existing SP.NET.SETTLEMENT record if the user prefers to re-net an existing netted transaction with additional trades. User can specify the additional netted transactions in the New Txn Ref field. After the re-net transaction, the system recalculates the residual quantity ( Net Nominal ) and the net transaction code ( Net Trans Ind ).

On authorisation of SP.NET.SETTLEMENT , the system triggers the cancellation of earlier MT 54X and sends a new MT 54X based on the residual nominal results in positive or negative quantity.

1. The system enables you to split a netted transaction. For example, after netting the buy and sell trades, if there is a residual nominal of 3000, you can further split this quantity into 1000 and 2000 through SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT . To split a netted transaction, SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT accepts SEC.TRADE ID and SP.NET.SETTLEMENT ID.
2. After splitting, the system cancels the MT 54X sent for the net quantity when the settlement advice is triggered ( Send Sett Adv ), and in turn sends two or more MT 54X for the split quantity from SP.SPLIT.SETTLEMENT based on how the residual quantity is split.
3. After receiving MT 544- 547s for confirmation of each split quantity, the system identifies the SP.RECONCILIATION record related to the underlying trades that are netted via SP.NET.SETTLEMENT and triggers settlement through SP.RECONCILIATION .


##### Defaulting of Market Indicator at Transaction Level

Market indicator refers to Tag 22F in SWIFT messages MT540/MT541/MT542/MT543. This is a mandatory tag in mandatory sequence E (settlement details). The SWIFT specifications for this tag is available in the below link.

https://www.iso20022.org/15022/uhb/mt541-63-field-22f.htm

The format of Tag 22F is:

- Option F :4!c/[8c]/4!c (Qualifier)(Data Source Scheme)(Indicator)

The tag is made of three components out of which the middle component is optional. All the components has to be SWIFT compliant, that is, it must be one of the pre-defined values as published by SWIFT (The list of predefined values for each of this component is available). This tag can occur multiple times within the same message. Few example values are provided below for reference.

> **⚠️ Note:** This is a non-exhaustive list and SWIFT can further add values in future.

| Qualifier | Data Source Name | Indicator |
|---|---|---|
| SETR | STRA | TRAD |
| STAM | SMPG | INTE |
| BENE | XASX | IEYX |
| STCO | CRST | GBOX |
| RTGS | - | GBTX |
| - | - | NBEN |
| - | - | MKDW |

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| @Id | The ID of this application is the record ID of the COMPANY |
| Xx | Rule name can be updated in this field. For example, Rule 1. This field is the start of the multi-value set |
| Depo Sub Account-XX-Xx | Holds the CUSTOMER ID of the custodian * sub account ID. The customer must be defined as depository in CUSTOMER.SECURITY application. The sub-account ID is optional if the rule has to be defined for individual sub-accounts of the custodian. The field can also accepts the value ALL. This is a sub-value field |
| ISIN Country-XX-Xx | Accepts a valid country record or the value ALL |
| Sec Type-XX-Xx | Accepts either a SECURITY.MASTER ID or SUB.ASSET.TYPE or an ASSET.TYPE . ( SUB.ASSET TYPE must be prefixed with ‘S-‘, ASSET.TYPE must be prefixed with ’A-‘). Also, accepts the value ‘ALL’. All sub-asset types (with prefix ‘S-’) and asset types (with prefix ‘A-‘) are displayed in a drop down. For records in SECURITY.MASTER , drop down is not available, the user can directly input the SECURITY.MASTER ID |
| Stock Exch Dom-XX-Xx | Accepts a valid country record. All stock exchanges domiciled in this country is applicable for this rule. Also, accepts the value ALL |
| Stock Exch-XX-Xx | Accepts a valid record in STOCK.EXCHANGE . These criteria are ignored for transfer transactions. Also, accepts the value ALL |
| Trans Type-XX-Xx | Accepts a valid record in SC.TRANS.NAME or the value ALL |
| Application-XX-Xx | Accepts the following values: SEC.TRADE SECURITY.TRANSFER POSITION.TRANSFER ALL |
| Message Type-XX-Xx | Accepts the following values MT540 MT541 MT542 MT543 ALL |
| Pset-XX-Xx | Accepts PSET in Bank Identification Code (BIC) format. BIC address is to be prefixed with ‘B-’. Also accepts the value ALL. |
| Qualifier-Xx | Corresponds to the first component Qualifier of Tag 22F. This is an EB.LOOKUP related field. |
| Data Source Name-Xx | Corresponds to the second component Data Source Name of Tag 22F. Accepts blank or null values This is an EB.LOOKUP related field. |
| Xx | Corresponds to the third component Indicator of tag 22F. This is an EB.LOOKUP related field. |

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Mkt Ind Qualifier | Corresponds to the first component Qualifier of Tag 22F. This is a multi-value field and is an EB.LOOKUP related field. |
| Mkt Ind Dsn -XX | Corresponds to the second component Data Source Name of Tag 22F. This is an associated multi-value field which accepts blank or null values. This is an EB.LOOKUP related field. |
| XX | Corresponds to the third component Indicator of Tag 22F. This is an associated multi-value field and is an EB.LOOKUP related field. |

Settlement of securities is a business process whereby securities or interests in securities are delivered, usually against (in simultaneous exchange for) payment of money, to fulfill contractual obligations, such as those arising under securities trades. As part of performance on the delivery obligations entailed by the trade, settlement involves the delivery of securities and the corresponding payment.

Message MT540 is a receive free message sent to a custodian instructing the receipt of financial instruments for free of payment. In our core banking system, this message is sent to the customer in the Depository field present in the SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER application, for free of payment transactions.

Message MT541 is a receive against payment message sent to a custodian instructing the receipt of financial instruments against payment. In our core banking system, this message is sent to the customer updated in the Depository field present in the SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER application for free of payment transactions.

Message MT542 is a deliver free message sent to a custodian instructing the delivery of financial instruments, free of payment. In our core banking system, this message is sent to the customer updated in the Depository field present in the SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER application for free of payment transactions.

Message MT543 is a deliver against payment message sent to a custodian instructing the delivery of financial instruments against payment. In our core banking system, this message is sent to the customer in the Depository field present in the SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER application for delivery against payment transactions.

### 5.65  SRDII Events


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Shareholder Rights Directive II(SRD II) is a European Union (EU) directive, which improves shareholder transparency and strengthens the position of shareholders trading in the EU regulated markets. SRD II gives the companies the right to identify their shareholders. This in turn creates an oblig...*
> 
> **Applications:** `SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE`, `SC.SRD.HLD.RESQUEST`, `SECURITY.MASTER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Below Threshold*, *Canc Delivery Inref*, *Depository*, *Err Reason*, *Error Reason*, *ISIN*, *Nominal*, *Outward Canc Gen Method* ... +20 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Shareholder Rights Directive II(SRD II) is a European Union (EU) directive, which improves shareholder transparency and strengthens the position of shareholders trading in the EU regulated markets. SRD II gives the companies the right to identify their shareholders. This in turn creates an obligation on the intermediaries to transmit the necessary information (shareholder’s identity) back to the issuer or company.

The ISO20022 has specific messages to handle the disclosure of shareholder identification in the context of the SRD II. The Shareholder Identification Disclosure messages are used by,

- the issuer or a third-party nominated by an issuer to notify the request for disclosure
- the intermediaries to send back the shareholders or account holder’s identification and account holding information

Temenos Transact supports the following Shareholders Identification Disclosure Maintenance Messages:

| Messages | Description |
|---|---|
| seev.045 Inward - Shareholders Identification Disclosure Request | Indicates the message sent by an issuer or by a third party nominated by the issuer to request the disclosure of shareholders identity. |
| seev.046 Inward - Shareholders Identification Disclosure Request Cancellation Advice | Indicates the message sent by an issuer or by a third party nominated by the issuer in order to withdraw/cancel the previously sent Shareholders Identification Disclosure Request (seev.045). |
| seev.047 Outward - Shareholders Identification Disclosure Response | Indicates the message sent in response to the Shareholder Identification Disclosure Request message (seev.045) to the recipient designated by the issuer. |
| seev.048 Outward - Shareholders Identification Disclosure Response Cancellation | Indicates the message sent to cancel the previously sent Shareholder Identification Disclosure Response (seev.047). |
| seev.049 Inward - Shareholders Identification Disclosure Response Status Advice | Indicates the message sent by an issuer or by a third party nominated by the issuer in response to a seev.047 to report about the acceptance status of the received Shareholder Identification Disclosure Response message/report. |


#### ⚙️ Configuration

In order to support the MX Shareholders Identification Disclosure Maintenance Messages, the following setup is required.


##### SC.SRD.BNK.STATIC.DTLS

The applications holds the necessary details for processing the Shareholders Identification Disclosure Response messages. The ID of SC.SRD.BNK.STATIC.DTLS is a valid record in COMPANY .

If the Outward Canc Gen Method field is set as CANC.RESEND, the system cancels the last sent response and generates a new response. This value is set to support the generation of outward seev.048 message.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section describes the workflow for the Shareholder Rights Directive II(SRD II) messages and covers the following topics.

- Overview about the SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST and SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE applications
- Processing the SRD II MX messages (seev.045, seev.046, seev.047, seev.048, seev.049)


##### SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST

For processing the SRD II messages, the SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST application records the details of the event and is similar to the DIARY application of a corporate action event. Each Shareholders disclosure request will have a unique request id that identifies the event.

When the user authorises SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST record and the Status field is set as OK, the XXX/SC.SRD.CREATE.RESPONSE service creates records in SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE for each customer having positions belonging to the given Depository as on the Record Date . The record is always created in the authorised stage. This application is similar to the ENTITLEMENT application of a corporate action event. The ID of the application is made up of

- SRD.HLD.REQUEST ID
- CUSTOMER
- DEPOSITORY
- SUB.ACCOUNT


##### UpdatingNominal

The Nominal field holds the cumulative nominal for a security across multiple portfolios for a given customer, depository and sub-account combination. If multiple securities are available for a given ISIN, the Nominal field holds the cumulative nominal across multiple portfolios and securities for a given customer, depository and sub account combination.

| Portfolio | Holdings (SM1) ISIN US02079K1079 | Depository |
|---|---|---|
| A-1 | 1000 | 100472 |
| A-2 | 1500 | 100472 |

| Portfolio | Holdings (SM1) ISIN US02129K1119 | Holdings (SM2) ISIN US02129K1119 | Holdings (SM3) ISIN US02129K1119 | Depository |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-1 | 1000 | 2000 |  | 100472 |
| A-2 | 1500 |  | 500 | 100472 |

| Portfolio | Holdings (SM1) ISIN US00999K1119 | Depository | Holdings (SM2) ISIN US00999K1119 | Depository |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-1 | 1000 | 100472 | 2000 | 100472 |
| A-2 | 1500 | 100472 | 500 | 100492 |


##### UpdatingSecurity No

The Security No field in SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE holds all the SECURITY.MASTER ids for the given ISIN irrespective of the customer position.

| Portfolio | Holdings (SM1) ISIN US02129K1119 | Holdings (SM2) ISIN US02129K1119 | Holdings (SM3) ISIN US02129K1119 | Depository |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-1 | 1000 | 2000 |  | 100472 |
| A-2 | 200 |  |  | 100472 |

Even when the customer has no position in SM3, the system creates SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE for Customer A with Security No as SM1, SM2, and SM3 and Nominal as 3200.

To recheck the qualified holdings as on Record Date , the Rerun field in SC.SRD.HLD.RESQUEST is set to Yes and the SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE is regenerated to reflect the changes in eligible holdings. If any new customer is eligible then SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE is created for that customer.


##### Processing of MX Messages

The processing of SRD II Events is explained in the following sections.

The issuer or its agent or the third party nominated by the issuer sends a Shareholder Identification Disclosure Request message (seev.045) to the first intermediary or to any of the intermediaries in a custody chain in order to request the disclosure of shareholders identity.

When an incoming seev.045 is received with function as NEWM, the system records the details of the message in the SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST application. The record is always created in authorised stage. The ID is prefixed with the value SRDREQ followed by 10-digit numbers.

The incoming message is processed as given below

- The International Securities Identification Number (ISIN) in the message is used to identify the SECURITY.MASTER records and populate the Security No field in the SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST application. When multiple SECURITY.MASTER records have the same ISIN, the Security No field in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST is multi-valued and populated with all the security numbers.
- The system checks whether the incoming message is received from the depository based on the value given in the Sender Bic field. If the BIC does not correspond to any depository but is a valid BIC, then it implies that the message is directly received from the issuer. In such cases the Depository field is set to ALL.
- If the system is unable to find the mandatory attributes such as the Record Date, Srd Req Id, Security No and so on in the message, the Status field is updated as ERR and the Err Reason field indicates the reason for the user to take corrective action.
- If the system has all mandatory attributes such as Record Date, Srd Req Id, Security No and so on in the message, the Status field is updated as OK.
- If there are more than one record with same Srd Req Id, Sender Bic, Record Date and I S I N . combination and if NEWM is received with same combination, then the system creates a new record in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST with the Status field updated as ERR and the Err Reason field updated as “SRD Request exist for the security”. User can choose to continue with this message by manually setting the Status field to OK. Else, user needs to manually reconcile the issue.

When an incoming seev.045 disclosure request message is received with an REPL function, it indicates that the message is sent to replace the previously sent request. Under such cases the incoming message is processed as given below:

- The system identifies the respective SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST record by comparing the previous disclosure request ID from the incoming message with the value in the Srd Req Id field. Additionally, the system checks the Sender Bic and I S I N.
- Once the respective record is identified the system overwrites the details of the existing record. The original record (before receiving REPL) moves to the history table.
- If there exists more than one record with same Sender Bic, Srd Req Id and I S I N , system creates a new record with the incoming message details and updates the Status field as ERR and updates the Err Reason field as ‘Multiple NEWM found’.
- If the system is unable to identify the record in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST , system creates a new record and updates the Status field as ERR and the Err Reason field as “REPL received no NEWM found”. User can choose to continue with this message by manually setting the Status field to OK. Else, user needs to manually reconcile the issue.

The incoming seev.046 denotes that the earlier Shareholders Identification Disclosure Request notification is being cancelled. When the incoming seev.046 is received, the system identifies the respective record in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST application based on the Srd Req Id, I S I N, Sender Bic and the Record Date . If the system can locate the record, it updates the delivery reference in the Canc Delivery Inref field in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST and update the Status field in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST to CANC. If there is any response created, the user needs to manually reverse the SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE records using the enquiry Cancelled SRD Requests (SC.SRD.REQUEST.CAN).

Shareholders Identification Disclosure Response Message is sent in response to a Shareholder Identification Disclosure Request message (seev.045) to the recipient designated by the issuer. The message provides the requested information on the identity of the shareholders and their account holdings serviced by the intermediary, for the requested financial instrument.

To generate an outward seev.047 message, the user sets the Response Gen field in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST to Yes. The system passes on the customer details to the party given in the Recipient Bic field. The respective outward delivery reference is stored in Resp Delivery Outref in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST record and the Status field is updated to RESPONDED.

In certain cases, the issuer can request to disclose the identity of shareholders holding more than a specified number of shares. These details are received in the incoming seev.045 message and is recorded in the Threshold Qty field in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST .

- If the Threshold Qty in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST is blank then the system passes on all the customer details to the party given in the Rspn Recipient Bic field.
- If the Threshold Qty in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST has a value defined, then the system compares the Threshold Qty with the Nominal field in SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE . In case if the eligible holding is lesser than the given threshold quantity, the system marks the Below Threshold field in SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE to Yes. The system passes only those customer details where the Below Threshold field in SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE is not set.

The seev.048 message is sent to cancel the shareholder identification disclosure response. When Outward Canc Gen Method is set to CANC.RESEND, the system generates an outward seev.048 under following scenarios

- In case when there is change in the overall nominals The system cancels the previously sent response by sending out seev.048 and resend a new response seev.047. The system updates the seev.048 delivery reference in the Resp Canc Outref field of the respective Resp Delivery Outref multi-value set in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST . The system also creates a new multi-value set and updates the delivery reference of the new seev.047 in the Resp Delivery Outref field in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST .
- When seev.046 is received post sending out seev.047, The user manually reverses the SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE records via enquiry Cancelled SRD Requests (SC.SRD.REQUEST.CAN). The system sends out a seev.048 message once all the SC.SRD.HLD.RESPONSE records are reversed. The system updates the seev.048 delivery reference in the Resp Canc Outref field of the respective Resp Delivery Outref multi-value set in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST . The system also updates the Status field in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST to RESPOND.CANC.

The incoming seev.049 holds the status advice for the earlier sent Shareholders Identification Disclosure Response Message (seev.047).

When an incoming seev.049 message is received, the system identifies the respective SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST record based on the Srd Req Id, Sender Bic, Record Date and I S I N . combination.

The system identifies the correct seev.047 based on the Response ID sent and updates the Response Status field in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST application with values as ACCEPTED or REJECTED.

The system updates the inward delivery reference in Resp Status Inref of the respective Resp Delivery Outref multi-value set in SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST .

- If incoming seev.049 is unable to identify the correct the SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST record, then the record in DE.I.HEADER is updated as “Repair”.
- If incoming seev.049 is able to identify the correct the SC.SRD.HLD.REQUEST record but cannot find the corresponding seev.047 outward multi-value set, the record in DE.I.HEADER is updated as “Repair" with reason as “Matching outward details not found”.


#### 📋 Tasks

The Shareholder Rights Directive II (SRD II) is a European Union (EU) directive that improves shareholder transparency and strengthens the position of shareholders trading on EU regulated markets. The SRD II Directive helps the companies to identify their shareholders. This creates an obligation on intermediaries to transmit the necessary information they hold on shareholder identity back to the issuer or company. ISO20022 messages handle the disclosure of shareholder identification in the context of the Shareholder Rights Directive II.

### 5.66  Standard Settlement Instructions

These agreements allow the related counter-parties to settle the receiving agents. SSIs play a crucial role in the end-to...*
> 
> **Applications:** `ASSET.TYPE`, `CUSTOMER`, `CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `EB.LOOKUP`, `POSITION.TRANSFER`, `SC.AGENT.PLACE`, `SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT`, `SC.CLEARING.CODE` ... +13 more
