#### 📖 Introduction

Standard Settlement Instructions (SSIs) are the agreements between two financial institutions which fix the receiving agents of each counterparty in ordinary trades of some type. These agreements allow the related counter-parties to settle the receiving agents. SSIs play a crucial role in the end-to-end treatment of a transaction to obtain the maximum level of STP.

SSI automatic determination helps to:

- Maintain high level of Straight Through Processing (STP) capabilities
- Reduce the settlement failures and hence, maintain a high level of efficiency in the quality of instructions to our custodians
- Avoid un-necessary non-STP fees at custodian or market level
- Communicate SSI-related information to our counter-parties
- Populate the instructions to the custodians

The Place of Settlement (PSET) is the final depository, where the transaction settles. PSET is one of the keys to determine the counter-party settlement instructions (SSI). Temenos Transact allows the set-up of rules to default the PSET in the transaction.

Temenos Transact allows a set-up of SSIs in advance, so when a transaction is entered, the system automatically defaults the appropriate SSI.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The below section explains the SSI setup for a broker or depository and the configuration required for PSET.


##### Setting up SSI for a Broker or Depository

To default the settlement instructions at transaction level, the following setup is needed:

Temenos Transact can define whether the system needs to apply the SSIs automatically, if the SSIs are available in the system. The Ssi Stp field indicates whether the SSI can be automatically applied for the broker or depository. When the Ssi Stp field is set to No, the SSI is defaulted (if found) but the system throws an override as ‘Ssi Stp is set to NO’ .

The Ssi Status field indicates whether the counterparty SSI status is active or deactivated. If the Ssi Status field is set to Deactivated and during transaction level if the Validity Check field is set in SC.SSI.PARAM , then the system raises an override as ‘Counterparty Ssi Status is given as Deactivated’. In such case, the system does not default the securities or cash SSI details of the broker or depository.

The SC.SSI.PARAM application defines the priority for defaulting broker or depository SSI using the Stock Exchange , ISIN Country , Place of Settlement and Security fields. In addition to the above mentioned priority list, the user can additionally define the priority based on the issuer of the security. In such cases, the system defines the priority for defaulting broker or depository SSI using the Stock Exchange , ISIN Country , Place of Settlement , Security and Issuer Grp fields.

The SSI records are searched based on the priority defaulted in the parameter and the most appropriate SSI is defaulted in security trade and transfer transactions.The user can state the priority among the Stock Exchange , ISIN Country , Place of Settlement , Security and Issuer Grp fields. For example, Stock Exchange can be priority 1, Pl Sett as 2, Security as 3, ISIN Country as 4 and Issuer Grp is 5. The priority list is built by the system as shown in the below screenshot.

The SC.SSI.PARAM application also defines the priority for defaulting broker or depository cash settlement instructions, if the Cash Ssi Process field is set to Yes. The priority is always in the following order

- Currency
- Security
- ISIN
- ISIN Group
- Sub asset type
- Asset type
- Issuer
- Issuer Group

- When Issuer Grp field has a priority number, then the Issuer field in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT and SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT are mandatory input field.
- When Issuer Grp field does not have a priority number, then the Issuer field in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT and SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT is a no input field.

Additionally, there are scenarios where several ISINs are grouped together to setup a single SSI. In such scenarios, the Isin Grp field must be set to Yes in SC.SSI.PARAM application. When this field is set to Yes, then the Asset Sub field in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT and SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT allows a valid ISIN group prefixed with ‘IG-‘. When trade is placed for a security belonging to the ISIN group, the system checks the group ID in the Ssi Isin Group field in SECURITY.MASTER and determines the appropriate SSI based on the ISIN Group.

The user can also have multiple settlement details for the same SSI combination. To allow setting up of duplicate SSI for same SSI combination in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT and SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT , the Allow Duplicate field is set to Yes in SC.SSI.PARAM application. The Validity Check field checks the validity period and status of the SSI in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT and SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT applications.

The SC.SETT.INSTRUCT application holds the standard settlement instructions for each broker. The instructions set are automatically defaulted in the SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER applications, if a particular broker is involved. Multiple SSIs can be created for a broker. The ID is a free format field. If it is a valid broker number, the system defaults the SSI instructions, where this broker is used in SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER record.

If the ID is set in the format BROKER.NO "." PORTFOLIO.NUMBER, the system first considers the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT record with the broker portfolio combination ID only for SECURITY.TRANSFER . If found, it defaults the SSI from this record. If not, it searches for a record with a broker ID and defaults from there. The users can also create free format ID records, which can be used in SECURITY.TRANSFER . The ID must be entered in the Ssi Code field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application, and the system defaults the relevant SSI Instructions from the specified record.

The value in the SSI field is defaulted based on the following combinations such as Stock Exchange , ISIN Country , Place of Settlement , Asset Sub and Issuer fields. If the Allow Duplicate field is set in SC.SSI.PARAM , then the system appends a numeric value against the SSI field in SC.SETT. INSTRUCT application when duplicate SSIs are created as shown above.The Pl Code field records the place of security settlement considering the Ssi Code , Broker Addr Bic and Broker No field priority. The Pl Safekeep field records the place of safekeep of the security considering the Ssi Code , Broker Addr Bic and Broker No field priority.

The value EXCH of the Stock Exchange field is checked for delivery against payment (DAP) transactions and FOP is checked for free of payment (FOP) transactions. The value ALL can also be set. This field also accepts a valid STOCK.EXCHANGE record and this can be set with prefix S-. The system would search for the SSI set of the specific stock exchange first, else EXCH or FOP as required.

> **⚠️ Note:** For security transfers, the stock exchange refers to the stock exchange set in SECURITY.MASTER and for trades, the stock exchange in the SEC.TRADE record.

If the Pset field is entered in SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER , the system fetches the correct SSI based on the Pset entered in SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER application. If Pset is not entered in SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER application, then system fetches the SSI based on the Pl Sett in the SECURITY.MASTER application.If the Pl Sett field is not defined in SECURITY.MASTER , the value mentioned in this field is checked against the security domicile of the security being traded or transferred. However, the domicile is checked only if Sec Domicile Ssi field in the SM.PARAMETER application is set to Yes.

The Asset Sub field accepts a valid ISIN prefixed with ‘I-‘, a valid SECURITY.MASTER ID, a valid SUB.ASSET.TYPE prefixed with ‘S-‘, a valid ASSET.TYPE prefixed with ‘A-‘ or a ISIN group prefixed with ‘IG-‘ (if the Isin Grp is set to Yes in SC.SSI.PARAM ).

The record ALL indicates the default condition for all asset, sub-asset, and security records. The ISIN Country field indicates the type of country records. If priority is set in Issuer Grp in SC.SSI.PARAM , then the Issuer field becomes a mandatory input field and allows an Issuer prefixed with ‘IS-‘ or Issuer Grp prefixed with ‘ISG-‘ or the value ALL.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Stock Exchange, Pl Sett, Asset Sub, and ISIN Country fields are mandatory for input.

The Delivering Agent , Receiving Agent , Delivering Custodian , Receiving Custodian , Buyer and Seller fields indicate the address, bank identification code or customer id in the following cases:

- If the value of this field is prefixed by A-, then address is used from the SC.AGENT.PLACE application.
- If the value of this field is prefixed by B-, then BIC address is used.
- If the value of this field is prefixed by C-, then Customer ID is used.
- If the value is prefixed with R-, then a proprietary code is used.

The Delivering Agent Account , Receiving Agent Account , Delivering Custodian Account , Receiving Custodian Account , Buyer Account and Seller Account fields hold the account numbers defaulted in the respective fields in the SEC.TRADE application.

The Validity From and Validity To fields denotes the validity period for the SS. When the Status field is set to Deactivated or if the validity is less than the system date, then the system does not check the specific SSI while defaulting at the transaction level. At the SSI level, it is possible to indicate whether the system needs to apply the SSIs automatically by setting the Ssi Stp field to Yes. When Ssi Stp field is set to No, the system still updates the SSI in the transaction with an override stating that ’STP indicator is set to No’.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Ssi Stp field can be set to Yes, only if the Ssi Stp field is set to Yes in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the broker or depository. In case when the Ssi Stp field is set to No in CUSTOMER.SECURITY , the system displays the following error 'SSI.STP.1 Invalid input when STP is not set in CustomerSec level', when the user tries to set Ssi Stp field to Yes in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT .

The SC.SETT.INSTRUCT application is also used to hold the SSI for each depository. The instructions set are automatically defaulted in POSITION.TRANSFER when the respective depository is involved. The POSITION.TRANSFER has two legs:

- One side is from where the security is moved out and
- Another is the side where the security is received

The receiving side settlement instructions is defaulted from the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT of the depository given in the Depository To field in POSITION.TRANSFER . The delivering side settlement instructions is defaulted from the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT of the depository given in the Depository From field in POSITION.TRANSFER .

A counterparty can maintain an account with the issuing bank or in some other bank. When an account is maintained with the bank, the system can directly make the payments. When the counterparty does not have an account with the bank, the system generates an external payment.

However, for the external payment (SWIFT) the funds might need to move between different banks before they reach the recipient. The SC.CASH.SSI.INSTRUCT application holds the account details of the counterparty and the intermediary bank details, if any. The ID of the application is the CUSTOMER ID of the broker or depository. If it is a valid broker number, then the system defaults the cash SSI details where this broker is used in SEC.TRADE .

The Ssi Id is combination of Currency , Asset Sub and Issuer group. If the Allow Duplicate field is set in SC.SSI.PARAM , then the system appends a numeric value against the Ssi Id field when duplicate SSIs are created (as shown in the above screenshot). The Asset Sub field accepts a valid ISIN prefixed with ‘I-‘, a valid SECURITY.MASTER ID, a valid SUB.ASSET.TYPE prefixed with ‘S-‘, a valid ASSET.TYPE prefixed with ‘A-‘ or a ISIN group prefixed with ‘IG-‘ (provided the Isin Grp is set to Yes in SC.SSI.PARAM ).

If priority is set in the Issuer Grp field in SC.SSI.PARAM , then the Issuer field becomes an input field and allows an issuer prefixed with ‘IS-‘ or Issuer Grp prefixed with ‘ISG-‘. The record ALL indicates the default condition for all currency, all asset, sub-asset, security record, ISIN and all issuer groups.

The Br Sett Acc field holds the broker account to be defaulted in SEC.TRADE based on the SSI combination. This can be a Nostro account or a customer account or internal account prefixed with ‘C-‘. If broker account is a valid Temenos Transact cash account, then the system does not allow the user to set the beneficiary bank and other details. The user can provide beneficiary and intermediary bank details through which the payment needs to be routed. The End Beneficiary field holds the details of the beneficiary details to whom the payment is to be made.

When the Validity Check field is enabled in SC.SSI.PARAM , the system makes the Validity From , Validity To and Status fields as an input field. The user can denote the validity period for the SSI. When the Status field is set to Deactivated, then the system does not check the specific SSI while defaulting at the transaction level. At the SSI level, it is possible to indicate whether the system needs to apply the SSIs automatically by setting the Ssi Stp field to Yes. When Ssi Stp is set to No, the system still updates the SSI in the transaction with an override stating ’STP indicator is set to No’.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Ssi Stp field can be set to Yes, only if the Ssi Stp field is set to Yes in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the broker or depository. The system displays an error when the user tries to set Ssi Stp field to Yes when the Ssi Stp field is set to No in CUSTOMER.SECURITY .

The SC.AGENT.PLACE application is used to setup the place of settlement or print address for agents with no customer ID in Temenos Transact or a BIC code. The Address.1 field indicates the print address of either the agent or place of settlement.


#### 🔧 Working With

In private banks, for the various products (for example, equities, bonds and ETFs), the counter-parties can play various roles like brokers or custodians. The SSI for each counter-party may change according to the role they play. Each counter-party has their own life cycle and thus, to ensure faster payments and settlements, the SSI details for each broker and depository needs to be setup.


##### Determining SSI at Transaction Level

The below explains the SSI determination for the broker, depository and PSET determination at transaction level.

| Fields in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT | Mapped to SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER |
|---|---|
| Delivering Agent | Br Agent for broker sell |
| Receiving Agent | Br Agent for broker buy |
| Delivering Custodian | Broker Depo for broker sell |
| Receiving Custodian | Broker Depo for broker buy |
| Buyer | Buyr Seller to the BUYR tag in the message, for broker buy |
| Seller | Buyr Seller to the SELL tag in the message, for broker sell |
| Delivering Agent Account | Br Agent Ac for broker sell |
| Receiving Agent Account | Br Agent Ac for broker sell |
| Buyer Account | Buyr Seller Account to the 97a SAFE tag in SETPRTY, for broker buy |
| SellerAccount | Buyr SellerAccount to the 97a SAFE tag in SETPRTY, for broker sell |
| Pset | Pset |
| Pl Code | Pl Code |
| Pl Safekeep | Pl Safekeep |

Based on the setup in the SEC.TRADE application, the SSI instructions are defaulted from the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT application after the broker is created and validated. The SSIs can also be manually amended, if required.

If the system finds the corresponding SSI for the broker, the system checks the mismatching details. If a match is not found, then the system raises an override ‘No SSI found for Sec SSI’. If a match is found, the system checks the value in the Status field of the SSI and the values in the Validity From and Validity To fields. The SSI status must be Active or null and the Trade Date field in SEC.TRADE must fall within the range defined in the Validity From and Validity To fields.

If the system finds the corresponding SSI for the broker but duplicate SSIs exist, them the system checks if the duplicate SSI is active or deactivated. If the duplicate SSI is deactivated, then the system does not raise any override else an override ‘Duplicate SSIs exists’ is raised, and no SSI details is updated by the system. The Sec Ssi Id field in SEC.TRADE holds the SSI ID selected by system for the transaction.

When the system is not able to fetch the correct SSI, the user can manually select the SSI against the Ssi Id field in SEC.TRADE . The Broker Settlement Instructions (BROK.SETT.INSTRUCT) enquiry in the Ssi Id field lists the available SSIs for the combination. The user can use the enquiry to select the SSI ID that needs to be applied. Once the Ssi Id is selected, the system defaults the SSI based on the selection.

When the transaction in SEC.TRADE is committed, a SWIFT message is generated for the customer instructing the receipt or delivery of financial instruments against payment or free of payment. The SWIFT message defaults the values from the SEC.TRADE application. The below screenshot displays the sample SWIFT message.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Br Deliv Instr | The value in this field is defaulted from the Br Del Instr field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY . The CUSTOMER.SECURITY record of the broker is referred for a default value. If unavailable, the default is obtained from the Dap Code field in SC.STD.SEC.TRADE . The instruction defaulted is defined in the SC.DEL.INSTR application. |
| Cu Deliv Instr | The value in this field is defaulted from the Dap Code field in the SC.STD.SEC.TRADE application. |
| Br Acc No | The value in this field is defaulted based on the value in the Br Deliv Instr field. If the With Payment Flag field in the respective Br Deliv Instr is set to Yes in the SC.DEL.INSTR application, the payment is routed through the Depository defined in the SEC.TRADE application. The Depository Acc field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record of the Depository in SEC.TRADE is defaulted based on the Trade Ccy field in SEC.TRADE . The account number and currency defaulted in Br Acc No and Trade Ccy in SEC.TRADE matches. If the With Payment Flag field in the respective Br Deliv Instr is set to No in the SC.DEL.INSTR application, the payment is sent or received from the broker, directly. The Br Set Acc field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the respective broker is defaulted based on the Trade Ccy field in the SEC.TRADE application. |
| Broker Depo | The default Broker Depo is obtained from the Br Def Depo field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record of the respective broker. |
| Br Sec Depot Ac | This field is defaulted from CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the broker, when the Depository and Broker Depo in SEC.TRADE are defined in the SC.CLEARING.SYSTEM and SC.STD.CLEARING with the Direct Link field in SC.CLEARING.SYSTEM set to Yes. The default is obtained for CEDEL, EUROCLEAR and SEGA. The account number of CEDEL, EUROCLEAR and SEGA must be defined in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the broker[RJ1] . |
| Br Ben Bank1 | This field is defaulted from the agency record of the broker. The default is based on the currency of the account defaulted in the Br Acc No field. |
| Trade Time | This field enables the user to enter the time of execution of the transaction. This field is in HH:MM:SS format and is defaulted from the most recent input into a Br Trade Time field. |

| Field in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT | Mapped To POSITION.TRANSFER |
|---|---|
| Delivering Agent | Deli Agent |

| Seller | Seller |
| Seller Account | Seller Ac |
| Delivering Custodian | Deli Cus |
| Delivering Custodian Account | Deli Cus Ac |
| Place Code | Deli Pl Code |
| Place Of Safekeep | Deli Pl Safekeep |

##### Defaulting the Place of Settlement in the Transaction

The place of settlement (PSET) is determined using clearing code, country code, product type, product sub-type and stock exchange.

| ID Name | Type | Length | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| ID | Alphanumeric | 20 | The possible record IDs are Broker ID. Should be a valid customer in Temenos Transact r custodian ID for transfer between custodians ( POSITION.TRANSFER ), SYSTEM (optional) If system is not able to find an exact match for the counterparty or if counterparty record does not exist in this application, the SYSTEM level record is searched. |
| Depository | Alphanumeric | 20 | Allows the Custodian ID or ALL. It should be a valid Temenos Transact customer. It is multi-value field. |
| Depository Type -XX.XX | Alphanumeric | 20 | Defaults from the corresponding field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the depository. It is an associated multi-value field with Depository |
| Asset Type -XX.XX | Alphanumeric | 20 | Holds the valid product type records from ASSET.TYPE or all records in Asset type |
| Sub Asset Type -XX.XX | Alphanumeric | 20 | Holds the valid product sub-type records from SUB.ASSET.TYPE or all records in sub asset type |
| XX.XX | Alphanumeric | 20 | Holds the valid stock exchange records from STOCK.EXCHANGE or all records in stock exchange. Applied where stock exchange is applicable. This field can also be left blank for the transactions where stock exchange is not applicable. The system checks for rule with specific stock exchange like NYSE, LSE or Blank. If the mentioned values are not found, then the system checks for all values in stock exchange |
| Clearing Code .XX | Alphanumeric | 20 | For the combination of stock exchange and clearing code fields, the clearing code can be set up in this field. Dropdown values through EB.LOOKUP to list the clearing codes that are applicable for the bank |
| Status -XX |  |  | Indicates the status of the clearing code rule. The possible values are Active or Inactive |

|---|---|---|---|

| Clearing Code | Alphanumeric | 20 | The value is defaulted from ID and it is a no input field |
| Custodian Type | Alphanumeric | 20 | The value is defaulted from ID and it is a no input field |
| Priority -XX |  |  | The values are: Stock.exchange.country Isin.country Custodian.country Zz |

|---|---|---|---|
| ID | Alphanumeric | 20 | Accept values from the EB.LOOKUP created for clearing codes or accepts the value ALL |
| Clearing Code | Alphanumeric | 20 | Defaulted from the ID and cannot be changed |

Either Asset Type or Sub Asset type can be set and not both. Valid record from ASSET.TYPE or SUB.ASSET.TYPE application should exist and both records cannot be null. |

| PSET-XX | Alphanumeric | 20 | For each clearing code + country code + asset + sub-asset type combination, the PSET that is applicable for the combination is setup in this field. |

| ID Name | Type | Length | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pset Clearing Code | Alphanumeric | 20 | Defaulted from SC.CLEARING.CODE based on the rules set up. Can also be amended by the user |
| Pset Country | Alphanumeric | 20 | Defaulted by the system based on the transaction and rule set up. Can be amended by the user |
| Pset | Alphanumeric | 20 | If the Pset Txn Dflt field is set in SC.SI.PARAM , this field is defaulted based on the Criteria in SC.PSET.RULES . This can be amended by the user |

The following steps are:

1. Where Pset Txn Dflt in SC.SSI.PARAM is set and a transaction is input, system first determines the clearing code based on the rules set up in SC.CLEARING.CODE and updates the same in the Pset Clrn Code field in the transaction.
2. Then, the system determines the Pset Country value using rules set up in SC.PSET.COUNTRY application. If country cannot be determined and default is unavailable in PSET.COUNTRY , system raises a warning that Pset Country cannot be determined. The user can provide the value manually or leave the record unauthorised, create the required tables and then revalidate the transaction. The system then picks the values.
3. Using the Pset Clrng Code and Pset Country values, system determines the PSET. If PSET cannot be determined, system raises an error or override and user has to manually provide a PSET value or revalidate the transaction after updating the SC.PSET.RULES application (user can leave the record unauthorised, create the required applications and then revalidate the transaction. The system then picks the values. For trade, if PSET is missing, the override is configured as error by the bank. The PSET available in the transaction is used to determine the SSI.
4. Defaulting of Clearing code, Country code and PSET based on the various rules is done for all transactions created manually or via swift.
5. Temenos Transact allows Pset Clrng Code or Pset Country or even PSET to be updated in the transaction directly. So, when a transaction is interfaced from some specific channel, the values can be interfaced directly in the application. If a transaction is interfaced from external source with Pset Clrng Code updated, the system uses that to determine the PSET.

If values are interfaced, the system does not try to calculate the values again unless the user changes either the security number, or stock exchange, or counterparty or depository in the transaction.

If the Pset Txn Dflt field is set as ‘Rule.or.Sm’ in SC.SSI.PARAM ,

The system tries to determine the PSET using the PSET rules table. If no PSET is found based on the rules, the PSET in Transaction is initially blank. The system tries to determine the correct PSET based on the below logic.

- If Sec Domicile Ssi in SM.PARAMETER is not set, The system checks the Pl Sett field of the respective security’s record in SECURITY.MASTER that determines the SSI for the corresponding broker or depository based on the Pl Sett value and other attributes, and defaults the SSI in the transaction. The PSET defined in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT is therefore populated in the Pset field in SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER .
- If Sec Domicile Ssi in SM.PARAMETER is set and if Pl Sett is not defined in SECURITY.MASTER , The system checks the Security Domicile field in the respective security’s record in SECURITY.MASTER that determines the SSI for the corresponding broker or depository based on the Security Domicile value, and defaults the SSI in the transaction. The PSET defined in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT is therefore populated in the Pset field in SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER . If no PSET is found, the Pset field in SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER is left blank and the system raises an override ‘Pset Not Determined Automatically From Pset Rules’.

##### Using Settlement Parties Tag Format

The Tags 95 and 97 are related to settlement parties (subsequence E1 in MT540, MT541, MT542, and MT543). These messages are settlement instructions (SSI) sent to the custodian.

Tag 95a - Party

The following qualifiers are relevant for this tag.

| Qualifier | Description | Options |
|---|---|---|
| DEAG | Delivering Agent | P, Q or R |
| REAG | Receiving Agent | P, Q or R |
| DECU | Deliverer’s Custodian | P, Q or R |
| RECU | Receiver’s Custodian | P, Q or R |
| BUYR | Buyer | P, Q or R |
| SELL | Seller | P, Q or R |

The formats are described below:

- Option P :4!c//4!a2!a2!c[3!c] (Qualifier)(Identifier Code)
- Option Q :4!c//4*35x (Qualifier)(Name and Address)
- Option R :4!c/8c/34x (Qualifier)(Data Source Scheme)(Proprietary Code)

Tag 97a – Safekeeping account

| Qualifier | Description | Options |
|---|---|---|
| SAFE | Safekeeping account | A or B |

The formats are described below:

- Option A :4!c//35x (Qualifier)(Account Number)
- Option B :4!c/[8c]/4!c/35x (Qualifier)(Data Source Scheme)(Account Type Code)(Account Number)

> **⚠️ Note:** Option B is not supported by Temenos Transact .

The tag format to be used can be defined in a configuration table in the form of rules. This definition can vary by the receiver of the SWIFT message and/or place of settlement.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| @Id | The ID is in the following format, * The place of settlement is defined in BIC (P option) format and prefixed with ’B-‘, the second part of the ID corresponds to the BIC address of the SWIFT receiver. The receiver of the SWIFT message is the bank’s Custodian. In brokerage only trades, it can also be the customer’s custodian. The allowed values are: *BIC *ALL ALL*BIC |
| Depo Bic | Defaults from @ID |
| Pset | Defaults from @ID |
| Rule Name | Indicates the name of the rule, for example Rule 1. The multi-value field starts from this field |
| Reag | The available values are: P (Option P) Q (Option Q) R (Option R) Not Allowed Optional When ’Not Allowed’ is set, this Tag or Qualifier cannot exist in the SSI. This is a mandatory field, and user has to select from the drop down list. When Optional is selected, the tag or qualifier can be in any format. |
| ReagAc | This is a mandatory field. The available values are: A (Option A) Not Allowed - cannot exist in the SSI. Optional – can exist in the SSI in any format. |
| Deag | This is a mandatory field. ### 5.67  StockReconciliation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Stock reconciliation involves the matching of Temenos Transact SECURITY.POSITION records against the depository’s position. This is done by using MT549 SWIFT messages to request a statement of holdings from the depository and matching the returned MT535 messages (that is, the statement of holdings).*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *All Depositories*, *Automatic Matching*, *Date Time From*, *Date Time To*, *Date Type*, *Depository*, *External Location*, *Globus Location* ... +25 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Stock reconciliation involves the matching of Temenos Transact SECURITY.POSITION records against the depository’s position. This is done by using MT549 SWIFT messages to request a statement of holdings from the depository and matching the returned MT535 messages (that is, the statement of holdings).

The following are the process in the stock reconciliation module:

- Generating MT549 messages
- Capturing messages for incoming SWIFT MT549
- Capturing Temenos Transact SECURITY.POSITION records in the form of a MT549 messages, diverted from the delivery process
- Holding extraction from aforementioned messages into Temenos Transact applications
- Defining controls
- Automatic matching procedure
- Manual matching procedure
- Manual holding input procedure
- On-line and batch enquiries and reports
- Controls and audit trail
- Archiving

A holding in stock reconciliation may be either from depository statements or Temenos Transact position records, which have to be matched in order to reveal reconciliation discrepancies. Each holding is independent and no other products are affected by the stock reconciliation functionality.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic details the configuration of stock reconciliation related Temenos Transact applications.


##### Stock Reconciliation Parameters

The SR.PARAMTER application records the retention and delivery data interfaces for the stock reconciliation feature. The application which contains the incoming messages are defined in the DE.SWIFT.DIVERSION application and in the External Location field (in SR.PARAMTER ).

The application name where the position (outward) messages are found, for example, the Globus Location field is set to DE.O.MSG.STKREC and the Globus Type field is set to MESSAGE.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Globus Location field excludes the F.prefix application names.

The user must setup the incoming and outgoing delivery requirements, before inputting and authorising this record.


##### Delivery Requirements - Incoming Statements

The DE.SWIFT.DIVERSION application is setup for MT535 messages as shown in the below screenshot.

The Inward File and Inward Record fields are set (as shown in the above screenshot) to divert a copy of all incoming MT535 messages to the IN record in F.SR.DIVERT. A copy of outgoing messages can be diverted for some other purpose and in that case, the user must leave the Outward File and Outward Record fields unchanged. The outward related fields are mandatory and the values are defaulted as shown in the above screenshot. Generic carrier is used to capture outgoing records for reconciliation.

The SWIFT carrier must be running, in order to divert the messages to the diversion application.


##### Delivery requirements - Position messages

Each depository for automatic reconciliation must be setup to generate daily statements in the form of MT535. Delivery controls and formats the messages, and passes them to a generic carrier to be handed on to the reconciliation system.

The DE.INTERFACE application must be setup with the ID of the carrier for stock reconciliation. A model record is released with the application.

The messages to this interface are written to the F.DE.O.MSG.STKREC application. The name of this application must be entered in the SR.PARAMETER record, to notify the statement decoding process for message locations.

The DE.CARRIER application must be setup to define the carrier to which the MT535 messages are routed. A model record is released with the application. The DE.CARRIER record setup for stock reconciliation is shown in the below screenshot.

The DE.ADDRESS must be setup for each depository for the STKREC carrier. The DE.ADDRESS record defined for a specific carrier is shown in the below screenshot.

A new deliver carrier for stock reconciliation must be defined in the Outward Carrier field as STKREC in the DE.PARM record, as shown in the below screenshot.

The DE.PRODUCT application is setup for reconciling each depository in order to send the statement messages to the stock reconciliation carrier and the statement requests to SWIFT.

The DE.PRODUCT record setup for a request for statement is shown in the below screenshot.

The DE.PRODUCT record setup for statement of holdings is shown in the below screenshot.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the various processes involved in the working of stock reconciliation feature.


##### Statement Requests

A SWIFT MT549 message must be sent to the depository for which reconciliation has to be performed. This message request can be performed either automatically or on an adhoc basis.


##### Automatic Request

The CUSTOMER.SECURITY record pertaining to the depository for reconciliation must have the Reqon Freq field setup with a frequency. With this setup, the COB Batch record (BNK/SC.BATCH.RECON), automatically sends the MT549 request message. The user can specify a particular report format required in the Date Type field. The values in this field can be:

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| TRADE | Denotes the positions that comprise the trades up to and including the statement date. |
| VALUE | Denotes the positions that comprise the trades for value up to and including the statement date, This basis is the same as the CONTR format in SWIFT. |

Currently, the system does not support the ACTUAL and BOOKD SWIFT formats. Although all mandatory fields within the message type are reported, the optional fields for which all valid codes are not available and are not supported.

This screenshot illustrates a typical setup for generating MT549 statements, comprising trade-dated positions on a daily basis.


##### Manual Request

The SR.STATEMENT.REQUEST application generates a manual or adhoc request. This application allows a more specific request for performing reconciliation, if required. The following are the allowed options:

- All securities must be configured in a specified sub-account (as explained above) and a valid sub-account must be entered in the Sub Account field.
- A list of securities in all sub-accounts (as explained above) and use the Security Code multi-value fields to add the security codes and the Sec Sub Account field is left blank.
- A list of securities specified in sub-accounts (as explained above) and use the Security Code multi-value field to add the security codes and setup the Sec Sub Account field as required.

In the above example, a SWIFT MT549 message requesting a statement of holdings is sent to the EUROCLEAR depository for the period ending 27 AUG 2004. The request is specific for all sub-accounts, but the particular security code 000001-000 is required.

The Statement Period allows any date to be entered, but for trade dated reconciliation only the current bank date is allowed. The statement request process sends a SWIFT MT549 message to the depository and simultaneously updates the Temenos Transact SECURITY.POSITION records. This record is used for reconciliation against the returned MT535.

The following SWIFT message is generated for the depository, based on the above SR.STATEMENT.REQUEST .


##### MT535 Message Capture

Messages in the format of MT535s can be generated from the SECURITY.POSITION application to update the holdings. These messages are suppressed and not sent to SWIFT.

Within Temenos Transact , the Delivery module performs the function of mapping and formatting the messages for the delivery of outgoing and incoming messages either by SWIFT or through other proprietary transfer mechanisms. The Delivery module captures the incoming and outgoing messages. When the incoming message from the depository is received, the following MT535 message is diverted from the SWIFT out queue and it is used in the matching process comparison.


##### Holding Extraction

The SR.HOLDINGS application is entered on a composite key comprising a:

- Depository code
- Sub-account
- Security code
- Position indicator (P stands for the Temenos Transact position and S stands for the depository statement position)
- Statement date

These items are extracted from the SWIFT MT535 message. The sub-account is extracted from the Sub Account field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application, whereas the message contains the value from the Sub Acc Ext Id field. The security code is the ID to the SECURITY.MASTER application, whereas the message contains the ISIN code.


##### Automatic Matching

Automatic matching is performed if the statement date, depository, sub-account, security code and quantity of two items match, where the indicator is different.

> **⚠️ Note:** A record with a P indicator is matched only to an item with S indicator.

As explained above, the statements are received, extracted and transferred to the SR.HOLDINGS applications. Automatic and manual matching processes are available for the user once COB and SOD processes are completed successfully. The automatic matching is run for either one or all accounts. Two items are matched, if the statement date, depository, sub-account, security code and quantity match and the indicator is different.


##### Manual Matching

The concept of reconciliation is not required if all items have matching correspondent items. If the items do not necessarily have a corresponding matching item, then this process needs user intervention.

When automatic matching is not possible, an enquiry lists the unmatched items available for manual matching.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is assumed that the automatic matching process matches a large percentage of holdings. However, there might be occasions where a match cannot be performed resulting in some unmatched items on the system. These unmatched items require some user intervention (by the stock reconciliation department), to match the items successfully.

> **⚠️ Note:** Items are matched only to a single item.


##### Match Revoke Procedure

Matches achieved manually may be incorrect. In such instances, the user performs the following steps to revoke the matching process:

1. Clears the Matched To field in one of the items
2. Validates the transaction
3. Thus, the matched counterpart are reset to a status of unmatched

> **⚠️ Note:** This is possible only when the match is not authorised.


##### Manual Holding Input

On certain instances, statements may be received with missing pages and the depository may send these to the bank by some means other than SWIFT. When this is done, , the holdings may be manually entered into the SR.HOLDINGS applications through the holdings input application. The matching items details are captured through the take-on process and automatic matching takes place for those items. This facility caters to the correspondent banks that do not transmit the statements by SWIFT. The data is entered into the holdings for automatic matching.


##### Online Enquiries and Reports

Interlinked within Temenos Transact , the ENQUIRY application enables the user to create their own online enquiries and reports as per their requirements.


##### Archiving

All holdings are retained in the SR.HOLDINGS application for a period of time which is determined by a parameter. The transfer of live SR.HOLDINGS records to an archive table on disk or any other media, safeguards the historical data and keeps the item record tidy, thereby enhancing the performance. Both matched and unmatched holdings are transferred to archive. The archive process is run as part of the COB batch processing and transfers only those items that are matched and has exceeded the specified retention period. These items are available for online enquiry and reporting purposes, even after the items are transferred to the archive table.


##### Processing the Holdings

This topic explains the processing of stock reconciliation holdings.

The SR.DECODE record in the TSA.SERVICE application is a process to convert the inward (MT535 message received from the depository) and outward (MT535 created by Temenos Transact for reconciliation purposes) messages. This application creates the records in the SR.HOLDINGS application.

The ’IN’ record in the SR.DIVERT table in the back-end, contains the message text of statements from correspondents. The sender’s address and the account identifier are compared with the appropriate fields in the DE.SWIFT.ADDRESS to find the local depository number.

The F.DE.O.MSG.XXX record (for example, xxx is STKREC) contains the message text of the position information in MT535 format in Temenos Transact .

The purpose of reconciliation is to identify the differences between statement and position. In order to perform this, the corresponding items are matched and the the balance is the differences. The following are the two phases of matching:

- Automatic - Performed by the system.
- Manual - Performed when user intervention is required (for example, sub-account or quantity differences).

Automatic matching may be run for a selected depository or depositories or for all depositories by verifying a record in the SR.AUTOMATCH.MT571 application.

Once the SR.AUTOMATCH.MT571 records are verified, the automatic matching process is performed by running the TSA.SERVICE agents TSM and SR.AUTOMATCH.SERVICE.

The SR.HOLDINGS application contains the records for each statement or position entry. Holdings are matched by entering the ID of one of its matching item in the Matched To field. The process of manual matching is explained in the below screenshot.

To revoke a match, the user must change the Matched To field to blank. Then, both sides of the match becomes unmatched. But, this is possible only when the match is unauthorised. The un-matching items in the SR.HOLDINGS application is shown in the below screenshot.

This facility can be used for easy input of paper statements. It may also be used for the following:

- Correction of statements on which errors are detected .
- For a missing page where a re-transmission is not possible.

The statement may be inputted either partially or completely. The statement input in the SR.HOLDINGS application is shown in the below screenshot.

If a holding is input, the user can make changes to the SR.HOLDINGS record until it is authorised. Once the record is authorised, the only field that may be input is the Matched To field. The input correction in the SR.HOLDINGS application is shown in the below screenshot.


##### Daily workflow

The COB batch process generates the position information or internal statements in the MT535 format. Most correspondents send the statements from their EOD process. This means that, they arrive during the working day depending on the difference in time zones.

The EB.PHANTOM process statement decodes the messages into SR.HOLDINGS records and are shut down before the EOD backups and then restarted when the system is back online. This process can be performed by the system operator or by someone in the stock reconciliation department.

Automatic matching can be run any time during the online day. The idle time to run the automatic matching are:

- All accounts - Start of the day.
- An account for which the user receives a statement - During the day.


##### Statement of Transactions

An MT536 is sent by an account servicing institution to an account owner or its designated agent. It provides the details of increase and decrease in the holdings (that is, complete list of individual transactions) done for a portfolio over a specified period of time.

A bank can act as:

- An account servicing institution towards its custody customers
- An account owner where the account is managed by a local custodian or a clearing house

In the former role the system generates an outbound MT536 message and in the latter role the system processes the inbound MT536 message for reconciliation purposes. Temenos Transact can be configured to generate outbound MT536 messages (as an account servicing institution). However, it cannot process inbound MT536 messages, as an account owner. Temenos Transact provides a facility to generate outbound MT536 messages on a periodical basis (on a set frequency) or on demand. It is also possible to generate reversal MT536 messages. To activate this functionality, the following setup must be carried out.

The Produce Mt536 field in SC.PARAMETER record must be set to YES. Additionally, if there is any cap on the maximum number of transactions that can be carried per message, then it needs to be specified in Mt536 Max No Txns field.

The MT536 is generated at the portfolio level and it is mandatory to set the frequency so that the system can generate MT536 messages. The below screenshot shows the SEC.ACC.MASTER application with frequency set.

Once the above mentioned setup is done, the system automatically records all the necessary information for all the transactions for the particular portfolio. The following are the two ways in which the statements can be generated on a set frequency or on demand.

During COB processing, the system selects the portfolios for which statement generation is due and then automatically generates a MT536 message containing a complete list of transactions that are done during the statement period. It also creates a new record in the SC.MT536.INSTRUCT application with the Statement Type field set to SCHEDULE, for every portfolio processed. It also automatically cycles the dates in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application according to the frequency.

The below screenshot shows a sample record generated as a part of COB on the frequency date.

The SC.MT536.INSTRUCT application is used to generate the statement requests on demand (adhoc). The user can input the portfolio ID for which an ad-hoc statement is to be generated. The values in the Date Time From and Date Time To field indicates the required statement period. The date fields in SC.MT536.INSTRUCT does not accept a date greater than current system date. The below screenshot is a sample record setup for generating ad-hoc statements on the frequency date.

When a MT536 is generated either through a COB processing or ad-hoc basis, it is generated only for the customer. But if there is a requirement that, a customer’s multiple MT536 must be sent to different interested parties, then the valid SWIFT id’s ( DE.ADDRESS in SWIFT format) of those interested parties must be specified in the Mt536 Recipients field in SEC.ACC.MASTER . This field can be multi-valued to give multiple SWIFT ID’s. Also, if no recipient is specifiedthe only one message is generated for the customer. The below screenshot shows the field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER record, with a valid SWIFT ID ( DE.ADDRESS in SWIFT format).

Temenos Transact allows to reverse only the latest statement for the portfolio. Cancellation can be done by selecting the latest statement for the portfolio in SC.MT536.INSTRUCT and then reversing the particular record. Upon reversal, the system automatically generates a MT536 message with relevant tags indicating reversal of the statement.

To generate an MT536 message online, it is necessary to run the following service record available for the company. (If the company is BNK, it is necessary to run BNK/SC.MT536.DELIVERY service). The below screenshot shows a sample of MT536 message in SWIFT format.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Perform Stock Reconciliation
- Trading Processes

Stock reconciliation involves matching the security positions held in the system against the depository’s position. This is achieved by using MT549 SWIFT messages to request a statement of holdings from the depository and matching the returned MT535 messages, that is, the statement of holdings.

A holding in stock reconciliation can be either from depository statements or security positions files, which have to be matched to reveal reconciliation discrepancies.

The stock reconciliation functionality in core banking system covers the following:

- Generation of MT549 messages for Statement Request
- Capture of security position records in the form of MT535 messages.
- Capture of incoming statements via S.W.I.F.T. MT535 messages.
- Statement extraction from aforementioned messages into files in the system
- Automatic Matching
- Manual Matching
- Manual Position Capture
- On-line and Batch Enquiries and Reports

### 5.68  StraightThroughProcessing(SWIFT)


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The set of ISO 15022 messages supported by SWIFT Straight Through Processing (STP) is the next step in the evolution of banking systems for the securities industry. ISO 15022 is the messaging standard supported by SWIFT for the securities industry. It is in response to market demand for STP. It repl...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Advice Index*, *Aggr Version*, *Eb Class Type*, *Exe Hlt*, *In Dir Rtn*, *In Queue Dir*, *Msg Type*, *Out Queue Dir* ... +5 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The set of ISO 15022 messages supported by SWIFT Straight Through Processing (STP) is the next step in the evolution of banking systems for the securities industry. ISO 15022 is the messaging standard supported by SWIFT for the securities industry. It is in response to market demand for STP. It replaces the following ISO 7775 standards:

- Scheme for Message Types and ISO 11521
- Scheme for Inter-Depository Message Types

The ISO 15022 series of messages replaced the ISO 7775 series of messages from November 2002 onwards. The ISO 15022 series of messages facilitates a T+1 (trade date + 1) settlement scenario.

STP is an initiative used by companies in the financial world to optimise the speed at which transactions are processed. This is performed by allowing information that has been electronically entered to be transferred from one party to another in the settlement process without manually re-entering the same pieces of information repeatedly over the entire sequence of events.


##### Product Configuration

The following parameter files are configured for SWIFT STP feature.

The SP.STP.PARAM parameter application drives the STP functionality. The application facilitates the controlling of STP in separate components. The components of STP are the SWIFT messages, which are controlled by the securities STP module. All the components of STP are to be selected, if a full STP system is to be installed. As there might be a requirement for partial STP (for example, settlement is controlled through STP and order processing is done manually), the SP.STP.PARAM can be setup accordingly to suit the business requirement.

The ID of SP.STP.PARAM is the company ID. Each company has a separate parameter record.

An OFS.SOURCE record is to be setup as shown in the below screenshot. This OFS.SOURCE record defines the In Queue Dir , Out Queue Dir and the In Dir Rtn fields.

A record must be setup in EB.PHANTOM as shown in the below screenshot.

Read OFS User Guide for more information OFS.SOURCE and EB.PHANTOM applications.

The Sc Class Type and Eb Class Type fields in SC.PARAMETER must be updated as shown in the below screenshot.

The Sc Class Type is the internal class used in the SC module. The Sc Class Type and Eb Class Type provides the class mapping between internal securities classes and EB.MESSAGE.CLASS . The Eb Class Type allows a valid EB.MESSAGE.CLASS record to be input. The EB.MESSAGE.CLASS must be used in the EB.ADVICES record. This facilitates the addition of new mapping records locally for each activity.

With the above setup, all the inward messages is processed and the respective applications are updated and authorised.

Delivery address is maintained for specific portfolio in DE.ADDRESS . The address can be set for each carrier (like email, print, sms, SWIFT). For each carrier, a new record can be created in DE.ADDRESS and the appropriate address (BIC in case of SWIFT carrier, physical address in case of print carrier) can be setup in this application as shown below.

The carriers can be configured for each portfolio in DE.PRODUCT application. In the DE.PRODUCT application, new records are created for specific portfolio that is DE.PRODUCT specific to the SEC.ACC.MASTER records. The delivery address is linked to specific portfolio, by mapping DE.PRODUCT in the Advice Index field of the respective SEC.ACC.MASTER portfolio. Read Product table (DE.PRODUCT) for more information on Delivery Message.

The portfolio 50060-1 is mapped to SCP1 in DE.PRODUCT as shown in the below screenshots.

In a full STP order process, orders are placed and executed. Thus, the trades are created in LIVE status automatically. However, there may be scenarios where it is required to amend market settlement instructions, broker fees and or non-standard value date and so on. In such cases, it is possible to halt the STP process to allow manual intervention.

It is possible to parameterise this at CUSTOMER.SECURITY level for specific brokers or at SECURITY.MASTER level for specific securities. It is also possible to set this at the time of order creation (that is, at SEC.OPEN.ORDER level) or even at execution stage (that is, in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS level). The following two fields are available in all the above applications and can be set as required:

- Exe Hlt - Indicates whether to halt the execution and raise an override. If this field is set, the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record is left in Hold status, irrespective of the STP inward confirmation being received. Users can make amendments and then authorise the record.
- Trade Hlt - Indicates if the automatic trade authorisation is to be halted. “If this is set, the SEC.TRADE record is left in IHLD status, irrespective of the inward confirmation being received through STP. Users can make amendments and then authorise the record.

> **⚠️ Note:** In SEC.OPEN.ORDER application, these fields are populated from the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record of the broker (if it is available) or else from the SECURITY.MASTER record. The fields in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS are populated from the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The model parameters for Straight Through Processing are explained below:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Msg Type | Allows 502, 509, 513, 514, 515, 544, 545, 546, 547, 549, 576 messages |
| Aggr Version | Accepts the version record used to authorize SP.AGGREGATION through STP |
| Recon Version | Accepts the version record used to authorize SP.RECONCILIATION through STP |
| Trade Version | Accepts a version record that is used to authorise SEC.TRADE as a part of aggregated MT515 |
| Settle Version | Accepts a version record that is used to authorise SC.SETTLEMENT as a part of aggregated MT545 or MT547 |

Specific record in OFS.SOURCE need to be setup to define the In Queue Dir , Out Queue Dir and In Dir Rtn which enables STP.

Model products are not applicable for this module.

>

> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The structured note is a debt security issued Financial Institutions (FI). Its return is based on the equity indexes, single equity, basket of equities, interest rates, commodities or foreign currencies. The return on a structured note is linked to the performance of the underlying asset, group of assets or index. The structured notes are handled in the Securities (SC) module in Temenos Transact .


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The SECURITY.MASTER and SC.NOTE.PRICE.BARRIER.TYPE records are configured for structured notes.


##### SECURITY.MASTER

A structured note is defined as a security in the SECURITY.MASTER application. The existing SECURITY.MASTER (SM) fields are used for the standard attributes of a structured note.

For example, Issue date, maturity date (for perpetual notes, this field is blank), sub classification (sub asset type), coupon (where applicable), price (last price to be used for MTM valuation), price type (whether the price is a unit price or a percentage of the nominal or a discount to the face value or yield), day basis for calculating accrued interest or coupon amounts, currency, minimum investment, multiples (trading units), etc.

The existing Asset Type and Sub Asset Type fields classify and sub-classify notes, respectively.

Apart from the standard attributes, structured notes have specific characteristics. These are recorded using the fields below.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Structure Notes | Indicates whether the instrument belongs to structure notes |
| Issuer Name | Indicates the issuer name (if any) even without an issuer customer record |
| Option Strategy | Indicates the option strategy linked to the structured product. This attribute is applicable to all variants. |
| Underlying | Indicates the link to the SECURITY.MASTER ID, which is the underlying for the note |
| Other Underlying | Indicates the other underlying (apart from the security) such as the currency, commodity, index, currency ID, DX.CONTRACT.MASTER ID or any free format definition for the underlying. For other underlying, the system does not track spot price changes (such as comparison with strike, stop loss and knock-out prices and the like) for generating status reports. |
| Underlying Description | Indicates the short name from SECURITY.MASTER (underlying securities or free format description) |
| Market Identifier | Indicates the market identifier. If the underlying is the SECURITY.MASTER ID, the market identifier is ISIN. |
| Spot Price | Indicates the spot price of the underlying. This is provided by the issuer and is not automatically updated based on the Last Price in SECURITY.MASTER . |
| Weight | Indicates the weight of each underlying. If a single underlying is linked to a note, the weight is assumed as 100%. In case of multiple underlying instruments (basket), this weight is of each underlying. The total weight should be 100%. |
| Price Barrier Type | Indicates the record ID from SC.NOTE.PRICE.TYPE to denote whether the price is issue price, strike price, barrier, knock-out, bonus level, coupon strike level, or airbag level. As the records are user-defined, any type of price or barrier information can be recorded. |
| Price Percentage | Indicates the price percentage for the automatic update of the price or barrier level based on the spot price (provided there is a single underlying). |
| Note Price Barrier | Indicates the issue, strike price or barrier as specified above, which is manually or auto calculated. |
| Reset Date | Indicates the date on which barrier levels is reset (for example, stop-loss price for mini-futures is reset by the calculation agent). This is generally the last day of the month. If the last day is not a working day, then the next business day is considered. The values in this field depend on the value in the Reset Frequency field. Any changes to the stop-loss price is communicated to the customer. |
| Reset Frequency | Indicates the frequency of reset date rollover |
| Pr Trigger | Indicates the onset of the trigger |
| Pr Trigger Date | Indicates the date on which the event is triggered |
| Worst Of | Indicates whether worst-of feature is applicable for these multiple underlying instruments. |
| Investment Date | Indicates the date from which the note is available for investment (earliest). If this date is not specified, issue date is considered. Any transactions involving the note prior to this date results in a system override. |
| Fixing Date | Indicates the date (number of days prior to maturity) when the fixing is done to determine the payout. Any payout processed before this date results in a system override. |
| Digital | Indicates if this instrument is a digital variant of principal protected product. |
| All In Cost | Indicates the percentage of the investment amount, which is the all-in-cost applicable to the product. This covers the financing cost, issuance cost and so on. |
| All In Cost Basis | Indicates whether the all in cost is part of the issue price. The values are: Inclusive - All in cost is a part of the issue price. The system calculates and stores it at the trade level for information purpose only. Exclusive - All in cost is not a part of the issue price. It is calculated and posted in Cu Misc Fees field of the trade to be posted. |
| All In Cost Issuer | Indicates whether the all in cost is calculated for the issuer (broker or counterparty) side of the trade and posted in Br Misc Fees field. |
| Price Tracker | Indicates how the spot price of the underlying is monitored against the barrier levels. If this field is set to MATURITY, the knock-out or barrier comparison is done at maturity. If it is set to CONTINUING, the knock-out or barrier is tracked throughout the life cycle. |
| Leverage | Indicates the leverage applicable for products. For example, the values 1 to 4X denotes the leverage applicable for products like mini futures. |
| Effective Leverage | Indicates the effective leverage which is auto-calculated based on the values in the Spot Price and Issue Price fields (Spot/Issue = nX) |
| Capital Protection | Indicates the percentage of the protected capital |
| Participation Level | Indicates the participation level on the upside over strike |
| Downside Participation | Indicates whether the investor receives the invested amount and the percentage in the downside movement of the underlying. This is applicable for a product like twin-win certificate. |
| Cap | Identifies the percentage above strike, which is used to cap the maximum returns. |
| Rebate | Indicates the percentage above strike received by the investor. This is applicable only with a knock-out feature (on principal protected products). |
| Cpn Observe Dt | Indicates the capital protection notes with coupon to specify the dates on which, the coupon is observed to check for cap or floor levels. |
| Cpn Observe Fqu | Indicates whether the coupon observation date is auto rolled over. If the date happens to be a holiday, the rollover is to the next business day. |
| Cpn Cap | Identifies the cap rate of coupon applicable for capital protection notes with coupon |
| Cpn Floor | Identifies the floor rate of coupon for capital protection notes |
| Cpn Range Start | Indicates the start of the range for range accrual notes product (for example, if the Euro Interbank Offer Rate (Euribor) is in the range of 2 to 3% on all days, then coupon rate is 5% for which, this field is set as two). |
| Cpn Range End | Indicates the end of the range for range accrual notes product (for example, if the Euribor is in the range of 2 to 3% on all days, then coupon rate is 5% for which, this field is set as 3) |
| Coupon Reference | Indicates the reference for annual coupon (for example, 3 month Euribor) |
| Memory | Indicates whether a memory feature is applicable for memory notes |
| Pay Out Formula | Indicates whether the payout amount is calculated manually or based on routine indicated in the Pay out Routine field (at either SM level or sub asset type level). For products like mini futures, a formula can be specified, which is a term sheet element but not used for any calculation. |
| Pay Out Routine | The routine to calculate the payout details and update SC.NOTE.PAYOUT |
| Credit Event | Indicates the credit event. |
| Cr Event Triggered | Indicates whether the credit event occurred or not |
| Cr Trigger Date | Indicates the date of the credit event |
| Cr Recovery Rate | Indicates the percentage of the initial investment received by the investor, in case of principal default credit event. |

> **⚠️ Note:** Some of these attributes are applicable only for specific products and are not defined for other products or variants. There is no system validation for the allowed or not allowed status of the fields based on the products.


##### SC.NOTE.PRICE.BARRIER.TYPE

Each structured note can have different prices and barriers. The prices can vary from the issue price, strike price, barriers, knock-out and stop loss prices.

For the various prices, barriers or levels (stop loss, knock-out, knock-in, barrier, airbag, coupon strike, issue price, strike price, and so on) a record is created in SC.NOTE.PRICE.BARRIER.TYPE . It specifies what it relates to (the ID is stop loss, knock out, strike, issue, bonus level, and so on.) and its description. The SC.NOTE.PRICE.BARRIER.TYPE ID is linked to SECURITY.MASTER using the Price Barrier Type and Price Percentage fields.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with the working mechanism of structured notes in Temenos Transact .


##### Trade

The structured notes transaction (trade) is captured in the SEC.TRADE application to record the details of trade in equities and fixed income securities. The issue price determines the investment (consideration) amount and is updated in the existing Price field in SEC.TRADE .

These fields are updated either from SECURITY.MASTER or can be user-defined. For the details of other instrument attributes (underlying, barriers, caps, participation, etc.), the users can access the SECURITY.MASTER .


##### Triggers and Fixing

For structured notes, Temenos Transact supports:

- Recording of instrument or trade attributes
- Booking and management of customer holding
- Accounting reporting and valuation.
- Life cycle management and notification of triggers (like, stop-loss, knock-out and barrier) are managed externally and interfaced to Temenos Transact .

The following fields in SECURITY.MASTER notify if a stop-loss, knock-in, knock-out or barrier has been triggered.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Pr Trigger | Indicates if there is a breach of the associated price barrier. This field is display-only. The values are YES and NO. |
| Pr Trigger Date | Indicates the date of the price barrier breach |
| Cr Even Triggered | Indicates the occurrence of the credit event specified in the Credit Event field |
| Cr Trigger Date | Indicates the date on which on which the credit event has occurred |
| Price Barrier Type | Indicates a valid record in SC.NOTE.PRICE.BARRIER.TYPE . The price barriers could be KNOCK OUT, STOP LOSS, BONUS LEVEL and so on. |

These fields can be multi-valued if more than one event (price level) is triggered. For example, if a knock in the price level is triggered, a cap level can also be reached. For knock-outs and barriers tracked only at maturity, the system raises an override if the Pr Trigger field is set to YES before the fixing date.


##### Pay-out

The pay-out processing involves the SC.NOTE.PAYOUT record and DIARY application.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Description | Indicates the description of the structured note instrument. This field defaults from SECURITY.MASTER . This is a display-only field. |
| Diary Type | Indicates a valid record in the DIARY.TYPE record |
| Issue price | Indicates the issue price of the structured note. The value in this field defaults from the Issue Price field in SECURITY.MASTER . This is a display-only field. |
| Strike Price | Indicates the strike price for the underlying equity. The value in this field defaults from the Strike Price field in SECURITY.MASTER . This is a display-only field. |
| Underlying | Indicates the underlying for the note defaulted from SECURITY.MASTER . This is a display-only field. |
| Maturity Price | Indicates the rice of the associated underlying at the time of pay-out. The value in this field defaults from the Last Price field in SECURITY.MASTER . This is a display-only field. |
| Cap Protection | Indicates the percentage of the capital. The value in this field defaults from the Last Price field in SECURITY.MASTER . This is a display-only field. |
| Cap | Indicates the percentage above strike used to cap the maximum returns. The value in this field defaults from the Cap field in SECURITY.MASTER . This is a display-only field. |
| Participation Level | Indicates the participation level on the upside over strike. The value in this field defaults from the Participation Level field in SECURITY.MASTER . This is a display-only field. |
| Knock Out Barrier | Indicates if the knock out barrier is allowed or not |
| Rebate | Indicates he percentage above strike that the investor receives for knock-out. The value in this field defaults from the Rebate field in SECURITY.MASTER . This is a display-only field. |
| Coupon Rate | Indicates the rate at which the coupon is payed out. This field is mandatory for the COUPON event and is mapped to the Rate field in DIARY application. |
| Payout Price | Indicates the price at which the note is redeemed. If a pay out routine is defined for this instrument or Sub Asset Type , the value is either defaulted based on the routine logic or manually updated. This field is mandatory for the REDEMPTION event and is mapped to the Rate field in DIARY application. |
| Payout Underlying Price | Indicates the price at which the underlying is paid out. This field is mandatory for the CONVERSION event and is mapped to the New Price field in DIARY application. |
| Underlying Old Ratio | Indicates the ratio to covert the note to the underlying stock. This field is mandatory for the CONVERSION event and is mapped to the Old Ratio field in DIARY application. |
| Underlying New Ratio | Indicates the ratio to covert the note to the underlying stock. This field is mandatory for the CONVERSION event and is mapped to the New Ratio field in DIARY application. |

Based on the fixing details entered, the system automatically creates a DIARY (with payment date as the date in the record ID) and process entitlements for all the eligible holdings. All the other processing such as valuation, fees and so on are similar to any other security trade.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Structured Notes feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Structured Notes feature.

### 5.70  ThirdPartyCustody(ExternalPositions)


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
