#### 📖 Introduction

There are many situations where the bank has to deny a transaction or prompt to seek approval from a suitable higher authority.

Some examples are as follows:

- Customers has specifically stated that he does not want to trade in certain stocks as they are against his risk tolerance or due to his personal beliefs and so on. For example, not wishing to trade in tobacco stocks.
- The transaction has deviated from the bank’s policy.
- Regulatory restrictions.

Trading constraints can be set in Temenos Transact using the following applications:

- RESTRICTION and SC.SECURITY.CONSTRAINT - Works only for SEC.OPEN.ORDER , SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER and POSITION.TRANSFER .
- EB.GC.CONSTRAINTS . Works for any application.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Restrictions configuration is recorded in the SC.PARAMETER and AM.PARAMETER applications. The relevant settings are described below:

- SC.PARAMETER - The Constraint Failure field indicates that the system must stop testing restrictions after the first violation is found. The input value can be either SINGLE or MULTIPLE. If MULTIPLE is input, the program cycle through all error conditions until all restrictions are tested, therefore giving the user a chance to view all errors before taking action to fix them.
- AM.PARAMETER - To test holdings restrictions, the minimum requirements are to have the RESET.POSITION and SET.POSITION routines parameterised in the Set Pos Rtn field.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains how trading constraints can be set using the RESTRICTION and SC.SECURITY.CONSTRAINT methods.


##### RESTRICTION

This application is used to setup relationships between certain customers, portfolios, accounts or all customers and trading restrictions. This allows certain transactions to search through this application and obtain the lists of restrictions ( SC.SECURITY.CONSTRAINT ) which apply to that transaction.

Restrictions are not to be confused with asset allocation guidelines or models for investment management. They are compliance related rules that must be tested to prove that the bank is not acting against the customer’s wishes, mandate, risk tolerance, bank policy or regulatory restrictions.Restrictions can be applied to different customers or groups of customers. Defining these customer groups depends on the business needs of various area of a bank. For example, a department or service or a particular manager. A single customer may belong to different groups or have his own unique rules.

The ID format of this application is KEYTYPE.PRODUCT:

- PRODUCT - This is a valid Temenos Transact product located in the EB.PRODUCT application. However, it is currently only applicable to SC.
- KEYTYPE - Four different types of ID can be entered and they are as follows:

| ID Type | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| ALL | All transactions are applicable to this group of restrictions | ALL.SC |
| CUSTOMER | This group of restrictions applies only to this customer number | 100113 |
| PORTFOLIO | This group of restrictions applies only to this portfolio | 100113-1 |
| ACCOUNT | This group of restrictions applies only to this account number | 18934 |

If a customer, portfolio or account restrictions are entered, the following screen format appears:

The following are two types of restriction:

- BATCH - Used when the system is in BATCH mode, usually during the COB procedure.
- ONLINE - Used during normal operation of the system.

The restriction(s) can be limited to a date range or if the dates are omitted the restriction(s) remains valid until the record is updated accordingly.

If the Application field is populated the restriction is limited to the application(s) entered. If this field is left blank, the restriction(s) applies to all applications. The Restriction field is mandatory and contains a user defined ID which indicates the restriction(s) that applies must meet all the selection criteria. The field must start with R-. The field is sub-valued to allow multiple restrictions to be applied to the selection criteria.


##### AM.ENTITY

Modelling analysis portfolio positions on different axis (view) are based on basic data. This basic data (also named attribute) is defined in AM.ENTITY . Depending on the type of the position (security, account and so on) the basic information is extracted from a different file using different fields.

For example, the currency for an account is the value in the Currency field in the ACCOUNT application, but the currency for a security is the value in the Security Currency field in the SECURITY.MASTER application. Thus, the AM.ENTITY application allows the user to define for each type of position and how the system gets the information.


##### SC.SECURITY.CONSTRAINT

This application is used to configure trading restrictions for certain applications like SEC.TRADE , SEC.OPEN.ORDER , SECURITY.TRANSFER and POSITION.TRANSFER. But if the user does not want the check to happen in all these applications, they can specify them one by one. The ID of the record can be:

| Priority | ID | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Security Master | If the ID is a security number, the restrictions are applied only to that security. | 000001-000 |
| 2 | Domicile | If the ID is D-US, the restrictions are applied to all securities that have US in the Security Domicile field. | D-US |
| 3 | Local Reference | If the ID is L-10, restrictions are applied to all customers that have a particular local reference field equal to 10. The local reference field concerned is identified in the Product Type field in the SC.PARAMETER application. | L-10 |
| 4 | Sub Asset Type | If the ID is S-301, the restrictions are applied to all securities that have a Sub.Asset.Type of 301 | S-301 |
| 5 | Asset Type | If the ID is A-10, the restrictions are applied to all securities that have an ASSET.TYPE of 10 | A-10 |
| 6 | Restriction | If the IS is R-CCYGT30, the restrictions are applied to all security holdings that has an individual currency holding more than 30%. | R-CCYGT30 |

Override is displayed in a restriction constraint, if any currency total is greater than 30% of the portfolio holding. This shown in the below screenshot.


##### Creating various sorts of Restrictions

The restrictions functionality encompasses a broad range and flexible combination of rules that are based on criteria defined by the customer. These criteria and the categories which they fall into cover a wide range which are not able to pre-determine all possible scenarios. Sub-routines can be attached to restrictions for extremely complex rules.

Generic restrictions can be created and linked to one or several portfolios. Here, the user can define two main functions in the restrictions process:

- Identify the type of instrument to be checked and establish the rules
- Apply the restriction to the appropriate portfolios

The restriction must be clearly defined, so that the criteria to be used to identify the transaction in Temenos Transact terms can be established. The instrument to check is identified through a series of selection criteria and can ideally be any type of instrument in a portfolio (stocks, derivatives, bonds, cash, and so on).

The following are the various types of restriction in Temenos Transact .

These are rules that a bank imposes on all accounts. All restrictions are not related to instruments held in a portfolio. For example:

- If the bank has decided to create a restriction on a specific security or market, a restriction can be built that applies to all portfolios.
- The customer risk tolerance must be checked before transactions of a defined type are entered. For example, if tolerance is high, it allows purchase of derivatives.
- Restrictions exist relating to customer commissions on a transaction.

These are rules imposed on accounts handled by certain areas of the bank (for example, Private Banking, Discretionary Wealth Management, Mutual Fund Administration and so on) relating to its own internal policy. For example:

- Bonds must be rated A or better
- Bond maturities must be greater than five years
- Hold no more than x% of any single issuer
- All positions in the portfolio must be less than x% of total value
- A single bond position must not be more than x% of all bonds in the portfolio

It covers the needs of all customers falling within a certain group. The customer selection is based on characteristics defined on the bank's customer or portfolio record, such as reference currency, account officer, residence or nationality. For example:

- US customers cannot hold unseasoned securities
- Portfolios must hold x% in the customer reference currency
- No more than x% of high-risk securities in conservative portfolios

These are the most basic restriction to apply at the lowest or portfolio level and these are the rules the customer has imposed on his (managed or non-managed) portfolios that may have nothing to do with strategy, except personal considerations. For example:

- Customer’s sacred holdings cannot be sold
- Follow criteria established for environmentally friendly portfolios
- Do not buy certain sectors, like tobacco, technology and so on
- Do not buy a particular security

Restrictions are limited to securities defined in the SECURITY.MASTER application, elements of the transaction records and elements of the portfolio valuation. Related elements that are not found on these tables can be mapped to them using local references and ID descriptors. Restrictions must be tested against any type of transaction generated (simulated or actual) and based on a single position or on the sum of selected or all holdings in a portfolio. They must be tested when transactions are being entered into the system, as well as when transactions are generated by modelling sessions.

Restriction management is designed to deal with transaction restrictions in the Securities (SC) module and to allow holdings restriction testing by users of the Wealth Management module.

The above diagram illustrates the flow of information when restrictions are tested from an application. On validation of a transaction, the restrictions logic is called and a check is made to verify if there are any existing restrictions on the portfolio, customer group or asset. If a restriction is violated, an override message is returned to the application. This message either warns the inputter of the violation or actually block the transaction depending on the parameters setup for the rule.

For the Wealth Management (AM) module restrictions are checked in the modelling session, when the Check Order field is set in the AM.COMPARE application. If a restriction is violated, a violation is flagged against the proposed order. Constraints are checked by default in the following applications:

- SECURITY.TRANSFER
- SEC.TRADE
- POSITION.TRANSFER
- SEC.OPEN.ORDER

The following topics describe about defining restrictions and linking restrictions to portfolios:


##### Defining Restrictions

Restrictions can be defined at security and portfolio level. Security restrictions are grouped through SC.SECURITY.CONSTRAINT using the following criteria:

- SECURITY.DOMICILE
- LOCAL.REFERENCE
- SUB.ASSET.TYPE
- ASSET.TYPE

Restriction criteria can be entered in a more generic manner on any field of the following applications:

- CUSTOMER
- SEC.ACC.MASTER
- SECURITY.MASTER

For portfolio restriction processing, the ID of SC.SECURITY.CONSTRAINT allows a user-defined code prefixed by R-. This ID notifies the application to treat the restriction as a portfolio constraint and can be applied to RESTRICTION related to the portfolio(s).

Selection criteria for restrictions testing are composed of static data elements and dynamic data elements as described below.

- SECURITY.MASTER criteria can be setup for a single security or different classifications of instruments such as, issuer, sector, industry, currency, country or combinations of criteria. For example, issuer is IBM, security is NOKIA and currency is CHF.
- SEC.ACC.MASTER criteria can be added to further refined selection, for example, portfolio value
- CUSTOMER criteria is based on the selection on criteria like documentation signatures, residency, nationality and tax status.

Application data elements in SEC.OPEN.ORDER , SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER or POSITION.TRANSFER criteria relates to transaction amount, transaction currency or transaction fees, stock exchange and so on. The SC.SECURITY.CONSTRAINT application allows the administrator to build these rules.

The application is divided into several important areas. The administrator can give a general description to the restriction and indicate if it affects debit or credit type transactions. The multi-value Restriction field, list the rule or rules that are applied. These rules are entered further down in the record, where the filter is defined and one must indicate if the rule is for a holding or transaction check.

The below example uses the version SC.SECURITY.CONSTRAINT,REST.TRANS created for transaction checks. If the Direction field is blank and labelled as Credit or Debit, the rule prohibits all activity on the instrument type. The instrument is defined as any security in the SECURITY.MASTER application with a Maturity Date less than January 1, 2003 and categorised as a bond (BOND or SHARE set to B).

When a transaction is validated for this type of instrument, an override message appears. If it is accepted, it is written in the record.


##### Transaction and Holdings Restrictions

Once the criteria are determined, rules must be applied to determine:

- What action is taken?
- Will the securities selected be permanently held in the portfolio?
- Should buying be prohibited?
- Does the manager wish to keep the holding at a certain level or in a range?
- Should there be a test against the transaction amount?

These rules fall into two main categories namely:

Transaction restrictions are based on transaction entries in a portfolio. When a transaction is created, the system must check the condition to verify if the restriction is met. For example, do not purchase ABC & Co., do not sell XYZ stock and transaction amount cannot be greater than 100,000 USD.

The below screenshot is an example of a simple transaction restriction, which recommends not to buy the stock 000401-000. The record indicates that the restriction applies to credit type transactions. Thus, in a SEC.OPEN.ORDER or SEC.TRADE for example, the rule prohibits purchases. The selection criteria indicates that the transaction SECURITY.CODE must be equal to 000401-000 for the rule to apply.

In the below example of another transaction restriction, a combined selection criteria is indicated to establish the rule that any security with a currency of ZAR on a SEC.OPEN.ORDER , where the stock exchange is not 100, generates an error and the transaction is blocked. This case uses static and dynamic data elements.

With this rule, all transactions meeting the criteria is blocked and the transaction occurs in SEC.OPEN.ORDER . However, the same conditions is passed in a SEC.TRADE.

Temenos Transact provides several ways of grouping data elements from similar applications in order to treat them as a single entity. For transaction restrictions, this is possible using the SYNONYM application. The applications and common fields are indicated on a user-defined SYNONYM application.

In the above example, the transaction currency is defined as TRADE.CCY and the appropriate fields in SEC.OPEN.ORDER , SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER are listed. This allows the administrator to apply the SYNONYM definition of TRADE.CCY in a generic rule for all applications as in the following example.

The rules for holdings restrictions are more complex. The customer may have a requirement for a percentage of the portfolio to be held in a particular stock, sector or geographical region. A single portfolio position may be tested against the entire portfolio or against the sum of its category. For example, No more than 10% Japanese equities in the portfolio or no more than 10% Japanese equities in the equity portion of the portfolio. No more than 5% of technology stocks must be German companies.

Holdings tests use the most system resources as the portfolio valuation must be run and then one or more filters must be calculated. Therefore generic holding rules must be defined for BATCH processing rather than online. The Validation Type field on the linked RESTRICTION can be used to define whether this restriction is to be applied online or not.

The holdings valuation routine takes the criteria indicated in Rest Appli , Rest Field and Rest Value fields, as the first filter or the numerator. The Hold Field and Hold Value fields if not blank are used as the second filter or denominator. If the HOLD criteria is blank, it is assumed that the rule applies to the total value of the portfolio.

All holdings filter criteria are defined in the AM.ENTITY application. The following is an example of a restriction where currency USD must be 60% of the total portfolio.

The currency for all elements of the valuation is defined in the CCY record in AM.ENTITY. The SC.SECURITY.CONSTRAINT indicates that the generic field CCY must be USD and the value specified in the Range field must be less than 59.

The valuation routine takes all positions and as criteria is not specified for the denominator, it calculates the total market value of the portfolio. It then calculates the total market value of all USD positions including cash and return the result to the restrictions processing, where it is compared to the value in the Range field. As in the above example, if the result is less than 59%, an override message is displayed.

Many elements defined in the AM.ENTITY application must be setup only once. They can then be used for portfolio modelling as well as restrictions. The below example utilises the instrument type (that is, bond or share) and industry code.

These two codes IND and BOS can be used in numerous restrictions as in the above screenshot, where they are used to define the filters for a restriction and where the technology stocks are less than 20% of all equities. Passing these parameters to the holdings valuation results in the calculation of the market value of all technology stocks and the market value of all equities. If the result is less than 20%, an override message is displayed.

In the above example, the holdings routine filters all bonds to calculate their market value and then it filters all those with currency EUR, to obtain the calculation of EUR/ALL bonds.


##### Creating a Restriction Link

Restrictions can be maintained for groups of portfolios to cover broader compliance needs. For example,, groups include all private customers, banks own portfolios, in-house mutual funds, customers of a certain religion, nationality, country, risk profile and so on. These groups can have restrictions and those restrictions can theoretically be shared. Several customers might need environmentally friendly portfolios, or need the same tax considerations.

The application of the restriction may have a validity period or may only be necessary when using certain modules, for example, only on order entry or during the modelling session. Temenos Transact provides the ability to easily group customers and attach the appropriate restriction to the portfolio, as well as set parameters such as validity period.

The application where Temenos Transact stores the link between portfolios and their restrictions is the RESTRICTION application. Using this, the administrator can attach restrictions at the portfolio, customer or group level.

A restriction is linked to a portfolio by indicating the portfolio number in the ID of the record with the suffix SC. For securities restrictions, SC is suffixed for all codes. The format of this ID allows future development of the application for other modules that may have restrictions.

In this example, the restriction R-USDONLY, which is a record in the SC.SECURITY.CONSTRAINT application is attached to portfolio 50013-1. The restriction has no validity period, as it is effective immediately and indefinitely. It is only tested online in the SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER applications.


##### Trading Constraints usingEB.GC.CONSTRAINTS

The following are the five main applications that needs to be setup for global constraints:

- EB.GC.PARAMETER - System and company level parameter file
- EB.GC.ACTIVE - Application level definition file
- EB.GC.CONSTRAINTS - Constraints definition file
- EB.GC.GLOBAL - Global fields definition
- EB.GC.GROUP - Global constraints group definition EB.GC.PARAMETER This application must be setup for each company, where constraints processing is used the default SYSTEM, record. System Level In this level, the Com Processing is set to NO specifying that constraint processing or diagnostics recording is not done. This can be overridden at company level, as well at application level. The Com Diag is set to OFF specifying that diagnostics of constraints breaching does not occur. The Com Diag Life is set to 1 denoting that the diagnostic stays on record for 1 day only. This value is used to calculate the expiry or death date of the diagnostic record. The Com Method is significant on how constraints are to be processed. Here, it is set to SINGLE specifying that if the constraint with precedence of 1 exists, it is tested first and if not, the next constraint is tested and so on. Only one constraint is checked whether successful or not. If CUMULATIVE is set, all constraints are checked and reported as necessary. Normally for certain cases with less restrictive constraints, it may be easier to use SINGLE. However for more restrictive and additional constraints CUMULATIVE is suggested. There are five precedence fields pertaining to user, currency, account, portfolio and customer. A unique value of 1 to 5 can be specified for each, to define the order of checking. If these are set, it takes priority over all other institutional constraints. Company level The below example illustrates that for company US0010001, constraints processing as well as diagnostics are on. The precedence is unchanged. These override the SYSTEM setting, when the company US0010001 is used. Similarly, the parameter setting for company DE0010001 can be different. Constraints processing as well as diagnostics are on. The precedence may be changed. These override the SYSTEM setting, when the company DE0010001 is used.

Apart from the precedence, the EB.GC.PARAMETER setting can be overridden at the application level by setting up the EB.GC.ACTIVE parameter for the application. It also defines which fields on the application relate to customer, portfolio, account, currency and date and also whether they are associated to the customer or not. Further, the usage of any special routine can be defined. The total number of active constraints relating to the application is updated during the COB processing.

The below DX.TRADE example illustrates that for the application constraint processing and diagnostic reporting are on and the cumulative App Method denotes that all constraints are processed.

The customer fields on DX.TRADE, the Account , Currency and the Transaction Date fields are identified. The Selection Routine is set with the name of the selection routine that is being used or the blank.

As there are more than one customer field, the Portfolio Fld is linked to the Customer Fld within the same multi-value set on the source application (the Port Fld Assoc field is set to CUSTOMER). Similarly, as the Account Fld is linked to the Customer Fld within the same multi-value set on the source application, the Acct Fld Assoc field is set to CUSTOMER.

Again, if the Currency Fld is linked to the Customer Fld within the same multi-value set on the source application, the Curr Fld Assoc field is set to CUSTOMER. If set to CUSTOMER, both Acct Fld Assoc and Port Fld Assoc must also be set to CUSTOMER.

The following examples explain the possible setup for foreign exchange and funds transfer. For each application which needs the constraints processing, corresponding EB.GC.ACTIVE needs to be defined.

Any breach of a single rule is a breach of the whole constraints record. ### 5.74  Trailer Fees


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Trailer fee is a commission paid by an issuer of security to the bank for providing the bank’s customer with services such as holding, investment advices and other handling services of those financial instruments.*
> 
> **Applications:** `ACCR.REV.PARAM`, `CATEG.ENTRY`, `CUSTOMER`, `FT.COMMISSION.TYPE`, `RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY`, `SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS`, `SC.PRICE.CHANGE`, `SC.TR.FEE.PARAMETER` ... +12 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accr Amt Pay Ccy*, *Accr Per Port*, *Actual Calc Amt*, *Amount*, *Autodebit Rec Acc*, *Avg Recal Price*, *Back Value Eff Date*, *Calc Ccy* ... +47 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Trailer fee is a commission paid by an issuer of security to the bank for providing the bank’s customer with services such as holding, investment advices and other handling services of those financial instruments.

Bank usually enters into an agreement with the issuer to define how and when to calculate and receive trailer fees. The fee is booked as a receivable commission on a periodical frequency to the profit and loss (P/L) and is reconciled when the issuer pays the actual fees to the bank.

From an accounting point of view, the trailer fees are qualified as non-transaction related revenue. The booking of accruals aims to smooth and forecast the bank’s P/L and to avoid peaks in accounting as trailer fees payment occur. This functionality handles the trailer fees from the bank’s perspective.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Trailer fees set-up involves four steps as follows:

1. Setting-up the broad governing rules in SC.TR.FEE.PARAMETER record.
2. Creating customer record for the issuers in CUSTOMER record.
3. Defining an arrangement that exists between the bank and the issuer in SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT record.
4. Linking the issuer and securities by attaching the issuer in SECURITY.MASTER record.

Following section contains the detailed explanation of the setup required for trailer fee calculation.

1. Setting up the SC.TR.FEE.PARAMETER record as shown in the below screenshot.

The default product under which the bank reports their P&L earned as trailer fees is set here. The accrual method can be set to DAILY or it can be NULL. If it is set to DAILY, then daily accrual of trailer fees occurs. If the field is set as NULL, then accruals happen only on the respective calculation dates. The Day Basis field is used as the basis for accrual of trailer fees.

Trailer fee suspense category is the category that is used as a wash account for the purpose of:

- consolidation of accounting entry while pro-rating the difference amount when payment is processed
- during posting of capitalized amount into the receivable account on the payment generation date.

The No Rounding Accrual field is set to Yes, to record the trailer fees amount up to nine decimal places in SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT and SC.TRAIL.FEES.EXTRACT . If the No Rounding Accrual field is left blank (default value), the system records the values in respective currency specific decimal format. It is mandatory to set this record at company level record before creating SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT and other related applications.

1. Creating the CUSTOMER record for the issuer of trailer fees.

The issuing banks must have a valid customer ID for processing the trailer fees.

1. Creating the SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT record.

Broad rules that govern the calculation and payment of trailer fees that are agreed between the bank and the issuer of the security are set in this record. This is the parent application, which controls the process of calculation and payment of trailer fees for the particular issuer.

It is necessary to have an issuer level arrangement before proceeding to create a security level arrangement. Trailer fee calculation is performed for all the securities issued by the issuer only, if all the securities have individual arrangements at security level.

Some of the salient fields that affect the processing of trailer fees are explained below:

1. Calc Frequency : Calculation frequency dates are the exact dates on which calculated amounts are considered as amounts that are expected to be paid by the issuer on the scheduled payment dates. For example, if there are three calculation dates (31st of January, 29th of February and 31st of March) before a payment date (31st of March), then the amount calculated on the above three dates are summed up and the equivalent amount in payment currency is posted as expected payment amount in the SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record.
2. Payment Frequency : Payment frequency dates are the dates in which issuer is expected to pay the fees to the bank. The system automatically creates a SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record for the issuer on COB of the payment frequency date. For example, if payment date is on 31st of March and if the next working day is 01st of April, then payment record is available in the system on 01st of April. Amount reflected in the holding record includes the amount calculated as part of COB on 31st of March.

Payment frequency can be set only at the issuer level arrangement record and all amounts that are calculated at different security level arrangements are aggregated and then posted as a single consolidated amount due from the issuer in the SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record. Hence, the details related to payment are not allowed to be input at the security level arrangement.

The user is able to specify the country or issuer specific calculation rules by attaching a routine. The routine supports the calculation methods in addition to the methods supported as a standard. In addition, for a memo portfolio, the system can be parametrisedto reimburse the trailer fees to an internal suspense account.

The reimbursement for memo portfolios and for the portfolios where accounts are closed are done to the internal account category specified in Tr Reim Susp Cat in SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT .

Fees can be reimbursed to an internal account for all portfolios, instead of directly reimbursing to customers’ accounts.

If a category is defined in the Reimburse Category field in SC.TR.FEES.PARAMETER or SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT , the system automatically reimburses the fees to this category.


##### Setting up Portfolio for Reimbursement

When the portfolio is eligible for a partial customer reimbursement, then the Reimburse Tr Fee field in SEC.ACC.MASTER must be set to Yes and the Reimburse Tr Rate field holds the rate of reimbursement a customer is entitled to receive from the bank.


#### 🔧 Working With

Following section contains the detailed explanation of the trailer fees calculation.


##### Trailer Fees Calculation

All the calculation frequency dates that are set across different security level arrangements for a particular issuer should be set in such a way that the final calculation date coincides with the payment frequency date ( SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING generation date) set at the issuer level arrangement.

Once set, payment frequency can be changed on the next working day after the payment frequency date, that is, if payment frequency date is on 31st of March and the next working day happens to be 02nd of April, then the system allows changing the frequency only on 02nd of April.

If the payment frequency is modified, then the system raise an override to the effect that Calc Frequency date at the Security level arrangement must be reviewed. This override must be treated with importance and it is suggested to ensure that Calc Frequency date at all the security level arrangements are synchronised with the amended payment frequency at the issuer level. An example on synchronisation of dates is provided below for better understanding. While creating issuer level arrangement, the system insists to set calculation date and calculation frequency. For example, assume the following.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Current Day | 01 JAN 2008 |
| Calculation Date | 30 JUN 2008 |
| Calc Frequency | 30 JUN 2008 M0631 |
| Payment Frequency | 31 DEC 2008 M1231 |

For the above setup, there are two calculation dates before the payment date for the issuer is reached, that is, 30 JUN 2008 and 31 DEC 2008 (last calculation date before the payment date). The possible combination of calculation frequency allowed at the security level are explained in detail in the below table.

| Calculation Date | Calc Frequency | Actual Calculation Dates | Allow/Restrict | Remarks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31 JAN 2008 | M0131 | 31 JAN, 29 FEB, ….., 30 NOV, 31 DEC | ALLOW | Because the last calculation date coincides with the payment frequency date in the Issuer record. |
| M0231 | 31 JAN, 31 MAR, 30 MAY, 30 JUL,….., 30 NOV | RESTRICT | Because the last calculation date possible before the payment date is 30th of November and it does not coincide with the payment frequency date in the Issuer record, the system raises an error. |  |
| 01 JAN 2008 | BSNSS | 01 JAN, 02 JAN, ………………………30 DEC, 31 DEC | ALLOW | Because the last calculation date coincides with the payment frequency date in the Issuer record. |
| 29 FEB 2008 | M0231 | 29 FEB, 30 APR, 30 JUN,……, 31 OCT, 31 DEC | ALLOW | Because the last calculation date coincides with the payment frequency date in the Issuer record. |
| 01 FEB 2008 | M0231 | 01 FEB, 31 MAR, 30 MAY, 30 JUL,….., 30 NOV | RESTRICT | Because the last calculation date possible before the payment date is 30th of November and it does not coincide with the payment date in the Issuer record, the system raises an error. |
| 30 MAY 2008 | M0631 | 30 MAY, 30 NOV | RESTRICT | Because the last calculation date possible before the payment date is 30th of November and it does not coincide with the payment date in the Issuer record, the system raises an error. |
| 30 JUN 2008 | M0631 | 30 JUN, 31 DEC | ALLOW | Because the last calculation date coincides with the payment frequency date in the Issuer record. |

Finally, while setting up calculation frequency at the security level the system validates whether last calculation date of the security level arrangement coincides with the payment frequency date set at the issuer, if the condition is not met then an error message is raised.


##### Calculation Formula and Frequency Basis

There are six different methods of calculating trailer fees and additionally each of these six methods can be used with three special frequency methods. In total, there can be 24 different combinations possible.

For example, following four different combinations are possible for Calculation Formula = 1.

- Calculation Formula = 1 Calc Frequency = any monthly frequency Frequency Basis = NULL
- Calculation Formula = 1 Calc Frequency = M01 frequency Frequency Basis = AVERAGE
- Calculation Formula = 1 Calc Frequency = M06 frequency Frequency Basis = AVERAGE
- Calculation Formula = 1 Calc Frequency= M12 frequency Frequency Basis = AVERAGE

Different calculation formulas available for calculating trailer fees are explained below.

(from SECURITY.MASTER )

(Asset Holding could either be trade dated or value dated depending on the setup in SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT record.)

Where:

- Rate = % from FT.COMMISSION.TYPE
- Period = Number of days elapsed between calculation dates; (if calculation frequency basis is monthly then it is expressed in number of months.) Special cases where Calculation Formula used along with frequency basis as average and monthly frequency set to M01, M06 and M12 are discussed below.
- When frequency is M01: Asset holding on month M = Average of Asset Holding ((M-1) + (M -2)) Period = 1 (always equal to 1)
- When frequency is set to M06: Asset holding on month M = Average of Asset Holding of ((M) + (M-3)) on Calc Frequency dates = Asset holding as on last day of month for Intermediary month Period = 6 on calculation frequency dates = 1 for intermediate month between the Calc Frequency dates
- When frequency is set to M12: Asset holding on month M = Average of asset holding of ((M) + (M-6)) on Calc Frequency dates = Asset holding as on last day of month for intermediary months Period = 12 on calculation frequency dates = 1 for intermediate month between the Calc Frequency dates Special cases where Calculation Formula (2 to 6) used along with frequency basis as average and monthly frequency set to M01, M06 and M12 are discussed below.
- When frequency is M01: Asset holding on month M = Average of Asset Holding ((M-1) + (M -2))
- When frequency is set to M06: Asset holding on month M = Average of Asset holding of ((M) + (M-3)) on Calc Frequency dates = Asset holding as on last day of month for intermediary months
- When frequency is set to M12: Asset holding on month M = Average of Asset holding of ((M) + (M-6)) on Calc Frequency dates = Asset holding as on last day of month for intermediary months

Asset Holding = Security position as on the calculation date (could either be trade or value dated depending on the setup in the arrangement record)

Index = Index value taken from the individual SECURITY.MASTER record

Rate = % from FT.COMMISSION.TYPE

The trailer fee can be based on the management fee of the portfolio. The formula is

Trailer Accrual Fees = Asset Value x (Trailer Fee Rate x Management Rate) x Period

Where, Asset Value = Asset Holding x Last Price (from SECURITY.MASTER )

If the above formula is used, then while calculating the trailer fees; the system uses the management fee rate defined in Mgmt Fee Rate field in SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT application. In case Mgmt Fee Rate is not defined at SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT application, then the system takes the Mgmt Fee Rate defined in SC.MIFID.PRODUCT.DETS . If rate is not mentioned in both the fields, then it is defaulted to 100%. Temenos Transact maintains an extract of all trailer fees calculated by portfolio for each security position. These details are available in the SC.TRAIL.FEES.EXTRACT application, which is built on every calculation date. These rate are noted in the SC.TRAIL.FEES.EXTRACT application on every accrual. The defaulting of management fee happens in SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT at security level only.


##### Receivable Account, P/L Category and Trailer Fee Suspense Category

Receivable account is the account where trailer fee amount receivable from the issuer is parked on the payment generation date. It should ideally be an account of the issuer or any other valid customer account.

PL category is the category used for accrual of trailer fees and trailer fee suspense category. This is the category that is used as a wash account for the purpose of consolidation of accounting entry during the pro-rating of difference amount when payment is processed, and during posting the capitalised amount into the receivable account on the payment generation date.

The Receivable Acc field in SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT application accepts any Nostro or Internal account or any account not belonging to the issuer.

> **⚠️ Note:** The bank user must create an internal account using the category and enter the complete account number in the Receivable Acc field in order to input the internal account. For example, USD1420000010001 is an internal account created.


##### Payment Currency, Calculation Currency

Payment currency is the currency in which Issuer is expected to pay the fees and so all the accruals happen in this currency. Receivable account opened at the Issuer level must be valid customer account in payment currency. This field can be set at the Issuer level and not at the security level arrangements. This field cannot be modified, once it is set.

Calculation currency is the currency at which calculation of fees occurs. Then, it is converted into payment currency equivalent at the mid-rate. It can only be set at the security level and not at the issuer level. When a security level arrangement is opened and this field is defaulted with the security currency, however it can be changed manually. Once the Currency field is set, it cannot be modified.


##### Tolerance Min Amount, Tolerance Max Amount, Tolerance Currency, Tolerance Level

These fields are used to capture the tolerance levels (between the calculated and actual payment amount) allowed for an issuer. Tolerance can be defined either in percentage terms or in absolute terms or both. The Tolerance Min Amt and Tolerance Max Amt fields are used to capture the absolute values of tolerance. If both absolute amounts and percentage are used, then it considers the minimum of the two amounts and uses it for tolerance validation. If the payment is set as complete and if difference amount exceeds the tolerance, then an override is displayed.

Tolerance currency is used in tandem with Tolerance Min Amt and Tolerance Max Amt fields, if the currency is different from Payment Currency , then the absolute values of tolerance are converted into Tolerance Currency at mid-rate and are used for tolerance validation.


##### Tax on Trailer Fees

The trailer fees arrangement record updates the:

- tax code
- tax P/L
- details of whether the fees received from the issuer is inclusive or exclusive of taxes

If fees is set to be inclusive of taxes, it means that the service tax and other taxes (if any) is included in the Trailer Fees received from fund house. Then, the bank has to remit this tax to the tax authorities. If set to exclusive, the amount received from the issuer is only the fees and tax is not received from the issuer. The tax in this case would have been paid directly by the issuer. However, in this case, the system calculates the taxes for reporting purposes.

The total estimated tax per position is calculated and shown in each extract file. Entries for tax are not posted at the extract level. Any difference in the tax on final trailer fees and the system calculated fees is apportioned to the individual extracts on a pro-rata basis and updated in the Diff Tax field in SC.TRAIL.FEES.EXTRACT .

> **⚠️ Note:** If trailer fee is reimbursed to customers, only the fees portion is reimbursed.


##### Trailer Fees Process

After the issuer level arrangement is competed and if the SECURITY.MASTER record is attached to the issuer, then the system allows to setup the security level arrangement. When a security level arrangement is opened, some fields are defaulted with the values available at the issuer level arrangement. However, it can be changed at the security level. As explained above, the payment related fields are no-input at the security level, whereas the calculation currency can be set only at the security level arrangement and not at the issuer level.

Attaching the issuer to securities issued by the issuer in SECURITY.MASTER record is shown in the below screenshot.

The Trailer Issuer field is used to identify the issuer of the security. Index, Trailer Reference Level and Initial Reference Level are the other fields related to trailer fees calculation.

Once the above-mentioned setup is done and if a position is built in a security, then the system automatically creates SC.TRAIL.FEES.EXTRACT records during COB and accruals are posted on a daily basis (based on the setup in SC.TR.FEE.PARAMETER ). Extract records for a given security are maintained at the customer or depository level. The accrued amounts calculated on different calculation frequency dates are individually held in multi-value sets in SC.TRAIL.FEES.EXTRACT .

The total estimated tax per position is calculated and shown in each extract file. Entries for tax are not posted at the extract level. Any difference in the tax on final trailer fees and the system-calculated fees are apportioned to the individual extracts on a pro-rata basis and updated in the Diff Tax field.

> **⚠️ Note:** If trailer fee is reimbursed to customers, only the fees portion is reimbursed.

The SC.TRAIL.FEES.EXTRACT record for which payment is already generated is shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Ext Accr Amt and Accr Amt Pay Ccy fields hold the value of accrued amount up to nine decimal places if No Rounding Accrual is set to Yes in SC.TR.FEE.PARAMETER , else it holds the values in the respective currency decimal format.

All details used for calculating the accrual amount are available in this record. Date-wise calculation of trailer fees are held at the extract level. If the payment date is reached for a particular issuer, then this screen records the suffixed with the payment date generated containing all details pertaining to that payment period. Subsequent screen that are built for the next fee period has the usual ID without the date component.

If a back-valuation (explained in next section) is triggered, then the relevant changes that must be recorded are updated in the SC.TRAIL.FEES.EXTRACT record. Depending on timing of the back-value trigger, appropriate fields are updated (either the existing field or a new field). The fields with BV prefix are used to indicate that they are updated as part of back-valuation.

Reimbursement is required for certain customers, whereas for some customers the trailer fee received is retained by the bank. The reimbursement is to the extent of fee calculated based on their individual holdings. On the COB of payment frequency date, the system automatically creates SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record for the issuer in live status. SR.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record holds the actual calculated amount expressed in payment currency. Actual calculated amount comprises of amounts calculated for all the security level arrangements belonging to that particular issuer. The details of the calculation currency wise consolidation along with the exchange rate used and the payment currency equivalent are also available in the holding record.

For example, an issuer is expected to pay in GBP and has ten different security level arrangements, where the first three arrangements has calculation currency as USD, next three securities has calculation currency as EUR and the remaining four securities in SGD. The SR.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING actual calculated amount is GBP and the break-up of amounts at EUR, USD and SGD along with the payment currency equivalent and exchange rates are used.

The SR.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING provides the user to capture the fees paid by the issuer to the bank (in the Payment Amount field).

When SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record is created by the system, the accruals equivalent to the Actual Calc Amt is already booked to the PL Account with the corresponding debit to the Receivable Account specified in the SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT of the Issuer.

All the postings to the P&L account occurs at the customer or product level. To illustrate this point further, if there are two customers holding position in three different securities, which are issued by the same issuer, there are six different entries for each of the customer or security combination. Though the trailer fee amount is to be received from the issuer, the primary reason to book the PL entries at the customer or security level is to enable the bank to have the break-up of contribution to trailer fees at the customer or product level.

It is possible to record any number of partial payments received from the issuer. When a partial payment is received, amount received is stored and summed up in Settled Amount field and entries are not raised. When Settlement Status in a SR.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record is marked as Complete, further input in the SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record is not possible and the following processes can take place depending on combination of values in:

- Actual Calc Amt

##### Recalculation using Average Price

The Issuer may use an average price to calculate the Trailer Fees for a period. Temenos Transact calculates the Trailer Fees using different methods and some of them are based on the daily price of the security. This could result in a difference between the Temenos Transact calculated fees and the fees received by the issuer. The system can recalculate the fees if the issuer provides the average price.

To achieve this, the trailer fees holding record has a multi-value set of fields with the fund ID and the average price. The average price per fund can be specified in the Avg Recal Price field in the SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING application. Once the average price for all the funds are given, the Recal With Ap field should be set to Yes in the SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING application. This triggers an automatic recalculation by the system.

> **⚠️ Note:** Recalculation can be run only before the payment status is complete and recalculation can be run only once.

The average price is considered for the full calculation period and the date is not associated with the same. If the recalculated amount still does not match with the amount received, then the difference is apportioned to all extracts on pro-rata basis as is currently done. Entries for the difference is to be raised.

The amounts displayed in the last column (booking) is the amount that is posted to the PL entry on a daily basis. It is assumed that while reversing the previous day’s accrual, same exchange rate between which it is booked is used. The calculation used to arrive at the booking amount is explained below.

| COB date | Bank date | POSITION(as on COB date) | AMT IN CALC CCY | AMT IN PAY CCY(EUR) | PL entry in USD (pro-rated amounts) Reversal Booking |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01st Jan | 02nd Jan | 10000 | 100 | 130 (@.769) |  | 6.5(@1.5) |
| 02nd Jan | 03rd Jan | 10000 | 100 | 130 (@.769) | -6.5 | 13(@1.5) |
| 03rd Jan | 29th Jan | 25000 | 250 | 350 (@.714) | -13 | 522.66(1.6) |
| 29th Jan | 31st Jan | 8000 | 80 | 104(@.769) | -522.66 | 156(@1.5) |
| 31st Jan | 02nd Feb | 10000 | 100 | 130(@.769) | -156 | 195(@1.5) |
| 02nd Feb | 25th Feb | 15000 | 150+100 | 312.5(@0.8) | -195 | 400(@1.6) |
| 25th Feb | 27th Feb | 0 | +100 | 153.84(@0.65) | -400 | 193.33(@1.45) |
| 27th Feb | 29th Feb | 20000 | 200+100 | 428.57(@0.7) | -193.33 | 600(@1.5) |
| 29th FEB | 01st Mar | 30000 | 300+100 | 571.42(@0.7) | -600 | 914.28(@1.6) |

On 01st of March, SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record for the issuer is generated with Actual Calc Amt as 571.42 expressed in EUR (payment currency). The entries for the above examples in Temenos Transact are:

| Bank Date | CATEG.ENTRY in USD | SPEC.ENTRY in EUR | STMT.ENTRY in EUR | Reversal | Booking | Reversal | Booking | Trail Fee Suspense Category | Receivable Account |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 02nd Jan |  | 6.5 |  | -4.33 |  |  |  |  |  |
| 03rd Jan | -6.5 | 13 | 4.33 | -8.67 |  |  |  |  |  |
| 29th Jan | -13 | 522.66 | 8.67 | -326.66 |  |  |  |  |  |
| 31st Jan | -522.66 | 156 | 326.66 | 104 |  |  |  |  |  |
| 02nd Feb | -156 | 195 | -104 | 130 |  |  |  |  |  |
| 25th Feb | -195 | 400 | -130 | -250 |  |  |  |  |  |
| 27th Feb | -400 | 193 | 250 | -133.33 |  |  |  |  |  |
| 29th Feb | -193 | 600 | 133.33 | -400 |  |  |  |  |  |
| 01st Mar | -600 | 914.28 | 400 | -571.42 |  |  |  |  |  |
| 01st Mar |  |  |  | +571.42 | -571.42 |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  | +571.42 | -571.42 |  |  |  |
| TOTAL | 914.28 | 0 | 0 | -571.42 |  |  |  |  |  |

Following are the sequence of entries that are posted from the start of the accrual until the payment generation date:

- Accrual entries happen between the CATEG and SPEC from the start of accrual until the payment generation date. The system reverse and re-book the accruals based on the settings in ACCR.REV.PARAM record.
- Accrual entries are at customer or product level in both the CATEG and SPEC entry.
- On the COB of the payment frequency date, the amount that is accrued in the SPEC entry is capitalised and is consolidated in an intermediary account opened with category specified in Trail Fee Suspense Category field.
- If there are five entries at customer or product level in the SPEC, all these five entries are capitalised and consolidated into a single amount using the intermediary wash account. Then, consolidated amount is booked to the receivable account mentioned in the SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT record.

The explanation of how the PL amounts are calculated on a daily basis is given below. Since the next calculation date is 31st of January, accruals must be pro-rated until the calculation date.

On COB 01st of January, the position is 10000 and rate is 1%

Then, the calculated amount is 10,000 x 1% = 100 GBP (calculation currency)

Amount in Payment CCY = 100 /0.769 = 130 EUR (for entire period (01st to 31st of Jan))

Accrual to be posted as on 01st of Jan COB = Amt in Calc CCY x (no of days elapsed)/30

Days elapsed = 02nd of Jan – 01st of Jan = 1 day

Total days = 30 (since day basis is 360/360)

Amount booked = 130 x 1/30 = 4.33 EUR

Local currency equivalent = 4.33 x 1.5 = 6.5 USD

On COB 2nd of January, everything remains the same, only change in calculation is in the number of days (2) (03rd Jan – 01st of Jan) that must be factored in. Previous day’s accrual is reversed (an entry (-6.5 USD) and booking of new amount).

Previous day’s accruals are reversed = -6.5 USD

Amount booked = 130 x 2/30 = 8.66 EUR

Amount booked in LCY = 8.66 x 1.5 = 13 USD

On COB 3rd of January, the customer position and exchange rates between the Calc Ccy or Payment Currency and Payment Currency or local currency are changed. The following occurs as part of COB.

Previous day’s accrual are reversed = -13 USD

Amounts are recalculated as:

Calculated amount = 25000 x 1% = 250 GBP

Amount in payment CCY= 250/0.714 = 350 EUR

No. of days elapsed = 28 (29th Jan – 01st Jan)

Amount booked = 350 x 28/30 = 326.66 EUR

Amount booked in LCY = 326.66 x 1.6 = 522.66 USD

On COB 29th of January, the customer position and exchange rates between the Calc Ccy or Payment Currency and Payment Currency or local currency are changed. The following occurs as part of COB.

Previous day’s accrual are reversed = -522.66 USD

Calculated amount = 8000 x 1% = 80 GBP

Amount in payment CCY= 80/0.769= 104 EUR

No. of days elapsed = 30 (31st Jan – 01st Jan)

Amount booked = 104 x 30/30 = 104 EUR

Amount booked in LCY = 104 x 1.5 = 156 USD

> **⚠️ Note:** On COB of 31st January (calculation date), the amounts are not pro-rated but the amount arrived as part of calculation is booked as PL amount.

Customer position has changed from previous day, but the exchange rates between Calc Ccy or Payment Currency and Payment Currency or local currency are not changed. The following occurs as part of COB.

Previous day’s accrual are reversed = -156USD

Calculated amount = 10000 x 1% = 100 GBP

Amount in payment CCY= 100/0.769= 130 EUR

Equivalent in local currency = 130 x 1.5= 195 USD

Similar process continues into the February month. Since a calculation date is crossed (31st of January), the amount calculated in calculation currency ( Calc Ccy ) on that day is crystallised and is always added up to the amount calculated on subsequent days. Accrual days are always from the last calculation date to the next. For example, on 25th February, the number of days elapsed is 24 (01st Feb – 25th Feb).

When last calculation date is not available (usually this happens before the first calculation date as the Arrangement is reached), the system works backwards to find the theoretical date based on the calculation frequency and it uses that date as the accrual start date. For example, if an arrangement is open on 01st of January with calculation frequency set as 31st Jan 2008 M0331, then based on this frequency the system works backwards to find out the theoretical previous calculation date (31st OCT 2007) and uses that date as the Accrual start date. Therefore, on 01st Jan COB, with 360/360 basis, the number of days elapsed is (01st Jan 2008 – 01st Nov 2007) 61 days.

On COB of 02nd February, the customer position and exchange rates between the Calc Ccy or Payment Currency and Payment Currency or local currency are changed. The following calculation occurs as part of COB.

Previous day’s accrual are reversed = -195USD

Calculated amount = 15000 x 1% = 150 GBP

Amount in Calc Ccy as on 31st of Jan = 100 GBP

Net amount in calculation currency = 250 GBP (150 + 100)

Amount in payment currency= 250/0.8 = 312.5 EUR

No. of days elapsed = 24 (01st of Feb – 25th of Feb)

Amount booked = 312.5 x 24/30 = 250 EUR

Equivalent in local currency = 250 x 1.6= 400 USD

Same process continues until the SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record is generated.


##### Trailer Fees - Back Valuation

In real time, the actual calculated amount may not be in line with what is to be received from the issuer, this could be due to many reasons like a change in rate that was agreed between the Issuer and bank, but was not captured in the system or some of the components (like trailer reference level, initial reference level, index not updated properly) or it could be because of a trade not being captured in the system.

In order to handle such exceptions, Temenos Transact captures these changes in the system on a later date and then running Back-valuation service to effect the changes with retrospective results. In order to trigger the Back-valuation, the following steps must be followed in the same order. Amend the static data that were incorrect or not present earlier or allows capturing the new transactions that were missed out. Following is the exhaustive list of components that goes into the calculation of trailer fees across all formula that might affect Back-valuation.

| Component | How and where it needs to be set | Used in formula |
|---|---|---|
| Asset holding | Any Back- valuation which affects a change in security position. For example, it can be triggered by a backdated SEC.TRADE . | 1,2,3,4,5,6 |
| Rate change | FT.COMMISSION.TYPE attached to Fee Code field in the SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT record. | 1,2,3,4,5,6 |
| Price | SC.PRICE.CHANGE record of the SECURITY.MASTER . For example, if 31st of Jan 29th of Feb and 31st of March are the calculation dates and if a new price is to be used for 31st of Jan, then the price must be amended in the relevant SC.PRICE.CHANGE record with ID (SM.ID.31st of Jan). The system uses that price and recalculates the amount for 31st of Jan, alone during Back-Valuation. | 1,4 |
| Index | Trailer Index field present in the SECURITY.MASTER record. | 2 |
| Trailer Ref Level | Trailer Reference Level field present in the SECURITY.MASTER record. | 3 |
| Init Ref Level | Initial Reference Level field present in the SECURITY.MASTER record. | 3 |

Once the appropriate changes are made, the date from which these changes are to take effect must be input in the Back Value Eff Date field of SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT record.

When a back-value effective date is set at the issuer level, then by default the Back-valuation is carried out for all the security level arrangements that belong to that particular issuer. For any reason, if Back-valuation is to be triggered from a different date for a particular security level arrangement, then that date has to be input at the security level arrangement.

| Arrangement level | Back Value Eff Date |
|---|---|
| ISSUER | 01st of January |
| ISSUER.SECURITY.1 | - |
| ISSUER.SECURITY.2 | - |
| ISSUER.SECURITY.3 | - |

| Arrangement level | Back Value Eff Date |
|---|---|
| ISSUER | 01st of January |
| ISSUER.SECURITY.1 | - |
| ISSUER.SECURITY.2 | 01st of February |
| ISSUER.SECURITY.3 | - |


##### Trailer Fees - Amortisation

The SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record can be created manually to capture the advance fees paid by the Issuer. The ID of SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record is in the ISSUER.STARTDATE-AMORT format, to enable the same. On the authorising the SR.HOLDINGS record, the Issuer account is debited and the corresponding credit is held in amortisation category. Amount is dripped into PL account until the Period End date is available in the SR.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record.

The below screenshot displays the SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record that was created manually to record the receipt of USD 300 from the issuer. Amount is to be amortised until 4th of December (Period End).

> **⚠️ Note:** Only at this point, the total trailer fee is rounded-off to the respective currency specific decimal format irrespective of the condition set in SC.TR.FEE.PARAMETER .

On authorising the SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING record, the issuer’s account is debited and SPEC is credited.

Amortised amount drips into P/L on a daily basis till the period end date.


##### Debiting the Receivable Account

The Autodebit Rec Acc field in SC.TR.FEE.PARAMETER controls the debit to the receivable account. If this field is left blank, the debit to receivable account is done automatically on the pay date.

If this field is set to No, the system

- does not automatically debit the receivable account on the pay date.
- credits the bank’s P&L and debits the trailer fees suspense account on the pay date for the amount that is not reimbursable. The system does not raise entriesy to debit receivable account and credit trailer fees suspense account.

When the payment is received and updated in SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING application and the Sett Status is set to Completed, the system debits the receivable account for the actual money received and credits the trailer fee suspense account.

###### Reimbursement of Trailer Fees

Banks receive Trailer fees as commission from the issuer for providing the customers of the bank with services such as holding and investment advices.

The banks can choose to reimburse the received trailer fees to the customer or retain the same. The Reimburse Tr Fee and Reimburse Tr Rate fields in SEC.ACC.MASTER controls whether the trailer Fees need to be reimbursed to the customer. In Reimburse Tr Rate , the bank can set how much percentage of trailer Fees should be Reimbursed.

When the SC.TRAIL.FEES.HOLDING is marked as completed, the system posts the reimbursement amount per portfolio to the customer’s account directly where a portfolio is set for reimbursement of trailer fee. Only percentage of the net fees (after tax) is reimbursed.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system cannot withhold the tax on reimbursement as there is no specific field.


###### Reimbursement to Internal Account instead of Customer Account

The system can be parameterised to post the reimbursement amount to an internal account instead of client’s account directly, if the reimbursement amount is modified or taxes are deducted.

The Reimburse Category field in SC.TR.FEE.PARAMETER and SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT defines the internal account to credit the trailer Fees.

- The system checks the internal account input in Reimburse Category in the issuer record of SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT to credit the trailer fees.
- The system checks the internal account input in Reimburse Category in the company record of SC.TR.FEE.PARAMETER , when account is not defined in SC.TRAIL.FEES.ARRANGEMENT

When the SC.TRAIL.FEE.HOLDING is marked as complete, system debits the trail fees suspense account and credits the internal account defined in the Reimburse Category field.

> **⚠️ Note:** To transfer the adjusted reimbursement amount from internal account to customers is not automatic and is done manually.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Maintain Trailer Fees
- Administration and Static Data and Corporate Actions

Trailer Fee is a commission paid by an issuer of security to the bank for providing the bank’s customer with services such as holding, investment advices and other handling services of those financial instruments.

Bank usually enters into an agreement with the Issuer to define how and when to calculate and receive Trailer Fees. The fee is booked as a receivable commission on a periodical frequency to the Profit and Loss and is reconciled when the actual fees is paid by the issuer to the bank. From an accounting point of view, the Trailer Fees is qualified as non-transaction related revenue. The booking of accruals aims to smooth and forecast the bank’s Profit and Loss and to avoid peaks in accounting as Trailer Fees payment occurs.

### 5.75  TransactionFees Charges Taxes


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
>

>

#### 📖 Introduction

Security transactions entail fees charged by the bank, broker and by other market players such as the stock exchange. There are taxes levied by the regulators also. The fees and taxes vary in nature and depend on several factors such as the type of transaction, type of instrument and exchange where the transaction is executed and so on.

This feature elaborates how transaction fees, charges and taxes are configured and calculated in Securities (SC) module.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic details the configuration of transaction fees, charges and taxes in Securities (SC) module.

There are named fees fields in order and trade applications in the SC module to handle the following:

- Customer commission (bank’s own commission) and tax on customer commission
- Broker commission
- Stock exchange fees (EBV fees)
- Foreign fees
- Stamp tax
- Miscellaneous fees

There are also named fees to handle taxes such as:

- Withholding tax
- Other taxes

Apart from the named fees, it is also possible to setup any number of fees and taxes using the multiple charges framework.


##### Configuring Named Fees and Tax Fields

The following section details about the configuration required to setup the fees and taxes for different types of transactions.

Customer commission is determined by the group to which the customer belongs to for the purpose of transaction charges. To group the customers, the first level configuration is done in the SC.TRADING record in CONDITION.PRIORITY . The fields in CUSTOMER and SEC.ACC.MASTER that are used to group customers has to be defined in the SC.TRADING record, along with the priority to be considered amongst the fields.

The groups can also be defined using SCTR.GEN.CONDITION .

The actual commission that is to be charged for each group is defined in SCTR.GROUP.CONDITION .

When a CUSTOMER record is created in Temenos Transact , the system determines the default group to which customer belongs for trading commission, and updates the group details in CUSTOMER record in CUSTOMER.CHARGE . User can change the system calculated group and update the actual group for the customer and/or for each portfolio.

Banks can setup generic groups in SCTR.GROUP.CONDITION application with record ID starting with G-XXXXXX. These generic groups can be set when the banks want to create groups that do not follow criteria from CUSTOMER or SEC.ACC.MASTER or FATCA.CUSTOMER.SUPPLEMENTARY.INFO applications. These generic groups can be created without any corresponding record in CONDITION.PRIORITY and SCTR.GEN.CONDITION applications.

The generic group ID needs to be manually linked to the Sc Act Group field under Sc Trading record in CUSTOMER.CHARGE application for the applicable customers.

Banks can attach the generic group at the transaction level rather at CUSTOMER.CHARGE level, by providing the generic record ID in the Charge Code field in SEC.TRADE or SEC.OPEN.ORDER or SECURITY.TRANSFER application. If this field has a valid input, then the system calculates the fees using the group input in Charge Code field.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system does not check the CUSTOMER.CHARGE application to determine the group if the Charge Code field has a value.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Security Type | Holds a valid record in SECURITY.MASTER , ASSET.TYPE , or SUB.ASSET.TYPE |
| Domicile | Holds a valid country code or ALL. Value of this field is mapped with the Domicile field in the SECURITY.MASTER application. |
| Stock Exchange | Holds a valid STOCK.EXCHANGE ID or ALL. The user can enter the value for either domicile or stock exchange. It is not logical to enter both the values |
| Transaction Type | Holds a valid transaction type for BUY or SELL or ALL |
| Index | This is a no input field. Defaults the value based on the following combination. Security Type*Stock Exchange*Domicile*Transaction Type |

The following applications need to be configured in order to setup taxes for transactions.

A record needs to be created for each tax. The ID of this application is a numeric ID followed by the date. If there is a change in the rate, a new record for the same ID with the new effective date needs to be created. The rate of tax and the internal account category to which the tax is to be posted is defined in this application.

The tax record in condition.priority allows the user to define the fields in CUSTOMER and FATCA.CUSTOMER.SUPPLEMENTARY.INFO applications that can be used to group customers for tax calculation.

This application is used to create different tax types and the date from which the taxes are effective. If the tax has to be split between more than one customer (such as joint customers) in the customer relationship attached to SEC.ACC.MASTER , it needs to be specified here.

Customers are grouped for each tax type using the fields defined in CONDITION.PRIORITY .

Each customer group is linked to a record in TAX .

Withholding tax can be deducted at the time of redemption and also at the time of sale of fixed income securities.

A record in the TXN.TAX.CODE application must be setup that states the TAX or TAX.TYPE.CONDITION that has to be applied and the applications where the taxes should be applied. The Amount Base field must be set to DISCOUNT for tax on discount calculations.

The Redem Price field in the SECURITY.MASTER application is populated with a value to calculate the discounted amount per sale transaction. In this case, the redemption price is 100. The TXN.TAX.CODE should then be attached to the SECURITY.MASTER application. The withholding tax (WHT) can only be calculated when a security is redeemed or sold. The record in SECURITY.MASTER displays the setup for consideration rounding and withholding tax on sales.

This application defines the Tax Basis field for calculating the withholding tax.


##### Configuring Multiple Fees and Taxes

The following section details about the configuration required to setup the multiple fees and taxes for different types of transactions.

This application is used to define any fees and taxes applicable for an application.

The ID of SCDX.CHARGE.PARAMETER application is Application*Company Code. If the parameter setup is done for an application (such as SEC.TRADE ), the charge type is defaulted in the respective application on the customer side or broker side, which is defined in Chg Tax Cust Brok field. The Charge Tax Type field can be multi-valued to define multiple charges and taxes. This is a free format text field. However, each multi-value should have a unique name.

The Priority field defines the criteria based on which the fee can vary. For example, a fee varies by stock exchange (and no other criteria), then stock exchange is only priority defined. If more than one criteria applies (for example, in National Stock Exchange (NSE), turnover fee for equities is 0.005% and for debt instruments is 0.0003%), both the criteria are defined as priority (for example, the value in Priority 1.1 is Stock Exchange and Priority 1.2 is Txn Type). The category codes and transaction codes are defined in SCDX.CHARGE.PARAMETER only when the charges or taxes are manually input. If not, the category or codes in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE or TAX are used.

Charge Tax Nature field is used to identify if the charge mentioned in Charge Tax Type is Fee or Tax.

If the input is,

- Tax – The charge is recognised as Tax and Tax Code in SC.CHARGE.TAX.CALC is mandatory.
- Fee – The charge is recognised as Fee.
- Blank – The charge is recognised as Fee or Tax based on category codes in Charge Tax Cat .

Charge Tax Ind is a free format text field to indicate the corresponding charge or tax name in an external system like TAP Front Office.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| External | Indicates that it is an external fee. For example, turnover fee levied by stock exchange or securities transaction tax |
| Bank | Specifies any additional fee or charge levied by the bank on top of brokerage or commission |


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic details how transaction fees, charges and taxes are calculated and accounted in Securities (SC) module.


##### Calculating and Accounting of Named Fees and Taxes

The calculation for commission and taxes is explained in this section.

The system checks the CUSTOMER.CHARGE to determine the actual trading group that the portfolio or customer belongs to. System calculates the customer commission using the FT.COMMISSION.TYPE application defined for the type of security in the trade for the group defined in SCTR.GROUP.CONDITION . System applies the percentage applicable and determines the customer commission, which is updated in Cu Commission field in SEC.TRADE .

If there is a tax defined for the commission in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE , then tax is calculated and updated in the Cu Comm Tax field.

Charges based on Nominal

It is possible to charge commission based on nominal. For example, if the Nominal is 1000 units and the commission is set as 0.05 cents per unit, the system will charge Cu Commission of 50 Dollars.

To calculate the charges based on the Nominal ,

- The user must set the Base Code field in the SCTR.CHARGE.PARAMETER record as Nominal for the type of Security selected. For example, S-302 or A-30.
- The user must set the Calculation Basis field as Unit and the Unit Charge field as the amount per unit that needs to be charged for the FT.COMMISSION.TYPE application to be used. For example, 0.05 cents.
- In SCTR.GROUP.CONDITION , for the Sec Type (Asset or Sub Asset Type) selected, attach FT.COMMISSION.TYPE as above against the Chg Comm Cd field.

With this setup, the system calculates

- Cu Commission in SEC.TRADE based on the nominal value from Cust Tot Nom
- Charges in SECURITY.TRANSFER based on the nominal value from the No Nominal field .

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| All In Fee | Indicates whether the customer broker commission is waived or not. If this field is set to Yes, the value in the Cu Brkr Comm field (broker commission on customer side) in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is updated as zero and the bank directly pays the commission to the broker. |
| Product Type | Indicates a valid SECURITY.MASTER ID, where the asset type records are prefixed by A- and sub-asset type records are prefixed by S- or ALL |
| Security Domicile | Indicates a valid country code or ALL. A corresponding record in SECURITY.MASTER is created, if this field is set to US and sub-asset type as 301. This record is used while creating the orders. |
| Index | Indicates the value defaulted from the combined values of the Product Type* Security Domicile fields. This is a display-only field. |

The withholding tax on discount amounts are illustrated below with examples.

Consider a SEC.TRADE sale transaction that had truncated, discount amount and withholding tax calculated as shown below:

Nominal: 135000

Price: 97.2245%

Consideration = 135,000 * 97.2245% = 131,253.075

The Discount Amount field in SEC.TRADE records the difference from the redemption price as stored in the Redem Price field in the SECURITY.MASTER and the traded price from the Cust Price field in SEC.TRADE . In this case, the calculation is as follows:

(NOMINAL* REDEMPTION PRICE) - (NOMINAL* TRADED PRICE)

= 135,000 * 100%) – (135,000 * 97.2245%) = 3,746.93

A withholding tax rate of 5% is applied in the Discount Amount field and an amount of 187.35 is calculated.

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Include Source Tax | Indicates whether Source Tax Amt in ENTITLEMENT is to be included in deal amount calculation from ENTITLEMENT . By default, the source tax is not considered for calculating tax. |
| Total Discount/ Premium | Indicates the total discount or premium of a security in a company for exemption of European Union Services Directive (EUSD) tax calculation. The tax exemption is applicable only if the total discount and period discount is calculated using Issue Price and Redem Price of SECURITY.MASTER and does not exceed the values defined in Total Discount/ Premium and Period Discount/ Premium fields. |
| Period Discount/ Premium | Indicates the discount or premium of a security in a company for current period for exemption of EUSD tax calculation |
