### 5.76  Transfers


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Transfer feature explains about the transfer of holdings into or out of a portfolio and transfer of a position from one depository or sub-account to another. This is useful in the following important cases:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *ADR/GDR Transfer-in Txn*, *Advice Default*, *Asset Sub Asset*, *Authorize*, *Auto Select*, *Bct Quantity*, *Bct Sec Acc Master*, *Bct Security No* ... +143 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Transfer feature explains about the transfer of holdings into or out of a portfolio and transfer of a position from one depository or sub-account to another. This is useful in the following important cases:

- In the initial setup of positions on a newly delivered system (migration).
- In case, the customers (for whom the bank maintains custody operations) either purchase or sell the holdings to third parties directly, such positions have to be captured in the system (off-market trades).
- When there is a movement of position between two portfolios within the books.

The SECURITY.TRANSFER and POSITION.TRANSFER applications are used to handle the transfer of holdings. The SECURITY.TRANSFER application enables the transfer of holdings in and out of the customer’s portfolio account (free of payment) to handle off-market transactions. The POSITION.TRANSFER application enables transfer of one or all securities from one portfolio account to another or from one depository account to another.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The SC.STD.POS.TRANSF application is used to set the default values at the company level for both the SECURITY.TRANSFER and POSITION.TRANSFER applications. The user must setup a record for each company in the system as shown in the below screenshot.

Apart from the transaction and category codes that has to be used within these applications, this parameter also defines the OFS source and version (in the OFS Source and Default Version fields) to be used for bulk transfers.


##### Setting theSC.STD.POS.TRANSFParameter Record

To create a record in SC.BULK.TRANSFER , the user must set the Ofs Source and Ofs Version fields in the SC.STD.POS.TRANSF application. It is possible to parameterise the default charge category for the bulk charges. The security and funds transfer generated from the bulk transfer can be either authorised or unauthorised, based on the values in SC.STD.POS.TRANSF . The bulk transfer related fields are explained in the following table:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Ft Pl Chg Cat | Accepts a valid PL Category (50000 to 69999). If a single charge is collected for a bulk transfer and the Charge Account field is not set in SC.BULK.TRANSFER , then the PL Category given in this field is defaulted to Charge Account |
| Fund Trans Status | Accepts the values NAU and AUTH. It specifies the record status to which the FUNDS.TRANSFER record is moved on authorising the SC.BULK.TRANSFER record. If this field value is left blank, the FUNDS.TRANSFER record is changed to IHLD status. The value in this field is defaulted in the Fund Trans Status field of the SC.BULK.TRANSFER application |
| Sec Trans Status | Accepts the values NAU and HOLD. It specifies the record status to which the SECURITY.TRANSFER records is moved on authorising the SC.BULK.TRANSFER record. If this field value is left blank, the SECURITY.TRANSFER record is authorised. The value in this field is defaulted in the Sec Trans Status field of the SC.BULK.TRANSFER application |


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains booking transactions in Temenos Transact using the POSITION.TRANSFER and SECURITY.TRANSFER applications.


##### POSITION.TRANSFER

The POSITION.TRANSFER transaction moves single or multiple positions from one portfolio account to another or from one depository to another. For example, a customer may decide to move some of his holdings to other portfolios, or move some or all of his holdings from one custodian to another.

All securities belonging to portfolio 100297-1 are transferred to portfolio 100297-2 as shown in the below screenshot. Though the wholesale transfer between different portfolios of different customers are rare, the flexibility of such a transaction is shown below. This scenario would require an override to effect the input.

The POSITION.TRANSFER application is used for the following scenarios:

- Transfer some or all positions from one portfolio to another portfolio belonging to a different customer.
- Transfer some or all positions of one portfolio from one depository to another.
- Transfer some or all positions to a customer with more than one portfolio from one depository to another.
- Transfer some or all positions from one sub-account to another.

The following fields have to be setup in POSITION.TRANSFER :

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Auto Select | This field is set to Y to display all the security positions relating to the selection criteria and the system makes the required changes (like nominal amount and so on). If this field is left blank, the whole position within the specified criteria is transferred |
| Exchange | This field is set to either Effective or Trade. The options are explained below: Effective - Select this option to use the exchange rate on the trade date of the transfer transaction Trade - Select this option to use the exchange rate on the trade dates of the underlying trade transactions |
| Trans Type Dr Trans Type Cr | The values are defaulted from the Sec Dr Trans Code and Sec Cr Trans Code fields in SC.STD.POS.TRANSF . The values in both the Trans Type Dr and Trans Type Cr fields are used as transaction codes for debiting and crediting STOCK. These fields allow a valid record in SC.TRANS.NAME . The settlement instructions can also be defaulted for both From and To depositories in the Depository From and Depository To field. |

When positions are transferred between portfolios or depositories, banks can decide whether the system should default the average gross cost (purchase price) or average net cost (purchase price + commissions and charges) in the Price field in the POSITION.TRANSFER application by setting the Pos Transf Price field in SC.STD.POS.TRANSF to Gross or Null.

When the Pos Transf Price field is set to Gross and then when the positions are transferred from one portfolio to another or from one depository to another, the system defaults the average gross (Purchase) price of the acquired nominals. The Gross Cost Sec Ccy field in SECURITY.POSITION is used to calculate the average gross price of the underlying nominals. When the Pos Transf Price field is set to Null, the system uses the average cost price. This cost price is calculated based on the value in the Cost Inv Sec Ccy field in SECURITY.POSITION .

| Defaulted from Depository To field | Defaulted from Depository From field |
|---|---|
| Rece Agent | Deli Agent |
| Rece Agent Ac | Deli Agent Ac |
| Buyr | Seller |
| Buyr Ac | Seller Ac |
| Rece Cus | Deli Cus |
| Rece Cus Ac | Deli Cus Ac |
| Rece Pl Code | Deli Pl Code |
| Rece Pl Safekeep | Deli Pl Safekeep |
| To Pset | From Pset |

The authorised records of POSITION.TRANSFER cannot be amended. The original transaction must be reversed and a new transaction has to be input to handle the amendments. However, there might be differences between the changes in the transactions of an exchange rate, as it is not possible to input the exchange rates in a transfer.

The fields in POSITION.TRANSFER enable the input of contra transactions, if amendments are required. The To Contra Ref field specifies whether the transfer entered is a contra to an existing transaction and the transaction reference of the original transfer. The Contra By Ref field specifies the transaction reference of the contra transfer on the original transaction. These fields support the entry of contra transactions through versions. The versions and the associated version routines populate the transaction details of the original transaction on the contra transaction. The version details are not part of the release, but sample versions are available in the data library, which can be downloaded and configured onsite. The sample version records are generic and local developments may be required to tailor them, so that they are suitable for the business environment of these records.

For a faster bulk transfer of 50 and more positions, system uses the SC.BULK.POSITION.TRANSFER service. The No of Position field is set to 50 by default. The user can also input a number which is less than 100 (maximum allowed value for this field). If the number of positions to be transferred exceeds the number in this field, then the system is forced to use the SC.BULK.POSITION.TRANSFER service. Otherwise, the transfer goes through without a service.

The POSITION.TRANSFER application is also used to transfer a position to a sub-account. The Sub Account To field accepts the sub-account to be transferred to, which must be a valid sub-account defined for the depository, to which the position is to be transferred. If this field has a valid value, then the selected position is moved to this sub-account irrespective of the default setting in SC.SUB.ACC.ROUTING . If this field is left blank, then the Sub Account To field is defaulted based on the setting in SC.SUB.ACC.ROUTING . However, if the position has to be moved from one sub-account to no sub-account, the user must set this field to NULL. The system does not default any sub-account even if any defaulting is setup in SC.SUB.ACC.ROUTING for the portfolio position that is being transferred.

The Beneficial Owner Change field indicates whether there is a change in the beneficial ownership as a result of the transfer. If this field is set to Y, then stamp tax is calculated for all the transfers. The Bene Change Reason field in POSITION.TRANSFER records the reason for the change in beneficiary ownership. This field is linked to SC.OWNER.CHG.REASON in which the customers can add the required reasons. From this field, the reason is mapped to the respective tags in the settlement messages generated from the respective internal asset transfers. This field is also available in SECURITY.TRANSFER .

Whenever there is a change in ownership, the Beneficial Owner Change field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER and POSITION.TRANSFER applications are populated. If this field is populated and the reason for change in ownership is not provided in the Bene Change Reason field, the system displays an override, to alert the user.

Commission and tax can be levied as part of position transfer (internal asset transfer), where there is change in ownership. The commission can be levied either as:

- Flat fee
- Fee based on customer group and group conditions

The commission and tax for position transfer is calculated using the following steps:

- The user inputs a single flat commission for all the positions transferred in the Flat Commission field.
- Provide the respective commission category) in the Flat Commission Code field.
- The tax on commission is calculated based on the Tax Code field (defined in the respective FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ) given in the Flat Commission Code field.
- The calculated tax amount is captured in the Flat Tax field and the respective tax code is updated in the Flat Tax Code field.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Flat Tax and Flat Tax Code fields are no-input fields.

- The charges are calculated only when the portfolios in the From Portfolio and To Portfolio fields belong to different customers.
- The calculated commission and tax are charged against the account in the Charge Acc field. This field is defaulted with the first local currency account of the portfolio from which the positions are transferred out, that is, the local currency account pertaining to the portfolio in the From Portfolio field. The user can overwrite the Charge Acc field value by providing a different local currency account.

Commission and tax are defined based on the asset or sub-asset types for each position transferred for every customer group using the SCTR.GROUP.CONDITION application. The Pos Transf Comm field is set to Yes in SC.STD.POS.TRANSF to default the commission and tax in position transfer based on group conditions.

For a particular customer group, the commission rates for different asset or sub-asset types are defined in the SCTR.GROUP.CONDITION application. The Trade Activity field in the SCTR.GROUP.CONDITION application is set to POSITION.TRANSFER to charge commission and tax. The asset or sub-asset types and their respective commission codes are setup using the Security Type and Charge Comm Code fields.

Based on the record in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE defined for the asset or sub-asset type for a customer group in SCTR.GROUP.CONDITION , the commission for the respective security position transferred is calculated and stored in the Commission field in POSITION.TRANSFER . The respective commission code is stored in the Commission Code field in POSITION.TRANSFER .

The tax on the commission is calculated based on the Tax Code field defined for the respective FT.COMMISSION.TYPE using which the commission for the position transferred was computed. The Tax field captures the tax amount and the respective tax code is stored in the Tax Code field. The commission and tax related fields are manually amended by the bank user and once amended, the system does not default the calculated commission or tax amount.

For each position transferred, a consolidated debit entry is raised against the customer’s account for commission and tax. On the bank’s side, individual credit entries are generated against the bank’s P&L and internal tax account per position that is transferred.


##### SECURITY.TRANSFER

The SECURITY.TRANSFER application transfers securities in or out of a customer’s portfolio account, either against payment or free of payment. It is envisaged that this transaction is used to transfer securities, when a customer’s portfolio is being transferred or setup for the first time in the bank's system.

It may also be used to transfer securities in or out, where a bank’s customer deals directly with a broker (referred to as third party deals or off-market trades). Depository advice for the security movement can be generated from the application. The below screenshot shows a record in SECURITY.TRANSFER .

After a transfer is authorised, only the Price field can be amended. The Charges and Local Tax fields (which are defaulted based on the customer charge conditions that are set for SC.TRADING ) can be amended. The SECURITY.TRANSFER application also supports input of additional charges and tax in the Cu Commission and Cu Tax fields. The categories or accounts to which the additional commission and tax are posted is defined in the SC.STD.POS.TRANSF application.

The customer tax amount is posted to an internal account in the local currency. The Cu Tax Scy field in SC.STD.POS.TRANSF must be set to YES, to post the customer tax amount to an internal account in the security currency. The exchange rate between the customer account currency and security currency takes the buy or sell rate based on the transaction. The exchange rate can also use the mid-rate by setting the Def Mid Rate field in SC.STD.POS.TRANSF to YES.

The Cum Ex Ind field specifies the price conditions applicable to the transaction. To allow input in the Cum Ex Ind field, the Price Qual Format field in SM.PARAMETER must be set to SWIFT. The value entered in the Cum Ex Ind field affects the holding balance for a corporate event and it is validated against the Cum Indicate and Ex Indicate fields in SM.PARAMETER . This depends on the parameter setup within the corporate actions (CA). Read Corporate Actions User Guide for more information.

The Sc Bulk Trans Id field is used to record the bulk transfer-out ID from which SECURITY.TRANSFER is generated. The Buyr Seller Ac field defaults the values of either Buyr Ac or Sell Ac fields in the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT application.

The Pl Code and Pl Safekeep fields record the place of settlement and safe keep of the security respectively. These fields are defaulted from the record in SC.SETT.INSTRUCT . This record is fetched based on the Ssi Code , Broker Addr Bic and Broker No fields in SECURITY.TRANSFER . Read Standard Settlement Instruction for Broker for more information on the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT application.

The following fields are used to map SWIFT MT540 to MT543 settlement instruction messages:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Stamp Indicator | Defaults from SC.SETT.INSTRUCT based on the broker transaction code. . The user can overwrite this field value. The value must be in AAAA/BBBB or BBBB format and is mapped to 22F tag, stamp duty indicator in sequence E of MT54X (X= 0 to 3). This is a free format field and requires no validation |
| Stamp Price | Defines the user input stamp price which is mapped to 90B tag of TRADDET block in MT54X (X= 0 TO 3) instead of using the existing broker price |
| Sprty Narr Qual | Indicates the qualifier pertaining to narrative in 70A tag of the SETPRTY block in MT540 to MT543 |
| Sprty Narr | Indicates the free format narrative mapped to 70A tag of the SETPRTY block in MT540 to MT543. If the narrative is entered with the qualifier DECL or PACO, it is mapped to 70E or 70C tag, respectively in the SETPRTY block. |
| Bene Owner | Indicates the user-defined beneficial owner. It is mapped to 22F tag qualifier BENE in SETDET block. The value must be entered as per the SWIFT guidelines. |
| Buyr Nation | Indicates the user-defined country code of the buyer. It is mapped to the 95C tag in the qualifier INVE of the OTHRPRTY block |

The user can suppress the instructions or advices to customers, brokers, depositories or any combinations by updating the corresponding field values as YES or NO appropriately, as shown in the below screenshot. The default value for these fields are controlled by the Advice Default field in the SC.PARAMETER application.

| Field | Functionality |
|---|---|
| Event | Defines the TRANSFER option to calculate stamp tax for the SECURITY.TRANSFER application |
| Sec Domicile | Defines the valid country |
| Stock Exchange | Defines the valid stock exchange |
| Sec Master | Defines the valid SECURITY.MASTER record |
| Asset Sub Asset | Defines the valid asset or sub-asset type |

It is also possible to have any number of different charges and taxes in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application using the multiple charges framework. Read Transaction Fees, Taxes and Charges feature for more detail on the setup and calculation.

A customer’s security position is not updated until the actual receipt of inward free SECURITY.TRANSFER . This functionality is used along with the contractual and actual settlement method to update the record in SECURITY.POSITION , only after the nominal is actually settled.

The Sect Pend field in SC.PARAMETER controls this functionality. This field accepts any one of the following values:

- Yes – If this option is selected, only SECURITY.TRANSFER is subject to processing.
- Post – If this option is selected, both SECURITY.TRANSFER and POSITION.TRANSFER are subject to processing.

Irrespective of the option selected in this field, the associated Sc Trans Name field allows the user to identify the transaction types that are subject to this processing.

The below screenshot displays a SECURITY.TRANSFER transaction with the Transaction Type field set to TPI. Therefore, this is treated as a pending free receipt.

The above transaction is also processed through the contractual or actual process. This creates a record in SC.SETTLEMENT upon authorisation. The Free Nom Pend field in SECURITY.POSITION is updated instead of the Closing Bal No Nom field.

As the securities are not available, they are not included in portfolio valuations, CAs, and hence errors or warning messages are not generated, while processing the securities orders and transactions. The Free Nom Pend field is cleared and the Closing Bal No Nom is updated when the securities are delivered and settled using the SC.SETTLEMENT process and the nominals are settled.

When the Sect Pend field is set to Post, POSITION.TRANSFER with transaction type defined in SC.TRANS.NAME undergoes the processing. When a POSITION.TRANSFER is placed, the Free Nom Pend field in SECURITY.POSITION is updated for both source and target portfolio. Only after the settlement of the POSITION.TRANSFER , both the source and target portfolio are updated with nominal in Closing Bal No Nom field in SECURITY.POSITION . The Sec Hold Settle field must be set to Yes, for the processing to be applicable.


##### Bulk Transfers

There are two types of transfers: Bulk security transfer and bulk custodian transfer that are explained below.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Trans Type | Determines the type of transaction. This is a mandatory field and its value is mapped to Transaction Type field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application |
| Portfolio No | Accepts a valid portfolio in which the movement of securities take place. This is a mandatory field and its value is mapped to Security Acc field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application |
| Counterparty | Identifies sender or receiver of the transfer. This field accepts a valid customer from the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application. The role of the customer has to be BROKER, COUNTERPARTY or CLIENT. It is mapped to the Broker No field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application |
| Payment Reqd | Maps to the Payment Reqd field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application |
| Broker Advice Reqd | Maps to the Broker Advice Reqd field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application |
| Nominee Code | Maps to the Nominee Code field of the SECURITY.TRANSFER application |
| Cust Remarks | Maps to the Cust Remarks field of the SECURITY.TRANSFER application |
| Sec Trans Status | Accepts the values NAU and HOLD. The value in this field is defaulted from the Sec Trans Status field of the SC.STD.POS.TRANSF application. If this field values is left blank, then the SECURITY.TRANSFER record is authorised When set to INPUT.INAU, the record in SECURITY.TRANSFER is created in INAU status when the record in SC.BULK.TRANSFER is created in INAU. When record in SC.BULK.TRANSFER is authorised, the record in SECURITY.TRANSFER continues to be in INAU The record in SECURITY.TRANSFER must be authorised individually. If bulk authorisation is required, then the Authorize field can be set to Yes in SC.BULK.TRANSFER application . If the Authorize field is enabled, then the system triggers the service to authorise all records in SECURITY.TRANSFER created by the bulk transfer |
| Fund Trans Status | Accepts the values NAU and AUTH. The value in this field is defaulted from the Fund Trans Status field of the SC.STD.POS.TRANSF application. If this field is left blank, the FUNDS.TRANSFER record is changed to hold status |
| Authorize | Set to Yes to trigger the service to authorise the underlying records in SECURITY.TRANSFER . If a particular record in SECURITY.TRANSFER is already authorised, then that particular record is skipped (not authorised) |
| Ssi Code | Defaults with a valid ID of the SC.SETT.INSTRUCT application. This field is mapped to the Ssi Code field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application |
| Rerun | Accepts the value ENRICH. When set to ENRICH, the value in the Ssi Code field is mapped to SECURITY.TRANSFER application. This can be used to assign a settlement instruction to all the transfers generated out of the bulk transfer. This is useful when a technical broker is used in the transaction and a settlement instruction has to be specified for this particular transaction. A technical broker is used when the counterparty is not on-boarded into the system (as the interaction with the counterparty is one time, banks sometimes prefer not to on-board these counterparties) |
| Transfer Price | Accepts the values Gross or Null. When set to Gross, in the SC.BULK.TRANSFER application, the system populates the average gross price (purchase price) of the acquired nominals in the Price field. This price is mapped to the Price field in the underlying SECURITY.TRANSFER that is created. The Gross Cost Sec Ccy field in SECURITY.POSITION is used to calculate the gross price of the underlying nominals. When set to Null, in the SC.BULK.TRANSFER application, the system populates the market price in the Price field. This field is selected only for Transfer Out scenario, that is, when the Transaction code implies a debit of securities. |

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Transfer Type | Indicates that the transfer is BCT when this field is set to Custodian |
| Depository From | Holds the Custodian Id from whom the position is moved out |
| Sub Account From | Holds the sub-account held with the custodian from whom the position is moved out |
| Sec Account From | Used when position is moved from one portfolio to another portfolio. In such scenario, this holds the portfolio from which the position is moved out. |
| Depository To | Holds the Custodian Id to whom the position is moved to |
| Sub Account To | Holds the sub-account held with the custodian to whom the position is moved to |
| Sec Account To | Used when position is moved from one portfolio to another portfolio. In such cases, this field holds the portfolio id of the Portfolio to which the position is moved to. |
| Bct Security No | Holds the id of the instrument master. This is used when only specific instruments are to be moved. If this field is left blank, all positions held with in the From Custodian field is moved out. This field can be multi-valued to add multiple instruments. |
| Bct Sec Acc Master | Holds the customer security account. Used only when the Bct Security No is input. This field is used to specify the portfolio, which is in scope of this transfer. This is a sub-value field. Multiple portfolios holding the position in Bct Security No can be specified. If this field is left blank, all portfolios holding position in Bct Security No is transferred. |
| Bct Quantity | Holds the quantity associated with Bct Security No and Bct Sec Acc Master . If this field is left blank, the complete holdings of the portfolio on the Bct Security No is transferred out. |

### 5.77  UpfrontPayment IndirectMethod


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In this method, a dummy security is created to handle the upfront payment. The amount paid upfront is treated as investment in a dummy security. Subsequently when the NAV is known, position is moved from the dummy security to the actual fund security. This process is explained in detail in this feat...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Activity*, *Broker Advice Reqd*, *Calculate Chrgs.1*, *Cash Amount.1*, *Client Number*, *Depo Advice Reqd*, *Depository*, *Fund Id* ... +5 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In this method, a dummy security is created to handle the upfront payment. The amount paid upfront is treated as investment in a dummy security. Subsequently when the NAV is known, position is moved from the dummy security to the actual fund security. This process is explained in detail in this feature.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

In order to trade hedge funds for which Net Asset Value (NAV) is not available, the upfront security needs to be created manually. The Upfront Sec field in the SECURITY.MASTER application holds the details of the dummy security that is credited for the customer's portfolio upfront on debit of funds. This field must be setup with a NAV of one currency unit. This upfront security must be attached in the original fund master for which NAV is declared at a later date.

The Upfront Sec field can be defined at the SC.PARAMETER level, instead of creating a dummy (upfront) security for each fund. A generic upfront security can be created for each currency and/or sub-asset type, which is defaulted automatically.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details the upfront payment method using a dummy security.


##### SEC.OPEN.ORDER

In order to process upfront security, the cash security order must be input with the amount to invest. In this order, upfront security is defaulted from SECURITY.MASTER .


##### SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS

The order is executed with a price of one and the nominal is the amount invested against a dummy security master. The execution can be triggered automatically based on incoming acknowledgement (MT509 or its equivalent).


##### SEC.TRADE

Trade is generated against the dummy security with respect to the trade date and value date set for the execution date. Upon trade completion, the dummy security is credited to the customer’s portfolio.

The customer’s cash account is debited as the customer has to pay upfront for the funds and the fund company nostro is credited with the cash settlement. The underlying messages are automatically suppressed and the system defaults the Broker Advice Reqd and Depo Advice Reqd fields to No.

Upon processing the trade, the funds are debited from the customer's account and the customer's portfolio is credited with the dummy security position, as shown in the below screenshots.


##### SC.BUILD.UPFRONT.POSITION

When the NAV is received, the user must update the SC.BUILD.UPFRONT.POSITION record with the details of upfront security and it’s price (NAV), as shown in the below screenshot.

The users can specify a date range, based on which the system automatically selects the trades. When this record is authorised, the system automatically creates payment free SECURITY.TRANSFER transactions in order to transfer out the dummy position and performs another transfer in transaction to create the position in upfront security based on the NAV.

Upon authorising the security transfer, the dummy position is transferred out and a new position is added in the fund security when the NAV is updated as shown in the below screenshot.


##### Upfront Payment on Fund Subscription

NAV for hedge funds and certain types of funds are computed on monthly or quarterly basis. If NAV is not available for a new subscription, a dummy instrument (representing the fund) can be setup in Temenos Transact . As the user has to make upfront payment of the subscriptions amount, update to customer’s position is made with units in the dummy fund. Upon receipt of actual NAV, the system computes the actual units and updates the customer’s position with the actual fund. The Upfront Sec field in SECURITY.MASTER holds the details of the dummy security.


#### 📋 Tasks

In core banking system, a dummy security is created to handle the upfront payment through indirect method. The amount paid upfront is treated as investment and subsequently when the NAV is in a known position is moved from this dummy security to the actual security.


##### Workflow

In Upfront Payment Indirect Method, the user can perform the following activities:

This enquiry displays the list of upfront payment funds available in the core banking system. Further drill-down is available to view the fund details and place new orders.

6. Click the Validate icon.
7. Click the Commit icon.

### 5.78  Vault Control


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The VAULT.CONTROL application maintains the details of certificates and other miscellaneous items on behalf of the bank’s customers. The entry into a vault is direct and anything belonging to the bank (for example, collateral items) may be stored in the strongroom which can be controlled and monitor...*
> 
> **Applications:** `CONTEXT.ENQUIRY`, `CUSTOMER`, `CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `DIARY`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `NOMINEE.CODE`, `POSITION.TRANSFER`, `SC.VAULT` ... +8 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Balance Cert*, *Certificate*, *Certificate No*, *Customer No*, *Depository*, *Memo Account*, *No Nom Date*, *No Nom Recd Del* ... +5 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The VAULT.CONTROL application maintains the details of certificates and other miscellaneous items on behalf of the bank’s customers. The entry into a vault is direct and anything belonging to the bank (for example, collateral items) may be stored in the strongroom which can be controlled and monitored. To enable a wide variety of differing items, the VAULT.CONTROL application contains a free-format narrative field.

The VAULT.PARAMETER application enables the Temenos Transact to identify the security transactions containing depositories for which the bank wants to maintain details. These vaults are mostly ‘on the premises’ but can be extended to outside depositories as well. The main purpose of this application is to handle physical share certificates and to monitor the outstanding balance certificate requests by recording the vault movements pertaining to partial deliveries or receipts.

The following illustration is a typical example of the vault setup in an organisation.

| ID | Description |
|---|---|
| VAULT 1 | Nominee-registered |
| VAULT 2 | Own name registered |
| VAULT 3 | Unregistered |
| VAULT 4 | Miscellaneous items |

The VAULT 1 to 3 involve the movements of securities from Temenos Transact security trades, security transfers, position transfers or certain corporate actions. The VAULT 4 enables the recording of miscellaneous items like sealed envelopes, insurance certificates, collateral items, strong boxes and property deeds. The contents of this vault are entered directly using VAULT.CONTROL . Most of these items belong to private customers and may be allotted an ID for easy and safe tracking.

The splitting of the vault into various areas helps in easier identification of specific items. This also enables easier production of separate entries on statements, enquiries and reports ensuring overall control of the safe custody operation.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The working mechanism of vault and safe-custody control involves the following processes in Temenos Transact .


##### Updating the Vault

To update the vault, a source transaction must request receipt into or withdrawal from one of the depositories specified in the VAULT.PARAMETER application as illustrated in the below screenshot comprising a SECURITY.TRANSFER that expects:

- Nominee Registered - Nominee field is populated with BD1
- Eligible Depository - Depository field in VAULT.PARAMETER application

If the Depository field is set to 5500, the Nominee field remains blank and the system assumes that the securities must be registered in the name of the customer displayed in the Customer No field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application.

The same logic applies for SEC.TRADE , POSITION.TRANSFER and ENTITLEMENT , if the Depository field is updated against the VAULT.PARAMETER record. If the specified depository exists in the VAULT.PARAMETER record, a VAULT.EXPECT record is raised automatically. The below screenshot illustrates how an own name registered transaction is processed.

In this case, the certificate is registered in the name of the customer and not the user entity’s nominee name. The Nominee field is not displayed and the depository ID recorded in the VAULT.PARAMETER record is for the safekeeping of 'own name' registered paper.


##### VAULT.EXPECT

The VAULT.EXPECT record functionality is explained in this section.

The VAULT.EXPECT contains the details of the expectation records. Temenos Transact builds an expectation record to remind that a receipt into or a withdrawal from the vault is required, as soon as a candidate transaction is initiated. The VAULT.EXPECT enables the recording of expectation records regarding any balance certificates as required. This is raised when a VAULT.CONTROL record is used for a later withdrawal of a lesser amount of the security.

The custodian can monitor and control all the entries from other Temenos Transact transactions with an enquiry before the vault is updated to keep a track of the outstanding or overdue receipts. The expectation records update the vault only when sufficient delivery or receipt details are available and then these records are moved to history. These records are designed to allow partial receipts and receipt of a single nominee-registered certificate concerning the multiple beneficial ownership of the underlying security. For example, if a SEC.TRADE record contains 25 customer purchases of a security, with a nominee assigned for all the purchases. Thus, the expectation record contains all the 25 purchases. This is based on the understanding that the custodian expects only a single bulk registered certificate from the registrar although multiple receipts recording is feasible. The below screenshot illustrates a VAULT.EXPECT receipt record.

The expectation details are recorded in the VAULT.EXPECT application until the physical certificate is available and therefore enabling the user to complete the details and the record remains in unauthorised status. The user can monitor the outstanding records and the list of overdue certificates using the standard enquiry. After the user has entered the details, the expectation record is authorised automatically and an unauthorised VAULT.CONTROL record is created. Read the VAULT.CONTROL for more information. The below screenshot displays the remainder of the VAULT.EXPECT record. These fields are used to confirm the receipt or delivery as required.

The completion of receipt expectation records is a simple process, which requires the entry of the details from the source certificates as received. After the arrival of the certificate, the user can complete the VAULT.EXPECT record as shown in the below screenshot.

This straightforward process requires the certificate nominal, certificate number, certificate date and process date. The date in the No Nom Date field is the date of the input but this can be backdated (if required).

> **⚠️ Note:** The VAULT.EXPECT records the receipt and delivery of certificates and the VAULT.CONTROL application controls the movements in the vault.

The completion and authorisation of VAULT.EXPECT builds a VAULT.CONTROL record, which indicates the custodian that the certificates are available to be placed in the vault. After the custodian finds the certificates, the user must locate the relevant VAULT.CONTROL record in INAU status. This can be located either by enquiring on the security ID or certificate number.

The below screenshot illustrates how the INAU status in VAULT.CONTROL application is displayed.

The transaction is authorised to enter in the vault after the certificate indicated in the Certificate No field in VAULT.CONTROL is available.

In case of an own name registered certificate, the VAULT.EXPECT record is built in the same way but the Nominee field is left blank. Instead, the Portfolio No field is populated as displayed in the below screenshot. After the relevant certificates are received, the VAULT.EXPECT is completed in the same way as a nominee-registered certificate.

The committed transaction builds a VAULT.CONTROL record for the custodian to record the receipt of the certificate into the vault. The below screenshot displays the receipt of an own name registered certificate. In this case, the VAULT.CONTROL displays the registered holder in Portfolio No field, rather than a nominee ID in the Nominee field.

Therefore, the custodian may authorise the above record in the normal way, once the certificate identified in the Certificate No field is received.

The following are the different types of withdrawal of certificates for delivery.

The Temenos Transact drill down facility can be used for completing a delivery withdrawal from the vault, though these can be manually completed in the same way as a receipt. This drill down method enables the user to interrogate the vault to locate a suitable certificate. This also indicates when the user has to make a delivery for the customer’s securities registered in a nominee name. For the certificates registered on the own name, the interrogation is done using the customer as part of the search criteria. In both the methods, if the user has located a suitable certificate (or certificates, if necessary), then simply select the VAULT.CONTROL item into the VAULT.EXPECT record. However, whichever method is used the system response depends on the security entered in the No Nom Recd Del field in the VAULT.EXPECT record. For example, if the amount entered is greater than the amount to be satisfied, the user is prompted to specify whether a balance certificate is required. If the No Nom Recd Del field is set to Y, the original VAULT.CONTROL and VAULT.EXPECT records are moved to history and a fresh expectation record for the balance is automatically generated. When the user adds the new details (if required), this new expectation record remains in the unauthorised status as it is pending the receipt of the balance certificate from the registrar.

The user can also drill down to obtain more than one certificate until sufficient certificates are available to satisfy the delivery. The user always attempts to obtain an exact match, but a balance certificate is necessary in most cases. In addition, the user has the option to re-select multiple certificates among the selected list, which can cause the total to be more than required. However, the user can still advise the system for a balance certificate.

If the No Nom Recd Del field in VAULT.EXPECT is set to N, the amount of security delivered is recorded in the original certificate until it is exhausted by further deliveries. After this stage, the record in the VAULT.CONTROL application is moved to history.

The system contains in-built safeguards to prevent the user from using an own-name registered certificate, which satisfies a delivery on behalf of a nominee-registered security. In addition, the user cannot utilise a nominee-registered certificate to satisfy a delivery, which the user wants to make on behalf of an own-name registered security. The user can now extract a certificate from the vault. The below screenshot illustrates how a VAULT.EXPECT record appears for a delivery request.

The user must locate a suitable certificate or certificates, which can be delivered to the registrar to effect the transfer to the new beneficial owner. Therefore, the user must be in INPUT mode, to enable the interrogation of the vault.

To list the suitable certificates, invoke the CONTEXT.ENQUIRY by clicking the 'i' button to the left of the Vcl Reference field. The eligible certificates are listed as shown in the below screenshot.

Select the relevant Eligible Certificates enquiry to list all the eligible certificates currently held in the vault, the certificates listed are used to partly, completely, or over satisfy the delivery. If the delivery is over satisfied, a balance certificate is requested (if necessary).

In the above example, the underlying VAULT.EXPECT locates a certificate to enable a delivery of 600 shares (third item). The below screenshot displays the copy function performed in the certificate chosen to satisfy the delivery. In this case, the total shares matches exactly with the number of shares to be delivered.

The required ID is pasted into the source transaction using the pointer device in the Vcl Reference field of the VAULT.EXPECT application as shown in the below screenshot.

Then the user may either validate or commit the transaction. In this example, commit is requested. The system validates the selected certificate the transaction is committed, as the VAULT.EXPECT transactions are self-authorised.

When a single certificate does not satisfy a delivery request, multiple certificates are located as shown in the below example where, the user has to deliver 1,000 shares. The vault certificates for nominal 355 and 655 are chosen to suit the needs.

The CONTEXT.ENQUIRY is launched to locate the suitable certificates for the security in question.

The required ID is pasted into the source transaction using the pointer device in the Vcl Reference field of the VAULT.EXPECT application. The above screenshot displays two available certificates for 345 Shares and 655 Shares. These two share sum up to 1,000, which the user wants to deliver. The Vcl Reference field is expanded to repeat the action for the next certificate.

The above screenshot shows that the transaction can be committed. The VAULT.EXPECT application is self-authorised and the underlying VAULT.CONTROL records satisfy the delivery, and the service agent writes the delivery to the history table. The below screenshot confirms that the certificates have satisfied the delivery of 1000 shares.

The balance certificate request is raised, when a suitable certificate is not available to match the withdrawal amount. In such cases, a certificate for a greater number than actually required can be withdrawn after the registrar provides a balance certificate. The Temenos Transact system indicates if the balance certificate is required. For a transaction with balance certificate, a new expectation record is built for the receipt of the balance after the delivery is committed in the VAULT.EXPECT application.

The process of multiple certificates for delivery is applicable for the balance certificates as well. The following screenshot displays a delivery request with a balance certificate. In this example, the user searches for the certificate(s) to satisfy a delivery of 750 shares, registered in the nominee name.

The CONTEXT.ENQUIRY is launched to display the list of eligible certificates that may be used to satisfy the delivery request as shown in the below screenshot.

If only one certificate is available for 1,500 shares, then copy the value of Certificate field (using the pointer device) and paste into the Vcl Reference field in the VAULT.EXPECT (as shown in the below screenshot).

The certificate of 1,500 shares is used to satisfy a delivery requirement of only 750 shares. The user requires a balance certificate for the remaining 750 shares. To ensure this, an expectation record is built for the 750 shares. The user must validate the value in the Balance Cert field in the VAULT.EXPECT application, before committing the transaction.

The system validates the selected certificate the transaction is committed, as the VAULT.EXPECT transactions are self-authorised.

> **⚠️ Note:** The service agent for vault processing must be active for locating the VAULT.EXPECT records in history table and building the balance certificates to be processed by the TSA.SERVICE .

The user can validate the expectation record, which is built as a new VAULT.EXPECT for the remaining 750 shares, which are to be returned to the vault. In the below screenshot, the VAULT.EXPECT record (ID as SECTSC0304300013.BD1.BAL) indicates that the transaction has a balance certificate request.

Now the VAULT.EXPECT may be treated just the same as a normal receipt of a certificate, by entering the required details once the actual certificate is received in hand.

> **⚠️ Note:** A VAULT.EXPECT record, cannot be authorised until fully satisfied. For any partial receipts, it is mandatory that the total receipts matches the expected number of shares and only then, the VAULT.EXPECT can be authorised. The VAULT.EXPECT record cannot be over-satisfied and an error message is displayed, if the user attempts to do so.


##### VAULT.CONTROL

The VAULT.CONTROL record has the details of the vaults setup in the VAULT.PARAMETER application. The VAULT.CONTROL can only be updated either manually by the user or automatically by certain Temenos Transact security transactions that meet the selection criteria, which is defined in the VAULT.PARAMETER application.

The VAULT.CONTROL record functionality is explained in this section.

Temenos Transact builds an expectation record and does not automatically update the vault, as soon as a candidate transaction with a depository (which is recorded in the VAULT.PARAMETER application) is raised. These records are maintained in the VAULT.EXPECT application and has the details of the expected vault entry, which may be either a receipt or delivery (withdrawal) of securities.

The vault enables the user to keep track of the location of specific securities, certificates and other items of value and does not support cash. The below screenshot displays a VAULT.CONTROL record of a nominee-registered certificate. A certificate registered in an own name is indicated by the value in the Portfolio No field and it depends on the source transaction.

For example, a SEC.TRADE defaults the securities bought and sold on behalf of the organisation’s customers to the nominee name provided, as follows:

1. The underlying SECURITY.MASTER record is setup for the default depository to be displayed in the Default Depository field.
2. This depository is recorded in the VAULT.PARAMETER application.
3. In the VAULT.PARAMETER application, the depository is indicated as a nominee and the nominee code is recorded.

Other applications, such as the corporate actions ( DIARY and ENTITLEMENT ), use the existing holding details to define how the new securities (if any) are to be recorded. For example, if the source securities are nominee-registered, Temenos Transact records the available entitlements similarly.

The VAULT.EXPECT record self-authorises after fully satisfied and builds a VAULT.CONTROL record in INAU status. The VAULT.CONTROL record is authorised only when the expected certificate is confirmed and ready to be deposited into the vault.

As mentioned earlier, Temenos Transact allows the user to enter records directly into the vault. For manual updates, supporting expectation record is not available and the securities destined for the vault, which are received, from another Temenos Transact application creates the expectation records. To record and maintain any item in the vault using Temenos Transact , the user must enter the relevant details into a VAULT.CONTROL record directly, as VAULT.EXPECT is not required for manually controlled items.

The Certificate No field in VAULT.CONTROL categorises the contents of the vault by defining an ID to mark or label the item entered in the vault. Unlike a VAULT.CONTROL record, which arrives automatically through an expectation record, the user can define a beneficial owner (Customer), portfolio (Portfolio No) or a nominee (Nominee Code). Only the user-owned nominee names can be as defined on the NOMINEE.CODE record subjected to override. The below screenshot displays a manually entered VAULT.CONTROL record when entering a miscellaneous item into the vault.

The miscellaneous items remain in the vault for the required time. For the deletion of these items, locate the required VAULT.CONTROL record, validate the details and select the checkbox of the Remove field. After the transaction is authorised, the VAULT.CONTROL record is processed by the TSA service agent and is sent to the history table.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Remove and Release Marker fields have different functionalities. The Release Marker field indicates the deletion of a non-manual item from the vault before the authorisation of the withdrawal transaction by building VAULT.EXPECT record. The Remove field is used to withdraw any item that was lodged in the vault directly using the VAULT.CONTROL application.

The manual updating method is preferably used for recording the miscellaneous items. If the organisation holds securities on behalf of any customer, the user can only ensure the timely control and monitoring of any collections (proceeds of dividends, coupons and maturities) by entering the securities in the SECURITY.TRANSFER application. Read the Securities Application User Guide for more information.

The user must set up memo only portfolios to group and record securities belonging to non-portfolio customers without any accounting. To setup a memo only portfolio, the user must set the Memo Account field in the customer’s SEC.ACC.MASTER application to Y. This eliminates the need to record the details of the customer’s cash accounts.


##### Vault Enquiries

Only one enquiry is available for the user to interrogate any of the depositories defined in the VAULT.PARAMETER application.

The List of Certificates in Vault ( SC.VAULT ) enquiry, enables the user to locate the items held, using a number of selection criteria (as shown in the below screenshot). In the below example, the user can locate all certificates held for the SECURITY.MASTER ID 003615-000 under the user entity’s nominee name. These are held in the depository 5502.

Once this enquiry is launched and the required selection criteria are set, a list of items are displayed (as shown in the below screenshot).

There are two certificates of 1,500 and 750 shares, totaling to 2,250 shares.

In the case of own name registered certificates, the selection criteria must indicate which share issue to be enquired. The input of the vault is not necessary as the enquiry sorts the value of each vault to differentiate own name and nominee-registered certificates.


#### 🔧 Working With

Before Temenos Transact begins to control the contents of the vault, it is mandatory to complete the configuration of the VAULT.PARAMETER application, which enables the system to identity the vault(s), depositories or areas within the vault.

A VAULT.PARAMETER record is required for each company to use the vault application facilities provided by Temenos Transact . The vaults must also be setup on the CUSTOMER and CUSTOMER.SECURITY records before they are defined in the VAULT.PARAMETER application.

The VAULT.CONTROL application enables the user to record the physical movements of the securities within the vault. The details of the actual securities retained in the bank’s vault can be updated here.

### 5.80  COB


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Sections:** ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This feature detects lock collision in a batch and diverts the allocated agents to the parallel batches that are running in the same stage during COB. This reduces lock collisions during a job processing.


##### Threshold Setup

A field Lock Retry Threshold is configured in TSA.PARAMETER . This is an editable field and can accept any valid numeric value greater than zero. It specifies the maximum number of times the batch can be retried and assigned to the agents, before it is skipped to the next batch in the same stage.


##### Example

The following example shows that the system can keep track of number of times a lock contention is encountered with the help of a field ( Lock Retry Count ) in the BATCH application. This is possible only if you configure the threshold in TSA.PARAMETER .

The latest value from Lock Retry Count in BATCH is compared to the threshold value setup in TSA.PARAMETER , before allocating agents to a batch. If the threshold is breached for a batch and if there are other incomplete batches in the same batch stage, then those batches are processed before allocating an agent to the batch encountering the locking contentions.

> **⚠️ Note:** We do not proceed to the next batch stage before all the batches in the current stage are completed and this feature does not override the current batch stage.


#### 📋 Tasks

This feature allows posting a message into an activation file or in a queue when a transaction is done through version.

When a transaction is processed through a version, the Link Activation field is enabled at version level or in VERSION.CONTROL . The activation file or queue is then updated based on the configuration maintained in the EB.VERSION.ACTIVATION.LINK application. This allows you to achieve communication through activation table and helps avoid writing the local code.

The EB.VERSION.ACTIVATION.LINK application contains the service name and job to be used for updating activation table. This application also allows you to configure ID and message to update activation file. If you do not configure ID, then a unique ID will be generated and updated in the activation file.


##### Enable Link Activation

Enabling link activation for a version or VERSION.CONTROL allows you to update the activation file. You cannot disable the link activation after enabling it and configuring the EB.VERSION.ACTIVATION.LINK application. However, you can disable the link activation by reversing the EB.VERSION.ACTIVATION.LINK record.


##### Setting up Services

You need to create an EB.VERSION.ACTIVATION.LINK record to specify the service and job required to update the activation file.

To setup Services, Specify Queue Service and Queue Name . These are mandatory fields. Set Emit Reversal to Yes in the EB.VERSION.ACTIVATION.LINK table. This is done to update the activation file for reversal transactions. Optional: You can set multiple queue services to update multiple activation files at the same time. Authorise the record.


##### Updating the Activation File

This section shows you how to update the activation file using version and EB.VERSION.ACTIVATION.LINK .

To update the activation file, Enable the Link Activation field in the VERSION.CONTROL record. Configure the EB.VERSION.ACTIVATION.LINK record as shown below. Message to the activation file is picked from the Queue Message field. Set Activation File to Yes in PGM.FILE . Perform a transaction using the version. The activation file is updated as below.


##### Updating a Priority File

To update a Priority File, Enable the Link Activation field in the VERSION.CONTROL record. Set Queue Priority to Yes in EB.VERSION.ACTIVATION.LINK . Set Priority File to Yes and specify the Priority Table Name field in PGM.FILE . The Activation file is updated as below.


##### Updating a Queue

Open TSA.PARAMETER and set Queue Jobs to ALL or the required job name.

The queue gets updated with the following details when a transaction is done through a version for which Link Activation is enabled and EB.VERSION.ACTIVATION.LINK is sent.

### 5.82  Queues


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This section explains how queues can improve the processing time for large select jobs.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

This section explains how queues can improve the processing time for large select jobs.

When a service is run, agents allocated to it need not wait for the selected agent to complete the service. Instead, processing of request happens in parallel when initial set of IDs are available in a queue. The IDs are flushed to the queue once 10 records are available or based on the commit size. The commit size is calculated based on the TSA.PARAMETER or PGM.FILE configuration. This reduces the processing time taken for jobs with larger select.

Dynamic bulking is done internally for queue jobs and is excluded when:

- Total writes exceeds 500.
- Count of lock time out exceeds the value configured in the F.LOCKING record ( TIMEOUT.COUNT ).
- Last commit time exceeds review time interval.
- There are activation or online services.
- There are jobs with fixed bulk number.


##### Prerequisites

Before you begin, you should have the following components available in your system:

- TAFJ
- All application servers
- Active MQ broker attached to database


##### Setting up Application Server

Procedure

1. Deploy the following WAR files in the deployments folder. TAFJEE.war , TAFJJEE_Micro and TAFJConfiguration.war are available in TAFJ\appserver\micro . You can use this location to copy and deploy in standalone.
2. Add the following system properties in T24.xml .
3. Add the connection definition and transaction support properties for active MQ setup as shown below:

2. Run InstallService.bat from bin. This starts the service.
3. Add the following properties in the activemq.xml file ( AMQ_HOME/conf ) and restart the broker service.
4. services.msc and open the ActiveMQ service properties.
5. Verify that Startup type is set to Automatic .
6. Start the service.
7. Use the http://localhost:8161/admin/ URL to verify if ActiveMQ is running. Log in using account admin and password admin .

temn.tafj.runtime.services.queue.pull.timeout=100

- Specify batch job to enable queue processing for a particular job in the batch. For example, BNK/SYSTEM.END.OF.DAY3-IC.COB . > **📇 Quick Reference Card**

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The System Tables user guide explains the Customer and related reference tables and the Core Reference tables.

- Customer and related reference tables – This includes the following: The customer application and associated static tables. The customer centric functionalities.
- Core Reference tables – This includes core tables that act as reference for transaction processing as listed below: Country and related tables (like REGION , HOLIDAY and DATES ) Currency Category Interest related tables (like Accrual Parameter, Interest Basis, Basic Interest and Periodic Interest) Charge related tables Tax related tables Card Management tables Cheque Management tables Treasury and Settlements related tables Other Core Reference Tables


#### Product Configuration

The following system-wide applications help in grouping the customers and defining rules for the group based on the business purposes, like defining customer group specific charges and tax.

- CONDITION.PRIORITY
- XXX.GEN.CONDITION and XXX.GROUP.CONDITION, where XXX refers to the business application.
- APPL.GEN.CONDITION


##### Condition Priority

The purpose of the CONDITION.PRIORITY application is to specify, for certain applications, which data elements in other reference applications can be specified to determine condition groups. CONDITION.PRIORITY records can be created with the following IDs:

- ACCOUNT
- FIDUCIARY
- FUNDS.TRANSFER
- FX.MARGIN
- LETTER.OF.CREDIT
- SC.MANAGEMENT
- SC.SAFEKEEPING
- SC.TRADING
- STATEMENT
- TAX
- POR.TRANSACTION

CONDITION.PRIORITY is a CUS level application. Records of this application can be shared between companies, which share the same customer company, or there could be company-specific CONDITION.PRIORITY records by suffixing a hyphen and a Company Code in the ID.

For the

application, it is possible to have a specific record for the Company DE0010001 with the ID ACCOUNT-DE0010001.

The (parameters) records without a Company ID suffixed is applicable to the Master Customer Company (specified as Customer Company in the COMPANY application) as well as to Companies that do not have their own CONDITION.PRIORITY records.

An existing CONDITION.PRIORITY record cannot be modified. However, it is possible to specify parameters that are applicable in future (after the COB processing on a specified date, which can be either the processing date or any future date) by creating CONDITION.PRIORITY records by suffixing a hyphen and a date after the company code in the ID.

The record with ID ’ACCOUNT--20040702’ (with a null Company ID for the customer company) is applicable to the Master Customer Company and the record with ID ‘ACCOUNT-DE0010001-20040702’ is applicable to the Company DE0010001, both records to be effective after the COB processing on 2nd July 2004. The date specified can either be the processing date or it could be a future date.

It is possible to specify the priority items (fields) using the Priority Item field. This is a multi-valued field which defines the order in which fields are used, when matching conditions against values specified in the XXX.GEN.CONDITION records.

- Fields from CUSTOMER application can be specified in all CONDITION.PRIORITY records.
- Fields from ACCOUNT application can be specified only in the CONDITION.PRIORITY records related to ACCOUNT or STATEMENT.
- Fields from SEC.ACC.MASTER can be specified only in the three CONDITION.PRIORITY records related to Wealth application (with IDs SC.MANAGEMENT, SC.SAFEKEEPING and SC.TRADING).

The priority items specified in the CONDITION.PRIORITY records are defaulted as the field names in the corresponding XXX.GEN.CONDITION records.

While determining the condition groups of applications, the priority of the data items (specified as Priority Item ) is determined by their relative position in the CONDITION.PRIORITY record.

For each priority item specified in CONDITION.PRIORITY , users can also specify a validation, which ensures that a value entered for a priority item (in XXX.GEN.CONDITION applications) exists as a record ID in another table. This can also be used to display an enrichment when the value is entered.

In the

record for

, the

CATEGORY’ can have a validation specified in the

DESCRIPTION’. In this case, when a value for the CATEGORY is entered in

, the value entered should be a valid record ID in the

application, and the value of the

field in that

record will be displayed as an enrichment.


##### Parameters and Rules for Groups

The XXX.GEN.CONDITION applications provide the parameters to calculate the default groups for some applications. The priority data items, which are used in the XXX.GEN.CONDITION tables, are defaulted from the corresponding CONDITION.PRIORITY records.

The XXX.GEN.CONDITION applications and the corresponding CONDITION.PRIORITY records from which the priority data items are defaulted are listed below:

| XXX.GEN.CONDITION Applications | CONDITION.PRIORITY record ID from which priority data items are defaulted |
|---|---|
| ACCT.GEN.CONDITION | ACCOUNT |
| FD.GEN.CONDITION | FIDUCIARY |
| FT.GEN.CONDITION | FUNDS.TRANSFER |
| LC.GEN.CONDITION | LETTER.OF.CREDIT |
| SCPM.GEN.CONDITION | SC.MANAGEMENT |
| SCSK.GEN.CONDITION | SC.SAFEKEEPING |
| SCTR.GEN.CONDITION | SC.TRADING |
| STMT.GEN.CONDITION | STATEMENT |
| TAX.GEN.CONDITION | TAX |
| FX.GEN.CONDITION | FX.MARGIN |
| PP.GEN.CONDITION | POR.TRANSACTION |

The parameters specified in FD.GEN.CONDITION , FT.GEN.CONDITION , LC.GEN.CONDITION , SCPM.GEN.CONDITION , SCSK.GEN.CONDITION , SCTR.GEN.CONDITION , TAX.GEN.CONDITION , and PP.GEN.CONDITION are used to default the condition groups in the CUSTOMER.CHARGE application.

The parameters specified in ACCT.GEN.CONDITION are used to default the account group ( Condition Group ) in ACCOUNT , while those specified in STMT.GEN.CONDITION are used to default the frequency in ACCOUNT.STATEMENT .

For each XXX.GEN.CONDITION application, there is a corresponding XXX.GROUP.CONDITION application (except for STMT.GEN.CONDITION ) to define the various parameters for each group. The following XXX.GROUP.CONDITION applications exist:

- ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION
- FD.GROUP.CONDITION
- FT.GROUP.CONDITION
- LC.GROUP.CONDITION
- SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION
- SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION
- SCTR.GROUP.CONDITION
- TAX.TYPE.CONDITION
- FX.GROUP.CONDITION

All the XXX.GEN.CONDITION and XXX.GROUP.CONDITION applications referred here are of the FTD level, which may be company specific or shared between companies depending on the configuration of Default Finan Com or Spcl Fin File fields in the COMPANY record.

If the FTD type files for the Company DE0010001 are unique, then the

records for the Company DE0010001 can have the data items defaulted from the

record with ID as ‘ACCOUNT-DE0010001’ if that record exists, else from the default

record with ID as ‘ACCOUNT’.

While defining CONDITION.PRIORITY records to be applicable in future, it is possible to specify which XXX.GEN.CONDITION and XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records need to be retained, by specifying their IDs in the Gen Cond Keep and Group Cond Keep fields respectively. During COB processing on the specified date, these XXX.GEN.CONDITION records are automatically modified with priority data items applicable for the new structure, by retaining existing priority data items and their values. New priority data items are updated with null values.

Further, in conjunction with dated CONDITION.PRIORITY records, it is also possible to specify dated XXX.GEN.CONDITION records, which can become effective in future. Such XXX.GEN.CONDITION records are defined by suffixing a hyphen with a date (either processing date or a future date) in the ID. Priority data items in these records are defaulted from the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY records. These record IDs must not be defined as retention record IDs in the Gen Cond Keep field of CONDITION.PRIORITY .

After COB processing on the specified date, the dated XXX.GEN.CONDITION records replace the corresponding records without a date in the ID.

Those XXX.GEN.CONDITION records that are not included in the Gen Cond Keep field of the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY record or those records that do not have a corresponding dated XXX.GEN.CONDITION record are dropped after the COB processing on the specified date.

With the exceptions described below, future dated XXX.GROUP.CONDITION can be created with an ID of the format ‘xxx-Date’, provided the ID is not already specified in the Group Cond Keep field of the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY record. After COB processing on the specified date, the dated XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records replace the corresponding records without a date in the ID.

There is an exception to the above referred functionality (which existed before the CONDITION.PRIORITY application has been enhanced to accept dated records). The ID format of the SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION and SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION applications is ‘xxx.date’ (both parts mandatory and connected by a dot) to allow definition of parameters, which applies on various dates. The first part of the ID is validated against the first part of the corresponding XXX.GEN.CONDITION records. When the records in these applications are entered, there is no validation against the CONDITION.PRIORITY records.

The XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records whose IDs are not included in the Group Cond Keep field of the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY record, or which do not have a corresponding dated XXX.GROUP.CONDITION record (suffixed to the ID with a hyphen and date), will be dropped after the COB processing on the specified date. However, customer-specific XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records with ID format as ‘C-Customer ID’ is not dropped after COB processing.

For Payments, the parameters and conditions applicable for a group of customers is defined in PP.CLIENT.CONDITIONRECORD application. Please read Introduction to Client Conditions for more details.


##### Parameter to Default Groups UsingTemenos TransactRoutine

The APPL.GEN.CONDITION application is used to define group conditions for contracts based on a combination of decisions and calls to locally developed subroutines. For example, it allows specific tax codes to be applied to particular types of contract for particular types of customer.

There is one record per application for which many sets of group conditions can be defined. User must ensure that multiple set of groups are defined correctly, as the first set of conditions that pass the validation checks result in that contract group code being applied.

A Temenos Transact subroutine, APPL.GRP.CONDITION can be called to evaluate the current contract record using relevant APPL.GEN.CONDITON . It returns the first group code where all decision checks evaluate to true.

The MM.MONEY.MARKET and LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSIT applications call the evaluation routine automatically. Other applications can call the evaluation routine from VERSION routines to update local reference fields with the relevant group code.

The subroutine processes these decisions and updates the Contract Group field in the application record whenever the contract is changed. If changes to the contract cause the conditions to break, then a new Contract Group code is generated, which results in a different tax code being applied. A default group code can be defined as the last group code without associated conditions, if required. TAX.TYPE.CONDITION allows the Contract Group code to be linked to the allocation of specific tax codes.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

Specifications for System Tables are grouped into different functionalities.

Core Reference tables available in the model bank are given below:

| S.No. | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | COMPANY | Contains details such as company's name, mnemonic, classification details, applications that are to be run, company level defaults and parameters. |
| 2. | DATES | Each company has a Date record, which contains the run dates for the previous, current and the next working day. Batch (overnight) processing system updates the record automatically. |
| 3. | CONDITION.PRIORITY | Used to specify the data elements to determine the condition groups for each application. In addition, the order of general conditions to be applied when more than one general condition is involved can also be defined. |
| 4. | COUNTRY.GROUP | Used to group the countries based on residence or non-residence when applying charges. |
| 5. | COUNTRY | Contains the static details of each country such as country name, currency code and so on. The key for this application must be a standard I.S.O country code. The CURRENCY codes must be in the system before setting up the country parameter. |
| 6. | EB.TIME.ZONES | Defines the standard zones that have uniform mandated standard time. The ID must be a valid time zone name as specified in the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) time zone database. |
| 7. | HOLIDAY | - Indicates the public holidays for each country, or region within a country for the calendar year. |
| 8. | LANGUAGE | Identifies the languages that are to be used in the system when defining multi-language fields. The Abbreviation code assigned to each Language is used as a screen prompt. |
| 9. | INTEREST.BASIS | Determines the component for interest calculation based on the inputs provided in the INT.BASIS field. |
| 10. | CURRENCY.PARAM | Contains the common details such as Numeric Currency Code , Currency Name , Number of Decimal Places and the Interest Basis for each currency. This table ensures that the same numeric code and no of decimals are used on all the different currency files. |
| 11. | CURRENCY.MARKET | Helps to identify the correct exchange and revaluation rates to be applied for each currency. |
| 12. | TRANSACTION | Contains information about all the Transaction Codes that can be used in Temenos Transact . |
| 13. | SECTOR | Sector codes are defined in this table and assigned to each Customer record to group them into broad classifications like Private Sector, Public Sector, and Corporate Banks and so on. |
| 14. | INDUSTRY | Helps to define and assign the Industry codes to each Customer record to identify the industry of the customer. |
| 15. | CATEGORY | Category codes are used to classify financial transactions in Temenos Transact according to the type of business operation or product. |
| 16. | AC.CONSOLIDATE.COND | Allows the user to define the rules for the consolidation of entries for either an Account or a Category record. |
| 17. | INTERCO.PARAMETER | Determines if automatic balancing entries are raised when processing transactions in a multi-company or a multi-department (in the same company) environment. |
| 18. | EB.DUPLICATE.TYPE | Defines duplicate check criteria for applications. |
| 19. | EB.LOOKUP | This is a generic template to hold all the lookups for data access service. The user can create an EB.LOOKUP record with the definition and use them as drop-down list in applications. |
| 20. | EB.SYSTEM.ID | Provides a description for the SYSTEM.ID field in the accounting entry files, which include STMT.ENTRY , CATEG.ENTRY , CONSOL.NET.TODAY and RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY . |

Application Access Link - The user can provide a field name that will be referred to identify the presence of the customer data. |
