### 5.86  Tax


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Apply Split*, *Banded Rate*, *Base Round Type*, *Base Round Unit*, *Calc Type*, *Highest Tax*, *Rounding Type*, *Rounding Unit* ... +1 more
> 
> **Sections:** ⚙️ Configuration


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Follow the below steps to configure the tax related reference applications:

1. Setup different type of taxes on the TAX.TYPE application. For example, VAT (Value Added Tax) is a type of tax in this application.
2. Establish the rules to determine different types of customers. To establish these rules, the user must create a record for tax on the CONDITION.PRIORITY application. This record indicates the fields in the CUSTOMER application that are to be examined when determining the type of customer for tax purposes. For example, the user may decide that the customer's tax status can be identified from the sector and residence codes.
3. Define the different types of customers by setting up the TAX.GEN.CONDITION application. For example, the user may decide that private individuals who are resident in the local country are a type of customer for tax purposes.
4. Define the different rates of tax that may be charged, on the TAX application. For example, the user may input records for VAT full rate, VAT reduced rate and VAT zero rate.
5. The APPL.GEN.CONDITION application links the customer types with the type of contract to create a contract group code. This code can be used to identify different TAX codes for the same type of customer for different type of contract.
6. Link the different applications together using the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application.


##### Tax Type

The TAX.TYPE application allows the definition of the types of tax that are calculated within Temenos Transact . The TAX application may have different uses, depending on the local practice. Different types of tax may be calculated based on different types of transactions and products. The following screenshot shows the VAT tax type record in TAX.TYPE .

Income tax may be calculated on interest earned and VAT may be calculated on charges and commissions. There may be several types of VAT, such as GST (Government Service Tax), or a local regional tax.

Each type of tax may have different criteria to determine if a customers is liable to pay tax. Conditions for applying tax for a given set of customer conditions is defined using the CONDITION.PRIORITY ( TAX record) and TAX.GEN.CONDITION applications. Actual tax rates to be applied for tax groupings are specified using the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION and TAX applications.

The system calculates the tax splits between the various joint holders based on the tax types linked to them. There are multiple credits to the various types of taxes linked to the joint holders associated to the underlying portfolio, with a debit to the account linked to the underlying portfolio.

- The Highest Tax field selects the tax which has the highest percentage and applies to all customers of the group.
- The Apply Split field parameterises whether tax split can be applied for a specific tax type or not. If Apply Split field is set to Yes, the system calculates the tax split on the income split amongst the joint customers.

The system calculates the income splits between the various joint holders linked to the portfolio. The total income is credited to the account linked to the underlying portfolio.

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Debit | Interest | USD 100.00 |
| Credit | Account linked to the Portfolio | USD 71.00 |
| Credit | WHT-FR | USD 24.50 |
| Credit | WHT-LR | USD 4.50 |


##### Condition Priority for Tax

The purpose of this application is to specify for certain applications, which data elements in other reference applications could be specified to determine condition groups. The following screenshot shows the CONDITION.PRIORITY for TAX applications.


##### Tax General Condition

The TAX.GEN.CONDITION application identifies the specific group of customers through a user defined ID. This is then related to the GROUP.CONDITION application to define tax conditions applicable to that group.

The ID of this application is specified in the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application for specified tax types which allows the definition of the applicable tax rates. To create a GROUP.CONDITION record, the user must identify the group using the general condition number defined in this application. The group of customers is then identified by using the details held within this application.

To select a customer, it must conform to every field value defined within the TAX.GEN.CONDITION to qualify for a specific group. Amending a CUSTOMER record may therefore result in reclassification of the customer (or account) into another group or even to return to the normal conditions.


##### Defining Tax Rates

The TAX application defines various tax rates that are applicable on any type of transaction or service that the customer is doing with the bank.

The TAX application ID can be configured up to four numeric value appended with an effective date. The tax rate defined for each record determines the amount of tax to be added to or subtracted from the amount to be given or received by the customer.

Tax can either be set to be a flat rate or to be banded. If it is a flat rate, the tax is calculated using the sum of entire principal. If the tax is banded, then banding needs to be setup for at least one currency and a default currency must be set from one of them.

If the tax is charged in a currency where banding is not setup, it is converted using the mid-rate of the default currency.

For each level of a band a Calc Type field is set. The options in this field are Level or Band, where:

- BAND – Any amount for the principal to fall between the corresponding Upto Amt and the previous bands Upto Amt (or 0 if the user is in the first band) are charged to the corresponding Banded Rate field.
- LEVEL – If the principal lies between the current and preceding Upto Amt, the tax is calculated with the associated Banded Rate field against the entire principal.
- The values in Calc Type field can only be changed from Band to Level and cannot be changed in any other way.

The maximum and minimum amounts can be applied to each band and to the tax as a whole.

Rounding of the tax amount can be done based on the currency by specifying the rounding type (Natural, Lower or Higher) in the Rounding Type field and the unit to which the amount should be rounded in the Rounding Unit field. By specifying the rounding type and unit using the Base Round Type and Base Round Unit fields, the base amount such as interest, commission, charges and so on can also be rounded for tax calculation.

The user can update the Tax In Local field to indicate whether the tax should be credited to the tax account in local currency or in the currency of the deal on which it is being applied. If this field is left blank, the tax is credited in the currency in which it is calculated.

If the CURRENCY.MARKET application is not blank, the currency conversion uses the mid-rate applicable at the time of the calculation using that currency market, in all other scenarios mid-rate from the deal currency market is used. It is recommended that a market between 10 and 19 should be used to define the tax market, since the standard revaluation rate for market 1 is used at the COB.

Tax debited from the customer’s account is posted in the currency in which it is calculated. Only the credit to the tax account is posted in the local currency. All applications where tax is currently used accepts the increased length ID of four numeric characters. For example, FT.COMMISSION.TYPE and FT.CHARGE.TYPE .

To increase the length of the TAX code, an EB.OBJECT record for TAX is created and the maximum length is set to 18. Applications that accept TAX codes, automatically take the maximum length specified in the EB.OBJECT for TAX record.


##### Tax Type Condition

The TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application links the types of customer to the types of tax enabling the Temenos Transact to calculate different levels of tax depending on the type of customer. This mechanism enables to charge a different rate of VAT for residents and non-residents.

The following screenshot shows the VAT record if the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application:

At least one record should be established in this application for each TAX.TYPE application. This record then links the type of customer and contract group with the tax rates to be applied.

A single record may indicate that for VAT, the resident individuals should be charged 15% and all non-residents should be charged 0%. More than one record may be setup in

for each type of tax by addition of a numeric sequence. Thus, the record with ID as VAT and VAT-001 may exist.

This facility is used when there is more than one set of rates for a particular tax. For example, full rate VAT and reduced rate VAT.

### 6.1  Straight Through Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Straight Through Processing (STP) is used by companies in the financial world to optimise the speed at which transactions are processed. This is performed by allowing information that has been electronically entered to be transferred from one party to another in the settlement process without manual...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Straight Through Processing (STP) is used by companies in the financial world to optimise the speed at which transactions are processed. This is performed by allowing information that has been electronically entered to be transferred from one party to another in the settlement process without manually re-entering the same pieces of information repeatedly over the entire sequence of events.

The generated SWIFT messages are not supported for STP. Processing of SWIFT messages happens faster when BIC codes are used. The SWIFT messages generated mostly uses the name and addresses which need manual intervention to convert to BIC codes. This delays the settlement time and increases the transaction cost for the bank.

STP product (VS) integrates with Integration Framework (IF) for SWIFT messages. They are enhanced by an external STP processing software for better STP compliance. It reduces the time of settlement and transaction costs for the bank.

---


### 6.2  Repo Contract


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *REPO is short form of sale and repurchase agreement. It is essentially a transaction whereby two parties involved agree to perform two deals as a package. The first deal is a purchase (or sale) of a security, often a government bond, for delivery straight away (the exact settlement date varies accor...*
> 
> **Applications:** `REPO`
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

REPO is short form of sale and repurchase agreement. It is essentially a transaction whereby two parties involved agree to perform two deals as a package. The first deal is a purchase (or sale) of a security, often a government bond, for delivery straight away (the exact settlement date varies according to the market convention for the security involved). The second deal is a reversal of the first deal, it is the settlement on some future date.

It is understood that the first deal is reversed, it is clear that both parties intend the transfer of securities (in one direction) and the transfer of cash (in the other direction) to be temporary rather than permanent. Therefore, the transaction is equivalent to a loan of securities in one direction and a loan of cash in the other.

The REPO is structured, so that the economic benefit of owning the securities, income and capital gains or losses, remains with their original owner. These are the driving factors behind the REPO market, all REPO’s are driven by either:

- The need to lend or borrow cash, which is collateralised by securities or
- The need to borrow specific securities

The prices for both the original sale and the repurchase are agreed at the outset. The difference between the two prices are calculated to be equivalent to the cost of borrowing secured money.

- For lenders of cash, a REPO has the advantage of double security. If counterparty defaults, they can rely on the collateral. Therefore, they can verify the creditworthiness of both the counterparty and the issuer of the collateral.
- For borrowers of cash, an advantage to make use of an investment in their portfolio to borrow funds either more cheaply or in a case where they would not normally be able to borrow at all.

A REPO is defined as an initial sale of securities followed by a subsequent repurchase. A reverse REPO is the opposite case, where an initial purchase of securities followed by a subsequent re-sale. As there are two parties involved in a REPO contract to perform the opposite transactions, one of the party performs a REPO while the other party performs a reverse REPO. The term REPO is based on the securities side of the deal and not the Money Market (MM), therefore if the dealer is selling securities (seller)/borrowing cash (buyer) the deal is REPO. And, if the dealer is purchasing securities (buyer)/lending cash (seller) the deal is reverse REPO.

Temenos Transact supports a wide variety of REPO and RESO type of transactions, such as:

- Bond REPO
- Gilt REPO
- Equity REPO
- Bilateral REPO
- Trilateral REPO
- Cross currency REPO
- Open REPOs
- Intra-day REPO
- Buy/Sell Back
- Sell/Buy Back
- Stock borrow/Lending

Temenos Transact also, provides the options such as:

- Multiple securities (classic security driven contracts only on delivery against payment trades)
- Substitution of securities
- PSA/ISMA or GMRA agreements
- REPO contracts on behalf of a customer (customer REPOs)

The REPO application enables the cash side as well as the security side of a REPO or RESO transaction to be booked. The input of the security side is not mandatory, if a trilateral REPO or RESO is specified (because it is quite possible that the securities as collateral may not be known at the time of the deal).


> **Related Applications:** `REPO`

### 6.4  Accounting


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This feature details the accounting process for Corporate Actions (CA). The accounting entries for CA in Temenos Transact is relevant in the below two stages:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account No*, *Actual Settlement*, *Auto Brok Sett*, *Auto Brok Settle*, *Auto Cust Sett*, *Auto Cust Settle*, *Broker Txn Id*, *Cash Hold Settle* ... +19 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

This feature details the accounting process for Corporate Actions (CA). The accounting entries for CA in Temenos Transact is relevant in the below two stages:

- Entitlement accounting flow for customer portfolios
- Accounting entries after entitlement authorization

Several configurations affect how accounting entries are handled for CAs.


##### Set-up Controlling Forward Accounting Entries

SC.PARAMETER - The field Sup Act Fwd Ent determines whether the forward accounting entries must be raised in Securities (SC) module. If this field is set to YES, no forward accounting entries are raised.

DIARY.TYPE - The field Fwd Acct should be set to YES, if forward accounting entries must be raised for entitlements. This field can be set to YES only if the Sup Act Fwd Ent field in the SC.PARAMETER is set to NO.


##### Contractual or Actual Settlement Configuration

SC.PARAMETER - If the Actual Settlement field is set to YES, system raises a SC.SETTLEMENT record for each entitlement, which can be overridden at the transaction (DIARY) level. Also, the suspense categories to which entries need to be posted till settlement is complete are recorded in the SC.PARAMETER application.

DIARY - If the Cash Hold Settle and Sec Hold Settle fields are set to YES, it indicates that the actual settlement is on for cash and stock. These fields can be set to YES only if the Actual Settlement field is set to YES in the SC.PARAMETER application.


##### Accounting Flow when Entitlements are Created

The ENTITLEMENT records are created in INAU status, if:

- There are no validation errors
- There are no optional events and
- The field Verify Requried is set to NO in the DIARY.TYPE application for this event

The ENTITLEMENT records are created in IHLD status, if:

- The Verify Required field is set to YES
- There are validation errors or
- The DIARY has optional events

Although this also depends on the set-up in the Gts Control field in the VERSION application which is used to create the ENTITLEMENT version. Refer the appropriate User Guide sections elaborating the VERSION and OFS applications, for the values in the Gts Control field.

If ENTITLEMENT records are created in INAU status, forward accounting entries are raised for customer accounts if the DIARY.TYPE event field Fwd Acct is set to YES and for nostro accounts if the Update Nostro field is set to YES. Such accounting records have a forward key (for example F). All accounting entries are validated when the ENTITLEMENT records are created in INAU status.

If a DIARY contract is input with the Cash Hold Settle field set to YES, the subsequent running of the TSA.SERVICE for CAs create the ENTITLEMENT records in INAU status.

Unauthorised forward entries are not raised if the Auto Cust Sett field on the ENTITLEMENT record is set to YES or the value date of the ENTITLEMENT is back dated.

Authorised forward entries are raised for customer net amounts and nostro accounts, if the Fwd Acct field in DIARY.TYPE is set to YES, whereas no unauthorised forward entries are raised for outstanding amounts.

When entitlements are authorised, the above entries are backed out and new forward entries are raised for outstanding amounts, provided the Sup Act Fwd Ent field in the SC.PARAMETER application is set to NO. If this field is set to YES, the forward entries are not raised for outstanding amounts. The above forward nostro entry is backed out when the last ENTITLEMENT of a depository is authorised. The accounting process in ENTITLEMENT is amended to process the accounting entries based on the value in the Split Comm in the SC.PARAMETER application. If this field is set to Yes, it posts the commissions as a separate entry to the account mentioned in the Account No field in the ENTITLEMENT application.


##### Accounting Entries After Entitlement Authorisation

When SC.PARAMETER is set for actual settlement, the Auto Cust Settle and Auto Brok Settle fields are set to NO.

- The customer suspense account is credited with the customer net amount.
- The broker suspense account is debited with amount due from broker and depository.
- The miscellaneous suspense account is debited with source tax, local tax and commission.

The forward entries being raised for the unsettled amount is shown in the below screenshot.

Only one entry is raised for the net amount after deducting the source and local tax, if the COUPON.TAX.CODE for the appropriate country code has the fields Source Tax Split and Local Tax Split set to NO.

The ENTITLEMENT record is updated with statement numbers for the above entry. If the Auto Cust Settle or Auto Brok Settle field is set to YES in the ENTITLEMENT application:

- If the he Auto Brok Sett field is set to YES and the value date is less than or equal to the current date, the customer outstanding amount is settled and the SC.SETTLEMENT record is created in the LIVE file.
- If Auto Brok Sett field is set to YES and the value date is less than or equal to the current date, the broker outstanding amount is settled and the SC.SETTLEMENT record is created in the LIVE file.

Else, the SC.SETTLEMENT records are created in IHLD status, as an exception.

If entitlement is set for actual settlement, system posts the P&L on fees, charges and commissions to a miscellaneous suspense account, upon authorising the entitlement. The P&L entry is posted, only when the SC.SETTLEMENT record for the entitlement is authorised. However, if the Sup Mis Susp field in the DIARY application is set to YES, the P&L entries for fees, charges and commissions (and tax entries) are posted immediately upon authorising the entitlements.

If system is parameterised for actual settlement and settlement method is set as US, it is not possible to contractually settle a CA event. However, for a diary involving cash, it is possible to set Cash Hold Settle to NO. In this case, system debits customer and credit Nostro immediately, upon authorising all entitlements.

The customer and broker amounts can independently or partially be settled in the SC.SETTLEMENT application. This application raises the accounting entries in INAU status and updates the STMT.ENTRY on authorisation. For the above ENTITLEMENT the customer has settled 25% of the outstanding amount.

All customer entries are settled by 25%.

When the customer is settled, the customer suspense is debited with the settlement amount and the customer account is credited with the same. For tax and commission entries, miscellaneous suspense is credited. If the broker is settled, the broker suspense is credited and corporate suspense is debited. Existing forward entries are backed out and new forward entries are raised for the outstanding amounts.

In the SC.PARAMETER application, if the Sup Act Fwd Ent field is set to YES, the forward entries are not raised for the outstanding amounts.

When the broker side of the last ENTITLEMENT is fully settled, real nostro entries are raised upon authorising the SC.SETTLEMENT record, for the DIARY application. The existing forward entries for the nostro account is deleted and the statement numbers for the nostro account is updated in the DIARY application.

The nostro account is credited and corporate suspense is debited.

After the nostro entries are raised, if an existing ENTITLEMENT is reversed or a new one is input manually, the existing nostro entries in the DIARY are reversed and new nostro entries are raised.

Unsettled nominals at the Ex Date in the DIARY application are considered as outstanding, which means that, the amount is due from the broker, not the depository. If a Record Date is given in the DIARY and if it is less than the Ex Date , the settlements that have taken place between the Record Date and the Ex Date for transactions whose Value Date is less than the Ex Date, are treated as unsettled. If the Record Date is greater than the Ex Date , the settlements that have taken place between the Ex Date and the Record Date for transactions whose value date is greater than the Ex Date are treated as unsettled. Unsettled transactions are updated in the Broker Txn Id field in the ENTITLEMENT application.

The broker suspense account is debited with the net amount of each broker for outstanding transactions and the depository for settled transactions. The nostro entries for broker and depository are raised separately, as shown in the below screenshot.

If the Auto Cust Sett and Auto Brok Sett fields are set to YES in the ENTITLEMENT application and the value date is back dated, the washing customer, broker entries and miscellaneous entries are suppressed.

Accounting entries are validated for customer accounts and corporate suspense accounts, if Cash Hold Settle is not set to YES in the DIARY when entitlements are in INAU status.

Corporate suspense is debited and the customer account is credited directly. The real entries are raised, upon authorisation.

Nostro entries are raised, upon authorising the last ENTITLEMENT of a depository.

In the ENTITLEMENT application, the Sbl Qualify Hold and Depot Holding fields are calculated as follows, when the Sbl Div Proc field is set to YES, as shown in the above DIARY.TYPE record.

Upon authorization of the following SBL entitlement,

the accounting entries are as follows.

Customer, broker and miscellaneous suspense are either credited or debited. For borrow amount, customer suspense is debited and dividend control account is credited. Upon settlement of the borrow amount, customer account is credited with the borrow amount and corporate suspense (the DIARY.TYPE field Suspense Account ) is debited with the same.


##### Cash Dividend or Coupon Payments

In the ENTITLEMENT application, for cash or coupon events, the commission amount is posted as separate accounting entry to the entitlement cash account, only if the Split Comm is set to YES in the SC.PARAMETER application.

- Customer net amount (Gross amt – Foreign charges – Source tax – Local tax)
- Commission amount

For all income entitlements irrespective of the commission being greater or less than the entitlement, the income and commission amount are posted to the customer accounts separately, that is the income and commission is always shown separately on the customer records, statements etc. The existing cash net amount and commission to be posted to the customer account are displayed as separate entries, as shown below.

= (500 – 15) = 485 Commission amount = -50

The local tax amount is displayed in the ENTITLEMENT application, when Local Tax Split is set to Yes in the SC.PARAMETER application.

Entitlement amount = 500 Local tax = –15 (since local tax split is set in SC.PARAMETER ) Commissions = –50

### 6.5  Accumulation Units


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Accumulation Units Corporate Action event is an event where the income results in increasing the share capital of the company, without being paid out to the holders. The income is retained within the company and re-employed. Thus, this event results in an increase in book cost.*
> 
> **Applications:** `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `SECURITY.POSITION`, `SECURITY.TRANS`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accum Income*, *Cash*, *Choices*, *Commission Amt*, *Demerge Book Cost*, *Entitlement Amt*, *Equalisation*, *Equalisation Amt* ... +14 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Accumulation Units Corporate Action event is an event where the income results in increasing the share capital of the company, without being paid out to the holders. The income is retained within the company and re-employed. Thus, this event results in an increase in book cost.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following configuration is required for the accumulation event to be processed.


##### DIARY.TYPE

In DIARY.TYPE application, the Accum Income field has Yes or No options. If this field is set to Yes, then:

- accumulation unit functionality is turned on.
- validation is done in DIARY.TYPE application and the following settings are made.

| Field Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Cash | Yes |
| Update Holding | No |
| New Security | No |
| Choices | No |
| Reinvest | No |
| Rights | No |
| Free Securities | No |
| Retain Original | Yes |
| Demerge Book Cost | No |

The DIARY.TYPE application is created as shown below.


#### 🔧 Working With

As explained, accumulated units event results only in increasing the book cost. No cash is received and hence no accounting entries are raised. Accounting is done only for charges if any.

Source tax details can be input and the amount in the Tax Credit field is calculated to enable the preparation of tax vouchers and advices. A DIARY application for simple accumulated income functionality is shown below.

In the DIARY application, the Rate Type field allows only the value NET. The value GROSS is not allowed for DIARY.TYPE application, where Accum Income field is set to Yes.


##### ENTITLEMENT

The below entitlement is generated for DIARY.TYPE application with the Accum Income field set to Yes.

The amount for Entitlement Amt field is calculated similar to CASH dividend, though the income is not physically received. There is no change in the calculation of Tax Credit and Commission Amt fields. The amount for Net Amt Acc Cur and Net Amount fields are calculated excluding the Entitlement Amt field. These fields reflect only the chargeable commission amount.


##### Accounting Entries

Accounting entries raised for the ENTITLEMENT application are shown below. Accounting is done only for the charges or commission amount.

The below screenshot displays the enquiry for Transaction Entry.


##### SECURITY.POSITION

There is a change to the cost fields in the SECURITY.POSITION table. The SECURITY.POSITION table before generating the entitlement is shown below.


##### SECURITY.TRANS

The SECURITY.TRANS table is generated to adjust the cost and book cost, without changing the No Nominal field.


##### Accumulated Units with Equalisation

If the Equalisation field in DIARY.TYPE for accumulation units is set to Yes, then Group2 Rate and Equalisation Rate fields become mandatory when DIARY record is input. The values in the Group2 Amt and Equalisation Amt fields are calculated in the ENTITLEMENT application based on the Group2 Rate and Equalisation Rate fields.

The Group2 Amt calculated in the ENTITLEMENT application is included in the Entitlement Amt field for adjusting the cost and book cost related fields in the SECURITY.POSITION table. The value calculated for the Entitlement Amt field is not considered for adjusting the cost fields in SECURITY.POSITION table.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Accumulation Units feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Accumulation Units feature.

#### 📖 Introduction

A convertible bond gives an option to the bondholders to convert or exchange the bond for common stock in the issuing company. The bond conversion ratio determines how many shares an investor will receive in exchange of the bonds.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic details the setup of bond conversion feature.


##### Diary Type Definition

The first step to setup the bond conversion is to define the event type (that is, DIARY.TYPE ) in the system. The DIARY.TYPE application contains the processing details and the rules associated with the bond conversion.


#### 🔧 Working With

The bond conversion event should result in converting a bond-type security to a share-type security and ensuring that positions are moved correctly.

If the bond 006733-000 is nearing maturity, the bond holder receives the coupon in the regular way. In this case, the maturity proceeds are used to obtain a new holding of shares. The conversion is not dependent upon the cash value of the bond, but it is based on the nominal (face) value of the bond. As the conversion is performed at the maturity date, the cash and face values are similar.

The below screenshot displays an established position in the bond 006733-000 of USD 100,000, that matures on the current bank day. The transaction is in an established position because the Consol Trading Bal field is populated.

A suitable DIARY application is setup and the user provides the details to drive the conversion process and the coupon is used during conversion.

> **⚠️ Note:** As this is an established position, the last COB identifies the upcoming maturity and coupon that is due. The COB builds the required DIARY transactions that are set to IHLD status.

The DIARY application for the coupon is used as it is, but the DIARY application for maturity must have the value in the Event Type field changed that indicates a conversion is about to happen. The DIARY application relative to the coupon is shown below.

The record is entered and authorised without any change.

The COB generated DIARY application has a normal maturity, as the DIARY application is set to IHLD status and the user can change the value in the Event Type field to BOND.CONVERSION. The below screenshot illustrates how the DIARY application is updated with Event Type field set to BOND.CONVERSION, by changing the original default value.

Run the coupon and conversion DIARY records through the service agent to produce the transactions related to the ENTITLEMENT application.

Once the service agent has completed the processing, the ENTITLEMENT records can be checked and authorised, if no changes are required. Options are not available for either ENTITLEMENT and therefore both records are set to INAU status.

The system has calculated USD 7,250 coupon on the holding of USD 100,000. This represents an annual coupon on a 360/360 basis.

The Nominal field of 180 new shares is expected after the conversion of the original 100,000 bonds.

100,000 / 1,000 x 1.8 = 180 (after rounding, with no fractions)

A corporate action similar to the above scenario involves the switching from one position to another position that requires a CRF update. The CONSOL.UPDATE.WORK table is validated to check whether the switching is scheduled for processing during the next COB. The CONSOL.UPDATE.WORK table should have two entries, one for the bond and the other for the share. The work file credit entry used to remove the bond security is shown below.

This is identified by referring the CRF ID in which the sub-asset type of 100 indicates a position in a bond-type security. The work file debit entry that is required to build the new share security asset record is shown below.

This is identified by referring the CRF ID in which the sub-asset type of 101 indicates a position in a share type security. The work file entries are similar as the carrying value or cost of the securities must be the same because the conversion is performed without cost. The positions for both securities are updated in the SC.TRADING.POSITION table.

The SC.TRADING.POSITION table is generated for the original holding in bond after processing both the DIARY and ENTITLEMENT applications. The Current Position field indicates a zero holding even though the Consol Trading Bal field is updated only during the next COB. Check the SC.TRADING.POSITION table for the new position in shares (as shown in the below screenshot), to ensure that the values are updated correctly after all entitlement actions are performed.

The number of shares is 180 in the Current Position field, each having a cost price of USD 555.41666667. However, the Consol Trading Bal field is not indicated in the screenshot and it is required to run a COB to update this field using the appropriate CONSOL.UPDATE.WORK table details. The system is backed up and a COB is run to check whether the last process takes place correctly.

On completion of COB, the user can check the SC.TRADING.POSITION table for the details of original bond and new share. The position for the bond is shown in SC.TRADING.POSITION table where the value in the Consol Trading Bal field is cleared and shows zero. The same file is checked for sharing the record.

On completion of COB, the Consol Trading Bal field for the share position (as shown in the below screenshot), is updated with the same cost value of USD 99,975.00 as the original bond position.

Under normal circumstances, the conversion happens on the maturity date of the bond. The conversion assumes that the bonds has a value equal to the face value that uses the conversion rate provided by the paying agent responsible for the security. For position updates, this is not relevant as only the cost of the bonds must be provided.

A Bond is a fixed income instrument that represents a loan made by an investor to a borrower, often bonds are of corporate or governmental. They are units of corporate debt issued by the companies and securitised as tradeable assets. Bond prices are inversely correlated with interest rates. When interest rate increases, bond price decreases and vice-versa. The principal amount must be paid back in full on the maturity date of the bond. Bond type security can be converted into a share type security.

#### 📖 Introduction

Redemption is repayment of a fixed income security (such as, a bond) on or before its maturity date. The position is surrendered and redemption proceeds are received.Redemptions can be either mandatory or voluntary in nature.

Majority of the redemptions are bonds which reach the maturity date and the capital is returned to the shareholders. Voluntary redemptions are those where the company offers the shareholders the choice of redeeming their bonds, or retaining them to redeem later.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The user has to create a record in the DIARY.TYPE application to handle the processing of bond redemption at maturity.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic helps the user to understand the functionality of bond redemption at maturity.


##### Full Redemption

Dealer book positions exist for a bond and a Close of Business (COB) is run to build the Central Reporting Files (CRF) base values. For full redemption, the CRF is created and the corresponding value is displayed in the CONSOL.TRADING.BAL (as shown in the below screenshot). Also, the coupon is updated, so that the interest due is from the last coupon date to the system date.

The SC.POSITION application displays the details relating to a bond. If the bond is due for maturity on the current bank day, then the system generates the DIARY records the last COB.

The two automatically built DIARY records are,

1. For the redemption
2. For recording the coupon or interest details

These are built from the details provided in the SECURITY.MASTER application and requires the input and authorisation without any changes. The below screenshot shows the two DIARY records built during COB.

The generated DIARY record relates to the coupon, it advises the rate and value date on which the coupon is payable.

The next DIARY record advises the maturity date and rate of the bond. In this case, the defaulted 100% (par value) is assumed. The DIARY records are entered, authorised and processed through the service agent.

The corresponding ENTITLEMENT record is created and shows the interest or coupon amount due on the dealer book holding of 10,000,000.

The record is authorised to generate two CONSOL.UPDATE.WORK entries.

The maturity DIARY is also authorised. The below screenshot shows the LIVEDR entries required to close out the security balance.

The contra accounting entry where the expected proceeds are held on suspense and are pending evidence of receipt on the nostro account is shown in the below screenshot.

The SECURITY.POSITION is examined when the system is on-line. The subsequent COB cleans the application.

The SC.TRADING.POSITION table is examined (considering that the CONSOL.TRADING.BAL is not cleared down until the next COB is run). The position is now cleared and that the CONSOL.TRADING.BAL together with the realised profit are posted during the next COB (as shown in the below screenshot).

Once COB is completed, the SECURITY.POSITION and SC.TRADING.POSITION tables are validated. The SECURITY.POSITION in the bond is set to zero and the bonds matured or redeemed when a DIARY and ENTITLEMENT records are entered as shown below.

The SC.TRADING.POSITION that is prior to the processing of DIARY contains the CRF balance in the Consol Trading Bal field and this field is also set to zero. The SC.TRADING.POSITION is cleared, including the contents of the Consol Trading Bal field that reports the current CRF (LIVEDR balance) in respect of the security.

The face value proceeds are displayed in the Amount Fcy field of the RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY application.

The security is carried at 10,200,000 and therefore a P&L entry is required for posting the entry.

The transaction entries for the coupon DIARY is checked by mentioning the child ENTITLEMENT .

The expected coupon are posted to the coupon suspense account which is pending the confirmation of receipt on the nostro account. The suspense account is validated to check if the maturity proceeds and final coupon are posted correctly.


##### Partial Redemptions

Partial redemptions are also possible. The position details associated to a bond is shown in the below security position enquiry.

The bond is due to mature in 2014. If the bond must be redeemed partially before the final maturity date, then the same is handled by using the Redemption % field in DIARY .

If 50% of the holdings are to be redeemed, then the user enters the value 50 in the

field.

Based on the redemption percentage specified in this field, the Retain Nominal field in the ENTITLEMENT record is automatically updated in all the resultant entitlements. In this case, only 50% of the qualifying holding are redeemed and the remaining are retained.

#### 📖 Introduction

Share consolidation is also known as Reverse Stock Split. It is a Corporate Action (CA) to decrease the total number of outstanding shares and increase the nominal or par value of each share. After the CA, the shareholder owns a fewer but theoretically higher priced shares due to the decrease in the total outstanding shares in the market.

This topic enables the user to understand the processing of consolidated CA in Temenos Transact .


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The event type ( DIARY.TYPE ) is defined in the system to handle the consolidation corporate actions. The DIARY.TYPE contains the processing details and the rules associated with the CA. The below screenshot shows a DIARY.TYPE record for consolidation.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Security No is replaced using New Security No field as shown in the below screenshot. This activity is without cost (similar to a free conversion). The DIARY is run using the service agent to obtain the ENTITLEMENT .

An ENTITLEMENT confirms an expectation of 3,750 newly issued share replaces the 15,000 of the original security.


##### Consolidation of Own Book Holdings

A SC.TRADING.POSITION record should exist for the own book position in the equity to be consolidated.

The SC.TRADING.POSITION simulates a dealer trading position in which a position of 15,000 is maintained. Once the own book related ENTITLEMENT is authorised, the user can view the details in the CONSOL.UPDATE.WORK (CRF work file).

When the CRF is switched between the two positions without undergoing any change, the cost of the old 15,000 is switched over and populates the cost of the new 3,750 shares. To ensure the process continues correctly, the SC.TRADING.POSITION is checked to ensure that the CRF switches over.

The CONSOL.TRADING.BAL switches to the new position after the next COB as shown in the below screenshot.

The cost of the position has switched over to the new security and the user ensures the COB does the same with the CRF value. After completion of the next COB, the user checks if the original is regularised and all the datas are cleared out.

The original security position is cleared along with the carrying value in the Consol Trading Bal field to represent the CRF equivalent. The user checks the new security position to confirm if the values are relocated into the new position correctly, including the CRF equivalent. The book values are transferred to the new position along with the CRF, which is reported in the Consol Trading Bal field.

#### 📖 Introduction

Some voluntary corporate actions (CA) provide options to the shareholders, where the shareholder has to provide their choice or election. The shareholder can give a standing instruction upfront on the preferred option and the same can be applied automatically without waiting for a response from every event.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic helps the user to configure the default instructions for CA.


##### Configuring Default Instructions throughSC.ENT.INSTR

The SC.ENT.INSTR application allows the user to enter standing instructions for customers and/or portfolios for various event types.

The user can enter the instructions in this application at different levels. The ID of the record can be:

- Customer
- Portfolio
- Default

Within the record, the standing instructions for various event types can be indicated. For example, as shown above, in the rights event, the customer can choose the standing instruction as Take-up (Exercise), Sell, or Buy-more. Similarly, in a stock cash dividend event, the standing instruction could be to always receive the dividend in stock or in cash.


###### Configuring Standing Instructions throughINVESTMENT.PROGRAM:

Standing instructions for the above mentioned events can be set at an investment program level also. The fields in SC.ENT.INSTR are also available in the INVESTMENT.PROGRAM application. All instructions at the most granular level are also applied.

In a voluntary event, the following process is followed for applying the standing instructions in the customer’s entitlement.

1. The system validates if a record exists in SC.ENT.INSTR for the portfolio.
2. If standing instructions are not found for the portfolio, then the system validates if the record is available for the customer.
3. If standing instructions are not found for the portfolio and customer, then the system reads the Investment Program field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application and checks if the instructions exist in INVESTMENT.PROGRAM .
4. Finally, system checks the DEFAULT record in SC.ENT.INSTR .

The Apply def instructions field in the DIARY.TYPE application must be set to Yes to activate the default instruction process. When the Apply def instructions flag is set as Yes, the user can enter the parameters used to calculate the action date. The standing instructions for a stock cash event are applied two days prior to the Value Date.


#### 🔧 Working With

For processing the CA with options, the standing instructions for events can be set at customer, portfolio or default levels using the SC.ENT.INSTR application. Based on the value in this application, the system applies the default instructions. If SC.ENT.INSTR is not setup, the system uses the default option setup at the DIARY level.


##### Setting Standing Instructions

The standing instructions for CAs can be setup for:

- Rights
- Stock or cash (options)
- Re-invest income
- Odd lots
- Multicurrency dividends
- Any event (that is, for any record in DIARY.TYPE )

Standing instructions in SC.ENT.INSTR can be set up at the following levels.

Instructions can be set up for each event for different security types. The types can be entered in the fields based on the event for which the standing instruction needs to be set. The user can define the asset type, sub-asset type, product type or a valid security master or all.

> **⚠️ Note:** The product type refers to the field in SC.PARAMETER and SECURITY.MASTER that is used to define local reference fields which can be used for defining default instructions.

Instructions can be set up based on the domicile of a security. When a standing instruction is set based on a domicile (that is, US), the system applies the standing instruction to the securities that holds the same domicile in SECURITY. MASTER application.

As per the above example, the standing instruction is set up as Buy More for customer 100271 when there is a rights event on the securities domiciled in US and trading in USD currency.

When standing instruction is set based on currency, the system applies the standing instruction to the securities that hold the same currency in Security Ccy in SECURITY.MASTER .

| Values | Description |
|---|---|
| Buy More | Generates a SEC.OPEN.ORDER application to complete the number of rights to be exercised according to the specified ratio in the related record in DIARY |
| Sell | Generates a SEC.OPEN.ORDER application to sell the rights |
| Take-up | Exercises the rights according to the ratio and generates a SEC.OPEN.ORDER application to sell the remaining rights |

Additionally, the standing instructions can also be set at various investment program levels, which are basically customer and portfolio categories (like balanced, aggressive and so on). The INVESTMENT.PROGRAM application is used to set up standing instructions for each investment program. The fields available in SC.ENT.INTR are also available in this application. Read the Configuring Default Instructions for Corporate Actions section for more information.


###### Defaulting Account to Credit Cash from a CA

The user can also create standing instructions by portfolio, for the default account to which any cash from a corporate action is to be credited. The Account Def System Code field in SEC.ACC.MASTER accepts the input of a SECURITY.MASTER and DIARY.TYPE application.

For the unique combination of SECURITY.MASTER and DIARY.TYPE application, the specified cash account in the Account Default Sc Account field is credited. These instructions are effective at the portfolio level after the specific rule matching criteria takes place. The matching criteria rules are:

- DIARY.TYPE ID (corporate actions event type)
- SECURITY.MASTER ID (internal security number)

For a portfolio 100295-1, the default account 100218 is applied in the entitlement for all credit and debit to the account arising out of the corporate action (with SC.TRANS.NAME as STR).


###### Processing the Default Instructions

When creating a record in DIARY , Temenos Transact checks the related DIARY.TYPE application if the Apply def instructions field is set to Yes. Then, it calculates the date on which the default instruction is applied in the records in ENTITLEMENT . The date is calculated using the No of Days , Prior/ After and Select date fields and is stored in the Default Instrument Date field in DIARY .

The Default Instrument Date field in DIARY is optional. The date either calculated as above or manually entered must be greater than the current bank date. It must not be prior to the date in the Diary Auto Authorisation Date field and cannot be after the date in the Entitlement Auto Authorised Date field. If the Default Instrument Date field is left blank, then the default instructions are not applied even if the Apply def instructions field in DIARY.TYPE is set to Yes. If the Default Instrument Date is available in DIARY , then the date is copied to the Default Instrument Date field in all the records in ENTITLEMENT generated from this record in DIARY .

During the start of the day process, Temenos Transact searches for any unauthorised records in ENTITLEMENT for which default instructions must be applied. At this stage, instructions only for rights or options (stock or cash) is validated. The instructions in the Reinvest Income and Sell Odd Lots fields are applied in the authorisation stage of the records in ENTITLEMENT . When defaulting the account in the records in ENTITLEMENT , the system checks if any default account setup exists in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application and it defaults the account accordingly.


###### Applying Standing Instructions on Corporate Action Event Creation

The user sets Gen Ent Stand Instr in DIARY.TYPE to Yes to apply the standing instructions while creating an entitlement record. If the standing instructions are available for the customer in SC.ENT.INSTR and the user sets Gen Ent Stand Instr to Yes, then the system applies standing instruction as soon as the entitlement is generated. The entitlement is created in INAU status with Stand Inst updated with the ID of the record in SC.ENT.INSTR from which it was applied. If in case, there is a buy or sale of securities post entitlement generation and the diary is re-run with this setup. The standing instruction is re-applied when the entitlements are regenerated.

However, the user can modify the instruction any time before the final cut-off date. If the user modifies elections even after standing instruction is applied, then the manually modified elections take precedence for further processing and standing instruction is not re-applied.

If Gen Ent Stand Instr in DIARY.TYPE is set to No, then on Def Instr Date , the system checks if any standing instruction is received in SC.ENT.INSTR and applies them. If standing instruction is not received, Temenos Transact applies the default instruction for the particular event as set in DIARY . If default instructions are not available, the customer must elect the option manually.

The following points identify how the option is elected for the events.

- Stand Inst in ENTITLEMENT displays how the option is elected.
- If an existing standing instruction of the customer is applied, Stand Inst is updated with the record ID in SC.ENT.INSTR from which it was applied.
- If the option is manually modified even after applying standing instruction, Stand Inst is cleared and does not have any value indicating that it is a manual election.
- If default option (in DIARY ) is applied to the event, Stand Inst is set to default option.


##### Suppressing MT565 for Default Option

The No Def Opt Inst field in SC.PARAMETER controls the default option to suppress MT565.

When the No Def Opt Inst field is set to No, then the system sends MT565 for the quantity elected in default option and if this field is set as Yes, then the system does not send MT565.

The system receives an MT566 for the default option on the payment date even after MT565 is suppressed, and reconciliation of the confirmed quantity is possible for this option.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Default Instructions for Corporate Actions feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Default Instructions for Corporate Actions feature.


> **Related Applications:** `DIARY`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `SC.ENT.INSTR`, `SC.PARAMETER`

#### 📖 Introduction

This feature explains how Corporate Actions (CA) are processed straight through in the system through the SWIFT messages. This feature also provides stepwise instructions to process the CA events through Straight Through Processing (STP). Temenos Transact processes an incoming MT564 message notifying a CA. The system automatically creates DIARY and generates ENTITLEMENT records for eligible portfolios, based on the event details.

For optional events and events with choices, the user can make an election in the ENTITLEMENT records and MT565 messages are sent out to the depository indicating the elections made. Temenos Transact can also process the incoming confirmation messages (MT566) that automatically completes and authorises the ENTITLEMENT records. During the event, the incoming status messages (MT567) is received and the status (acknowledgement and rejection) is recorded in the system.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic helps the user understand the configuration of CA events for STP.


##### Processing Corporate Actions in STP

A version is created to generate the SC.PRE.DIARY for the STP. This version name is used in the DE.MESSAGE record for MT564. (The version is SC.PRE.DIARY , STP). The DE.INTERFACE application specifies the interface for the SWIFT messages.

The user must setup the DE.CARRIER record for SWIFT, and the DE.ADDRESS record for depository and company. The below tables are setup:

The OFS.SOURCE record is built for a SWIFT source by mapping a routine in the In Dir Rtn field.

A new OFS.SOURCE record is created for the processing of inward swift message type. The In Dir Rtn field contains the name of the routine that allows the creation of Open Financial Source (OFS) messages from the inward swift messages.

A service record should be created to process the OFS messages.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Swift Caev | Holds a unique value for each DIARY.TYPE record. Any event type mentioned in the swift incoming messages should match with the value in this field of one DIARY.TYPE record. On authorisation of the DIARY.TYPE record, the F.SC.CON.SWIFT.CAEV internal table is updated according to this field value of the DIARY.TYPE record. |
| Diary Create | Indicates the status (HLD, NAU or AUT) of the DIARY records. AUT - If the version used is for authorising, the DIARY is authorised immediately upon creation. This is the default value. NAU - A DIARY record is validated and it is in NAU status until a date is entered in the Dia Auto Auth Date field of the related DIARY record. The COB process automatically authorises it. When it has to be authorised before the date mentioned in Dia Auto Auth Date field, the user can bypass it. HLD – When a DIARY record is created in HLD status, automatic process is not done until the user validates it. |
| Auto ent create | Indicates automatic creation of the ENTILEMENT records. This field is set to Yes, to allow the system to creates an ENTILEMENT for this DIARY record. |
| Tolerance Category, Tolerance Percentage and Tolerance amount | Computes the tolerance limit applicable for the specific diary event. Checks if the value specified in an inward MT566 message is within the tolerance. If yes, then the system automatically updates the DIARY , else the system writes the error message to the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG application. The user has to resolve and commit the DIARY manually. |
| Partial STP | Accepts a valid record from the SC.PARTIAL.STP application. The value ALL denotes that Partial STP flow is followed for the specified records or for ALL records. |
| Pre Dia Days, Pre Dia Pri Aft and Pre Dia Sel Date | Allows auto authorisation of SC.PRE.DIARY . When MT564 is received with PREC or COMP status, the SC.PRE.DIARY record is auto authorised. |


#### 🔧 Working With

This section helps the user to understand the process of CA events using STP.


##### Processing of MT564 Inward Messages

An account service person sends this message to an account owner or its designated agent. This message provides an account owner with the details of a CA event with possible election choices. This message provides the account owner with the details of the impact of a CA event on a safekeeping or cash account, for example, entitlement calculation. An incoming MT564 message creates a SC.PRE.DIARY record. The SC.PRE.DIARY application is a copy of the DIARY application. It receives the information from SWIFT message MT564 such as security number, event type and depository. The inward SWIFT is processed as below:

- The International Securities Identification Number (ISIN) in the message is used to identify the SECURITY.MASTER (SM) . When multiple SECURITY.MASTER records have the same ISIN, the Security No field in SC.PRE.DIARY is blank and the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG application is updated accordingly. Then the user enters the correct SECURITY.MASTER manually. The error log update for multiple SM records are controlled by the parameter settings in the Mult Sm Ca Event field in the SC.PARAMETER application. If the parameter field is not set, then the SC.PRE.DIARY is created for all SM records that are linked to ISIN.
- The SWIFT event identifier (CAEV//XXXX) in the incoming message is checked against the Swift Caev field to identify the DIARY.TYPE . The various corporate action code indicators are sent as part of Tag 22F in sequence E (CA options) of MT564. This is matched against the SC.CA.OPTION.DESC records and the Option Ind field is updated.

The data required by the DIARY application is received and updated in the SC.PRE.DIARY record, from the incoming MT564. Simultaneously, the system updates the message details and status in the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG application. When the mandatory information required for creating a diary is missing, the SC.PRE.DIARY is on IHLD and the reason for the error is updated in the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG application.

If all critical information is updated in SC.PRE.DIARY and the record is authorised, then OFS process creates the DIARY record. The DIARY is created in HLD, NAU or AUT status depending on the setting in the corresponding DIARY.TYPE record. If the DIARY record is created in AUT and if the Auto Ent Create field in DIARY.TYPE is set to Yes, then the authorisation of the DIARY record generates the ENTITLEMENT records automatically.

The SC.PRE.DIARY record can be auto authorised to create a DIARY record. The settings in DIARY.TYPE allows the user to specify when the pre-diary records needs to be authorised for a specific event (for example, two days prior to ex-date, on ex-date).

When an MT564 message is received, system checks if it is a duplicate message. It also checks for a duplicate diary within a date range. The number of days before or after ex-date, to check for duplicate diary can be specified in the Dup Check Days field in SC.PARAMETER .

Whenever the SC.PRE.DIARY is authorised and the Dup Check Days field in SC.PARAMETER is not set, system checks if there is any prior DIARY created for the same event, security, custodian and ex-date. If a record in DIARY already exists for this event, system creates new diary on hold and updates the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG stating that duplicate diary exists.

If a value is provided in the Dup Check Days field, on authorisation of SC.PRE.DIARY, the system checks if there is any prior DIARY created for the same event, security, custodian and ex-date ( Ex-date +/- Dup Check days ). If a diary exists, instead of creating a new record in DIARY , system replaces the details in the existing DIARY that was found and updates the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG that existing diary has been replaced. But, if more than one DIARY exists for the combination, system updates the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG stating multiple diaries exist and further diary records are not created.

| Pay Date in E1 (SECMOVE) | Pay Date in E2 (CASHMOVE) | Opt Pay Date in SECU option of SC.PRE.DIARY and DIARY | Opt Pay Date in CASH option of SC.PRE.DIARY and DIARY | Pay Date in SC.PRE.DIARY and DIARY |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| UKWN | UKWN | UKWN | UKWN | Blank |
| UKWN | 08/05/2024 | UKWN | 08/05/2024 | Blank |
| May 08, 2024 | UKWN | May 08, 2024 | UKWN | Blank |
| May 18, 2024 | May 12, 2024 | May 18, 2024 | May 12, 2024 | May 12, 2024 (Earliest date available) |

When MT564 is received with function REPL or ADDB, automatic update of changes to the DIARY is controlled by a flag in DIARY.TYPE . When Temenos Transact receives an MT564 with function as REPL, the SC.PRE.DIARY record is identified and updated with the changes. The original record (before receiving REPL) moves to the HISTORY table ( SC.PRE.DIARY $HIS) and the amended SC.PRE.DIARY record is in LIVE table.

When Upd Diary Repl field in DIARY.TYPE is set to No, the amendments from incoming message are reflected in the SC.PRE.DIARY and DIARY applications. When this field is set to Yes, only SC.PRE.DIARY is updated with the amendments from the incoming message. The DIARY application is not automatically updated.

Where this field is set to Yes, user can launch the PreDiary - REPL Changes enquiry (SC.MANUAL.UPD.DIARY.LIST). This enquiry lists all the SC.PRE.DIARY records for which an amendment notification (REPL or ADDB) is received. The enquiry also has a drill down to the DIARY application for manual update of the amendments.

| Value | Security identified based on |
|---|---|
| Currency | Security currency (Tag 11A) |
| Plis | Place of listing (Tag 94B) |
| Safekeep | Place of safekeeping (Tag 94C) |

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Message Type | Stores the message type. That is, 564. |
| From Address | Stores the sender's address. |
| Receiver Address | Stores the receiver’s address. |
| Time Stamp | Stores the time and date when the message was received. It is mapped from DE.I.HEADER record. |
| Link Reference | Stores the Corp Reference ( Corp Ref ). For example, 20C :CORP. |
| Transaction Ref | Stores the SC.PRE.DIARY reference ID (that is, record ID) created upon receiving the incoming MT564. |
| Event Type | Stores the Event Type ( DIARY.TYPE ) in SC.PRE.DIARY . |
| Sender | Stores the T24 customer ID corresponding to the BIC code in From Address . This is usually Depository (in DIARY ) |
| Sender Acc External | Stores the Sub Account Ext ID received in the 97A:SAFE tag. |
| Sender Acc Internal | Stores the sub-account corresponding to the Sub Account Ext ID received in the 97A:SAFE tag. |
| Block Name | Stores the start of the block (in a sequential order from 1) represented by the 16R tag. 16R: GENL is stored as Block Name.1 : GENL.1 If another 16R tag is repeated within a block, it considers the first block name followed by the second, separated by a delimiter (*). 16R: LINK within 16R:GENL is stored as, Block Name.2 : GENL.1*LINK.1. If multiple 16R tags are repeated within a block, it stores them in the sequence they are received, delimited with * and incremented with numbers. If 16R: LINK is received for the second time within 16R:GENL, it is stored as Block Name.3 : GENL1*LINK2 Similarly, it stores the end of block (represented by the16S tag) in sequence, separated by the delimiter (*). |
| Tag Name | Stores the tag name received under each block (like 16R, 16S, 93B). 16R: GENL is stored as Tag Name.1 : 16R. |
| Qualifier | Stores the qualifiers received in each tag. The system considers the values before '//' as Qualifier and maps it in the field and anything after '//' is considered as Tag Value . If '//' is not present, the entire value is treated as Tag Value and Qualifier is not updated. Consider the tag, 93B::ELIG//UNIT/7000. Here, ELIG is Qualifier 93B is Tag Name UNIT/7000 is Tag Value |
| Tag Value | Stores the value received with respect to each tag. The value after '//' is mapped in this field. If '//' is not present, the entire value is treated as Tag Value . For the tag :23G:NEWM, Tag Value is NEWM and there is no Qualifier . In case of :93B::SETT//UNIT/7000, the Tag Value is UNIT/7000. |
