##### Understanding MT568 Corporate Action Narrative

- Temenos Transact handles processing of inbound MT568 messages. MT568 is sent by an account servicing institution to the account owner or designated agent. The message is used to provide complex instructions or narrative details relating to a corporate event.
- MT568 is sent or received to continue corporate action instructions or narrative details in addition to the MT564 message. Therefore, MT568 may link back to a previous MT564.
- Any MT564 of more than 10,000 bytes has the excess information mapped in narrative tag 70E: ADTX (optional sequence F) and moved to the MT568 (which follows the MT564).
- On receipt of the MT568 message, the system updates the relevant SC.PRE.DIARY record which was created by processing the incoming MT564 message with the narrative details.
- The narrative details are stored in the Addl Narrative field of the SC.PRE.DIARY record. The updated SC.PRE.DIARY record is identified based on the Link Ref field, which is updated when the MT564 message is processed.
- Temenos Transact handles multiple MT568 messages for a single event.
- When issuers give incentives to holders for voting well before the final deadline in the case of a MT564 for CA notification, the Early Deadline field in the DIARY and SC.PRE.DIARY applications holds the effective date. The date appears in the ETPD qualifier of the MT564.
- The MT568 messages are sometimes used without a preceding MT564. On receipt of such messages, Temenos Transact creates the records in SC.PRE.DIA
- RY and stores all the important fields from the incoming message, particularly the narrative. However, the processing of corporate events through DIARY and ENTITLEMENT are not triggered in this case.


##### Monitoring non-receipt of MT564

When the first MT564 is received from any custodian, the receipt of MT564 from other custodians is monitored. The Monitor Msg field in SC.PRE.DIARY record in SC.CA.PARAMETER is set to monitor such receipts. When this field is set to Yes, the system monitors the receipt of MT564 through the SC.DEPO.MSG.MONITOR application (live).

The fields in .DEPO.MSG.MONITOR are explained in the below table.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Monitor Depo | Indicates the depositories from which the MT564 has not been received, even though position of the security is held. It is a multi-value and no input field |
| Msg Recd Date | Indicates the date when the first MT564 was received |
| Depository | Holds the ID of all the depositories, where the position of the security is held. It is a multi-value field |

When the system receives MT564 from any depository, the record in SC.PRE.DIARY is created for the event.

Once the system creates the record in SC.PRE.DIARY for the received MT564, the system searches for the record in SC.DEPO.MSG.MONITOR with Security Pre Diary ID , Security No , Event Type , Ex Date matching the same in SC.PRE.DIARY .

- If such a record exits in SC.DEPO.MSG.MONITOR , the depository for which SC.PRE.DIARY is created is removed from SC.DEPO.MSG.MONITOR .
- If no such record exits, SC.DEPO.MSG.MONITOR is built during COB. The depositories from which MT564 is not received, is updated.

When the MT564 is received from all the depositories, the record in SC.DEPO.MSG.MONITOR is deleted.


##### Processing of MT565 Outward Message

The following applications must be setup to generate MT565 messages.

DIARY.TYPE

A corporate event that requires MT565 messaging must have the Swift Caev field defined in the relevant DIARY.TYPE record within Temenos Transact . This field serves as a link between the Temenos Transact definition of a corporate event and the associated SWIFT code for that event. The below screen shot of DIARY.TYPE record for a stock dividend with the associated Swift Caev field set as DVOP. The Confirm Req field is set to YES in the DIARY.TYPE , DIARY or ENTITLEMENT records.

The Update Nostro field in the DIARY.TYPE is set to YES, for all the event types which must generate a MT565.

SECURITY.MASTER

For the 565 messages, SWIFT recommends to use the ISIN code to identify the financial instrument. The system checks the ISIN Number field in SECURITY.MASTER and hence this field needs to be populated with the ISIN.

The CA module in core banking product can generate MT565 messages to the depository or custodian. An account owner sends this message to those who service the accounts (account servicing institution). This message provides the custodian with instructions on how the account owner wants to proceed with a CA event. Instructions include investment decisions regarding the exercise of rights issues, the election of stock or cash when the option is available and dividend reinvestment.

When all the ENTITLEMENT records linked to a particular depository is setup, the system checks if any decisions are to be made concerning the corporate action. For example, a rights issue or a stock or cash choice. Once the elections are made, MT565 message is generated and sent to the depository informing them of instructions in relation to eligible holding.

Core banking product generates MT565 before authorising the entitlements. When the elections are made, the system generates the MT565 even before the entitlements are authorised. The entitlements remain in INAU and is authorised on receipt of confirmation (MT566 or otherwise).

This is achieved by setting the Mt565 Unauth field in SC.CA.PARAMETER to Yes.The MT565 can be automatically generated on a specific date, For example, two days prior to Reply By Date . This is done by setting the Select date field to Reply By Date in the DIARY.TYPE record.

MT565 can be generated separately for each option. For example, if there is an event with one cash and one stock option, then one MT 565 is generated for cash and the other for stock. If there are more than two options, then there are more than two MT565s. The option ID in core banking product must match the ID as in the SWIFT message, that is, if in a SWIFT (MT564), the option is :13A::CAON//098, then the core banking product must send the option number 098; irrespective of the multi-value in core banking product. If the customer elects for multiple options (for example, part cash and part stock), then multiple MT 565s are generated for the same entitlement. To generate MT565 per option, the MT565.Per.Option field in SC.CA.PARAMETER needs to be set to Yes.

> **⚠️ Note:** MT565 is generated for NOAC option (No action).

These MT565 messages can be when the bank requires, that is, an online process (as opposed to a COB) informing the agent of the elections that have been made to date. This is done using SC.MT565.INSTRUCT application. Any subsequent elections are also sent online and to avoid duplication of instructions, the MT565 generated for them does not include any details whatsoever of the previously instructed elections.

Temenos Transact can select the diary event and any related entitlement records for which the elections are made (but not sent), is included (on an aggregate basis) in the MT565 to the agent. The delivery reference for the message is updated in the DIARY record after all the entitlements are authorised.The below shown is a sample MT565 message for a STOCK.DIV CA event. The safekeeping account (100104) holds 25,000 shares which are eligible for the CA .The custodian is instructed to take advantage of the cash option for 11000 shares and of the stock option for 14000 shares.

D CORPORATE ACTION INSTRUCTION

D CORPORATE ACTION INSTRUCTION

The repetitive sequence D from its position of 20,100 rights can inform the depository to exercise 20,000 rights and to lapse 100 rights in respect to its entitled position of 20,100

The MT565 sent out for omnibus or segregated accounts can be cancelled. The MT565 for segregated accounts is sent from the entitlement record. Where the entitlement is deleted, the cancellation message is sent. The cancelled message carries the original Corp Reference. When a fresh entitlement is created and options are re-elected, a new MT565 is generated.

In the case of omnibus accounts, the MT565 is generated automatically once all options are elected or using the MT565.INSTRUCT application. This MT565 for omnibus accounts is cancelled using the MT565.INSTRUCT application. The field Cancel Message Ref holds the SEME reference of the message to be cancelled. This is available in the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG . Cancellation of the omnibus MT565 is allowed only if none of the entitlements are authorised. In case of a cancellation ENTITLEMENT , the tag 23G contains the key word CANC as illustrated below.

This application allows Temenos Transact to send MT565 messages to their agents online, when elections on optional corporate events are received from their clients. The user specifies the diary record number and if required the depository and sub account in the multi-valued set of the Diary ID to Sub Account fields. The Diary ID and Depository fields are multi-valued; whilst the Sub Account is a sub-valued field.

After verification, Temenos Transact scans for matching the ENTITLEMEN T records relating to this DIARY event that is updated with the customers’ elections, but not yet instructed to the agent.

The key to the application is a five digit alpha-numeric. When MT565 is sent to the agent, the ENTITLEMENT application writes back the delivery reference into the multi-value set Activity Code to Delivery Key fields.

When sending the MT565s, Temenos Transact selects ENTITLEMENT records relating to the specified Diary ID that is updated with the customer’s elections (that is, the ENTITLEMENT record is authorised) but yet not instructed to the agent, that is, have no associated MT565 delivery reference. When the ENTITLEMENT records are selected, Temenos Transact aggregates the nominals for each of the options available and the aggregated nominals are then mapped to the message(s).

| Options | Deadlines |
|---|---|
| CASH | Oct 05, 2020 |
| SECU | Oct 10, 2020 |
| NOAC | Oct 10, 2020 |

To generate a MT565 for a specific option, the Option No field in MT565.INSTRUCT application is populated with the option number from the diary mentioned in Diary Id field.

For various options available in the event, the user can create multiple records in MT565.INSTRUCT application and triggers MT565 to the custodian. In the case of omnibus accounts, a single MT565 is sent for the consolidated nominal in the option selected. In the case of segregated accounts, individual MT565s are sent from each entitlement for the option selected. If MT565 has already been sent for the option and another record in MT565.INSTRUCT is triggered for the same option, then system cancels the previous MT565 and resends a new MT565.


##### Processing of MT566 Inward Message

Inward MT566 identifies the DIARY record and updates the Total Cash Received field. The Total Cash Local Currency field is the amount in PSTA cash tag 19B of MT566, Total Security , Total Credit and Total Debit . If the event is set for full STP and if the values matched are within tolerance levels, then the system automatically authorises the DIARY record and creates a SC.ENT.AUTHORISE record. This is used to automatically authorise the entitlements.

In some cases, there are multiple MT566 received for multiple movements for the same event. In this case, when the first MT566 is received with only partial movement details, the system updates the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG application with the status as RECO. If subsequent MT566 updates the additional details and if all the values matched are within tolerance, then during diary re-run, the system automatically generates the SC.ENT.AUTHORISE record and authorises the entitlements.

If there is any error during the processing of the MT566, then the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG application is updated with status as error or warning (as required).

In case of diary corresponding to full STP which involves cash and security movements, the system performs authorisation of entitlement only when cash and security movements are matched or within tolerance. When the first MT566 is received (for cash) and values are matched or within tolerance, the system updates the status in

application as RECO and it denotes that reconciliation process has started.

However, in case of first MT566 the status is updated as:

- Error and remains the same, if values are outside tolerance and even if subsequent MT566 match with other movements.
- Warning and remains the same, if values are within tolerance and even if subsequent MT566 match with other movements.

The three scenarios possible for second MT566 provided the first MT566 exactly matches are:

- If second MT566 is received (for stock) and does not match, then the status is updated as error.
- If second MT566 is received and does not match but within tolerance, then the status is updated as warning.
- If second MT566 is received and matches, then the status is updated as OK.

> **⚠️ Note:** For some events, a full STP process may not work and in such cases, the system can be parameterised to follow a partial STP flow. In such an instance, the DIARY record and ENTITLEMENT s must be authorised manually.

The cash and stock movements are posted once the entitlements are authorised. Cash and stock movements are to be considered contractual as there are no further messages or updates post MT566. Therefore SC.SETTLEMENT is not updated.


##### Creation of Diary with MT566

If the 566 Create Diary field in SC.CA.PARAMETER is flagged with the ID as DIARY, the system allows diary creation with an incoming MT566.

Whenever an MT566 message is received, the system first checks whether a diary record exists for the event using the CORP reference. If an existing record in DIARY with the same CORP.REF as incoming MT566 is not found, the system looks for a record in DIARY with the same event type, depository, security and ex-date.

- In case the system finds an existing record as above, it authorises all the entitlements using the details of MT566.
- In case the system is unable to match an existing record in DIARY with the incoming MT566, then the system identifies the DIARY.TYPE corresponding to the incoming message, using the CAEV tag. If the event is a mandatory event that is, Options flag is not set in DIARY.TYPE , the system creates a record in DIARY using the details of the incoming MT566 message. The SC.CA.ERROR.LOG states that DIARY is created from MT566. If the event is mandatory but the MT566 does not contain sufficient information to create a diary, the record in DIARY is created in hold and also a record is created in SC.CA.ERROR.LOG with ID ( Deliv Ref - Security No ), and with the error message as Insufficient Information. If the event is not a mandatory event that is, the Options flag is Yes in DIARY.TYPE , the system does not create a diary but creates a record in SC.CA.ERROR.LOG with ID as the CORP.REF ID and with the error message as Unable to locate DIARY.

There are Corporate Action events that are not standard. These events have a CAEV code as 'OTHR'. To handle such events, a DIARY.TYPE with CAEV code set to OTHR is used. Such events can come directly via a standalone MT566. The MT566 Narrative in 70E tag under ADDINFO block holds the details of the event. When standalone MT566 with CAEV tag as OTHR is received, the system creates a record in DIARY (in IHLD status) with additional details stored in Narrative .

Example where ADR fees are collected as a Corporate Action event with CAEV as OTHR. During the above event, the system updates the fee rate in Narrative . The user must update a negative rate in Rate in DIARY . The negative rate indicates that the amount is debited from the customer.

Once the DIARY is authorised, the system calculates Entitlement Amt and updates as a negative value. Once the user authorises the record in ENTITLEMENT , the system debits the customer and credits the corporate action suspense account. Once the user authorises all the entitlements in DIARY , the system debits the corporate action suspense account and credits the Nostro account.

To deduct any tax locally, the user must update the same in Local Tax Code . Based on the absolute value of Entitlement Amt , the system calculates and debits the tax from the customer and credits the tax suspense account. When the tax is to be debited, the user must set Rate Type to Gross in DIARY .


##### Processing of MT567 Corporate Action Status and Processing Advice

An account servicer (custodian or sub-custodian) sends this message to an account owner. The message is used to advise the status, or a change in status of a CA related transaction previously instructed by the account owner. This includes:

- Acknowledgement or rejection of a CA instruction.
- Acknowledgement or rejection of a request to cancel an outstanding instruction.

It also provides a reason as to why a CA event is not completed within the announced payment dates.The status code (Tag 25D – Sequence A2) denotes:

1. Instruction processing status (IPRC) – Provides the status of an instruction.
2. Corporate action event processing status (EPRC) – Provides the status of a corporate action or the status of a payment.
3. Cancellation processing status (CPRC) – Provides the status of a cancellation request.

| Status Code | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|
| IPRC – Instruction processing status | CAND | Instruction is cancelled |
| DFLA | Default action is taken |  |
| PACK | Instruction is processed |  |
| PEND | Instruction’s processing is pending |  |
| REJT | Instruction is rejected due to system reasons |  |
| STIN | Standing instruction is applied |  |
| EPRC – CA event processing status | COMP | Processing is completed |
| PEND | Processing is not completed |  |
| RECD | Indicates funds paid is reconciled with funds received |  |
| CPRC – Cancellation processing status | CAND | Cancellation request is completed |
| CANP | Cancellation request is pending |  |
| PACK | Cancellation request is accepted for further processing |  |
| REJT | Cancellation request is rejected |  |

The reason code in the message (Tag 24B – Sequence A2a) provides the reason for the various statuses as follows:

- Cancellation reason (CAND)
- Cancellation pending reason (CANP)
- Accepted reason (PACK)
- Pending reason (PEND)
- Rejection reason (REJT)

The system maintains the list of status and reason codes as shown in the below screenshot.

The status and reason codes received are updated in the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG application.

Corporate Actions are considered as one of the most critical processing for the banks and asset managers. Each investor investing in securities needs to be informed of the Corporate Action occurrences so that the investors can make their decisions accordingly.

Our core banking system supports Corporate Actions processing through Straight Through Processing (STP).

Straight Through Processing is an automated electronic process which does not allow any human intervention and is used by the companies to speed up the transaction processing time.

3. Click the Validate a deal icon to check for errors and overrides.
4. Click the Commit the deal icon to submit the record.

#### 📖 Introduction

A corporate action (CA) event has a long life cycle starting from receiving notification of the event up to the time the proceeds of the event are settled. The entire life cycle can be handled straight through with minimal user intervention, provided all pre-requisites are parameterized. However, in reality, most users would like to verify details and manually handle events to ensure that events are closely controlled. This feature document provides an overview of how various events in the life cycle of a corporate action are handled.

> **⚠️ Note:** This document only covers topics that are not discussed in CA related features.

The following topics are discussed in this feature:

- DIARY for event capture
- Generation of entitlements based on ex dated holdings
- Setting standing instructions for a corporate action (CA)
- Blocking of holdings during a CA event
- Bulk authorisation of entitlements
- Handling odd lots
- Handling remaining Cash in the case of fractional events
- CA monitor
- Record date processing


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no specific configuration required for this feature. All event specific configurations are explained in the respective features.


#### 🔧 Working With

The stages in a corporate action event are:

- Receiving pre-notification (read Straight Through Processing SC.PRE.DIARY feature for more information)
- Updating event details in DIARY application
- Checking the entitlements generated and re-running the DIARY , if required
- Applying default standing instructions given by customers
- Blocking positions for some events to ensure customers do not dispose off their holding while the corporate action event is pending
- Authorising the entitlements


##### DIARYfor Event Capture

The DIARY application records the details, which relate to a particular event. For example, a cash dividend of EUR 2.75 per share is entered along with the identity of the security and the dates relative to the particular activity. The type of detail which Temenos Transact requires to build the entitlements for any qualifying holdings in the security is shown in the below screenshot. Capturing the Corporate Action event details differs from event to event. Refer the specific feature document to input event details.

This security offers the holders with the choice of either cash or additional securities.

The qualifying holding for the entitlement is determined based on Ex Date field. In case of events without the Ex Date (for example, tender offer), the system considers the date after the reply by date ( Reply By Date +1) as the Ex Date, and the Reply By Date as the Record Date . If the Reply By Date (cut-off date) is not present, it is based on the last date of the period of action (PWAL – 69A – Sequence E).

It is possible to specify a CA that affects only specific portfolios. To do this, the user must enter the specific portfolios in the multi-valued Portfolio No field in DIARY .

A DIARY with multiple options can be created. When the record in DIARY.TYPE has Options field set to YES, the system allows the user to multi-value the fields from Option Desc to create multiple options. The number of options that can be added to a DIARY are not restricted.

The Local Tax Code and Source Tax Code are automatically defaulted from the COUPON.TAX.CODE record. The Local Tax Code field supports the linked tax functionality. This means that, if the Link Tax field in the TAX record is populated, all the linked tax codes is shown in this field. The Local Tax Perc displays all tax percentage rates. This functionality is passed through to the ENTITLEMENT application. Separate source and local tax entries can be generated for the customer by entering YES in the Source Tax Cust and Local Tax Cust fields in the COUPON.TAX.CODE application.

Depository accounting entries can also be split into gross amount and gross amount less source tax, by selecting Yes in the Src Tax Deducted field in DIARY .

| Portfolio | 100291-1 | 100292-2 |
|---|---|---|
| Qualify Holdings | 1000 | 2000 |
| Entitlement Amount | 10000 | 20000 |
| Foreign Charges | 500 | 1000 |
| Tax on Foreign Charges | 50 | 100 |
| Net Amount | 9450 | 18900 |

A value-dated entitlement can also be generated by selecting the Value option in the Trade or Value field in the generated DIARY . All security movements that have a Value Date before the Ex Date in the DIARY are included. All positions where the Ex Date is less than the Value Date are ignored. Entitlements are generated only when the Ex Date is greater than the Value Date .

The Block Position field in DIARY.TYPE indicates whether the position is to be blocked by the CA or not. The possible options as explained below:

- Null (Blank) - Block is not required.
- Diary - The block is created when the DIARY is authorised and the unauthorised records in ENTITLEMENT are created. The block is released when the ENTITLEMENT is authorised.
- Entitlement - The block is created only when the ENTITLEMENT is authorised.
- Option - The block is created when the option is elected (for example, for tender offer, the block is created only if the customer elects to take the offer).

The system can block either the event security or the resultant security (the new stock received as entitlement). To block the new security, the Block New Sec field in DIARY.TYPE should be set to Yes. The block on new security is effective until the date when the new security is available for trading. The default value for this field is held in DIARY.TYPE . If a block is required, then the qualify holding is blocked by creating a record in SC.BLOCK.SEC.POS .

The Block From field is set for the corporate actions where the eligible security positions needs to be blocked from the ex date or record date. If the positions should be blocked from the ex date, then select the Ex Date option in the Block From field and the system creates the records in SC.BLOCK.SEC.POS with the Eff From Date field as ex date. If the positions should be blocked from the record date, then select the Record Date option in the Block From field and the system creates the records in SC.BLOCK.SEC.POS with Eff From Date as record date.

The Block From field can be selected only if the Block Position field is set as Diary. If the Block Position field is set as Diary and the Block From field is not marked, then the positions blocked from the DIARY are authorised. If there is a new MT564 REPL with new ex date or record date, after the re-run of the diary the old positions are unblocked and new positions are blocked from the new blocking date (that is, Ex Date or Record Date as specified in the Block From field).

If the new ex date or record date is a future date, then the old positions are unblocked and the new positions are blocked from the future date, that is, the records in SC.BLOCK.SEC.POS are created with Eff From Date as the future date. If new ex date or record date is back date, then the old positions are unblocked and the new positions are blocked from current bank day, that is the records in SC.BLOCK.SEC.POS are created with Eff From Date as current bank day (after DIARY is re-run).

The SC.CA.OPTION.DESC application allows the users to create different options applicable for CA. The option description is mapped based on definition in this application. The various CA code indicators are sent as part of Tag 22F in Sequence E (CA options) of MT564. Some of these indicators are ABST (abstain), CONY (consent granted), CONN (consent denied) and so on. The Option Desc field is updated based on description provided for the indicator. A record in DIARY is created for optional events (for example, STOCK and CASH) as shown in the below screenshot.

In the case of voluntary events, No Action (NOAC) is the default option for investors who are not willing to participate in the event. There is no impact on the customer positions for customers who do not participate (no reversal, rebook of positions).

For events involving securities traded in restricted currencies, it is possible to specify the settlement currency and the Forex (FX) rate (between restricted and settlement currency) at DIARY level. The list of restricted currencies are maintained in the SC.RESTRICTED.CURRENCY application.

For all the events involving restricted currencies defined in this application, the settlement currency along with the FX rate becomes mandatory at DIARY level. The settlement currency and FX rate can be manually input in DIARY , or it is defaulted from SC.RESTRICTED.CURRENCY (and from CURRENCY for the FX rate) or can be mapped from SC.PRE.DIARY . This is applicable for all events (cash receipt or payment) involving restricted currencies. The event ( DIARY ) is authorised and the entitlements are created only after the settlement currency and the FX rate are entered.

In the ENTITLEMENT application, the Entitlement Amount field holds the settlement currency equivalent. Source or local taxes and other charges are also calculated in the settlement currency. Also, the record in Entitlement holds the event currency equivalent amount for information purposes.

Transact handles MT564 per sub-account. The system creates a separate record in DIARY per sub-account and enable reconciliation at the sub-account level. The following are the possible options.

- Set Ca Stp By Sub Acc as Yes in SC.PARAMETER . The STP processing of any corporate action creates entitlements based on the sub-account of the message.
- Set Ca Stp By Sub Acc as No in DIARY.TYPE , if the user wants to exclude the processing of depository by sub-account for any specific event.

The sub-accounts can be omnibus sub-accounts or segregated accounts as per the portfolio. The omnibus sub-accounts can be created in two ways:

- By including the different sub-accounts inside the same Depository in the record of CUSTOMER.SECURITY .
- By creating separate records in CUSTOMER.SECURITY for each sub-account and linking them using the same value in the Parent Depository field.

Whenever a corporate action notification is received from depository with sub-account, the system checks for the existence of the parameter to create a record in DIARY by sub-account. If yes, then the system checks for the 97A tag in MT564 to fetch the sub-account external ID. The external ID is then checked in the system to determine the creation of a record in DIARY .


###### Processing Message

The following are the various message processing.

The system identifies the TAG97A value of the incoming message corresponding to Sub Acc Ext Id in CUSTOMER.SECURITY . The following steps are performed by the system based on the details in CUSTOMER.SECURITY .

1. Creates a record in SC.PRE.DIARY by updating the Sub Account field with Transact sub-account.
2. Creates a record in DIARY with the Sub Account field set as corresponding Transact sub-account.
3. Creates entitlements for eligible positions with the Transact sub-account corresponding to Sub Account in DIARY record.

The system identifies the Tag 97A value corresponding to Dep Ext Acc Id in CUSTOMER.SECURITY . The following steps are performed by the system based on the details in CUSTOMER.SECURITY .

1. Creates a record in SC.PRE.DIARY with the Depository field set as the CUSTOMER.SECURITY ID and Sub Account to MAIN.
2. The same is created in DIARY record.
3. Creates entitlements for the eligible positions of the depository set in the Depository field in DIARY .

In this case there would be many portfolios having a segregated account. Therefore, when a message is received for any one segregated account, the system creates a single record in SC.PRE.DIARY/DIARY for all the segregated accounts. Any future MT564 for segregated accounts are ignored.

When a message is received with the Tag 97A corresponding to a Sub Acc Ext ID in SEC.ACC.MASTER , the following steps are performed by the system.

1. Creates a record in SC.PRE.DIARY with the Depository field set as the depository from where the message is received and Sub Account to SEGREGATED.
2. The same is created in DIARY record.
3. Creates entitlements for all the segregated account positions in the Depository field.

On receiving subsequent messages for the other segregated accounts, the system does not create a new record in SC.PRE.DIARY or DIARY rather would record the details in SC.CA.ERROR.LOG with the sub-account of the incoming message. For such segregated entitlements, MT566 is received as per the segregated account and reconciled directly with the corresponding entitlement.

| Scenario | Canc Auto Process Value |
|---|---|
| DIARY by sub-account | First - Reversal is performed when the system receives the first notification with CANC or WITH function from the depository. All - Reversal is performed after cancellation notifications are received for all segregated accounts. |
| Single DIARY for multiple sub-accounts | First – Reversal is performed when the system receives the first notification with CANC or WITH function from the depository. All - Reversal is performed after cancellation notifications are received for all sub-accounts. |

When Transact receives a Corporate Action notification message (MT564), the system processes it and creates records in SC.PRE.DIARY , DIARY , and ENTITLEMENT . The user can view the latest incoming corporate action notification messages (MT564 – NEWM, REPE, REPL) for,

- Omnibus sub-accounts - Through the context enquiry attached in the respective DIARY record.
- Segregated sub-accounts - Through the context enquiry attached in the corresponding ENTITLEMENT record.

When Ca Stp By Sub Acc is set to Yes, the system creates a DIARY record for each omnibus sub-account upon receiving the corresponding message. Thus, the latest message received for the omnibus sub-account is stored in the context enquiry of DIARY . If the message is received for a segregated sub-account, the message can be viewed only in the respective ENTITLEMENT record.

When Ca Stp By Sub Acc is set to No, the system creates only one DIARY record irrespective of the number of sub-accounts. Thus, if the incoming message with 97A:SAFE contains an omnibus sub-account, it can be viewed at the DIARY level. However, if the incoming message with 97A:SAFE contains a segregated sub-account, it can be viewed at respective ENTITLEMENT record.

The below screenshot shows the DIARY enquiry displaying the messages received for two omnibus sub accounts ( Ca Stp By Sub Acc is not set).

The below screenshot shows the ENTITLEMENT enquiry displaying the MT564 message received for a segregated sub-account.


##### Generating Entitlements

If the user authorises the completed record in DIARY , any resultant entitlements to be built on-line is the subject of a TSA.SERVICE request. Temenos Transact uses the details in DIARY together with the various rules as specified in the DIARY.TYPE application, to ascertain whether there are any qualifying holdings in the specified security. If there are entitlements to be processed, then the appropriate CA’s record in TSA.SERVICE must be run. The ID of this record is in the XXX/SC.CORPORATE.ACTIONS format, where XXX is the company mnemonic for the appropriate company. The entitlements are not created unless the TSM in TSA.SERVICE is also set to run, this identifies that CAs are to be processed.

If the process does not take place and there were entitlements expected, re-check the date details in DIARY and check whether the positions exist as of Ex Date . In case of any incorrect date, change it on the DIARY and select Yes in the Rerun field. Upon authorisation, the system performs a further search for qualifying the holdings. After creating the record in DIARY , the user runs the CA service to generate the records in entitlement . The generated entitlement records are in IHLD/INAU status, based on Option field in DIARY.TYPE .

For the events, where the field Option field in DIARY.TYPE is set to No, election in entitlement is not required and total qualifying holding is applied for the available option. For the events, where the Option field in DIARY.TYPE is set to YES, election in entitlement is required and the customer can choose to elect in single option or multiple option. The user can input option no in the Option field to indicate whether the user wants to accept the first or second option. User can also elect in each of the options partially by inputting the nominal in Option Nominal field.

The below shown entitlements are created in IHLD as the DIARY is created for optional events.

A sample of the generated records in Entitlement are shown in the below screenshot.

The election can be done in the entitlement record and the record is moved to INAU status. Based on the setup MT565 message can be sent to the depository confirming the customer election.

| Fields | Values |
|---|---|
| Auto Rerun | DAILY |
| Auto Days | 2 |
| Prior After | PRIOR |
| Upto Date | PAY.DATE |

| Before Rerun | After Rerun |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qualifying Holding | STOCK | CASH | Pending Nominal | Record Status | New Qualifying Holding | STOCK | CASH | Pending Nominal | Record Status |
| 1000 | 1000 | - | - | INAU | 1200 | 1200 | - | - | INAU |
| 1000 | 500 | 500 | - | INAU | 1200 | 500 | 500 | 200 | INAU |
| 1000 | 400 | 400 | 200 | INAU | 1200 | 400 | 400 | 400 | INAU |

If there is an event level change in the DIARY after ENTITLEMENT s are generated and qualifying holdings are reconciled, there is a possibility to preserve the existing entitlements (qualifying holdings and local reference related fields) and update the changes from the DIARY into the ENTITLEMENT .

- For this purpose, the Rerun field in DIARY is set to Retain. Whenever the user performs a change in the DIARY fields and if the Rerun field is set to Retain, the system does not rerun the DIARY (entitlements are not dropped and regenerated). Instead, the changes in the DIARY are updated into the existing ENTITLEMENT . New entitlements are not generated during the update.
- Validations are made to ensure that whenever there is a change to the fields in DIARY , the Rerun field is set to Yes or Retain.

> **⚠️ Note:** This ensures that the qualifying holdings are locked and other fields in the existing entitlements are preserved when the DIARY is rerun. This helps in scenarios where reconciliation of the qualifying holding has been done with the custodian or registry.

Overrides are raised, if the user selects the option after the value in Reply By Date and Cut Off Time fields.

Even after some records in ENTITLEMENT are authorised, DIARY can be re-run by setting Rerun to Retain. This is possible only for those events in which the records in DIARY.TYPE has Refresh Remain set to YES. For such events, the user can re-run DIARY , even after some records in ENTITLEMENT are authorised. The unauthorised entitlements are refreshed (that is, fees and charges are recalculated) but no other change happens.

For any corporate action events, transactions that take place between diary creation date and ex-date impacts the client’s eligible holding. It is important for the client to view their updated eligible holding on a near real time basis to change or make their election based on the revised holdings. For events that requires a near real time update to the eligible holdings, the user must set the Ent Qh Online Update field as Yes in DIARY . The user can configure the same by setting Ent Qh Online Update in DIARY.TYPE .

The screenshots below show Ent Qh Online Update setup in DIARY and DIARY.TYPE .

A trade or transfer can take place with a trade date before the ex-date of an open Diary. Post authorisation of the transaction, the system identifies the Open Diary records for the Instrument, depository/sub-account and place of safekeeping (if the positions are built by PSAF) combination based on the below criteria:

- Ent Qh Online Update set as Yes in DIARY .
- No entitlement is authorized.

Once the open diary records are identified, the system updates the Qualify Holding field in ENTITLEMENT record pertaining to the portfolio in the transaction by running the XXX/SC.ENT.QH.ONLINE.UPDATE service. The system behaviour under different scenarios are as follows:

Scenario A: Purchase transaction for an existing position/ Reverse of an existing Sale transaction

- The system increases Qualify Holding in ENTITLEMENT to the extent of the purchased nominal or to the extent of reversed sale nominal.
- The system re-calculates the entitlement amount or the new nominal to be received.
- For mandatory events, the system leaves the record in INAU.
- For optional events, if no elections are made, the system leaves the record on IHLD.

For optional events if elections have been made and Retain Option is not set in DIARY , then the system does not retain any elections and the record status is moved to IHLD. Retain Option is set as Yes in DIARY , then if Multi election is enabled (Multi Election is set to Yes in DIARY.TYPE), the system retains the election and updates the pending nominal with the increased quantity. The record will be in INAU. Multi election is not enabled, the system retains the elections made (quantity specified in Option Nom and Retain Nom). However, an error will be raised asking the user to correct the elections, since there is a mismatch between the Qualifying Holding and the elected quantity. The record will be in IHLD. Multi election is enabled ( Multi Election is set as Yes in DIARY.TYPE ), the system retains the election and updates the pending nominal with the increased quantity. The record will be in INAU. Multi election is not enabled, the system retains the elections made (quantity specified in Option Nom and Retain Nom). However, an error is raised asking the user to correct the elections since there is a mismatch between Qualify Holding and the elected quantity. The record is updated to IHLD. Retain Option is set as Always in DIARY , then if Multi election is enabled, ( Multi Election is set as Yes in DIARY.TYPE ), the system retains the election and updates the pending nominal with the increased quantity. The record will be in INAU. Multi election is not enabled, the system retains the elections made (that is, quantity specified in Option Nom and Retain Nominal ). However, an error is raised asking the user to correct the elections since there is a mismatch between Qualify Holding and the elected quantity. The record is updated to IHLD.

Scenario B: Sale transaction for an existing position/ Reverse of an existing Purchased transaction

- The system decreases Qualify Holding in ENTITLEMENT to the extent of the sale nominal or to the extent of reversed purchase nominal.
- The system re-calculates the entitlement amount or the new nominal to be received.
- For mandatory events, the system leaves the record in INAU.
- For optional events, if no elections are made, the system leaves the record on IHLD.
- For optional events if elections have been made and, Retain Option is not set in DIARY , then the system does not retain any elections and the record status is moved to IHLD. Retain Option is set as Yes in DIARY , then if, Multi election is enabled ( Multi Election is set as Yes in DIARY.TYPE ), the system does not retain any elections and the record is moved to IHLD. Multi election is not enabled and, Only a single option is elected, then the system updates the election with Option Nom equal to the newly updated qualify holdings. More than one option is elected, then the system does not retain the election and moves the record status to IHLD. In this case, the user must re-elect the options. Retain Option is set as Always in DIARY , then if Multi election is enabled, ( Multi Election is set as Yes in DIARY.TYPE ), If the new qualifying holding is greater than or equal to the elected quantity (that is, quantity given in Elect Nominal and Retain Nominal ), then the system retains the elected quantity ( Elect Nominal and Retain Nominal ) and updates Pending Nominal with the remaining quantity. The record status is updated as INAU. If the new qualifying holding is lesser than the elected quantity (that is, quantity given in Elect Nominal and Retain Nominal ), then the system still retains the elected quantity ( Elect Nominal and Retain Nominal ). However, an error is raised asking the user to correct the elections, since there is a mismatch between the qualifying holding and the elected quantity. The record is updated as IHLD. Multi election is not enabled, the system retains the elections made (that is, quantity specified in Option Nom and Retain Nominal ). However, an error is raised asking the user to correct the elections. The record status is retained as IHLD.

Scenario C: Complete Sale of Position

- For both mandatory and optional events, the system updates the Qualify Holding in ENTITLEMENT as 0.
- Any elections made are removed. On rerunning the DIARY , the respective ENTITLEMENT record is dropped off provided the transaction is settled completely.

Scenario D: Purchase transaction creating fresh position

- For both mandatory and optional events, the system creates an ENTITLEMENT record for the respective portfolio with Qualify Holding equal to the buy nominal.
- The Entitlement will be placed on hold.

In all the above scenarios, the system updates Manual Creation in ENTITLEMENT as ‘Online’. For events where the qualify holding are updated in such a manner,

- The system does not allow authorisation of any entitlements belonging to the diary until the DIARY is Rerun.
- The user cannot generate MT565 instruction from MT565.INSTRUCT until the DIARY is Rerun. However, the users can continue to elect or change election or cancel election for entitlements updated in such a manner.
- The system creates a record in ENTITLEMENT.BROKER for unsettled transaction.
- The system does not update the total cash, stock or any other details at the diary level. In other words, the Diary is not in sync with the entitlement details until the DIARY is Rerun.

During the end of day process, for entitlements updated in such a manner, the respective DIARY record is automatically Rerun, immaterial of what is set for auto re-run of Diary. When DIARY is Rerun, the system:

- Updates the total cash/stock and any other details at the Diary level.
- Updates the Manual Creation field in ENTITLEMENT as No.

- If an entitlement has been manually created, that is, Manual Update is Yes in ENTITLEMENT , the system does not update any transaction impacting the qualifying holding for the respective entitlement. The user has to manually edit the qualifying holdings in this case.
- To avoid performance issues and delay in processing DIARY records, the user must set Ent Qh Online Update as Yes only for events involving choice and not for the events such as mandatory dividend or coupon payments which are generally voluminous.
- For transactions that are authorised during the end of day processing, the XXX/SC.ENT.QH.ONLINE.UPDATE does not process any transactions during the COB stage - "B". The system takes care of this during the automatic rerun.
- If MT566 is received before rerun of DIARY record, the system updates the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG as ‘Entitlements are updated online. Rerun required’.

The SC.EX.DATE.MTR application records the details of the underlying transaction and the corresponding Diary and entitlement records which are impacted due to it. The system records the below details in the application.

- Entitlement Id – To store the details of the entitlement which are impacted due to the transaction.
- Diary Id – To store the corresponding diary ID of the entitlement.
- Online Upd Status – To store the status of the corresponding entitlement. The possible values are Pending – if the XXX/SC.ENT.QH.ONLINE.UPDATE service is yet to update the respective entitlement. This status is applicable only when Ent Qh Online Update set as Yes in DIARY and no entitlements are authorised. Processed – if the qualify holdings of the entitlement are updated successfully. This status is applicable only for those entitlements eligible for an online update. Manual – if the user has to manually take action to update the Qualify holding for the entitlement by either rerunning the diary or reversing the existing diary and create a new one.

Once ENTITLEMENT authorisation has commenced and a major error is observed or it is required to cancel the event, the only recourse is to reverse the DIARY . This action is necessary because once authorisation has commenced, the Temenos Transact on-line accounting entries are built for all entries that are authorised. Once DIARY is reversed, the accounting entries are also reversed. The user can easily raise a corrected or second DIARY to start the process once again. However, individual records in ENTITLEMENT can be reversed (if necessary).

Once the DIARY is authorised and system successfully locates any qualifying holdings, the authorised record in DIARY contains the details of total nominal or cash expected as per the system. The benefits attributable to each option is in turn broken down by depository. There are also fields to manually record (or map from 566) the nominal or cash received from the depository. User can then reconcile differences between system calculated values and that received from the depository.

> **⚠️ Note:** Some depositories may be excluded for CA events. To set the eligible depositories for CA processing, the user must select Y or No as required in the Corporate Actions field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY (for each depository).

The multi-value sets from the Rp Account to Rp Tot Cash Lcy fields allows to have the total cash amount of the nostro in case of repo positions. This is done, if the Split Debit Cpn field is set to Yes in the REPO.PARAMETER application. There is a REPO account defined in the Account field (for the REPO application) in the NOSTRO.ACCOUNT application (Read REPO feature for more information).

The Entitlement Amount field holds the system calculated entitlement amount. This can be amended by the user, if required. The Orig Ent Amount field in ENTITLEMENT holds the system calculated amount. This can be used for audit and reporting purposes to view the calculated amount and the manually amended value.

After authorising the records in ENTITLEMENT , it is possible to reverse the records unless an adjustment is done at the depository level . For each record reversed in ENTITLEMENT , the Entl Reversed field in DIARY is updated per depository. The last record in ENTITLEMENT linked to this depository cannot be reversed, instead the record in DIARY must be reversed.

For pure non-cash events, if the Taxable field is set to Yes in DIARY.TYPE and if the Post Local Tax field is set to Y in DIARY application, then the corresponding local tax amount is posted in the entitlements created.

For events such as DRIPS, if the Reinvest Net field is set to Y in DIARY application, then the Gross or Net field is defaulted automatically to Net in the ENTITLEMENT . Under such cases the nominal are calculated after subtracting the source tax amount from the entitlement amount, that is

In case of an entitlement offering more than a single option, the actions to be performed are very different. The below screenshot illustrates a typical example which provides the customer with two options.

As seen from the sub-fields, there are two possible options available. The user can now decide depending on the rules as defined in the underlying DIARY.TYPE application in respect of the corporate activity being processed. In those cases, where the user wants to take all of a particular option, the user can input either 1 or 2 into the Option field to indicate whether the user wants to accept the first or second option. In this particular case, if the user enters 1, it advises Temenos Transact that the user has elected to receive the full cash dividend offered. User can also elect in each of the options partially.

There are several CAs such as redemption, fractional cash for conversion, coupon payment and so on, where the custodian notifies the cash amount rather than providing a rate. The cash amount needs to be pro-rated based on customer qualifying holdings. For cash CAs, the payout amount can be specified instead of a percentage or rate. Core Banking product calculates the entitlement amount by prorating the total amount based on customer qualifying holdings. The following fields in DIARY are used to record, calculate and pro-rate the cash amount.

- Event Nominal - Nominals as provided by the issuer or depository
- Event Amount - Amount provided by the issuer or depository
- Sys Event Nominal - Total of all qualifying nominals. This is calculated by the system and is used to calculate the entitlement amount, if Event Nominal is not given.

The entitlement amount is calculated as:

Qualifying holding = USD 150

Event Amount = USD 3750

Event Nominal = USD 750

Entitlement amount = 150 * 3750/750 = USD 750

If the cash amount or units received from the issuer or depository does not match the sum of the individual amounts or units in the customer entitlements, the users can amend the Entitlement Amt field manually in entitlement . This is the final amount. The amendment has to be done before the entitlement is authorised. The system-calculated amount is retained in entitlement in the Orig Ent Amount field and can be used for audit and reporting.


##### CA Default Option

The user can choose a default option at the DIARY level. This default instruction overwrites any Default Option . If the user enters the option number in the Def Ins Option field in DIARY , then this option is set in DIARY.TYPE .

In the above example, the Def Ins Option is 1. This is the number of option in the current record in DIARY .


##### Settlement Transformations

Temenos Transact has the ability to process different CAs including cash and security dividends, bonus, conversions, and rights issues. In case of corporate events where one security is converted to another, the system creates two settlement records for all eligible portfolios:

- One for moving out the old security position and
- One for creating a position in the new security, if the DIARY event is to be processed on an actual settlement basis.

When these settlements are processed, the positions in the original security are cleared out and positions in the new security are created. The unsettled trades, if any, in the original security must be settled manually. The settlement transformation functionality automatically closes out the unsettled trades in the original security while processing the conversion corporate event. The Auto Conversion field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY automatically processes the unsettled trades in the original security, while processing the corporate events when one security is converted to another. This field can be set to Yes only and it allows the input only if the Customer Type is DEPOSITORY.

The Auto Conversion field in DIARY is used for this purpose. The valid inputs for this field are Yes or No and input is allowed only for corporate events, where one security is being converted to another. While processing the records in ENTITLEMENT for conversions, if the Auto Conversion field is set to Yes at transaction level then all unsettled trades in the original security is automatically settled on value date (pay date) of the event. It is assumed that for stock events, pay date and value date are the same. If Auto Conversion field is set to No at the transaction level, the unsettled trades are not automatically settled and the functionality of manually processing unsettled trades continues.

If the Auto Conversion field is not set at transaction level, then the Auto Conversion if any, defined in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY level is considered. For depositories with Auto Conversion set to Yes, all unsettled trades in the original security pertaining to those depositories are automatically settled. In cases where DIARY is to be processed on actual settlement basis, the auto settlement as defined above is only for the nominal side. The cash settlement in respect of unsettled trades are processed while settling the broker due (on a pro-rata basis to the Stock Settlement) in respect of new stock.


##### Price Conditions

Cum Dividend and Ex divided are price conditions that determine whether the stock is traded with the value of dividend or without the value of the dividend payment. The SM.PARAMETER application holds the details for the identification of Cum and Ex markers. Transactions containing these indicators are considered when calculating the nominal that is entitled to a corporate event. Read Instrument Master for more information on setup of cum and ex markers. The markers can be used in DIARY.TYPE as shown in the screenshot below.

The Cum and Ex markers are identified together with the time scales before and after the Ex-date that these markers are effective. The markers are followed through order entry processing, trading and security transfers onto the transaction file. If these markers are identified, then transactions containing them are considered when calculating the nominal that is entitled to a corporate event. The Cum Time Scale field stores the period of time after the Ex-date of the event, to be checked for Cum transactions. The Ex Time Scale field stores the period of time before the Ex-date, to be checked for Ex transactions.

The routines that calculate ENTITLEMENT examines at the above mentioned fields on DIARY.TYPE , which establishes the Cum and Ex markers applicable to the event type and the periods to which they apply. The Qualify Holding field in ENTITLEMENT is initially calculated without considering these markers. The SECURITY.TRANS application is used to identify any transactions that have the Cum marker and Ex marker in the Cum Ex Ind field, within the Cum Time Scale and Ex Time Scale after the ex date of the event. The Qualify Holding is then adjusted by these transactions (security credit transaction increases it and security debit transaction decreases it).


##### Short Position Processing

The Allow Short Posn field in DIARY.TYPE indicates whether to process the corporate events on short or zero positions or not process the events at all. Zero positions are processed only when either an outstanding debit/credit transaction or a settled non-returned borrow/lend exists. The Allow Short Posn field is set to Yes only (processing enabled), if the Actual Settlement field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Yes and the Settle Method field is set to US. This is not affected by the setting of customers or transactions to contractual settlement (which does not disable processing).

> **⚠️ Note:** If the broker side of a transaction is set to contractual settlement, then it is not possible to establish the outstanding transactions and the desired result may not be achieved.

When the Allow Short Posn field in the DIARY.TYPE application is set to Yes, the fields in the ENTITLEMENT are populated with details of both credit and debit outstanding transactions, details of any non-returned settled loans and borrows along with details of the effect the portfolio is having on the depot position. The records in ENTITLEMENT are also created for positions that are short as of the Ex Date . In this case, the Qualify Holding field is updated with a negative amount. Non-returned settled loans or borrows are established as of the Record Date in DIARY application.

If the Allow Short Posn field in the DIARY.TYPE application is set to No, the ENTITLEMENT related fields are only populated with details of the outstanding credit transactions and existing functionality is then followed to calculate the outcome of the event. Only long positions as of the Ex Date -1 is processed and short positions does not create records in ENTITLEMENT . The record in DIARY.TYPE displays Allow Short Posn set to Yes as shown in the below screenshot.


##### CA Monitor

Temenos Transact checks for any pending record in DIARY when a SECURITY.POSITION is changed. For example, if a SEC.TRADE is generated to buy a security for which a DIARY is created, Temenos Transact generates a record in SC.EX.DATE.MTR . This is the case when the Trade Date field of the trade is prior to the Ex Date in DIARY .

The ID of SC.EX.DATE.MTR is equal to the SECURITY.TRANS ID and the Narrative field contains the action to be undertaken.


##### Record Date Processing

The record date of a corporate event does not affect the beneficial entitlement to the event, but it affects the way the event is processed with regard to who receives the outcome of an event directly and where the outcome is due to or from (market claims). The DIARY and ENTITLEMENT applications considers the Record Date when creating and processing the records in Entitlement . This processing:

- reflects the correct depot (agent) position as of the Record Date.
- identifies the debit and credit transactions, where the outcome of the event is due to/from the counterparty using the record date of the event. This includes the process when the record date is before or after the ex-date and transactions that settle after the Ex Date but before the record date.

Overrides warn the user when they are authorising a record in ENTITLEMENT that is created either before the Ex Date or Record Date . This functionality does not affect the calculation of the portfolio beneficial entitlement to an event. The Record Date field in DIARY is used to input the record date of the event. The values in this field are used by the routines that create the record in ENTITLEMENT to establish the settled non-returned SBL (Read the Stock Borrow Lending section for more information) transactions position for the processing of all corporate events.

The record in DIARY shows the value in Ex Date after Record Date .

The records in ENTITLEMENT are created by DIARY includes the following information:

- Short customer positions
- Debit transactions that were outstanding as of the Ex Date -1, which are due to the counterparty
- Lending and borrowing transactions that were settled but not returned before or on the record date
- The position at the depot (agent)

A long position that is created for one customer and a borrow for another customer is shown in the below screenshot.

Record date processing does not affect the calculations for the beneficial holding for the portfolio, but affects the transactions that are identified as due in/out to the Counterparties (market claims) and the amount that is shown at the depot (agent). The calculation of the depot (agent) holding, which is updated in the Depot Holding field is amended to reflect the amount of the holding as of the Record Date , instead of the Ex Date . The records in ENTITLEMENT are created by DIARY for the above SECURITY.POSITION as shown in the below screenshots.

Override messages are issued when authorising a record in ENTITLEMENT . A check is made to compare the creation date of the record to the ex date and record dates of the event. Overrides are issued when the record is created before either of these dates, which warns the user that the information may be out of date and therefore inaccurate. Then the user must decide which of the following manual actions must be taken:

- Accept the override and continue processing, if the positions are unchanged.
- Re-run the event, if the position has changed and all of the related records in ENTITLEMENT are unauthorised.
- Reverse and re-input the event, if the position has changed and any of the records in ENTITLEMENT are authorised.

##### Creating Individual Orders from CA Events

For corporate action (CA) events like Dividend Reinvestment and Rights issue, corresponding records are created in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER table, as the entitlements are authorised based on the customer election in the entitlement record. The CA Separate Orders field in SC.PARAMETER is used to control the creation of records in SEC.OPEN.ORDER through a corporate action event. If this field is set to Yes:

- System always creates a single order per entitlement.
- Entitlement ID is updated in Cu Entl Id field of the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application.

Any order created from corporate action event is created in unauthorised status (INAU).


##### Setting Order Type for CA orders

Order Type is a mandatory field in DIARY.TYPE that identifies the order type for the SEC.OPEN.ORDER records created from the CA event. The order type for any corporate action event is updated based on the input in this field. If this field is not set for an event that creates the order, all the corresponding records in SEC.OPEN.ORDER are placed in IHLD status. Back office users should set the order type for each record manually and place the orders in INAU to trigger a back-end to front-end flow.

This field is used only for CA events that create orders. The same is ignored when set for events other than CA.

The Order Ofs Version field in DIARY.TYPE is used to input the valid version name to be used to create the record in SEC.OPEN.ORDER .

Whenever, a record is created from ENTITLEMENT , system checks the Order Ofs Version field and based on the input, the values in SEC.OPEN.ORDER are defaulted. If this field is blank, system creates records in SEC.OPEN.ORDER in IHLD status.


##### Reconciling Eligible Holdings

An eligible balance notification in SWIFT is indicated by MT564 with the function of the message (:22F/) as REPE indicating the eligible balance per account owner (:97A://SAFE).

Generally, MT564 (REPE) is received from the custodian on the ex-date. For each advice that is received, the system maps the holdings per depository and sub-account combination in SC.CA.ERROR.LOG .

The Temenos Transact computed holdings for the depository and sub-account combination are updated in the Sys Holdings field in SC.CA.ERROR.LOG . Whenever the diary is rerun, the respective SC.CA.ERROR.LOG is updated with the revised quantity. If subsequently a new MT564 REPE message is received for the same event, the quantity is overwritten in SC.CA.ERROR.LOG .

The Diary Holding Details (SC.DIARY.ELIG.HOLDINGS) is launched by the bank’s corporate action user to compare holdings in the system against the holdings reported by the custodian.

If the holdings match, the status is updated as 'OK' in the enquiry. If the holdings are within tolerance, the status is updated as ‘WARNING’. If the holdings are outside the tolerance, the status is updated as ‘ERROR’. The tolerance can be specified in the Elig Holdings Tol Perc field in SC.CA.PARAMETER .

Reconciliation is based on the latest values available in SC.CA.ERROR.LOG while launching the enquiry.

The below screenshot shows the enquiry output for a corporate action event. The reconciliation status shows 'ERROR', as the custodian holdings do not match with the holdings in Temenos Transact.

In the below screenshot the quantity advised by the custodian matches with the quantity in Temenos Transact. Hence, the reconciliation status is updated as 'OK'.


##### Usufruct Arrangement

- Usufruct is a legal right that allows a person or party to use and derive income or benefit from someone else's asset, while the ownership of the asset belongs to another person.
- The usufructuary is the person who derives the benefit from the usufruct asset and is not entitled to dispose of the asset.
- There can be one or more usufructuaries for an asset with a percentage of usufruct defined for them and each usufructuary can have one or more usufruct accounts linked to them for receiving the usufruct income. The usufructuary for a portfolio (SEC.ACC.MASTER) is defined in the SC.USUFRUCT.MASTER . If the Usufruct Status field is set to Active, the usufruct arrangement is considered.
- If the field is set to INACTIVE, Usufruct arrangement is not considered, and income is booked into the portfolio owner’s account instead of usufructuary.
- The usufruct arrangement in Transact is only applicable for corporate action events involving only cash income, such as Cash Dividend and Coupons.. The events which involve securities movement are not enabled for Usufruct functionality.
- A single or multiple usufructuaries can be setup for a single portfolio. In case of multiple usufructs, the percentage share of the income needs to be specified in the Usufruct Percent field (Example: 40% to customer 1 and 60% to customer).
- For each usufructuary, the cash account, to which the income will be paid to, is defined in the Usufruct Account field. At least one cash account is mandatory for a usufructuary. Also, multiple cash accounts can be defined for the usufructuary in different currencies. In case of multiple usufructuaries, the number of cash accounts in different currency linked to all the usufructuaries of a portfolio must be equal. For example, if there are three usufructuaries say A, B, C for a portfolio. If two cash accounts – one with currency USD, one with currency GBP are linked to Usufructuary A, it is mandatory to link two cash accounts with USD and GBP currencies to other two usufructuaries B, C . Also, all the usufructuaries linked to a portfolio must have accounts linked in the same currency. For example, for the three usufructuaries A.B.C linked to a portfolio must have account with USD currency. It is not possible to have A with account in USD currency, B in GBP currency and C in EUR currency. The system defaults the account based on event currency in the applications like SEC.TRADE , ENTITLEMENT . If in case no cash account exists in event currency for the usufructuary, the system defaults the first cash account applying currency conversion.

A single usufructuary linked for a portfolio is shown below.

Multiple usufructuaries linked with multiple cash accounts in different currencies for a portfolio are shown below.

The Usufruct Arrangement field in DIARY.TYPE is used to enable Usufruct setup. However, it can be still disabled at the DIARY level. This arrangement can only be setup for the DIARY.TYPE only if Cash set to Yes, and Retain Original set to Yes and all other fields related to security movement are set to NO and also Factor Payment must be NO.

If the field is set to Yes:

- Net income paid as Cash The net income paid as cash because of corporate action event is booked to the usufructuary account instead of the portfolio owner’s default account. For example, Portfolio 100285-1 holds 10,000 of equity A on Ex Div date. A dividend of USD 1.00 per share is declared giving a gross dividend of GBP 10,000. There is a withholding source tax of 15 percent which is withheld at source giving USD 8,500 and there is no local tax. If Portfolio 100285-1 has defined only customer-131261 as its usufructuary with 100% usufruct percentage. Then the dividend of 100285-1 (USD 8,500) is paid to the cash account of the customer 131261. If Portfolio 100285-1 has defined two customers-131261 with usufruct percentage of 40, 131271 with usufruct percentage of 40 as its usufructuaries, then 40 percent of the dividend of 100285-1 (USD 8,500) is paid to the cash account of the customer 131261 and 60 percent is paid to the customer – 131271.The USD cash account of 131271 (51235) receives USD 3,400 and USD cash account of 131271 (54321) receives USD 5,100. In case no account exists for the usufructuary in the event currency, the first account of the usufructuary is considered for applying the conversion rates from the event currency to account currency.
- Accrued Interest (Coupon) to the Usufruct account: If usufruct arrangement is in place, the net interest(coupon) bought/sold is posted to the usufruct account. The income is split based on the usufruct percentage in case of multiple usufructuaries defined. The account to which the income has to be posted is identified based on the account (in trade currency) defined for the usufructuary linked to the portfolio.

The source tax and local tax with respect to the usufructuary are calculated by multiplying the Usufruct Percentage of each usufructuary with the source or local taxes calculated for the portfolio’s owner in the entitlement . This is updated in the Usufruct Source Tax and Usufruct Local Tax fields of corresponding usufructuaries. The tax entries are raised to the usufructuary account.

For example, for the portfolio 100285-1 if there are two usufructuaries defined, say A with Usufruct Percent as 45 and B with Usufruct Percent as 55. If the calculated Source Tax Amt in the entitlement is USD 90 , then Usufruct Source Tax of A is USD 40.5, which is (USD 90*45%) and for B is USD 49.5, which is (USD 90*55%). Similarly, if the calculated Local Tax Amt in the entitlement is USD 100, then Usufruct Local Tax of A is USD 45 which is (USD 100*45%) and for B is USD 55, which is (USD 100*55%).

- Enter Diary Events

- Administration and Static Data and Corporate Actions

A corporate action is an activity or event that brings material change to an organisation and affects its stakeholders. The company’s board of directors generally approve these events. In addition, shareholders are permitted to vote on some events as well.

Corporate Actions are considered as one of the most critical processing for the banks and asset managers. Each investor investing in securities needs to be informed of the Corporate actions occurrences so that investor can make his decisions accordingly. They are classified into three types:

- Mandatory – Affects all the shareholders of the company when the corporate actions is effective in market.
- Voluntary – Only a certain amount of shareholders who voluntarily decides to participate in the event.
- Mandatory with Choice – Affects all the shareholders, but are given with the choice to elect either in cash or stock or reinvested in the form of stock.

Most common types of Corporate Action Events are:

- Cash Dividend
- Stock Dividend
- Interest Payment
- Bonus Issue
- Merger
- Stock Split
- Spin Off
- Tender Offer


##### Workflow
