### 6.13  CustomerInitiatedCorporateActions


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Holders of a convertible bond have the right to convert the bond into ordinary shares before maturity. During the lifetime of the bond, when a customer chooses to make this conversion, the bond is redeemed and the customer receives the shares proportionately.*
> 
> **Applications:** `SC.ADR.GDR.DETS`, `SC.ADR.GDR.DETS:`, `SC.CUST.EVENT.CREATE`, `SC.PARAMETER`, `SC.STD.POS.TRANSF`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.TRANSFER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Adr Gdr Trans Type*, *Br Acc No*, *Br Net Amt*, *Broker No*, *Ca End Date*, *Ca Start Date*, *Conv
 Exer Price.2*, *Conv
 Exer Sec No.1* ... +55 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Holders of a convertible bond have the right to convert the bond into ordinary shares before maturity. During the lifetime of the bond, when a customer chooses to make this conversion, the bond is redeemed and the customer receives the shares proportionately.

In case of bonus options, eligible shareholders of a security are offered with bonus options in a certain proportion exercisable into ordinary shares before expiry. The holder of such bonus options can choose to exercise the options at certain price any time before the expiry of the option.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The below screenshot shows the static setup of SC.CA.PARAMETR , where the Conversion Event and Exercise Event fields are setup with the event type to be used. The event type configured in SC.CA.PARAMETER is defaulted in SC.CUST.EVENT.CREATE as explained below:

- If the Options Flag is set to Y in SECURITY.MASTER of the event security, the DIARY.TYPE defined for OPTION.EXERCISE is defaulted in SC.CUST.EVENT.CREATE .
- If the Convertible Flag is set to Y in SECURITY.MASTER , the DIARY.TYPE defined for BOND.CONVERSION is defaulted in SC.CUST.EVENT.CREATE .

The below fields in SECURITY.MASTER facilitates the customer initiated bond conversion and option exercise.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Options Flag | Indicates whether the security is exercisable into ordinary shares. This field is enabled in the option security’s SECURITY MASTER . |
| Conv Exer Sec No | Denotes the number of the new security issued through the conversion or exercise |
| Conv Exer Price | Denotes the price of the new security. For bond conversion, based on the price, the conversion ratios can be input manually by the user |
| Ca Start Date | Denotes the start date for initiating the corporate action (bond conversion or option exercise) |
| Ca End Date | Denotes the end date for initiating the corporate action (bond conversion or option exercise) |
| Old Sec Ratio | Works in conjunction with the New Sec Ratio field. This field denotes the quantity of bond or options for which the new shares are issued. This is defaulted into the Old Ratio field in the DIARY at the time of event creation |
| New Sec Ratio | Works in conjunction with the Old Sec Ratio and Conv Exer Price fields indicating the quantity of a new security issued for holdings in the event security. This is defaulted into the New Ratio field in the DIARY at the time of event creation |
| Rounding | Captures the rounding methods to handle ratios, which lead to fractional shares. The accepted values are Standard, Up and Down. |

> **⚠️ Note:** In SECURITY.MASTER for options ( Options Flag is set to Y) if the fields Old Sec Ratio and New Sec Ratio are left blank, the system defaults to 1 in both the fields. If the security is flagged as Convertible or Exercisable ( Convertible Flag is set to Y or Options Flag is set to Y), the Conv Exer Sec No , Old Sec Ratio and New Sec Ratio fields become mandatory. Otherwise, overrides are generated.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Conv Exer Sec No | 802000-100 |
| Conv Exer Price | 6.67 |
| Ca Start Date | MAY 19, 2010 |
| Ca End Date | JUN 10, 2015 |
| Old Sec Ratio | 100 |
| New Sec Ratio | 14.99 (100/6.67) |


#### 🔧 Working With

The SC.CUST.EVENT.CREATE application handles the customer initiated corporate actions, which triggers the DIARY for that initiating customer. The ID of the application is a system generated ID.


##### Trigger to Create Event for the Initiating Customer

To initiate an event for a customer, a record must be created in SC.CUST.EVENT.CREATE . The initiating customer has to input the details such as the Customer ID, Portfolio ID and the Instrument Master ID (event security).

The Event Nominal field specifies the quantity for conversion/or exercise, which is used as qualifying holdings in the entitlements.

After the SC.CUST.EVENT.CREATE application is authorised, the system creates a DIARY for the initiating customer (portfolio) and stores the DIARY reference in this application. When the service to generate entitlements is run, the ENTITLEMENT (for the initiating customer) is generated (and authorised if configured). The qualifying holdings (in entitlement) are taken from the Event Nominal field in SC.CUST.EVENT.CREATE .

On authorising the record in SC.CUST.EVENT.CREATE , the system creates a DIARY and ENTITLEMENT for the customer (729281) and stores the DIARY reference in SC.CUST.EVENT.CREATE .


##### Customer Initiated Conversion on ADR or GDR

American Depository Receipt (ADR) and Global Depository Receipt (GDR) holders may get an option to convert the holding in ADR or GDR to the underlying security.

The Underlying Security field in the SECURITY.MASTER application is used to store the underlying security number in case the security is an ADR or GDR.

For example, if Amazon is listed as a GDR security in a European market, the record created in SECURITY.MASTER for the Amazon GDR security must hold the Amazon securities as its underlying security in the SECURITY.MASTER record.

After providing the value in the Underlying Security field , the user can define the conversion ratios in the SC.ADR.GDR.DETS application. This application allows the user to store the ratios for converting ADR to GDR, GDR to another GDR, or converting the ADR or GDR to its underlying instrument. The user can also manually update the conversion fees for each conversion in the SC.ADR.GDR.DETS application.

| Underlying Security Transfer Fields | Values |
|---|---|
| Transaction Type | Credit transaction code of the transaction type defined in SC.PARAMETER |
| Security No | Target Security from the primary security transfer |
| Customer No | Defaulted from the primary security transfer |
| Security Acc | Defaulted from the primary security transfer |
| No Nominal | The nominal is calculated based on the ratio defined for this conversion in the SC.ADR.GDR.DETS application. If the quantity of incoming security calculated using the ration is in decimals, then it must be rounded down. |
| Trade Date | Defaulted from primary security transfer |
| Value Date | Defaulted from primary security transfer |
| Broker No | Defaulted from primary security transfer |
| Delivery Instr | *See Steps below |
| Conversion Fee | *See steps below |
| Cost | COST of the parent transfer (SECURITY.TRANSFER OUT) |

| Securities | Ratio | Conversion price |
|---|---|---|
| 654543-000 | 2:1 | 10 |
| 657543-000 | 5:1 | 25 |
| 656543-000 | 10:1 | 50 |

### 6.14  Demerger


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Demerger is a corporate action event in which the original security (event security) is demerged into new securities. Eligible holders of the original security as on the ex-date/record date of the event, receive additional shares in the new demerged security through the event.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Book Cost*, *Book Cost Perc*, *Corp Reference*, *Demerge Book Cost*, *Depot*, *Event type*, *Ex date*, *New Market Price* ... +6 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Demerger is a corporate action event in which the original security (event security) is demerged into new securities. Eligible holders of the original security as on the ex-date/record date of the event, receive additional shares in the new demerged security through the event.

The shareholder’s cost in the original security (event security) is apportioned across the resulting new securities.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic details the setup for a demerger event.

Additionally, if the Demerge Book Cost flag is set to Y, Temenos Transact apportions the shareholder’s cost in the original security.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section below details the life cycle of a demerger event in the system.

In the above demerger event (DIARY), existing holders of security 100055-000 on the ex-date receive new shares in 100047-000 in 5:1 ratio. In ENTITLEMENT for a customer who holds 1000 shares (100055-000) on the ex-date, receives 200 shares in the new security (100047-100).


##### Cost Apportionment

As explained earlier, the demerger event involves cost apportionment between original security and demerged security. The acquisition cost of the original security is split between the original and new securities based on the following methods:

The system can apportion the cost of original security before the demerger based on the market value of the new security. The New Market Price in DIARY and the Nominal in ENTITLEMENT is used to calculate the market value of the new security. Once the market value of the new security is calculated, the system arrives at a ratio of market value of new security to the total market value (sum of original and new security). This ratio along with the original cost (before demerger) becomes the cost of new security position. The remaining is the cost of original security position.

In the below screenshot, the cost of the original security before the demerger was 25,000. Based on the above DIARY , the customer is expected to receive 200 shares. The market price of the new security (33.9375) is used to calculate the market value.

Based on the ratio of market value of the new security to the total market value, the system calculates the cost of new security position and original security position. The cost of original security and the cost of the new security is calculated as shown in the below screenshots.

The system can also apportion the cost based on the book cost of the new security. A Book Cost field under the New Sec No multi-value field, records the book cost per new security. This is used along with the quantity of new shares received to calculate the cost of new security position.

> **⚠️ Note:** If both New Market Price and Book Cost are available at the time of event creation, the system does the cost apportion based on the Book Cost .

Consider the below example, where the book cost of the new security is 15 USD.

Suppose, the customer holds 1000 shares before Demerger at a cost of 10,000 USD. Based on the ratio, the customer is expected to receive 200 shares in the new security.

In this example, the Book Cost is 15 and Nominal is 200. The system assigns the cost of new security position as 3000. The remaining cost 7000 gets apportioned to the original security position.

For apportionment of the cost base based on a percentage split between original and new security, the Book Cost Perc field must be set to Y. The Book Cost field under the New Sec No multi-value filed is used to enter the percentage of cost to be apportioned to the new security. The remaining percentage is used to update the cost of the original security.

Consider that the cost apportioned to the new security is 85.71% of the original cost before demerger and the remaining 14.29% to the original security. The DIARY is updated as shown in the below screenshot.

At the time of ENTITLEMENT authorisation, 85.71% of the total cost is apportioned to the new security and 14.29% of the total cost is apportioned to the original security.

Consider that the customer holds 1000 shares before demerger at a cost of 10,000. Based on the ratio, the customer is expected to receive 200 shares in the new security.

In this example, Book Cost Perc is set to Y and Book Cost is 85.71%. The system assigns the cost of new security position as 8571 and the remaining cost 1429 is assigned to the original security.

The dividend with choice (stock or cash) is a Corporate Action (CA) event, which allows the shareholder to receive the d...*

> **Applications:** `COUPON.TAX.CODE`, `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `SC.CA.ERROR.LOG`, `SC.CA.PARAMETER`, `SC.ENT.AUTHORISE`, `SC.PRE.DIARY` ... +1 more
>

>

> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A dividend is a distribution of a portion of a company's earnings. While dividends are mandatory, some events offer a choice to receive the dividend in the form of shares or cash. The dividend with choice (stock or cash) is a Corporate Action (CA) event, which allows the shareholder to receive the dividend either in the form of new shares (same issue) or cash.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

A record in DIARY.TYPE for the Dividend option is set up as shown in the following screenshot.


##### Handling Events with Unknown Attributes

The system can create a pre-diary and diary even if critical attributes such as Stock ratio are missing in the initial event notification. The Allow Ukwn Fields field in DIARY.TYPE must be set as ‘Ratio’ if the bank expects the DIARY creation and customer election with the missing stock dividend ratio for SECU option.

If the ratio is known after authorising one of the other options, set the Auth Per Option field as ‘YES’ to allow rework of stock nominal in entitlement.


#### 🔧 Working With

Consider the following Corporate Action (CA) event where the shareholders have the right to either:

- Receive new shares at a rate of 1 new share for each 12 shares
- Receive a cash dividend of USD 5 per share

The following screenshot shows a DIARY record created for the event. The shareholders are entitled to choose either Stock or Cash or both the options. For the cash option, the source tax and local tax are calculated based on the Entitlement Amount in ENTITLEMENT application. However, there are cases where tax needs to be calculated for customers who choose the stock option. To cater to this need, the Tax Price field is used to ascertain the cash value of a stock dividend for tax purpose. However, accounting entries are not raised for taxes under the Stock option.

In events with options such as stock or cash, due to the terms of the offer, there may be unused holdings.

Consider the shareholder elects to take option 1 and the trading units of the stock is 1. For 1,000 nominals, the shareholder receives 83 nominals free of charge; however, the user cannot receive an extra share for the remaining 4 shares nor receive cash as the shareholder has elected option 1.

If the Cash Remain field is set to Yes in DIARY.TYPE , then the system automatically assigns any unused entitlement nominal to the cash option. Else, the user manually needs to allocate 996 nominals to option 1 and 4 nominals to option 2 to avail the cash option for the unused nominal. Thus, in either case, the user receives 83 additional shares free of charge for 996 nominals and, at the same time, receives a small cash dividend of USD 20 for the remaining 4 shares.

Stock Option

- Shares received =1000 / 12 = 83
- Option Nominal =83*12 = 996

Cash Option

- Option Nominal = 1000 – 996 = 4
- Entitlement Amount = 4*5 = USD 20

In case when Trading Units is set to 0.01 in SECURITY.MASTER and Cash Remain is set to No in DIARY.TYPE , then the system updates the shares received as 83.33, and in case if Cash Remain is set to Yes, the system additionally updates the amount as 0.20 for the remaining .04 nominals (83.33*12 = 999.96).

When the first option is entered and authorised, the ENTITLEMENT is examined. In the record in ENTITLEMENT , the user can view the 83 new shares in the Nominal field.

The Net Amount field displays the cash to be received amounting to USD 14 (that is, gross entitlement amount of USD 20 minus the source tax amount of USD 2 and local tax amount of USD 4).

The following accounting entries are generated when the record in ENTITLEMENT is authorised. For the cash option, since the Source Tax Split and Local Tax Split fields in COUPON.TAX.CODE are set to Yes, the customer is credited with a gross cash amount of USD 20. A debit entry for the source and local tax calculated for the respective cash option is shown from the customer account. However, accounting entries are not generated for the stock option.

The following screenshot confirms that the position has increased from 1,000 of the security to the current position of 1,083 after adding the 83 new shares received.


##### Processing Dividend with Choice with Unknown Attributes in Initial Announcement

For optional corporate action events offering both cash and security options, companies might provide the event details related to the cash option separately from the information on the security option. For example, it is common for the cash rate to be informed but not the stock ratio. The stock ratio could be received later, sometimes only when the confirmation MT566 is received. However, banks may want to process the event even though a critical attribute is unknown. When the event is configured to handle unknown attributes and the bank receives CA notifications with some attribute values marked as ‘UNWN’, the system creates SC.PRE.DIARY and DIARY , mapping the field values as ‘UKWN’.

| CA Attribute | MT564 Tag | Possible Values in SWIFT | Field in SC.PRE.DIARY to DIARY |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ratio | 92K | ADEX//UKWN or NEWO//UKWN | Old Ratio and New Ratio in NEW.SEC.NO multi-value set |
| Date | 98B | PAYD//UKWN or PAYD//ONGO | Opt Pay Date in OPTION.DESC multi-value |

| CA attribute | MT566 Tag | Sample Values | DIARY field |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ratio | 92D under the SECMOVE block of CACONF for the SECU option | 92D::NEWO//1,/123,5532 or 92D::ADEX//1,/123,5532 | The Old Ratio and New Ratio fields in NEW.SEC.NO multi-value set For the given sample value, the update is, OLD.RATIO = 123.5532 NEW.RATIO = 1 |
| Date | 98B of SECMOVE block of CACONF for the SECU option | 98A::PAYD// 98A::POST// 98A::EARL// | Opt Pay Date in OPTION.DESC multi-value set. When the 566 is received with the PAYD, POST or EARL qualifiers, the Opt Pay Date field is updated in the below order. EARL – Earliest Pay Date PAYD – Pay Date POST – Posting Date |

The user can create and authorise a DIARY even without the mandatory details of the SECU option such as Ratio, when the Allow Ukwn Fields field in DIARY.TYPE is set as ‘Ratio’. The values of the Old Ratio and New Ratio fields under the New Sec No multivalue set of the SECU option must be set as ‘UKWN’.

The system allows the customer election to be updated in ENTITLEMENT across different options, even though the quantity of security to be received is blank.

The user can authorise the CASH option entitlements individually or through bulk authorisation using the SC.ENT.AUTHORISE application, by providing the option number of the CASH option in the Option field.

The user can update the stock details such as Ratio in DIARY and the system updates the stock details into the ENTITLEMENT record through the XXX/SC.CORPORATE.ACTION service.

The user can authorise the SECU option entitlements individually by setting the Reval Ent field in ENTITLEMENT as ‘YES’, or through bulk authorisation when all the required details of the SECU option are available. The system raises an error when the ratio, price, or pay date is missing in the SECU option.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system does not allow authorisation of the SECU option if ratio is not known.

| Field | SC.PRE.DIARY or DIARY Field | MT564 Tag | Value of MT564 tag in outward message |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ratio | OLD.RATIO and NEW.RATIO in NEW.SEC.NO multi-value set | 92K | ADEX//UKWN |

### 6.16  DRIPs DelayedReceiptOfPrice


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A dividend reinvestment program or dividend reinvestment plan (DRIP) is an equity investment option offered directly from the underlying company. Based on regulatory requirements, the dividend reinvestment can be handled using the below options:*
> 
> **Applications:** `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `SC.CA.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Cash Remain*, *Cust Or Bank*, *Drips*, *New Price*, *Nominal*, *Pl Category*, *Rate*, *Rate Type* ... +3 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A dividend reinvestment program or dividend reinvestment plan (DRIP) is an equity investment option offered directly from the underlying company. Based on regulatory requirements, the dividend reinvestment can be handled using the below options:

- Reinvestment parameter – See Reinvestment via Order The cash value of the dividend is credited to the customer’s account and immediately an order or trade is created to invest the funds in the security at the reinvestment price.
- Direct reinvestment – See Reinvestment Feature Cash is not credited to the investor but reinvested nominal is directly credited to the customer.
- DRIPS fields and cash remain functionality Nominal in multiples of trading units is directly credited to the customer and balance for fractional quantity is paid in cash (if any). Allows update of reinvestment price after authorising the DIARY record.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following configuration helps the user to process the Dividend Reinvestment Plan through Direct credit of Stock or Cash credit followed by stock.


##### Direct Credit of Stock

The cash dividend received from the custodian through MT566 is credited only for customers who have selected the ‘Cash’ option. The cash dividend amount equivalent to stock is credited to an internal wash account for customers who have selected the ‘Reinvest’ option.

Subsequently, when stock is received through MT566 for stock option, for those who have chosen reinvestment, the system debits the cash from the Internal account and credits the stock directly to the customers. The below table lists the configurations required in DIARY.TYPE for direct credit of stocks.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Drips | The dividend re-investments are enabled when this field is set as ‘Yes’. Cash proceeds of the stock option are parked in the suspense account until the price of the new stock is declared. |
| Cust Or Bank | If the Cash Remain field is set as Yes, then a value must be entered in the Cust Or Bank field. The options available are either Customer (default value) or Bank. It controls whether the remaining cash, if any, is to be credited to the customer or the bank. |
| Pl Category | When Cust Or Bank field is set as ‘Customer’, the Pl Category field is a no input field. However, if Cust Or Bank field is set to ‘Bank’, then the Pl Category field becomes mandatory and accepts any valid Pl Category already setup in Temenos Transact. |


##### Cash Credit followed by Stock

The cash dividend received from the custodian though MT566 is credited fully to all customers, immaterial of the option selected.

Subsequently when stock is received through MT566 for stock option, for those who have chosen reinvestment, the system debits the cash from the customers’ accounts and credits the stock to the customers.

Configuring DIARY.TYPE for Full cash credit followed by stock

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Drips | When this field is set to ‘Cash. Reinvest’, the cash proceeds of both CASH and SECU options are credited to the Customer Account on the pay date of the CASH option. |


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the working of DRIPs with delayed receipt of price.


##### Direct Credit of Stocks

Temenos Transact allows the user to specify whether the remaining cash (if any) is to be paid or not. This is done at DIARY.TYPE level, using the Cash Remain field. When this field is set to Yes, the customer is credited with the remaining fractional cash. This application allows the user to specify whether any remaining cash must be credited to the customer or PL account of the bank. The suspense account that is used for reinvestments can also be recorded.

Where DIARY.TYPE has the Drips field setup, the DIARY application allows the New Price field to store the re-investment price (to be entered after a DIARY record is authorised). To record the re-investment price for a specific DIARY event, once it is announced by the agent or depository, the record can be re-opened to include the value in the New Price field.

When the Drips field is set as Yes, the entries before entering the price is posted to the internal suspense account ( Reinvest Susp field). The remaining cash is credited to the customer based on the value in Cust Or Bank field. Alternatively, if bank is specified, then a Pl category must be specified to credit the remaining cash after re-investment.

A position of 100000 is created.

A Corporate Action (CA) for the above event is entered. When Drips field is set as Yes, input of the re-investment price for the stock option need not be furnished at this instant.

The corresponding record in ENTITLEMENT is shown below.

The security position is not updated after authorising the ENTITLEMENT as the re-investment price is yet to be furnished.

Since, an option of 60,000 is mentioned for the cash and the balance is re-investment and the entries are raised as shown below. The cash amount of 60,000 minus the charges is credited to the customer account.

The price is entered in the DIARY application.

When the service agent is initiated, the ENTITLEMENT record is updated.

The option nominal of 60000 at a price of 41 gives 1250 nominals and the remaining entitlement amount of 8750.

60000/41 = 1463, where the rounding down of the trading units of 250 gives 1250. Now, the remaining cash is calculated as:

60000 – (1250 * 41) = 8750.


##### Cash Credit followed by Stock

In the Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRIP) of corporate action, the eligible clients can elect CASH, SECU, or partially in both options. The stock price is not available during the initial announcement of the event. As a common market standard,

- The custodian sends the full cash amount of the total eligible holdings in MT566 for CASH option.
- The system processes CASH 566 and credits the cash to all eligible clients by authorising all the entitlements once. Later, when MT566 for SECU option is received with the stock ratio or price details, the system updates the details in DIARY .
- The system updates the price or ratio in stock entitlements through the execution of the XXX/SC.CORPORATE.ACTIONS service and calculates the resultant stock in each entitlement.

Based on the number of authorisations configured for the ENTITLEMENT version in SC.CA.PARAMETER , the system authorises the entitlement records or leaves them in unauthorised status for further user action.

The below diagram illustrates the workflow for DRIPS – Cash Credit followed by stock.

| Portfolio | Qualify Holdings |
|---|---|
| 100990-1 | 6000 |
| 100996-1 | 10000 |
| 100997-1 | 12500 |

| CA attribute | MT566 Tag | Sample Values | DIARY field |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ratio | 92D under the SECMOVE block of CACONF for the SECU option | 92D::ADEX//1,/123,5532 or 92D::NEWO//1,/123,5532 | OLD.RATIO and NEW.RATIO in NEW.SEC.NO multi-value set of the SECU option. For the sample value, the update would be, OLD.RATIO = 123.5532 NEW.RATIO = 1 |
| Price | 90B of CASHMOVE block of CACONF for the SECU option | 90B:PRPP//ACTU/USD25,3987 | NEW.PRICE of NEW.SEC.NO of the SECU option. |

When processing the DRIPs – Full cash credit followed by stock and when the event currency is different from the customer’s account currency, the FX rates at the time of authorising the CASH 566 could be different from the FX rates at the time of receiving the Stock 566. To handle this, the system works as shown below.

Consider the EVENT.CCY = GBP; Customer Account Currency = USD

When 566 for CASH is received, the system applies the FX rate between the event currency and the customer account currency of the entitlement for crediting the entire dividend amount to the customer account.

When 566 for STOCK is received, the system updates the FX rate applicable currently and uses the same for debiting the customer account for the cash proceeds of stock-elected nominals.

### 6.17  Enhanced Scrip Dividend


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *An enhanced scrip issue (cash, stock and/or sell stock) is very similar to a basic scrip dividend. The one exception is that, in the case of enhanced scrip the holder has a choice of three different options as:*
> 
> **Applications:** `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `SC.TRADING.POSITION`, `SECURITY.TRANS`, `STMT.ENTRY`
> 
> **Prerequisites:** `DIARY`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.POSITION`, `CUSTOMER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount Fcy*, *Consol Trading Bal*, *Cur Cost Position*, *Current Position*, *Reval Unreal Pl*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

An enhanced scrip issue (cash, stock and/or sell stock) is very similar to a basic scrip dividend. The one exception is that, in the case of enhanced scrip the holder has a choice of three different options as:

- Take cash at given rate
- Take stock at given ratio
- Take sale proceeds of stock (stock entitled is worked out based on the given ratio)

Partial elections are permitted.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

A DIARY.TYPE record with the below setup is created in Temenos Transact to enable the processing of enhance scrip Corporate Action (CA).


#### 🔧 Working With

The below screenshots show how a typical enhanced scrip dividend may be requested. In this case, the DIARY application explains that the following options are available to each holder:

1. Basic cash dividend at 0.151p per share held
2. Scrip dividend equivalent to a cash dividend of 0.2265p per share
3. Scrip dividend with cash offer equivalent to a cash dividend of 0.22197p per share

Now, the user must authorise the above record and process it through the service agent to obtain the ENTITLEMENT that provides the expected details of each option.

The above ENTITLEMENT offers the following options for user election:

1. Cash dividend of 2,265.00 (15,000 x 0.151p per share)
2. Receive 619 new shares (15,000/24.22611p)
3. Receive cash of 3,187.85 ( 619 x 515p)

Partial elections are permitted and as the basic cash dividends are processed correctly, the focus is on the first and second options. The below screenshot shows the various elections requested.

The user started by entering 8,000 in second option. Temenos Transact application reduced this to 7,995 which was the highest number of shares that can be utilised at a 24.22611 ratio, thus producing 330 new shares. Then, the user enters the balance 7,005 (15,000 – 7,995) into the third option. Temenos Transact updates this to 7,002 which is the highest usable number of shares for this option. Therefore, the balance of three shares is entitled for cash dividend only, as shown in first option.

Now, the user must authorise the ENTITLEMENT and check if the positions are updated correctly for the receipt of the new shares in second option. The below screenshot shows the original holding of 15,000 which has been increased by the 330 new shares received as part of the scrip election.

All the cost fields remain unchanged, which is correct. In reference to the SC.TRADING.POSITION application, the Current Position field is updated with the holding of 15,330 (comprising the original position with the addition of the 330 new shares received under the scrip option).

> **⚠️ Note:** It is assumed the shares that were processed under the SCRIP and SELL option has washed over the position without impacting upon the original cost. This can be checked by ensuring that there are two SECURITY.TRANS records, one for the receipt of the new shares and another for the sale thereof.

The screenshots confirms that a SECURITY.TRANS record was built for both the receipt and sale of the scrip and sell portion.

Now, the user can check the cash accounting to ensure the correctness.

The STMT.ENTRY posted to the suspense clearance account indicates that an amount of GBP 1,488.80 is expected. This can be verified by working out the component parts of the various entitlements associated with the DIARY application. Option 2 is related to the receipt of shares only and therefore cash is not associated with this option.

Option 3 is related to 7,002 eligible shares to create new shares at a rate of 24,22611 old to one new. On this basis, 7,002 / 24.22611 produces 289 new shares. These are sold immediately at 5.15 each, therefore 289 x 5.15 = GBP 1,488.35. Option 1 related to the three shares is remaining after options 2 and 3. The cash dividend is 15.10p, therefore 3 x 0.151 = GBP 0.45. Add GBP 1,488.35 and GBP 0.45 to get the total of GBP 1,488.80 as shown in the Amount Fcy field in the STMT.ENTRY record.

Once the integrity of the accounting associated with the CA under review is established, it is necessary to run a COB to perform the Central Reporting Files (CRF) updates. In this case, as the new security received was 330 new shares, the change to the carrying value is handled by the revaluation process. Now, back-up the account and run the COB.

The revaluation process has posted GBP 62,499 profit for the position. In this case, the cost of the original 15,000 shares amounted to GBP 18,750. The current market price of the security is GBP 5.30, therefore 15,330 x 5.30 = GBP 81,249 less cost GBP 18,750 = GBP 62,499.00. This is also updated in the SC.TRADING.POSITION application relating to the portfolio or security combination, so this must be checked.

The Cur Cost Position and the Consol Trading Bal fields indicates the original cost of the position. The Reval Unreal Pl field reports the revaluation profit of GBP 62,499 as described above.

### 6.18  Equalisation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This topic enables the user to understand income distribution under equalisation.*
> 
> **Applications:** `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `SC.TRANS.NAME`, `SC.TRANS.TYPE`, `SEC.ACC.MASTER`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.SUPP` ... +3 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Entitlement Amount*, *Equalisation*, *Equalisation Acc*, *Equalisation Code*, *Equalisation Date*, *Equalise Amt*, *Equalise Ex Rate*, *Equalise Hlding* ... +18 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This topic enables the user to understand income distribution under equalisation.


##### Unit Trusts - Equalisation of Distribution

Unit trusts distribute income in the form of a distribution (as opposed to a dividend or other income received). One of the features of unit trusts distribution is equalisation.

The price of a unit is calculated by including the income received and receivable income at that particular time. A user who purchases units is entitled to their share of income received after the date of purchase. A part of the price paid for the units is in respect of income received before the money was introduced to the trust.

The user receives the same income as all other holders on the first distribution date. A part of this is taxed income and represents income received after the date of purchase. A part of this is untaxed and is in effect a return of the part of purchase price (that part which represents income receivable up to the date of purchase). The sum of all income is termed as equalisation.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

A dividend type record with EQUALISATION is setup in the DIARY.TYPE application as shown below:

For an equalisation type dividend, the New Securities , Options , Rights and Free Securities fields are set to No and the Retain Original field is set to Y. The below fields are taken into account, to advise the system that a particular corporate action is of equalisation type:

- The Equalisation field is set to Yes.
- In the Equalisation Code field, the user enters the SC.TRANS.TYPE denoting this activity.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user should setup appropriate SC.TRANS.TYPE and SC.TRANS.NAME records for processing the corporate activity type.


#### 🔧 Working With

Temenos Transact includes the processing of equalisation. A DIARY.TYPE is used to define an equalisation corporate action. Additionally, the two other fields are used for validation which allows the user to enter three new rates in the DIARY record:

- Rate 1 - Group 1 unit rate (using the Rate field)
- Rate 2 - Group 2 unit rate (using the Group 2 Rate field)
- Rate 3 - Equalisation rate (using the Equalise Rate field)

These rates are then entered in the ENTITLEMENT records generated by the DIARY . The system calculates the holding at the start of the equalisation period (date of last unit trust distribution) and the holding on ex-date. The equalisation processing starts only if the holding on the ex-date is greater than the holding at the beginning of the equalisation period.

In this case, the difference is used for equalisation processing. This difference is known as the equalisation nominal (the rate for holding at the start of the equalisation period is treated solely as income).

The Group Rate field is used to calculate a reduced rate for the equalisation nominal. This amount is treated as income and posted to the same account as the income from the Group 1 Rate. The equalisation rate is used to calculate the amount of returned capital on the equalisation nominal and it is posted separately. The returned capital and income can be posted to separate accounts, if required.

The equalisation processing cannot be performed on a re-invested dividend. Further, the equalisation processing cannot be used on a corporate action, where the user has a choice of options. The equalisation amount received by the portfolio is used to reduce the book cost of the security position. A zero nominal SECURITY.TRANS record is generated specifically for this purpose.


##### Calculating Equalisation

Temenos Transact follows three methods for calculating the equalisation nominal namely:

- FIFO
- LIFO
- SUMLIFO

The value in this Grp1 Grp 2 Method field in SUB.ASSET.TYPE is defaulted in the Sub Asset Type field of the SECURITY.MASTER record during entry. The Grp1 Grp2 Method field in SECURITY.MASTER defaults the value from the SUB.ASSET.TYPE , but the user can manually override the value. The options in this field are Fifo, Lifo and Sumlifo and Default. The Default value copies the record from the SUB.ASSET.TYPE record.

The system calculates Group 1 holdings at the start of the equalisation period (date of last unit trust distribution). Any purchases from this date to the end of the equalisation period (ex-date) is classified as Group 2 holdings. This field dictates which Group sales need to be deducted from (during the equalisation period).

| Event | Transactions | Group 1 Units | Group 2 Units | Total Units |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Last Distribution |  | 10,000 | 0 | 10,000 |
| Sale | -2,000 | 8,000 | 0 | 8,000 |
| Purchase | 5,000 | 8,000 | 5,000 | 13,000 |
| Sale | -1,500 | 6,500 | 5,000 | 11,500 |
| Total | 6,500 | 5,000 | 11,500 |  |

| Event | Transactions | Group 1 Units | Group 2 Units | Total Units |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Last Distribution |  | 10,000 | 0 | 10,000 |
| Purchase | 5,000 | 10,000 | 5,000 | 15,000 |
| Sale | -2,000 | 8,000 | 5,000 | 13,000 |
| Sale | -1,500 | 6,500 | 5,000 | 11,500 |
| Total | 6,500 | 5,000 | 11,500 |  |

The ENTITLEMENT application calculates the Group 1, Group 2 and equalisation amounts using the information available in the DIARY and SECURITY.SUPP applications. The DIARY application specifies the distributed Group 1 dividend rate, the reduced Group 2 rate and the equalisation rate to be applied.

The Group 1 position comprises the position held as on the previous dividend date. Therefore, the system requires the previous dividend date which splits the current ex-dividend position into the position, as at the previous ex-dividend date and those purchased since that date. The dividend history is maintained within the SECURITY.SUPP application, but if history should not exist, the user is prompted to provide the previous date in DIARY transaction. The following fields are set in the DIARY application for equalisation.

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Rate | Records the G1 dividend rate |
| Group Rate | The G2 rate representing the income |
| Equalise Rate | The equalisation rate representing the capital portion |
| Equalisation Date | The previous ex-dividend date |

Once the DIARY is committed and assuming that a TSA.SERVICE is requested for on-line processing, the user can immediately examine the underlying entitlements that are built. The ENTITLEMENT record involving an equalisation type dividend is shown below:

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Qualifying Holdings | Records the position held as on the previous dividend date, therefore qualifying for the normal G1 dividend, which is reported in the Entitlement Amount field |
| Equalise Hlding | Displays the total purchases since the previous date, on which the G2 and equalisation dividends are to be paid |
| Group2 Amt | Displays the amount of G2 income dividend |
| Equalise Amt | Displays the amount of equalisation dividend (capital) to be received |

The equalisation amount is treated as the capital and this facility enables the user to post it to a separate capital account (if one exist, belonging to the underlying customer). This is done within the customers’ SEC.ACC.MASTER portfolio accounts, where various defaults are setup using the SC.TRANS.NAME , which specifies the accounts to which various security activities are to be posted. However, if necessary the user can enter a different account, which is defaulted in the Equalisation Acc field.

### 6.19  Golden Source


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Various market providers can provide information regarding a Corporate Action (CA) in addition to custodians. The list of providers from whom the bank receives CA notifications is configured in the system.*
> 
> **Applications:** `CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `Pre Diary`, `SC.CA.MKT.PROVIDER`, `SC.CA.MKT.PROVIDR`, `SC.CA.PARAMETER`, `SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION`, `SC.PRE.DIARY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Criteria Date*, *Event Type*, *Ex Date*, *Gen Ca Advice*, *Gen MT564*, *Golden Source*, *Golden Source Master*, *Golden Source Ref* ... +10 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Various market providers can provide information regarding a Corporate Action (CA) in addition to custodians. The list of providers from whom the bank receives CA notifications is configured in the system.

The bank arrives at the Golden Source information by reconciling the notifications received from the providers and custodians. The bank can notify their customers (including institutional clients) about the event from the golden source.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Following are the configurations required to capture and process CA notifications from various providers, and to arrive at the golden source.


##### Handling Notifications from Non-custodian

The Non Depo Msg field in the DIARY.TYPE table for the corporate action is set to Yes to process the notifications from non-custodians.


##### Configuring Data Providers of CA Notifications

The user must configure the data providers of corporate actions notifications in the SC.CA.MKT.PROVIDER table.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user must define the Custodian BIC if the custodian information is required to be used to arrive at the golden source.


##### Configuring Golden Source Reconciliation of Various Notifications

To reconcile the corporate action notification from multiple providers and to arrive at the golden source of information, the user must set the Golden Source field to Yes in the SC.CA.PARAMETER table. When it is set to Yes, the bank can define the master provider in the Golden Source Master field from the list of providers defined in the SC.CA.MKT.PROVIDR table.


##### Configuring Tolerance Days for Duplicate Checking

When a corporate action notification is received from various market providers and custodians, the system checks if the notification is for the same event, where the SC.PRE.DIARY table is already available in the system. This is required to group and consider these records for golden source reconciliation.

The system checks the following for duplicates:

- The values of Ex Date and Pay Date field in the SC.PRE.DIARY table.
- The ISIN and SWIFT qualifier of the incoming MT564.

However, the SC.PRE.DIARY table created from non-custodian notifications may not have an ex-date or the ex-date may be tentative. So, while checking for duplicates, the ex-date (or pay date) can be checked within a range of dates.

This range is specified in the SC.CA.PARAMETER table with the record ID as SYSTEM. The Criteria Date field is a multi-value drop-down field that holds the values of ex-date and pay date.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic explains the processing of CA notifications for an event from various data sources and how the bank arrives at the Golden Source of information.

> **⚠️ Note:** To arrive at the Golden Source of information,, ensure that the set up for Golden Source reconciliation exists as explained in the Configuring Golden Source Corporate Action Notifications section.


##### Processing First Notification for an Event

Processing of the first notification involves the following steps:

When the system receives an incoming MT564, it checks whether the sender is a custodian (that is, the sender BIC is the BIC address of a depository as defined in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY table).

If the sender is a non-custodian, the system checks whether the sender’s BIC is available in the SC.CA.MKT.PROVIDER table. If so, the system identifies the sender as a non-custodian and treats the message as a non-custodian message.

If the sender is a non-custodian and the CA Data Provider configuration does not exist for this sender, then the system does not process the notification.

When the system receives an incoming MT564, and if the sender is a non-custodian, then the system creates a record in the SC.PRE.DIARY table with source set as ‘Non-custodian’ and maps the Provider ID along with other event details. As being the first notification for an event, the system also creates a Golden Source Pre-diary record, which is a copy of the pre-diary from the non-custodian. The system establishes the link between the pre-diaries by updating the Golden Source Ref field with the id of the Golden Source Pre-diary record. As this is a message from a non-custodian, the system does not create a DIARY record.

> **⚠️ Note:** A Single Golden Source Pre-diary is created for an event.

When the Golden Source Pre-diary record is created, the value of the System Master field is the pre-diary ID, which is used as the source of creation of this Golden Source Pre-diary record.

If the sender is a custodian and the sender BIC is configured in the SC.CA.MKT.PROVIDER table, then the system creates the SC.PRE.DIARY table for the custodian and the Golden Source Pre-diary record. The system also establishes the link between the pre-diaries by updating the Golden Source Ref field in the Pre Diary table.

In case, the BIC of the custodian is not configured in the SC.CA.MKT.PROVIDER table, this custodian message is not considered for Golden Source reconciliation and the system does not create the additional Golden Source Pre-diary record.

The regular process of creating DIARY and other corporate actions workflow are processed as usual for the custodian message.


##### Processing Subsequent Notifications

Processing of subsequent notifications involves the following steps:

When a subsequent MT564 is received for the same event from a different provider, the system performs the duplicate check using the following pre-diary attributes.

- ISIN
- Event type
- Ex Date and Pay Date

> **⚠️ Note:** The system performs the duplicate check for the Ex Date and Pay Date within the range based on the values in the Criteria Date and Tolerance Days fields in SC.CA.PARAMETER .

When a new message (NEWM) is received from a different data provider for the same event and the system identifies the Golden Source Ref field for this event using duplicate check, it creates a SC.PRE.DIARY table for this provider and updates the Golden Source Ref field into it.

If the sender of this message is configured as the Golden Source Master in the SC.CA.PARAMETER table, then the system automatically updates the System Master field of the Golden Source Pre-diary record and updates the content of Golden Source Pre-diary record with this message content.

When the 564-replacement message (REPL) is received for the event by any of the configured providers, the system checks if the provider is a master provider by checking the Golden Source Pre-diary record. If so, the system updates the content of the REPL message into the actual pre-diary and the Golden Source Pre-diary record, else it just updates the actual pre-diary of this provider and leaves it for further reconciliation.


##### Reconciliation of Notifications

The main objective of this corporate action Golden Source is to reconcile the SC.PRE.DIARY table created from various data providers and arrive at the Golden Source of information for the event. Transact supports this by using an enquiry that pulls data from the SC.PRE.DIARY table for the given event with the specific Golden Source Ref , where the Golden Source pre-diary is pending for reconciliation (Golden Source Status of Golden Source Pre-diary is not marked as Complete).

The enquiry displays the Master pre-diary of the event as the first row which enables the user to compare the other pre-diary records created from various other providers. If there is a difference in data, between the Master and other record, the system displays it in RED enabling easy reconciliation.

Similarly, when Option Number between two notifications is different, the same is also highlighted. When creating a record in SC.PRE.DIARY from incoming MT564, the system concatenates the Option Indicator and Option Number and updates the concatenated value in the Option Desc field.

The enquiry compares the Option Desc and highlights the change in the sequence of Option Number , as shown below.

This enquiry can be used by the bank to communicate with any custodian if their data varies with that of the Master and wait for further update from the custodian.

Also, the bank can amend the Golden Source Pre-diary record manually using the data provided in the enquiry.


##### Notifying Clients

The system generates any notification to institutional clients or any pre-notification to clients from the Golden Source Pre-diary record. The system creates the records in the SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION table for the Golden Source Pre-diary record to identify the entitled customers. The MT564 message (and pre advice) is triggered to the entitled customers to inform them about the CA notification of the corporate action event.

> **⚠️ Note:** The MT564 and pre-advice are sent to the customers, where the Gen Ca Advice field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY table is set to Yes.

The user can enable the system to send notification to clients by setting the Gen MT564 field to STP in the DIARY.TYPE table. The user can also send the notification manually from Golden Source by setting the Golden Source Status field to 'Notify Clients' and the Gen MT564 field to Yes.


##### Amending Golden Source Pre-diary Manually

Amending Golden Source pre-dairy manually involves the following steps:

When it is not possible to create and update the notification from data providers through MT564, the user can manually create the SC.PRE.DIARY table for the provider. The user can also amend the related Golden Source Pre-diary record manually by setting the Golden Source Status field to 'Update Golden Source'.

Once the Golden Source Pre-diary record is manually amended, no further STP-based update to the Golden Source Pre-diary record is possible.

Transact supports configuring the Master for Golden Source reconciliation at the event level as well. The event-level master supersedes the configuration done in the SC.CA.PARAMETER table. By setting the Golden Source Status field as Update Master, the bank user can update the Manual Master field with the pre-diary ID other than the one already defined as ‘System Master’.

Once the Manual Master field is updated, any REPL message from this Manual Master is considered to update the Golden Source Pre diary, ignoring the Master defined in the SC.CA.PARAMETER table.

Once the bank completes reconciliation of the given event, its related Golden Source Status field should be marked as ‘Complete’ in the Golden Source Pre diary.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Golden Source Corporate Action Notifications feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

The user can view the below list of enquiries and reports pertaining to Golden Source Corporate Action Notifications feature.


##### Enquiries and Reports

This section allows the user to view the below list of enquiries and reports.

Golden Source Recon

The enquiry displays the list of Golden source pre-diaries for the given Event Type and Security No . The Golden source pre-diaries where reconciliation is pending are displayed in this output. Further drilldown is available to compare and the event details can be reconciled.


##### SWIFT Messages

##### Advices

NA

In this case, the entitlements are not based on ex/record dated position, but are based on certain conditions given in the event. Examples of linkages based on electi...*

>

#### 📖 Introduction

The concept of linked diary is to derive the attributes of event based on the actions of customers from another event (linked event). In this case, the entitlements are not based on ex/record dated position, but are based on certain conditions given in the event. Examples of linkages based on election in parent event are given below:

- In a Demerger event, customers can elect to either retain or sell the new shares that they receive out of the event. The election to sell or retain is done in the parent event (Demerger). However, the sell is done as a linked event by linking the elections from the parent event.
- Exercise rights is to participate in a priority offer based on the election in the parent rights event.
- Linking parent takeover/tender event is to process additional cash to participants of a takeover event.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

In DIARY the below fields are used for linking the parent event.

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Link Diary Id | Indicates the DIARY ID of the parent event |
| Link Condition App 1 | Indicates the application based on which entitlements need to be generated for the linked event (Allowed values are CUSTOMER/ENTITLEMENT/SEC.ACC.MASTER) |
| Link Cond Field 1 | Indicates the field from which the application is linked using the Link Condition App. |
| Link Cond op 1 | Allows the input of EQ or NE |
| Link Cond Value 1 | Indicates the value based on which entitlement are generated |

| Fields in DIARY | Description or Value |
|---|---|
| Link Diary Id | DIARSC0821800077 (linked DIARY ID, that is, original rights) |
| Link Condition App 1 | Entitlement |
| Link Cond Field 1 | Option |
| Link Cond op 1 | EQ |
| Link Cond Value 1 | 1 (assuming this is the rights) |
| Link Impact 1 1 | SUBSCRIPTION CAP |
| Link Impact Value 1 1 | EXERCISE.ADDL |

### 6.21  Handling Market Claims


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The account servicer (custodian) sends as MT 566 message to an account owner to indicate that the securities and/or cash is either credited or debited to an account as the result of a corporate action event. Generally, the custodian sends the confirmation based on the settled quantity as on a specif...*
> 
> **Applications:** `C.CA.ERROR.LOG`, `CUSTOMER.SECURITY`, `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `ENTITEMENT`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `ENTITLEMENT.BROKER`, `SC.CA.ERROR.LOG` ... +3 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *566 Claim Date*, *Br Outs Nom*, *Broker Txn Id*, *Cash Mkt Claim*, *Cash To Settle*, *Claim Status*, *Claim Txn Id*, *Corp Ref* ... +24 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The account servicer (custodian) sends as MT 566 message to an account owner to indicate that the securities and/or cash is either credited or debited to an account as the result of a corporate action event. Generally, the custodian sends the confirmation based on the settled quantity as on a specific date, for example, record date. However, there are scenarios where the settlement fails, and the trade is settled after the intended settlement date (record date). In such cases, the following scenarios occur.

- Where the customer receives more than what he or she is entitled. That is, there are unsettled sale transactions.
- Where the customer receives less than what he or she is entitled. That is, there are unsettled purchase transactions.

In both the cases, the proceeds of the distribution to the contractually entitled party is done later through a process called market claim. For mandatory cash events, there are two ways of handling the market claim:

- Custodian retains funds for unsettled sale transactions and handles the market claims.
- Custodian does not retain funds for unsettled sale transactions and the Bank handles the market claims.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section provides the configuration required to enable market claim processing for mandatory cash events.


##### CUSTOMER.SECURITY

The Cash Mkt Claim field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the depository should be set to either:

- Custodian - When a custodian retains the funds on unsettled sale transactions and sends out the remaining amount in initial MT566 message. For the unsettled purchase transactions, the custodian collects the amount either from the counterparty or counterparty's custodian and handles market claims through subsequent MT566 message.
- Bank - When custodian does not retain funds on unsettled sale transactions and sends out the entire amount in initial MT566. For the unsettled purchase transactions, the bank later contacts either the counterparty or counterparty's custodian and handles the market claim.

The value is defaulted to Mkt Claim in SC.PRE.DIARY and DIARY application.


##### DIARY.TYPE

When the bank handles the market claim, the amount received for the unsettled sale transactions is credited to the Mkt Clm Categ defined in DIARY.TYPE as shown in the screenshot below.


##### SC.CA.PARAMETER

The 566 Claim Date field denotes the date to be mapped from the incoming MT566 market claim message. When market claims are handled by the custodian, the system raises entries for claim amount with value date based on this setup. The possible values of 566 Claim Date are:

- Value.date – The system records the :98A::VALU of the CASHMOVE block from the incoming MT566 message against the Proceeds Date field in SC.CA.ERROR.LOG .
- Posting.date – The system records the :98A::POST of the CASHMOVE block from the incoming MT566 message against the Proceeds Date field in SC.CA.ERROR.LOG .
- Null – The system does not record the date from the incoming MT566 message.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains how market claims are handled in Transact for mandatory cash events. The market claims can be handled either by Custodian or Bank. The below image demonstrates the system’s behaviour on receipt of MT564.

The below chart image the system’s behaviour on receipt of MT566.

> **⚠️ Note:** The below functionality does not work when Depository in DIARY is set to ALL.


##### Market Claims Handled by Custodian

When the custodian handles the market claim, the custodian retains the cash for unsettled sale transactions and sends out the remaining amount in initial MT566 message. The system reconciles confirmed balance and posting amount and authorises all the entitlements for that sub account. In case of mismatch the system will wait for another initial MT566.

Once the unsettled transactions are settled,

- For a sale transaction, either the counterparty or counterparty’s custodian contacts the bank’s custodian to receive the claim amount. There is no action at the bank’s end.
- For a purchase transaction, the bank’s custodian contacts either the counterparty or counterparty’s custodian to receive the claim amount. Once the claim amount is received, the custodian sends subsequent or delta MT566 to the bank with the transaction reference in RELA reference and tag 22F as ADDB//CLAI to indicate it as a Market claim. The system identifies the transaction based on Corp and Rela reference and post the cash credit if reconciled.

When custodian handles the market claim, the Mkt Claim field in DIARY should be set as Custodian. The system updates this field when:

- An incoming MT 564 is received along with the tag 22F in sequence D with qualifier ADDB and indicator as ACLA.
- Cash Mkt Claim in CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the depository is set as Custodian.
- Manually by the user.

The system raises an override if the value of Cash Mkt Claim in CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the depository and Mkt Claim in DIARY is different.

| Portfolio | Sub Account | Settled Quantity | Unsettled Quantity | Qualify Holdings | Depository Holdings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 12345 | 2000 | 1000 | 3000 | 2000-0 = 2000 |
| B | 456789 | 3000 | -2000 | 1000 | 3000-2000 =1000 |
| C | 12345 | 1000 | 0 | 1000 | 1000-0 =1000 |
| D | 12345 | 1500 | -200 | 1300 | 1500-200=1300 |
| Total |  | 7500 |  |  | 5300 |

| Portfolio | Debit CA suspense Account | Credit Portfolio account | Debit Customer Account | Credit Tax account | Debit Tax account | Credit P&L |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | USD 3600 | USD 3920 | USD 400 | USD 400 | USD 400 | USD 80 |
| C | USD 1800 | USD 1960 | USD 200 | USD 200 | USD 200 | USD 40 |
| D | USD 2340 | USD 2548 | USD260 | USD260 | USD260 | USD 52 |


##### Market Claims Handled by Bank

When the bank handles the market claim, the custodian does not retain the cash for unsettled sale transactions and sends out the entire amount in initial MT566 message. The system reconciles confirmed balance and posting amount and authorises all the entitlements for that sub account. The system automatically credits the customer to the extent of eligible amount (settled position -unsettled sale) and credits the proceeds received for unsettled sale transaction to a market claim suspense account. Once the unsettled transactions are settled,

- For a sale transaction, either the counterparty or counterparty’s custodian contacts the bank to receive the claim amount.
- For a purchase transaction, the bank contacts either the counterparty or counterparty’s custodian to receive the claim amount.

When bank handles the market claim, Mkt Claim in DIARY should be set as Bank. This field is updated,

- When Mkt Claim in CUSTOMER.SECURITY of the depository is set as Bank.
- Manually by the user.

| Portfolio | Sub Account | Settled Quantity | Unsettled Quantity | Qualify Holdings | Depository Holdings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 12345 | 2000 | 1000 | 3000 | 2000 |
| B | 456789 | 3000 | -2000 | 1000 | 3000 |
| C | 12345 | 1000 | 0 | 1000 | 1000 |
| D | 12345 | 1500 | -200 | 1300 | 1500 |
| Total |  | 7500 |  |  | 7500 |

MT566 is received only for the positions settled as on record date. The initial MT566 handling process is similar as explained under market claim handled by Custodian. Since the custodian is not handling the claim, the only difference is that the amount received includes the amount for unsettled sale transaction. The system then credits this amount received for unsettled sale transaction to the suspense account given in Mkt Clm Categ in DIARY.TYPE .

Assume an MT566 is received on as 20th May 2024 :20C::CORP//CASH001, :97A::SAFE//456789, :93B::CONB//UNIT/3000 and :19B::PSTA//USD6000. Since the quantity matches with the system calculated quantity for the sub account 456789 and the cash received is within tolerance, the system credits the dividend for portfolio B and raise the below entries. Assume source tax split is set.

The entries raised at Entitlement:

- Debit CA suspense Account 5400 USD [Entitlement amount (6000) -source tax amount (600)]
- Credit Client account 1940 USD [Entitlement amount (2000) -commissions (60)]
- Debit client account 200 USD (Source tax amount)
- Credit tax suspense 200 USD
- Debit tax suspense 200 USD
- Credit P&L 60 USD
- Credit market claim susp account 3600 USD

The entries raised at Diary:

- Debit Custodian Nostro 5400 USD
- Credit CA Suspense Account 5400 USD

For trades settled post the record date, the bank has to follow up with the counterparty or counterparty's custodian to receive the market claim for the portfolio. There is no STP process, and the bank has to manually mark the Claim Status as Complete or Closed.

Once the claim amount is received, the bank can credit the amount by posting an account transfer or through ENTITLEMENT . In case if the bank does not use the ENTITLEMENT to complete the market claim for unsettled transaction, then the user has to mark Claim Status under Broker Txn Id multi value set as Closed. This in turn updates Claim Status of the respective ENTITLEMENT.BROKER as Closed. In case if the bank wants to raise entries from the respective ENTITLEMENT record, then Claim Status is marked as Complete. The system raises the below entries by debiting the broker nostro account and crediting the customer if it’s a buy transaction or debit the market claim suspense account and credit the broker nostro if it is a sell transaction.

For parent child trades, if the claim amount is received for the parent trade, the user can authorise all the child trades through the SC.ENT.AUTHORISE application. The user can input the parent transaction ID in Claim Txn Id and Claim Status as Complete. This marks the Claim Status of the corresponding child transactions and raise entries.

The user can also use the SC.ENT.AUTHORISE application to mark the claim status as complete or closed for all the pending market claims. The user needs to input Diary Id , Depository and Claim Status with the required values and authorise the record.

The table below shows the uses cases involved in handling market claims for mandatory cash events:

| Cases | Market Claim Handled by Custodian | Market Claim Handled by Bank |
|---|---|---|
| Depository Holding Calculation | Settled positions minus unsettled sale transactions as on record date | Settled positions as on record date |
| Initial MT 566 from Custodian | Retains the cash amount for unsettled sale transactions and send the remaining amount. | Does not retain any cash and send the entire amount for the settled position as on record date. |
| Accounting Entries for Initial MT 566 | Debit the Custodian Nostro Account Credit the Customer Account Credit Tolerance Category (for tolerance amount) | Debit the Custodian Nostro Account Credit the Customer Account Credit Market claim suspense account for the unsettled sale transaction Credit Tolerance Category (for tolerance amount) |
| Unsettled Sale Transaction | Counterparty or counterparty'scustodian contacts the bank’s custodian for claim amount. No action on bank side | Counterparty or counterparty's custodian contacts the bank for claim amount. Bank should action by marking Claim Status in ENTITLEMENT as Closed or Complete. |
| Unsettled Purchase Transaction | Bank’s custodian contacts the counterparty or counterparty'scustodian for claim amount. Bank’s custodian sends delta Mt 566 for claim amount. No action on bank side provided there is no reconciliation failure. | Bank contacts the counterparty or counterparty's custodian for claim amount. Bank should action by marking Claim Status in ENTITLEMENT as Closed or Complete. |

> **⚠️ Note:** In case if record date is not available in DIARY record, the system updates the settled positions before ex-date.


#### 📋 Tasks

Market claims processing ensures the benefit of a distribution reaches the contractually entitled party. This happens when a transaction resulting from a trade with dividend is not settled by the record date of the distribution of the dividend. The seller of the securities is obliged to transfer the dividend to the buyer. There are two ways of handling the market claim:

- Custodian retains funds for unsettled sale transaction and handles the market claim.
- Custodian does not retain funds for unsettled sale transaction and bank handles the market claim.


##### Workflow

In Handling Market Claims for Mandatory Cash Events, the user can perform the below activity:

When market claims are handled by the bank, the custodian sends the dividend/coupon amount for the settled balance as on record date which includes the amount for any unsettled sale position. This enquiry displays the list of such unsettled sale transactions and the corresponding amount to be credited to the counterparty. Further drilldown is available to complete the settlement and market claim.

To view the market claims to be credited to the counterparty,

1. Pending Market Claims - To Pay .
2. In the Pending Market Claims - To Pay screen, enter values in the required field and the click the FIND button. The user can view the details of the claim amount to be given to the counterparty.
3. Click the Edit Settlement icon to settle the underlying transaction by giving Nominal To Settle and Cash To Settle of both client and broker.
4. Click the Validate a deal icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit the deal icon to submit the record.
6. Click the Edit Entitlement to mark Claim Status for the respective broker transaction as Complete in case if the user wishes to credit the counterparty or closed in case if the user has already settled the claim.
7. Click the Validate a deal icon to check for errors and overrides.
8. Click the Commit the deal icon to submit the record.

The enquiry displays the amount to be received from the custodian or counterparty due to unsettled credit transaction. The user can view the details of the claim amount to be received from either custodian or counterparty. Further drilldown is available to complete the settlement and market claim.

To view the market claims that are yet to be received,

1. Pending Market Claims - To Receive .
2. In the Pending Market Claims - To Receive screen, enter values in the required field and the click the FIND button. The user can view the details of the claim amount to be received along with the taxes and commissions to be charged.
3. When custodian is handling the market claim, the details of MT 566 received for the claim can be viewed by clicking the View Error Log icon.
4. Click the Edit Settlement icon to settle the underlying transaction by giving Nominal To Settle and Cash To Settle of both client and broker.
5. Click the Validate a deal icon to check for errors and overrides.
6. Click the Commit the deal icon to submit the record.
7. Click Edit Entitlement to mark Claim Status for the respective broker transaction as Complete in case if the user wishes to credit the counterparty or closed in case if the user has already settled the claim.
8. Click the Validate a deal icon to check for errors and overrides.
9. Click the Commit the deal icon to submit the record.

The enquiry displays the mismatch between the system calculated quantity and incoming MT 566 cumulative quantity for pending market claims. This enables the user to follow up with custodian for subsequent MT566 or to check if corrections are needed on the Bank side. Further drilldown is available to complete the settlement and market claim.

To view the market claims that are yet to be fully received,

1. Pending Claims - Quantity Mismatch .
2. In the Pending Claims - Quantity Mismatch screen, enter values in the required field and the click the FIND button. The user can view the details of the claim amount and the corresponding quantity received so far from the custodian.
3. Click the Edit Settlement icon to settle the underlying transaction by giving Nominal To Settle and Cash To Settle of both client and broker.
4. Click the Validate a deal icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit the deal icon to submit the record.
6. Click Edit Entitlement to mark Claim Status for the respective broker transaction as Complete in case if the user wishes to credit the counterparty or closed in case if the user has already settled the claim.
7. Click the Validate a deal icon to check for errors and overrides.
8. Click the Commit the deal icon to submit the record.

The enquiry displays the pending claims to be credited to the customer due to underlying transaction not settled in the system. This is when the custodian handles the market claim and MT 566 message is received for the outstanding quantity, but the underlying transaction is not settled. Further drilldown is available to complete the settlement and market claim.

To view the pending claims for a fully received claim amount,

1. Pending Claims - 566 Received Claim Pending .
2. In the Pending Claims - 566 Received Claim Pending, enter values in the required field and the click the FIND button. The user can view the details of the claim amount received from the custodian.
3. Click the Edit Settlement icon to settle the underlying transaction by giving Nominal To Settle and Cash To Settle of both client and broker.
4. Click the Validate a deal icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit the deal icon to submit the record.
6. Click Edit Entitlement to mark Claim Status for the respective broker transaction as Complete in case if the user wishes to credit the counterparty or closed in case if the user has already settled the claim.
7. Click the Validate a deal icon to check for errors and overrides.
8. Click the Commit the deal icon to submit the record.
