### 6.22  Incremental Customer Election


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *For optional events, the customers can elect incrementally that is, the customer can elect the same or different options multiple times during the election period. The customer election is sent to the custodian through MT565 incrementally for each option and for each election. On the pay date of the...*
> 
> **Applications:** `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `MT565.INSTRUCT`, `SC.CA.ERROR.LOG`, `SC.CA.PARAMETER`, `SC.ENT.AUTHORISE`, `SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION` ... +1 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Addl Narr*, *Auth Per Option*, *Await Elect Status*, *Bene Own Narr*, *Block Nominal*, *Block Type*, *Blocked Nominal*, *Conf Qty, Conf Cash, Conf Date, Conf Delivery Ref* ... +31 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

For optional events, the customers can elect incrementally that is, the customer can elect the same or different options multiple times during the election period. The customer election is sent to the custodian through MT565 incrementally for each option and for each election. On the pay date of the event, the custodian confirmation is received through MT566 for each option which is authorised independently.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details the configuration of incremental election and confirmation for each option.

- The Multi Election field in SC.CA.PARAMETER and DIARY.TYPE is setup for the incremental instruction to the custodian. The Multi Election is enabled only when Mt565 Per Unauth and Mt565 Per Option fields are set to Yes in SC.CA.PARAMETER .
- The Auth Per Option field in DIARY.TYPE controls the authorisation of each option when MT566 is received from the custodian or when the user manually confirms the options.


##### Configuring MT565 Generation in Multi-Election

If multi-election is enabled in the DIARY.TYPE and SC.CA.PARAMETER applications, MT565 is generated and sent from each entitlement or at an omnibus level. This generation is controlled by the Skip Multi Ele Delivery field in the same applications.

- If this field is set to Yes, each time MT565 is generated for the cumulative quantity based on DIARY .
- If this is set to No, each time MT565 is generated from ENTITLEMENT per election.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section provides the details the incremental customer election and confirmation per option in a multi-election scenario. This is explained with an example below.

|  | Customer A | Customer B | Customer C |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qualifying Holdings | 1000 | 3000 | 5000 |  |  |  |
| Options | Stock | Cash | Stock | Cash | Stock | Cash |
| Day 1 | 200 |  | 1200 | 1200 | 0 | 0 |
| Day 2 | 800* |  | 1000 ** | 2000 | 0 | 0 |
| Day 3 (cut-off date) |  | 200 *** |  |  | 0 | 5000 |
| Total Quantity elected | 800 | 200 | 1000 | 2000 | 0 | 5000 |


##### Recording the Election

The process of recording the election in ENTITLEMENT when multi-election is allowed (if Multi Election is set to Y in SC.CA.PARAMETER and DIARY.TYPE ) is described below. The following fields in ENTITLEMENT under each option records the election details.

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Elect Nominal | Indicates the quantity elected |
| Elected Date | Specifies the date of election received |
| Elect Time | Specifies the time of election received |
| Elect User | Mentions the user who makes the election (system if the election is made through standing or default instruction) |
| Bene Own Narr | Indicates any narrative with regards to the underlying beneficial owner |
| Addl Narr | Indicates any additional narrative |

The above fields helps the user to update an election partially or fully in ENTITLEMENT . At each customer level, the uninstructed holdings are available in ENTITLEMENT at all stages in the Pending Nom field. At an event level, the uninstructed quantity is recorded in the Pending Nom field in DIARY . If the user wants to cancel a previous election, or if a cancellation is received through MT565 (CANC) from the institutional customer, the cancelled quantity is mapped to Elect Nominal (with negative sign) field along with the date of cancellation in the Elected Date field. The system maintains the election details for each option in SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION application as a sub-value for each election.


##### Generating MT565 Manually

For an event with multi-election, the value of Skip Multi Ele Delivery in DIARY specifies the generation of MT565. The system populates the default value from DIARY.TYPE and the user can change the value of this attribute.

- If it is set to Yes (consolidated 565), it can be changed to No until the first 565 message is triggered from MT565.INSTRUCT . Once a consolidated message is triggered, no change is allowed.
- If it is set to No when authorised (565 from each entitlement), it can be changed back to Yes until the user performs first election in any entitlement. If the user performs election in an entitlement, the system does not allow the field to be changed to Yes.

The value set in Skip Multi Ele Delivery in DIARY determines the MT565 generation method.

If the user sets Multi Election in DIARY.TYPE to Yes and Skip Multi Ele Delivery to No in DIARY , then the MT565 can be triggered manually from each entitlement. This is done by setting Depo Adv Req to Yes in ENTITLEMENT or in bulk using MT565.INSTRUCT .

| Election | Options | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Election 1 | Customer elects in Option 1 for 100 units and Option 2 for 200 | The system updates the Pending Nom field as 700. At this stage, when Depo Adv Req is set as Yes in the ENTITLEMENT , an MT565 for Option 1 with 100 nominal and for Option 2 with 200 nominal is generated |
| Election 2 | Customer elects in Option 1 with additional 50 units and no change in Option 2 | The system updates the Pending Nom as 650. If Depo Adv Req is set to Yes, an MT565 is generated for Option 1 for 50 units |
| Election 3 | Customer cancels the previously instructed 100 units in Option 1. Hence -100 is updated in Elect Nominal field in Option 1. No change in Option 2 | The system updates the Pending Nom field as 750 and if Depo Adv Req set to Yes, an MT565 is generated to cancel 100 units in Option 1 |

When Depo Adv Req is set to Yes in ENTITLEMENT :

- The Elect Nominal , Elected Date , Elect Time , Elect User , Bene Own Narr and Addl Narr fields under each option are cleared without any values.
- The system sends out separate MT565 from the ENTITLEMENT for each elected quantity for which MT565 message has not been sent. Subsequently, if institutional customer makes another election, then user can trigger another MT565. Thus, multiple MT565 messages can be triggered for the same entitlement on the same day.
- The MT565 messages of institutional customers has the omnibus external account ID mapped in tag 97A://SAFE, even though the MT565 messages are sent from individual entitlements.
- The quantity cancelled by the institutional customer should be equal to the total of previously instructed quantities. MT565 is re-triggered by the user from the entitlement. The system identifies which outward MT565 needs to be cancelled based on reference and quantity (if cancellation is through MT565 from an institutional customer), and sends out the MT565 CANC accordingly.
- On option cut-off date, the default option is applied for any uninstructed quantity. If default option is No Action (NOAC), it is applied for all institutional customers who have not elected and for pending nominal of customers who have partially elected. However, MT565 is not automatically generated. User manually triggers the MT565 message from each entitlement or uses the MT565.INSTRUCT application and select to send the MT565 for default option. Then, the system sends out separate MT565 per election though the trigger is from the MT565.INSTRUCT application.
- When the record in ENTITLEMENT is deleted, MT565 CANC is sent to cancel all the previous MT565 messages. The audit trail is maintained in SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION application.

The screenshots provided below illustrates MT565 generation for an event with two options (cash and stock).

- Cash and stock options are selected and the corresponding fields are input with appropriate values.
- Incremental elections are done using Elect Nominal , Elected Date , Elected User , Elected Time fields.
- On committing the ENTITLEMENT , the system updates the election details in SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION application. However, MT565 is not yet triggered from the ENTITLEMENT .
- When Depo Adv Req is set in ENTITLEMENT , the delivery key (D2020826931520467501) in Delivery Ref field is updated in SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION .

The Elect Nominal , Elect Date , Elect User , and Elect Time fields are cleared from the ENTITLEMENT so that subsequent elections can be made.

If Multi Election in DIARY.TYPE is set to Yes and Skip Multi Ele Delivery in DIARY are set to Yes, then the user triggers MT565 from DIARY for the uninstructed quantity. When MT565 is instructed in this setup:

- MT565 is generated for the cumulative quantity in DIARY . The cumulative quantity is the elected quantity of all the entitlements under each option.
- The delivery reference of each MT565 is updated in DIARY and ENTITLEMENT .
- Subsequently, when a new MT565 is instructed and the quantity elected is changed (at omnibus level), the system sends out a cancellation of previous MT565 and sends a new MT565 for the updated quantity if the Mt565 Gen Method field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Canc Resend.


##### Unblocking Elections based on MT567

The unblocking of the elected quantity based on the MT567 is applicable when the user sets,

- Multi Election in DIARY.TYPE to Yes
- Skip Multi Ele Delivery in DIARY to No
- Block Type to Option in DIARY.TYPE
- Await Elect Status to Yes in DIARY.TYPE

The customer makes partial election which in turn sends an MT565 to the custodian for each election per option from ENTITLEMENT based on the above setup. The elected quantity and the unelected quantity are updated in the Block Nominal and Pending Nom fields, respectively. The system also increments the blocked quantity with each election based on DIARY.TYPE setup.

The system proceeds with the MT567 based unblocking of the elected holdings, when the

- Custodian rejects the new instruction
- Customer cancels the new instruction

If the custodian sends a MT567 rejection while rejecting the instruction, then the system reverses the blocked quantity and uninstructed quantity (pending nominal) reversed to the previous state .

The value in the Delivery Reference , Status (IPRC/REJT ), and Reason Code fields from MT567 are updated in the SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION application under the respective election.

If a customer holds 1000 units and has elected 200 units in option-1 (CASH), then Block Nominal is 200 and Pending Nom is 800, respectively in ENTITLEMENT . The MT565 instructed quantity is 200.

If the custodian rejects the MT565, then the system automatically updates Block Nominal and Pending Nom as 0 and 1000 respectively.

The overall election details for an option along with the status mapped from MT567 in the SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION application is updated as shown in the below screenshot.

When the customer amends an instruction, the system sends out an MT565 CANC message. The custodian can either accept the cancellation through MT567 (CPRC/CAND ) or reject the cancellation through MT 567 (CPRC/REJT ).

If Await Elect Status field is set to Yes in DIARY.TYPE and SC.CA.PARAMETER , then the values in the Blocked Nominal and Pending Nom fields are not changed immediately, when the previous election is cancelled.

The customer is not allowed to make a new election in the option until the MT567 acceptance or rejection is received for the cancelled election. If the customer makes an election, the system displays an override .

If the custodian accepts the cancellation (MT567 CPRC/CAND ), then the value in Blocked Nominal and Pending Nom fields are changed automatically to exclude the cancelled quantity which in turn allows the customer to amend to the election.

If the custodian rejects the cancellation (CPRC/REJT), then the values in the Blocked Nominal and Pending Nom fields are not changes, which in turn restricts the customer not to amend the election.

In SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION , the Delivery Reference of the MT567, the values in Status and Reason Code fields are stored against the respective cancellation to the corresponding status.


##### Handling Manual Update of Status

In ENTITLEMENT , the user updates the status manually when the

- Bank did not receive MT567 due to technical issues,
- Bank received a rejected status (IPRC/ REJT or CPRC/REJT) but subsequently the custodian accepted the new or the cancelled instruction

The bank inputs the status of MT565 (NEWM/CANC) against the respective instruction and the system updates the Blocked Nominal and Pending Nom accordingly.

The bank gives the sender’s reference (Seme Ref) of MT565 for which the system updates the status manually in the Elect Ref field and thus updates the status in the Elect Status field, thus overriding the previous status that is updated manually or through MT567.


##### Confirming per Option

When MT566 is received and the system is parameterised for authorisation per option (if Auth Per Option in DIARY.TYPE is set to Yes), the system does not automatically reconcile any quantity and record in ENTITLEMENT is not authorised, but stores the cash or stock movements present in the incoming message in DIARY and SC.CA.ERROR.LOG .

The quantity received for each option from the custodian is updated in DIARY . The quantity is updated for every MT566 that is received. The user must reconcile and authorise the entitlements manually. If the total quantity received through MT566 for stock option matches with the quantity calculated by the system, then the user can choose to credit the stock (instead of matching the cash portion) to customers who have elected stock. To facilitate authorisation for each option:

- The Opt Auth field is set to Yes in the respective Opt multi-value field in ENTITLEMENT , or
- The corresponding Option Number field (from ENTITLEMENT ) to be authorised in given in the Option field specified in SC.ENT.AUTHORISE application.

On setting the Opt Auth field to Yes:

- All the entitlements that have elected fully in Option 1 is authorised.
- For entitlements that have elected partly in Option 1 and Option 2, the position movement or cash accounting is done (based on whether the Option 1 is stock or cash).

When the MT566 for the cash option is received and manually reconciled, the user can set the Opt Auth as Yes for the other option. For an event with NOAC as one of the options, if confirmation is received through MT566 for the other options and the cash or stock portion is reconciled, the user can authorise the entitlements without waiting for confirmation for NOAC option. If the system is parameterised for confirmation per option, the system updates the reason as shown below in SC.CA.ERROR.LOG for each MT566 received.


##### Reconciling MT566 Automatically for Multiple MT565 Elections

The customers can elect multiple times for voluntary events (VOLU) such as takeover or voluntary merger before the cut-off date, a custodian can send the confirmation multiple times before the payment date.

For mandatory with choice events (CHOS), customers can elect multiple times before the cut-off date and custodian typically sends the confirmation on the payment date.

Irrespective of the event type (CHOS or VOLU), the system provides STP support for the below cases:

- Single MT565 per option on the cut-off date and single MT566 confirmation on the payment date with the event type CHOS
- Several MT565 on or before the cut-off date and several MT566 on or before the payment date with the event type VOLU
- Several MT565 on or before the cut-off date and single MT566 on the payment date with the event types CHOS or VOLU

When the customer sends multiple MT565, the system triggers MT565 for the incremental quantity.The below sections explain the system configuration and system behaviour required for the above scenarios.


###### Single MT565 on the cut-off date and Single MT566 confirmation on the payment date (CHOS)

The customers can elect multiple times before the cut-off date for a CHOS type of event like STOCK.CASH. in DIARY.TYPE The system records each election through the Elect Nominal and Elected Date fields in ENTITLEMENT and also captures the elected user in the respective fields in ENTITLEMENT .

The user sets up the below fields in DIARY.TYPE , to trigger MT565 and automatic reconciliation of MT566.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Multi Election | Elects a portion of the eligible holdings at a time and uses the value in the Pending Nominal field to store the unelected quantity. The possible values of this field are Yes, No and Null. This field is set to Yes in this scenario. |
| Skip Multi Ele Delivery | Allows to skip MT565 generation from each ENTITLEMENT . The possible values of this field are Yes, No and Null. This field is set to Yes in this scenario. The system sends a consolidated omnibus MT565 per option for the elected quantity from DIARY, if an MT565 is triggered through MT565.INSTRUCT or when all the entitlements are elected. |
| Multi Ele Ent Conf | Configures whether a single MT566 or multiple MT566s will be received from the custodian for the event type. This field is set to Single in this scenario where the possible values of this field are Single, Multi and Null. The system reconciles the custodian confirmed quantity or cash against the system quantity or cash and automatically authorise the entitlements that are reconciled on the pay date when MT566 is received. If the reconciliation between the system and custodian quantity or cash fails, then the system updates the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG application with the error log for the mismatch |


###### Several MT565 on or before the cut-off date and several MT566 on or before the payment date (VOLU)

This scenario typically occurs for long voluntary events like, takeover which can last up to six months. The customers can elect multiple times before the cut-off date and custodian can confirm the election multiple times before the payment date.

Each election is recorded through the Elect Nominal and Elected Date fields in ENTITLEMENT . The elected user, beneficial owner narrative are also captured in the Elect User and Bene Own Narr fields in the ENTITLEMENT .

The user sets up the below fields in DIARY.TYPE , to trigger MT565 and automatic reconciliation of MT566

| Field Name | Description |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi Election | Possible values of this field are Yes, No and Null. This field is set as Yes in this scenario. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Skip Multi Ele Delivery | This field is set as No in this scenario where the possible values of this field are Yes, No and Null. MT565 is generated from each entitlement for every election. (the Swift tag :97A//SAFE is the omnibus safekeeping account). This can be triggered in bulk multiple times through MT565.INSTRUCT or by setting the Depo Adv Req field in each entitlement manually. An L3 version automates the valur in the Depo Adv Req field to Yes |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Multi Ele Ent Conf | The possible values of this field are Single, Multi and Null. This field is set as Multi in this scenario as multiple MT566 could be received before pay date. Each MT566 refers the MT565 through the 20C://RELA tag. This tag contains the SEME reference of MT565. An example of a MT566 link to MT565: Swift Tag Description :16R: LINK :13A:: LINK//565 :20C:: RELA//245643454 :16S: LINK | Swift Tag | Description | :16R: | LINK | :13A:: | LINK//565 | :20C:: | RELA//245643454 | :16S: | LINK |
| Swift Tag | Description |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| :16R: | LINK |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| :13A:: | LINK//565 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| :20C:: | RELA//245643454 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| :16S: | LINK |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

The system records the quantity or cash confirmed by each MT566 against the respective MT565 in SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION .

If the quantity confirmed matches with the respective MT565 quantity or within tolerance, the system does the position or cash movement associated with that MT566, with some unelected quantity. The system debits the elected quantity, if the position or cash movement is completed when the Retain Original field is set to No in DIARY.TYPE .

If the MT566 quantity does not match with MT565 quantity (outside tolerance), then the respective message is updates only in SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION . Position or cash movement is not done automatically.

The Conf Qty, Conf Cash, Conf Date, Conf Delivery Ref and Conf Status sub-value fields (to report the reconciliation status of MT566 against the respective MT 565) in SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION to record the quantity confirmed by MT566 in each option against each MT565. These fields are added within the Elect Date multi-value field under each option. In this case, each MT565 and corresponding MT566 does not update SC.CA.ERROR.LOG .

The customer can elect further for which the confirmation can be received subsequently.


###### Several MT565 on or before the cut-off date and Single MT566 on the Payment Date (CHOS or VOLU)

This scenario occurs in short voluntary events (EXRI) or in mandatory with choice events (DVOP or DRIP). Each election is recorded through the Elect Nominal and Elected Date fields. The elected user can also be captured in the respective fields in the ENTITLEMENT .

The user sets up the following fields in DIARY.TYPE to trigger MT565 and automatic reconciliation of MT566.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Skip Multi Ele Delivery | Possible values- Yes/ No/ Null. This field is set as, Yes for CHOS events No for long VOLU events like Takeover Yes for short VOLU events like say optional conversion. |
| Multi Ele Ent Conf | Holds the setup whether a single MT566 or multiple MT566s are received from the custodian for the event type. The possible values for the field are Single, Multi and Null. If this field is set to Single and the reconciliation between the custodian quantity or cash and system quantity or cash is successful, all the entitlements that belongs to that omnibus are authorised. If reconciliation fails, SC.CA.ERROR.LOG or SC.ENT.MULTI.ELECTION is updated with the error log of the mismatch. When the system sends a single MT565 from DIARY or multiple MT565s from ENTITLEMENT, reconciliation against a single MT566 per option on the cut-off date is possible. |


###### Incremental MT 565

When the system sends MT565 from each entitlement, it triggers the incremental instruction. The system sends MT565 for the incremental quantity for any new increase in the elected quantity.

This function is not available when the MT565 is instructed at omnibus level ( DIARY ). Hence, a new value is added in SC.PARAMETER as MT565 Gen Method . If the bank sets up the MT565 Gen Method field as Increment, then all omnibus MT565 becomes incremental for any increase in the quantity elected. Any reduction in quantity at the omnibus level cancels the previous MT565 and triggers a new MT565 for the reduced quantity.

In a voluntary event with two Options, if the quantity elected in Option-1 is 1500 in the omnibus level, then an MT565 is instructed for 1500 for Option-1 at the end of Day-1.

On Day-2 when the quantity elected in Option-1 becomes 1800 in the omnibus level, the system sends out an MT565 only for 300 units.

If the quantity becomes 1400 due to change in quantity elected in one of the customers, then the system cancels the previously instructed MT565 and sends out a new MT565 for 1400 units.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Incremental Customer Election and Confirmation Per Option feature.

This is done by setting Multi Election as Yes and Multi Ele Ent Conf as MULTI in DIARY.TYPE of voluntary events. Automatic reconciliation is processed, and the status is updated against each election reference.

### 6.23  Incremental Election without exdate


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *For some optional events (such as takeover), there may be no ex-date or record date provided by the issuer or custodian. In such events, the election period is long. Customers can incrementally elect until the earliest date provided in Opt Reply By Date field (election cut-off date). The ex-date is ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Mt565 Per Option*, *Mt565 Per Unauth*, *Multi Election*, *No Ex Date*, *Opt Reply By Date*, *Opt Reply By Date.1*, *Opt Reply By Date.2*, *Opt Reply By Dates*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

For some optional events (such as takeover), there may be no ex-date or record date provided by the issuer or custodian. In such events, the election period is long. Customers can incrementally elect until the earliest date provided in Opt Reply By Date field (election cut-off date). The ex-date is considered as the earliest of opt reply by dates.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Set the No Ex Date field to Early Reply By Date in DIARY.TYPE to default the ex-date as the earliest of dates in provided in Opt Reply By Dates field.

For incremental elections, the Multi Election field is enabled in SC.CA.PARAMETER and DIARY.TYPE for setting up incremental instruction to the custodian.

The Multi Election field is enabled only when Mt565 Per Unauth and Mt565 Per Option fields are set to Yes in SC.CA.PARAMETER .


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains about the defaulting of ex-date in no ex-dated or record dated events.


##### Defaulting the Ex-date in No Ex-Dated Events

In no ex-dated or record dated events, the entitlements are generated based on current position of securities at the time of generation. Upon rerunning DIARY :

- New entitlements are generated if some customers have bought securities and
- Existing entitlements are removed if some customers have sold securities.

Consider a takeover event with the below details. The above event has no ex-date or record date defined by the issuer. The event can be open for elections for about six months. As shown in the below screenshot, the value in the Opt Reply By Date.1 is 17 DEC 2009 and the value in the Opt Reply By Date.2 is 11 DEC 2009.

If No Ex Date field is set to Early Reply by Date then as per the setup, the ex-date is defaulted as 11 DEC 2009.


##### Electing Multiple Times in No Ex-Dated Events

The customers can participate multiple times during the events without ex-date. New customers can also participate in the events by purchasing the event security. Read Incremental Customer Election and Confirmation Per Option for more information on detailed workflow on multiple or incremental elections until the cut-off date.

### 6.24  ISO 20022 General Meeting Messages


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The General Meeting events is where the company’s shareholders, directors and other interested parties gather to make decisions on resolutions such as:*
> 
> **Applications:** `DIARY.TYPE`, `MEETING.DIARY`, `MEETING.ENTITLMENT`, `SC.CA.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Meet Def Vote Typ*, *Meet Vote Type*, *Meeting Event Mx*, *New Security*, *Option*, *Security Update*, *Vote Instr Type*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The General Meeting events is where the company’s shareholders, directors and other interested parties gather to make decisions on resolutions such as:

- Appointments to the company's board of directors
- Executive compensation
- Dividend payments
- Selection of auditors and so on

The various types of meeting are:

- Annual general meeting
- Extraordinary general meeting
- Statutory meeting
- Court meeting and so on

The meeting notifications are different from other corporate action notifications in which each option or resolution in the meeting notification can be separately elected. Some resolutions might be for information purpose and may or may not need shareholders voting.

Therefore, ISO 20022 has specific messages to handle the meeting related events. Temenos Transact supports the MX meeting messages:

- seev.001 – Meeting Notification message informs the company's shareholders about the time, date and place of a corporate meeting along with the resolutions and voting options.
- seev.002 – Meeting Cancellation message where the sender sends out to cancel the incoming Meeting Notification message (seev.001)


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic details the configurations to support the MX Meeting messages in Temenos Transact

The SC.CA.PARAMETER application defines the OFS attributes for creating and updating the records in the MEETING.DIARY and MEETING.ENTITLMENT applications through STP.

The Option field in DIARY.TYPE is set to Yes and the other key parameters such as New Security and Security Update are set to No. The Meeting Event Mx field is set to Yes and all the Meeting Vote Types are entered.

When the system receives an incoming Meeting Notification (seev.001), it considers only those records in DIARY.TYPE where the Meeting Event Mx field set to Yes.

The Meet Vote Type field lists the various vote options available for the event. The voting options that are specified in the Vote Instr Type field in the record in MEETING.DIARY supersedes the vote options given for the meeting event in the respective record in DIARY.TYPE . If the resolution remains unvoted, then the default vote option to be applied is given in the Meet Def Vote Typ field.


#### 📋 Tasks

The user can view the below list of tasks pertaining to ISO20022 General Meeting Messages in the Temenos Transact .

The General Meeting Notification message (seev.001) is used to announce the meeting details, resolutions for the meeting, vote type, and so on. Few resolutions require shareholders voting. The system records these details from the incoming message.

When the meeting notification message is received, the system creates a record in MEETING.DIARY application. Once the required information is updated in MEETING.DIARY and the record is authorised, a service generates records in MEETING.ENTITLEMENT for each portfolio in IHLD. The MEETING.ENTITLEMENT record holds the details of qualified nominals, meeting date, and resolutions where the shareholder has the right to vote. If information such as meeting resolution is missing in the incoming seev.001 message, the system updates the error log with appropriate errors or warnings.

If the incoming meeting notification message contains errors or incorrect information, the sender sends a meeting cancellation message. When the incoming seev.002 is received, the system identifies the corresponding record and updates the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG . The user reverses the MEETING.DIARY record manually.


##### Workflow

User can perform the following activities:

If the meeting notification message seev.001 is processed with incorrect or missing information, the system updates the error log with incoming message with error details and creates the MEETING.DIARY in IHLD or INAU status.

To view the MEETING.DIARY record, perform the following steps:

1. Meeting Diary Notifications in Error
2. Click the View icon for the corresponding record.

To edit the MEETING.DIARY record, perform the following steps:

1. Meeting Diary Notifications in Error
2. Click the Edit icon for the record that require amendment.
3. Amend values in the required fields.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon.

To update the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG after editing the MEETING.DIARY record, perform the following steps:

1. Meeting Diary Notifications in Error .
2. Click the Update icon.
3. Amend values in the required fields.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon.

If the meeting notification message seev.001 is processed with incorrect or missing information, the system updates the error log with incoming message with warnings and creates the MEETING.DIARY in IHLD or INAU status. If resolution is not part of incoming message, system updates the error log with warning and creates the MEETING.DIARY in INAU status.

To view the MEETING.DIARY record, perform the following steps:

1. Meeting Diary Notifications with Warning .
2. Click the View icon for the corresponding record.

To edit the MEETING.DIARY record, perform the following steps:

1. Meeting Diary Notifications with Warning .
2. Click the Edit icon for the record that require amendment.
3. Amend values in the required fields.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon.

To update the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG after editing the MEETING.DIARY record, perform the following steps:

1. Meeting Diary Notifications with Warning .
2. Click the Update icon.
3. Amend values in the required fields.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon.

If the incoming meeting notification message contains errors or incorrect information, the sender sends a meeting cancellation message. When the incoming seev.002 message is received, the system identifies the corresponding record and updates the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG . The user can reverse the MEETING.DIARY record manually.

To reverse or delete the MEETING.DIARY record, perform the following steps:

Meeting Diary Cancellations .

2. Click the Edit icon of the corresponding record.

The live records are reversed and unauthorised records are deleted.

To view the incoming cancellation message, perform the following steps:

Meeting Diary Cancellations.

2. Click the View icon for the corresponding record.

### 6.25  Loyalty Bonus on Public Offers


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Loyalty Bonus is a corporate action event, wherein investors who received allocations through IPO and held those shares for a certain period are rewarded with additional bonus shares. This loyalty bonus is announced as part of the IPO and encourages investors to subscribe to the IPO and to hold on t...*
> 
> **Applications:** `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `ENTITLEMENT`
> 
> **Prerequisites:** `DIARY`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.POSITION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Alloc Date*, *Alloc Trans Type*, *Allocation Date*, *Ex Date*, *Qualify Holding*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Loyalty Bonus is a corporate action event, wherein investors who received allocations through IPO and held those shares for a certain period are rewarded with additional bonus shares. This loyalty bonus is announced as part of the IPO and encourages investors to subscribe to the IPO and to hold on to the received allocations.

The additional bonus shares are provided to investors holding the shares until the loyalty period followed by the allocation of shares as a part of IPO allocation.

The IPO allocation can be processed within or outside Transact. In either of the case, the allocations are reflected in Transact as a security transaction. Loyalty bonus is distributed as a corporate action.

For an IPO loyalty bonus Corporate Action, the system

- Identifies customers who have participated in an IPO and held the position till loyalty bonus determination date.
- Identifies the relevant parcels and prorate the cost between old and new parcel to facilitate Capital Gain calculations.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Loyalty Bonus issue on IPOs and FPOs in Corporate Actions (CA) is defined for an event type using the DIARY.TYPE application. This application contains the processing details and the rules associated with CA. The below screenshot shows a record in DIARY.TYPE for loyalty bonus issue.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details about processing the loyalty bonus for a given security.

To process the loyalty bonus, the user must input the following fields in the DIARY application:

- Alloc Date which holds the IPO allocation date.
- Alloc Trans Type which holds the credit transaction code used in the IPO or FPO allocation. The IPO allocations are booked using this transaction code.
- Ex Date which holds the loyalty bonus determination date.

Based on the above combination the system determines the eligible holdings. The system generates records in ENTITLEMENT for those customers who acquired the securities as on the Alloc Date with the transaction type specified in Alloc Trans Type and continue to hold the positions till the Ex Date .

The system determines the eligible holdings as below:

Any new customer who purchases the units after the Alloc Date is not eligible to receive the loyalty bonus, and hence entitlement is not generated. If existing customers acquire new holdings after the Alloc Date , the loyalty bonus is capped to the IPO allocation quantity. The eligible holdings are minimum of the holdings held as on Ex Date and Allocation Date .

The determination of qualifying holdings are explained with the below examples.

Consider an IPO on Amazon security as on 15 APR 2021. Participants of the IPO offer are eligible to receive loyalty shares of Amazon as on the ex-date of 15 OCT 2021. The ratio of loyalty bonus is 5:1.

The transactions captured in the system on 15 APR 2021 are shown in the table below.

| Portfolio | Transaction Type | Quantity | Transaction Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100292-1 | IPO | 50 | SCTRSC1910788524 |
| 100291-1 | IPO | 100 | SCTRSC1910767832 |
| 100285-1 | IPO | 500 | SCTRSC1910755858 |

The transactions captured in the system after the IPO allocation date are shown in table below.

| Portfolio | Date | Transaction Type | Quantity | Transaction Reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100291-1 | 20 APR 2021 | SELL | 80 | SCTRSC1910767113 |
| 100285-1 | 10 SEP 2021 | BUY | 100 | SCTRSC1910769123 |
| 100291-1 | 10 SEP 2021 | TRI | 50 | SECTSC21123ZTBT3 |
| 100297-1 | 11 SEP 2021 | BUY | 100 | SCTRSC1910768976 |

A record in DIARY created for a Bonus event. The user needs to input the Ex Date as 15 OCT 2021, Alloc Date as 15 APR 2021 and Alloc Trans Type as IPO. The system generates records in ENTITLEMENT for 3 customers (100292-1, 100291-1 and 100285-1).

With respect to the eligible units,


###### For customer 100291-1

As on Ex Date , the customer holds 70 units of Amazon. But as on Alloc Date , the customer was allocated 100 units.

As the eligible holdings will be minimum of the holdings held as on Ex Date and Alloc Date , the Qualify Holding in ENTITLEMENT record will be 70 and the customer would receive 14 additional units.


###### For customer 100292-1

As on Ex Date and Alloc Date , the customer holds 50 units of Amazon.

Hence the Qualify Holding in ENTITLEMENT record will be 50 and the customer would receive 10 additional units.


###### For customer 100285-1

As on Ex Date the customer holds 600 units of Amazon. But as on Alloc Date , the customer was allocated 500 units of Amazon.

As the eligible holdings will be minimum of the holdings held as on Ex Date and Alloc Date , the Qualify Holding in ENTITLEMENT record will be 500 and the customer would receive 100 additional units.


###### For customer 100297-1

As on Ex Date , the customer holds 100 units of Amazon. But as on Alloc Date the customer holds no units of Amazon share

Hence no record is created in the ENTITLEMENT application for the portfolio.

#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs for Loyalty Bonus on Public Offers.

### 6.26  Maintaining Portfolio Value


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In a mandatory Corporate Action (CA) event (like, Bonus/Demerger) once the event is announced, the price of the event security reduces on the ex-date to compensate for the new shares issued at the end of the event.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Incl Pend Sec*, *Pend Nominal*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In a mandatory Corporate Action (CA) event (like, Bonus/Demerger) once the event is announced, the price of the event security reduces on the ex-date to compensate for the new shares issued at the end of the event.

During the period between market price drop date (ex-date) and the new shares credit date (pay date), the portfolio value of the customer holding this security drops to the extent of market price correction.

This feature explains how to maintain the portfolio value of all the customers between the ex-date and the pay date of the event. In the Bonus event type, the portfolio value drop due to change in market price of the security after ex-date is calculated as:

| Qualifying holding | 500 |
|---|---|
| Price prior to ex-date | 80 USD |
| Bonus ratio | 1:1 |
| Portfolio value at ex-date | 500*80=40000 USD |
| Price after ex-date | 41 USD |
| Portfolio value after ex-date | 500*41=20500 USD |
| Portfolio value shortfall (to be adjusted from ex-date to pay date) | 40000-20500 = 19500 USD |

In the above case, the market price before the ex-date is 80 USD. On the ex-date, the price drops to 41 USD. The portfolio value of the customer before ex-date was 40,000 USD and it reduces to 20,500 USD.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The required setup for maintaining the portfolio value during the Corporate Action (CA) is shown below. Set the Incl Pend Sec field to Yes in DIARY.TYPE .


#### 🔧 Working With

The below topic explains how the portfolio value is maintained during a Corporate Action (CA) event. If Incl Pend Sec is set to Yes in DIARY.TYPE , the entitlements are generated and:

- The quantity of expected security is updated in Pend Nominal field in SECURITY.POSITION of the new security, along with the transaction reference (diary ID) and the ex-date of the event.
- The pending quantity is also included in the SC.POS.ASSET (valuation table) from the ex-date until the entitlements are authorised, thereby maintaining the portfolio value of the customer.
- On the allotment date (pay date), when the new shares are credited to the portfolio, the pending quantity is removed from SECURITY.POSTION and SC.POS.ASSET .

The value in Pend Nominal field for a Bonus event, where the customer is expected to receive shares at the end of the event is shown in the below screenshot.

The value in Pend Nominal field is also updated in the SC.POS.ASSET application.

The value in Pend Nominal field updated in the Portfolio Valuation – Cost (SC.VAL.COST) enquiry.

When the entitlements are authorised, the value in Pend Nominal field is removed from the SECURITY.POSITION , SC.POS.ASSET and the Portfolio Valuation – Cost (SC.VAL.COST) enquiry


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Maintaining Portfolio Value feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Maintaining Portfolio Value feature.

### 6.27  Market Notifications


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Information regarding a corporate action is usually available in the market, before it is officially informed through the custodian.*
> 
> **Applications:** `SC.CA.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Criteria Date*, *Delivery Inref*, *Ex Date*, *Gen Ca Advice*, *Inw Corp Reference*, *Link Record Ref*, *Non Depo Msg*, *Pay Date* ... +3 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Information regarding a corporate action is usually available in the market, before it is officially informed through the custodian.

The bank receives this information as a feed from their market providers. Banks notify their customers, particularly their institutional customers, about the event as soon as the market information is received. After the official notification is received from the custodian, further market notifications are ignored and Straight Through Processing (STP) flow continues for the event.

Temenos Transact receives market notifications and also pre-notifies the eligible customers.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the set up required for handling market notifications for corporate action events.


##### Configuring Non-Custodian Notifications

The corporate actions has to be pre-defined, where early notification from non-custodian is handled. The Non Depo Msg field in DIARY.TYPE for the corporate action is set to Yes to configure early notifications from non-custodian.


##### Configuring Tolerance Days for Duplicate Checking

When a corporate action notification is received from the custodian, the system checks if there is an existing market notification in SC.PRE.DIARY already in the system. This ensures that the customers are not sent duplicate NEWM messages for the same event (one from market notification and one from custodian notification).

The Ex Date and Pay Date values in SC.PRE.DIARY are checked for duplicates. Also, the ISIN and SWIFT qualifier of the incoming MT564 are checked for duplicates. However, SC.PRE.DIARY created from non-custodian notifications may not have an ex-date or the ex-date may be tentative. While checking if an incoming MT564 from a custodian pertains to an event for which pre-diary is created from a non-custodian message, the ex-date (or pay date) can be checked within a range of dates.

This range is specified in SC.CA.PARAMETER with the record ID as SYSTEM. The Criteria Date field is a multi-value drop-down field. This field holds the values of ex-date and pay date.


#### 🔧 Working With

This following section explains the handling of market notifications from non-custodian.


##### Handling Market Notification from Non- Custodian

The following topics provides details on the creation of an event for non-custodian notification and inform the entitled customers who can receive pre-notifications.

The market notification is interfaced with Temenos Transact through MT564 like message.

When system receives an incoming MT564, system checks if the sender is a custodian that is, the sender BIC is the BIC address of a depository as defined in CUSTOMER.SECURITY . If the sender is not a custodian, then system treats the message as a non-custodian message. The system checks the SWIFT qualifier in the incoming message to identify the DIARY.TYPE of the event.

If the Non Depo Msg field is set to Yes in the DIARY.TYPE , then system treats the notification as a non-custodian notification. Once the notification is received from a non-custodian, the record in SC.PRE.DIARY is created with the Source field updated as Non Custodian. When it is not possible to interface a market notification through MT564 like message, the Source field in the SC.PRE.DIARY can be manually set as Non Custodian.

If the Source field is marked as Non Custodian, record in DIARY is not created for the SC.PRE.DIARY as this is only a pre-notification and not the official notification. However, in order to send notification to customers, system generates records in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION . The ID of the records in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION file is:

SC.PRE.DIARY ID * Portfolio * Depository* Sub Account * SECURITY.MASTER ID

Records are created for all entitlements as on the Ex Date value defined in the SC.PRE.DIARY . If Ex Date is not available in the market notification, system generates records for all holders as on the current bank day. The eligible customers are notified about the corporate action event through outward MT564 generated from SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION . Every re-run of the SC.PRE.DIARY adds new records, if new holdings are identified and records are cancelled if the customers are not eligible.

REPL or CANC message received from the non-custodian amends the existing pre-diary until a custodian message is received for the event. Every REPL or CANC message is notified to customers through SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION . Once the announcement is received from the custodian or the pre-diary is manually amended, then the non-custodian notifications are ignored.

The records in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION created for the pre-diary to identify the entitled customers and MT564 message (and pre advice) are triggered to the entitled customers to inform them about the early notification of the corporate action event.

> **⚠️ Note:** The MT564 and pre-advice are sent to the customers, where Gen Ca Advice field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY is set to Yes.

The Rerun field in SC.PRE.DIARY reruns the diary to identify the positions acquired after the first run. The Rerun field has three options:

- MT564
- Yes
- BOTH

If the Rerun field is set to MT564, then system reruns the pre-diary and generates the MT564 to customers whose positions are acquired after the rerun. If the Rerun field is set as BOTH, then both MT564 and pre advice are generated to the clients whose positions are acquired after the first run.


##### Handling Custodian’s MT564 message

The following topic details on how the MT564 messages from a custodian are handled.

| Field | Value | Resultant Action |
|---|---|---|
| Criteria Date | Ex Date | If the incoming MT564 from the custodian carries an Ex Date as 15 August 2018, system checks the record in SC.PRE.DIARY for the same event with Ex Date in the range from 3 August 2018 to 27 August 2018 |
| Tolerance Days | 12 |  |

When an incoming MT564 is received from a valid custodian and system has identified that a SC.PRE.DIARY exists for the same event from a non-custodian source, the system creates a new SC.PRE.DIARY for the custodian. This SC.PRE.DIARY in turn creates a diary for the custodian and system continues the corporate action flow for the diary. Read Corporate Actions Workflow for more information.

The existing non-custodian pre-diary is linked to the new pre-diary using the Link Record Ref field in custodian pre-diary records. In the non-custodian SC.PRE.DIARY , this field is updated with DEPOSITORY* SC.PRE.DIARY ID for each record in SC.PRE.DIARY created from the incoming custodian MT564.

In the custodian SC.PRE.DIARY , the Link Record Ref field is updated with the ID of the non-custodian SC.PRE.DIARY .

The incoming custodian MT564 is linked to the existing record in SC.CTDY.CORP.ACTION (created for non-custodian pre-diary), using the Inw Corp Reference field. The Inw Corp Reference field is populated with the tag in the incoming MT564 from custodian.

There may be deviations in certain values between the two records in SC.PRE.DIARY , such as coupon rate or pay date. If there are any deviations, the customers are informed through MT564 (REPL), where MT564 (NEWM) is already sent to the customers from the non-custodian pre-diary. The Deviation - Custodian Notification vs Non-Custodian Notification (SC.PRE.DIARY.DEVIATION) enquiry lists the deviations between custodian and non-custodian pre-diary records.

The user can manually amend the SC.PRE.DIARY created by MT564 from non-custodian, but changing the value of the Source field to Manual and updating the DEPOSITORY with valid custodian is mandatory. Diary is created for this pre-diary. After the record is amended manually, MT564 (or like) message from non-custodian or custodian for the respective event is ignored and updated in the SC.CA.ERROR.LOG .


##### Creating Market Notification Manually

When a user creates a record in SC.PRE.DIARY based on notification from non-custodian, custodian or any other source, the Source field is automatically updated as Manual (system identifies that it is manual entry as the Delivery Inref field is blank). The system ignores any non-custodian or custodian updates to the created SC.PRE.DIARY including cancellation messages.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Market Notifications for Corporate Action Events feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

The user can view the below list of enquiries and reports pertaining to Market Notifications for Corporate Action Events feature.

Custody vs Non-Custodian Deviation

This enquiry displays the deviation in values between the custodian pre-diary and the linked non-custodian pre-diary such as, Rate, Exdate, Paydate and so on.

To generate the output from this enquiry, values in the below fields must be provided.

- Security No
- Event Type

### 6.28  Meeting and other non-financial events


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *There are a number of Corporate Action (CA) events that involve no debit or credit of resources, that is, cash or stock is not changed. The events are as explained in the below table:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Other Date Type*, *Other Date Type and Other Date*, *Suppress Entitlement*, *Swift Caev*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

There are a number of Corporate Action (CA) events that involve no debit or credit of resources, that is, cash or stock is not changed. The events are as explained in the below table:

| Event | Description |
|---|---|
| MEET | Annual general meeting |
| XMET | Extraordinary or special general meeting |
| CHAN | Information regarding any change described in Corporate Action details (for example, change of name) |
| CONS | Proposal to obtain a consent from the investors without having a meeting (for example, change in terms of a bond) |
| BRUP | Bankruptcy |
| CERT | Certification requirements |

The cash or stock movement are not involved in these events. The event can be classified as:

- Mandatory (for example, CHAN – change of name without change of underlying security) or
- Voluntary (for example, extraordinary or special general meeting).

The events provide an option to the user (for example, Yes or No). The user elections need to be instructed to the custodian (through SWIFT MT565). The system handles meeting and other events that are non-financial in nature, that is, cash or stock movement is not involved.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic helps the user to configure the event types for this feature.


##### Defining Event Type

The first step in the handling of meeting or notification type events is to define the event type ( DIARY.TYPE ) in the system for events where cash or stock movements are not involved. Some of these events offer options to the user (for example, meeting with an option to give or deny consent). The default option for these voluntary events are No Action (NOAC – option for the account owner not to take part in the event).


##### Defining Meeting Event Type – with Options

If in a meeting event type the following attributes are sent, then it means that the user has to instruct his choice (provided the user is participating in the event).

- No cash movement
- No stock movement
- Options set as Yes

The Swift Caev field in the record has the value of XMET. This is used to match the incoming MT564 with the DIARY.TYPE in Temenos Transact


##### Changing the Name of Event Type Definition – Mandatory


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic enables the user to create events.


##### Creating Events

The SC.PRE.DIARY application is created automatically based on the incoming MT564. Alternatively, the SC.PRE.DIARY or DIARY is manually entered in case of non-STP events.

The option description is mapped from the SC.CA.OPTION.DESC application.


##### Creating Suppress Entitlement

The entitlements for certain events can be suppressed (based on the settings in Suppress Entitlement field in DIARY.TYPE ), where further processing is not required. Based on Corporate Action (CA) event notice received, an advice is sent to the user to inform the event details. Further processing is not required.


##### Additional Details about the Event

The system captures additional details relating to the event such as, announcement date, effective date, meeting date, meeting time, meeting venue, new name (in case of change of name), filing date, hearing date and other additional details or narrative.

The various dates associated with the events are:

- Announcement date
- Certification deadline date
- Effective date
- Further announcement date
- Deadline to register
- Second meeting date
- Filing date
- Hearing date
- Court approval date

The Other Date Type and Other Date fields are used to capture various dates. The various date types are defined in the SC.CA.DATE.TYPE application and the description is mapped to Other Date Type field in the event.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Meeting and other Non-Financial Events feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Meeting and other Non-Financial Events feature.

The Corporate Action module allows to record and process a corporate action (CA) event. The processing of the CA events can be done manually or through Straight Through Processing (STP). This module supports the CA processing for both omnibus and segregated accounts.


##### Product Configuration

The parameters for Securities Corporate Actions (SC-CA) are explained below:

### 6.30  Multiple Currency Dividend


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Cash dividend is distribution of cash to shareholders, in proportion to their equity holding. It is a mandatory event where shareholders must take cash. However, in some instances, the shareholders may be offered a choice of currency.*
> 
> **Prerequisites:** `DIARY`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.POSITION`, `CUSTOMER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Ca Fee Adjust*, *Cash Div Ccy*, *Event Currency*, *Option*, *Options*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Cash dividend is distribution of cash to shareholders, in proportion to their equity holding. It is a mandatory event where shareholders must take cash. However, in some instances, the shareholders may be offered a choice of currency.

From the options provided by the issuer, the shareholders can choose a currency in which to receive the dividend. This feature explains the processing of multiple currency dividend in Temenos Transact application.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The multi currency dividend in Corporate Actions (CA) defines the event type using the DIARY.TYPE application. The DIARY.TYPE application contains the processing details and the rules associated with CA. The Options field is set to Yes to enable this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

In case of cash dividends where there are currency options, the participation in CA is mandatory and further instructions (regarding the choice of currency) from the account owner is required, unless a default option has been specified by the owner.

Cash dividend with currency choices is shown below.

The customer can also receive part of the dividends in one currency type and the remaining part of dividends in different currency types.

For the HSBC dividend, the customer can elect to receive his dividend in multiple currencies (like, US dollars for 40% of the holding, in HK dollars for 30% of the holding and in GBP for the rest of the holdings).

The dividend is credited to the respective currency accounts of the customer (the customer should have accounts in the currencies opted for receiving the dividend).

The source or local taxes and fees or other charges are prorated based on the nominal elected for each currency and net dividend is credited to the respective currency accounts. The SECURITY.MASTER record holds the list of currencies in which dividends can be paid out.

> **⚠️ Note:** The new or additional currencies can be defined at event level in using the DIARY application.

The currency choices are available in the event (manually updated or based on incoming SWIFT MT564) in SC.PRE.DIARY or DIARY application.

The exchange rates between the default (value in the Event Currency field) and the dividend (value in the Option field) currency is also updated. The exchange rate is either known upfront or at later date when it is available.

The ENTITLEMENT records are created with these options for the customer to elect. If default instructions are available for an entitlement, it is also are applied. Once the customer has elected, an instruction (MT565) is with the customer’s choice and on receipt of the confirmation (MT566) the ENTITLEMENT records are authorised and the account is posted.


##### Standing Instructions for Multi Currency Dividends

The standing instructions are setup for the choice of currency. If the customer elects to receive the dividend in multiple currencies, the elections are specified only in the ENTITLEMENT record as there is no provision to specify the standing instructions for payment in multiple currencies. The SC.ENT.INSTR application defines the default instructions for the customer’s choice of currency.

In this case, the customer’s choice (based on dividend currency) is specified. As per the above example, the customer elects to receive the dividend in US dollar, if the dividend is declared in US dollar. The Cash Div Ccy multi-value field can be expanded to define the customer’s choice for other currencies (for example, if the dividend is declared in HKD, the customer elects to receive the dividend in USD).

Cash dividends paid out for a specific event may be lower than the standard commission or fees charged for CA event. In such cases, the commission charged should be reduced so that it is not more than the dividend amount. The Ca Fee Adjust field in SC.PARAMETER application controls whether the fee applicable for CA events are to be restricted to the extent of dividend payment. Cash dividend is the distribution of cash to the shareholders in proportion to their equity holding. It is possible to specify a fee that is charged for the event (flat or percentage of dividend). If a minimum fee is specified and the fee is more than the dividend amount, then the customer account is debited.

CA Fee (min) – HKD 100

Dividend Paid – HKD 50

In this case, the customer account is debited as the fee exceeds the dividend and there is amount due from the customer for the event. In such scenarios, there is a provision to adjust the fees or commission so that it is not more than the dividend amount.

CA Fee (min) – HKD 100

Dividend Paid – HKD 50

In this case, the customer is charged a fee of HKD 50 even though the minimum fee chargeable for the event is HKD 100. There could be cases where a tax (for example, service tax) is applicable on the fee. In such a scenario, the fee has to be adjusted taking into account the tax to be levied.

CA Fee (min) – HKD 100

Dividend Paid – HKD 75.

A service tax (ST) of 20% is applicable on the dividend fee. In this case, fee has to be adjusted where the fee plus 20% ST does not exceed HKD 75. The system determines the tax rate applicable, adjusts the fee and calculates the tax on revised fee.

The revised fee is HKD 62.50 and tax is 20% on HKD 62.50 (that is, HKD 12.50).

If the dividend is subject to tax, there is a provision to adjust the fee to the extent of net dividend.

CA Fee (min) – HKD 100

Dividend Paid – HKD 50.

The income is subject to a source tax of 10%. In this case, dividend net of source tax is HKD 45.

In this case, the fee has to be adjusted to HKD 45 so that there is no outgo from the customer. The Ca Fee Adjust field in SC.PARAMETER application determines whether the fee is adjusted to the extent of gross or net dividend. The fee adjustment is applicable for other events like stock dividends (cash portion), where there is a cash payout.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Multiple Currency Dividend feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Multiple Currency Dividend feature.

### 6.31  OffMarketBuyback


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The off market buyback feature enables the shareholders of a company to receive an offer to buy back some or all of the shares in the company. Customers can choose to participate in the event or lapse the event. If the customer participates and the company accepts the shares, the customer receives t...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Block Position*, *Buyback Disc*, *Buyback Income*, *Buyback Prc*, *Buyback Price*, *Buyback Tax*, *Corp Ref*, *Def Opt* ... +19 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The off market buyback feature enables the shareholders of a company to receive an offer to buy back some or all of the shares in the company. Customers can choose to participate in the event or lapse the event. If the customer participates and the company accepts the shares, the customer receives the cash proceeds. In this event, the shareholders can choose to tender the shares from various discount percentages (as allowed by the offer) or lapse the offer (as the event is voluntary).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The configuration for off market buyback is shown in below screenshot.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic explains the event creation including the various options available for the eligible customers and also explains how the elections are recorded.


##### CreatingDIARY

The following are the three possible options available for customers to participate in the event:

Customers can tender shares at various discount percentages to the final market price as allowed in the offer. The Buyback Disc field in DIARY is updated with the buyback percentages announced in the offer.

Customers can tender shares at a minimum price. If the final buyback price is below the minimum price the customer’s tender is not accepted. The Min Price - field in DIARY is updated with the minimum price.

Customers can tender shares at a finally accepted buyback price. The Final Price Opt field in DIARY is updated to Yes or No. Additionally, the customers can choose to tender the shares at final price subject to a minimum price. In that case, the Min Price has a value within the final price option.

Customers who do not wish to participate in the offer, can elect to lapse the offer. The lapse option is the default option. Hence, if instruction is not received from the customer the lapse option is applied.

Some buyback events might have additional criteria for the customers holding, lesser than a minimum quantity. These customers can tender their holdings under a single discount option or the final price option. This minimum quantity is an event level attribute and is captured in Small Holdings field in DIARY .

The below event allows the customers to tender the shares at 8%, 9% and 10% discount from the final market price. The event also allows tendering at final buyback price. Additionally, the customers can also tender the shares at minimum price of 55 AUD.

Event creation in DIARY for this event announcement is shown in the below screenshot.


##### Customer Election

The system identifies the customers holdings eligible units on the ex-record date for generating the entitlements. Any sale done post the ex-record date until the election, is reflected in the quantity available to tender (eligible holdings). However, any purchases done during this period is not included, except that the new quantity is more than the ex-dated quantity.

| Customer | Ex-record dated quantity | Sell | Purchase | Quantity allowed for tender |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Customer A | 1000 | 200 | 0 | 800 |  |
| Customer B | 2000 |  | 1000 | 2000 |  |
| Customer C | 3000 | 2000 | 500 | 1500 | 1500 |

### 6.32  Parallel Trading


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This feature explains the working of parallel trading in stock split and conversion. In certain markets, stock split and conversion events involve issuance of temporary security and there is a period of parallel trading pursuant to these events.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Parallel Trading*, *Settlement Days*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This feature explains the working of parallel trading in stock split and conversion. In certain markets, stock split and conversion events involve issuance of temporary security and there is a period of parallel trading pursuant to these events.

Parallel trading is classified by different periods where the system allows the following actions:

- Initial period, where the trading in original or mother or an underlying security is suspended and trade is allowed only in temporary security. During this period, the position in the underlying security is moved to the temporary security.
- Period when parallel trading is allowed. At the start of the parallel trading period, the position in temporary security is moved back to the original security.
- Period when parallel trading stops and the final conversion to the mother or underlying security happens.

Thus, there are three conversion events. For each event (parent), additional diaries (child) are run during the settlement days to convert any residual positions.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

In DIARY.TYPE application, the Parallel Trading field is set to YES in order to enable the parallel trading feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

If the event type is configured for parallel trading, the system automatically creates additional child diaries based on the value set in the Settlement Days field in the STOCK.EXCHANGE application as explained below:

1. The parent diary creates additional child diaries (two child diaries in case of T+2 settlement) automatically to split or convert any residual position (that is, settled on T+1 and T+2).
2. The created child diary is in LIVE or HOLD status, based on the entitlements created and authorised in the parent diary. If the parent entitlements are created and authorised, then the child diary is created in LIVE status, else the child diary is created in HOLD status.
3. The system maintains a link between the parent and child diaries.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Parallel Trading feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Parallel Trading feature.

### 6.33  Partial Redemption


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Certain securities are redeemed in part, before their scheduled final maturity date without reduction in nominal value of the securities. This is done by a reduction of pool factor value of debt instrument which results in the payment of a cash amount calculated on the basis of pool factor reduction...*
> 
> **Applications:** `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `SC.PRE.DIARY`, `SECURITY.MASTER`
> 
> **Prerequisites:** `DIARY`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.POSITION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Retain Original*, *Sinking Fund*, *Swift Caev*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Certain securities are redeemed in part, before their scheduled final maturity date without reduction in nominal value of the securities. This is done by a reduction of pool factor value of debt instrument which results in the payment of a cash amount calculated on the basis of pool factor reduction.

The below event illustrates how redemption is processed without actually reducing the nominal.

The redemption rate is 0.005690705 (difference between old and new factor) and the redemption amount is calculated using the formula given below.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Sinking Fund field in the SECURITY.MASTER application is set for the instruments, where processing of partial redemption based on pool factor is required.

A separate DIARY.TYPE record is available to capture the key attributes of the corporate action event ( Swift Caev field as PRED). The Retain Original field is set to Yes as nominal reduction is not available.


#### 🔧 Working With

On receipt of MT564 (corporate action notification) for the PRED event, the system updates the details of old and new factors in the SC.PRE.DIARY or DIARY application. The factor details are available in the SWIFT message and the below screenshot is an example of the same.

NWFC denotes the new factor and PRFC denotes the existing or previous factor. The difference is used to determine the redemption amount. Based on the old factor and new factor, the system calculates the rate (old factor – new factor). For example, if old factor is 0.9 and new factor is 0.8, then the redemption factor is 0.10. The factor details are mapped from SC.PRE.DIARY application to DIARY application.

The redemption details are input manually in the DIARY application for non-STP events. The redemption factor is used to calculate the entitlement amount (difference between old and new factor multiplied by the nominal).

### 6.34  Record Dated Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This feature explains about the generation of entitlements based on record date.*
> 
> **Applications:** `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `SC.PARAMETER`, `SC.TRANS.NAME`, `SEC.TRADE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Eff Date Processing*, *Rec Date Trd*, *Rec Date Trfr*, *Rec Dt Txn Code*, *Unsett Trf Pr Ex*, *Unsett Trf Pre Ex*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This feature explains about the generation of entitlements based on record date.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The settled trades and transfers that occurs while creating the entitlement (based on the record date) is configured as below:

- DIARY at the event level or
- SC.PARAMETER at the company level or
- DIARY.TYPE at the event level.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic details about the record dated processing based on settled position.


##### Qualifying Holding based on Settled Position on Record Date

In certain markets, the Corporate Actions (CA) processing is based on settled position as on record date. Transfer-in, transfer-out and internal transfers are some transactions that impacts the qualifying holding (eligible holding), if they are settled on or before the record date.

For determining qualifying holding, the system can be setup to include certain transactions done on or after ex-date, but settled on or before the record date for CA processing . The transactions could be security transfer-in, security transfer-out or internal transfers (such as position transfer).

The transactions in SEC.TRADE application can also be included based on the parameter setting.The Rec Date Trfr and Rec Date Trd fields, for transfer and trade respectively, are the fields that controlling the qualifying holding based on settled position as on record date. These fields can be set to YES in:

- DIARY at the event level or
- SC.PARAMETER at the company level or
- DIARY.TYPE at the event level

The record dated processing is applicable based on settings in these fields at three levels, which is tabulated below:

It is possible to exclude certain transactions from the purview (for qualifying holding calculation) by specifying a valid SC.TRANS.NAME (for example, TRO) in Rec Dt Txn Code field in DIARY or SC.PARAMETER or DIARY.TYPE application.

If a transfer has been initiated prior to the ex-date but not settled by record date, then by default the same is included in eligible holding calculations. It is possible to exclude those transfers from the calculations, if required, based on the value in the Unsett Trf Pre Ex field (if this field is set to NO, the transactions are excluded from qualifying holding calculations) in DIARY or SC.PARAMETER or DIARY.TYPE application.

For events like stock split and reverse stock split (where the ex-date and pay date are the same), the qualifying holding is based on settled positions as at COB of the day prior to the effective (record) date. The events are identified based on settings in Eff Date Processing field (applicable if set to YES) in DIARY or SC.PARAMETER or DIARY.TYPE application. As these fields are available in all three applications, the hierarchy based on which the value is considered is explained below:

| Application Name | Level | Description |
|---|---|---|
| DIARY | Event level | First priority. Default values based on settings in SC.PARAMETER or DIARY.TYPE (if SC.PARAMETER is blank). Can be overridden at DIARY level. |
| SC.PARAMETER | Company level | Default settings applicable for a company |
| DIARY.TYPE | Event Type level | Default settings applicable in all companies for the event type (overridden by SC.PARAMETER level settings for specific locations). For selected events like stock split, the Eff Date Processing field can be updated at this level so that value defaults from DIARY application. |
