### 6.35  Reinvestment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A dividend reinvestment program or dividend reinvestment plan (DRIP) is an equity investment option offered directly by the underlying company. Reinvestment is a special event to reinvest the cash dividend into the same security at a reinvestment price that declared by the company. The reinvestment ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *Amount Lcy*, *Fcy*, *Net Amount*, *New Market Price*, *New Price*, *Opt Nom Dep*, *Option Desc Dep* ... +1 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A dividend reinvestment program or dividend reinvestment plan (DRIP) is an equity investment option offered directly by the underlying company. Reinvestment is a special event to reinvest the cash dividend into the same security at a reinvestment price that declared by the company. The reinvestment price is usually at a discount to the market price at the time of announcement.

Based on regulatory requirements, the Dividend Reinvestment can be handled in different ways.

- Using Reinvestment Parameter - The cash value of the dividend is credited to the client’s account and immediately an order or trade is created to invest the funds in the security at the reinvestment price.
- Direct Reinvestment - No cash is credited to the investor but reinvested nominal is directly credited to the client.
- Using DRIPS fields and Cash remain functionality - Nominal in multiples of trading units is directly credited to the client and balance for fractional quantity if any is paid in cash. Allows update of reinvestment price after DIARY is authorised.

This topic illustrates the direct investment method.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The reinvestment event is defined for an event type using the DIARY.TYPE application.


#### 🔧 Working With

The DIARY record with the reinvestment details are shown in the below screenshot. The offer is either cash of 11.375% per share or more of the same security.

The rate for the reinvestment is set later and is dependent upon the market price prevailing at the announcement date.The DIARY record is changed to save the New Market Price (New Market Price) field as 127.50. The New Price field is changed to 115.00 as an incentive for the holder to invest in new shares rather than taking the alternative cash option. Then the DIARY record is re-run through the service agent to produce the following ENTITLEMENT record.

In the ENTITLEMENT record, the user can view the auto-generated fields for both options (cash offer and reinvestment option). The cash option at 0.11735 per share

The user must make a partial election in which case the user specifies 8,000 for the reinvestment option.

The cash option totalling GBP 796.25 is derived from 7,000 shares where each share is due a dividend of GBP 0.11375 per share. For the re-invested portion of 8,000 shares, 791 new shares are expected. This is derived from

The new shares are allocated at a value of GBP 1.15 each, therefore 910 / 1.15 = 791 new shares. The cost of 791 new shares are 791 x 1.15 = GBP 909.65 which leaves GBP 0.35 additional cash dividend to receive. The total cash of GBP 796.60 (GBP 796.25 + GBP 0.35) is seen reported in the Net Amount field.

Authorise the ENTITLEMENT record and validate the transactions in the SECURITY.TRANS application for the position updates and cash postings.

The additional shares totals to 791. The cash value associated with the share option is posted on the SECURITY.TRANS application and therefore the system updates the Central Reporting Files (CRF).

The CONSOL.UPDATE.WORK table is responsible for the subsequent building of the CRF during the next COB. All the online accounting excluding CRF is shown in the below screenshot.

Back up the system and run a COB to ensure the CRF entry is raised appropriately. After the COB, check the RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY record for the ENTITLEMENT record to ensure that the Local Currency (LCY) equivalent is calculated from the Foreign Currency (FCY) original amount.

The Amount Lcy field is showing the local currency equivalent to the ENTITLEMENT record amount reported in the Amount Fcy field.

The conversion of GBP 909.65 to local currency USD is done by multiplying the GBP amount with the exchange rate.

In order to see the values in the Opt Nom Dep field in the ENTITLEMENT application, a new DIARY record for a similar activity is entered and run through the service agent.

The new DIARY record is processed by the service agent and builds the ENTITLEMENT record.

The ENTITLEMENT record generates the expected values as given below:

### 6.36  Reinvestment through Order or Trade


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A dividend reinvestment program or dividend reinvestment plan (DRIP) is an equity investment option offered directly from the underlying company. Based on regulatory requirements, the dividend reinvestment is handled in different ways.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Br Deliv Instr*, *Br Trans Code*, *Cu Trans Code*, *Narrative*, *Net Trade*, *Ofs Source*, *Reinvest Param*, *Stock Exchange* ... +1 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A dividend reinvestment program or dividend reinvestment plan (DRIP) is an equity investment option offered directly from the underlying company. Based on regulatory requirements, the dividend reinvestment is handled in different ways.

- Using Reinvestment parameter - Reinvestment through order - The cash value of the dividend is credited to the customer’s account and immediately an order or trade is created to invest the funds in the security at the reinvestment price.
- Direct Reinvestment feature - No cash is credited to the investor but the reinvested nominal is directly credited to the customer.
- Using DRIPS fields and cash remain feature - Nominal in multiples of trading units is directly credited to the customer and balance for fractional quantity (if any) is paid in cash. The reinvestment price can be updated after the DIARY application is authorised.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This sections details the settings required for dividend reinvestment through order or trade.


##### SC.REINVEST.PARAM

The SC.REINVEST.PARAM application is created to set all the data that is used to generate the order.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Narrative | Holds the description of the current record used for enrichment |
| Stock Exchange | Indicates a valid ID of the STOCK.EXCHANGE record, which is used to generate trade(s) |
| Cu Trans Code | Specifies the customer’s transaction code to be used in the trade |
| Br Trans Code | Indicates the broker’s transaction code to be used in the trade |
| Br Deliv Instr | Delivery instructions to be used in the trade |
| Net Trade | Indicates whether the trade generated is a net trade or not |
| Ofs Source | Indicates a valid ID of the OFS.SOURCE record used to generate a SEC.TRADE record through OFS |


##### OFS.SOURCE

In cases where Temenos Transact generates a SEC.TRADE application, the system creates it through OFS. The OFS.SOURCE record for dividend reinvestment is set up to achieve this. Read the OFS User Guide for more information.

- Version - This field contains the VERSION name to be used to generate the trade. Usually the version is a full view version with zero authorisers to authorise the record automatically.


##### TSA.SERVICE

In conjunction with OFS.SOURCE record, a TSA.SERVICE record must exist that allows the system to use a service process. The TSA.SERVICE application is setup with the SC.CORPORATE.ACTIONS record as shown below.

Refer the OFS and TSA Service documentation in the Temenos Transact User Guide for more information.


##### DIARY.TYPE

To enable dividend reinvestment through order or trade, a specific DIARY.TYPE record is created. A standard cash DIARY.TYPE application is setup with one more parameter entered in the Reinvest Param field. This field contains the SC.REINVEST.PARAM record, which is used as the parameter application.


#### 🔧 Working With

There is a special process to reinvest the cash dividend into the same security that has generated the cash entry, that is, as used for mutual funds.

For example, the fund manager has paid a dividend and reinvested it in new shares. The system posts a cash entry to the customer’s account and generates a trade to reinvest the cash. The system assumes that the depository acts as a broker.

Temenos Transact generates either a SEC.TRADE or SEC.OPEN.ORDER record depending on whether the reinvestment price is known or not. Read the OFS User Guide documentation for more information. The price must be input in the DIARY record. The orders are generated while authorising the ENTITLEMENT records.


##### DIARY

Once all the parameters have been set up, the user is able to generate a new DIARY record for dividend reinvestment. The Reinvest Price field is set up at this stage. This field must contain the price that is applied on the trade. If the price is entered, then Temenos Transact generates a SEC.TRADE through OFS and authorises it (if a zero authoriser version is set up in OFS.SOURCE ), otherwise it generates a SEC.OPEN.ORDER in HOLD status.


##### ENTITLEMENT

Once the ENTITLEMENT records are authorised, a SEC.TRADE or SEC.OPEN.ORDER record is generated. Hence, the Reinvest Order field of each ENTITLEMENT record is populated with the related transaction number.

The reinvestment process can be fully automated to generate a SEC.TRADE transaction. The SC.REINVEST.SERVICE automates the reinvestment process and reinvests the income generated from an ENTITLEMENT record. The resultant SEC.TRADE transaction is automatically created without any manual intervention.

### 6.37  Rights


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A rights issue is an invitation to existing shareholders to purchase additional new shares in the company. This type of issue gives securities called rights to the existing shareholders, in proportion to their existing holdings. With the rights, the shareholder can purchase new shares at a discount ...*
> 
> **Prerequisites:** `DIARY`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.POSITION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allow Retail Prem*, *Block Rights*, *Br Rights Nom*, *Channel (MARKET/CUSTODIAN)*, *Corp Reference*, *Cust Nominal*, *Customer No*, *Depo Rights Nom* ... +55 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A rights issue is an invitation to existing shareholders to purchase additional new shares in the company. This type of issue gives securities called rights to the existing shareholders, in proportion to their existing holdings. With the rights, the shareholder can purchase new shares at a discount to the market price on a stated future date. If the shareholder is not interested in acquiring additional shares, he can choose to lapse his rights.

The rights can be processed either as:

- Single event – The rights are credited to the portfolios first and then within the same entitlement. It is possible to elect to exercise or lapse the rights.
- Two corporate action (CA) events – One event is a mandatory distribution of rights securities to existing shareholders at a given ratio and the other event is to exercise or lapse the rights. The second event works similar to the single event method, except for crediting rights positions as that is done by the rights distribution event.

This feature defines a single event right processing.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configuration of various applications related to rights in Temenos Transact .


##### DIARY.TYPE

To handle the processing of rights, a DIARY.TYPE application is created in Temenos Transact with the below setup. The Rights field is set to Y.

If the event allows multiple exercise(where the Rights can be exercised multiple times during the offer period) and retail premium(where the holder of the rights receives cash for the lapsed rights), the Multiple Exercise and Allow Retail Prem fields, respectively, should be set to Yes.


##### SECURITY.MASTER

Rights are securities that can be traded independently in the market, until the time they are converted to the original security. Hence, a separate record in SECURITY.MASTER needs to be created for a rights security with the Rights Flag field set to Y.


#### 🔧 Working With

The processing of rights through the Corporate Actions (CA) module is detailed below:

- This CA type involves the distribution of rights to holders. Rights are issued based on the ratio given in the issue.
- The rights are held based on the pending decision as to which option(s) to take.
- It is possible to buy and/or sell rights within the trading period (from rights issue until exercise dates).
- Exercising a right allows the holder to buy further shares at a favourable price compared to the current market price.
- If the rights issue allows multiple exercise, the customers can exercise the rights multiple times during the offer period.
- The unexercised rights can be allowed to expire (lapse) where election should not be communicated to the registry or depository.
- If the rights issue allows retail premium, the customers receive cash for the lapsed rights.

Assume a rights event, where one rights is given for one share held as on record date. The customers can exercise the rights to receive the new shares. For every four rights exercised, the customer receives one new share.

The system recognises the purchase and sale of rights booked during the rights trading period and consequently updates the ENTITLEMENT application automatically.

Consider the below security position in a security that is undergoing a rights issue.

Enter the values in DIARY for the rights CA event as shown in the following screenshot. The customers receive one rights for each share held. The rights can be further exercised to receive the new shares. In this case, the entitlement enables the exercising of four rights to obtain one new share.

Once the above record in DIARY is authorised and run through the service agent, the system creates the records in ENTITLEMENT for all the eligible customers. The rights security is credited to all the entitled customers. The rights are available for trading during the trading period.

In case of fractions of rights (that is, not exactly divisible by four), those left over may be sold or further rights can be purchased to ensure that all rights can be exercised. It is also possible to allow any rights to simply lapse without taking any action. The records in ENTITLEMENT are created for all the customers as shown in the following screenshot.

The first holding of 1,500 rights is shown in the following screenshot.

The customer received 1,500 rights and can exercise these rights to receive 375 shares. These rights can be exercised at a cost of USD 30.00 for each share. Because the entitlement is for 375 new shares, this requires a payment of USD 11,250.

The customer can also choose to lapse because the holder exercising the rights does not have any obligations and the rights may be allowed to expire. It is also possible to buy and sell options during the trading period. Temenos Transact updates the underlying ENTITLEMENT (without rerun), for any rights security trade. For example, a purchase of additional 25 rights (as shown in the following screenshot) automatically updates the ENTITLEMENT relative to the portfolio. The screenshot below shows a typical record in SEC.TRADE , where an additional 25 rights are purchased from the market.

When the user enters the values, the ENTITLEMENT is updated automatically.

The above screenshot shows how the ENTITLEMENT is updated with respect to the values entered in the SEC.TRADE. application.

The Cust Nominal field in SEC.TRADE requested a purchase of 25 rights which, when added to the existing holding of 1,500, gives a new holding of 1,525 rights. As the ratio at which exercise can be done is provided (that is, four rights to one new share), it gives an opportunity to subscribe for 381 new shares.

The user can exercise the rights by entering the exercise quantity in the Option Nominal field. In case of partial exercise, the remaining nominals are defaulted to lapse.

The customer had 1,525 rights and chose to exercise 1,000 rights. Once the entitlement is authorised, the customer receives 250 shares and the customer’s account is debited for USD 7,500. The remaining 525 rights are lapsed.

Once the user exercises the rights, the rights’ security position is blocked for the exercised quantity (if the Block Rights field is set to Yes in DIARY.TYPE ). This is done to block the user from selling the rights in the market after electing to exercise.

If the user buys the rights security after exercising the rights, the buy quantity is updated in the Pending Nom field and the user has to re-elect in the ENTITLEMENT application.


##### Multiple Exercise of Rights

If the rights issue allows multiple exercise, the Multiple Exercise field in DIARY.TYPE should be set to YES. If this field is set to Yes, the customer can exercise the rights received or purchased multiple times during the offer period. For each exercise, the customer account is debited for the exercised amount. The credit of new shares is the cumulative of all the exercises. In case of renounceable or tradable rights, the exercise date can be treated as the acquisition date.

The customer received 1,500 rights based on the ratio 1:1. Further, the customer purchases 25 additional rights from the market. At this stage, the Option Status field in ENTITLEMENT is marked as Pending.

The customer first chose to exercise 500 rights on April 30, 2019 by entering the exercise quantity 500 in the Elect Nominal field and the date as April 30, 2019 in the Elected Date field. If the user does not enter Elected Date , the system defaults the current date. The remaining quantity is updated in the Pending Nom field. In the following screenshot, the Pending Nom field is set to 1,025 (1525-500). At this stage, the Option Status field is updated as Paid. The user can exercise multiple times before the cut-off date, and the Option Status field remains in Paid status. Once the Option Status is moved to Paid, the record status of the entitlement shows as authorised.

The customer can choose to exercise the remaining rights by entering the exercise quantity in the Elect Nominal field. The previous election is shown in the Int Elected Date and Int Elected Nom fields. The remaining quantity is updated in the Pending Nom field and the Option Status is set to Paid.

On the cut-off date, the quantity in the Pending Nom field is updated in the LAPSE option and upon authorisation of the ENTITLEMENT , the Option Status field is set to Completed. The security position is updated once the Option Status in ENTITLEMENT is set to Completed.


##### Credit of Retail Premium for Lapsed Rights

If the rights issue allows credit of retail premium for the lapsed rights, the Allow Retail Prem field in DIARY.TYPE is set to YES. If this field is set to Yes, the customer receives cash for the lapsed rights. The issuer declared USD 1.5 as retail premium for the lapsed rights. The Retail Premium field in DIARY is updated as 1.5.

In the below scenario, the issuer declared 1.5 USD as retail premium for the lapsed rights. The Retail Premium field in DIARY is updated as 1.5.

After the DIARY is authorised, the record in ENTITLEMENT is updated with the retail premium amount. After the ENTITLEMENT is authorised with Option Status as Completed, the customer account is credited with the retail premium amount. The customer has lapsed 525 rights and received USD 787.5 as retail premium.

In the below scenario, the customer has lapsed 525 rights and receives 787.5 USD as retail premium.


##### Early Allotment

In events like rights, there is a possibility that customers, who exercise the rights before a certain date, are eligible for early allotment of the new shares. The system records the early allotment date at the event level. On the early allotment date, the custodian sends the confirmation for the exercised rights for the eligible customers. Upon confirmation, the eligible customers get the shares allotment for the rights exercised until the early allotment date. Other customers can continue to exercise the rights or elect after the early allotment date also.

| Customer | Election Date | Allotment Date (value date) |
|---|---|---|
| A | September 06, 2018 | September 13, 2018 |
| B | September 11, 2018 | September 13, 2018 |
| C | September 15, 2018 | September 26, 2018 |


##### US Settlement Method - Outstanding from Broker

Temenos Transact supports both US and non-US settlement methods for rights processing. When the Settlement Method field is set to US in the SC.PARAMETER application, the rights event-specific fields in ENTITLEMENT are updated both on the broker and depository end.

| Nominal | Settled (with Depo) | Unsettled (with Broker) | Event Nominal | Rights Nominal | Depo Rights Nom | Broker Rights Nom |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15,000 | 10,000 | 5,000 | 45,000 | 67,500 | 30,000 | 15,000 |


##### Buy and Sell of Rights through Custodian

Rights can be bought or sold in the market in the interim trading period. However, in some instances, the custodian offers the option to buy or sell rights as part of the rights event. In case the event terms include options to buy or sell rights during the interim trading period, the system allows electing the option (to be instructed to the custodian) and generates trades automatically for sale or purchase of rights, after confirmation is received.

In the following DIARY record, the custodian provides an option to buy or sell the rights security directly from the custodian. If the Rights Multi Trad field in DIARY.TYPE is set to No, then the purchase or sale of rights is done only through custodian.

After the DIARY record is authorised, the system creates entitlement for all the eligible customers. The system also creates a record for all the customers and the depository in SC.CA.BUY.SELL . The system maintains the allowed trading period (from and to dates) for interim security and raises warnings if the trade is outside this period. The customer can enter the sale or purchase quantity in SC.CA.BUY.SELL and commit the record. The ID is the entitlement ID and instructions (MT565) can be generated to the custodian based on the option elected. After the confirmation for the MT565 is received from the custodian, the event is processed and trade is generated for the sale or purchase of rights.

Subsequent exercise is for the adjusted quantity considering the sale or purchase.

The sale or purchase can be done only after the rights credit date and prior to the rights expiry date.


##### Purchase and Sale of Rights through Market or Custodian

In a rights event, the purchase and sale of rights can be done in both market or custodian route in certain markets. The user can decide to place the purchase or sale instruction through market or custodian.

- If the user decides to place the instruction through market route, an order is created for the requested quantity and the order is executed in the market.
- If the user decides to place the instruction through custodian route, the instruction is communicated to the custodian.

The purchase and sale of rights can be done multiple times during the trading period of a rights event. The Rhts Multi Trad field in DIARY.TYPE is set to Yes to enable the purchase or sale of rights through market and custodian using SC.CA.BUY.SELL . The rights that are tradable in the market are called quoted rights. For quoted rights, the Sec Status field in SECURITY.MASTER is set to Tradable and a record is created in SC.CA.BUY.SELL for all the customers. For unquoted rights, the Sec Status field in SECURITY.MASTER is set to Non Tradable) and no record is created in SC.CA.BUY.SELL .

In the below scenario, the customer had 216 rights. The customer first places a purchase order for 36 rights through the market. After the record in SC.CA.BUY.SELL is authorised, SEC.OPEN.ORDER ref (SOO ID) is generated for the order. Then, the customer enters one additional order for 50 rights as shown in the following screenshot.

Consider a rights event for a quoted rights where customers can:

- Purchase or sell rights during the trading period.
- Instruct the quantity rights to be exercised.
- Instruct the quantity of new shares to be received.
- Not instruct any option (in this case, default instruction is applied).

The customers can elect the amount in Qty field in SC.CA.BUY.SELL according to the option (BUYA or SLEE) in the Sell Buy Opt Desc field in DIARY . The back office user can select the channel through the Trade Channel field in SC.CA.BUY.SELL .

- If the Trade Channel field is set to MARKET, an order is created by the system for the quantity instructed by the customer. Further, the order can be transmitted to the market for execution by the user. The quantity of rights (to be purchased) is entered in the Qty field according to the option (BUYA or SLEE) in SC.CA.BUY.SELL. Each time the customer wants to purchase or sell the rights, the quantity of rights can be entered in the Qty field of the respective option (BUYA or SLEE), as the previous purchased quantity is cleared by the system. An order in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is automatically created by the system in IHLD. The details in the order such as Security No , Customer No , Security Acct , Transaction Code and Nominal are updated from the SC.CA.BUY.SELL application. The user can now enter the values in the Order Type , Limit Expiry Date and Limit Price fields in SEC.OPEN.ORDER and commit the order. When the order is executed and a trade is created, the system updates the new rights quantity in the respective record in ENTITLEMENT .
- If the Trade Channel field is set to CUSTODIAN, an MT565 is generated for the quantity instructed by the customer. The quantity of rights (to be purchased) is entered in the Qty field of the respective option (BUYA or SLEE) in the Sell Buy Opt Desc field in SC.CA.BUY.SELL . Each time the customer wants to purchase or sell the rights, the quantity of rights can be entered in the Qty field of the respective option (BUYA or SLEE), as the previous purchased quantity is cleared by the system. Each time trading is done through SC.CA.BU,Y.SELL , when the record is authorised, an MT565 message is sent to the custodian indicating the quantity purchased or sold by the customer. In case of omnibus scenario, the system generates the MT565 message from the custodian record in the SC.CA.BUY.SELL application and not from the individual customer record. On receiving confirmation on the purchased or sold quantity from the custodian through incoming MT566 message and if the quantity is reconciled, then the system updates the Price , Trade Date and Value Date fields and updates the Status field as PROCESSED in SEC.OPEN.ORDER . Once the Status field in the multi-value set is updated as PROCESSED, a record in SEC.TRADE is generated. The revised rights quantity is updated in that respective record in ENTITLEMENT .

Within the election period, after purchase and sale of rights, the customers can elect the quantity of rights allotted. The allotment updates the net quantity of rights pending for exercise in the ENTITLEMENT record.

- Once the purchase and sale of rights are confirmed, the customers can exercise the rights using the Option Nominal field in ENTITLEMENT .
- When the customer elects for a specific quantity of shares, the user enters the quantity of desired shares in the Tgt New Share Qty field in SC.CA.BUY.SELL . Based on the initial quantity of rights held and quantity of shares requested, the system determines the quantity of rights that need to be purchased or sold to receive the target shares and updates the value in the Qty field in the respective options (BUYA or SLEE).

In the below scenario, the customer receives 214 rights. The customer chooses to receive 250 new shares and enters 250 in the Tgt New Share Qty field. Based on the ratio (1:1), the system updates the rights share that has to be purchased in the Qty field.

- The channel of purchase or sale of the rights can be through market or custodian.
- The quantity of rights is updated in the customer’s ENTITLEMENT record that is pending for exercise.
- After the allotment of rights (confirmed through SEC.TRADE if the Trade Channel field is set to MARKET, or confirmed through MT566 if the Trade Channel field is set to CUSTODIAN), the equivalent rights needs to be exercised under the Option Nominal field in ENTITLEMENT .

For Rights event, the customer can set the standing instructions upfront using the SC.INT.INSTR application. The customer can give the below standing instructions:

- Take-up – If the customer sets the standing instruction as Take-up, the given rights are exercised to receive the new shares.
- Sell – If the customer sets the standing instruction as Sell, the given rights are sold.
- Buy More – If the customer sets the standing instruction as Buy More, a buy order for additional rights is placed to receive the round up nominal.

The defined standing instruction is applied on the ENTITLEMENT record based on the rounding, and if the Gen Ent Stand Instr field in DIARY.TYPE is set to Y.

Consider a rights event (quoted rights) with the option to exercise the rights with round-up or round-down and sell the rights. On authorising the below record in DIARY , records are generated in ENTITLEMENT and SC.CA.BUY.SELL .

If the customer chooses to exercise with round-up option or if the standing instruction of a customer (the Rights field) is set to Buy More in SC.ENT.INSTR , the system automatically calculates the additional rights to be purchased due to the rounding up instruction. This updates the Qty field in SC.CA.BUY.SELL for the BUYA option.

Consider a customer holding 1,000 rights. The exercise ratio for share and rights is 1:35. If the standing instruction of customer A is to exercise with round up option, then additional rights required for receiving the shared rounded up is purchased and the entire quantity is exercised. In this case, 1,015 rights are auto exercised when confirmation is received for purchase of 15 rights. The customer receives 29 rights.

If the customer chooses to exercise with round down or if the standing instruction (the Rights field) is set to Take-Up in SC.ENT.INSTR , the system automatically calculates the rights that need to be sold due to the round down instruction. This updates the Qty field for the SLEE option in SC.CA.BUY.SELL .

Consider a customer holding 1,000 rights. The exercise ratio for share and rights is 1:35. If the standing instruction for customer A is to exercise with round down option, the excess rights that needs to be sold and the remaining quantity is exercised. In this case, 980 rights are auto-exercised when confirmation is received for the sale of 20 rights. The customer receives 28 shares by exercising 980 rights.


##### Rights – Upfront Payment

In certain rights issue, the payment for rights subscription needs to be made upfront (at the time of election). The Upfront Payment field should be set to YES in DIARY.TYPE . If this field is set to YES, customer account is debited during each exercise for the subscription amount.

After the customer exercises the rights, the record in ENTITLEMENT needs to be authorised and the Option Status must be set to PAID. On authorisation (interim) the following updates happen:

The user account is debited for the amount due (Nominal * Rights issue price plus charges, if any) and the the CA suspense account is credited (Nominal * Rights issue price). The charges are posted to P&L.

User Holding – 25,000 shares

Rights – 1 for every 5 shares held

Price – 15 USD

User exercises:

= (5,000*15) = 75,000 USD

The following entries are raised:

Dr – User Account 75,000 USD

Cr – Corp action suspense 75,000 USD

The payment to the custodian is a manual process. The Update Nostro flag in DIARY.TYPE is set as NO for such events.

- The security position (of the underlying security) is updated to reflect the paid up amount (equal to consideration paid upfront). As the cash is paid upfront and the nominal is yet to be allotted, the paid up amount is included in valuation.
- The underlying security position is not changed as the underlying securities are received later only.
- The Entitlement Status is set to Paid. The DIARY application cannot be re-run even for a single entitlement, after the status changes to Paid.

Upon authorising the entitlements and once the confirmation is received (either manually or based on MT566), the system performs the following:

- The Entitlement Status is changed to Completed from Paid.
- If the underlying security position is updated to reflect the new security received on exercise of rights (paid up amount becomes zero), the rights security position becomes zero.
- There are no accounting entries as the payment has been made upfront.

If the event includes an oversubscription option, there is a provision to make upfront payment similar to upfront payment for exercise.

In case of oversubscription, there is a possibility of a partial or no allotment. The amount that the user has paid upfront is refunded (either partially or fully) for the unallocated quantity.

If the user decides to let the rights lapse, the rights position is withdrawn on the lapse withdrawal date, in case it is specified.


##### Oversubscription of Rights

Companies sometimes make an offer to the security holders to subscribe for additional securities. This option to purchase additional shares is represented by rights. Each share of stock carries rights representing a pro rata interest in the additional shares.

To stockholders who have exercised their privilege of subscribing to additional shares, the company may offer the opportunity to purchase the unsubscribed remaining shares at the subscription price on a pro rata basis. This is called oversubscription. In effect, an oversubscription is a bonus privilege extended to stockholders who have participated in a rights offering that gives them an opportunity to participate in residual portion of a corporation’s offering of shares to its stockholders.

While most rights offerings are underwritten (guaranteed by an investment firm), thereby eliminating oversubscription offering, some companies bypass underwriting and offer shares directly to their stockholders through the option of oversubscribing. In this event, if the unsubscribed shares to fill oversubscription orders are insufficient, the company allots the unsubscribed shares on a pro rata basis. An investor may participate in the oversubscription without owning shares, if he first purchases rights. This establishes privilege to subscribe to shares and additional shares at the termination of the rights offer. In case the oversubscription option is available, it is recorded in the DIARY of events.

Holders of stock or Rights security, who exercise their rights to subscribe, have the privilege of oversubscribing. If a customer elects to oversubscribe, the details of the election are recorded in ENTITLEMENT . In the Over Subscribed Nom field, the customer has to input the number of new shares he wants to subscribe in the event security.

The oversubscription option is directly communicated to the custodian through SWIFT MT565 (there is separate MT565 messages by option – one for exercise, one for oversubscription), which indicates that the oversubscription is over and above their entitlement as per their current holdings.

In the event where the unsubscribed shares to fill oversubscription orders are insufficient, the company allots unsubscribed shares on a pro rata basis.

After the allotment details are notified (can be manually recorded or updated based on incoming SWIFT MT566), the system allocates new shares to the individual investors, who have oversubscribed on a pro rata basis. The customer pays for the entire quantity (shares entitled based on rights and the oversubscribed shares allotted) at the price specified.


##### Handling Bonus Option for Rights Issue

In some rights issue, the issuer attaches a free bonus option (exercisable later) in proportion to the quantity of rights exercised. In the following example, the customer receives a bonus option for every two rights exercised.

The customer receives 2,000 rights as per the issue. The customer chooses to exercise all the 2,000 rights. As per the ratio, the customer receives 500 shares (4:1) and 250 bonus options (a bonus option for two rights exercised). For the exercise of rights, the customer account is debited for USD 15,000. After the entitlement is authorised, the security position of event and bonus security is updated accordingly.


##### Rounding

For rights processing, the calculation of the Nominal in ENTITLEMENT (the number of new shares after exercising) is always rounded down. If the Rounding field in the related DIARY.TYPE is set to UP or STANDARD, an override message is displayed to warn the user about the change in the calculation.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Manage Corporate Event - Rights
- Administration and Static Data and Corporate Actions

Rights issues are Corporate Actions Events, whereby a company seeks to increase its capital by issuing new securities. Existing shareholders need to be given a chance to maintain their stake in the company to prevent dilution. So, rights are credited to existing shareholders of a company.

The Rights can be exercised to subscribe to new securities during the exercise period.

On the paydate of the event, the shareholder, who exercised the rights will receive the resulting securities and will pay the company the exercise price per share. (Sell entitlement, Buy Additional rights, Over subscribe than the additional limit).

The Rights, which are not exercised will be lapsed.


##### Workflow

This section allows the user to perform the below task:

Diary for rights is used to input rules and details specifically for rights event.

1. Rights Diary .

### 6.38  Rounding, Odd Lot and Fraction Handling


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The nominal received from a corporate action may not always be in multiples of trading units. Based on the event rate or event ratio (ratio of new nominal to existing nominal), there are situations when some investors may end up with odd lots or fractions. The following are the ways to handle such d...*
> 
> **Applications:** `CURRENCY`, `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `SEC.ACC.MASTER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Adjust*, *Adjust Cash*, *Adjust Nom*, *Adjust Sec*, *Amt*, *Cash*, *Cash Rounding Methd*, *Depo Adjust* ... +33 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The nominal received from a corporate action may not always be in multiples of trading units. Based on the event rate or event ratio (ratio of new nominal to existing nominal), there are situations when some investors may end up with odd lots or fractions. The following are the ways to handle such distributions:

- Round the nominal to trading units - either up or down or standard.
- Allow fractions - not rounding the nominal, but allowing fractions to be credited.
- Odd lot processing - hold the odd lots separately.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section explains the setup required for handling rounding, odd lot and fractions.


##### DIARY.TYPE

The rounding method is defined using the Rounding field in the DIARY.TYPE application. The different types of rounding available are:

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Down | Always rounds down the value. This is the equivalent to the Round Down Only field being set as YES. |
| Standard | Follows the standard rounding rules. This is the equivalent to the Round Down Only field being set as NO. |
| Up | Rounds up the value. |
| Fraction | Takes the fractional amount of the trading unit. |

The value of 33.33 is rounded as:

- Down - 33
- Up - 34
- Standard - 33
- Fraction - 0.33

In addition to nominal rounding, the system also allows rounding of cash entitlements for corporate action (CA) events that involve cash movements. This is defined using the Cash Rounding Methd field in the DIARY.TYPE application. This field accepts the following values:

- Blank - Indicates the standard rounding rules. This is the default option which is standard rounding.
- Dn - Indicates to round down the value always.

If the value is USD 33.336 and if the USD record in CURRENCY accepts decimals up to two places, then:

- Blank (standard) - USD 33.34
- Dn (round down) - USD 33.33

> **⚠️ Note:** The number of decimals to be rounded is based on the No of Decimals field in CURRENCY .


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section details about the various methods of handling the nominal received on result of a corporate action.


##### ROUNDING.LEVEL

There are three levels of rounding in corporate actions:

- Customer level
- Depository level
- Depo Rerun

The Rounding Level field allows of the user to select either CUSTOMER or DEPOSITORY or Depo Rerun. The default is CUSTOMER. If the Rounding Level field is set to DEPOSITORY, then the Rounding field should be set as STANDARD or DOWN.

| Scenario | Tolerance status | Entitlement status |
|---|---|---|
| Matched | No difference between the nominal due to customer and the nominal due from depository | Entitlements are authorised. |
| Unmatched | Difference within tolerance | Entitlements are authorised but error is updated in the log (Nominal Difference – within Tolerance). |
| Unmatched | Difference exceeds the tolerance set | Entitlements are not authorised but error is not updated in the log (Nominal difference – Exceeds Tolerance). |

| Customer | Position (no. of shares) |
|---|---|
| Customer 1 | 10 |
| Customer 2 | 40 |
| Customer 3 | 40 |
| Total Holding | 90 |


##### Lot and Dec Rounding

Besides the rounding methods of Up, Dn, and Lg (legal), the Nom Rounding Methd field has two further options namely, Lot and Dec.

When the nominal resulting from a corporate action is calculated, the system validates the Nom Rounding Methd field. If this field is set to LOT, then the new holding uses a lot rounding method to calculate the resulting position. The lot rounding method performs the rounding before multiplying the result by the denominator of the ratio. The lot rounding method is controlled by the value in the Rounding field. It cannot be used with the adjustment method.

If there is a holding of 20 in a stock that is subject to a stock split corporate action with a ratio of three new shares for seven shares held, then the rounding is calculated as:

- If the result is rounded down, then the position receives six new shares with six lots remaining.

- If the result is rounded up, then the position receives nine new shares with no lots remaining.

The odd lots nominal can be consolidated in a single position under the same security number as tradable units. This option is available when the Rounding field is set to FRACTION and the Nom Rounding Methd field is set to DEC.

The following is an example with all cases of calculation.

A portfolio has 10,000 shares. A split gives two new shares for three old ones.

The XXX value is rounded based on the settings in the Nom Rounding Methd field as explained in the below table.

| Rounding or Rounding Method | Normal | Lot | Dec |
|---|---|---|---|
| Up | 6667 | (3334*2) 6668 Odd Lot = 0 | 0 |
| Down | 6666 | (3333*2) 6666 Odd Lot = 1 | 0 |
| Standard | 6667 | (3333*2) 6666 Odd Lot = 1 | 0 |
| Fraction | 0.666 | (3333*2) 6666 Odd Lot = 0.333 | 6666 Odd Lot = 0.666 |


##### Odd Lot Handling

A separate record in SECURITY.MASTER needs to be created for the Odd Lot security in order to handle odd lots. The fields in this application are used to define a security number as an odd lot. The Odd Lot field can be set as:

- YES - If the security number is an odd lot.
- NO - If the security number is not an odd lot.
- Null - If there is no instruction (the security number can be an odd lot).

If the Odd Lot field is setup, then the Odd Lot Security field must be updated with:

- The security ID of the Odd Lot security, if the Odd Lot field is set to NO (the odd lot security should have been created previously).
- The security number that is, the ID itself, if the Odd Lot field is set to YES.

The Odd Lot Units , Odd Lot Trade , Odd Lot Broker and Odd Lot Exch fields define the conditions for the trade of this odd lot:

- The trading unit of the odd lot.
- If the odd lot can be buy, sell or both.
- Which broker can trade in odd lot.
- On which stock exchange the odd lot can be traded.

When a new DIARY record is created, the Odd Lot Sec field is updated if an odd lot number is defined for the security number on which the event occurs. When the DIARY record is authorised, the Odd Lot Nom and Odd Lot Num fields in the ENTITLEMENT records are automatically updated with the nominal (if not zero) and the number of the odd lot. The Odd Lot Ref field contains the multi-value number of the security number linked to the odd lot number.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the odd lot number is equal to the security number, then this field is blank and the other set of Odd lot fields are updated in the same multi-value as the security number.

The odd lots process records are updated in the ENTITLEMENT record as shown in the below screenshot.

The odd lot can sell only if it comes from a corporate action. The Odd Lot Trade field in SECURITY.MASTER should be set to SELL or BOTH to generate a SEC.OPEN.ORDER record. The odd lot are sold if there are instructions based on the portfolio or the customer through the SC.ENT.INSTR or INVESTMENT.PROGRAM application. If there is an order to sell, then a SEC.OPEN.ORDER record is created with IHLD status from the details of the ENTITLEMENT record.

The Odd Lot Order field indicates that it is an order for an odd lot, which means that some validations are done. For example, Broker or the Exchange can be populated differently for odd lot orders. Another validation is done to check the value in the Odd Lot Consolid field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record of the Depository. If this field is set to YES, then the odd lots are consolidated at this depository. The odd lots can be sold only in the same tranches as received. If not, the odd lots can be sold as a tradable units.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Rounding, Odd Lots and Fraction Handling feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Rounding, Odd Lots and Fraction Handling feature.

### 6.39  Sale or Notice of Retension


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**

Generally, unmarketable shareholders find it difficult to sell the shares in the market. Hence, the issuer of the company comes up with events for unmar...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Corp Ref*, *Depository*, *Entitlement Amt*, *Event Type*, *Event type*, *Ex date*, *Final Debit Qty*, *Final Subscr Amt* ... +27 more
>

#### 📖 Introduction

The event is for shareholders whose holdings are unmarketable (holdings worth less than a specific quantity/value on the record date of the event). Generally, unmarketable shareholders find it difficult to sell the shares in the market. Hence, the issuer of the company comes up with events for unmarketable shareholders where the customer can:

- Retain the unmarketable parcel.
- Top-up the unmarketable parcel to marketable parcels.
- Sell the unmarketable parcel.

| Customer | Qualifying Holdings | Value of holdings on Record Date (Closing price = 0.028 USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Customer A | 14,286 | 400.01 USD |
| Customer B | 16,071 | 449.98 USD |
| Customer C | 17,678 | 494.98 USD |


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The below is the configuration for unmarketable parcel events.

The Qual Hold Chk field in DIARY.TYPE enables the creation of entitlements based on specific criteria. If this field is flagged to N or is left blank, the system generates the entitlements for all the shareholders who hold a position as on ex/record date. However, if this field is flagged to Y, the system generates the entitlements for the customers who satisfy the additional qualifying holding check criteria defined in DIARY .


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic explains the attributes required for a sale or notice of retention event.


##### Creating Event

In a sale or notice of retention and top-up facility, an existing shareholder is allowed to participate in the event, provided that the shareholding is an unmarketable holding as on ex/record date (holdings less than specific quantity/value on the ex/record date).

The holdings check criteria can be defined based on the value of the holdings or quantity of holding as described in the below table.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Qual Hold CRI | Defines the holding check criteria. If set to AMT, the entitlement generation criteria is based on the shareholder value in the event security If set to NOM, the entitlement generation criteria is based on the shareholder’s quantity in the event security |
| Qual Hold Val | Represents the shareholder value or quantity of shareholdings in the event security below which the entitlements are generated for the shareholder |
| Qual Hold Pri | Holds the price of the event security. This price is the closing price on the record rate. The price input in the field calculates the shareholder’s value in the event security when the Qual Hold CRI is set to AMT. |
| Mktble Holding | Indicates the marketable quantity. It is a system computed field and it is calculated as Qual Hold Val or Qual Hold Pri (is calculated only when Qual Hold CRI is set to AMT). The field is updated based on trading units of the SECURITY.MASTER . |


##### Creating a Diary

In the below screen, a sample DIARY is shown where a marketable parcel is defined as 500 USD. Any customer holding less than 500 USD is eligible to participate in the event.


##### Generating Entitlements

The system automatically generates the entitlements based on the criteria defined in Qual Hold Cri , Qual Hold Val and Qual Hold Pri fields.

In the above example (where, Qual Hold Cri is set to AMT, Qual Hold Val is set to 500), the system generates entitlements for shareholders, whose value in the event security on the record date is less than or equal to 500 USD.


##### Handling Elections

For the shareholders who elect to:

- Retain their holdings post the event, all of their eligible holdings ( Qualify Holdings ) are mapped to Option Nom under the Lapse option.
- Sell their holdings, the eligible holdings ( Qualify Holdings ) are mapped to Option Nom under the Sell option. For reconciliation with the custodian/registry, the quantity in Option Nom of the Sell option is mapped to the Final Debit Qty field. The Final Debit Qty is the quantity of security debited from the customer’s security account when the entitlement is authorised.
- Top-up their holdings to specific amount, the subscription amount is mapped to Opt Elect Amt under the respective subscription amount option. There is upfront debit for the top-up amount.

The customer has elected to top-up the holdings to 2000 USD (marketable parcel) as shown in the below screenshot.


##### Attributes received Post Cut-off Date

The following field valued are received post cut-off date.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Sale Price | This is mapped to the Rate field under the Sell option in DIARY . Using the Rate and Final Debit Qty , the system calculates the expected cash receivable for shareholder ( Entitlement Amt ) in the entitlements for all the customers who have elected to sell. |
| Top up Price | This is mapped to the New Price field under the top-up option. This in turn triggers the calculation of Nominal in the entitlements for all the customers who have elected to top-up. |

> **⚠️ Note:** In case of events with a Sell option, if the customer elects to sell, the quantity is blocked at the time of election.


##### Confirmation for Sale or Notice of Retention

When the price is known, the system updates the receivable amount in the ENTITLEMENT . After authorisation, the system debits the shares from the customer’s holdings and the block is removed. If the actual settlement is ON, the equivalent cash can be settled through the back office settlement application ( SC.SETTLEMENT ).


##### Confirmation for Top-up

Based on the confirmation from the registry/custodian, the entitlements of customers who have elected to top-up are reconciled. The fields Final Subscr Amt and Final Subscr Qty fields in ENTITLEMENT are used to map the confirmed allocation amount or shares. If the confirmation from the registry is based on amount, the system uses the New Price field in the Top-up option to derive the allocated nominal ( FINAL.SUBSCR.QTY ).

> 
> **Applications:** `CONSOL.UPDATE.WORK`, `DIARY`, `DIARY.TYPE`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY`, `SC.TRADING.POSITION`, `SECURITY.POSITION`, `SECURITY.TRANS`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Consol Trading Bal*, *Corp Reference*, *Depot*, *Event type*, *Ex-Date*, *New Ratio.1.1*, *Nominal*, *Old Ratio* ... +3 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In a share conversion event, a share (Stock A) is converted into another share (Stock B). This is a mandatory event where the customer holding Stock A holds Stock B on the pay date. Cash is not paid or received during this event.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The DIARY.TYPE configuration for a share conversion is shown in the below screenshot.


#### 🔧 Working With

The conversion of a share into another new share is illustrated below. One position is removed and replaced by another new position. This process is done by reference to the generated SECURITY.TRANS records, where one record handles removal and another record handles the receipt of new securities. Cash is not received or paid. The ratio of old to new usually depends upon several market factors.

A share (S/N 3615) is to be converted to a new share (S/N 5615) and the ratio of old is to new is considered based upon the market prices of the two securities. The old security is GBP 1.275 per share and new security is GBP 3.5 per share, therefore equating to approximately 2.745 old to new. Set the

field to 2.75 (rounded to the nearest value) in the

application.

The user starts with the same positions and raise an appropriate DIARY to record the conversion details.

The DIARY application is run through the service agent and the resultant ENTITLEMENT table is validated.

The number of new shares ( Nominal field) 5,454 is rounded based on original holding of 15,000 / 2.75 = 5,454.545454, which is rounded to 5,454 new shares. The ENTITLEMENT table is authorised and two SECURITY.TRANS records are generated for both old and new shares. The first SECURITY.TRANS record removes the original holding of 15,000 shares.

The second record generates the new holding of 5,454 new shares.

Now, the SECURITY.POSITION and SC.TRADING.POSITION applications are validated for both old and new shares.

As shown above, the SECURITY.POSITION application for the old share (that is now converted) is updated and shows a zero position.

The SECURITY.POSITION application for the new shares is built. The same validations are performed in the SC.TRADING.POSITION application in both securities. The SC.TRADING.POSITION application for the converted security shows a zero position.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Consol Trading Bal field is updated only during the next COB.

The SC.TRADING.POSITION application for the new security now shows a position of 5,454 new shares.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Consol Trading Bal field is not present and is updated only during the next COB.

The CONSOL.UPDATE.WORK table is validated and used during the COB to produce the required RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY records for both old and new shares.

Check the position after a COB during which the Consol Trading Bal field in both SC.TRADING.POSITION records must be updated. Now, the COB is completed and so a quick check is done whether there are two spec entries, one each for old and new positions.

The RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY record for the removal of the original share is now generated. The user must check if there is a spec entry on the receipt of new shares.

The RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY record confirms a receipt entry raised in respect to the new securities that are received. This updates the SC.TRADING.POSITION record for the new security. The SC.TRADING.POSITION application with respect to the original security (that is now converted) confirms that value is not available in the Consol Trading Bal field.

The CRF cost is transferred to the new security. As both issues are in the same currency, the CRF for the new security is also recorded as GBP 18,750.00.

The Consol Trading Bal field displays the CRF cost as 18,750.00.

A share is an indivisible unit of capital, expressing the ownership relationship between the company and the shareholder.

The denominated value of a share is its face value, and the total of the face value of issued shares represent the capital of a company which may not reflect the market value of those shares.

One share can be converted into another new share. In such a scenario, no cash is received or paid. This ratio of old share to new share depends upon several market factors.

### 6.41  Share Purchase Plan and Priority Offer


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A share purchase plan corporate action event, entitles the eligible shareholders of a company to purchase shares up to a certain value per year, usually at a discount to the current market price. The benefit of subscribing through this plan is that the eligible customers can subscribe the shares at ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Cap New Ratio*, *Cap Old Ratio*, *Corp Ref*, *Def Instruction Date*, *Def Instruction opt*, *Depot*, *ELIG.SEC.NO*, *Eligible Sec No* ... +25 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A share purchase plan corporate action event, entitles the eligible shareholders of a company to purchase shares up to a certain value per year, usually at a discount to the current market price. The benefit of subscribing through this plan is that the eligible customers can subscribe the shares at a discount from current market price without incurring brokerage and commissions.

A priority offer corporate action event, entitles eligible shareholders of a group company to get new shares in the offer of an associated company. Generally, when a company chooses to go public through Initial Public Offer (IPO), it may choose to allocate a portion of shares on a priority basis to existing shareholders of an associated company, before the shares are open to the public.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The static setup of a DIARY.TYPE share purchase plan is shown in the below screenshot. This is a voluntary corporate action event with Upfront Payment field set to Yes.

Additionally, if the Refund Allow field is set to Y, Temenos Transact processes the refund if there is a scale back due to over subscription of the offer.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details the event creation and election in voluntary subscription events where customers can choose to subscribe for specific worth of security or lapse the offer.


##### Handling Subscription based Events

In subscription events like share purchase plan (SPP) and priority offer, the eligible shareholders can participate in the event to subscribe for shares worth a certain dollar amount. This is a voluntary event with options to subscribe or lapse the offer. There could be two types of subscription events:

- Bid for minimum subscription amount or in increments up to a capped amount. Under share purchase plan, the eligible shareholders may apply for a minimum shares of worth 1000 USD or in increments worth 1000 USD up to 15000 USD. Under priority offer, the eligible shareholders of a company a can apply for a minimum shares of worth 5000 USD in company B or subscribe for shares in increments of worth 1000 USD in company B.

- Bid for one of the various subscription amounts as specified in the offer. The eligible shareholders participating in SPP may apply from one of the below options: 15,000 USD 10,000 USD 5,000 USD 2,500 USD 1,000 USD

- The eligible customers for participating in SPP and priority offer events are those who hold the particular instrument as on record date. Customers can subscribe irrespective of the quantity they currently hold. A customer holding 100 shares in security A, can subscribe for shares of worth 15000 USD under share purchase plan of security A.
- Whenever an election is made to subscribe for additional shares, the customer’s account is debited for the subscription amount (upfront debit).
- In both share purchase plan and priority offer, the allocation of shares may not be guaranteed and may be subject to scale back (refund).

The event explained below allows the eligible holders to subscribe for:

- Minimum of 1000 USD
- In increments of 1000 USD
- Maximum of 15000 USD

The below screenshot shows the DIARY creation for a SPP event with subscription is based on minimum amount, increment amount and maximum amount.

In case of priority offer, the Eligible Sec No field is multi-valued to input the eligible securities numbers. The entitlements are generated for all the customers who hold securities in any of the eligible securities.

On committing the DIARY the system creates entitlements for customers who hold the eligible security on the ex/ record date. Once the Entitlements are generated, the customers can elect until Reply by Date. The elections are recorded in the Opt Elect Amt field against the respective options. The customer can elect under only one option. When the Opt Status is set to PAID in ENTITLEMENT and the Upfront Payment is set as Y in DIARY and DIARY.TYPE , the system generates debit entries.

Once the cut off for election is over, confirmation is received for the customer’s elections. The confirmed nominal is input in the Final Subscr Amt or Final Subscr Qty field in the ENTITLEMENT . If there is a difference between Opt Elect Amt and Final Subscr Amt , the system processes the refund amount based on the settings in the Refund Allow field in DIARY.TYPE . Once the entitlement is authorised, the Option Status field is set to Completed.


##### Eligibility of Shareholders to Participate in Event in Priority Offer

In certain priority offers (where there is no ex-date), if the shareholder has held the relevant security in a period between the offer announcement date and the election cut-off date (reply by date), the customer is eligible to participate in the event.

In priority offers, purchase or sell is allowed after entitlement generation (after announcement date) where, Subscr Event and Incl Txn Post Ex fields are set to Yes in DIARY.TYPE application.

Once the DIARY is created and authorised for the priority offer event, the system generates entitlements record for all the customers holding the security on the entitlement generation date.

From the entitlement generation date till the offer cut-off date the customer can trade the eligible security. If the DIARY is rerun using the field Rerun with Retain option the following would be the system’s behaviour:

- A new entitlement is created for a customer who has purchased the event security after the entitlement generation.
- An entitlement is retained for a customer who has sold the event security after entitlement generation.

Customer A had 1000 shares at the time of announcement. Customer A is eligible to participate in the offer although the customer sold the 1000 holdings before election cut-off date (reply by date).

Customer B had no shares at the time of announcement. If the customer purchased 1000 shares subsequently before the election cut-off date (reply by date), the customer is eligible to participate in the offer. Hence, a new entitlement is created for customer B, when the

application is

with Retain option.

#### 📖 Introduction

Stamp tax is a duty levied by the federal government on financial services. Certain governments expect banks to deduct the stamp tax before remitting any consideration to the investor or customer.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configuration and workflow for stamp tax on corporate action events.


##### SC.TAX.PARAMETER

The SC.TAX.PARAMETER application is used to define the tax payable for STAMP.TAX record. Different tax rates can be applied based on the application (trade and transfer) and security, stock exchange, sub-asset type or combinations thereof.

The Tax Code field is used to define the tax code that helps to calculate the tax payable. The Tax Code field accepts either the tax code defined in the TAX application or the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application. If the user defines the Tax Code field with any defined TAX.TYPE.CONDITION record, the system calculates the tax based on the tax codes defined for the respective customer group, which is defined in the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application. If the user defines the Tax Code field with defined tax code, the system performs tax calculation based on the TAX.CODE record defined in the TAX application.


##### DIARY.TYPE

The following three fields in the DIARY.TYPE application are used for calculating stamp tax:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Stamp Calc Rtn | This field indicates the name of the routine that calculates the amount subject to the tax and updates it on the ENTITLEMENT application. Validation is not made against the routine name entered in this field. |
| Stamp Min Amt | This field contains the amount in charge of the bank. Only the stamp tax amounts which are greater than this amount are charged to the customer. |
| Stamp Cat Bk | This field indicates the category to which the stamp tax (in charge of the bank) is posted. |


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic details the related applications for tax calculation.


##### DIARY

The Stamp Tax Calc field is set to YES to calculate the stamp tax on this particular DIARY or it is set to NO to bypass the tax calculation.


##### ENTITLEMENT

The following stamp tax fields in the ENTITLEMENT application are automatically populated by the system.

- Stamp Tax Code – Indicates the tax code applied on this transaction.
- Stamp Base Amt – Specifies the amount on which the tax is calculated.
- Stamp Bk Lcy – Specifies the amount in charge of the bank.
- Stamp Sec Ccy – Holds the stamp tax amount in security currency.
- Stamp Acc Ccy – Holds the stamp tax amount in account currency.
- Stamp Loc Ccy – Holds the stamp tax amount in local currency.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Stamp Tax on Corporate Actions feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Stamp Tax on Corporate Actions feature.

#### 📖 Introduction

A stock split is a Corporate Action (CA) in which a company divides the existing shares into multiple shares to increase the liquidity of the company shares. As the number of shares increases, price per share decreases, thus making it affordable for the investors.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The event type configuration of DIARY.TYPE application for the stock split event is shown in the below screenshot.


#### 🔧 Working With

The DIARY application is used for creating actual diary events. The Event Type field links the DIARY.TYPE application that is used for the event.

The request is raised to split the current holding into several shares. As illustrated above, the holder of a share with security number 003615-000, have five shares of the same security at the end of the event. As the DIARY application is processed through the service agent, the ENTITLEMENT records must be authorised to ensure that the nominal amounts are increased five times.

The new security is a new issue. In addition, the Consol Trading Bal field of the old security must be transferred to the new security upon completion of the resulting COB. Before authorising any ENTITLEMENT records, a screenshot of the old security SC.TRADING.POSITION is required to obtain the Central Reporting Files (CRF) amount from the Consol Trading Bal field.

The ENTITLEMENT record is split into two extracts and displays the qualifying holding as 15,000 and the expected new shares as 75,000. Cash is not involved in this activity.

This is a mandatory event, hence the user is not required to provide an election, so the ENTITLEMENT records can be authorised. Then the system must build the required CONSOL.UPDATE.WORK table that is used to build the CRF movements during COB. These are necessary to move the accounting cost from the old position to the new position.

The debit (DR) and credit (CR) entries agree as expected. Now, backup the system and run the COB to ensure the value in the Consol Trading Bal field is updated. When COB is completed, check the SC.TRADING.POSITION and SECURITY.POSITION applications for both old and new securities. The position in the old security which is standardised as expected is shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Consol Trading Bal field is cleared during the COB and the value previously reported in this field must be moved to the new security.

The new security position now contains the correct data and the Consol Trading Bal field is populated with the value that previously belonged to the old security. All the fields are cleared in the SECURITY.POSITION application for the old security.

The SECURITY.POSITION application for the new security is shown in the below screenshot. The data is transferred to the relative fields exactly as it appeared in old security position.

As it is a stock split event in which the term involved 1:5 split, the new position in the Closing Bal No Nom field is increased from 15,000 to the 75,000 (as shown in the above screenshot).


#### 📋 Tasks

A stock split is a corporate action in which a company divides its existing shares into multiple shares.

Basically, companies choose to split their shares so they can lower the trading price of their stock to a range deemed comfortable by most investors and increase liquidity of the shares.

The most common split ratios are 2-for-1 or 3-for-1, which means that the stockholder have two or three shares, respectively, for every share held earlier.

>
