> 
> **Applications:** `DIARY`, `ENTITLEMENT`, `SC.PRE.DIARY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Consol Trading Bal*, *Corp Ref*, *Current Position*, *Def Opt*, *Elected Nom*, *Ent Amt Settle Ccy*, *Event Type*, *Int Elected Date* ... +15 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This feature is about the takeover corporate action event and how it is handled in Temenos Transact .

A takeover occurs when one company makes a bid to assume control of or acquire another company, often by purchasing a majority stake in the target company. In the takeover process, the company making the bid is the acquirer (predator), while the company it wishes to take control is called the target.

There can be several types of takeover, like:

- Shares in the predator company received in lieu of shares held in the company being taken over.
- Shares in the predator company along with the cash-in-lieu of shares held in the company being taken over.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The DIARY.TYPE application is setup for takeover event.


##### Configuring Takeover with Multiple Settlements

The Multiple Sett field in DIARY.TYPE record of takeover should be set to Yes.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details about the how the takeover is handled in the following cases:

- Predator Shares not Held
- Holding in both Predator and Target Shares


##### Type 1 - Predator Shares not Held

The details pertaining to the terms of the takeover as offered by the predator company is setup in the DIARY application.

A customer with 15,000 shares in the security number 003615-000 is setup. The terms are offered to comprise two new shares in the predator company for every 9.5 units of the existing shares that is held. As 15,000 shares are held, the current holding is calculated after some rounding.

The DIARY record is authorised and processed through the service agent to obtain the ENTITLEMENT record that is shown in the below screenshot.

The new shares are calculated as:

For example, 15,000 / 9.50 x 2 = 3,158 new shares.

The underlying DIARY.TYPE record specifies that standard rounding should be used. Options are not associated with the takeover corporate action, so the user can only authorise the record and check if the updation is performed correctly. In this case, the underlying cost should switch to the new holding irrespective of the current market value of the new share.

The ENTITLEMENT record is authorised and the new SECURITY.POSITION is created as shown in the below screenshot.

The position is updated to include the expected 3,158 new shares. The main fields from the old record are transferred to populate the same fields on the new position. The SC.TRADING.POSITION record for this security is updated to include the expected 3,158 new shares in the Current Position field ,as shown in the below screenshot.

The CONSOL.UPDATE.WORK record is built for the corporate action before running the COB.

The debit and credit movements are the same as the cost of position is transferred from the legacy position to the new position.

The position for the source security is regularised in the SC.TRADING.POSITION record.

The Consol Trading Bal field is also blank, as the original value must be transferred to the new security. If the new position is regularised, it includes the newly updated Consol Trading Bal field which is built using the cost of the source security position. The SC.TRADING.POSITION record of the new security is generated as shown in the below screenshot.

The new security position is regularised correctly in the SECURITY.POSITION and SC.TRADING.POSITION records, therefore it is assumed that the takeover has happened appropriately.


##### Type 2 - Holding in both Predator and Target Shares

In this case, the dealer book has a holding in both companies involved in the takeover. Under normal circumstances, it is believed that the two companies merge to form a new company. If this is the case, then in a real world situation it is not possible to set up a DIARY record to combine two holdings into one new holding, due to the different ratios of new for old. Instead, the process requires two separate DIARY records that can be done by the system.

The user can recreate the initial takeover, but in this instance the target company share is incorporated into the existing share holdings issued by the predator company. The user must first create the holding in the predator company shares, then run a COB to ensure that both predator and target share positions have their related Central Reporting Files (CRF) amounts stored in the SC.TRADING.POSITION record. After creation, the system uses a takeover diary record with options and the ability to take shares plus a minimal amount of cash or only cash.

The DIARY record shows that the offer comprises either:

- straight cash offer of 1.30 per share held or
- new shares at a rate of one new share for every 1.55 old share and the cash of 0.15 per share

Run the DIARY record through the service agent to build the ENTITLEMENT record for the shareholder.

This ENTITLEMENT is completed manually before examining the remainder of the transaction. After the setup is completed, the takeover is calculated.

Takeover = 10,186 new shares in security 003618-000 (holding 15,791/1.55 = 10,188) + cash of 2,368.35 (15,789 * 0.15) + cash of 2.60 for the odd shares (2 *1.30)

The original holding removed due to the takeover is also found in the security 003615-000. The original holding is not displayed until the ENTITLEMENT record is authorised.Once the ENTITLEMENT record is authorised, the resultant SC.TRADING.POSITION record is generated with the source security belonging to the target company (company being taken over). As shown in the below screenshot, the value in the Current Position field confirms that the holding is taken over and the value in Consol Trading Bal field remains the same. This field requires the running of the next COB before being regularised.

After validating the target share position, the predator position is checked to review if the number of shares has increased by the expected number of new shares (in this case, 10,186 new shares).

The above position confirms the holding at 45,186 shares. This comprises of 15,791 originally held old shares, which were taken over by the predator company for which new shares were offered at a rate of one new for every 1.55 old.

- User requested : 15,789 / 1.55 = 10,186
- Current holding predator share : 35,000
- New position : 45,186

As a result of the corporate action, 2,370.95 cash is received. This cash amount can be checked to ensure if it was posted by locating the relative STMT.ENTRY application or by checking the coupon suspense account. The user can do this by invoking the standard enquiry Stmt Ent Book and by specifying the coupon suspense account ID together with the relevant booking date, that is, the system date.

The cash received is 2,370.95 as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** Normal Temenos Transact practice requires the expected dividend to remain on suspense until the actual cash dividend on nostro is available.

Further, when the SC.TRADING.POSITION record is referred the cost of position is updated as follows:

- Original cost of predator holding : 75,025.00
- Original cost of target position : 19,659.65


##### Handling Multiple Settlements in a Takeover Event

Takeover events in some markets run for more than six months. During this period, the shareholders can choose to tender the shares multiple times during the offer period. New shareholders can also purchase the shares from market and participate in the event.

Consider a takeover event, where the offer opens for election from December 22, 2009. Let us assume the takeover price is 3 USD per share. For the customers who elect to tender the shares, the shares are disposed and the proceeds are paid within five days.

For the above event, the DIARY has the following details.

Once the DIARY is authorised, entitlements are created for all the customers. Below ENTITLEMENT is generated for customer 600001-1, holding 1200 nominal.

The customer can elect to tender the shares by inputting the tender quantity in Elected Nom field. Once the it is updated, system automatically updates the elected date and the expected proceeds in the Int Elected Date and Int Entitlement Amt , respectively. If the first election is partially instructed quantity, the remaining quantity is updated in the Pending Nom field. The status after the first election is changed to Interim.Elected.

For each tender, when the ENTITLEMENT is authorised with status as Interim.Elected, the system generates a SC.SETTLEMENT record (in IHLD) with the pending cash and stock to be settled. When the proceeds are received, the respective SC.SETTLEMENT record is authorised. The customer can again tender the remaining shares by inputting the quantity in Elected Nom field. A new SC.SETTLEMENT record is created for the second election. On the cut-off date, the quantity in the pending nominal is moved under the default option and the Status in ENTITLEMENT is marked as Completed.


##### Takeover with Incentives

In a takeover bid, the company informs the investors to avail Solicitation Fee (SOFE) and Early solicitation fee (ESOF) in addition to the applicable tender amount (OFFR).

Temenos Transact captures these rates from incoming MT564 in SC.PRE.DIARY and DIARY . It uses the rates to calculate the fee amount per entitlement. The system updates the calculated fee or premium in each ENTITLEMENT . Consideration amount of an entitlement is calculated as below.

For Tender or Takeover event, when the system receives a message with SOFE and ESOF along with OFFR, it captures the code and values in Rate Code and Rate Value of SC.PRE.DIARY for further processing.

When the system receives multiple cash moves for tender event, the system captures these rates defined in each cash move.

A record is created in SC.PRE.DIARY as shown below.

During the processing of MT564 with these rates, the system creates diary record with OFFR, SOFE, and ESOF values in the multi-value set corresponding to Rate Code and Rate Value .

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Sys Calc Rate Amt | Holds the system calculated amount for reference. |
| Rate Amount | Holds the calculated amount for each qualifier (OFFR/SOFE/ESOF). The user can further amend the value, if required. |
| Ent Amt Settle Ccy | Holds the total value of rate amount for each qualifier applicable. |


#### 📋 Tasks

A Takeover occurs when one company makes a bid to assume control of or acquire another company, often by purchasing a majority stake in the target company.


##### Workflow

This section helps the user to perform the below tasks:

This enquiry helps the user to create tender.

1. Create Tender with Incentive .
2. In the Tender with Incentives screen, enter values in the following fields: Security Event Type Record Date Corp Ref
3. In the Option Details tab, enter values in the following fields Option Desc Option Ind Opt No Def Opt Rate Code Rate Value
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon to submit the record.

| List of Entitlements | In the List of Tender with Incentives screen, Click View Ent to view the details of the entitlement. Click the Edit Ent to edit the entitlement. Click the View Diary to view the details of the diary. |

> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This feature discusses about the procedures for setting tax in Corporate Actions (CA). This feature also explains how taxes are calculated for joint portfolios.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Customers may have to pay taxes on the gross amount of some CAs. Temenos Transact calculates and stores the amount of taxes.


##### Global Process

The following diagram summarises the tax-related applications and conditions in Temenos Transact.


##### CONDITION.PRIORITY

The CONDITION.PRIORITY application allows the user to define the data elements that are used in segregating the customers into customer tax groups and also define the priority selection when more than one condition is satisfied. Only fields from the application defined in the Apps Allowed field can be used in the Priority Item field. The system refers the CUSTOMER or FATCA.CUSTOMER.SUPPLEMENTARY.INFO application to define the Priority Item . The highest priority is given to the residence of the customer.

Assume that a customer falls under the following two tax groups (based on

):

- Group 1 – Residence equals US
- Group 2 – Nationality equals IN

The system automatically considers the Group 1 tax rates as the highest priority is given to residence.


##### TAX.TYPE

The TAX.TYPE application allows to define the type of taxes that may be calculated within Temenos Transact . As many TAX.TYPE can be defined, conditions for applying a tax for a given set of customers are specified in the TAX.GEN.CONDITION application and the actual tax rates for the group are defined in the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application. Both TAX.GEN.CONDITION and TAX.TYPE.CONDITION IDs are prefixed with the TAX.TYPE ID.

In case of joint portfolios, certain countries have regulations to report the income split and the respective tax among joint holders. To cater this, the Highest Tax and Apply Split fields are used, where tax has to be calculated on the split income among the joint holders of a contract. The Apply Split field is used to parameterise whether tax split can be applied for a specific tax type or not. The tax split is based on ownership percentage defined in CUSTOMER.RELATIONSHIP table.

Customers A and B are joint customers with customer A being the primary owner. The ratio of split is 40% and 60% of the income and tax thereof. The

field is set to Yes in the

application.

- Customer A has WHT TAX.TYPE with tax of 10%.
- Customer B has WHT TAX.TYPE with tax of 35%.

Total income for the portfolio: 1000

- A’s tax amount: 400 (income split) * 10/100 = 40
- B’s tax amount: 600 (income split) * 35/100 = 210

The Highest Tax field picks the tax that has highest percentage and applies that to all the customers of the group.

Customers A and B are joint customers with customer A being the primary owner. The ratio of split is 40% and 60% of the income and tax thereof. The

field is set to Yes in the

application.

- Customer A has WHT TAX.TYPE with tax of 10%.
- Customer B has WHT TAX.TYPE with tax of 35%.

Total income for the portfolio: 1000

- A’s tax amount: 400 (income split) * 35/100 = 140
- B’s tax amount: 600 (income split) * 35/100 = 210


##### TAX.GEN.CONDITION

The TAX.GEN.CONDITION application takes all the conditions in the CONDITION.PRIORITY application to define groups.

In the following screenshot, all customers with residence as US are grouped under customer tax group 008.

> **⚠️ Note:** WHT refers to TAX.TYPE.


##### CUSTOMER.CHARGE

For the tax to be defaulted in any event, the customer group must first get defaulted in CUSTOMER.CHARGE . Whenever a record in TAX.GEN.CONDITION application is defined and a CUSTOMER record is created, the customer is evaluated for each TAX.GEN.CONDITION and the respective group gets defaulted (for the applicable group) in the Tax Default Group field. In CUSTOMER.CHARGE , there is customer group for each TAX.TYPE . The TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application links the applicable rate to the customer through the CUSTOMER.CHARGE application.

In the CUSTOMER.CHARGE application, the default group can be overridden using the value in the Tax Actual Group field.


##### TAX

The TAX application holds the various tax rates and the respective category code to be credited with the calculated tax.


##### TAX.TYPE.CONDITION

The TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application links the customer group to the tax, thus enabling the system to calculate different levels of tax depending on the type of customer. Using TAX.TYPE.CONDITION, the user can define tax rates for combinations of customer groups and contract groups. Contract groups can be formed using the APPL.GEN.CONDITION application and for the combination of customer tax group and contract group (sub value), a TAX record can be attached. The following screenshot demonstrates a WHT record with

- The Cust Tax Grp field based on the static data as defined in CONDITION.PRIORITY and TAX.GEN.CONDITION
- The Contract Group field based on the transaction level attribute, which depends on the group formed using APPL.GEN.CONDITION. For customers falling under tax group 008 and if the customer falls under a particular contract group (for example, 022) during a transaction, then a WHT tax of 10% is charged. If the customer does not fall under any contract group, then a WHT tax of 35% is charged.


##### APPL.GEN.CONDITION

This application can be used to allocate group codes based on a number of defined conditions for any application in Temenos Transact .

Consider the following record is created for

in

where the depository 100472 falls under the contract group 022 and the depository 100492 falls under the contract group 044. The same group is attached under contract group in

as shown in the above screenshot.


##### CA Taxation

There are two possible ways of taxation:

- COUPON.TAX.CODE
- TXN.TAX.CODE

The COUPON.TAX.CODE application records the source and local tax rates applicable for a security. Source tax is the tax withheld by the custodian, the income received is net amount and the tax setup is done only for reporting purposes. Local tax is the tax withheld by the bank. The income received from the custodian is gross income, bank withholds the tax and pays the net income to the customer. The bank has to remit the tax to the tax authorities.

The screenshot shown below shows the setup of a COUPON.TAX.CODE application. The user can either enter a TAX or TAX.TYPE.CONDITION record in the Src Bonds Tax, Local Bonds Tax, Src Share Tax and Local Share Tax fields. When a TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application is used, the tax rate depends on the rules setup in the CONDITION.PRIORITY , TAX.GEN.CONDITION and TAX.TYPE.CONDITION applications.

The Source Tax Cust and Local Tax Cust fields specify whether the conditions are applicable to the customer or depository when calculating source tax and local tax based on the rules defined in the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application. When set to Depository, the system refers the tax group of the depository to define the source and local tax percentage. For some CAs, the customer can recover a part of the tax paid. The Recoverable Share Tax and Recoverable Bond Tax fields hold the recoverable tax code, which is either a valid tax code identifying a specific tax record from the TAX application or the key of a specific record on the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application.

The Coupon Tax code field in the SECURITY.MASTER application holds the record in COUPON.TAX.CODE applicable for the corresponding security type. The following screenshot shows the SECURITY.MASTER application updated with a record in COUPON.TAX.CODE .

> **⚠️ Note:** Whenever the Coupon Tax code field is set for SECURITY.MASTER , the Source Tax Code and Local Tax code fields in the DIARY application is populated with the respective tax codes.

The TXN.TAX.CODE application can also be used to configure taxes, in addition to COUPON.TAX.CODE . The TXN.TAX.CODE application holds the tax that is to be charged for a particular application or event. This record is attached to the SC Tax Code field in the SECURITY.MASTER application. Both TXN.TAX.CODE and COUPON.TAX.CODE can coexist for a contract and has no impact on each other. The Txn Applic field displays the application on which the tax is applied and the Trans Type field indicates for what kind of transaction.

For

, in case of SEL, a WHT tax is applied, and in case of BUY, tax is not applicable. In case of cash dividend event, WHT tax is applied. When a cash dividend event takes place for that security, the system defaults the corresponding tax type in the

field in

automatically.

> **⚠️ Note:** Whenever the SC Tax code field is set for a SECURITY.MASTER , the Sc Tax Code and Sc Tax Type fields in DIARY are populated with the respective tax code and tax type associated with the event. The Source Or Local field in DIARY allows the user to define whether the tax is a source or local tax.


##### Configuring Notional Dividend

The below setup is done for taxation of income from US securities under Section 871(m). The Swift Caev field is set to TNDP in the notional dividend event type. When an MT564 is received with this CAEV, a record in SC.PRE.DIARY is created for this notional dividend event type where there are no proceeds but withholding tax is calculated and accounted.

The Supp Ent Proceeds field in DIARY.TYPE controls the generation of accounting entries for the income amount on the customer side and Nostro side for the income portion. If set to N, then accounting entries are not generated for the dividend amount. When an MT564 is received with CAEV=TNDP, this event is created in SC.PRE.DIARY application.

When the user is creating the NOTIONAL.DIV record in DIARY.TYPE manually, the system checks if the instrument is eligible for taxation under Section 871(m) using the Tax Non Dist Proceeds flag in SECURITY.MASTER . If ineligible ( Tax Non Dist Proceeds field in SECURITY.MASTER field set to N), the system raises an override. The eligibility check is not done when MT564 is received.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details about the three main procedures for tax calculation in Corporate Actions (CA).


##### Corporate Action Taxation

The CA taxation calculation is performed in the following two applications: DIARY and ENTITLEMENT .

Temenos Transact calculates the tax amount only on the taxable part of the income specified in the SC.PRE.DIARY or DIARY application. There is a provision in the system to divide the income into taxable part and exempt part. The system applies the source and local tax on the taxable part only. The following rate-related fields in the DIARY application are used in tax calculation.

- Taxable Rate – Denotes the taxable rate of dividend or coupon. Either it can be an absolute rate or a percentage (based on the Percentage field, which can be set to Yes or No).
- Tax Exempt Rate – Denotes the tax exempt rate of dividend or coupon. Either it can be an absolute rate or a percentage (based on the Percentage field, which can be set to Yes or No).
- Rate – Denotes the sum of taxable rate and tax exempt rate. Alternatively, if one rate is entered, the system derives the other rate based on RATE provided.

If the total income is USD 3000 and tax needs to be applied only on USD 1000, then it can be specified in the

or

application using the

and

fields.

The Rate field is set to 3.00, the Taxable Rate field is set to 1.00 and the Tax Exempt Rate field is set to 2.00. The Coupon Tax Code is configured and set for the contract, which in turn defaults the Source Tax Code and Local Tax Code fields at the DIARY level. As the Local Tax Code field is defined as 99 ( TAX record), its percentage is displayed in the DIARY application. However, the applicable rate of Source Tax Code is defined in the ENTITLEMENT application, as the Source Tax Code is defined as a TAX.TYPE.CONDITION and this taxation is at the customer level.

The source and local tax are calculated only on the taxable part of the income.

As in the above example, only USD 1000 of the total income is qualified for tax entitlement amount.


##### Multiple User-defined Taxes

In addition to the taxes defined above, the CA module also allows multiple user-defined taxes to be included in the transactions. Multiple taxes can be defined at the transaction level by multi-valuing the SC Tax Code field manually or as a static setup by multi-valuing the SC Tax Code field in SECURITY.MASTER . The taxes to be levied are defined in the DIARY application and defaulted into the records created in ENTITLEMENT . These user-defined taxes can be either source or local taxes depending on the Source Or Local field in DIARY . By default, these taxes are considered to be local. Multiple taxes can be set up for an event as shown in the following screenshot.

The record in ENTITLEMENT has values defaulted from the DIARY application as shown in the following screenshot.

In case of taxes deducted at source, there is a possibility of excess tax deduction by the paying agent who may not be aware of the exemption details of the customer. In such cases, the bank deducts less tax before making the payment to the customer and then claims a refund from the authorities for the excess tax deducted. This is handled in the ENTITLEMENT application by entering the excess tax manually in the Source Tax Adj Amount field. This field allows the input only for taxes deducted at source. The adjusted amount is posted to the tax adjustment category defined in the DIARY.TYPE application. A record in ENTITLEMENT with tax adjustment is shown in the following screenshot:

The Tax Adj Category field is defined in DIARY.TYPE as shown in the following screenshot.


##### Recoverable Tax

For some CAs, the customer can recover a part of the tax paid. This recoverable tax amount is for information purposes and accounting entries are not generated. The Coupon Tax Code field in SECURITY.MASTER defines the source, local and recoverable taxes applicable for each security type. At the DIARY level, the Rcvbl Tax Code field is defaulted automatically when the event is taxable and the Rate Type field is set to GROSS. However, the user can enter a new tax code, if required.

At the ENTITLEMENT level, the tax rate is defaulted from the DIARY record and the recoverable tax amounts in Reference Currency, Local Currency and the Instrument Currency are generated.

These amounts are recalculated if the entitlement amount, nominal or the tax percentage are modified.

> **⚠️ Note:** The tax amounts are for information purposes only and used for reporting; however, accounting entries are not generated.


##### Tax Credits on Corporate Actions

A tax credit is defined as the difference between the gross dividend or interest amount declared and the net dividend or interest amount paid or the withholding at source, regardless of how the dividend or interest is declared.

> **⚠️ Note:** This requirement pertains only to UK securities but is not limited to just funds or unit trusts.

Tax credit tracking is required for the regular dividends and the income portion of unit trust distributions. Temenos Transact currently supports tax credit processing for cash and stock movements. The value displayed in the Tax Price field in the DIARY application is the price that is used to ascertain the cash value of a stock dividend.

When the records in ENTITLEMENT are generated in INAU status, that is, after the user enters a value in the Options field, the Source Tax Amount , Local Tax Amount and Tax Credit fields are reflected for each and every option. When the Rate Type field is set to Gross in the DIARY application, the values for the Opt Source Tax and Opt Local Tax fields are calculated for each option. A record in ENTITLEMENT created for the above DIARY record is shown in the following screenshot.

If the Rate Type field is set to Net in the DIARY application, the Opt Tax Credit field is updated.

> **⚠️ Note:** The above fields are only for information purposes and does not impact accounting. Accounting is driven by the existing Source Tax and Local Tax fields in the ENTITLEMENT application.


##### Tax Split for Joint Portfolios

In case of joint portfolios where the tax split needs to be shown, ensure that the TAX.TYPE is set up as shown in the configuration section. In addition, the CUSTOMER.RELATIONSHIP table should be configured for the joint portfolio defining the ownership percentage and the same needs to be linked to the Customer Relationship Id field in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application.

The following screenshot shows the CUSTOMER.RELATIONSHIP table of the joint portfolio.

A CA event occurs where the shareholders receive a cash dividend of USD 5. The following screenshot shows the DIARY record where the Source Tax code and Local Tax code are automatically defaulted based on the Coupon Tax code record in the Coupon Tax Code field set in SECURITY.MASTER .

The following screenshot shows the record in ENTITLEMENT for the joint portfolio.

Once the above record is authorised, the system updates the ST.TAX.REPORT.DETAILS application. This application stores customer-wise tax details against a single transaction. The Source Tax Amount in ENTITLEMENT is calculated based on the tax split. The following screenshot shows the ST.TAX.REPORT.DETAILS application.


##### Accounting Entries

When taxes are applicable for a corporate action event, the following accounting entries are generated when an ENTITLEMENT is authorised.

Consider that the COUPON.TAX.CODE is set for a security to define the source and local tax. A Cash Dividend event of USD 5 is announced. The portfolio is entitled to receive gross amount of USD 6000. The source tax is 10% and the local tax is 20%.

There are two ways entries can be generated.

Case 1 – The Source Tax Split and Local Tax Split fields are set to Yes in COUPON.TAX.CODE .

If tax split is required, then the entries are generated as shown in the following screenshot. Customer account is credited with the gross amount of USD 6000, and debited with USD 1200 for local tax and USD 600 for source tax amount.

Case 2 – The Source Tax Split and Local Tax Split fields are set to No in COUPON.TAX.CODE .

If tax split is not required, then the entries are generated as shown in the following screenshot. The customer account is credited with net amount of USD 4200 (Gross amount - source tax amount - local tax amount).

Consider that the SC Tax Code field is set for a security to define the source and local tax. A Cash Dividend event of USD 5 is announced. The portfolio is entitled to receive a gross amount of USD 6000.

The entries are generated as shown in the following screenshot. The customer account is credited with net amount of USD 4200.


##### Adjusting Tax after Authorisation of Entitlement

Tax can be adjusted after the event by using the SC.ADJ.TXN.UPDATE application. The SC.ADJ.TXN.UPDATE application is used to adjust the withholding income or tax rate of the entitlement transaction and create the FUNDS.TRANSFER record for the overall adjusted amount based on the parameters set in the SC.WHT.ADJ.PARAM application. The user needs to enter the values in the Customer and the Transaction Ref fields for which tax needs to be adjusted. The Adj Type field can be set to Over or Under. If the Adj Type field is set to Over, then the system debits the Reimb Tax Acct Cat and credits the Reimb Cu Account , and if set to Under, then the system credits the Reimb Tax Acct Cat and debits the Reimb Cu Account .

The New Wht Income field holds the new withholdable income on which new tax based on New Tax Rate is calculated and populated in the New Tax Txn Ccy field.

After the above record is authorised, the system generates a record in FUNDS.TRANSFER which is stored in the Transaction Ref field. The following screenshot shows the record in FUNDS.TRANSFER for the above transaction.


##### Withholding Tax based on Notional Proceeds

The Section 871(m) of US tax regulation requires the banks to process withholding tax on notional income, based on information received by custodian (through SWIFT or manual). The following are the two types of withholding processing:

- Withholding tax calculation and accounting, when bank is the withholding agent (local tax)
- Withholding tax calculation and no accounting entries on the customer’s account, when the issuer is the withholding agent and tax is withheld at source (source tax)

The Tax Non Dist Proceeds field in SECURITY.MASTER identifies the instruments which are eligible for taxation under this regulation.

The below section explains withholding tax calculation and accounting through the notional corporate action events.

If the issuer is the withholding agent, the tax is withheld at source. The system calculates and displays withholding tax for the eligible customers. The tax rate (source tax) in this case, is a default percentage applied on the notional gross dividend amount, for example 30%. For each tax type in TXN.TAX.CODE , customers with similar static attributes are grouped together. Once the customers are grouped, each group can be assigned a tax rate. This is set up through the TAX.TYPE.CONDITION application. For example, US residents can be taxed at 35% while non-US residents can be taxed at 10%. This is achieved by linking a TAX record to the group.

1. After setting up the tax conditions and the tax rates , these are linked to the transaction and then to the instrument. The TXN.TAX.CODE application is used to link the transactions to the TXN.TAX.CODE application
2. The final step is linking the TAX.TYPE to the instrument. The record in TXN.TAX.CODE is linked to the instrument through the SC Tax Code field in SECURITY.MASTER .

For transaction processing, the below steps are done by the system

1. Where the issuer is acting as the withholding agent (tax withheld at source), MT564 is not received. The user creates the Diary manually (by setting TNDP in the DIARY.TYPE application ) with the event and tax information. The SC Tax Code defaults the TXN.TAX.CODE attached to the SECURITY.MASTER of the event security.
2. If Supp Ent Proceeds field is set to N in DIARY.TYPE , there are no accounting entries for the dividend amount and source tax amount. However, the tax amount is displayed in the ENTITLEMENT .

Where bank acts as the withholding agent, an MT564 is received (when Swift Caev is set to TNDP ) from the custodian. When the message is received, the system creates a record in SC.PRE.DIARY with the event type for notional dividend. The Dividend Equivalent Payment (DEP) per share is mapped to Rate field.

If Supp Ent Proceeds field is set to N in DIARY.TYPE , then the system does not post the accounting for the dividend amount ( Net Amt Acc Curr field in ENTITLEMENT ). However, the system posts accounting entries for the taxable amount in Local Tax Amt in the ENTITLEMENT .

Consider a customer who has an eligible holding of 1000 units.

Taxable Basis = Eligible holdings * DEP =

that is, QUALIFY.HOLDINGS * RATE

=1000*0.5= $500

If the customer is applied a tax rate of 10%, the total tax is calculated as:

Withholding Tax = Taxable Basis * Tax rate

= $500*10% = $50.

The accounting entries where bank is acting as the withholding agent is shown below.

• Debit (Dr) Customer account - $50

• Credit (Cr) Tax Account - $50

> **⚠️ Note:** The debit of the tax amount (in case where the bank is the withholding agent), is in the customer’s account currency. If the customer’s account currency is different from the security currency, then the customer account is debited in the account currency and is converted to security currency using the latest exchange rate available in the system.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Tax in Corporate Actions feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Tax in Corporate Actions feature.

### 6.46  InstrumentMaster


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The instrument master or securities master is a record of all the instruments that are available for trading in the system. Securities can be broadly categorised into equities and debts. However, the system can support different types of securities including equities, fixed income, debt, funds, note...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The instrument master or securities master is a record of all the instruments that are available for trading in the system. Securities can be broadly categorised into equities and debts. However, the system can support different types of securities including equities, fixed income, debt, funds, notes and so on. Each type of instrument has unique attributes.

In Temenos Transact , all attributes of different instruments are captured in the SECURITY.MASTER application. This feature describes the creation of the securities master and the underlying tables required to support the creation.

### 7.1  Bilateral Cancellation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Under the CSDR regulation, matched instructions cannot be settled unilaterally. This means that matched instructions can only be cancelled if both counterparties request a cancellation of their instructions. Until the cancellation confirmation is received from the market, the instruction remains eli...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Bilateral Canc*, *Canc Deliv Ref*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Under the CSDR regulation, matched instructions cannot be settled unilaterally. This means that matched instructions can only be cancelled if both counterparties request a cancellation of their instructions. Until the cancellation confirmation is received from the market, the instruction remains eligible for settlement.

When the counterparty has requested a cancellation of a matched transaction, the central securities depositories (CSD) informs the bank of the pending cancellation request. In case of cancellation initiated by the counterparty, the account owner can accept (send MT54X cancellation) or ignore the request. When the bank has requested a cancellation of a matched transaction, the CSD informs the bank of:

- The status of the cancellation request
- Acceptance of cancellation by the counterparty once received

Upon receipt of the cancellation request, an MT548 is triggered (from the custodian) in the following format.

:23G::INST :25D::IPRC//CANP :24B::CANP//CONF

It denotes ‘The cancellation request that has been sent has not been executed yet. It is pending. Your counterparty must also cancel their trade and we are waiting for the confirmation it is done’. Simultaneously, another MT548 is triggered to the counterparty acknowledging the cancellation request. :23G::INST :25D::IPRC//CPRC

It denotes ‘A cancellation request from your counterparty for this instruction is pending waiting for your cancellation request.’ Once both counterparties have sent cancellation messages, the instruction is immediately cancelled and reported accordingly through MT548 in the Tag IPRC//CAND.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The depositories for which bilateral cancellation is applicable must be defined in the SC.CSDR.PARAMETER application. The Bilateral Canc field is flagged as Yes for the depositories where the bilateral cancellation is applicable.

Bilateral cancellation is enabled for both depositories 100492 and 100472 in the screenshot below.


#### 🔧 Working With

A security transaction is placed in the system as shown below.

Trade confirmation messages are sent to the depository, after the transaction is authorised. MT541 is sent to the depository.

To initiate a cancellation, a record is created in the SC.INST.CANCEL table for the transaction. The Request Cancel field is set to Yes.

After the record is authorised, CANC message is sent to the custodian for the previous instruction sent. The delivery reference of the CANC message is recorded in the Canc Deliv Ref field. The message status is updated as Cancelation Initiated.

The transaction is cancelled in the system only on receipt of MT548 confirming the bilateral cancellation.

On receipt of MT548 from the depository with status CAND, message status in the table SC.INST.CANCEL is changed to Cancellation Accepted.

The record in SEC.TRADE is automatically reversed by the system.

> **⚠️ Note:** The settlement record in hold is automatically deleted by the system.


#### 📋 Tasks

Under the regulation, matched instructions cannot be settled unilaterally. The matched instructions can be cancelled if both counterparties request a cancellation of their instructions. Until the cancellation confirmation is received from the market, the instruction remains eligible for settlement.

2. Click the Send Cancel Instr button.

2. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
3. Click the Commit icon to send the instruction.

To view a trade or transfer, follow the below steps:

### 7.2  Hold and Release


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Hold and release mechanism enables users to hold back or release instructions for settlement, while allowing matching to take place.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Depo Advice*, *Depo Advice Reqd*, *Hold Req*, *Hold Request*, *MT530 Hold Rel*, *Release Req*, *Sett Txn Type*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Hold and release mechanism enables users to hold back or release instructions for settlement, while allowing matching to take place.

Temenos Transact has the capability to allow a user to put an instruction on hold and release it again later at any stage in the instruction life cycle before the transaction has settled.

By setting an instruction to ‘on hold’, the system undergoes a matching process but is not eligible for settlement until both parties have released their respective settlement instructions. Such ‘On hold instructions’ that fail to settle on the intended settlement date are subject to penalties.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

There are two scenarios in hold and release:

- Released instruction that is on hold
- On hold original instruction

In Temenos Transact, these functionalities can be handled through MT541 or MT543 or through MT530. The MT530 Hold Rel field indicates whether the Hold and Release is handled through MT530 or the other method.

In this scenario, an instruction (MT541 or MT543) is first released (Function: NEWM) once the transaction is placed in the system. A security transaction is placed in the system as shown below.

Trade confirmation message is triggered to the depository. In this case, MT541 is triggered to the depository.

After the transaction is authorised, the settlement record is created on hold.

The record in SC.MATCH.QUEUE is created on hold for the transaction.

To hold an instruction with a release status, a hold request must be sent. To trigger a hold instruction, a record is created for the transaction in the SC.INST.HOLD.REL application. The Hold Req field is set to Yes.

After the record is authorised, the status of the record is updated as Hold Requested.

A Hold request (MT540-MT543) with function PREA in 23G (with other contents being same as MT540-543 NEWM) is sent to depository as shown below.

An MT548 (Tag 22F::SETR//PREA) message is received from the depository to confirm that the transaction is on hold. The Sett Txn Type field in SC.MT548.MATCH.QUEUE is updated with SETR/PREA status, indicating that the transaction is on hold and not eligible for settlement.

By setting an instruction to ‘on hold’, the instruction is not eligible for settlement until both parties have released their respective settlement instructions. The settlement with on hold status (SC.MT548.TXN.HOLD) enquiry lists all the transactions that are on hold.

To release an instruction on hold, a record is created for the transaction in the SC.INST.HOLD.REL application. The Release Req field is set to Yes.

On authorisation of the record, the status of the record is updated as Release Requested.

A NEWM (MT540-MT543) message is generated and sent to the depository.

The settlements pending with the counterparty to release (SC.MT548.PEND.RELE.FROM.CPTY) enquiry lists all the transactions that are released from the system but pending release from the counterparty.

The instruction put on hold could have been released from the system but pending from the counterparty side. In this case, an MT548 is received with Tag 22F::SETR/TRAD (denoting released) but pending counterparty release (24B Reason PEND/PRCY). The status of the record is updated as Release Pending.

After both parties have released the hold, MT548 with PEND//FUTU in tag 24B is received. On receipt of MT548 (PEND//FUTU), the status of the record in SC.INST.HOLD.REL is updated as Released.

The Sett Txn Type field is changed to SETR/TRAD, indicating that the trade is ready for settlement.

In some scenarios, the original instruction being sent from the trade is on HOLD (that is a depository message, Pre-advice). For this, the Depo Advice Reqd field in SEC.TRADE is set to NO so that MT541 or MT543 instruction is not generated from the trade. The Instruction trade settlement with status Hold ( SC.SETT.NEW.INST.ON.HOLD ) enquiry lists all the Delivery versus Payment (DVP) transactions for which instructions are not sent.

The users can use the drilldown in the enquiry to trigger a HOLD instruction using the application SC.INST.HOLD.REL . After the hold instruction is sent, the rest of the process is the same.

| SUBCYY34 MT530 to NCSDXX21 (Holding Instruction) | SUBCYY34 MT530 to NCSDXX21 (Releasing Instruction) |
|---|---|
| :16R:GENL:16R:GENL | :16R:GENL:16R:GENL |
| :20C::SEME//PROCZYWVU-1 | :20C::SEME//PROCZYWVU |
| :23G:NEWM | :23G:NEWM |
| :98A::PREP//20040306 | :98A::PREP//20040306 |
| :97A::SAFE//333333333 | :97A::SAFE//333333333 |
| :16S::GENL | :16S::GENL |
| :16R::REQD | :16R::REQD |
| :20C::PREV//987654321 | :20C::PREV//987654321 |
| :22F::SETT//NPRE | :22F::SETT//YPRE |
| :16S::REQD | :16S::REQD |


#### 📋 Tasks

Settlement instruction can be put on hold and release it again later at any stage in the instruction life cycle before the transaction is settled. When instruction is ‘on hold’, it will undergo a matching process but will not be eligible for settlement until both parties have released their respective settlement instructions.

### 7.3  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Central Securities Depositories Regulation (CSDR) regulates settlement of financial instruments in the European Union, particularly cross-border settlements. It aims at harmonized settlement cycles, better settlement discipline and common requirements across central securities depositories (CSDs). I...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Central Securities Depositories Regulation (CSDR) regulates settlement of financial instruments in the European Union, particularly cross-border settlements. It aims at harmonized settlement cycles, better settlement discipline and common requirements across central securities depositories (CSDs). It requires firms to put in place measures to mitigate settlement delays and endorse straight through processing (STP) to maintain high settlement rates.

It also sets out rules aimed at reducing settlement failure rates and improving settlement discipline. For trades that do fail, CSDR will impose daily penalties or charges as well as mandatory buy-ins.

The main objective of the regulation is to increase the safety and efficiency of securities settlement and settlement infrastructures in the EU.

Transact is enhanced to comply with CSDR and will support the following:

- STP Settlement within tolerance
- Bilateral Cancellation
- Hold & Release of Settlement instructions
- Cash Penalties Late Matching Fail Penalties (LMFP) Settlement Fail Penalty (SFP)


##### Product Configuration

Parameter records contain critical settings that the system uses for various functionalities. The SC.CSDR.PARAMETER application needs to be setup to support the CSDR functionality within Transact. The ID of the record is a valid COMPANY id.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The SC.CSDR.PARAMETER application is a company level parameter to define the tolerance amount, which is to be linked with the settlement amount, depository wise.

Based on the settlement amount, the system applies tolerance check and process the settlement if the difference between the settlement amount in the confirmation and the intended settlement is within the tolerance range.

The difference is posted to P&L or internal suspense account defined in SC.PARAMETER .

- Depository – The ID of the depository for which the tolerance check is required.
- Transaction Amount – The actual transaction amount of the trade.
- Tolerance Amount – The tolerance range to apply the tolerance check.
- Bilateral Cancellation – To denote whether bilateral cancellation is applicable for this depository.


##### Illustrating Model Products

Model products are not applicable for this module.

### 7.4  Settlement Penalties


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *As a part of CSDR settlement discipline, the cash penalties regime was introduced across all Eurozone CSDs. The Central Securities Depository Regulation (CSDR) requires cash penalties collected by the CSD from the participants that caused a settlement fail or late settlement and re-distributed to pa...*
> 
> **Prerequisites:** `SEC.TRADE`, `NOSTRO.ACCOUNT`, `DEPOSITORY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *@ID*, *Net Monthly Penalty Post*, *Net Monthly Penalty Recd*, *Post Sett Penalty*, *Ref Price*, *Ref Price Date*, *Sett Fail Fee*, *Sett Pen Pl Susp*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

As a part of CSDR settlement discipline, the cash penalties regime was introduced across all Eurozone CSDs. The Central Securities Depository Regulation (CSDR) requires cash penalties collected by the CSD from the participants that caused a settlement fail or late settlement and re-distributed to participants suffering from settlement fails. The penalty rates are fixed by the regulator, and it is based on the instrument type, liquidity and market classifications and settlement instruction type.

The settlement failure can be

- Due to lack of security (which is based on whether the instrument is liquid/ traded in growth market) or
- Due to lack of cash

The penalty rate can be different for lack of security and lack of cash. This penalty rate is used in the calculation of the cash penalty for the late matching and the settlement failure.


##### Types of Penalties

The following section describes the types of penalties.

A settlement instruction is subject to LMFP, if the settlement instruction is matched with the counterparty instruction after the Intended Settlement date (ISD). LMFP is calculated only once on the business day when the instructions are matched but considering all previous business days from the ISD where it failed to settle due to late matching.

The system calculates the fee once, after the MT548 (for a transaction) or when MT537 (for a party) is received with the penalty information and whether the penalty is due for the party or the counterparty.

An instruction is subject to SEFP, if the instruction is matched before the relevant cut-off date, reached the ISD and has failed to settle on that ISD or on the day the instruction is matched, that is after ISD.

SEFP is calculated for each business day the matched instruction fails to settle.

SEFP is calculated every day during the end of day batch process after the first time an MT548 or MT537 reports the daily penalty information and until the time the instruction has fully settled.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section defines the configuration of SC.CSDR.PARAMETER and SECURITY.MASTER .


##### ConfiguringSC.CSDR.PARAMETER

The Sett Pen Msg field in SC.CSDR.PARAMETER enables to setup whether the daily penalty details should be received in MT548 or MT537 message. The allowed values are MT537 and MT548.

The bank decides whether the penalty amount should be posted to a suspense account or the bank’s PL. The Sett Pen Pl Susp field in SC.CSDR.PARAMETER helps to achieve this. It specifies whether the bank’s PL or a suspense account is credited or debited when the net penalty is posted.

- If an account belonging to suspense category is defined, then the penalty amount is posted to suspense.
- If PL category account is defined, then the penalty amount is posted to PL.

The SC.SETT.PENALTY.RATES table stores the penalty rates based on which Late matching penalty (LMFP) and Settlement Fail Penalty (SEFP) are calculated on a daily and monthly basis. The ID of the table is:

- Asset type
- Sub-Asset type
- Security Master ID

Security master ID has the highest priority followed by Sub-Asset type and Asset type respectively based on the granularity. The settlement failure due to lack of security is based on whether the instrument is liquid or traded in growth market.

The cash penalty rate is the official interest rate for overnight credit that is announced by the central banks in the settlement currency with a floor of zero based on the settlement failure due to lack of cash. This is the marginal lending facility rate published by the central bank. If the cash penalty rate is not set in SC.SETT.PENALTY.RATES table, the system uses the one-day rate from PERIODIC.INTEREST in the respective currency to calculate the penalty.

The penalty is calculated as below:


##### ConfiguringSECURITY.MASTER

In SECURITY.MASTER , the Sett Fail Fee field indicates whether the LMFP and SEFP are eligible for any transactions not matched or settled by the Intended Settlement date (ISD). For calculation of the penalty for the respective date, the system uses a reference price from the Ref Price Date and Ref Price fields respectively in SECURITY.MASTER .


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the calculation of Settlement Penalties in Temenos Transact.


##### UpdatingSC.SETT.PENALTY.DAILY

This section explains the computation and mapping of daily LMFP and SEFP from inward MT548 or MT537.

The system creates and updates a record in SC.SETT.PENALTY.DAILY application whenever a daily MT548 (:23G/ PENA) or MT 537 (:23G/ PENA and: 22F/SFRE/ DAIL) is received. MT548 is received per transaction, whereas MT537 is received for a party involving the set of transactions done against various counterparties. In case of MT537, a record is created or updated for each underlying transaction.

The ID of this application is the SEC.TRADE or SECURITY.TRANSFER ID.

The SC.SETT.PENALTY.DAILY application is used to update the daily penalty received from the above messages and when the system computes the daily penalty during COB.

1. Daily Late Matching Fee Penalty (LMFP) is calculated for a transaction from the day the penalty information is received (from the custodian) through MT548 or MT537. After the Intended settlement date (ISD), if the matching status is not received from the custodian, LMFP is calculated during Close of business (COB).
2. Daily Settlement Failure Penalty (SEFP) is calculated for each day a matched transaction remains unsettled (partially/ fully) after the intended settlement date (ISD). If a transaction is partially settled on a day, the quantity for calculating SEFP includes only the unsettled portion.
3. If the party that receives the message is expected to receive the penalty amount from the counterparty, then the currency before the reported penalty is EUR. However, if the party that receives the message is liable to pay the penalty, then the currency is prefixed with an ‘N’ before the penalty amount as NEUR.

Consider the following field values for which LMFP and SEFP are calculated as shown below.

- Trade date –Aug 17,2020
- Value date – Aug 19, 2020
- Cash penalty Rate - 0.25%
- Stock penalty rate- 0.25 BP
- Quantity =1000
- Reference price on:

The party’s settlement instruction is matched with the counterparty’s instruction on 21st Aug 2020 and is observed from the daily MT548 that is received. This indicates that the counterparty instruction is sent late. Hence the formula for RVP type of instruction is applied and the party receives the penalty.

The transaction is settled on 22nd Aug 2020, as per the daily MT548 and the late settlement is due to lack of cash by the party who is imposed with a cash penalty.

> **⚠️ Note:** When the bank receives the MT537 daily report from the custodian received with the tag: 22F::CODE/ FWAM in Sequence D (PENA), it indicates that the penalty list that has been amended (that is, the penalty list contains only updated and/or removed penalties that are already reported in a FWIS Penalty List). Based on this information in the amended MT537, the system updates the respective penalty based on the common reference.

This section explains how a monthly report via MT537 updates the system.

The SC.SETT.PEN.PARTY application is updated when an MT537 is received with :23G/ PENA and :22F/SFRE/MNTH.

The ID of the table - Safekeep ID of the party * Depository* Currency * Period.

##### Posting of Penalty Fee

The user triggers the posting upon the reconciliation of the computed and reported fees in SC.SETT.PEN.PARTY . The penalty amount is accounted per currency per counterparty custodian.

In SC.SETT.PEN.PARTY , the penalty amount per counterparty custodian per currency is stored in Net Monthly Penalty Recd which is mapped from the incoming MT 537 for the monthly report. On the payment date (typically 15th business day of every month), the penalty amount is triggered. This system defaults the value in Net Monthly Penalty Post (a user-amendable field).

The posting of accounting entry for the penalty amount is based on the value in Net Monthly Penalty Recd . The Post Sett Penalty field in SC.SETT.PEN.PARTY helps to trigger the posting of penalty amount. Once the system posts the penalty and generates the accounting, the field is cleared.

|---|---|---|

| Cr | Nostro Account | $8.18 |


#### 📋 Tasks

As per CSDR, two penalties LMFP and SFP are charged for the party that caused the settlement failure. The regulator fixes the penalty rate and it is based on the instrument type, liquidity and market classifications and settlement instruction type. The calculation and penalties of settlement failure will be on a daily or monthly basis.

### 7.5  Settlement Tolerance


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *CSDR aims at full STP settlement where possible and where the settlement amount is within a reasonable level of tolerance.*
> 
> **Prerequisites:** `SEC.TRADE`, `NOSTRO.ACCOUNT`, `DEPOSITORY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Overpost Settlement Tolerance*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

CSDR aims at full STP settlement where possible and where the settlement amount is within a reasonable level of tolerance.

Where the settlement amount in the incoming Settlement message is different from the anticipated settlement amount, Temenos Transact accounts for the settlement difference provided the difference is within tolerance.

The acceptable Settlement tolerance per Depository can be set and STP would break if tolerance is breached.

- EUR 2 for settlement amount up to EUR 100,000
- EUR 25 for settlement amount over EUR 100,000

For transactions where the settlement amount is less than or equal to 100,000 EUR, the tolerance is 2 EUR. If the difference between the anticipated settlement amount and settlement received through confirmation is more than the 2 EUR, settlement is not processed.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Overpost Settlement Tolerance field in SC.PARAMETER needs to be set as No, indicating that settlement should not be processed if the difference between the settlement amount received and anticipated settlement amount is greater than the tolerance defined.

The tolerance amount varies based on the settlement amount per depository. The tolerance amount setup is defined in the SC.CSDR.PARAMETER application as shown below.

For the depository 100492

- For transactions where the settlement amount is less than or equal to 100,000 EUR, the tolerance is 2 EUR.
- For transactions where the settlement amount is less than or equal to 200,000 EUR, the tolerance is 25 EUR.
- For transactions where settlement amount is greater than 200,000 EUR, the tolerance is 50 EUR where depository is 100492.

Similar setup is defined for depository 100472. For transactions where depository is other than 100492 and 100472, the system refers the setup defined for ALL to determine the settlement tolerance.

> **⚠️ Note:** If this setup is not defined, then the settlement tolerance computation and checks are done based on the setup in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application. Read Creating a Depository section in Configuring Depository and Broker feature for more information.

In case of settlement in currencies other than EUR, the EUR equivalent (settlement amount and tolerance) is derived using the official exchange rate for applying the tolerance checks. If the difference in amount is less than or equal to the tolerance specified, the system processes the settlement (no STP break) and posts the difference to a designated account.

> **⚠️ Note:** The tolerance checks are done only on final settlement (settled quantity matches the instruction quantity) and not at the time of partial settlement.


#### 🔧 Working With

A settlement record is created on hold in SEC.TRADE application.

On receipt of settlement confirmation, if the difference between the anticipated settlement amount and settlement received through confirmation is more than the tolerance, settlement record is not processed. As shown in the screenshot below, the difference is greater than tolerance defined in SC.CSDR.PARAMETER for this depository. Hence, the system throws an error, when the record in SC.SETTLEMENT is processed.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Settlement Tolerance feature.

### 8.9  EndPeriodProcessing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The delivery end of period processing consolidates all statistical data. It clears the application of deleted, acknowledged and printed messages. The delivery end of period processing is independent of the Temenos Transact close of business (COB) and is run whenever required by the user.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The delivery end of period processing consolidates all statistical data. It clears the application of deleted, acknowledged and printed messages. The delivery end of period processing is independent of the Temenos Transact close of business (COB) and is run whenever required by the user.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is suggested to run the processing weekly. However, it is up to the user to decide when they find it best to run and how often to process.

Running the delivery end of period removes the messages, for which processing is complete and places them in the HISTORY tables. Therefore, regular running of end of period keeps the LIVE tables in a reasonable size and therefore improves the processing time within delivery.

### 8.11  Generation of MX Message using ISOMX Carrier


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This functionality provides Business Applications a framework to forms the business message. The Business Applications hands off the message data to Delivery, Delivery maps the message and issues the details to the Integration Framework which applies the transformation to the final formal. The Deliv...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

This functionality provides Business Applications a framework to forms the business message. The Business Applications hands off the message data to Delivery, Delivery maps the message and issues the details to the Integration Framework which applies the transformation to the final formal. The Delivery Carrier associated to this processing is ISOMX.

To use the full benefits of the Delivery Transformation layer and the capabilities to handle headers please consult the Support MX messages through SWIFTNet Interact services section.

ISO 20022 MX is a new message type expressed in XML syntax, which is more flexible and easier to implement than the previous generation of message types (MT). These message types are developed in accordance with the ISO 20022 standard.

The current syntax format is xxxx.nnn.aaa.bb, where:

- xxxx is an alphabetic code in four positions (fixed length) identifying the business process.
- nnn is an alphanumeric code in three positions (fixed length) identifying the message functionality.
- aaa is a numeric code in three positions (fixed length) identifying a particular flavour (variant) of message functionality.
- bb is a numeric code in two positions (fixed length) identifying the version.

TREA.001.001.02, where:

- TREA refers to Treasury.
- 001 refers to NDF opening (notification).
- 001 refers to the variant.
- 02 refers to the version message format, in this case, version 2 of NDF opening type.


##### SWIFT Standards for MX Messages

| MX Identifier | Description |
|---|---|
| acmt.xxx.xxx.xx | Account Management |
| admi.xxx.xxx.xx | Administration |
| camt.xxx.xxx.xx | Cash Management |
| defp.xxx.xxx.xx | Derivatives |
| pacs.xxx.xxx.xx | Payments Clearing and Settlement |
| pain.xxx.xxx.xx | Payments Initiation |
| reda.xxx.xxx.xx | Reference Data |
| seev.xxx.xxx.xx | Securities Events |
| semt.xxx.xxx.xx | Securities Management |
| sese.xxx.xxx.xx | Securities Settlement |
| setr.xxx.xxx.xx | Securities Trade |
| trea.xxx.xxx.xx | Treasury |
| tsmt.xxx.xxx.xx | Trade Services Management |

### 8.14  Interbank Statement Request


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Banks send a request message to their correspondent requesting information related to their accounts (or accounts maintained for their customers, where a prior agreement is in place).*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Banks send a request message to their correspondent requesting information related to their accounts (or accounts maintained for their customers, where a prior agreement is in place).

Incidentally an MT920 request message is sent to the account servicing institution to transmit one or more MT940 Customer Statements, MT941 Balance Report(s), MT942 Interim Transaction Report(s), or MT950 Statement Message(s) containing the latest information available for the account as identified in the message. This message has a multiple sequence consisting of account(s) for which the information and required message type(s) is requested. The MT920 message requires implementation of special procedures and its use is governed by bilateral agreements between correspondents.

### 8.15  Interim Intraday Transaction Report


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The interim transaction report (MT942) should contain detailed and summary information about the entries debited or credited to the account since:*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The interim transaction report (MT942) should contain detailed and summary information about the entries debited or credited to the account since:

- The last statement (MT940 or 950) or balance report (MT941) or
- The last interim transaction (MT942) report (sent in the period since the last statement or balance report).

The interim report can be generated manually on an ad hoc basis or automatically through the Temenos Transact service.

MT942 is an intra-day transaction report, which is used to transmit detailed information about entries debited or credited to the account since:

- The last statement or balance report.
- The last interim transaction report (sent in the period since the last statement or balance report).

MT941 and MT942 message types are not linked and therefore the statement for these message types is generated independently, that is, the entries to be reported in the statement for the message type 942 do not depend on the last MT941 statement.
