> 
> **Key Fields:** *Action Narrative*, *Advice Index*, *Advice Reqd*, *Aggr Cut Off Time*, *Aggr Version*, *Aggregation*, *Amount To Broker*, *Amount to Broker* ... +78 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The set of ISO 15022 messages supported by SWIFT Straight Through Processing (STP) is the next step in the evolution of banking systems for the securities industry. ISO 15022 is the messaging standard supported by SWIFT for the securities industry. It is in response to market demand for STP. It replaces the following ISO 7775 standards:

- Scheme for Message Types and ISO 11521
- Scheme for Inter-Depository Message Types

The ISO 15022 series of messages replaced the ISO 7775 series of messages from November 2002 onwards. The ISO 15022 series of messages facilitates a T+1 (trade date + 1) settlement scenario.

STP is an initiative used by companies in the financial world to optimise the speed at which transactions are processed. This is performed by allowing information that has been electronically entered to be transferred from one party to another in the settlement process without manually re-entering the same pieces of information repeatedly over the entire sequence of events.


##### Product Configuration

The following parameter files are configured for SWIFT STP feature.

The SP.STP.PARAM parameter application drives the STP functionality. The application facilitates the controlling of STP in separate components. The components of STP are the SWIFT messages, which are controlled by the securities STP module. All the components of STP are to be selected, if a full STP system is to be installed. As there might be a requirement for partial STP (for example, settlement is controlled through STP and order processing is done manually), the SP.STP.PARAM can be setup accordingly to suit the business requirement.

The ID of SP.STP.PARAM is the company ID. Each company has a separate parameter record.

An OFS.SOURCE record is to be setup as shown in the below screenshot. This OFS.SOURCE record defines the In Queue Dir , Out Queue Dir and the In Dir Rtn fields.

A record must be setup in EB.PHANTOM as shown in the below screenshot.

Read OFS User Guide for more information OFS.SOURCE and EB.PHANTOM applications.

The Sc Class Type and Eb Class Type fields in SC.PARAMETER must be updated as shown in the below screenshot.

The Sc Class Type is the internal class used in the SC module. The Sc Class Type and Eb Class Type provides the class mapping between internal securities classes and EB.MESSAGE.CLASS . The Eb Class Type allows a valid EB.MESSAGE.CLASS record to be input. The EB.MESSAGE.CLASS must be used in the EB.ADVICES record. This facilitates the addition of new mapping records locally for each activity.

With the above setup, all the inward messages is processed and the respective applications are updated and authorised.

Delivery address is maintained for specific portfolio in DE.ADDRESS . The address can be set for each carrier (like email, print, sms, SWIFT). For each carrier, a new record can be created in DE.ADDRESS and the appropriate address (BIC in case of SWIFT carrier, physical address in case of print carrier) can be setup in this application as shown below.

The carriers can be configured for each portfolio in DE.PRODUCT application. In the DE.PRODUCT application, new records are created for specific portfolio that is DE.PRODUCT specific to the SEC.ACC.MASTER records. The delivery address is linked to specific portfolio, by mapping DE.PRODUCT in the Advice Index field of the respective SEC.ACC.MASTER portfolio. Read Product table (DE.PRODUCT) for more information on Delivery Message.

The portfolio 50060-1 is mapped to SCP1 in DE.PRODUCT as shown in the below screenshots.

In a full STP order process, orders are placed and executed. Thus, the trades are created in LIVE status automatically. However, there may be scenarios where it is required to amend market settlement instructions, broker fees and or non-standard value date and so on. In such cases, it is possible to halt the STP process to allow manual intervention.

It is possible to parameterise this at CUSTOMER.SECURITY level for specific brokers or at SECURITY.MASTER level for specific securities. It is also possible to set this at the time of order creation (that is, at SEC.OPEN.ORDER level) or even at execution stage (that is, in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS level). The following two fields are available in all the above applications and can be set as required:

- Exe Hlt - Indicates whether to halt the execution and raise an override. If this field is set, the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS record is left in Hold status, irrespective of the STP inward confirmation being received. Users can make amendments and then authorise the record.
- Trade Hlt - Indicates if the automatic trade authorisation is to be halted. “If this is set, the SEC.TRADE record is left in IHLD status, irrespective of the inward confirmation being received through STP. Users can make amendments and then authorise the record.

> **⚠️ Note:** In SEC.OPEN.ORDER application, these fields are populated from the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record of the broker (if it is available) or else from the SECURITY.MASTER record. The fields in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS are populated from the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The model parameters for Straight Through Processing are explained below:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Msg Type | Allows 502, 509, 513, 514, 515, 544, 545, 546, 547, 549, 576 messages |
| Aggr Version | Accepts the version record used to authorize SP.AGGREGATION through STP |
| Recon Version | Accepts the version record used to authorize SP.RECONCILIATION through STP |
| Trade Version | Accepts a version record that is used to authorise SEC.TRADE as a part of aggregated MT515 |
| Settle Version | Accepts a version record that is used to authorise SC.SETTLEMENT as a part of aggregated MT545 or MT547 |

Specific record in OFS.SOURCE need to be setup to define the In Queue Dir , Out Queue Dir and In Dir Rtn which enables STP.


##### Illustrating Model Products

Model products are not applicable for this module.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following messages are handled in STP module:

This message is primarily used for placing an order to the broker for a buy or sell. This message is generated from the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application. This message uses the soft delivery method for processing the deliveries. MT502 is generated if the Message Type field in SP.STP.PARAM is set to 502 and Advice Reqd field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is set to Yes. Soft delivery facilitates the preview of SWIFT messages in their unauthorised status.

The SWIFT carrier in the Ovr Carrier field can be overridden at the contract level. The SWIFT address of the broker can be input or overridden in the SEC.OPEN.ORDER application.

The MT502 order to buy or sell has three functions. The functions of MT502 are classified as follows:

- New message - A new order is placed to the broker.
- Replacement - The existing order with the broker is modified.
- Cancellation - The existing order with the broker is cancelled.

The above functions are defined as different activities in Temenos Transact . An example of a new order is shown in the below screenshot.

Once the MT502 new message is generated, the fields other than the No Nominal and Amount to Broker are not allowed for changing in SEC.OPEN.ORDER application. The change to No Nominal and Amount To Broker triggers an MT502 replacement message. An example of an MT502 replacement message is shown in the below screenshot.

The reversal of a SEC.OPEN.ORDER record and the deletion of a broker multi-value set, generates an MT502 cancellation message. An example of an MT502 cancellation message is shown in the below screenshot.

When an MT502 replacement or cancellation message is sent, the same is to be accepted or rejected by the broker with the MT509 trade status message. To facilitate this functionality, the following two application LIVE files are used to record the replacement and cancellation of the details.

When a SEC.OPEN.ORDER is modified or cancelled, then an application LIVE file SP.ORDER.DELIVERY.CONTROL is updated. This LIVE file holds the details of any modification made to the Amount to Broker field and the effect on the customer's No Nominal fields in SEC.OPEN.ORDER record.

This application is live file is updated when an MT502 replacement or cancellation is sent. This file denotes the status of an MT502 replacement or a cancellation that has been sent. If the Broker Msg Status field has the value LIVE, MT509 is not pending from the broker. If the Broker Msg Status field is null, MT509 trade status message is expected from the broker. If the status is accepted or rejected, the MT509 is received from the respective brokers and the update to SEC.OPEN.ORDER is pending.

This message is designed as an inward or outward message in Temenos Transact . The MT509 is processed only, if the Message Type field in SP.STP.PARAM is set to 509. This message is processed by a phantom defined in EB.PHANTOM . An MT509 trade status message can be used in Temenos Transact for receiving the status of previously sent MT502 messages for replacement or cancellation. The status advised in an MT509 can be ACCEPTED or REJECTED. Depending on the status advised, an action is triggered. If the MT502 replacement or cancellation is rejected by an MT509, then the SEC.OPEN.ORDER is modified accordingly. The Amount to Broker field for the respective broker is suitably modified.

When the Amount to Broker field in SEC.OPEN.ORDER is modified, the customer No Nominal field must also be modified. The modification details are stored in the SP.ORDER.DELIVERY.CONTROL application. When an MT509 advises acceptance or rejection, it is recorded in SP.ORDER.STP.ACTIVITY application.

Modifications to SEC.OPEN.ORDER and SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS are not allowed until all MT509 messages are received.

If a SEC.OPEN.ORDER must be modified or an execution is to be input, then the SP.ORDER.STP.ACTIVITY must be set to LIVE in Br Msg Status for all the brokers. This can be achieved manually through the SP.ORD.MANUAL.UPD application.

In the SC.ORD.MANUAL.UPD application, the respective broker number from whom the MT509 is pending can be input and the ACCEPTED or REJECTED status is manually entered. This action updates SC.ORDER.STP.ACTIVITY and triggers the necessary changes.

This is an inward message which is processed in Temenos Transact . The MT513 is processed only if the Message Type field in SP.STP.PARAM is set to 513. This message is received from a broker to whom previously the MT502 order to buy or sell was sent. This message advises the execution of the order in full or in part. This message is processed by a phantom job defined in EB.PHANTOM application. Now, Temenos Transact processes only the advice of execution (new message) and does not process a cancellation of execution.

This message updates the SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS with the execution details received from the broker. The following fields in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is updated from MT513 received from the broker:

- Broker No
- Nominal Recd
- Price

This is an outward message from Temenos Transact . The MT514 is processed only if the Message Type field in SP.STP.PARAM application is set to 514. This message is sent to the broker for each allocation made out of the execution MT514. The trade allocation message carries only one allocation at a time, hence there are multiple MT514s generated from an execution (MT513). Each MT514 trade allocation instruction has the SEC.TRADE ID as a reference. Trade allocation instructions are sent only if the Trade Creation field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is set as BY.PORTFOLIO.

The trade allocation instructions are sent only if the Trade Creation field in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS is set to BY.PORTFOLIO and Advice Reqd is set to Yes in SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS . The Advice Reqd can be set to Yes only if Trade Aggregation is not set to Yes for the broker.

| MT515 Tags | SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS |
|---|---|
| :98A::TRAD// | Trade Date |
| :98A::SETT// | Value Date |
| 90B::/DEAL//ACTU | Price |
| 36B::CONF/UNIT | Nominal Recd |
| :90B::TSTM// | Int Crt |
| :19A::CHAR// :19A::EXEC// :19A::OTHR// | Br Broker Commmission |

|  | Event | Temenos Transact Action | Message Type (Direction) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Input an order to buy or sell | Order is input using SEC.OPEN.ORDER | MT 502 (Outward) |
| 2 | Broker sends a status message | Status is updated in Temenos Transact | MT 509 (Inward) |
| 3 | Broker send advice of execution | SC.EXEC.SEC.ORDERS is updated witht he execution details. SEC.TRADE is created | MT 513 (Inward) |
| 4 | Trade allocation instruction is sent to the broker | One message is sent per allocation with the trade reference | MT 514 (Outward) |
| 5 | Broker sends the confirmation of purchase or sale | Pending SEC.TRADE authorised. | MT 515 (Inward) |

This is an inward message, which is processed in Temenos Transact . The MT544 is processed only if the Message Type field in SP.STP.PARAM is set to 544. This message is received from the depository to whom the MT540 receive free is sent. This message confirms the receipt of stock in full or in part from the respective broker with whom the trade is done.

The MT544 advises the receipt of stock which is recorded in the SC.SETTLEMENT application. The Broker Nom Recd Deld and Cust Nom Recd Delvd fields in SC.SETTLEMENT are populated with the settled nominal advised in MT544. As SEC.TRADE allows the multiple customers and multiple brokers at the same time, the receipt of stock from the respective broker is marked. Similarly, the nominal received or settled by the broker is prorated among the customers. This process of prorating customer nominal against the settled nominal from the broker is handled in MT544 inward processing.

This is an inward message, which is processed in Temenos Transact . The MT545 is processed only if the Message Type field in SP.STP.PARAM is set to 545. This message is received from the depository to whom the MT541 Receive against payment is sent. This message confirms the receipt of stock in full or in part, and the receipt of payment in full or in part from or to the respective broker with whom the trade is done.

The MT545 advises both the receipt of stock and payment made to a broker, which is recorded in the SC.SETTLEMENT application. The Broker Nom Recd Deld and Cust Nom Recd Delvd fields in SC.SETTLEMENT are populated with the settled nominal advised in MT545. Similarly, the Broker Amt Recd Paid and Cu Amt Rec Paid fields in SC.SETTLEMENT are updated with the payment made to the broker. As SEC.TRADE allows multiple customers and multiple brokers at the same time, the receipt of stock from the respective broker are recorded.

Similarly, the nominal received or settled by the broker is prorated among the customers. The cash to be paid to the broker is recorded in SC.SETTLEMENT record. In turn, the cash settlement from the customer is also recorded. This process of prorating customer nominals against settled nominals from the broker and prorating cash amounts is handled in MT545 inward processing.

This is an inward message which is processed in Temenos Transact . The MT546 is processed only if the Message Type field in SP.STP.PARAM is set to 546. This message is received from the depository to whom an MT542 Deliver Free message is sent. This message confirms the receipt of stock in full or in part from the respective broker with whom the trade is done.

The MT546 advises the delivery of stock which is recorded in the SC.SETTLEMENT application. The Broker Nom Recd Deld and Cust Nom Recd Delvd fields in SC.SETTLEMENT are populated with the settled nominal advised in MT546. As SEC.TRADE allows multiple customers and multiple brokers at the same time, the delivery of stock to a respective broker is marked as received in the MT546 deliver free confirmation.

Similarly, the nominal delivered to or settled with the broker is prorated among the customers. This process of prorating customer nominal against the settled nominal from brokers is handled in MT546 inward processing.

This is an inward message, which is processed in Temenos Transact . The MT547 is processed only if the Message Type field in SP.STP.PARAM is set to 547. This message is received from the depository to whom the MT543 Deliver against payment instruction is sent. This message confirms the delivery of stock in full or in part, and the payment received in full or in part from or to the respective broker with whom the trade is done.

The MT547 advises both delivery of stock and payment received from the broker, which is recorded in the SC.SETTLEMENT application. The Broker Nom Recd Deld and Cust Nom Recd Delvd fields in SC.SETTLEMENT are populated with the settled nominal advised in the MT547.

Similarly, the the Broker Amt Recd Paid and Cu Amt Rec Paid fields in SC.SETTLEMENT are updated with the payment received from the broker. As SEC.TRADE allows multiple customers and multiple brokers at the same time, the delivery of stock to a respective broker is recorded. Similarly, the nominal delivered to or settled with the broker is to be prorated among the customers. The cash received from the broker is recorded in SC.SETTLEMENT . In turn, the cash settlement to the customer is also recorded. This process of prorating the customer nominal against the settled nominal to the broker and prorating cash amounts is handled in the MT547 inward processing.

Though the actual settlement method is assumed for STP, entities may settle the customer or broker’s cash and nominal contractually. This method of partial contractual settlement or partial actual settlement is handled in Temenos Transact . In STP, if the contractual settlement method is used partially (for example, customer cash and nominal are contractually settled), the processing of the settlement confirmation messages becomes complex.

Inward processing handles this complex situation for the above messages (MT544, MT545, MT546 and MT547) and settles the broker and customer nominal appropriately. Any error or inability to perform an update to SC.SETTLEMENT is recorded in an exception log.

| Field | Content | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| Auto Compare | 513 515 544 545 546 547 | Allows the input of valid SWIFT DE.MESSAGE types for automatic comparison |
| User Routine | Routine name | Facilitates the validation of additional conditions for the triggering of an automatic MT509 message. The user routine, which must exist on the PGM.FILE , must be called in the compare routine when the above message is received. |
| Reason Code | Ulnk, Dsec, Ddea, Dqua, Ncrr | Allows the input of a set of reject codes as defined in the SP.REASON.CODE application leading to the automatically triggered generation of an MT509 through the SP.STATUS application, if there is reason to reject the incoming message |

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Total Ex Nom | Holds the total number of nominals executed for a particular order by a broker |
| Remain Nom Exe | Holds the remaining quantity of nominals to be executed by the broker as per the execution record |
| Remain Nom | Updated with the remaining nominals as per the MT576 message |

The MT578 swift message is a settlement allegement message sent by the custodian or sub-custodian to an account owner, stating that a counterparty has alleged an instruction against account owner's account at the account servicer and the account servicer could not find the corresponding instruction (MT54x) of the account owner.

The SC.ALLEGEMENT.INWARD table is used to record all the details from the incoming MT578. Each MT578 message creates a record in the SC.ALLEGEMENT.INWARD table. When all fields required to identify a transaction are available, the system marks the record status as Received. If any of the required fields in the record are not available, then system marks the status as ERROR and in the Error Reason field the system marks all the errors.

The fields that the system requires to identify the transaction and error message, if missing, are as below:

- Trade Date
- Security No
- Pay Instr
- Trans Instr
- Nominal
- Broker No
- Portfolio Id

User can investigate and accept the message. If the user accepts the message, user should mark the status of the record as Accepted. When a record is accepted, system automatically creates a SECURITY.TRANSFER record in INAU status and the ID reference of the SECURITY.TRANSFER is stored in the Security Transfer Ref field in SC.ALLEGEMENT.INWARD . The ID of the SC.ALLEGEMENT.INWARD gets recorded in the SECURITY.TRANSFER created.

After investigation, if the user, decides to reject the allegement, then the user should change the status as Rejected. User can also record the reason for rejection in the Reject Reason field, which gets linked to EB.LOOKUP , where standard set of reasons can be defined. If the user wants to reject the allegement after first accepting it, the user can do so only after he or she has manually deleted or reversed the SECURITY.TRANSFER that was created when record was accepted. The status cannot be marked as Rejected when the Security Transfer Ref is not null. Only if it becomes null, the status can be marked as Rejected.

When an MT578 inward with function as CANC or REMO is received, the existing record in SC.ALLEGEMENT.INWARD is updated with cancellation or removal status. If the CANC (or REMO) is received when the record is in Received or Rejected status, then system updates the function as CANC (or REMO) and marks the status as Cancelled.

If the CANC message is received after the record is in Accepted status and SECURITY.TRANSFER is already created, then system records the function as CANC (or REMO) and marks the status of the record as Error with Error Reason as Cancellation received-Transfer created. User can use the enquiry provided to list such records and manually reverse or delete the SECURITY.TRANSFER record, as required.

If International Securities Identification Number (ISIN) is not available for a security, the SWIFT messages (MT515, MT540-543 and MT518) can be put on hold until the ISIN is available. Once the ISIN is available, SC.GENERATE.INST is used to generate the SWIFT messages. The user can provide the list of transactions for which instructions (MT515, MT518, and MT540–543) are to be generated. The user can control the generation of advices for the trades listed by setting the values in the Cu Advice Reqd , Broker Advice Reqd and Depo Advice Reqd fields to Yes or No.

When this record is authorised, the delivery instructions are generated for the trade(s) and the references are updated in the trade(s). The delivery message details are from the underlying SEC.TRADE . The records in this application cannot be amended, once it is authorised by the user. Any amendments or cancellation of the instruction has to be from the trade.

In a Straight Through processing, when a trade confirmation message SETR027 is processed, then the system automatically authorises the trade, provided, if the trade details such as Nominal, Price, Security No. are matched properly. If the details does not match, the system holds the trade in unauthorised status and updates the status record SP.STATUS with the unmatch reason and details. The user can send the acknowledgement of these unaffirmed trades through SETR030 message.

This enquiry displays the list of these status records in unauthorised status with the un-match reason details applicable. The user can further authorise this record and send the acknowledgement message (SETR030) to the broker or counterparty who previously sent the confirmation message (SETR027).

The Corporate Action module allows to record and process a corporate action (CA) event. The processing of the CA events can be done manually or through Straight Through Processing (STP). This module supports the CA processing for both omnibus and segregated accounts.


##### Product Configuration

The parameters for Securities Corporate Actions (SC-CA) are explained below:

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Specifies the ID based on the setup in the SC.PRE.DIARY , DIARY , ENTITLEMENT and SC.CA.BUY.SELL applications |
| Ofs Source and Ofs Version | Creates or updates the SC.PRE.DIARY and DIARY applications. The ENTITLEMENT application is created or updated when the incoming MT56* messages are processed in STP |
| Tolerance Categ, Tolerance Pct, Tolerance Ccy and Tolerance Amt | Allows to setup a high-level tolerance limits |
| Tolerance Nom | Allows to setup the tolerance level while performing stock reconciliation from MT566. This is applicable for ENTITLEMENT |
| Update Diary | If this field is set to NO, the DIARY record is updated manually on receipt of REPL message. This is applicable for DIARY |
| Apply Default | Specifies the default option for processing the entitlement. This is applicable for DIARY |
| Mt565 Per Option | If this field is set to YES, the MT565 is generated at the option level. This is applicable for ENTITLEMENT |
| Apply Default | This field is used to determine whether default option is to be applied when there is no standing instructions |
| Conversion Event | This field holds the DIARY.TYPE record Id to be used for processing the customer initiated conversion event |
| Exercise Event | This field holds the DIARY.TYPE record Id to be used for processing the customer initiated exercise event |

| Parameters | Description |
|---|---|
| Cash | Indicates the cash update during the processing of the event, when set to YES |
| Security Update | Defines whether the security position update is applicable |
| New Securities | Defines whether new securities are updated to the customer’s position because of the processing. For example, RIGHTS event |
| Options | Identifies if this event holds multiple options for the investors to elect |
| Reinvest | Indicates that the cash offered (if any) can be reinvested in the original security |
| Free Securities | Indicates if free securities are applicable. For example, BONUS |
| Retain Original | Indicates if the portfolios retain their original holding once the event execution is completed |
| Swift Caev | Specifies the SWIFT indicator of the corporate action event |

### 9.2  Allocation Methods

#### 📖 Introduction

Capital gains are calculated based on disposal value of a position and the acquisition cost. The acquisition cost varies from one lot to another. Therefore, the gains differ depending on the lot selected for disposal.

Lots are selected in different methods. Selection or identification of tax lots is crucial as the choice of tax lot method has a significant impact on the amount of taxes the investor pays while selling the asset. In some countries, the method is pre-ordained by the tax authorities while in others, it is left to the bank or the investor to decide.

> **⚠️ Note:** The tax lot identification method is also referred to as CG method.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configuration required to support the tax lot selection methods in Temenos Transact.


##### CG.PARAMETER

The Cg Method field in CG.PARAMETER specifies the default tax lot allocation method, which is associated with a date. If the default method is changed, the Date To field is multi-valued. The date up to which the earlier method is applicable is specified and the new method is updated in the first multi-value set.

In the below screenshot, Last In First Out (LIFO) method is applicable till April 16, 2019, after which Fast In First Out (FIFO) method is applied.

> **⚠️ Note:** The CG Method specified in the first multi-value is the current applicable method.

The CG Methods Allowed field is used to specify the tax lot allocation methods that are applicable for the company. In many countries, tax authorities specify the methods that are used to determine capital gains (CG). Only the methods that are specified here are set for a portfolio or as a default method.


##### CG.INVENTORY.METHOD

The application provides the ability to define the tax lot identification method at various levels.

The record ID of this application consists of the following three parts:

1. A valid Customer ID or all
2. Portfolio Group Name or ALL Portfolio group name is the portfolio ID unless specifically different.
3. S-NNN (sub-asset type), A-NNN (asset type), NNNNNNN (security master) or NNNNNN (ISIN)

If the Cg Base Level field in CG.PARAMETER is set to ISIN, the system can accept only sub-asset type or ISIN and not security master ID. Thus, it is possible to define the tax lot identification method at various possible levels and combinations as follows:

- For all customers, portfolios and asset types (ALL.ALL.ALL record)
- For a particular customer and for all asset types (Customer ID.ALL. ALL record)
- For a particular portfolio or group and for a particular SAT (ALL.PortfolioGroupname.SAT record)

The following are valid records:

- ALL.ALL.ALL
- 100297.ALL.ALL
- ALL.AUCUST.S-300 (AUCUST is a Portfolio group name)
- 100297.100297-1.A-10

If an ALL.ALL record is defined, any value in Cg Method in CG.PARAMETER is ignored.

The most basic definition is applied. This is explained with the following examples.

The following records exist:

- ALL.ALL.ALL
- 100297.100297-1.ALL

For portfolio 100297-1, the second record is used whereas, the first record is used for other portfolios.

The following records exist:

- ALL.ALL.ALL
- 100297.ALL.S-300

Here, if portfolio 100297-1 uses a security master belonging to sub-asset type (SAT) 300, the second definition is used. If portfolio 100291-1 uses a security master belonging to SAT 302, the first definition is used as separate definition does not exists for SAT 302 for this portfolio.

The lot that generates the least capital gain or maximum capital loss is deemed to be the parcel sold. This method slightly differs from highest cost method as it incorporates Australian specific rules, while calculating CG.

Australian tax laws allows to calculate gain or loss based on three methods—Indexation, Discount and Standard method. The open parcels shown below include acquisition done prior to 1985 (no CG), acquired from 1985-1989 (indexation possible), held for less than 12 months (standard method) and for more than 12 months (discount method).

Further, in case of a loss,

Also, indexation and discount are not applied in case of a loss. Read the relevant feature for more information on capital gains calculation in Australia. Here, a sum of 25000 units are to be disposed of.

> **⚠️ Note:** While selecting the parcels, the pre 1985 parcel has been excluded in this scenario.

- The first parcel selected (parcel ref 3) is the one that generates the maximum capital loss (reduced cost base – proceeds per unit).
- The second parcel selected (parcel 8) has been held for less than 12 months. The capital loss is reduced cost base – proceeds per unit.
- The third parcel selected (parcel 6) also results in a loss.
- The fourth parcel selected (parcel 2) has a cost base less than the sale proceeds and this has resulted in a capital gain. However, the parcel was acquired in 1986, which means the indexation is available. The indexed cost base (25.13 USD) is more than the sale proceeds. However, the indexed cost cannot be used to calculate the capital loss (it is on reduced cost base). In this case, there is neither gain nor loss.
- The last parcel selected (parcel 5) is entitled to discount, as the holding is for more than 12 months and the CG is calculated after applying the discount.

The total loss (79,072 USD) is the sum of all capital gains or loss from the individual parcels allocated to the sale or disposal.

> **⚠️ Note:** If two parcels have the same loss or gain, the parcel selected are the one that was acquired earlier (FIFO).

The lot that generates the highest capital gain or least capital loss is deemed the parcel sold. This method slightly differs from lowest cost method as it is incorporates Australian specific rules while calculating CG.

Australian tax laws allows to calculate gain or loss based on three methods—Indexation, Discount and Other method). The open parcels shown below include acquisition done prior to 1985 (no CG), acquired from 1985-1989 (indexation possible), held for less than 12 months (other method) and for more than 12 months (discount method). In this example a total of 25000 units are to be disposed of.

In the example above, the lots selected are 9, 4,7,5,2 and 6 in that order.

When specific lots are selected, the system does not use the applicable tax lot allocation method but allocates the lots and quantities as specified.


##### Allocation of Lots

When a disposal transaction is input, system determines the tax lots to be allocated for the disposal using following logic:

- If specific lot and quantity are given in the transaction, system allocates the specific lot and calculate the capital gain.
- If specific lot is not given, system checks CG.INVENTORY.METHOD for the portfolio and determines the tax lot allocation method to be used. System checks for the most granular definition first.

The following records exist:

- ALL.ALL.ALL
- 100297.100297-1.ALL

For portfolio 100297-1, the second record is used. For all other portfolios, the first record is used.

The following records exist:

- ALL.ALL.ALL
- 100297.ALL.S-300

Here, if the portfolio 100297-1 uses a security master belonging to sub-asset type (SAT) 300, the second definition is used. If portfolio 100291-1 uses a security master belonging to SAT 300, the first definition is used as there is no separate definition for this portfolio. If no record matching the transaction parameters exists in CG.INVENTORY.METHOD, the system uses the default Cg Method specified in CG.PARAMETER .


##### Change of CG Tax Lot Allocation Method

The default method in CG.PARAMETER and CG.INVENTORY.METHOD are changed with an effective date. The new method is applied for disposals that happen after the change date and not with retrospective effect.

If it is required to re-work the CG by applying the method retrospectively, user must use the CG.REALLOCATE.BASE application. The ID can be ALL (if method is changed for all portfolios) or specific portfolio.

The tax lot method to be applied on the date from when reallocation and recalculation is to be done and the date up to which rework is to be done, must be given.

Once record is authorised, the CG.REALLOCATE.TXN.BASE service needs to be run and system rebuilds the tax base, and recalculate CG using the given allocation method.


#### 📋 Tasks

Capital gains are calculated based on disposal value of a position less the acquisition cost. The acquisition cost varies from one lot to another. Therefore, the gains differ depending on the lot that is selected for disposal.

There are different methods in which the lots can be selected. Selection or identification of tax lots is crucial as the choice of tax lot method can have a significant impact on the amount of tax that the investor may pay at the time of selling the asset.

In some countries, the method is pre-ordained by the tax authorities. While in others, it is left to the bank or even the investor to decide.


##### Workflow

This section helps the user to perform the below tasks:

This screen enables the user to define the Capital Gains (CG) allocation methods based on portfolio, only if the Cg Enh Process field is selected in the CG.PARAMETER application .

Possible to set the CG methods for the below combinations.

- For All customers, all portfolios and all asset types.
- For a particular customer and all asset types.
- For a particular portfolio or group and for a particular sub asset type.

1. Set Allocation Method-Portfolio .
2. Enter the record ID in the format of: Customer ID.Portfolio ID.Security Number
3. Enter a value in the Portfolio Setting field and click the Edit icon
4. Enter values in the following multi-value set fields: CG Method.1 Date to.1 Long Term Period.1 Short Term Rate.1 Long Term Rate.1 Discount Factor.1 Discount Factor.1 Adjustment Factor.1 Trade Date Included Revenue Asset
5. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
6. Click the Commit icon.

### 9.3  Australian Capital Gains

Many countries impose tax on capital gains. The rules to calculate capital gains, assets that are subject t...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *CG Calc Param*, *CG From Date*, *Cg Enh Process*, *Cg Index*, *Cg Lt Calc Method*, *Cg Lt Pl*, *Cg St Calc Method*, *Date* ... +11 more

> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Capital gains are gains realised on the disposal of an asset at a value higher than the purchase cost, where the disposal value is lower than the cost of the asset resulting in a capital loss. Many countries impose tax on capital gains. The rules to calculate capital gains, assets that are subject to capital gains tax and the tax calculation vary from country to country. Temenos Transact ’s Tax Lots (TL) module enables generic calculation of capital gains. It also handles the capital gains calculation pertaining to Australia.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the required setup for Australian (AU) Capital Gain calculation.


##### CG.PARAMETER

The Cg Enh Process field in CG.PARAMETER is set to Yes, to apply country specific Capital Gains (CG) settings. The CG Calc Param field allows input, when Cg Enh Process is flagged. The applicable record in CG.CALC.PARAM can be set in this application, which the system refers while calculating the CG.

> **⚠️ Note:** Temenos Transact supports rules specific to Australia only. Hence, the record with ID as AU is populated by default.


##### CG.CALC.PARAM

This application holds the default rules applicable for CG calculation. The record ID is the country code.

CG is calculated only on disposal of lots purchased after the date specified in the CG From Date field. If any lot purchased before this date is disposed-off, CG is updated as zero. The Date field is a multi-valued set, which specifies the start date from when the value in the multi-valued set is applicable. The Cg St Calc Method and Cg Lt Calc Method fields define the calculation methods applicable for calculating the short term and long term capital gains, respectively. Read Tax Lot Allocation Methods for more information on the various methods supported in Temenos Transact for this feature.

The Index Mtd Upto Date field holds the acquisition date up to which the index method can be used, that is, indexation method can be applied only to tax lots acquired before this date. The Index Qtr Numerator field accepts the period for which the index is considered for numerator of indexation factor to apply to cost basis. The Index Qtr Denom accepts the period for which the index is considered for denominator of indexation factor to apply to cost basis.

If the purchase date is 20 Oct 1995 and value is Cqtr, the index value for denominator is considered for end of current quarter (that is, 31 Dec 1995).


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the basics of how Temenos Transact handles Australian (AU) Capital Gain calculation on disposal of an asset.


##### Australian Capital Gain - Calculation Methods

The Australian Tax Office (ATO) has prescribed the rules to be followed for calculation CG in Australia. The following are the methods used to determine the capital gains/losses on securities in Australia::

- Standard method
- Indexation method
- Discount method

Capital gains (CG) is not applicable on disposal of assets purchased before 1985. For assets purchased after 1985, the standard method is applicable if the asset is disposed within 12 months of acquisition. The optimum of indexation method and discount method is applicable, only if the asset is disposed after 12 months of acquisition and is before 21 Sept 1999.


###### Standard Method

Temenos Transact calculates short term CG using standard method, where the tax lot is disposed-off within 12 months of acquisition. For directly purchased securities, the acquisition date is the purchase or transaction date. For indirectly acquired securities (like, by marriage settlement and death of benefactor), the acquisition date is the original acquisition date provided by the customer in SECURITY.TRANSFER . The 12 months holding period is determined from the acquisition date.

To calculate the capital gain using the other method, subtract the cost basis from the capital proceeds.

When both indexation and discount methods are eligible to be applied, the method which results in lower gain is applicable.

For Australia CG calculation, two methods can be used for calculating long term capital gains. Temenos Transact determines the capital gains as below:

- For each tax lot whose acquisition date is before September 21, 1999, Temenos Transact calculates the CG using both discount and indexation method. Values calculated under each method is updated in the Pur Lt Cg Discount and Pur Lt Cg Indexed fields in CG.TXN.BASE . The standard capital gain is updated in the Pur Lt Cg Std field . The total long term capital gain for the sale transactions is updated in the Cg Lt Pl field by totaling the values in the Pur Lt Cg Pl field.
- For each tax lot acquired after September 21, 1999, the capital gain is calculated using the discount method. This is updated in the Pur Lt Cg Discount field . For these tax lots, capital gains using indexation method is not calculated and the Pur Lt Cg Indexed field remains blank. The total long term capital gain for the sale transactions is updated in the Cg Lt Pl field by totalling the values in the Pur Lt Cg Pl field .

#### 📖 Introduction

Tax lots are maintained in Temenos Transact, every time a security is credited to the portfolio. The lots are maintained per security or portfolio and are uniquely identifiable. This feature document explains on the working of the Capital Gains (CG).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

Every purchase and sale of a security is recorded in the CG.TXN.BASE application, if the Cg Base Update is set to Yes in SC.PARAMETER . All details required to select a suitable tax lot at the time of sale is available in the CG.TXN.BASE application. Capital Gains (CG) arises at the event of security sale. Therefore, the choice of tax lot method has a significant impact on the amount of CG or taxes the investor pays. Whenever a security is sold, the system updates the CG.TXN.BASE with the details of the sale.

When the Cg Enh Process is set in CG.PARAMETER ,

- The system first refers to the CG.INVENTORY.METHOD to check if there is a separate set up for the corresponding portfolio and security, in order to select the lot for disposal. If there is an ALL.ALL.ALL record defined, any value defined in the CG Method field in CG.PARAMETER is ignored.
- Then, the system additionally refers to the Cg Calc Param field in CG.PARAMETER to ensure if there is any country specific set up for CG calculation. If Cg Calc Param is defined, the system calculates the CG based on this set up.

> **⚠️ Note:** The settings in CG.CALC.PARAM takes the highest precedence followed by the set up in CG.INVENTORY.METHOD whereas CG.PARAMETER set up takes the least.

The settings in CG.CALC.PARAM takes the highest precedence followed by the set up in CG.INVENTORY.METHOD whereas, CG.PARAMETER set up takes the least.

### 9.5  Capital Gain on Transfers


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *An investor holding a security can dispose the security in two ways:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Cg Exempt*, *Cg Tax Ef Date*, *Cg Tax Eff Date*, *Cost*, *Dest Base*, *Dest Trans Id*, *Master Lot Ref*, *Price* ... +6 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

An investor holding a security can dispose the security in two ways:

- Sell down or realise the security for cash proceeds or consideration, which always creates a capital gain (CG) event.
- Transfer-out the asset to another party without selling it, which is commonly referred to as an in-specie transfer.

In-specie transfers may require a change in beneficial owner (CBO transfer) or may proceed without a change in beneficial owner (NCBO transfer). In most regulations, when there is a change in beneficial owner, the transfer is treated like a sale and capital gains (CG) need to be calculated. When there is no change in beneficial owner the transfer is generally not considered as a CG event and no CG is calculated.

In-specie transfer can be internal (where both the source and destination portfolio are held within the Wealth Suite) or external (one of the portfolios resides outside the Wealth Suite). Similarly an investor may also acquire a security through a transfer-in either from an internally held portfolio or from an external portfolio.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Specific configuration is not required for this feature. Read the Capital Gain setup and workflow feature for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains how Capital Gains (CG) are calculated in the case of transfers-in or out.


##### Internal Transfer

Internal (in-specie) transfer is effected through the POSITION.TRANSFER application, where the tax lots are migrated from the source portfolio to the destination portfolio. Here, the tax lot details of the transferor portfolio are already available in the system.

The details of how the tax lots are disposed in the transferor portfolio and how they are built for the transferee portfolio are explained below:

If the transfer is without change in beneficial owner (NCBO), the Cg Exempt field must be manually set to Yes. The system does not automatically determine if there is a change in beneficial owner or not. For an NCBO position transfer, the lots are removed (disposed) from the source portfolio and migrated to the destination portfolio (on their respective records in CG.TXN.BASE ). The lots are removed using the disposal method (First In First Out (FIFO), Min-Gain and so on) applicable to the source portfolio. However, the CG is marked as zero. Lots are then created in the destination portfolio. Each lot disposed in the source portfolio creates a separate lot in the destination portfolio. The acquisition date and cost are the same, as in the source lot. The Cg Tax Ef Date field in CG.TXN.BASE is the Cg Tax Eff Date of the transaction record in POSITION.TRANSFER .

The CG.TXN.BASE for source portfolio is shown in the below screenshot.

The Dest Base and Dest Trans Id fields are updated with the details of the CG.TXN.BASE and SEC.TRANS.ID destination applications. This is required when there is any rework or rebuild of the source portfolio. This reallocates the tax lots of the source portfolio. As a part of re-allocation of the source portfolio, if there is any change to Pur Txn Id and Pur Txn Nom fields (associated with position transfer multi-value set), the CG.TXN.BASE of the destination portfolio is also rebuilt by removing the old lots and inserting the new lots.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Dest Base and Dest Trans Id fields are available only when Cg Exempt is set to Yes in the POSITION.TRANSFER application.

The CG.TXN.BASE for destination portfolio is shown in the below screenshot.

The Source Base field holds the CG.TXN.BASE ID of the source portfolio.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Source Base and Source Trans Id fields are available only when Cg Exempt is set to Yes in the POSITION.TRANSFER application.


##### External Transfer-In

The SECURITY.TRANSFER application is used to record a transfer-in from an external portfolio. A transfer-in with a change of beneficial owner (CBO) is similar to a purchase transaction. A single tax lot is created for the nominal transferred-in. The acquisition date is the trade date of the transfer-in transaction that is, the Trfr Eff Date is the trade date of the transaction.

A transfer-in without a change in beneficial owner (NCBO) is an in-specie transfer-in. The position being transferred in can be acquired at different points of time. Each acquisition is a tax lot for CG purpose. It is important to transfer in and hold the details of each lot, so that accurate CG can be calculated at the time of disposal.

If the breakdown of tax lots is known at the time of transfer in, separate transfer in records in SECURITY.TRANSFER needs to be created for each lot. The original acquisition date, price and tax effective date are recorded using the below fields.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Trfr Eff Date | Records the original date of acquisition of the security being transferred in. It defaults to the trade date of the transaction, if not specified. |
| Cg Tax Eff Date | Records the tax effective date of the transfer. It defaults to the trade date of the transaction, if not specified. |
| Price or Cost | Records the price or cost at which the lot was acquired. Input of one calculates the other. This is the price that is updated in CG.TXN.BASE as the cost of the parcel. |


##### Provisional Transfer

For an external transfer-in (NCBO) the tax lot history may not be known upfront. In this case, the transfer in record in SECURITY.TRANSFER is created with acquisition date being the trade date of the transfer. This results in a single provisional tax lot creation for the full position being transferred. This is a provisional transfer in.

Subsequently, when the customer provides the break-up of the tax lots of the position, the single lot created at the time of the provisional transfer in needs to be replaced with multiple lots, representing the break-up. This is done using the CG.ENH.MANUAL.INPUT application. If position has been transferred in provisionally, the CG.TXN.BASE is updated with a single parcel for the entire position transferred in.

Once the parcel wise break-down of the position is known, the single tax lot can be replaced by multiple tax lots using the CG.ENH.MANUAL.INPUT application, through the following steps.

1. Open a new record.
2. Provide the ID of the tax lot that needs to be replaced in the Master Lot Ref field

1. Provide the details of the multiple lots that made up this position.

1. Commit the record. The system validates that the nominal replaced equals the nominal of the master tax lot.

The system automatically replaces the old lot with the new lots. The Security Trans ID of each lot is the ID of the transfer-in record in SECURITY.TRANSFER suffixed by an index number. This ensures that the link to the original transaction ID is preserved.


##### External Transfer Out

While transferring out a tax lot, the tax lot method used is same as for a sale transaction. But if a transfer out is to be excluded from CG calculation, the Cg Exempt field should be set to Yes. In this case, the system relieves a suitable tax lot based on the tax lot method. However, CG are not calculated.

If the security is being transferred out to an external portfolio of the same customer, there is no CG. In this case, the tax lot should be relieved as in any other sale or transfer out but the capital gains or loss is not calculated.

### 9.6  Capital Gains on Corporate Actions


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Corporate actions (CA) may result in tax liabilities for investors, which may be in the nature of capital gains (CG) or income.*
> 
> **Prerequisites:** `DIARY`, `SECURITY.MASTER`, `SECURITY.POSITION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *>Ns Lot Cost*, *Ca Odd Lot*, *Calc Cg*, *Cash Remain*, *Cg Base Update*, *Cg Enh Process*, *Cg Pl*, *Cg Rollover* ... +18 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Corporate actions (CA) may result in tax liabilities for investors, which may be in the nature of capital gains (CG) or income.

The customer’s position in each security is maintained at the tax lot level for calculation of CG. Depending on the nature of the CA event:

- Either new tax lots may be created
- The cost or quantity of the existing lots may need to be updated
- Existing lots may need to be removed.

The CA events can have the following effects on the tax lots.

| Events | Description |
|---|---|
| Creation of new tax lots | When new positions are acquired from CA events, new tax lot IDs are created. The details such as event type, associated trades, date of acquisition, quantity, price, cost and others are recorded in the tax lots. |
| Adjustment of positions and cost in existing tax lots | The nominal and cost base are adjusted in the tax lots to reflect the exact nominal and cost after the CA events. Capital gain or loss may be calculated in certain scenarios. |
| Closing of tax lots | When a CA event moves out all the positions held in a tax lot, the tax lot is closed and capital gain or loss may be calculated. |
| Closing of existing lots and creating new lots | There are some CA events that require the existing lots to be closed and new lots be created. |
| Adjustment of tax lots | Adjusting cost in existing lots and creating new lots. |
| No change to tax lots | Pure income only events like cash dividends have no effect on tax lots. |

This feature explains how CG calculations are handled for CA in general. These calculations may be unique for certain complex CAs. Read each Securities – Corporate Action feature for more information.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This feature explains the setup to handle Capital Gains (CG) calculations for Corporate Actions (CA) in general.


##### SC.PARAMETER

The Cg Base Update field must be set to YES, to update the records in CG.TXN.BASE .


##### CG.PARAMETER

The following fields in the CG.PARAMETER are setup to CG calculation on CA event.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Cg Enh Process | Set to Yes for the working of all enhanced CG calculations. |
| Ca Odd Lot | Indicates how to adjust any odd nominal while apportioning nominal among the existing tax lots due to a CA. |
| Period Inc Td | Indicates whether trade date is included while determining the period of holding. If the field is set to: Yes - The trade date is included while determining the period of holding. No - It indicates that the period of holding starts from T+1 days. |

If the security is bought with trade date as 12 Jan 2018 and

is set as 12M, then the period of holding is considered to be long term on or after 13 Jan 2019.


##### CG.INVENTORY.METHOD

This application defines the conditions for individual portfolio. The value of the Period Inc Td field is defaulted from CG.PARAMETER , but the value can be changed in this application.


##### CG.CA.RULES

This application defines how CG transaction base needs to be updated for each CA event.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Income Event | If this field is flagged, then there is no update in the Cg Txn Base field. Instead, the system opens a record with entitlement ID in the ENTITLEMENT.INC.SUPP table and records the total income received from this event. This field can be set even for events such as, stock dividend where dividend is received in the form of stock. This helps to report income earned from CAs. |
| Upd Cost | If this field is flagged, then the cost of the tax parcel or lots changes because of the CA event. |
| Upd Lot Es | If shares are received or disposed as a result of CA and if this field is flagged, then the nominal or quantity of the existing tax lot is amended. |
| Es Lot Date | If nominal of existing lot is changed, then the acquisition date of the new nominal is based on the value of this field. |
| Upd Lot Ns | If new shares are received in a new security from the CA event, then this field needs to be flagged. For example, demerger event. |
| Calc Cg | This flag has to be set if CG needs to be calculated. This is critical for events where lots are disposed. |


#### 🔧 Working With

When a corporate action (CA) diary is run and entitlements are created, the system has the logic to determine the tax lots eligible for the event.

Portfolio A has qualifying nominal of 1000 on the ex-date of a CA event. Portfolio A had acquired and sold this security multiple times. Each acquisition would have created a tax lot and each disposal would have cleared out nominal from different tax lots. As on date, portfolio A may have eight tax lots of 100 nominal each.

But as on the ex-date the customer would have had 12 lots totaling 1000 nominal. When the entitlement is authorised, the system amends the 12 lots based on the setup in CG.CA.RULES . As a result, a rework of the value in Cg Txn Base field is required and the system automatically rebuilds the base and recalculates CG.


##### Cash Dividend or Coupon

Events such as cash dividend or coupon on bond are income events. Only the Income Event field is flagged as YES. The dividend or coupon amount is updated in the Corp Income Pl field in the CG.TXN.BASE application.


##### Reinvest

In reinvestment event, the customer is allowed to reinvest the dividend amount into additional securities on the dividend payment date. This can be handled in the following ways:

The reinvestment event with parameter set is handled as an income event.

- The Income Event field is set to YES.
- The entire event (dividend) amount is updated in the Corp Income Pl field in CG.TXN.BASE .

In dividend reinvestment plan (DRIP), the dividend amount is considered as income and is invested in additional securities of the same or new security. The Income Event field is set to YES. The new security is acquired at the dividend rate and acquisition date as event date. Hence the Es Lot Date or Ns Lot Date and Es Lot Cost or Ns Lot Cost fields are set to Event Date and Dividend, respectively.


##### Coupon Payment with Pool Factor

In the coupon payment with POOL.FACTOR event, the coupons are issued to the customer including the pool factor reduction. This is an income event, hence the Income Event field is set to YES. In pool factor reduction, the CG is calculated for the event. The Calc Cg field is set to YES.


##### Redemption

In REDEMPTION event, the lots redeemed are removed and the respective CG is calculated for the position.

- The Calc Cg is set to YES.
- The CG calculated is updated in the Cg Pl field in CG.TXN.BASE .


##### Bonus

In the BONUS event, the company gives extra shares to the existing shareholders. The bonus event can be handled as follows:

In the bonus event, the new security is updated as follows:

- Ns Lot Cost fields are marked as ZERO, if the event and new security are same.
- With demerged cost, the Es Lot Cost field is set to zero and the Ns Lot Cost field is marked as Demerge Cost, if the event and new security are different.
- With prorated cost if event and new security are same and with demerged cost if event and new security are different, then the Es Lot Cost field is set to Prorata and the Ns Lot Cost field is set to Demerge Cost.

Read the Stock Dividend section for more information on bonus as income event.


##### Stock Dividend

STOCK.DIV is an income event, where dividend is paid in the form of additional shares.

- The Income Event field is set to YES.
- The additional shares received are updated with cost as the dividend rate.


##### Exchange Offer

In the EXCH.OFFER event, the company exchanges the existing securities with new securities in the following ways:

- If the existing security lot is removed and replaced with new securities at the market price of the new security, then the Ns Lot Cost field is set to Mkt.Prc.
- If the existing securities are rolled over into new securities, then the Cg Rollover field is set to YES and the Ns Lot Cost field is set to Demerge Cost.


##### Stock Split

In the STOCK.SPLIT event, the new shares are issued to the existing stakeholder in proportion to their current holdings.

- The Upd Net Nom field is flagged as YES.
- The existing lots in the CG.TXN.BASE is updated based on the stock split ratio.


##### Call Payment

In the CALL.PAYMENT event, the cost of the existing securities is increased to convert the partly paid securities into fully paid securities.

- The Upd Cost field is set to YES.
- The cost of each existing lot in CG.TXN.BASE is increased by the proportionate call payment amount.


##### Worthless

The WORTHLESS event indicates that the market value of the stock has become zero. This CA always results in capital loss.

- The Calc Cg field in the CG.CA.RULES is set to YES.
- The capital loss is updated in the Cg Pl field in CG.TXN.BASE .


##### SC.ENT.INCOME.SUPP

Some corporate actions such as Cash dividend, Stock Dividend and so on are treated as income and the same is recorded for reporting to the customer. The event could result in pure cash income or in the form of stock or partly stock and partly cash. The SC.ENT.INCOME.SUPP application records the income from such events.

Certain event such as Capital Return, Demerger and so on, updates SC.ENT.INCOME.SUPP by default and certain other events can be updated only when Income Event field is enabled in CG.CA.RULES . The below table details when SC.ENT.INCOME.SUPP is updated and also how the cost of parcel (for income through stock event) is updated.

| Condition | Value in Income Type field in SC.ENT.INCOME.SUPP application | Value in Income Amt field in SC.ENT.INCOME.SUPP application | Calculation of Cost of New Parcel |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rights Event - When retail premium is declared as income | Retail Premium | Lapsed Rights * Retail Premium Rate | - |
| Capital Return | Capital Return | Qualify Holding * (Rate - Income on Rate) | - |
| Capital Return | Income | Qualify Holding * Income on Rate | - |
| Buy Back | Income | Buy Back Quantity * Income on Buy back price | - |
| Demerger –If dividend is applicable | Demerger Dividend | Nominal of New Security * Income Rate | - |
| Other Events – If Income Event is set in CG.CA.RULES | Income | Qualify Holding * Rate | - |
| Other Events – If Income Event is set in Cg.Ca.Rules | Stock Income (with rate) | Nominal of New Security * New Market price The New Mkt Price in DIARY defaults from Last Price in SECURITY.MASTER and should be changed, if required. | Nominal * New Market Price + Entitlement Amount (Residue stock remaining from Reinvest where Cash Remain in DIARY.TYPE is set to Y) |
| Other Events - If Income Event is set in CG.CA.RULES | Stock Income (with old to new ratio) | Nominal * New Market price The New Mkt Price in DIARY defaults to the Last Price in SECURITY.MASTER . If required, this should be changed to the New Price in DIARY that is, price used for Dividend Reinvestment nominal. | Nominal * New Market price The New Mkt Price in DIARY defaults to the Last Price in SECURITY.MASTER . If required, this should be changed to the New Price in DIARY that is, price used for Dividend Reinvestment nominal. |

### 9.7  Franking Credits


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Franking credits also known as an imputation credit arise from companies that are paying dividends on their earnings, where tax on these earnings are paid. These credits are granted to company shareholders to avoid the shareholders paying tax again on the dividend income.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Bond or Share*, *Cash*, *Cg Enh Process*, *Cg Method*, *Corporate Tax Rate*, *Entitlement Amount*, *Fc Hold Period Basis*, *Fc Hold Period Date* ... +33 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Franking credits also known as an imputation credit arise from companies that are paying dividends on their earnings, where tax on these earnings are paid. These credits are granted to company shareholders to avoid the shareholders paying tax again on the dividend income.

A company generates a profit and decides to pay dividend to the shareholders. If the company needs to pay a corporate tax of 30%, a corporate action event is announced at a rate of USD 10 per share. When the shareholders receive USD 7 per share (post deducting the tax) dividend, the shareholders are entitled to receive USD 3 of franking credits. The total assessable income or grossed up dividend is USD 10. The shareholders marginal tax rate determines if the shareholders have to pay the tax authority additional tax or potentially receive franking credits as a tax refund. If the individual tax rate is 30%, then the shareholder retains the USD 7 dividend per share and need not pay tax, as the company has already paid 30% tax on it.

Franking credit reduces or eliminates double taxation.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The franking credit can be set only when Cg Enh Process is set to Yes in CG.PARAMETER . The following configuration in CG.PARAMETER is necessary to calculate Franking credits.

Countries where franking credit provision is possible, the Franking Cr Allowed field should be set to Yes. This field indicates whether the system calculates franking credit details. The Franking Cr Method field defines the method to be used while calculating franking credits. The system allows Enhlifo value in Franking Cr Method field. Based on the value mentioned in the Franking Cr Method field, a CG.TXN.BASE.XXX (where XXX denotes the value in the Franking Cr Method field) is built automatically by the system.

The multi-value set Fc Sub Asset Type allows a valid record in SUB.ASSET.TYPE and the Fc Sector field allows a valid record in SECTOR for which the franking credits are set. A value ALL is set to indicate that the configuration applies to all the sub-asset types and all the sectors.

The customers are required to hold the shares for a minimum period to receive the benefits of franking credits. In CG.PARAMETER , the 45-day holding rule is applied where a customer must hold the equity shares for at least 45 days within the qualifying period, failing which the associated franking credits is lost. The Fc Holding Days field indicates the number of days the instrument must be held to qualify for franking credits, and the Fc Hold Period Date field indicates the date from which and to which the holding period is calculated.

Certain countries define the holding period exclusive of either the purchase date or the sale date or both. The Fc Hold Period Basis field is set to Neither which indicates that the customer needs to hold the shares for 45 days exclusive of the date of purchase and the date of sale. The Corporate Tax Rate field is the default corporate tax rate in the country, which is used for calculating franking credits.


#### 🔧 Working With

The working with franking credits is explained with appropriate scenario and example.

A Cash Dividend corporate action event is announced for the Google security. The bank has three portfolio holding positions in Google security, the CG.TXN.BASE of the portfolios is shown below.

Portfolio 1

The portfolio 1 has two buy transactions and a sell transaction. As the Cg Method for the portfolio is FIFO, the sale is allocated to the first transaction.

For portfolio 2 and 3, there are two buy transactions as shown in the below screenshots.


##### DIARY

A record in DIARY is created for the cash dividend event, and the following fields hold the franking credit details. The fields can be set only if Cash field is set to Y in DIARY.TYPE and Bond or Share is set to S in SECURITY.MASTER .

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Franked Credit Rate | Holds the rate or percentage that is used for computing franking credits. |
| Unfranked Rate | Holds the rate or percentage of the unfranked rate. If value is not provided, the value is defaulted as Rate (dividend rate) minus Franked Credit Rate. |
| Unfranked Cfi Rate | Holds conduit foreign income rate and should not exceed the value in Unfranked Rate field. Conduit foreign income is foreign income ultimately received by a foreign resident through one or more interposed Australian corporate tax entities (including companies and some trusts). When paid as an unfranked dividend, the payment is subject to non-resident withholding tax. |


##### ENTITLEMENTS

On authorising the record in DIARY and running the corporate action service, the record in ENTITLEMENT is created in INAU status. As the Rate is provided as 10 and the Qualifying Holdings is 1500, the Entitlement Amount is USD 15000.

| Date | Transaction Type | Quantity /Rate |
|---|---|---|
| March 25 | Buy | 1000 |
| April 8 | Buy | 1000 |
| April 23 | Ex-dividend date | USD 10 per share + franking credits |
| April 24 | Buy | 1000 |
| April 27 | Sell | 1000 |

| Field Name | Purpose | Formula | Values as per the screenshot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Franked Dividend | Holds the franking dividend amount for the entitlement. | Franked Credit Rate * Qual Holding | = 3* 1400 = USD 4200 |
| Franking Credits | Hold sthe Franking credits for this entitlement in Event Currency. | Franked Dividend * Corporate Tax Rate / (1- Corporate Tax Rate ) | = 4200 *30% /(1-30%) =USD 1800 |
| Unfranked Cfi | Holds the Unfranked CFI for this entitlement. | Unfranked Cfi Rate * Qual Holdings | =3*1400 = USD 4200 |
| Unfranked Ncfi Rate | Holds the Unfranked Non-Conduit Foreign Income (NCFI) rate. | Unfranked Rate – Unfranked Cfi Rate | = 7 - 3 = USD 4 |
| Unfranked Ncfi | Holds the Unfranked NCFI for the entitlement. | Unfranked Ncfi Rate * Qual Holdings | = 4 *1400 = USD 5600 |
| Net Dividend | Holds the entitlement amount. | Rate * Qual Holdings | = 10*1400 = USD 14000 |
| Gross Dividend | Indicates a dividend inclusive of franking credits. | Net Dividend + Franking Credits | =14000+1800 =USD 15800 |


#### 📋 Tasks

A Franking Credit is a tax credit paid by corporations to their shareholders along with their dividend payments. Countries such as, Australia, allow franking credits as a way to reduce or eliminate double taxation.

#### 📖 Introduction

Every transaction that results in crediting nominal to a position is maintained as a separate tax lot for the purpose of capital gain (CG) calculations. The tax lots undergo changes such as change in cost, nominal and so on, due to events like corporate actions (CA) or cost base adjustments. The system automatically updates these changes when such events occur.

However, there may be situations where the tax lots need to be manually adjusted. This is particularly the case for tax lots of externally held positions, where CA are handled externally and the effect of the event needs to be updated in the system.

This feature explains how tax lots are manually adjusted. Familiarity in all features of Capital Gains module leads to better understanding of this feature.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The capital gains processing are parameterised in the system. The Cg Enh Process field is set to Yes in CG.PARAMETER, to allow reconstruction or rollover of tax lots.


#### 🔧 Working With

Tax lots are adjusted in four ways:

- Increase cost - The cost of selected tax lots are increased
- Decrease cost - The cost of selected tax lots are decreased
- Reconstruction - The nominal and/or cost of selected tax lots are adjusted
- Rollover - All or part of the nominal in a tax lot is rolled over to a new CG.TXN.BASE

All the above adjustments are done using the CG.ADJUST.BASE application.


##### Reconstruction of Shared or Non-shared asset

This type of transaction allows adjustment of nominal and/or cost. The adjustments are automatically affected in CG.TXN.BASE . If there is an increase or decrease in total nominal due to the reconstruction, the system automatically updates SECURITY.POSITION . Similarly any change in cost is also adjusted in SECURITY.POSITION automatically.

When there is a change in nominal, the system creates either a SECURITY.TRANS out or a SECURITY.TRANS in record from this application to build the SECURITY.POSITION . If there are multiple positions, the system creates multiple records SECURITY.TRANS . The CG.ADJUST.BASE record ID is updated in the created record in SECURITY.TRANS .

The below screenshot shows The reconstruction of tax lots for a particular CG.TXN.BASE on pro rata basis upon adding 150 units.

The different fields and the corresponding application behaviour is explained in the below table.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Apply to all | If set to Yes, the system pro rates the Total Units to Adj or the Total Amt to Adjust among the retrieved lots. The system then automatically pro-rates and updates the value in Adj Red Cost and Adj Trd Cost fields in case of adjustment in cost and Adj Nominal in case of adjustment in nominal |
| Retrieve Lots | If set to Open, the system retrieve only the open credit tax lots as of current date for adjustment. If it is set to Open on Eff Dt, the system retrieves and displays all lots that were open as on the Tax Effective Date in the transaction |
| Create New Lot | If this field is set and the units are increased, the system: Creates the new units as a separate new lot with the acquisition date being the acquisition date of the old parcel Updates the tax effective date of the new parcel being the tax effective date specified in the CG.ADJUST.BASE transaction |

> **⚠️ Note:** In either case only lots open after the locking date is retrieved.

The unrealised gains of a security before reconstruction is shown in the below screenshot.

After reconstruction, the open nominal is increased based on Adj Nom field.


##### Increase Cost

The cost of selected tax lots are increased or decreased with respect to the Txn Type being set to Increase cost or Decrease cost. When the cost is increased or decreased, the cost of tax lot is also suitably increased or decreased along with history being maintained.

If the increase or decrease cost has an acquisition date given and such date is within the indexation period, indexed cost of the adjustment needs to be specified. Else, the system assumes that there is no change to the indexed cost.

> **⚠️ Note:** Either Per unit Cost Adj or Total Amt to Adjust must be specified and not both.

The unrealised gains of a security before increasing the cost is shown in the below screenshot.

After the increased cost transaction is authorised, the cost base is increased with respect to the value mentioned in the Adj Trd Cost field.


##### Decrease Cost

This is similar to increase cost. However, the Total Amt to Adjust or the Adj Cost Per Unit is specified with a negative sign.

The unrealised gains of a security before decreasing the cost is shown in the below screenshot.

The unrealised gains of a security after decreasing the cost is shown in the below screenshot.


##### Rollover of Shared asset

Selected tax lots are rolled over to a new security. The rollover is a full rollover, if system automatically moves all the lots to a new security or if Full Rollover is not flagged, user can manually select the lots and nominal to be rolled over.

If the Txn Type is set to Rollover, te system creates a SECURITY.TRANS out record for the rolled-over lots and a SECURITY.TRANS in record for the new security units with same external custodian as in the existing security. The SECURITY.TRANS in this case creates parcels as explained in the below table.

| Rollover | Description |
|---|---|
| Full | The system creates as many open lots in the CG.TXN.BASE of acquired security, as the open lots in the current security, with same acquisition date and cost as in the current security. |
| Blank | The system rolls over the parcels that the user has specified to rollover, along with mentioned cost. |

The full rollover from one security to another is shown in the below screenshot.

Unrealized gains report of a security before rollover is shown in the below screenshot.

Unrealized gains report of another security after rollover is shown in the below screenshot.
