#### 📖 Introduction

Customers licensing the tax lots feature of Temenos Transact must migrate the existing tax lots from their legacy system to Temenos Transact. During migration process, outstanding positions are first moved into Temenos Transact. This is done either by a single transaction or by re-capturing of certain transactions.

All individual transactions are rarely migrated. Hence, it is not advisable for the system to build the tax lots automatically while migrating transactions. The tax lots have to be captured separately after migrating the positions into the system.

This feature explains how Temenos Transact supports migration of tax lots from an external system to Temenos Transact and how the tax lots are built after the migration process.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Cg Base Update in SC.PARAMETER is initially set to No when the external positions are brought into the system. This ensures that tax lots are not built by the system, when positions are migrated.

Once the positions are migrated into the system, the Cg Base Update field in SC.PARAMETER needs to be set to Yes. This enables migration of tax lots using the process explained in this document. Also, tax lots are automatically handled for transactions input in the system post migration.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the workflow of various capital gains (CG) related applications pertaining to the migration of tax lots to Temenos Transact .


##### SECURITY.TRANSFER

Initially the external positions are brought into the system using the SECURITY.TRANSFER application and the Cg Base Update is set to No in SC.PARAMETER . The below screenshot shows that the entire positions are moved into the system to the respective portfolio and security.

The CG.TXN.BASE is not created as soon as the above record is committed.


##### CG.MIGRATE.INPUT

This application allows the migration of the tax lots. The CG.BASE.UPDATE must be set to Yes in SC.PARAMETER . This application has all fields related to CG.TXN.BASE . The ID of this record is same as that of CG.TXN.BASE and consists the following three parts:

- Customer ID
- Portfolio or Group ID
- Security ID

The user can migrate all the lots that make up the position by entering the transaction date and time, nomials, cost and other details for each lot. In this case, the Sec Trans ID must be keyed in, which could be the transaction ID in the old system used for tracking purposes or any free ID.

When a record in CG.MIGRATE.INPUT is committed, Temenos Transact checks if the total open positions match the closing nominal in SECURITY.POSITION . If it does not match, the system does not allow the record to be committed.

> **⚠️ Note:** Migration of tax lots can be done only once. However, the tax lots can be amended using either CG.ENH.MANUAL.INPUT or CG.ADJUST.BASE applications. Read the Manual Adjustment of Tax lots feature for more information.

Sell (debit) lots pertaining to current tax year can be migrated. Sell lots pertaining to previous year can be migrated provided the tax rework date for that year is not lapsed. Sell transactions can be migrated after this tax rework date. Once the above record is committed, the CG.TXN.BASE is updated with the details as shown in the below screenshot.


#### 📋 Tasks

Clients licensing the tax lots feature of core banking system should migrate existing tax lots from their legacy system to core banking system.

During migration process, outstanding positions are first moved into the core banking system. This can be done either by a single transaction or by re-capturing certain transactions.

All individual transactions are rarely migrated. Hence, it is not advisable for the system to build the tax lots automatically while migrating transactions.

The tax lots have to be captured separately after migration of the positions into the system.


##### Workflow

This section helps the user to perform the below tasks:

The ID of this record is same as that of CG.TXN.BASE and consists of three parts:

- Customer ID
- Portfolio or Group ID
- Security ID

2. In the Contract Screen, enter a value in the CG Migrate Input Details field and then click the Edit icon.
3. Enter values in the following fields: Trade Date Time.1 Sec Trans ID.1 Portfolio.1 Txn Type.1 Nominal.1 Value.1 Open Nominal.1 Open Nom Cost.1 Open Reduced Cost.1 Index Factor.1 Open Indexed Cost.1 CG Expenses.1 Cost Per Unit.1 Avg Cost Per Unit.1 Avg Cost.1 Ext Custodian
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon.

#### 📖 Introduction

Introduction to Retail Sweeping ⓘ Content migrated: Old structure mapped (To be planned)

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

Capital Gain (CG) is a gain realised when an asset is sold or disposed at a price higher than the acquisition price. In most countries, CGs are taxed in the hands of the investor. The method of calculating CGs differs for each country. Many countries have different rules based on the period the asset was held.

Some regulations allow the acquisition price to be adjusted based on the consumer price or inflation index. Further, certain individuals or asset categories can be exempt from CGs.

The key basis for CG calculation is storing details of the asset particularly the date and time of acquisition, the cost and the number of units acquired. Assets such as equities are bought and sold multiple times. The acquisition cost varies from one lot to another. Therefore, each acquisition must be stored as separate parcels or lots. The gains differ depending on the lot selected for disposal.

CG calculation is a complex process and hence Temenos Transact is flexible to handle a variety of calculation methods.

> **⚠️ Note:** Tax Lots (TL) module handles the enhanced CG processing. All features in the TL module pertain to the enhanced process. Simple CG processing can work even if TL module is not licensed. To understand what is supported in the simple method, Read the Capital Gains (tax lot handling) feature for more information.


##### Product Configuration

The following basic setup needs to be done in the system to calculate Capital Gains (CGs).

The CG Base Update field in the SC.PARAMETER indicates whether the CGs base is to be updated or not. If this field is set to YES, it indicates that the system maintains the CGs base ( CG.TXN.BASE ), where tax lot details are maintained and is the base for CG calculation.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Net Long Term Loss and Net Short Term Loss | Indicate if the long- or short-term loss can be offset only against long- or short-term gain or both |
| Lt Loss Cf Years and St Loss Cf Years | Indicate the number of years that the long- and short-term loss can be carried forward |
| Max Amt Cf Lt and Max Amt Cf St | Specifies the maximum amount of long- and short-term losses carried forward per year |
| Annual Adj Amt Lt and Annual Adj Amt St | Specify the maximum carried forward long- and short-term losses that can be set-off against gains per year. |
| Long Term Period | Specifies whether the disposal of security falls under long or short term. Any holding less than this period is treated as a short-term holding. |
| Short Term Rate and Long Term Rate | Specify the rate applicable for holding. |
| CA Odd Lot | Specifies whether the odd nominal are to be adjusted in the first or last lot. |
| CG Calc Param | Holds the relevant data for a particular country’s CG calculation. |
| Sep External Lots | This field is set to Yes to maintain separate tax records for external custody positions. If this field is left blank, then both the external and on-platform positions are updated in the same CG.TXN.BASE . |
| Franking Cr Allowed | This field is set to Yes only in countries where franking credits are allowed. |
| Retain Specific Lot | Ensures that any specifically selected lot remains untouched while reworking. It remains as originally allocated and only the other lots are reworked. |
| Recalc Lock Date | Reallocates and calculates capital gains or losses up to the mentioned date. |

This application supports the grouping of multiple portfolios into a group. The ID of the record is a valid customer ID. Only portfolios of the same customer can be grouped for CG calculation.

The name under which the portfolios are grouped is defined in the Group Name field. Under enhanced CG process, that is, where the CG Enh Process field is set to Yes in CG.PARAMETER , the portfolio grouping can allow only one portfolio in a group.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| CG Method | Defines the tax lot method applicable for each set. Only the methods allowed in the CG.PARAMETER can be set here. |
| Date to | Denotes the date till when the values defined in the corresponding multi-value set are applicable. These dates must be given in descending order, that is the oldest date in the last multi-value set. The first date must be left blank. |
| Long Term Period | The tax lot held less than the period defined in this field is treated as a short-term holdings. If left blank, then the value is defaulted from the CG.PARAMETER . |
| Long Term Rate and Short Term Rate | The tax rate applicable for short and long term holdings are defined in these fields. |
| Discount Factor | Denotes the discount factor (in percentage) used to calculate discounted PL. |
| Adjustment Factor | Calculates the tax liability under TAFO method. |


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

CG.PARAMETER is a company-level parameter to define the tax methods and the relevant attributes for capital gains (CG) calculations. The fields available in this parameter are listed below.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Cg Method 1 | Indicates the particular capital gains method applicable upto the date defined in the Date To field |
| Date To 1 | Used to set up the end dates for each of Cg Method . Dates need to be defined in descending order, that is, oldest date in the lowest sub-value. The Latest Date To 1 field cannot be populated with any value as it relates to the current period |
| Reacq Prd | Indicates the period of time elapsed between a sale and subsequent purchase, so that the purchase is not regarded as a repurchase of that sale |
| Reacq Drop Loss | Specifies whether this is a requirement to drop any loss associated with a sale |
| Cg Incl Accr Int | Indicates whether accrued interest is included in the calculation of the CG profit and loss or not |
| Cg Incl Expense | Indicates whether expenses are included in the calculation of the CG and loss or not |
| Wcg Incl Accr Int | Indicates whether accrued interest is included in the calculation of the CG withheld tax profit and loss |
| Wcg Incl Expense | Indicates whether expenses are included in the calculation of the CG withheld tax profit and loss |
| Wht Tax Type | Indicates the record from TAX.TYPE which is used for CG tax calculation |
| Use Infl Indx | Specifies whether inflation indexation is applied to the specified CG. If left blank, inflation indexation is not applied |
| CG Methods Allowed 1 | Indicates the list of methods allowed for tax lot allocation and CG calculations. The methods listed in this field can alone be used in setting up the portfolio-specific allocation |
| Long Term Period | Holds a time period that determines whether asset needs to be considered as long or short term. Any holding for less than this period is treated as a short-term holding |
| Trade Date Included | Determines the calculation of long-term period of holding |
| CG Enh Process | Set as YES for the working of all enhanced CG calculation |
| CG Calc Param | Holds relevant data for a particular country’s CG calculation |
| Tax Acquisition Date 1 | Indicates the acquisition date for the lots created through Corporate Action (CA) event |
| Tax Disposal Date 1 | Indicates the disposal date for the lots disposed through CA event |
| Cg Adj Txn Type | Defines the transaction codes used for CG adjustments |
| Retain Specific Lot | Indicates whether a specific tax lot needs to be retained or not during CG rebuild process. |
| Cg Fcy Acc | Indicates whether capital gain has to be calculated for movements in FCY account. |

### 9.11  Rebuild Capital Gains


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
>

#### 📖 Introduction

Capital gains (CG) are calculated when a position is sold at a cost higher than the cost of acquisition. Assets such as equities are bought and sold multiple times. The acquisition cost varies from one lot to another. Therefore, each acquisition should be stored as separate parcel or lot. The gains differ depending on the lot that is selected for disposal. Every time a security is disposed, the system determines the tax lots that need to be allocated for the disposal based on the tax lot allocation method. It then calculates the capital gain or loss on the disposal.

Sometimes, complete rebuild of the tax lot base is required and the rebuild results in different lots being allocated for disposal transactions. This in turn results in re-computation of CG.

Rebuilding of CG base is required in the following scenarios:

1. When a back-dated transaction is input in the system.
2. When a transaction is reversed.
3. When allocation or inventory method changes.
4. Where there is a position transfer from one portfolio to another and the source portfolio is rebuilt. Here the destination portfolio must also be rebuilt.
5. Where corporate action (CA) criteria is received late.
6. When a manual rebuild is triggered by the user.

This feature document describes how the CG base is rebuilt in each of the above scenarios.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Cg Enh Process field in CG.PARAMETER is set to Yes, as shown in the below screenshot.


##### Lock at Portfolio Level

Once the tax details are finalised for a year, it is not advisable to rebuild the tax base for the completed period. The lock date can be set at portfolio level or at parameter level. If the Recalc Lock Level field in CG.PARAMETER is set to Parameter, the lock date is specified at company level—in CG.PARAMETER . If it is set to Sec.acc.master, the lock date is specified only at portfolio level—in SEC.ACC.MASTER .

If

is 31 APR 2019, it means the parcels before April 31, 2019 are locked and cannot be reworked.

Only the portfolios for which the Recalc Lock Date is specified are considered locked. Other portfolios can be reworked from any date.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Recalc Lock Date is the last date of any earlier tax year. If system is currently in April 2020 and the tax year is from January to December, this date can be December 31, 2018 or 2019. If a rebuild is triggered in April 2020, disposals after December 31, 2018 or 2019 as the case maybe, is rebuilt.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section provides various scenarios where rebuilding of tax lots can take place.


##### Rebuild of CG base due to post adjustments: Corporate actions

In some corporate actions (CA) events like Demerger, a few tax related attributes during the event are updated based on provisional numbers. The attributes are confirmed post the event, based on a rule from the tax authority. Some of the tax related attributes that can change post the event are:

- Book cost split ratio (between the original and new security)
- Deemed market proceeds
- Notional capital return
- Capital return
- Tax acquisition date (this does not impact if the new parcels are updated with original acquisition date)
- Tax effective date
- Tax disposal date
- Rollover type (mostly moving from no rollover to full rollover or rollover relief or capital return)
- Rollover non resident
- Rollover for PRE CGT
- Capital return
- Income

Therefore, the SC.POST.EVENT.ADJUST application is used to adjust the tax base post entitlement authorisation. The ID of this application is the DIARY ID.


##### Rebuild Due to Change in Inventory Method or Rebuild from a Specific Date

Portfolios are reallocated through the CG.REALLOCATE.BASE application. This is predominantly used for any year-end adjustments where the customer chooses to change the inventory method (example, FIFO to LIFO). The ID is a valid portfolio ID.

The Retain Specific Lot field ensures that the parcels allocated to a sale through specific parcel selection are not affected by this year-end method change. If the Period Begin field is specified, the rework (based on new method) happens only for transactions on or after the period begin date—tax effective date of the transaction on or after this begin date. The Period End date can be either last date of the previous or current tax year.

If period begin date is December 01, 2018, any transactions with effective date from December 01, 2018 to December 31, 2019 are reworked based on the new inventory method.

Once the above record is authorised, the Status field of the record becomes Active. After running the CG.REALLOCATE.TXN.BASE service, the Status field of the record is changed to Processed as shown in the screenshot below.


##### Rebuild Source Portfolio After Position Transfer

For internal ’in specie’ transfer, the tax lots are migrated from the source to destination portfolio. The source portfolio is reallocated as a result of a change in inventory method, back-dated trade or a reversal of a transaction. As a result, the destination portfolio is also reallocated.

If position transfer is done, the

field should be manually set to Yes for not calculating CG.

The screenshot below shows the tax lot history of the source portfolio. The lots are removed (disposed) from the source portfolio and migrated to the destination portfolio (on their respective record in CG.TXN.BASE ). The Cg Method used is FIFO. Therefore, the first and second lots are allocated against the sell and transfer-out transaction.

To cascade the effect of reallocation to destination portfolio the Dest Base field in CG.TXN.BASE of the source portfolio stores the CG.TXN.BASE ID of the destination portfolio. As part of reallocation of the source portfolio, if there is any change to Pur Txn Id and Pur Txn Nom fields (associated with position transfer multi-value set), then the CG.TXN.BASE of the destination portfolio is reprocessed by removing the old lots and inserting the new lots.

The Dest Base and Dest Trans Id fields are available only when Cg Exempt is set to Yes in the POSITION.TRANSFER application. The below screenshot is the CG.TXN.BASE of the source portfolio after position transfer.

The CG.TXN.BASE of the destination portfolio is shown in the below screenshot. The Source Base field holds the CG.TXN.BASE ID of the source portfolio.

The Cg Method in source portfolio is changed from FIFO to LIFO. The CG.REALLOCATE.TXN.BASE service is used for the reallocation of tax base.

The tax lot history of the source portfolio after running the above service is shown in the below screenshot. The Cg Method is changed to LIFO. The sell transaction is allocated to the third lot and the transfer out is allocated to the second and third lot.

The tax lot history of the destination portfolio is shown in the below screenshot. The destination portfolio is changed as a result of change in source portfolio.


##### Rebuild of CG Base due to Trade Reversal

If a buy transaction pertaining to current or previous tax year is reversed after the rework locking date for that year, then the system checks if the buy transaction has been allocated to a sell. If not, that is, if the tax lot is fully open, then:

- The system allows the transaction to be reversed.
- The corresponding tax lot in CG.TXN.BASE is removed.

This lot is ignored for all future allocations.

> **⚠️ Note:** If a buy transaction pertaining to current or previous tax year is reversed before the rework locking date for that year, the system throws an error that the reversal of transaction before the locking date is not allowed.

If the lot has been fully or partially allotted to a sell transaction of the current year, the system allows the reversal. The tax lot is removed from the CG.TXN.BASE and the sell transactions to which this was allotted. The system re-allocates and re-works CG for all records in CG.TXN.BASE . If this lot is specifically allocated to a sell, the system is unallocated and simply use the default allocation method or FIFO to do the re-allocation.

However, if the lot has been fully or partially allotted to some sell transaction and if this transaction pertains to a locked period, the system does not allow the transaction to be reversed. The tax lot history before a reversal of trade is shown in the below screenshot. The sell transaction is allocated to the first buy.

If the first buy transaction is reversed, the system automatically reallocates the sell transaction based on the tax lot method prevailing at the time of the sale.


##### Rebuild of CG Base due to Back-dated Transaction

A back-dated buy or credit transaction is updated as of the backdate. The sell transactions during the current tax year are re-worked and tax lots are re-allotted based on the tax lot method prevailing at the time of each sale. In a back-dated sell or debit transaction, if the sell date is in the current tax year, the transaction is updated as of the backdate. The current years allotments are re-worked based on the tax lot method prevailing on the sell date. Assume that the portfolio 100285-1 has the following transaction as shown in the screenshot below.

A back-dated buy transaction is input as shown in the below screenshot. The system automatically reworks the sell transaction and the tax lots are reallocated based on the Tax Lot Method set as FIFO.


#### 📋 Tasks

Capital gains are calculated when a position is sold at a cost higher than the cost of acquisition. Every time a security is disposed, system determines the tax lots that need to be allocated for the disposal based on the tax lot allocation method. It then calculates the capital gain or loss on the disposal. Rebuilding of capital gains base is required in the following scenarios:

- When a back-dated transaction is entered in the system.
- When a transaction is reversed.
- When allocation or inventory method changes.
- Where there is a position transfer from one portfolio to another and the source portfolio is rebuilt. Here, the destination portfolio also have to be rebuilt.
- Where corporate action criteria is received late.
- A manual rebuild is triggered by the user.

### 9.12  Staples

#### 📖 Introduction

Stapled securities are formed when two or more securities are contractually bound together, so that they cannot be sold separately but are instead treated as a single security on the stock exchange. Different types of securities can be stapled together, for example, shares, units and debt instruments, for example, a stapled security consists of a share in a company and an interest in a trust.

The effect of stapling is that each individual security retains its legal character and variation to the rights or obligations are not attached to the individual securities. For tax purposes, each underlying component (share, unit or debenture) must be a separate asset with its own attributes (cost base and acquisition date).

A stapled security is dealt as a whole so that the individual securities that are stapled cannot be individually traded on the stock exchange. Stapled securities are commonly traded in Australia Securities Exchange (ASX). This document explains how Temenos Transact supports the working of staple securities and the necessary configuration required.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following configuration is required to record a stapled security instrument.


##### SECURITY.MASTER

This application holds the necessary attributes to indicate whether the security is a stapled security or not. The below screenshot shows the parent stapled security. The Stapled Security field indicates whether the security is a parent or a child stapled security.

The below screenshots demonstrates two stapled child securities indicated by the Stapled Security field. The Stapled Parent Sec field denotes the parent stapled security for the child.


##### CG.PARAMETER

This application holds the parameters pertaining to the capital gains processing. The Cg Method is set to Min Gain. When the Rebuild Staple Parcel field is set to No, then the parcels created through off-market transactions (such as SECURITY.TRANSFER , CG.ENH.MANUAL.INPUT and CG.STAPLE.ENH.MANUAL.INPUT) are excluded from the staples rebuild process. As these parcels are brought in manually, it is expected that the bank user makes the necessary adjustments manually as provided below. The Staple Alloc Level field denotes whether the allocation is at parent or child level. When Staple Alloc Level field is set to Parent, then the allocation is at the parent level (that is, all the child allocations are stapled together). When Staple Alloc Level field is set to blank, the child allocations are independent of other child allocations.

The Staple Parent Check field can be enabled only if Staple Alloc Level field is set to Parent. This field is used when the Cg Method field is set to Fifo. If the Staple Parent Check field is enabled, then during a disposal transaction the earliest open parcel of the primary child (based on the setup in SC.STAPLED.COMPONENT ) is allocated and the corresponding sibling is allocated for the other child. If this field is not set, FIFO is allocated independently, that is during the disposal transaction the earliest lot of each child would be allocated individually.

> **⚠️ Note:** Once the Staple Alloc Level field is set as Parent or blank and SC.STAPLED.COMPONENT is built for the staple securities, then the Staple Alloc Level field cannot be changed or amended.


##### SC.STAPLED.COMPONENT

This application captures the child component security for the parent security and its respective component ratio and value split. The first part of the ID contains the SECURITY.MASTER ID of the parent stapled security and the second part of the ID contains the effective date.

- The ID can accept a valid SECURITY.MASTER ID, where the Stapled Security field is set to Parent.
- The Effective Date can be back-dated or future dated.
- For back-dated acquisition, the attributes prevailing at the time of trade date is applicable.

For unrealised capital gains report, the prevailing value split at the time of the report run date is used in arriving at the market value of the child components.

| Effective Date | Value Split of 800009-002 | Value Split of 800009-003 |
|---|---|---|
| February 1 2020 | 70% | 30% |
| March 1 2020 | 20% | 80% |
| April 1 2020 | 50% | 50% |

When the Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set to Parent

The Comp Ratio field is to 1 and the remaining setup remains the same as Example 1.


#### 🔧 Working With

The processing of staples varies depending on the setup in the Staple Alloc Level field in CG.PARAMETER . When the Staple Alloc Level is set to blank in CG.PARAMETER , the child allocation is independent of another child allocation. However, when the Staple Alloc Level field is set to Parent in CG.PARAMETER , the child allocations cannot be independent and can be stapled together, that is, the parcel allocated for each child must be from the same parent purchase transaction.

There are a few changes on how Temenos Transact handles the allocation based on parent or child setup.


##### Acquiring a Stapled Security

The following transaction takes place for the portfolio 100404-1.

| Security | Date | Transaction Type | Quantity | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800009-001 | February 5 2020 | Buy | 200 | 15 |
| 800009-001 | March 10 2020 | Buy | 300 | 20 |

The below screenshot shows the SEC.TRADE for the parent security. For the securities where Stapled Security is set to Child, trading is blocked that is, an error is generated when a SEC.TRADE or SEC.OPEN.ORDER is booked for such child instrument.

When a stapled security is purchased, the CG.TXN.BASE of the stapled security (parent security) is not built. Instead, the CG.TXN.BASE for each component of the stapled (identified by Stapled Component in SC.STAPLED.COMPONENT application) is updated. The Traded Nominal is calculated as Buy Quantity * Comp Ratio of the associated component. The Traded Value is calculated as trade cost of the Parent * Value Split of the associated component in SC.STAPLED.COMPONENT .

| Date | Value Split | Comp Ratio | Quantity of Parent | Purchase Amount (AUD) | Traded Nominal | Traded Value (AUD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| February 5 2020 | 70% | 2 | 200 | =200*15 =3000 | =200*2 =400 | =70%*3000 =2100 |
| March 102020 | 20% | 2 | 300 | =300*20 =6000 | =300*2 =600 | =20%*6000 =1200 |

When the Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set to Parent.

The process is same as explained when the Staple Alloc Level is set to blank. However, the Comp Ratio of the child security is set as 1 in SC.STAPLED.COMPONENT , that is each unit of the parent security acquired corresponds to one unit of child security. The below screenshot displays the details of the CG transaction.

The screenshot below shows the CG.TXN.BASE of the child securities 800009-002 and 800009-003 which is updated similarly, as explained above. However, the Parent Tax lot Id field is updated with a unique identifier, which links the parcel to the parent transaction. For each purchase transaction (for the parent), the same identifier is updated to all the child parcels. The same Parent Tax Lot Id is used for both the child securities against the first buy transaction. Thus, the parcels originating from the same purchase transactions are stapled together.


##### Holding a Stapled Security

The process of valuation and unrealised gains reporting is same as the Staple Alloc Level field in CG.PARAMETER is set to blank or Parent.

When a staple security is acquired, positions are created for both the parent and underlying child components using the child parent ratio. Whenever there is a security movement on the staple security, the corresponding security movement in the child security also takes effect. However, the security positions for the child is excluded from valuation.

Daily valuation is done only at the parent level. The Stapled Security field in SECURITY.POSITION distinguishes between the child and parent stapled security and is used to exclude the child from valuation.

If the capital gain or loss is reported at the parcel level, the market value of the parent is apportioned (based on the prevailing value split ratio) across the child securities. The resultant market value of the child security is used in calculating the unrealized capital gain or loss.

As on April 17 2020, the price of 800009-001 is AUD 22 and the value split is 50%. The market value of 800009-002 purchased on 05 Feb 2020 is calculated as

22*0.5*400 = AUD 4400.


##### Disposing Stapled Security

The following transaction takes place for the portfolio 100404-1.

| Security | Date | Transaction Type | Quantity | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800009-001 | April 17 2020 | Sell | 200 | 25 |

The allocation is based on minimum gain as the Cg Method is set as Min Gain in CG.PARAMETER .

| Date | Value Split | Comp Ratio | Quantity of Parent | Proceeds (AUD) | Traded Nominal | Traded Value (AUD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| April 17 2020 | 50% | 2 | 200 | =200*25 = 5000 | =200*2 =400 | =50%*5000 = 2500 |

| Date | Value Split | Comp Ratio | Quantity of Parent | Proceeds (AUD) | Traded Nominal | Traded Value (AUD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| April 17 2020 | 50% | 2 | 200 | =200*25 =5000 | =200*1 =200 | =50%*5000 =2500 |


##### Transferring the Position of Stapled Security

‘In-specie’ transfer is effected through the POSITION.TRANSFER application, where a security position is transferred from one portfolio to another. In case of stapled security, the parcels of the component security (child security) is migrated from the source to the destination portfolio.

The transferring process is the same when Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set to blank or Parent.

When a stapled security is transferred from one portfolio to another portfolio without a change in beneficial owner, the child parcels are migrated from the source to the destination portfolio. The beneficial owner (No Change in Beneficial Owner (NCBO) transfer) is not changed and so the original acquisition cost and acquisition date is transferred to the destination portfolio.

The screenshot below shows the transfer of position of the parent security from the portfolio 100404-1 to 100404-2 using POSITION.TRANSFER . The Cg Exempt field is set to Yes to indicate the transfer is a NCBO transfer.

Once the above record is authorised, the CG.TXN.BASE of the source portfolio is updated as shown in the below screenshot. The lots are removed using the disposal method (by setting disposal method as Min gain as shown in the example below) applicable to the source portfolio. However, the capital gain is marked as zero.

The SECURITY.POSITION of the destination portfolio 100404-2 is shown in the below screenshot.

The CG.TXN.BASE of the destination portfolio 100404-2 is shown in the below screenshot. The Source Base field holds the CG.TXN.BASE ID of the source portfolio. The Trade Date and Time , Trade Nominal and Trade Value of the source portfolio are retained in the destination portfolio.


##### Performing Provisional Transfers

Off-market transfers can happen either when the parcel history is known upfront or not known upfront. Provisional transfers are done when the tax lot or parcel history is not known upfront. The SECURITY.TRANSFER application is used to bring the position into the system and a single provisional tax lot parcel is created. This is a placeholder parcel, which is subsequently replaced when the actual tax lot history is known. The below screenshot shows 200 nominal for Portfolio 100404-3 transferred on the date April 16 2020.

For such off-market transfers into the portfolio, the parcel history is provided by the investor or originating bank at a later stage. Such parcels are generally excluded from rebuilder process since the parcel history is owned by the investor or originating bank. In such cases, the Staple Parcel Rebuild field is set to No.

This provisional transfer functionality is extended to the components of the staple security, that is, when a security transfer is effected, positions are created for child securities.

When the Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set to blank.

The below screenshot shows that the SECURITY.POSITION is updated for both parent and child stapled securities.

The CG.TXN.BASE for the child parcels are updated as shown in the below screenshot.

Subsequently, when the break-up of the tax lot of the position is known, the single lot created at the time of the provisional transfer-in must be replaced with multiple lots representing the break-up. This is done using the CG.ENH.MANUAL.INPUT application.

> **⚠️ Note:** This break-up of tax lots is done manually for each child.

The below screenshot shows that the security 800009-002 for portfolio 100404-3 is split into two parcels. The Staple Parent Rebuild field indicates whether the parcels created by the transaction can be modified during staples rebuilder process.

Once the above record is authorised, the CG.TXN.BASE is updated as shown in the below screenshot. The Staple Rebuild field with the value set to No indicates the parcel is being ignored during staples rebuilder.

Read Capital Gain on Transfers for more information on CG.ENH.MANUAL.INPUT application.

When the Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set as Parent.

The below screenshot shows that the SECURITY.POSITION is updated for both parent and child stapled securities.

The CG.TXN.BASE for the child parcels is updated as shown in the below screenshot.

Since the allocation is at parent level it is necessary that the system retrieves the lot, based on the value in the Parent Tax Lot Id field. The CG.STAPLE.ENH.MANUAL.INPUT application replaces the single lot created with multiple lots.

The bank user has to enter the Portfolio No , Security No and the Master Lot Ref fields which is the parent tax lot ID. Once the bank user enters the details and validates it, the system retrieves the lots of both the child securities.

The user can now provide the tax break-up details for both the child securities and commit the record. The Parent Tax Lot Id field is automatically updated by the system. The Parent Tax lot Id against the first parcel is the same for both the child securities, and similarly the Parent Tax lot Id against the second parcel is the same. This means that breakup of tax lots happen, say into two parcels TL1, TL2 for child 1 and TL3 ,TL4 for child 2, the parent tax lot id for TL1 & TL3 are the same indicating they are from the same buy and TL2 and TL4 are the same.

> **⚠️ Note:** The child security can have different cost and acquisition dates. However, the nominal split for each child has to be the same.

Once this record is authorised, the system updates the parcel as shown in the below screenshot.


##### Migrating Tax Lots

The SECURITY.TRANSFER application is used for migration of position. This creates records in SECURITY.POSITION for a parent and for each child. The CG.MIGRATE.INPUT application is used for migration of tax lots. The migration of tax lots is done for each child separately. The migration process is the same when Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set to blank or Parent. However, the Parent Tax Lot Id field must be set to Parent when the allocation is at the parent Level.

> **⚠️ Note:** As each child is migrated separately, the user has to update the correct value in Parent Tax Lot Id field in each child.

Read Migration of Tax Lots for more information.


##### Rebuilding of Stapled Securities

The rebuilding of transactions occurs when the value split across the underlying securities is published with a backward effective date. The staples rebuilder process is the same when Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set to blank or Parent except that the allocation is at parent level when the CG.PARAMETER is set to Parent . The below example is a scenario when Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set to blank.

Example

If the SC.STAPLED.COMPONENT is built for the security 800009-001 (Read Configuring Staples for more information). The following is the trade for the portfolio 100291-2.

| Security | Date | Transaction Type | Quantity | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800009-001 | Feb 5, 2020 | Buy | 200 | 15 |
| 800009-001 | Mar 10, 2020 | Buy | 300 | 20 |
| 800009-001 | Mar 16, 2020 | Buy | 200 | 23 |
| 800009-001 | Apr 16, 2020 | Sell | 200 | 25 |

The screenshot below shows the position for the portfolio.

The capital gains calculation for the portfolio is shown below. As the allocation method is selected as Min Gain, the sale is allocated to the first buy for the security 800009-002 and is allocated to the last buy for the security 80009-003.

The staples attributes are updated on April 17 with a backward effective date.

| Effective Date | Value split of 800009-002 | Value split of 800009-003 |
|---|---|---|
| February 1, 2020 | 70% | 30% |
| March 1, 2020 | 20% | 80% |
| March 15, 2020 | 90% | 10% |
| April 1, 2020 | 50% | 50% |

> **⚠️ Note:** Rebuild can also take place when the Value Split field in SC.STAPLED.COMPONENT is changed for the existing records created. The Rebuild field must be set to Yes.

All transactions booked with tax effective date between March 15 and March 31 must be rebuilt using the attributes available (with effective date March 15). The SC.STAPLES.REBUILDER application is used to trigger the stapled rebuild processing when there are any back-dated changes in value split. The Staple Parent field accepts the value ALL or a valid stapled parent SECURITY.MASTER ID. Once the record is authorised, the Status field is updated as Activated in SC.STAPLES.REBUILDER application as shown in the below screenshot.

The XXX/ CG.STAPLES.REBUILDER service is used to rebuild the tax lots. The Status field changes to Processed once the service is completed.

The Stapled Component ID field in CG.TXN.BASE is reworked to store the record ID of the SC.STAPLED.COMPONENT . The below screenshot shows the capital gains calculation after the rework has taken place. The sale is allocated to the last buy for the security 800009-002 and is allocated to the second buy for the security 80009-003.


##### Allocating Specific Parcels

Banks have to allocate specific parcel at the end of the financial year that is, the parcels that were allocated by the portfolio parcel disposal method is now opened up for the user for manual allocation. The following are the cases when the Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set to blank or Parent.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Pur Txn Id and Pur Tax Lot Id or TL Alloc | Can be input only for disposal transaction. They hold the transaction ID and tax lot ID of the buy transaction, where the effective date of the buy transaction must be equal to or earlier than the effective date of the disposal. |
| Pur Txn Nom or TL Nom | Holds the nominal from the parcel to be allocated against the sale transaction |
| Pur Cg Pl or Cg Pl | Holds the CG calculated based on the allocation. When user does the allocation for a disposal transaction, the allocation must be done for all the disposed nominal |

When the Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set to Parent

Consider the portfolio 100404-1, which has the following transactions. The tax lot selection method is Min Gain.

However, in this case the child allocations cannot be independent but stapled together. This means that when it comes to specific parcel allocation method it needs to be set at parent level. Therefore, the CG.STAPLES.MANUAL.ALLOC application is used to perform the manual allocation of parcels. The user has to enter the value in the Portfolio No and Security No fields for which manual allocation of parcels is required.

> **⚠️ Note:** The value in the Security No field is the parent Security number and not the child security number.

When the Retrieve Lot field is set to Yes, the system retrieves the lots from CG.TXN.BASE . All the allocations done post the portfolio lock date is unallocated and presented to the user for manual allocation. Once the user manually allocates the parcels and set the Calc Cg field to Yes and validates, the system calculates the CG based on the new allocation.

The Parent Tax Lot Alloc field can be input only for disposal transaction. They holds the Parent Tax Lot Id of the buy transaction, where the effective date of the buy transaction should be equal to the effective date of the disposal or earlier than the effective date of the disposal. The Nominal Alloc field holds the nominal from the parcel to be allocated against the sale transaction. The Cg Pl field holds the capital gains calculated based on the allocation. In the screenshot shown 100 nominal is allocated to the first buy and another 100 nominal is allocated against the second buy. Once the above record is authorised, the CG.TXN.BASE of both the child parcels is updated and capital gains are calculated as shown in the screenshot below. The tax lot method is changed to SPECIFIC indicating specific parcel allocation.


##### Corporate Actions on Stapled Security

The Corporate Actions (CA) is done at the parent instrument level only. For example,

Bonus event on staples is similar to acquisition event where the existing shareholders receive additional shares. This is treated like a purchase, that is, parcels are not created at the parent instrument level. Parcels are created only for the child instruments.

Redemption events such as buy back or sale facility, where the holder of the security sells or redeems his position, is processed at the parent level and this behaves like any other disposal of the parent staple where the parent instrument is disposed off which in turn leads to the disposal of child instruments.

The Rights event is processed at the parent security level. To process rights on staple, the Rights No field in DIARY needs to be set up as a stapled instrument.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the rights instrument is not setup as a staple, the system raises the following error 'When event security is staple, then rights instrument should also be staple’.

- When rights are distributed on a stapled security, from a tax perspective these are in effect rights on the child securities, that is, the rights instrument itself is a staple instrument with underlying child rights. The unit ratio and cost split must be the same as the original staple (event security), else the system raises the following error ‘Component Ratio and Value split must be same in event and rights security’.
- When rights are distributed through a CA event, holdings in SECURITY.POSITION are updated for the parent rights and child rights similar to an acquisition. A child right position is excluded from valuation and does not appear in SC.POS.ASSET . Tax parcels in CG.TXN.BASE are updated only for the child instruments.
- On exercise of rights, the original staple instrument is acquired like any other acquisition and the holdings are updated for both the parent and child, while tax parcels are updated only for the child. On lapse of rights (rights position is liquidated), the holdings in SECURITY.POSITION of both the parent rights and all the child rights are removed. There is a disposal transaction in CG.TXN.BASE of the child rights.
- Rights can also be traded in the market, that is, rights are purchased and sold in the market. Similar to other staple, the acquisition and disposal of rights, results in holding update of both parent and the child. However, from a tax perspective only the CG.TXN.BASE of child parcels are updated. The below example is of a staple with underlying child securities. As illustrated, the rights is also a staple with underlying child rights.

There are a few CA events which is done only at the child level. Events such as stock split or consolidation are processed on the child instrument. For example if there is stock split of a child instrument, this does not affect the other child instruments in the staple. For such cases, the event takes place only at the child instrument.

A separate cost adjustment process is run to ensure that the cost of the parent is equal to sum of the child instruments. This cost adjustment process needs to be run in the following cases:

- Return of capital or call payment on one of the child instrument.
- A particular child has been de-linked from the parent instrument.

This is the event that affects the cost. This is an event where there is a capital return on one child and equivalent call payment on another child and there is zero cash payout as the capital return cancels out the call payment. These events are processed at individual child instrument’s level. However to switch off the accounting, the call payment and capital return are marked as notional. The following options are added to the Instal Distr field in DIARY.TYPE . Instalment - Selected when there is a cost increase, but no accounting entry. Distribution - Selected when there is a cost decrease without any cash distribution. When the Notional Event field in DIARY.TYPE is set to Yes, security update or cash movement is not done. The DIARY is used to create entitlement and capture the user elections, which is used in linked diaries, but cash entry or security movement are not effected. The user elections cannot be partial in this case. When the Notional Cost Adjust field in DIARY.TYPE is set to Yes, there is change in security position and CG.TXN.BASE for child parcels, but statement entries are not generated.

- Income alone events such as, cash dividend or stock dividend are processed on the parent security. The DIARY is created for the parent security based on the ex-dated position of the parent security. Any cost base adjustments is at the component or child security level.
- The income on staple must be apportioned to the child instrument. The apportionment ratio or percentage is not known upfront and is known later. In such cases, the income is attributed to the Primary Child field set in SC.STAPLED.COMPONENT until the actual split is known.
- Income can also have components that reduce the cost as tax free and tax deferred. These income components are at the child instrument level. Any cost adjustment arising out of the income is adjusted at the child instrument level.
- The CG.CA.COST.UPD application allows the cost adjustment at the child instrument level. The Stapled Security field accepts a valid child instrument of the parent or event security. This field indicates which child security undergoes cost adjustment.

When the Staple Alloc Level is set to Parent, the process is same as explained above. However, the following CAs are blocked on child security.

- Buy Back
- Take Over
- Scheme or Conversion
- Stock Split
- Consolidation
- Bonus


##### Staple Conversion

There are events where the staple instrument is exchanged for a standalone instrument. This can happen both ways, that is, a holder of a standalone security can surrender or convert the standalone security and receive the staple security. The other scenario is where the holder of staple surrenders or converts the staple and receives the standalone security.

The conversion is the same when Staple Alloc Level field in CG.PARAMETER is set to blank or Parent.

Standalone Security Exchanged or Converted to Staple

The new security (incoming security) is a staple. It is similar to an acquisition and hence the SECURITY.POSITION is updated for both the parent and the child securities while tax parcels are updated only for the child security. The cost of the acquisition is the deemed proceeds or market price of the staple (apportioned to the childs) and the acquisition date is the implementation date. It means that the cost is not rolled over.

Assume that the security 100046-000 is exchanged for a stapled security. The below screenshot shows the CGs for the portfolio 100291-1.

A CA event Conversion takes place for the above-mentioned security. The below screenshot shows the records in DIARY and ENTITLEMENT created for the CA event.

Once the record is authorised, the SECURITY.POSITION for the parent and child securities are updated and also the CG.TXN.BASE is updated for child securities only.

Staple Exchanged or Converted to a Standalone Security

The conversion process is similar to the above shown event except that the new security or incoming security is a standalone security and the outgoing is the stapled security. This is treated as a disposal of staple, that is, parent and child positions are removed and tax parcels of the child security are disposed. The cost of the standalone security is the deemed proceeds or market price and the acquisition date is the implementation date.

> **⚠️ Note:** Conversion is blocked where both the outgoing security and the incoming security are staples.


##### Stapling and Unstapling Events

A staple is originally formed by stapling together previously listed securities. Post the stapling process, the underlying security is no longer listed in the stock exchange. The stapling arrangement is usually effected by a series of corporate actions usually in the form of an in-specie distribution. For example, if the user holds one of the child security, then the other child security is allotted to the user as an in-specie dividend.

The in-specie distribution is preceded by a stock split or consolidation and a capital adjustment event, such as return of capital. This distribution is done to attain the correct unit ratio and cost value split. This series of CA events are executed on the underlying security, such that the tax parcels and the realised gains are adjusted, created or calculated at the child instrument level.

Post this series of CA events, the tax parcels and holdings on the child instruments are updated correctly in the system. Once the series of CA is over, the final step is to perform the stapling arrangement to create the parent position. The Operation Type field is set to Create Parent in SC.STAPLING.ARRANGEMENT to create the parent position.

Similarly, in certain cases, the staple is unstapled and child instruments become standalone instruments that is, the staple ceases to exist. This can be done by de-linking the child instrument from the parent and in some cases this is followed by removal of child position through a CA. The parent holdings must be removed from the system as the staple no longer exists. The Operation Type field is set to Remove Parent in SC.STAPLING.ARRANGEMENT to remove the parent position. The stapling and unstapling process is the same when Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set to blank or Parent. However, there are few operations allowed only when the Staple Alloc Level is set to Parent, which is explained in the later section.

However, there is a small difference when it comes to performing the stapling arrangement when allocation level is set to child. The following actions does not happen if Staple Alloc Level in CG.PARAMETER is set to blank:

- The Parent Tax Lot ID is not updated
- The system does not prorate the nominal

The system only updates or removes the parent position based on the value in the Primary Child field. The user must check whether the units are matched before performing the stapling process.

#### 📋 Tasks

Stapled securities are created when two or more different securities are contractually bound together so that they cannot be sold separately but are instead treated as a single security. It is especially used in Australia. Many different types of securities can be stapled together, for example, shares, units and debt instruments. More commonly, a stapled security generally consists of a share in a company and an interest in a trust.

In general, the effect of stapling is that each individual security retains its legal character and there is no variation to the rights or obligations attaching to the individual securities. For tax purposes, each underlying component (share, unit or debenture) shall have to be a separate asset with its own attributes (cost base and acquisition date).

A stapled security must be dealt with as a whole, and as such, the individual securities that are stapled cannot be individually traded on the Australia Stock Exchange (ASX).

The Stapled security is referred to as the ‘Parent’ and the individual securities that constitute the staple is referred as ‘Child’ Securities.

### 9.13  Wash Sales


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A wash sale is a transaction in which an investor sells a security at a loss and repurchases it within 30 days of sale. These kind of transactions are done for tax benefits in the form of capital losses. The wash sale is made of minimum three transactions, namely:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Cg Base Update*, *Cg Enh Process*, *Disallowed Loss To Rpl Txn*, *Disallowed Txn*, *Pur Txn Id*, *Replacement Txn*, *Replacement Txn.1*, *ReplacementTransaction.1* ... +3 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A wash sale is a transaction in which an investor sells a security at a loss and repurchases it within 30 days of sale. These kind of transactions are done for tax benefits in the form of capital losses. The wash sale is made of minimum three transactions, namely:

- Original purchase
- Sale
- Replacement purchase

The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) introduced the Wash Sale rule to prevent investors from taking tax deductions in the form of capital loss.


##### Defining Wash Sale Rule

The wash sale rule is an IRS rule that prohibits a taxpayer from claiming a loss on the sale or trade of a security in a wash sale. The IRS rule defines a wash sale as a sale that occurs when an individual sells or trades a security at a loss and within 30 days (before or after this sale) buys a substantially identical stock or security, or acquires a contract or option to buy the security. A wash sale occurs if an individual sells a security and the spouse or a company controlled by the individual buys a substantially equivalent security.


##### Defining Conditions

The conditions mentioned below determines the sale as a wash sale:

- The replacement purchase should be done within 30 days before or after the sale of the security
- The sale should result in a loss

When both these conditions are satisfied the sale is considered as a wash sale and the loss is disallowed. The acquisition date of the replacement transaction is reset to the acquisition date of the original purchase so that the user can have the holding period benefit.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following setup should be done for the wash sale to occur.

- Cg Base Update field in SC.PARAMETER is set to Yes
- Cg Enh Process field in CG.PARAMETER is set to Yes


#### 🔧 Working With

The following are the possible sequence in which wash sale can occur.


##### Replacement Transaction Occurring after the Sale

The sequence of transactions is:

- Initial Buy Transaction
- Sale
- Replacement acquisition

| Transaction Type | Transaction Reference | Date | Quantity | Price | Cost or Proceeds | Gain or Loss | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Buy | ST1 | 1 Jan | 300 | 20 | 6000 |  | Original acquisition |
| Sale | ST2 | 1 Apr | 100 | 13 | 1300 | -700 | Sale resulting in a loss |
| Sale | ST3 | 3 Apr | 100 | 22 | 2200 | 200 | Sale resulting in a gain |
| Buy | ST4 | 15 Apr | 250 | 16 | 3200 |  | Replacement transaction |


##### Replacement Transaction Occurring before the Sale

The sequence of transactions is

- Original acquisition
- Replacement transaction
- Sale

| Trans Type | Transaction Reference | Date | Qty | Price | Cost or Proceeds | Gain or Loss | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Buy | ST1 | 1 Jan | 150 | 20 | 3000 |  | original acquisition |
| Buy | ST2 | 15 Mar | 100 | 25 | 2500 |  |  |
| Sale | ST3 | 1 Apr | -100 | 13 | 1300 | -700 | Sale resulting in a loss |
| Buy | ST4 | 5 Apr | 100 | 18 | 1800 |  |  |


##### Processing of Wash Sales

When an order, transfer or entitlement option is updated in front office, a wash sale check is triggered. If the transaction results in a wash sale effect, then the Front Office (TAP) marks this transaction, as a possible wash sale trigger within TAP. When the resultant SEC.TRADE , SECURITY.TRANSFER or ENTITLEMENT is authorised in Temenos Transact, the same is updated in front office with an operation as accounted. If this transaction has a wash sale trigger set, the Front Office reworks and checks if at the final price and at the authorised date and time, this transaction still results in a wash sale. If yes, Front Office sends the details of adjustments to be made to Temenos Transact.

The following set of information is provided by the front office:

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Sale Txn | Indicates the transaction reference of the wash sale |
| Replacement Txn | Indicates the transaction reference that is identified as replacement transaction for a sale transaction that incurred loss. This is a credit transaction. |

This application holds the wash sale details as received from the front office. When the Sale Txn and Replacement Txn fields are updated, the system automatically fills in the rest of the fields.

> **⚠️ Note:** The other details are updated by the system only in case of loss. The system does not have logic to check whether repurchase has happened within 30 days before or after the sale. All these logic check takes place in front office.

The following screenshot shows that the record in CG.TXN.BASE prior to committing the CG.WASH.SALE.DETS application. The first screenshot is the initial buy transaction that was allocated against the sell transaction. The second screenshot shows the repurchase transaction of the security. The second buy transaction is done within few days of sale of the original acquisition.

When the record in CG.WASH.SALE.DETS is committed, the CG.TXN.BASE pertaining to that record is amended and rebuilt. The below screenshot shows the record in CG.TXN.BASE after committing the record in CG.WASH.SALE.DETS . The acquisition date of the replacement transaction is reset to the acquisition date of the original purchase. The Disallowed Loss To Rpl Txn field holds the loss that is not allowed as part of a wash sale. The Disallowed Txn field holds the transaction reference of original purchase transaction reference* sale transaction reference.

This application is a live file and stores the disallowed loss and replacement transaction used to repurchase the security that was sold. The Pur Txn Id holds the allocated buy transaction for which the sale is declared as Wash Sale.


#### 📋 Tasks

A wash sale is a transaction in which an investor sells a security at a loss and repurchases it within 30 days of sale. These kind of transactions are predominantly done to seek tax benefits in the form of capital losses. Wash sale is made up of minimum of three transactions

1. Original Purchase
2. Sale
3. Replacement Purchase

To prevent investors from taking tax deductions in the form of capital loss, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) introduced the Wash Sale Rule.

Wash Sale Rule

IRS rule that prohibits a taxpayer from claiming a loss on the sale or trade of a security in a wash sale. The rule defines a wash sale as one that occurs when an individual sells or trades a security at a loss, and within 30 days before or after this sale, buys a “substantially identical” stock or security, or acquires a contract or option to do so. A wash sale also results if an individual sells a security, and the spouse or a company controlled by the individual buys a substantially equivalent security.

## Appendix B: Consolidated Field Reference


This appendix consolidates all field description tables from across the documentation, grouped by sub-module. This provides a single reference for all field definitions.


### European Savings Directive (ET)


**Misc**

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Tax Option | Defines the company level settings on the levy of EU tax or exchange of information. Allowed values are Wht or Info. |
| Sc Hold Period | Allowed values are Buy Date, Eu Date or Status Date. This is a no change field, once the transaction base is built. |
| Tax Basis | Defines the method used to build the base amount for tax calculation. Allowed values are Fifo, Lifo or Average. This is a no change field, once the transaction base is built. |
| Cu Eff Date Fld | Holds the effective date for the customer in CUSTOMER application. |
| Sm Eff Date Fld | Holds the effective date for the security in SECURITY.MASTER application. |
| Cu Tax Grp | Specifies the customer group based on the revised condition priority which is under EU tax. For these customers, WHT is deducted. Customers falling under this group has the EU.TXN.BASE updated and it facilitates report generation. The calculated tax is also updated in the base. |
| Tax Upd Mode | Indicates whether tax needs to be updated online or during batch(COB). Temenos Transact now supports online mode only. |
| Cu Info Grp | The customer group based on the revised condition priority which is under the exchange of information. These are customers who have opted to report, instead of tax being withheld. This overrides the default setting in the Tax Option field. Customers falling under this group has the EU.TXN.BASE updated and it facilitates report generation. However, tax is not calculated and only allocation details of each buy against a specific sale is updated in the base. |
| Info Upd Mode | Indicates whether the EU.TXN.BASE needs to be updated online or in batch(COB). Temenos Transact now supports online mode only. |
| Cu Exempt Group | Holds the customer group which is exempt from EU tax. EU.TXN.BASE is not updated for this group. |
| Update Log | Is a Yes or No field. If the field is set to Yes, then the log is maintained for the sequence of updates to a specific holding. The log can be viewed in the EU.UPDATE.LOG application. |
| Total Disc Prem | Holds the threshold percentage below which tax is not deducted for interest earned on debt instruments. |
| Period Disc Prem | Holds the threshold discount or premium percentage per period below which tax is not deducted for interest earned on debt instruments. If different countries have different exemption percentages, the EU.TAX.PARAM application must be set company wise with respective values. |
| Inc Source Tax | This field determines if source tax that is already deducted on interest, must be included or excluded for tax calculation. |
| Eu Purge Date | Allows the user to purge transactions from the EU.TAX.LINK application and move them to the EU.TAX.LINK.PAST application. |

**Misc**

| Application Name | Routine | Description |
|---|---|---|
| SUB.ASSET.TYPE | V.SC.EU.TAXBASIS.CHECK | Input routine which allows the change only if the record in EU.TAX.LINK does not exist. |
| SECURITY.MASTER | V.SC.EU.TAXBASIS.CHECK | Input routine which allows the change only if the record in EU.TAX.LINK does not exist. |
| V.SC.EU.ORIGYIELD.CHECK | Input routine which calculates and populates the yield value. |  |
| V.SC.EU.PRICE.CHECK | Validation routine for which Issue Price and/or Redem Price fields allows input only for bonds. |  |
| V.SC.EU.PRICE.CHECK | Input routine, if EU retention tax is included in SC Tax Code and Issue Price fields. These are mandatory fields. |  |
| V.SC.EU.INTCTR.CHECK | Validation routine for Interest Counter field. Input allowed only for shares. |  |
| SEC.OPEN.ORDER | V.SC.EU.INTCTR.CHECK | Validation routine for Cu Int Ctr field which allows input only for shares and the value is defaulted from SECURITY.MASTER . |
| SC.EXE.SEC.ORDERS | V.SC.EU.INTCTR.CHECK | Validation routine for Cu Int Ctr field which allows input only for shares and the value is defaulted from SECURITY.MASTER . |
| SEC.TRADE | V.SC.EU.INTCTR.CHECK | Validation routine for Cu Int Ctr field which allows input only for shares and the value is defaulted from SECURITY.MASTER. |
| SECURITY.TRANSFER | V.SC.EU.INTCTR.CHECK | Validation routine for Cu Int Ctr field which allows input only for shares and the value is defaulted from SECURITY.MASTER. |
| V.SC.EU.TRFRDATE.CHECK | Validation routine for Trfr Eff Date field and the value should not be a future date. |  |
| POSITION.TRANSFER | V.SC.EU.INTCTR.CHECK | Validation routine for Interest Counter field which allows input only for shares. |
| V.SC.EU.TRFRDATE.CHECK | Validation routine for Trfr Eff Date field and the value should not be a future date. |  |
| DIARY | V.SC.EU.INTCTR.CHECK | Validation routine for Interest Counter field which allows input only for shares and the value is defaulted from SECURITY.MASTER . |
| V.SC.EU.INTDIST.CHECK | Validation routine for Int Dist Factor field and allows input only for shares. |  |
| ENTITLEMENT | V.SC.EU.INTCTR.CHECK | Validation routine for Interest Counter field which allows input only for shares and the value is defaulted from SECURITY.MASTER . |
| V.SC.EU.INTDIST.CHECK | Validation routine for Int Dist Factor field which allows input only for shares. |  |

**Misc**

| S.No. | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | EU.PARAMETER | This is a company-level parameter containing the details of each company that has to be converted. Each company must be converted sharing a currency file at the same time. This holds the following details: Currency that needs to be converted Date on which the conversion is to be run Category required for suspense accounts Relative transaction codes |
| 2. | EU.TAX.PARAM | This is a company-level parameter containing the details to be set up for EU Retention Tax. This holds the following details: Required tax options Tax inventory methods Tax updation mode |

**Tax on Redemption of Debt Instruments**

|---|---|
| Total Hpi | Holds the average total interest of the outstanding nominal |
| Avg Hpi | Holds the average interest of the position |
| Total Discount | Holds the average total discount of the outstanding nominal |
| Avg Disc | Holds the average discount of the position |


### Global Custody (GC)


**Misc**

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Custody Port No | Stores the alternate portfolio ID that is identified in the settlement instructions (MT 540-543). |
| Custody Eligible | Stores if the portfolio is authorised for custody business. |
| Eam Id | Stores the Eam Id, who has the mandate on behalf of this portfolio and sends the settlement instructions. |
| Mandate Recd | Stores the sub-asset type, for which the EAM has the mandate. |
| Hold Stmt Freq | Holds the time-frequency based on which the MT535 message is generated for this portfolio. Allowed frequencies are daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly. |
| Balance Type | Implies the type of balance to be sent in the MT535 message. Allowed values are : Traded, Contractual, and Settled. |

**Misc**

| Parameters | Description |
|---|---|
| Internal Broker | Indicates the internal broker used in creation of SEC.TRADE and SECURITY.TRANSFER while processing the incoming MT540-543 messages from institutional customers. |
| Trd Cr Txn | Defines the credit transaction of SEC.TRADE created out of incoming MT541 or MT543. |
| Trd Dr Txn | Defines the debit transaction of SEC.TRADE created out of incoming MT541 or MT543. |
| Ext Trf Cr Txn | Defines the credit transaction of SECURITY.TRANSFER created out of incoming MT540 or MT542. |
| Ext Trf Dr Txn | Defines the credit transaction of SECURITY.TRANSFER created out of incoming MT540 or MT542. |
| Int Trf Cr Txn | Defines the credit transaction code for internal security transfer created out of incoming MT542. |
| Ext Trf Dr Txn | Defines the debit transaction code for internal security transfer created out of incoming MT542. |
| Allowed Sec Type | Defines the allowed security types (asset type or sub-asset type) for custody or account service operations. Defining ALL in this field allows all product groups for this operation to create and authorise respective trades or transfers through incoming MT540-543 messages. |
| OFS Source | Indicates the OFS channel used for creation of trades or transfers. |
| OFS Version | Indicates the OFS version of trade or transfer that are used to create trade and transfers. |
| Mkt Fee Calc | Indicates whether the Market Fee for Security Trades has to be calculated based on Charge Calculation rules ( SCDX.CHARGE.PARAMETER ) or based on the value in the Incoming Swift. Default setup is to apply from Incoming 54n message. |

**Misc**

| Parameters | Description |
|---|---|
| Send MT564 Canc | Defines whether to generate MT564 when DIARY is reversed. |
| In MT564 Func | Holds the function of incoming MT564 for which outward MT564 needs to be sent. |
| In MT564 Status | Holds the status of incoming MT564 for which outward MT564 needs to be sent. |

|---|---|

| DealPrice | Price |

**Order Management for Institutional Customers**

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Msg Type | Holds the type of message received - SETR029 in this case |
| DealPrice | Holds the deal price |
| Sender ID | Indicates the Transact Customer ID of the sender or the BIC code, if the sender ID cannot be identified |
| Trade ID | Holds the @ID of the corresponding record in SEC.TRADE , based on the order ID above. If there are multiple trades available for the order, then this field appears blank. |
| Msg Process Status | If the Msg Type field is SETR029, this field is blank |
| Link Msg Ref | Displays the SETR027 message, for which the cancellation is received. The inward reference of SETR027 is identified and populated in this field. |
| Action Status | By default, this field remains blank and it is a free format field, where the user can enter any value to indicate that an action is taken |
| Action Notes | Allows users to enter any note regarding the action |

**MiFID Questionnaire**

| Field Name | Description |

| Suitability Chk | If this field is set to Yes, the following fields get enabled: Asset Type Sub Asset Type |
| Asset Type | Holds the valid asset type from the ASSET.TYPE application |
| Sub Asset Type | Holds the valid sub asset type from the SUB.ASSET.TYPE application The Sub Asset Type field is a subset of the Asset Type field. Thereby, assigning a value to the Sub Asset Type field is not allowed when the Asset Type field is empty. |
| Question ID | Holds the question ID. This is a free text field, where the input must be without space, for example, QUESTION.1 or QUESTION.TAX. |

| Mandatory | Indicates whether the question is mandatory or not. The values in this field are Yes or No and the default value is No. |

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|

| Max Score Points | Holds the maximum points for the score ID |
| Min Score Points | Holds the minimum points for the score ID |
| App Field | Assigns the points for determining the most suitable investment program. This field accepts any Question ID and the following field names from the SC.MIFID.CLIENT.INFO application: Age Education Level Profession Income Source * Income Assets Held * Value Assets Fin Commit * Val Fin Commit Invest Amount Invest Period Investment Objective Risk Appetite Expect Return Asset Class Sub Asset Class |
| Operand | Can be EQ (equal to) or RG (range) |
| Value | Holds the expected value in the App Field |

| Points Scored | Holds the total points scored |
| Eligible Invest Program | Holds the eligible investment program, based on the points scored by the customer |
| Default Invest Program | This is a mandatory field. If an eligible investment program cannot be determined using the points logic explained above, then value in this field is applied for the customer, by default. |

**MiFID Regulation Valuation Drop Notification**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Drop Percent Val | Stores the percentage drop in the portfolio value (and multiples) that should be recorded for MiFID II purpose. As per current MiFID II guidelines, this should be configured as 10. |
| Reporting Freq | Stores the reporting frequency. The allowed values are: Daily - The system checks the percentage drop set in the Drop Percent Val field with the closing balance of the previous day. Monthly - The system checks the percentage drop set in the Drop Percent Val field with the opening value on the first day of the month. Quarterly - The system checks the percentage drop set in the Drop Percent Val field with the opening value on first day of the quarter. Semi-annually Annually |
| Reporting Freq St Date | Stores the start date of the reporting frequency. If reporting frequency is set to Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-annually, Annually, the user should define the start date in this field. If the user sets the frequency to Quarterly, the user can define the quarter month. If the start date is set to Jan 1, the first quarter is set from January to March and the other quarters are set subsequently. If set to Feb 1, the first quarter is set from February to April and the other quarters are set subsequently. |

**MiFID Regulation Valuation Drop Notification**

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Portfolio No | Holds the portfolio ID for which the record is created |
| Currency | Holds the reference currency of the portfolio |
| xx | Holds the start date of the reporting period. This is updated based on the setup in SC.MIFID.PARAM |
| Reporting Prd End Date - xx | Holds the end date of the reporting period. This is updated based on the setup in SC.MIFID.PARAM |
| Drop Date - xx | Date on which x% drop occurred for the first time in the MiFID reporting period |
| Drop Pct Recorded - xx | Stores the actual drop (multiples of drops like 10%, 20% etc., as parameterised) in portfolio valuation that was recorded |
| Pf Value - xx | Stores the portfolio valuation on the drop day in the reference currency of the portfolio. |
| xx Sec Acc Master | The system defaults this configurable field to N. If set to Y, it indicates that this drop is recorded due to some internal system error and a letter need not be sent to the client to inform the drop. |

Where, pursuant to Article 26(5) of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014, a trading venue submits a transaction report on behalf of a firm that is not subject to Regulation (EU) No 600/2014, the trading venue shall populate this field with a number that has been internally generated by the trading venue and that is unique for each transaction report submitted by the trading venue. | SEC.TRADE reference |
| TradeIdIndicator |  | Updated as 1 always.Any other change has to be handled Locally |
| TradingVenueTransactionId | This is a number generated by trading venues and disseminated to both the buying and the selling parties in accordance with Article 12 of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/580(1).
